rows.defect: Foliage colour and the small dark green-black fruit carry the read, but the gnarled twisted fissured trunk - the single most recognisable thing about an olive - is the same perfectly straight smooth brown stick used by every other tree here. The leaves are one flat tone with no silver underside showing, and the crown is a solid glowing blob instead of open and airy.
rows.fix: Replace the straight trunk with a thick twisted fluted bole with deep dark fissures and a hollow, and flip a third of the leaves to their pale silver face.

rows.readsAs: an orange tree
rows.defect: The species reads correctly, which is exactly why Mango, Peach and Persimmon reading the same way is a problem. Two mustReads are still missing: there is no white five-petal blossom anywhere alongside the fruit, and no wing is visible on any leaf stalk. The rind is smooth with a specular dot rather than pitted, and the crown is a fuzzy cloud rather than a dense rounded evergreen mass.
rows.fix: Scatter six to eight small white five-petal flowers with yellow centres through the crown and stipple the fruit rind.

rows.readsAs: a palm or cycad sapling
rows.defect: The trunk FORKS into two brown limbs, directly contradicting the note that the plant has no branches, and it is smooth brown with no grey leaf-ring scars. The crown is a swept fan of stiff pinnate feather fronds, not large deeply lobed palmate blades on long hollow stalks. There is exactly ONE small fruit, wedged in the fork, instead of melons clustered in a ring packed against the trunk.
rows.fix: Make the trunk a single unbranched grey column banded with leaf-scar rings, ring a dozen fat green-orange melons around it directly under the crown, and rebuild the leaves as huge hand-lobed palmate blades.

rows.readsAs: an apricot or small orange tree
rows.defect: The narrow lance leaves are present but they radiate stiffly outward instead of drooping willow-like. The fruit are round orange-pink spheres with a hard specular highlight - no fuzz, no red-over-gold blush, and critically no suture cleft down one side, which is the peach's signature. The crown is the family blob on a straight stick, not a low spreading vase.
rows.fix: Add a visible dark suture groove down each fruit and a soft matt velvety edge instead of the glossy highlight, and let the leaves hang downward.

rows.readsAs: an apple tree
rows.defect: The fruit are round yellow-green spheres - the pear taper, the single mustRead that defines the species, is completely absent, so this is an apple. The crown is also broad and squat despite the 0.6 aspect calling for an upright narrow oval taller than an apple tree, and there is no white blossom with dark anthers anywhere.
rows.fix: Redraw every fruit with the classic pear profile - narrow shoulder swelling to a fat base - hanging on a long visible stalk, and compress the crown into a tall narrow oval.

rows.readsAs: an orange tree
rows.defect: The tree is in full green leaf with round orange spheres in it, which is the exact read of the Orange asset in this batch. The classic persimmon look the note demands - fruit still hanging on a completely leafless tree - is not attempted. There is no four-lobed green calyx cap on any fruit and no dark blocky checkered bark; the trunk is the same plain brown stick as everywhere else.
rows.fix: Strip the foliage entirely, leaving bare dark branch tracery with orange lanterns hanging on it, each capped by a stiff four-lobed green calyx.

rows.readsAs: a palm or cycad - and specifically the same drawing as the Papaya
rows.defect: This is the Papaya asset with the fruit recoloured: same forked brown woody trunk, same swept fan of stiff feather fronds, same tiny nub in the fork. None of the three mustReads survive - there is no green false trunk, no huge wind-torn paddle blades, and no heavy hanging bunch of straight green fingers, only a pale speck at the fork.
rows.fix: Rebuild as a green unbranched false stem with a few enormous ribbon paddle leaves torn into ribs, and hang one large bunch of straight angular green fingers below the crown.

rows.readsAs: a plum tree
rows.defect: The deep purple oval fruit carry the read, but they are rendered glossy with a bright specular highlight, which is the visual opposite of the pale waxy bloom the reference names as a mustRead. There is no white blossom and no twiggy thorny structure - the crown is again a soft cloud on a straight stick, so the fruit appear to float in foliage rather than sit on twigs.
rows.fix: Kill the specular highlight and dust each fruit with a soft pale blue-white bloom, hazier toward the shoulder.

rows.readsAs: a cherry tree
rows.defect: The fruit are three small glossy round red spheres with a plain stem dot on top - the crown of stiff points at the top of the fruit, listed first among the mustReads and the one thing that makes a pomegranate a pomegranate, is nowhere. There are no vivid orange-red crumpled trumpet flowers, and although the form is specified as a shrub it is drawn on the same tall bare single-trunk tree chassis as everything else in the batch.
rows.fix: Enlarge the fruit into a hard leathery red-gold globe topped with a splayed spiky calyx crown, and rebuild the plant as a low multi-stemmed twiggy spiny shrub carrying scarlet trumpet flowers.

rows.readsAs: a generic tropical fern-palm sapling with three tiny clusters of red berries — most strangers say raspberries or redcurrants stuck in a palm
rows.defect: The identity of a rambutan is the soft green-tipped hair covering the fruit; the rendered fruit is three clusters of small SMOOTH red spheres with no spines, hairs or fuzz of any kind at any pixel. The other must-read is inverted too: instead of a dense dark rounded crown the crown is a pale, airy, see-through starburst of radiating fern sprigs over a light-green mist, and the leaf glyph is a many-paired fern ladder rather than 2-4 pairs of big leathery oval leaflets.
rows.fix: Redraw the fruit at 2-3x its current size as ovals whose entire outline is broken by long soft curving hairs (red hairs with green tips), and replace the radial fern starburst with a dense, dark, opaque rounded crown mass of large paired leathery leaflets.

rows.readsAs: a small tree with three striped green watermelons or gooseberries sitting in the leaves
rows.defect: The fruit is drawn as three small round balls with vertical light stripes, floating in the middle of the leaf cloud. Soursop's identity is a single HEAVY, LARGE, HEART/KIDNEY-shaped fruit covered in soft curved spines, hanging off the trunk or a thick branch and visibly weighing it down — none of that is present: no heart taper, no spine texture on the outline, no mass, no attachment to the trunk, and the fruit is a fraction of the size it must be relative to the crown. The 'small open crown' is also the family's stock opaque green cloud, not an open one.
rows.fix: Replace the three balls with ONE large asymmetric heart-shaped fruit hanging on a short stalk from the trunk or a thick low branch, its silhouette entirely made of soft recurved spine hooks, and shrink/open the crown so the fruit dominates.

rows.readsAs: a small lemon or apricot tree — four plain glowing yellow balls in a fern bush
rows.defect: The fruit are four featureless yellow-orange spheres with a glow halo. The five sharp longitudinal wings ARE the organism — carambola is named for them — and there is not one rib, edge, facet or star-end visible on any of the four. There are also no lilac-pink flower clusters on old wood anywhere, and the fruit float on the crown face instead of hanging from trunk and branches. The ferny pinnate foliage is the only must-read that lands, and it is the same sprig glyph used on Rambutan and Walnut.
rows.fix: Draw the fruit as elongated waxy yellow bodies with three visible sharp ribs down the near face and a pointed star-notch at the bottom end, plus a couple of tiny lilac flower dots on the trunk/old wood.

rows.readsAs: the same fern-palm sapling as Rambutan and Starfruit, with three small brown nuts or cocoa pods stuck to it
rows.defect: Three must-reads all fail at once. (1) There is no broad open crown and no heavy grey furrowed limbs — the tree is one smooth flat-brown pole with zero branching and a small hazy blob crown, the opposite of a mature walnut's wide grey-limbed frame. (2) The leaf is the same tiny-many-leaflet fern ladder used on Rambutan and Starfruit, not big pinnate leaves with a few large smooth-edged leaflets. (3) The fruit is drawn as bare BROWN spheres, i.e. the shelled nut, when the packet's own note says the husk on the tree is a smooth GREEN plum-like ball — the colour actively contradicts the reference and pushes the read toward cocoa/nutmeg.
rows.fix: Recolour the fruit to smooth pale-green plum-like husks (one split to show the brown shell), and rebuild the tree as a broad open crown carried on two or three thick grey furrowed limbs that visibly leave the trunk inside the silhouette, with far larger and far fewer leaflets.

rows.readsAs: a bunch of cut fern stems with fuzzy purple thistle heads
rows.defect: The identity of blackberry is the long ARCHING cane that roots where it touches down; the render is a stiff upright vase of straight canes that never bends. The leaf is a fine feathery fern frond, not a palmate hand of 3-5 toothed leaflets. The fruit reads as soft purple pom-poms (flower heads), not glossy knobbly drupelet clusters, and there are no red unripe berries alongside. The white dashes on the canes read as pale twig stubs or tags rather than hooked prickles.
rows.fix: Draw two or three long canes that arch over past horizontal and re-root at the tip, hang mixed black/red knobbly drupelet clusters underneath them, and replace the fern frond with a 3-5 leaflet palmate leaf.

rows.readsAs: a leafy shrub with small blue berries — close enough to blueberry
rows.defect: The oval leaves and the blue berry clusters land, but neither of the two diagnostic details is present: no white urn-shaped bell flowers anywhere, and the berries are plain blue spheres with no five-point crown scar at the tip. The form is also wrong for aspect 0.8 — it is the family's tall narrow vase rather than a dense broad twiggy bush, and the leaves march in perfect opposite pairs when the reference calls them alternate.
rows.fix: Add a few nodding white urn-shaped bells among the fruit and put a small five-point star scar on the outward face of each berry.

rows.readsAs: an upright red-berried garden shrub, cotoneaster or holly-ish
rows.defect: Growth form is flatly wrong. Cranberry is a wiry creeping MAT over bog moss on hair-thin runners at aspect 2.5 — wider than tall, hugging the ground. What is drawn is the family's tall vertical vase on a thick woody basal trunk, taller than wide, with no moss, no runners and no ground plane at all. The berries sit as clustered pom-poms on top of the cane tips instead of single red fruit on thin upright stalks above a mat, and there are no backswept crane-head pink petals.
rows.fix: Rebuild it as a low horizontal mat: thread-fine runners trailing sideways across bog moss with tiny two-ranked leaves, and single red berries lifted on short thin stalks above the mat.

rows.readsAs: a lobed-leaf shrub with red flower clusters
rows.defect: The palmate lobed leaf reads and the canes are correctly thornless, but the fruit presentation — the single thing that separates currant from gooseberry — is inverted. The berries should hang DOWNWARD in a drooping string (raceme) below the branch; here they are packed into upright pom-pom clumps sitting on top of each cane tip, which reads as flower heads rather than fruit. Side by side with Gooseberry in this batch the two are the same picture with the tip blob recoloured.
rows.fix: Replace each terminal clump with a pendulous string of 8-12 small round berries hanging clear below the cane, graded from large at the top to small at the tip.

rows.readsAs: the same purple-flowered fern bundle as Blackberry
rows.defect: This is Blackberry's image again with a slightly bushier fan — same basal cone, same straight canes, same fine fern fronds, same fuzzy purple ball clusters. None of the three must-reads survive: there is no big FLAT plate-like head of creamy white flowers (the heads are small purple spheres), the berry heads do not nod or hang heavily, and the stems carrying them are plain brown rather than crimson. The pinnate leaf is drawn as a fine fern rather than 5-7 broad pointed toothed leaflets.
rows.fix: Give it one or two wide flat-topped white umbels held horizontally like plates, and a second heavy purple-black berry plate nodding over on a crimson stalk.

rows.readsAs: a shrub with pale green buds on top — indistinguishable from Currant
rows.defect: Both identity must-reads are absent. The berries should hang SINGLY beneath the stem; instead pale green spheres are bunched into clusters sitting on top of the cane tips, and they carry no pale longitudinal stripes and no translucency. Sharp spines at each leaf node are effectively missing — I can find one tiny white dash near the base of the trunk and nothing at any node. The result is the Currant render with the fruit recoloured green, which collapses the exact distinction the packet flags.
rows.fix: Hang individual striped translucent berries one per node on short stalks below the branch, and put a clear paired spine at every leaf node.

rows.readsAs: lavender or a loosestrife — tall bare stems with pink flower spikes
rows.defect: The slim purple-pink spires land, but the plant they sit on is wrong. The render is a tall open vase of largely BARE brown canes, not a low wiry twiggy mound; the negative space between the stems dominates the silhouette. The leaves are sparse grey slivers that stick out sideways from the stems, which is the opposite of the must-read (minute scale leaves pressed flat against the stem in four ranks). Foliage volume is far too low for a heather.
rows.fix: Compress it into a low dense cushion of many short wiry twigs and clothe every twig in tight scale leaves hugging the stem so no bare bark shows, with the flower spires just clearing the mound.

rows.readsAs: a generic lollipop cartoon tree wrapped in green smoke
rows.defect: The crown is a soft amorphous green fog blob with a few feathery sprigs poking out of it and two unexplained dark lens shapes floating inside — it reads as a rendering artifact, not foliage. The trunk is a straight unbranched vertical pole with a rounded top, which contradicts the must-read crooked LOW-BRANCHING trunk and wide FLAT crown. No paired straight thorns at any node, and no straw-coloured seed pods hanging in bunches anywhere.
rows.fix: Kill the fog layer and build the crown from discrete bipinnate sprays on a low, crooked, multi-forked trunk with a flat-topped spreading profile; hang pale straw pods in bunches and put paired white thorns at the nodes.

rows.readsAs: a pink daisy or cosmos plant
rows.defect: The upright wand-like stems from the base actually suit this species and the narrow grey-green lance leaves are right in shape. But the flowers are single many-petalled daisies, one per stem tip, with radiating thin petals — not dense terminal HEADS of five-petalled pinwheels, so the flower reads as the wrong genus entirely. The leaves are arranged in opposite pairs rather than whorls of three, they carry no pale midrib, and the foliage is too sparse for oleander's dense evergreen mass.
rows.fix: Replace each single daisy with a tight cluster of several five-petalled pinwheel flowers at the shoot tip, and set the leaves in visible whorls of three with a pale midrib stripe.

rows.readsAs: the Blackberry image with pink pom-poms instead of purple ones
rows.defect: The packet's own note says raspberry must NOT look like blackberry, and this is the same chassis, the same fine fern fronds and the same terminal ball clusters, recoloured. The fruit reads as pink flower pom-poms, not red thimble-shaped hollow-cored berries — there is no thimble profile and no hollow mouth. The white-felted undersides that are supposed to flash on the leaves are entirely absent; the foliage is one flat green. The leaf is a fern frond rather than 3-5 toothed leaflets.
rows.fix: Draw distinct red thimble berries with visible drupelet bobbles and a hollow open base, and flip some leaflets to show a chalk-white underside against the green.

rows.readsAs: a silver willow-leaved shrub with cream flower wands
rows.defect: The silver-grey foliage and the pale wands of flower heads above it do carry sagebrush colour. The two structural must-reads do not appear: the leaves are plain smooth lance/willow slivers with pointed tips and no sign of the three blunt teeth at the tip that name the plant, and the trunk is the family's clean smooth tapered brown cone with straight canes rather than a twisted gnarled woody stem with shredding grey bark.
rows.fix: Cut each leaf tip into three blunt lobes so the wedge shape reads, and replace the smooth cone base with a short gnarled twisting trunk showing vertical shredded grey bark strips.

rows.readsAs: a small sprig of silver-white leaves
rows.defect: The chalky white-grey foliage is the one thing that lands, and it lands well. But the seed structure is missing entirely — there is not a single papery fan-shaped winged bract anywhere on the plant, and the reference makes that the harvest. The form is also wrong: instead of a dense stiff ROUNDED twiggy mound this is a narrow top-heavy fan on a bare stalk, the smallest and thinnest silhouette in the batch, with open dark gaps through the middle where a saltbush should be solid.
rows.fix: Fill it out into a dense rounded dome of stiff short twigs with no see-through gaps, and hang clusters of small papery fan-shaped winged bracts through the foliage.

rows.readsAs: A generic strap-leaved ornamental clump - liriope, spider plant or a plantain - topped by a single dense foxtail/Timothy-style bead spike; nobody names Poa meadow-grass.
rows.defect: The identity must-read is absent. The reference calls for an airy OPEN PYRAMIDAL PANICLE on fine whorled branches; what is drawn is a narrow, dense, unbranched cylindrical column of pale beads on a bare stick - a contracted spike, which belongs to a different grass tribe entirely and is the visual opposite of a panicle. There is not one branch anywhere on the inflorescence, so the 'fine whorled panicle branches' must-read is also entirely missing. Secondary problems: the blades are broad, stiff strap-shaped ribbons rather than soft narrow flat blades, no boat-shaped (cucullate) tips are visible on any of them, and the tuft base is a single solid opaque green wedge rather than individual culms rising from a loose crown, which pushes it toward the thatch-mound look the reference explicitly forbids.
rows.fix: Replace the bead column with an actual panicle: a central rachis bearing 4-6 whorls of 3-5 fine hair-thin branchlets each, longest at the bottom and shortest at the top so the outline is a wide-based open triangle, with small two-to-four-floret spikelets only at the branch TIPS and clear dark background visible through the interior of the head.

rows.readsAs: a pink fern frond or a feather
rows.defect: Drawn on the leaf-ladder chassis: narrow lance leaflets in a strict opposite ladder, not the big soft broad oval-diamond alternate leaves specified. The must-read heavy plume — a thick fleshy drooping tassel of seed — is a 2px crimson bead thread barely taller than one leaflet, so the organ that IS amaranth is effectively absent. The crimson is applied to the leaf blades instead of the stem and veins.
rows.fix: Replace the thread with a fat drooping crimson tassel at least a third of the plant's height and half its width, and swap the ladder leaflets for a few large alternate broad leaves on a thick crimson grooved stem.

rows.readsAs: a generic green leafy rosette or a houseplant
rows.defect: The clump of broad lance-oval leaves is there and is the best-drawn foliage in the batch, but the leaves radiate from a single hidden point with no long sheathing stalks, and two of the three must-reads are simply not drawn: no small white asymmetric flowers anywhere, and no knobbly pale scaled rhizome at the base — the base is buried in the leaf fan with not even a shadow of a root.
rows.fix: Expose long sheathing petioles below the blades and draw a cluster of pale knobbly scale-ringed rhizomes at the base, plus two or three small white asymmetric flowers.

rows.readsAs: an ornamental gold grass with a brass screw pushed into it
rows.defect: The single feature that makes barley unmistakable — awns longer than the head itself, fanning up in a long bristling sweep — is reduced to a small flared cap sitting on top of a short ribbed cylinder, so the awns are shorter than the ear rather than several times longer. The head is also ramrod upright when the must-read demands it nod over when ripe. The head object is identical to the one on Millet, Oats, Rice, Rye and Sorghum.
rows.fix: Draw the awns as a long fanned sweep two to three times the ear's length streaming up and back, and tip the whole ear over on a bent neck.

rows.readsAs: a green caterpillar or a fern frond
rows.defect: Same leaf-ladder column as Amaranth, Potato and Quinoa with only the leaflet outline changed. The leaflets are plain rounded ovals — the arrowhead/heart shape that is the first must-read is nowhere on the asset. The stem is plain green, not red-flushed or jointed, and the three-angled pyramid seeds are absent; the only harvest cue is one small white blob at the apex.
rows.fix: Rebuild as a sparse open broadleaf herb with a handful of large alternate arrowhead leaves on a red jointed stem, and hang visible sharply three-sided brown seeds under the flower clusters.

rows.readsAs: a young hemp or cannabis bush
rows.defect: The palmate narrow-fingered leaflets on red-brown canes do carry the right leaf idea, but the leaflets are drawn at a fraction of the size the reference calls for (large palmate leaves), so they read as small hemp leaves scattered along bare sticks. The petioles are not distinguishable in colour from the canes, so the striking red leaf-stalk cue is lost, and the cluster of fat tapering tubers at the base — the entire reason cassava is a staple crop — is absent; the stems just vanish into the shadow.
rows.fix: Enlarge the palmate leaves three-fold on visible red petioles and draw four or five fat tapering brown tubers radiating out from the stem base.

rows.readsAs: a bamboo cane with a pink palm flower and a pine cone stuck to it
rows.defect: None of the three must-reads survives. The top tassel is a stiff radiating pink-salmon fan that reads as an anemone or palm inflorescence, not a feathery straw-coloured tassel. The cob is a bare brown pointed cone with a spray of stiff yellow spokes fanning off its tip — it reads as a shuttlecock or a cone with a broom, with no green husk and no soft drooping silk. The stalk is a slim jointed bamboo pole carrying only five narrow leaves, not a thick solid stalk with wide arching strap leaves, and there is no white midrib.
rows.fix: Sheathe the cob in green husks with soft drooping pale silk at its tip, recolour the top tassel to feathery straw, and thicken the stalk with wide white-midribbed strap leaves in two alternating ranks.

rows.readsAs: a yellow-green ornamental grass clump with a small ear
rows.defect: The straight central cane with a single dense grain head over arching narrow blades is roughly the right idea, but the head is a thin short cylinder — nothing like the thick bottlebrush the must-read asks for — and it carries the same flared trapezoid cap the other five grasses wear, which adds an awn-like flare millet does not have. It is the identical fountain silhouette used for Barley, Oats, Rice, Rye and Sorghum with only a hue change.
rows.fix: Fatten the head into a plump cylindrical bottlebrush three times its current width, packed with visible round beads, and delete the flared cap.

rows.readsAs: a cream grass clump with a screw head on a stick
rows.defect: The reference states the identity as a negative: no compact ear and no bristling awn mass, just a loose spreading panicle of teardrop spikelets dangling on fine threads. What is drawn is exactly the forbidden thing — a compact ribbed ear with a bristling flared cap, the same head object as Barley and Rye. The delicate open silhouette is replaced by the same dense fountain of blades. The asset directly contradicts its own must-read.
rows.fix: Replace the ear entirely with an airy branched panicle of dangling teardrop spikelets on thin drooping threads, and thin the leaf clump so light shows through.

rows.readsAs: a fern, or a bottlebrush conifer sprig
rows.defect: Leaf-ladder chassis again, here with dozens of tiny identical feathery leaflets stacked in two dense ranks — the opposite of the specified pinnate leaf of LARGE terminal leaflets with small leaflets between them, so the uneven-sized leaflet cue that makes a potato leaf recognisable is gone. There is one lone white star flower instead of a cluster, and no yellow anther cone. Most damaging: no tubers and no stolons at the base at all, so a plant grown entirely for its tubers shows none.
rows.fix: Draw a few large terminal leaflets with small ones interleaved on a sprawling angular stem, and add a knot of knobbly brown eyed tubers on short stolons at the base.

rows.readsAs: a pale bottlebrush or a fuzzy caterpillar on a pin
rows.defect: The mealy pale-green toothed leaves are the right colour and roughly the right outline, but they are packed onto the same rectangular leaf-ladder column as Amaranth, Buckwheat and Potato, which quinoa never looks like — quinoa is an open leafy herb topped by a chunky branched panicle. That panicle, the must-read that carries the identity and the hot cream/magenta/orange colour, is drawn as a single thin red bead thread poking out of the top. The grooved striped stem is a bare hairline.
rows.fix: Shrink the leaf mass and crown the plant with a broad chunky branched seed panicle in magenta-orange at least as wide as the foliage.

rows.readsAs: a green ornamental fountain grass with a screw in it
rows.defect: All three must-reads fail simultaneously. The seed head is bolt upright on a stiff culm instead of arching over and nodding under its own weight. It is a compact ribbed ear with a flared cap — explicitly the thing the reference rules out — rather than a loose branched panicle. And there is no water, no flooded ground and no clump of several separate tillers; it is one solid fountain from a single point on dry shadow. Identical chassis and identical head to Barley, Millet, Oats, Rye and Sorghum, recoloured green.
rows.fix: Bend the panicle over into a heavy nodding arch of loose branched grain and stand two or three separate tillers in a visible waterline.

rows.readsAs: a gold grass clump — indistinguishable from the Barley asset
rows.defect: Placed beside Barley this is the same picture: same fountain, same drooping outer blades, same short ribbed ear with a flared cap, same gold. The reference's whole point is that rye is taller and THINNER than wheat at aspect 0.22, yet the drawn silhouette is as wide as it is tall. The very long hair-fine awns are absent, the ear does not lean over at the tip, and the distinctly blue-green waxy bloom of rye foliage is nowhere — the leaves are the same gold as Barley's.
rows.fix: Redraw at a narrow upright proportion with a long slim ear leaning at the tip and hair-fine awns twice the ear's length, over blue-green waxy blades.

rows.readsAs: an olive ornamental grass with a rust-coloured screw
rows.defect: Sorghum's reference asks for a tall THICK corn-like jointed cane with broad arching blades and a pale midrib, crowned by a heavy compact head. What is drawn is the same fine-bladed fountain as the other five grasses with no cane visible at all, blades that are narrow and midrib-free, and a head that is the same small ribbed cylinder and flared cap — the opposite of heavy or crowning. Only the rust tint on the head distinguishes it from Millet.
rows.fix: Give it a stout visible jointed cane with broad white-midribbed arching blades and crown it with a fat dense red-brown grain head several times the current size.

rows.readsAs: a generic bean or pea vine floating on a diagonal
rows.defect: The leaves are plain flat circles — neither heart-shaped nor three-lobed, so the leaf must-read is missed outright. The runner does not hug the ground or spread wide; it hangs on a single 45-degree diagonal across the frame with the lower end stopping in mid-air, which reads as a fragment of a climbing vine rather than a trailing groundcover. The smooth spindle-shaped tubers are entirely absent, and the purple flush on stems and veins is absent too (the stems are plain green). Nothing in the picture says root crop.
rows.fix: Lay the runners horizontally along the ground, cut the leaves as heart-shaped or three-lobed blades on long purple-flushed stalks, and expose two or three smooth tapering orange tubers at the crown.

rows.readsAs: a clump of hosta or water-lily pads, or a green scallop shell / folding hand fan
rows.defect: All three must-reads are absent. The leaves are near-CIRCULAR paddles, not heart-shaped elephant ears, and every tip points sideways/upward around the fan arc — not one blade tip points down. There are no petioles anywhere: the seven blades emerge from a single buried point at the bottom centre with zero visible stalk, so the peltate 'stalk joins inside the blade, not at the notch' read cannot exist — there is no notch and no stalk to attach. No brown ringed corm, no fibrous hair, no purple flecking; the base of the plant is simply empty dark background. The whole thing is a flat overlapping shell of lens shapes with one straight centre-rib each, hugging the ground horizontally instead of standing up.
rows.fix: Rebuild it as 3-5 THICK UPRIGHT STALKS rising from a brown ringed corm sitting on the ground line, each stalk topped by a big heart-shaped blade hanging tip-DOWN with the stalk visibly inserted a third of the way into the blade face (peltate) rather than at the rim.

rows.readsAs: a golden ornamental fountain grass with a wood screw or a paintbrush ferrule stuck upright in the middle of it
rows.defect: The identity must-read — long stiff awn bristles fanning out from the ear — is absent. Zoomed in, the ear is a straight-sided ribbed COLUMN of tiny paired ticks that never break past the column's own width, capped by an inverted trapezoid flare; it reads unmistakably as a flat-head screw thread, not a grain ear. Nothing radiates. The second must-read also fails: instead of a single unbranched straw with a few widely spaced flat leaves, the plant is a dense tussock of roughly sixteen narrow arching blades all sprung from one point, with only one culm carrying a head — that is pampas/ornamental grass silhouette, not a wheat plant. No jointed culm, no leaf sheaths clasping it, no blue-green-to-gold ripening gradient.
rows.fix: Redraw the ear as a short plump spikelet body with 15-25 LONG straight awn bristles sweeping up and outward well beyond the ear's own width in a V-shaped spray, and cut the tussock down to one upright jointed straw carrying three or four widely spaced flat leaves.

rows.readsAs: a thin unsupported bean or morning-glory vine
rows.defect: No support at all — the must-read is a woody stem CLINGING to a pole/trunk with root pads, and the vine floats free with nothing to climb. Leaves are small narrow lance blades, not the broad ribbed heart-shaped leaves that are pepper's main tell. The fruit strings are two short colourless grey-white bead threads, not drooping green-to-red peppercorn catkins, and read as fungus or scale insects.
rows.fix: Draw a brown trunk/pole up the frame with the stem wrapped on it and visible root pads, swap the lance leaves for broad heart-shaped leaves with curved parallel ribs, and recolour the hanging spikes green-through-red.

rows.readsAs: an agave or dwarf fan palm
rows.defect: A flat radiating rosette of stiff spiked blades sitting on the ground — none of the three must-reads are present. There are no tall arching leafy canes and no clump of canes at all; there is no separate low flowering shoot snaking along the soil; and the pods are represented by one 12px dark grey speck lying on a leaf mid-rosette, which reads as a bug, not as pale green three-sided pods at the base.
rows.fix: Rebuild as 2-3 tall arching canes with two-ranked lance leaves, and run a distinct low shoot out along the soil to one side carrying a row of pale green ribbed pods.

rows.readsAs: a fern frond with a single daisy stuck on the tip
rows.defect: The white-rayed yellow-centred daisy does read, but the foliage is the identity and it is wrong: chunky oval leaflets in a rigid pinnate ladder instead of thread-fine feathery segments, so the plant reads as a fern. The flower centre is a flat yellow disc, not a hollow dome taller than it is wide, and the rays lie flat rather than folding back and down. One flower only, where chamomile is many-headed.
rows.fix: Replace the leaflet ladder with hair-fine three-times-divided threads and give the head a raised hollow cone with reflexed white rays, repeated on 3-5 branches.

rows.readsAs: a generic cartoon tree with pink blossoms
rows.defect: The lollipop chassis: solid orange rounded-rectangle trunk under a soft airbrushed green cloud. Not one of the three must-reads is present — the leaves are tiny featureless slivers with no visible veins let alone the three full-length ribs, there is no scarlet flush of young foliage (the four pink dots read as blossom clusters, not red leaves), and the trunk is a smooth solid lozenge with no cut, no peeling and no pale inner bark. Nothing in the frame says spice.
rows.fix: Draw a real trunk with a cut section peeled back to show curling pale inner bark, and put opposite leaves large enough to carry three drawn veins with a scarlet new-growth flush at the branch tips.

rows.readsAs: a generic tree infested with brown caterpillars
rows.defect: Same trunk-plus-cloud chassis as Cinnamon and Nutmeg. The crown is a wide round blob, not a narrow conical evergreen crown. The buds are the failure: four rust-brown bumpy vertical strings hanging INSIDE the crown that read as caterpillars or catkins, not as terminal sprays of pink-red nail-shaped buds at the branch tips. The leaves are scattered slivers with no opposite pairing visible.
rows.fix: Narrow the crown to a cone, pair the glossy lance leaves along visible branch tips, and put clusters of pink-red buds with a clear nail head and shaft at the ENDS of the outer branches against the sky.

rows.readsAs: a small pink daisy on a bare stalk
rows.defect: It is in the right neighbourhood but the coneflower has no cone: the centre is a flat dark disc a few pixels across, and the rays stick straight out sideways rather than sweeping back and down. The head is minuscule against a frame that is 80% bare green stem. The leaves are smooth narrow lances with no bristly rough texture and are the same rungs used on Mint and Oregano.
rows.fix: Triple the head size and give it a domed bristly orange-brown cone standing proud of the disc, with long pink-purple rays reflexed downward like a shuttlecock.

rows.readsAs: an agave or aloe with a wheat ear growing out of it
rows.defect: The identical fan rosette used for Cardamom, only larger and brighter. There is no clump of reedy canes and no two-ranked strap leaves — the blades radiate from one point like a palm. Worst, the rhizome, which IS the spice, is completely absent: the base is hidden where the blades meet the ground, with no knobbed fingered buff root exposed at all. The yellow bead spike on the bare stalk reads as a grass seedhead.
rows.fix: Stand the plant up as 3-4 slim reedy canes with strap leaves alternating left-right up each cane, and expose a fat knobbly pale-buff fingered rhizome breaking the soil at the base.

rows.readsAs: a young conifer or a hemp plant
rows.defect: The must-read is ONE stem topped by a SINGLE whorl of five-fingered leaves; the render stacks about ten palmate whorls the full height of the stem into a dense column, which destroys the diagnostic architecture entirely. The scarlet berry cluster sits on top of the column instead of nestled in the centre of the whorl, and the pale forked man-shaped root — the whole reason the species is famous — is nowhere in frame.
rows.fix: Strip it to one bare stalk with a single crown whorl of five-leaflet palmate leaves, berries in the middle of that whorl, and a pale forked man-shaped root exposed below the soil line.

rows.readsAs: lavender, or a bundle of dead twigs with purple tips
rows.defect: The violet spikes on long bare stalks do read, but the foliage is bleached straw-white and scattered up the whole length of the stems instead of silver-green and clustered low, so the bush looks dead rather than downy. The habit is a splayed open broom from a single trumpet base, not a tight rounded bush, and there is no woody mound at the bottom. It shares this exact chassis with Rosemary.
rows.fix: Recolour the leaves to silver-grey-green, mass them into a dense low mound at the base, and close the stem fan into a rounded dome so the flower stalks rise off a bush.

rows.readsAs: a willowherb or vetch weed with a lilac tip
rows.defect: Every leaf is a smooth narrow untoothed lance — mint's identity is a paired TOOTHED OVAL leaf and it is absent, so the plant reads as a different genus. The stem is a plain round green line with no square section and no flat faces, and the pairs sit flat in one plane rather than crossing at right angles at each node. Only the small lilac bead spike is right. The drawing is the Chamomile/Echinacea/Oregano ladder with a lilac tip.
rows.fix: Swap in broad oval leaves with clearly serrated edges in decussate pairs, and draw the stem as a square prism with a visible edge highlight down one face.

rows.readsAs: a bottlebrush cactus or a foxtail
rows.defect: A dense yellow-green column of stacked spiky whorls — the Ginseng chassis recoloured. The flowers are one 20px flat yellow smear on top with no four-petalled cross shape readable; the slender beaked seed pods held out below the flowers, which are the diagnostic feature, are entirely missing; and there are no big lyre-shaped lower leaves — every leaf on the plant is the same spike.
rows.fix: Open the plant into a thin branching stem with big lyre-lobed leaves at the bottom, a flat-topped head of four-petalled yellow crosses on top, and a zone of slim beaked pods angling outward just below the flowers.

rows.readsAs: an orange or apricot tree
rows.defect: The same trunk-lozenge-plus-cloud chassis as Cinnamon and Clove. The crown is a round blob, not a dense dark conical one. The fruits are four solid glowing yellow spheres — unsplit, with no crack, no scarlet lacy mace and no brown seed visible. The split fruit showing red mace over the nut IS nutmeg's identity and none of it is drawn, so the tree is indistinguishable from any yellow-fruited tree.
rows.fix: Split at least two fruits open into hinged halves and paint the scarlet net of mace wrapping a dark brown nut inside, and narrow the crown into a dark conical form.

rows.readsAs: a fern frond or a vetch with a scrap of white on top
rows.defect: The Chamomile ladder with denser olive leaflets. The leaves are long overlapping lance blades in a pinnate rank, not small oval leaves in opposite pairs, so the plant does not read as a mint-family herb at all. The stem is thin round and green with no square section and none of the reddish colour. The flowers are a single 20px white smudge at the tip instead of loose airy branched flat-topped sprays, and there is no sign of the dark purple bracts.
rows.fix: Rebuild as a branched reddish square stem carrying small paired oval leaves, topped by several airy flat-topped sprays of tiny white-pink florets sitting in dark purple bracts.

rows.readsAs: lavender in a blue colourway
rows.defect: This is the Lavender drawing with the leaf slivers turned green and the flower spikes turned pale blue — same splayed brown stem fan, same trumpet base, same scattered slivers, same beaded terminal spikes in the same positions. That terminal spike is the wrong flower architecture: rosemary carries small two-lipped flowers scattered ALONG the stems, not lavender wands at the tips. The needles are sparse and scattered rather than crowded in dense whorls up the woody stems, and none shows the white felted underside.
rows.fix: Delete the terminal spikes and scatter small pale blue two-lipped flowers in the leaf axils along the stems, then crowd short needles densely all the way up each stem with a white flash on the underside of the ones that twist over.

rows.readsAs: a cut bundle of willow or lavender wands
rows.defect: The identity must-read — the thick, pebbled, velvety grey-green leaf — is completely absent. The leaves are tiny flat green slivers stuck on thin brown wands, no wrinkle, no velvet, no width; leaf colour is olive-green, not the silvered grey the row demands. Stems are round brown twigs with no square woody base. The five wands are the family taper stem duplicated and fanned, and the pale violet apex spikes push the read straight to lavender.
rows.fix: Replace the sliver leaves with broad oblong grey-silver blades in opposite pairs, at least 6-8x their current area, carrying a visible pebbled/quilted vein grid and a pale velvety edge halo, on short square-sectioned woody stems.

rows.readsAs: a single tall weed stalk with one pink daisy on top
rows.defect: Every must-read fails. There is one ruler-straight vertical stem where thyme is a low spreading mounded subshrub — and the row even calls for aspect 1.6 (wider than tall), yet the render is a narrow vertical column. The leaves are large open chevrons, not tiny paired leaves, and there is no rolled-under edge. The harvest is drawn as a single stamped pink-purple daisy head rather than clusters of tiny lilac lipped flowers at many shoot tips. No wiry woody stems, no mound, no density.
rows.fix: Rebuild as a wide low mound of many short wiry woody stems radiating from a crown, each dotted with minute paired leaves, and cap several shoot tips with small lilac flower clusters instead of one daisy.

rows.readsAs: a squat rosette of jagged nettle or mint leaves
rows.defect: The leaf blades splay outward almost horizontally in a low flat rosette instead of rising as a tall upright fountain, so the plant's defining posture is inverted. The blades are saw-toothed with spiky jagged margins; turmeric leaves are smooth-edged entire lance blades on long sheathing stalks — the toothed edge alone sends the read to nettle or mint. The cone of pale green-and-pink bracts is absent, replaced by a thin bare wire carrying a small orange bead spike, and there is no knobby orange-fleshed rhizome anywhere.
rows.fix: Stand the blades up into a tall narrow vertical fan with smooth entire margins and a strong pale midrib, and set a fat overlapping cone of pale green bracts tipped pink low at the base with an orange rhizome knuckle at soil line.

rows.readsAs: a fern frond or a bottlebrush
rows.defect: The tall unbranched stem and the opposite pinnate ladder are present, but the flat-domed pale pink flower head — the crown identity and the harvest — is a tiny white pill barely wider than the stem, roughly a twentieth of the plant's width, with no dome, no florets and no pink. The leaflet ladder is so mechanically uniform (same blade, same pitch, top to bottom, no size gradient) that the silhouette reads as a single fern frond rather than a flowering herb, and it is the same asset as Yarrow in a different green.
rows.fix: Enlarge the terminal head to a wide flat-topped dome of many tiny pale pink-white florets, at least as wide as the foliage, and taper the leaflet ladder so the lower leaves are longer than the upper.

rows.readsAs: the same fern frond as Valerian, one shade greyer
rows.defect: This is Valerian's render with a hue shift — same stem, same shadow, same rung count and pitch, same white apex pill — so a stranger cannot tell the two apart, and neither yarrow must-read survives. The foliage is discrete little oval leaflets in a coarse ladder, not the feather-fine thrice-divided ferny fuzz that is yarrow's signature, and the flat dense PLATE of tiny white florets is reduced to a dot narrower than the leaf spread, when it should be the widest element in the silhouette. The stem is a smooth clean line with no stiff hairiness.
rows.fix: Replace the leaflet ladder with a fine feathery haze of hair-thin dissected segments and cap it with a broad flat white corymb plate spanning the full width of the plant.

rows.readsAs: a single broad green leaf blade, or a green wine glass on a stem
rows.defect: The reference calls for a hollow green sphere studded with many identical cells, daughter colonies visible inside, translucent jelly. The render is not a sphere and not a colony at all: it is the family's tapered spindle with the strands webbed into one solid opaque green membrane, flared to a straight square-cut top and pinched to a tiny green nub at the ground. There is no sphere, no cell studding, no daughter colonies, no translucency. It reads as a leaf, not a microbe.
rows.fix: Discard the seaweed spindle entirely for this one and draw a single large translucent circle whose rim is beaded with many small identical green cells, with two or three smaller beaded circles suspended inside it.

rows.readsAs: a husked ear of corn, or a closed mustard-yellow tulip bud
rows.defect: All three must-reads are missing. There is no claw holdfast and no rock — the whole plant narrows to a single point on bare ground. There is no distinct stiff stipe, because the stalk and the body are the same continuous taper. The blade is not wide or flapping; it is a narrow closed spindle no wider than Red Algae's. The colour is mustard-gold, not olive-brown to dark chocolate. The three flat ellipse blobs pasted on the midline belong to Sargassum's float description and are the wrong feature on the wrong asset.
rows.fix: Rebuild as three elements: a splayed root-like claw gripping a rock at the base, a clear narrow stipe above it, and a single wide dark-brown strap blade split into finger segments that is at least three times wider than the stipe.

rows.readsAs: a furled crimson umbrella or a bundle of red spaghetti stood on end
rows.defect: The colour is right — deep crimson with a purplish sheen. Everything structural is wrong. The identity must-read is fine, repeatedly forking branch structure, and there is not one fork anywhere in the image: the fronds are eight straight parallel rods running the full height without dividing once. The small disc holdfast is absent; the bundle converges to a bare point. The dark tips at the top read as burnt or clipped ends rather than frond apices.
rows.fix: Replace the parallel rods with a repeatedly dichotomous branch tree — each frond forking into two at least three times up the height — and seat it on a small flat crimson disc holdfast.

rows.readsAs: a furled golden umbrella; visually the same object as Kelp with the blobs removed
rows.defect: None of the three must-reads is present. There are no round pea-like gas floats on short stalks anywhere — ironically those blobs were drawn onto the Kelp asset instead. There are no toothed narrow leaf-like blades along the branches; there are no branches at all, only the same eight parallel unbranched rods. The mass is neither bushy nor tangled but tight, closed and symmetrical. Only the golden-olive colour is correct, and it is nearly the same value as Kelp's, so the two assets are not tellable apart.
rows.fix: Open the silhouette into a bushy tangle of forking branches and hang clusters of small round stalked berry floats plus narrow toothed blades along them, so the floats are the first thing the eye finds.

rows.readsAs: a generic cartoon bug / mascot beetle with one big googly eye — nobody says 'leafcutter'
rows.defect: The identity must-read is simply not drawn: there is NO leaf fragment carried overhead anywhere in the frame. The thorax is a plain smooth ovoid with zero backward-pointing spines. There is no pinched narrow waist — head and thorax overlap directly and the gaster hangs off a straight leg-thickness bar instead of a petiole node. The head has no mandibles or cutting jaws at all; instead it carries a single huge vertebrate-style eye with a white highlight, and the antennae sprout out of that eye socket as smooth backswept whiskers with a crook at the tip rather than as elbowed (geniculate) antennae with a long scape. Two of the six legs attach to the head and three to the gaster, so only one leaves the thorax; the gaster is a vertically striped beach-ball.
rows.fix: Rebuild it as an ant rig: put all six legs on the thorax with a visible femur/tibia elbow, cut a true pinched two-node petiole between thorax and gaster, add the backward-pointing propodeal spines on the thorax, replace the single mammal eye with a small compound eye plus a pair of forward cutting mandibles and elbowed antennae — and above all, add the semicircular green leaf fragment held overhead in those jaws, since that silhouette IS the species.

rows.readsAs: a small rust-coloured cartoon spider
rows.defect: None of the three must-reads are present. The body is two fat spheres with a deep waist between them, not a flat unsegmented teardrop wedge - the silhouette is round and tall where a tick is a low flat plate. There are no mouthparts of any kind: the front sphere is a bare ball with no capitulum, no palps and no barbed hypostome spear jutting ahead, so the single feature that IS the tick is absent. The legs are not bunched toward the front - they fan symmetrically fore and aft like a spider's, and they pass behind the spheres so they never visibly attach. A 2x2 cluster of four glossy black eyes is painted on the front ball although the reference calls for hidden eyes, and no deer tick has that. Rendered aspect is roughly 1.3, not the specified 2.2.
rows.fix: Redraw as a single low flat teardrop shield - one unsegmented body, wide at the rear and tapering forward, no waist, no eye dots - and put a short barbed spear (hypostome flanked by two stubby palps) projecting past the front point, with all eight legs crowded into the front third of the body.

rows.readsAs: a pale cream cartoon spider
rows.defect: It is the Deer Tick image recoloured with longer legs - same two spheres, same 2x2 eye dots in the same position on the front ball, same mottled blotching on the rear ball, same stick legs, same shadow. The defining pycnogonid trait is inverted: the body here is the largest, fattest part of the animal instead of being reduced to a thin stick between the legs, so nothing suggests that the gut and gonads have migrated into the limbs. There is no proboscis at all - no long tubular sucking tube at the front, just a bare rounded ball - and no small ocular turret carrying the four eyes; the eyes are flat dots painted on the sphere. The legs, while longer, are still the same two-segment sticks with no joints, no claws and no visible attachment to a segmented trunk.
rows.fix: Shrink the body to a narrow segmented rod barely wider than a leg, hang four pairs of very long jointed legs off visible lateral tubercles along that rod, and add a proboscis at least as long as the trunk projecting forward with a small four-eyed turret on top.

rows.readsAs: a numbat, or a striped short-legged cat
rows.defect: There is no armour anywhere. The bands are flat painted vertical stripes on a soft furry barrel with a fuzzy hair fringe along the topline and belly — no raised overlapping plate edges, no shadowed band gaps, no scapular or pelvic shield, no domed carapace breaking the topline. The topline is a smooth soft arc identical to a generic quadruped. The tail is a thin smooth up-curling cat tail with no rings or taper-plating, and the snout is only mildly pointed with a soft rounded ear rather than the long tube-snout and small tubular ears called for.
rows.fix: Rebuild the mid-back as hard geometry: a domed keratin carapace with a front and rear shield and 6-8 discrete banded plates between them, each band a crisp overlapping arc with a dark shadow line under its trailing edge, the band stack visibly stepping the topline; then run the same plating down the tail as tapering rings and lengthen the snout into a narrow tube.

rows.readsAs: a guinea pig or hamster taped under a dowel
rows.defect: The identity feature is entirely missing — the long hooked scythe claws. Both limbs terminate as blunt flat-topped rectangular straps that butt into the underside of the branch; nothing curls over or grips it, and there is no claw geometry of any kind. Only two limbs exist; the hind pair is absent. The limbs are featureless parallelogram slabs with no shoulder, elbow or wrist, so the body reads as an oval hung on two ribbons rather than a long-armed animal. The face is wrong too: a pointed rodent muzzle with a single bead eye on the side of the head instead of the small flat round forward-facing face with dark eye stripes and a faint smile. The fur is uniform pale cream with no greenish algal cast.
rows.fix: Replace the two straps with four long curved arms whose ends close into two or three big hooked scythe claws visibly wrapping over the top of the branch, and flatten the muzzle into a round forward-facing disc face with dark eye patches.

rows.readsAs: a cartoon mouse with paper wings; 'a bat', but nobody says flying fox
rows.defect: The fox face is not there. The skull is a smooth dome and the muzzle is a short blunt bump with a single dot nose - a mouse/teddy snout, not the long tapering dog muzzle that IS the flying-fox read, and the ears are little round mouse ears rather than the small neat naked ears set low on a long head. The clawed thumb at the wing bend is entirely absent: the leading edge runs unbroken to a bare point. The finger bones are only three straight hairlines fanning from the elbow that fade out before reaching the trailing edge, so the membrane reads as folded card stock, not a stretched hand.
rows.fix: Rebuild the head: pull the muzzle out to roughly a third of the head length as a tapering fox snout with a wet dark nose and a visible jaw line, shrink and lower the ears, and hook a distinct clawed thumb up off the top bend of each wing.

rows.readsAs: a Halloween sticker vampire bat - the trope, not the animal
rows.defect: The face has no face. Where the must-read flat pig-like nose pad should sit there is nothing at all: a featureless ball with two dots and no muzzle, so the short conical snout is missing too. What carries the read instead is exactly the thing the note forbids - two long white Dracula canines hanging clear of the jawline, where a real vampire bat shows small chisel incisors inside a stubby snub muzzle. The long thumbs are absent; the wrists are bare points, so the walking/wrist-propping anatomy that makes this species distinctive never appears. Only the tall pointed ears are correct, and they are the sole thing distinguishing this render from the Fruit Bat.

rows.readsAs: a shaggy tan blob with a spine halo - a porcupine or a hedgehog-boar, not a bear
rows.defect: The pelage is drawn as long straight bristles radiating outward past the body edge, so the silhouette reads as quills rather than fur. The body is a featureless ellipse with the highest point at MID-BACK, so the must-read shoulder hump over the forelegs is absent. The legs are two flat rectangular planks of uniform width that are pasted over the ellipse and simply stop, with no shoulder or haunch mass and no plantigrade paw - just a stub end with white claw dashes. No stub tail visible. Only the head (rounded ear, black nose, dished brow) reads as ursine.

rows.verifyWhy:
Upheld as FAIL, but THREE of the four stated causes are factually wrong and must not be fixed against. Corrections first, then the real defects.

WRONG #1 - 'the must-read shoulder hump is absent, the topline peaks at mid-back.' It does not. I traced the silhouette column-by-column: the animal spans x=96..350 in the 440px frame; the topline minimum-y (highest point) is y=130 at x=228-234, and the front leg plank occupies x=225-255. The crest is therefore DIRECTLY over the foreleg station, and it sits ~15px above the mid-back/rump line (y=143 at x=180, y=147-168 at x=120-160). The front of the animal is the tallest point. It is understated - it is the crest of a forward-tilted egg rather than a sculpted muscular mass, and there is a second, LOWER rounded nape blob between it and the skull (top y~136 at x~280) that can be mistaken for the shoulder - but 'hump absent' is false. The fix here is 'deepen/sculpt the existing hump', not 'add a missing one'.

WRONG #2 - 'two legs.' There are four. At each of the two leg stations a near plank and a far, darker-shaded plank are drawn side by side (rear station: dark plank x~131-150 plus light plank x~151-181; front station same arrangement). The near/far pairing is visible at 5x on both stations.

WRONG #3 - 'no plantigrade paw.' Every visible foot terminates in a flat horizontal elliptical ground-contact pad - a genuine plantigrade sole, not a hoof or a point - and each carries a row of four pale claws projecting forward off the toe end. That must-read is drawn. Its problem is execution, not absence: the claws are near-pure white against the mud palette so they read as a strip of teeth/pill beads, and the plank meets the pad at its midpoint instead of at a heel, so the foot looks like a disc pasted under a stick.

CORRECT in their claim: the pelage and the missing tail.

WHAT ACTUALLY FAILS:
1. LIMB MODEL. The four legs are untapered rectangles of constant width from body to ankle - no elbow, no hock, no knee, no shoulder mass, no thigh, no blend at the top (you can see the plank's straight top edge terminate under the belly ellipse). They are also far too thin and too long for a bear: the body is a fat egg standing on four stilts with a big belly-to-ground gap. A bear's limbs are massive columns continuous with the torso; these are the generic quadruped chassis and read closer to a table or a pony than a bear. Additionally the rear station sits ~40% of body length forward of the rump, so the entire hindquarters overhangs unsupported.
2. PELAGE / SILHOUETTE. The fur is a ring of long, straight, dark bristles set perpendicular to the body outline around the ENTIRE perimeter - standing straight up as a crest along the topline, fanning backward off the rump, hanging as a straight fringe under the belly. At up to ~20px on a 250px-long animal they are ~8% of body length. They do quill-ify the outline; the rump fan plus dorsal crest is exactly the porcupine cue. I would not go as far as 'reads as a porcupine' (the ursine head, rounded ears and clawed flat paws hold the read), but the silhouette is destroyed and the shoulder hump is buried inside the bristle halo, which is a large part of why the previous judge could not see it.
3. NO STUB TAIL. Confirmed at 5x on the rump - the rear of the ellipse is bare outline plus bristles, nothing protruding. Half of must-read #3 is simply not drawn.
4. HEAD IS NOT BROAD OR DISHED. The skull is a plain rounded blob and the muzzle is a smooth CONVEX cone with a small dark oval nose, reading mildly canid/foxy. There is a visible rectangular seam where the lighter muzzle patch is composited over the head. The ears are correct and should be left alone: small, low, rounded, with a near and a far ear both visible as overlapping arcs at the top-rear of the skull. The eye is small in absolute terms but is drawn with a full white sclera ring which reads cartoon rather than the small dark bear eye.

NET: it is recognisably a bear-ish quadruped, so the organism read is not lost the way the previous judge described, but the limbs are a bare chassis with no anatomy, the pelage breaks the outline, the stub tail is absent and the dished face is absent. FAIL stands.

rows.readsAs: a grey Herdwick sheep or a hornless ram
rows.defect: The sheep chassis: level topline, woolly barrel, four stilt legs off the corners, hoof-like nubs for feet. Every must-read misses. The facial profile is not straight - the muzzle is a heavy dark snout that turns down and curls forward like a ram's nose, and it is charcoal, not tan. The rump is NOT higher than the shoulders; the topline is flat and the front is the taller end because of the head mass, which is the brown-bear silhouette the note explicitly warns against. There are no ears at all on the head - the round pale shape by the eye is a face patch, not a tall rounded ear. No claws; the feet are dark cloven nubs.
rows.fix: Rebuild on a bear body - drop the barrel onto plantigrade feet with visible toes and claws, arch the topline so the hindquarters are the high point, and give it a straight tan-muzzled face with two tall rounded ears standing clear of the skull.
rows.verifyWhy:
UPHELD, but three of the four stated causes are wrong or imprecise and would send a fix at the wrong targets. I read the PNG at 1x and then re-cropped/upscaled the head (5x and 8x), the muzzle, both foot groups and the rump, and measured the silhouette's top edge per column programmatically.

WHAT IT ACTUALLY READS AS: a grey woolly Herdwick/Swaledale-type sheep or ram. Deep barrel trunk covered edge-to-edge in fine directional flecked FLEECE texture, four long slim straight evenly-tapering columnar legs with no haunch and no forearm bulk, a dark charcoal head carried high on a short neck, dark hoof-like foot tips. Cross-check: Brown_Bear.png in the same family is the IDENTICAL chassis recoloured tan — same barrel, same fleece flecking, same two dark face ovals, same down-curled snout, same hoof feet. The bear family is one sheep chassis in N colours; fixing this asset means replacing the chassis, not retouching features.

CORRECTIONS TO THE ORIGINAL CLAIM:

1. 'The rump is NOT higher than the shoulders (topline is flat, front is taller)' — HALF WRONG. Measured on the alpha silhouette (canvas 440x440, body bbox x=92..346, head on the RIGHT so rump is on the LEFT): trunk topline min-y is 167 at x=148-156 (hindquarter) versus 170-172 at x=196-220 (withers/shoulder). So the rump IS technically the highest point of the trunk — by 4 px on a 255-px-long animal, under 2%. The must-read still fails, but because the differential is IMPERCEPTIBLE, not because it is inverted. 'Front is taller' is false for the trunk (the trunk's front is 3-5 px LOWER); what makes the front look taller is the HEAD dome at y=115, carried well above the whole back. Fix = exaggerate the hindquarter rise into a visible arch over the pelvis and drop the head below the shoulder line, not flip the topline.

2. 'There are no ears at all on the head — the pale round shape is a face patch' — WRONG ON BOTH HALVES. (a) The pale round shape is the EYE: at approx x=272 y=157 there is a small cream/tan sclera ring with a black pupil and a white catchlight. It is not a patch. (b) Ears ARE drawn: two dark charcoal rounded ovals sit side by side on the upper face, roughly x=248-268 and x=278-292, y=128-155, the rear one larger and crescent-notched. They fail for two other reasons — they are charcoal-on-charcoal (near-zero luminance separation from the skull, invisible below ~8x zoom), and they sit entirely INSIDE the head mass so the skull silhouette carries zero ear protrusion. At full size they read as a lemur/panda eye-patch pair. The must-read 'tall rounded ears' fails, but the fix is contrast + breaking the ears out above the skull outline, not adding ears from nothing. There is also a lighter grey angular flap notched into the back-left of the skull (approx x=228-245, y=125-175) that reads as a cheek/jaw plate; it is not a readable ear either.

3. 'Feet are cloven nubs with no claws' — HALF WRONG. Each foot does end in a near-black rounded pad, but there IS a claw element: a single pale cream horizontal RECTANGULAR bar projects forward from the toe of the front-most foot of each pair (visible on both the fore and hind groups). It is one flat straight dash, not 'short curved claws' plural, and at full size it reads as a hoof toe-cap highlight rather than claws. The 'cloven' impression comes from two overlapping dark lobes per foot group, which are actually the near-leg and far-leg feet, not a split hoof. The real defect is that the foot is a small rounded hoof-scale terminal with no flat plantigrade sole and no separated digits.

4. 'Facial profile is a down-curled charcoal ram snout rather than straight with a tan muzzle' — CORRECT, and confirmed at 8x. From the brow the profile bulges convex over the nasals then curls downward to a large dark ellipse nose with a highlight; a classic Roman/ram nose. There is no tan muzzle anywhere: the muzzle is mid-grey in the same charcoal family as the skull, with only the faintest warm tint. A thin straight dark line runs from the nose corner back across the cheek as the mouth, reading as a stitched-on stroke rather than a jawline.

DEFECTS THE ORIGINAL JUDGE DID NOT NAME: (a) COLOUR — this is a BLACK bear rendered in pale-to-mid GREY; nothing on the animal is black except the foot tips, and the fleece flecking actively fights the idea of a bear's flat dense black coat. (b) The tail is a flat dark-grey angular wedge pasted on the rear of the rump (approx x=92-125, y=195-265) that reads as a rump shadow patch or a docked sheep tail, not a bear's stub. (c) Limb geometry is ungulate throughout — straight columns, no elbow/hock articulation, no bear's low-slung heavy-boned stance.

BAND: FAIL upheld. All three must-reads fail (no straight profile and no tan muzzle; rump-over-shoulder differential is 4 px and unreadable; ears carry neither contrast nor silhouette and the claw is a single flat bar). The organism itself reads as the wrong species, which is a FAIL condition independent of the must-read tally.

rows.readsAs: a tan-fleeced ram - the curled muzzle even reads as a horn
rows.defect: Identical sheep chassis, recoloured tan. There is no shoulder hump whatsoever - the topline runs flat and the withers are the same height as the rump, so the diagnostic that the note calls out as THE identity is absent. The face is not dished or broad-browed; it is a dark mask with a heavy blunt snout that rolls forward into a spiral that a stranger reads as the base of a ram's horn. No long pale digging claws - the feet are two tiny dark hoof nubs. The legs are smooth pipes with no elbow, wrist or digits.
rows.fix: Build the muscular hump as an actual mass of shoulder over the forelegs so it is the tallest point of the silhouette, and terminate the forelegs in a broad flat paw with a fan of long pale claws.
rows.verifyWhy: FAIL upheld, but three of the four stated causes are wrong in detail and must not be fixed as described. Measured silhouette (bg-diff bbox on the 440px PNG): body+head x86-353, y97-328, so w268 x h232, aspect 1.16 against a spec aspect of 1.5. The head occupies x222-353 = 131px of 268 total length (~49%) against headFrac 0.27, and its crown sits at y97 while the back sits at y179 — the head is carried a full 82px ABOVE the topline on an upright neck. That alert, high-carried, oversized head on slim columnar legs is the single biggest reason the asset reads ovine/caprine rather than ursine; no bear carries its skull above its back line. CORRECTION 1 — the shoulder hump is NOT 'completely absent' and the back is NOT 'a flat line with withers level with the rump'. Per-column topline: rump crest y179-180 across x134-158, a shallow saddle y181-183 at x162-186, then a continuous rise to y163-155 at x210-218 (verified in a 6x crop of x150-260,y130-260 — that rise is pale fleece, not head overlap). So the withers ARE the tallest point of the trunk, by roughly 16-24px (~12% of the 173px trunk height). The real defect is that the rise is a gentle unbroken ramp that merges straight into the neck instead of a discrete rounded mass sitting OVER the forelegs, and it is visually annihilated by the head towering 80px above it. Fix = make it a distinct convex boss above the foreleg with a clear dip behind it, and drop the head onto the shoulder line; do not 'add a hump to a flat back' — a rise already exists. CORRECTION 2 — there is NO 'dark mask' and nothing 'spirals'. At 9x (x225-315, y90-170) the two dark shapes on the skull resolve as the TWO EARS: the near one is a raised rounded tan pinna with a dark inset oval, the far one is a second dark oval without the pale rim. They are correctly rounded and bear-like in shape, but they are drawn flush on the skull surface (they never break the silhouette) and are placed far too low and far too forward — the near ear sits immediately behind and above the eye, exactly where a ram's horn boss would be, which is what produced the judge's 'horn base' misread. The face itself is a uniform sand/tan with no mask whatsoever. The judge IS right that the profile is not dished: from brow to nose the outline runs straight-to-slightly-convex over a long blunt rounded muzzle ending in a large dark-brown nose with nostril dots and a thin mouth line — a generic carnivore snout, not the concave brow-to-nose dish with a broad flat forehead the note demands. The skull also narrows toward the crown rather than being broad-browed. CORRECTION 3 — pale claws are PRESENT, not absent, but vestigial. Each foot terminates in a dark chocolate-brown rounded paw ellipse (the near forefoot shows two overlapping dark lobes = two toes) carrying exactly ONE small white dash on its leading edge, roughly 8x3 source pixels, visible only at 12x. That is a single blunt pale nub, not the 'long straight pale digging claws' the mustRead requires, and at any shipped size it disappears. The feet are also not literal hooves as claimed — they are dark rounded paw lobes — but they are small, dark and set on straight untapered cylindrical legs with no visible wrist, hock or flat forward-projecting plantigrade sole, so they still read as hoof nubs, and the dark-on-pale contrast makes them read as cloven at distance. Also noted: no tail stub at all (the rump at 9x is a clean unbroken curve), and the coat is rendered as long streaky lifted hair over a pale cream ground, which reads as fleece rather than dense brown bear pelage. Verdict: of the three mustReads, the dished broad-browed face is genuinely absent, the pale digging claws are present only as an unreadable 8px tick, and the hump exists but is not prominent and does not read; combined with a 49%-of-body head held above the topline and a fleece-textured pale coat, the organism reads as a woolly hoofed animal, not a brown bear.

rows.readsAs: a brown Herdwick sheep, indistinguishable from the Brown Bear asset except for a slightly warmer fleece
rows.defect: Same chassis again. The shoulder hump is missing - the back is a flat horizontal line, so the silhouette does not sit higher at the front and fails the note's own black-bear-opposite test. The facial profile is convex-and-curled, not dished concave. The 'long pale front claws' are two or three white hatch ticks at the hoof nubs, invisible at any normal viewing size. The grizzled fur is a flat tan wash with hair strokes, no silver-tipped guard-hair contrast. Read side by side with Brown Bear it is the same drawing.
rows.fix: Give it a distinct silhouette from Brown Bear by exaggerating the shoulder hump into a pronounced mound and adding real splayed front claws, plus pale-tipped guard hairs over a darker undercoat for the grizzle.
rows.verifyWhy:
UPHELD, but two of the four stated causes are factually wrong and must not be fixed as written.

WHAT I SAW (440x440, subject bbox x82-357 y103-323, 276x221 px, rendered aspect 1.25 against a declared 1.8). The organism reads as a fleeced sheep/ram, not a bear. A barrel fleece body with a hard fleece-edge boundary running from the brisket around the flank; a separate head/neck block dropped on top of the shoulder; four slender straight columnar legs of near-equal length front and rear, each ending in a dark oval toe cap that reads as a cloven hoof tip; and NO TAIL AT ALL at the rump (I zoomed the rump at 7x - the hindquarter is a plain fleece curve plus a flat tan haunch plate, no stub, no nub).

SAME-CHASSIS CLAIM: CONFIRMED, and stronger than stated. Cropping the Grizzly head (x235-365) and the Brown Bear head (x220-360) at 5x and putting them side by side, they are the SAME construction part-for-part: identical low crescent saucer flap over the crown with the same small notch bitten out of its lower-rear edge, identical large dark round disc behind the eye, identical dark eye-patch oval with the same small ringed eye at its lower-front, identical stub muzzle with the same kidney-shaped dark nose, identical single thin mouth line. Toplines match too (Grizzly mid-back y=186 -> shoulder y=160; Brown Bear mid-back y=180 -> shoulder y=154). It is one drawing with a coat recolour.

CORRECTION 1 - "No shoulder hump (flat horizontal back)" is WRONG as described. The back is not flat. Column-scanning the top edge: rump y=227 at x=82, rising to y=184-186 across the mid-back x=127-202, then rising again to y=160-164 at x=232-242 where the neck takes over. That is a real ~25px rise, and the front IS the tallest part of the body. The defect is different: it is a smooth gradual RAMP into the neck, not a discrete muscular bulge sitting over the forelegs, and - decisively - it is the identical ramp the Black Bear has (mid-back y=168 -> shoulder y=158) and the Brown Bear has. So the note's black-bear-opposite test does fail, but because all three bears share one topline, not because this one is flat. Fixing a "flat back" would produce no change; what is needed is a distinct convex withers mass whose apex sits AHEAD of the mid-back and clears the neck line, plus a genuinely rump-high Black Bear to contrast against.

CORRECTION 2 - "Fur is a flat wash with no grizzled guard-hair contrast" is WRONG. At 3x the coat is a dense directional hatch of pale blond/cream strokes over a mid-tan ground, with clearly readable light-tip contrast across the whole barrel; it is in fact the MOST grizzled coat of the three brown-bear-type assets, and paler than the Brown Bear's rather than "marginally warmer". The grizzled-fur half of must-read #3 is satisfied. Do not spend a fix pass adding hatch that is already there - the problem is that the hatch is applied to a fleece shape.

CORRECTION 3 - claw count. Not "two white hatch ticks". At 12x each foot carries a row of about five near-white ticks that do overhang the front edge of the dark toe cap, so pale claws are present in principle. They fail on scale and placement: the whole row is roughly 10x3 px on a 276px-long animal (~3.5% of body length, versus a real grizzly's claws at ~10-12% of forefoot length and highly conspicuous), they sit on top of the toe cap rather than emerging from a toe pad, and the identical row is repeated on BOTH HIND FEET, which contradicts the must-read's "front claws" and erases the front/hind claw asymmetry that is a grizzly signature.

MUST-READ VERDICT: (1) muscular hump over the shoulders - NOT READABLE as a hump (present only as an undifferentiated neck ramp shared with the black bear). (2) dished concave facial profile - ABSENT, and the judge is right here: the head zoom shows a domed forehead stepping down onto a muzzle whose upper edge bulges CONVEXLY out to the nose, a ram/roman profile; a dished face requires the nasal bridge to fall below the brow-to-nosetip chord and it plainly does not. (3) long pale front claws AND grizzled fur - split: grizzled fur PASSES, long pale front claws FAIL on size and are wrongly duplicated on the hind feet.

Also worth logging for the fix (not a listed must-read, so not the basis of the verdict): the ear is a large flat crescent flap lying against the crown plus a dark disc, breaking no part of the silhouette. A bear's ear must be small, round and stand PROUD of the skull outline. The limbs are the same slender ungulate columns used across the family and need the short, heavy, bent plantigrade bear limb with a flat foot on the ground.

Two of three must-reads absent or unreadable, the head is a ram's head, the feet are hooves, there is no tail, and the drawing is byte-for-byte the Brown Bear chassis. FAIL stands.

rows.readsAs: a black-and-white sheep - a Jacob or badger-faced ewe wearing a dark blanket
rows.defect: The head is the only part that reads panda: a white round skull with two dark eye patches. Everything below it is the family sheep. The black is in the WRONG places - a dark saddle sits across the shoulder and mid-torso and a second dark wedge sits on the rear flank, while all four legs are WHITE spindly pipes. The must-read black shoulder band joining black forelegs is therefore absent and actively contradicted. The body is not round and bulky, it is a flat-topped barrel on stilts. The eye patches are perfect circles, not teardrops, and no black round ears are visible - the ear reads as a pale notch in the skull outline. Feet are dark hoof nubs.
