rows.verifyWhy:
FAIL stands, but the stated causes are substantially wrong and must not be fixed as written. I decoded the PNG (440x440) and sampled pixels, then re-rendered a tint map classifying every dark-marking pixel red.

CORRECTION 1 (the judge's central claim, and it is FALSE): 'ALL FOUR LEGS ARE WHITE' is wrong. All four legs are filled with the SAME black ink as the eye patches and the shoulder mass -- RGB(21,24,30) sampled at hind leg (115,265) and foreleg (~230,270), identical to eye patch (266,155) and torso patch (230,215). The problem is contrast, not placement: the card background is RGB(6,9,15)-(9,14,20), so the 'black' is only ~15/15/13 above background. Against the dark card the black limbs disappear and only their pale hairline outlines and the mid-grey paw pads survive, which is exactly what produces the 'white stilts / Jacob sheep' illusion. The must-read 'black shoulder band joining black forelegs' IS drawn and IS topologically continuous (the chest mass flows straight into the near foreleg) -- it simply does not READ at delivered tone. Fix is tonal (lift the black ink so it separates from the card, or give limbs a real rim), not a re-placement of black onto white legs.

CORRECTION 2: 'a dark saddle over the shoulder/torso plus a rear-flank wedge' mis-describes the layout. There is NO rear-flank wedge and NO saddle -- the entire hindquarter and rump are white (sampled 242,243,242 at (110,175)), and the topline over the withers is white too. The actual marking is ONE black chest/shoulder mass spanning roughly x 222-290, y 178-265, plus four black legs. Two real defects there: (a) the band stops well below the topline instead of crossing the back over the withers -- at x=220 the back edge is y~154 but black does not begin until y~217; (b) the white torso's front edge is a RULER-STRAIGHT VERTICAL SEAM at x~224 from y~190 to y~250, a hard geometric artifact, not an organic band edge.

CORRECTION 3: 'no black round ears are visible' is half wrong. TWO round ears ARE drawn -- a mid-grey disc RGB(127,126,127) at approx x 250-268, y 138-165 and a light-grey disc RGB(206,203,204) at approx x 266-292 with a mauve inner pinna RGB(131,113,111). They are the wrong COLOUR (grey, not black) and in the wrong PLACE (sitting low on the forehead, overlapping the top edges of both eye patches, never breaking the head's silhouette). Fix = recolour to black and move to the crown so they notch the outline.

CONFIRMED from the judge: eye patches are flat perfect CIRCLES (~30px diameter), not teardrops. Worse than they said -- the single eye (tiny gold ring + pupil, ~(288,152)) sits BETWEEN the two patches on bare white face, inside neither. Also confirmed the leggy stance: torso is ~136x102px (reasonably deep and barrel-like, so 'not round and bulky' is overstated -- the head is in fact a near-perfect round white disc and reads very well), but the legs run ~50px, half the torso height, thin, straight and splayed with the pairs crossing, so the proportion is ovine/pony, not the panda's low stumpy stance. Topline is genuinely flat from x~150 to x~225.

NOT MENTIONED BY THE JUDGE, both in the asset's favour: the packet note's tail IS satisfied -- a small pale wedge tail nub sits at the lower rear of the rump around (95-110, 205-225). And the paws are NOT hooves: at 10x each paw is a mid-grey oval pad with a row of four to five tiny pale CLAWS at the leading tip. The grey pads still hurt (they read as shoes against black legs; panda paws should be black), but do not attribute a hoof.

BAND: FAIL held because at delivered tone the identity collapses -- the black limbs vanish, leaving a white barrel with a detached black shoulder wedge and a panda-ish head, which is the wrong organism at a glance. Ordered fixes: (1) lift the black ink off the card background; (2) carry the band OVER the withers and kill the vertical seam at x~224; (3) eye patches to slanted teardrops with the eye INSIDE each; (4) ears black, on the crown, off the eye patches; (5) legs ~35% shorter, thicker, un-splayed, black paws.

rows.readsAs: a white sheep or a shorn lamb
rows.defect: Same chassis in white. There is no long neck at all - the head is welded directly to the front of the barrel exactly as on every other member of this family, so the single feature that is supposed to separate it from a brown bear is missing. The head is not small and narrow; it is the same big round dark-masked skull, and the muzzle is the same forward-curling blunt snout rather than a straight Roman nose. The must-read HUGE furred paws are the family's tiny dark hoof nubs - the smallest feet in the batch relative to the body, the exact opposite of the reference. The forelegs read as slack white pipes.

rows.verifyWhy:
UPHELD. I looked at the 440x440 PNG whole, then at 5x crops of the head and the feet, then rendered Polar_Bear beside Bear, Black_Bear and Sloth_Bear. The organism reads as a white sheep/lamb. All three stated must-reads fail, and the third one (which the original judge did not mention) fails too.

CHASSIS: Polar Bear, Black Bear and Sloth Bear are pixel-for-pixel the SAME body with only hue changed - same barrel with a dead-flat topline, same four thin straight tubular legs, same two-toe grey hoof nubs, same big round masked skull welded to the front of the barrel with a hooked snout and an oversized round nose. Correction to the claim: it is NOT 'every sibling' - Bear (#1) is a different and older chassis (a fluffy oval blob on four column legs with plantigrade white-toed pads), so the sheep chassis is at least the Black/Sloth/Polar cluster, not the whole family. That distinction matters for the fix: the sheep chassis is what has to be replaced, and #1 is not the model to copy either.

MUST-READ 1, 'long neck with a small narrow Roman-nosed head' - FAILS. The head is huge, not small: it spans roughly 120px of a ~303px body, headFrac ~0.40 against a spec of 0.21, nearly double. Its shape is a round dome cranium with a short bulbous muzzle that hooks DOWNWARD to a big round black nose - a ram/sheep curl, the opposite of the long narrow tapering Roman-nosed polar bear skull. Partial correction on the neck: there IS a short angled neck wedge visible behind the jaw and the head does sit raised above and forward of the topline, so it is not literally welded flush - but it is a thick stubby junction, nothing that reads as the long low-slung polar bear neck, so the judge's verdict on this point stands even though 'no neck at all' overstates it. On the mask: the same face-panel geometry as Black/Sloth is there, but because it is white-on-white it survives only as a faint grey seam running from behind the eye down the cheek to the jaw plus a slightly raised crown panel - a fix must not assume a visible dark mask to delete, it is a shape seam.

MUST-READ 2, 'huge furred paws' - FAILS, and this is the loudest defect. These are the smallest feet in the batch. Correction of detail: they are not single 'dark hoof nubs'. Each leg ends in a pale wedge with a grey sole PLUS a separate grey nub set behind it - a two-toe CLOVEN hoof pair, identical to the feet on Black Bear and Sloth Bear. Reading them as cloven is what pushes the whole silhouette over into 'sheep'. Nothing furred, nothing broad, no toes, no claws.

MUST-READ 3, 'sloping shoulders on a long body' - ALSO FAILS (unreported by the first judge). The topline is flat from rump to shoulder with no forward slope, and the whole animal measures roughly 1.5 long-to-tall against the spec aspect of 1.9, so the body is short and boxy rather than long.

TWO further defects not in the original claim: (a) a rigid grey/white ROD protrudes forward out of the mouth past the muzzle tip, reading as a straw or thermometer clenched in the teeth - a lip/mouth element drawn as a hard bar; it is present on Black Bear and Sloth Bear too, so it is a chassis bug not a one-off. (b) The eye area holds a plain grey dot next to a speckled brown/dark smear, so the face carries what looks like a second broken eye. (c) At the rump there is a detached grey rectangular slab where the stub tail should be.

Nothing here rescues the asset: the head, the feet and the proportions are all wrong in the same direction, and the direction is 'sheep'.

rows.readsAs: a scruffy grey sheep with a matted belly fleece
rows.defect: The long hanging belly hair is the one thing that lands, but it hangs from the sheep barrel and reads as an unshorn fleece rather than a shaggy coat, and there is no shoulder mane - the neck and withers are the smoothest part of the animal. The pale U or Y-shaped chest blaze is entirely absent; the chest is uniform grey. The muzzle is the family's short dark down-curled snout, not the long pale grey mobile snout the note says is unlike any other bear's. No huge curved claws - the feet are dark hoof nubs with a white tick. Nothing distinguishes it from the Spectacled Bear asset except hue.
rows.fix: Give it the long pale prehensile snout projecting well past the skull, paint a bold cream U across the chest, and add oversized ivory sickle claws on the front feet.
rows.verifyWhy:
UPHELD as FAIL, but two of the stated causes are wrong and the real defects are worse than described.

WHAT I SAW (440x440, zoomed 5-8x on head, withers, chest, feet). The organism reads as a grey woolly SHEEP or RAM, not a bear: a rounded barrel torso covered edge-to-edge in pale grey-beige fleece strokes, a smooth rim-lit topline, four slim pale legs, and a small dark face carried at the front on a short neck. Silhouette, proportion and coat all say ovine.

COAT COLOUR (defect the original claim did not name at all): the must-read calls for a shaggy unkempt BLACK coat. The coat here is pale grey-beige/oatmeal over the whole body, lighter than the head. It is genuinely shaggy - long directional fur strokes plus sparse thin hair spikes that cross the topline and a fringe of hanging hairs under the belly and between the legs - so 'unshorn belly fleece' is a fair description, but the value is inverted from the reference. A pale fleece is the single largest contributor to the sheep read.

SHOULDER MANE - claim CORRECT in substance, slightly wrong in detail. There is no mane. At the withers the topline is a smooth continuous arc finished with a bright white rim-light stroke. It is not literally 'the smoothest area': a handful of thin hair spikes do protrude above the topline there, but at exactly the same sparse density as along the mid-back, so nothing reads as a raised shoulder mass. The highest point of the back is mid-body, not the withers.

CHEST BLAZE - claim CORRECT, with one correction. There is no pale U or Y. The chest and throat are the same pale fleece as the rest of the body. The chest is NOT quite 'uniform grey' however: there is a distinct DARKER grey angular wedge over the shoulder/upper foreleg (and a matching one on the rump). That wedge is the family's shared limb-attachment plate, not a marking - it is darker than the coat, so it cannot be mistaken for the blaze, and it actively occupies the place the blaze should be.

MUZZLE - claim WRONG as stated. It is not 'the family's short dark down-curled snout'. The head narrows into a clearly projecting broad muzzle roughly a third of the head's length, aimed forward and only very slightly downward, ending in a large dark rounded nose pad, with a thin straight mouth line running back from it. So it is neither short nor curled. It still fails the must-read on two counts: it is the SAME mid grey-brown as the rest of the head rather than pale/contrasting, and it is a blunt heavy wedge-and-blob rather than the long slender flexible protrusible tube the note calls for. Fix the muzzle's colour and taper, not its length.

HEAD MARKINGS: the dark face carries a thick dark crescent/arc low on the rear of the skull plus a separate dark oval above and behind the small ringed eye. Read together the crescent reads as a curled ram horn, which reinforces the sheep identity rather than any bear cue.

CLAWS - claim CORRECT and understated. Each foot terminates in TWO dark rounded ovals that read unmistakably as a cloven hoof, with a single tiny straight white horizontal dash at the front toe as the only claw. There is no plantigrade paw, no paw pad, and nothing curved or long. The hooves are a second major driver of the wrong-organism read.

FAMILY CONTEXT: I rendered Sun Bear at the same crop for comparison. It is the identical chassis - same barrel, same shoulder/rump plates, same slim legs, same two-oval hoof with the white dash, same skull and muzzle - differing only in fur texture density and head-marking placement. This asset is not an individually weak bear; it is one shared ovine chassis recoloured, and no per-species retouch of markings will rescue it. All three must-reads (black shaggy coat with shoulder mane / pale U-Y chest blaze / long pale mobile snout with huge curved claws) are absent or inverted.

rows.readsAs: a straw-coloured Herdwick sheep with a dark face
rows.defect: Sheep chassis with a dark head mask. The coat is not shaggy blackish - it is a pale straw-grey fleece, lighter than the head, so the value relationship is inverted from the reference. The pale eye ring does exist but it is the same generic round eye patch that appears on Black Bear, Brown Bear and Grizzly Bear, so it does not read as a species marking. The face is not short and rounded with a heavy muzzle; it is the family's forward-curling ram snout. Feet are hoof nubs, legs are jointless pipes, no tail.
rows.fix: Darken the coat to blackish-brown so the cream spectacles and chest drip read as the lightest values on the animal, and shorten the muzzle into a heavy blunt block instead of the curled snout.
rows.verifyWhy:
UPHELD, and the asset is worse than the claim states. I read the full 440px PNG, then 5x-8x nearest-neighbour crops of the head, the feet and the whole body, then built a 6-up comparison strip of Black/Brown/Grizzly/Sun/Sloth/Spectacled.

WHAT I SAW. Body: a barrel-shaped fleece torso in pale straw-putty (#b9ac9c-ish) covered in fine vertical hair striations with long loose wisps hanging off the belly line and standing up along the topline. High withers, level short back, tucked-up rear flank, slender straight legs of even thickness. Head is a darker warm grey-brown (#6f6055-ish) mounted high on a short neck, turned three-quarters toward the viewer, with a long wedge muzzle that tapers forward and DOWN to a rounded dark nose pad at the tip and a thin curving mouth line running back from it. Darker patches also sit on the shoulder and the hip. Total read: a Herdwick/Swaledale sheep. The claim's headline is right.

THE DEFECT THE JUDGE MISSED, AND IT IS THE BIGGEST ONE. The feet are CLOVEN HOOVES. At 4x the front and hind feet are glossy dark two-toed hooves with a visible split down the middle and a tiny pale keratin sliver at the front edge, sitting on slender ungulate pasterns. There is no plantigrade paw anywhere on this animal - no broad flat sole, no furred toe pads, no claws. A bear that stands on hooves cannot be repaired by recolouring; the foot has to be rebuilt. Every one of the nine bears in this batch has the same hoof.

CORRECTIONS TO THE CLAIM.
(a) 'Coat is pale straw-grey, LIGHTER than the head' - CONFIRMED exactly. The body is markedly paler than the skull, which is the inverse of the required blackish coat with (at most) a pale face marking. But the claim implies shagginess is absent; it is not. The coat DOES carry long hanging shag strands off the belly and the flank. The shagginess is present and is the one must-read fragment that survives - it just reads as a fleece rather than bear fur because of the pale straw value and the sheep silhouette carrying it. The fix is the VALUE and the body form, not the addition of texture.
(b) 'The pale eye ring is the same generic patch that also appears on Black, Brown and Grizzly Bear' - RIGHT THAT IT IS GENERIC, WRONG ABOUT WHAT IT IS. What is actually shared across all six heads is a pair of DARK ovals sitting side by side across the brow/eye zone - goggles that are DARKER than the surrounding face, not pale. The only pale element on the head is a ~2px cream sclera outline around the single visible eyeball, which is the family-wide eye glyph and appears identically on Black, Brown, Grizzly, Sun and Sloth. So the required marking is not merely non-diagnostic here, its POLARITY IS INVERTED: the packet asks for pale cream rings on a blackish face, and the art delivers dark blobs on a mid-tone face. A fix that recolours the existing eye ring will not work; the face must be made dark and the cream spectacles drawn on top of it.
(c) 'Face is the shared forward-curling ram snout, not a short rounded face with a heavy muzzle' - CONFIRMED, and it is pixel-identical in shape across all six bears I strip-compared. No short rounded face, no heavy bear muzzle.

EARS (small feature, checked deliberately): there IS an ear - a small notched triangular flap at the rear-upper edge of the skull, plus a paler angular flap just forward of it. Present but non-diagnostic; not a reason to soften the band.

FAMILY CHASSIS FINDING. The 6-up strip is unambiguous: Black, Brown, Grizzly, Sun, Sloth and Spectacled Bear are ONE SHEEP BODY recoloured. Identical fleece torso outline, identical high-withers topline, identical slender legs, identical cloven hooves, identical darker skull with paired dark eye-ovals and the same forward-tapering ram muzzle. Brown and Grizzly are the same asset in two golden-tan tints. Spectacled Bear is that sheep in straw-grey. Zero of the three must-reads (pale cream eye rings / shaggy BLACKISH coat / short rounded face with heavy muzzle) are readable, and the organism itself is the wrong order - an ungulate, not a carnivoran. FAIL stands.

rows.readsAs: a grey sheep - and one of the LARGEST-looking animals in a batch where it should read smallest
rows.defect: Same chassis, mid-grey. The golden-cream crescent chest patch - the single feature the species is named for - is completely absent; the chest is plain grey. The coat is neither short, sleek nor jet-black; it is the family's pale shaggy fleece with hair strokes. The muzzle is the shared down-curled ram snout, not a blunt short face. The very long curved climbing claws are two white hatch ticks on hoof nubs. Nothing about it reads small, stocky or loose-skinned - the proportions are identical to Brown Bear and Grizzly Bear.

rows.verifyWhy:
UPHELD as FAIL on the identity must-reads, but ONE OF THE JUDGE'S THREE STATED CAUSES IS FACTUALLY WRONG and must not be fixed against.

WHAT I SAW (440x440 PNG, read at 1x then re-cropped and nearest-neighbour upscaled 4x/6x/8x on head, chest, rump and feet).

ORGANISM READ - CONFIRMED WRONG. The animal is a barrel-shaped fleece body in pale-to-mid neutral grey, covered edge to edge in short vertical/diagonal hair flicks that render as carded wool, with a crisp pale rim-light along the topline. Set on four straight column legs that end in dark rounded nubs. The head is a separate near-black blocky mass carried face-on-to-three-quarter, with a flat trapezoid saucer ear notched at the back of the skull, TWO large dark ovals across the upper face (the ear pair drawn face-on), one tiny pale ring-highlight eye, and a short rounded muzzle boss with a single glossy nostril. Grey fleece body + dark face + ring eye + hoof nubs = a dark-faced sheep (Suffolk/Hampshire read), not a bear. The judge's 'grey sheep' is correct and if anything understated: the black head over a pale fleece makes the sheep read MORE specific, not less.

CHASSIS. I composited Brown Bear / Grizzly Bear / Sun Bear / Sloth Bear side by side. All four are ONE CHASSIS in four colours - identical fleece barrel with the same vertical flick texture, identical blocky face-on skull with the same trapezoid ear, the same paired dark ovals, the same ring eye, the same nostril boss, the same column legs and the same two-lobe hoof nub with a white tick. Only hue and scale change. This is the same single-chassis defect the packet header warns about.

MUST-READ 1 - 'golden-cream crescent patch on the chest': ABSENT. CONFIRMED at 8x on the chest/brisket. There is no cream, no gold, no crescent, no blaze of any kind anywhere on the animal. The only tonal event forward of the ribs is a flat mid-grey quadrilateral shoulder/foreleg wedge and the dark neck bib bleeding down from the head - both neutral grey-brown, neither crescent-shaped. The species' namesake mark is entirely missing. Judge correct.

MUST-READ 2 - 'short sleek jet-black coat': FAILS on BOTH axes. Colour: the trunk samples as pale/mid neutral grey, not black; only the head and a small throat bib approach black, so the value is inverted relative to a real sun bear (black body, PALE tan muzzle) - here the body is pale and the muzzle is dark. Texture: long shaggy striated fleece, the opposite of short and sleek. Judge correct.

MUST-READ 3 - 'very long curved climbing claws and blunt short muzzle': SPLIT. Claws FAIL - at 6x each foot is a dark rounded two-lobe nub with a tiny white hatch cluster sitting on top of the toe line; no length, no curve, no digit separation, reads as a cloven hoof with a highlight. Judge's description here is accurate. BUT the 'blunt short muzzle' half IS PRESENT and readable - a short rounded muzzle boss with a glossy nose, not an elongated snout. Do not report the whole must-read as absent.

JUDGE'S SIZE CLAIM - WRONG, DO NOT FIX AGAINST IT. The judge says it sits 'at proportions identical to Brown and Grizzly Bear' and 'looks like one of the largest animals in a batch where it should read smallest'. Measured subject bounding boxes on the source PNGs (hue-aware background rejection): Sun Bear 209x161, Sloth Bear 239x181, Panda 252x180, Black Bear 250x192, Bear 260x178, Brown Bear 268x231, Grizzly Bear 275x219, Polar Bear 299x211. Sun Bear has the SMALLEST footprint of all nine bears in the batch - roughly 78% of Brown Bear's width, 70% of its height, ~55% of its area - and this is obvious by eye in a side-by-side strip. The packet note 'the smallest bear' is HONOURED. The shared chassis SHAPE is real; the claim that it is drawn at the same scale, or reads as one of the largest, is not.

BAND. FAIL stands: the organism reads as the wrong animal (sheep), and the single defining namesake must-read (golden-cream chest crescent) is completely absent, with the coat inverted in both value and texture. Fixes should target coat colour/texture, the chest crescent, the claws, and the shared sheep chassis - NOT the overall scale, which is already correct.

One stray artefact worth noting for the fix pass: a short isolated black diagonal stroke sits on the outside of the near hind leg just above the pastern, unattached to any form - visible at 6x, reads as a rendering slip rather than a marking.

rows.readsAs: a dark brown gnat or small housefly
rows.defect: The identity must-read - broad bands of black and yellow fuzz - is completely absent: the whole animal is one flat dark chocolate-brown with zero yellow anywhere. The body is not fat or bulky either; it is the same slim three-bead chassis as the other two, and the wings are LARGE and long (they cover the entire abdomen and extend past the tail), the exact opposite of the 'wings small relative to the bulky body' must-read. Fuzz exists only as a thin spike halo on the thorax; head and abdomen are bare and glossy.
rows.fix: Paint 3-4 broad alternating black and saturated yellow fuzz bands across a genuinely inflated, near-spherical abdomen and thorax, and shorten the wings to roughly half the abdomen length so they stop hiding the banding.

rows.readsAs: a bee-ish amber insect, or an amber hoverfly
rows.defect: The amber colour and the spiky thorax fuzz do land, and there are two pairs of clear wings. But the banded amber-and-black abdomen is not there - the abdomen is one uniform amber ellipse with no dark bands at all, and it is additionally three-quarters hidden beneath the overlong wings, so the single most recognisable honeybee cue is invisible. The pollen baskets are also absent: the hind legs are the same bare uniform wires as every other leg, with no thickened, loaded tibia.

rows.readsAs: a green housefly - the Honeybee asset recoloured green
rows.defect: This is the Honeybee pixel-chassis with the fill hue rotated to green; nothing structural differs. Two of the three must-reads are flat absent: there is NO long tongue trailing back beneath the body (no proboscis of any kind is drawn), and there is NO swollen polished hind tibia - the hind legs are the same uniform hairline wires as the front pair. The third must-read only half-lands: the green is a soft matte plastic green with one dull highlight, not a brilliant jewel-metallic chrome. Worse, it still carries the honeybee's thorax fuzz corona, which the note explicitly says it should not - the animal should look polished and hairless.

rows.readsAs: a dark grey ladybug
rows.defect: None of the three must-reads is present. The elytra are a flat uniform dark grey-brown with zero orange blotching — the black-and-orange banded pattern IS the identity of a burying beetle and it is entirely absent. There are no clubbed knobbed antennae (no antennae of any kind). The wing covers cover the whole abdomen, so no abdomen tip is left exposed. The shape is the shared ladybug oval with a ladybug pronotum shield, so it is indistinguishable from the Dung Beetle in the same batch apart from a couple of percent of lightness.
rows.fix: Paint two bold orange transverse bands across the black elytra, shorten the wing covers to about three quarters of the body so two bare abdominal segments show behind them, and add short antennae ending in an obvious orange knob club.
rows.verifyWhy: FAIL upheld after direct inspection (read the 440x440 PNG, then re-read 4x and 2x gamma-lifted crops of the head and whole body, plus a pixel dump). WHAT IS ACTUALLY DRAWN: a near-circular top-down beetle. Elytra bounding box measures x146-292 by y154-304 = 147 x 151 px, ratio 1.03 - essentially a circle. One vertical midline seam splits the wing cases; one crescent specular highlight sits on the LEFT elytron only; a thin rim-light arc runs down each outer edge; the surface carries a few barely-visible darker speckles. Head is a rounded dark blob (RGB ~14,13,16) sitting on a wider trapezoidal pronotum, with two tiny white eye dots. Six hairline legs, 3 per side, plus an elliptical ground shadow. CLAIM 1 - no orange - CONFIRMED and stronger than stated: a full-image scan finds ZERO warm pixels (r>g>=b with chroma>18) and a maximum chroma of 21/255 across the entire 440x440 canvas. The elytra sample at (36,32,35): neutral dark grey with a faint violet cast, not brown, not banded, not blotched. The black-and-orange transverse banding that IS the burying beetle is completely absent. CLAIM 2 - no clubbed knobbed antennae - CONFIRMED and understated: there are NO antennae of ANY kind. The head silhouette is a clean unbroken dome; nothing projects from it except the two white eye pixels. Not a thread, not a stub, not a club. CLAIM 3 - abdomen fully enclosed - CONFIRMED: the elytra terminate in a smooth rounded apex at y=304 with no exposed abdominal segments, no truncate elytral margin, no protruding tip. All three mustReads are absent. CORRECTIONS / ADDITIONS to the judging claim: (a) The judge described this only as a colour failure; the SHAPE is wrong too and is arguably the larger defect. The row specifies aspect 2 (elongate, twice as long as wide) and 'flat oval elytra'. The drawn body is 1.03 - the ROUNDEST body in the batch, rounder even than the Dung Beetle (1.21) - and the heavy crescent specular reads as a strongly convex dome, which is the ladybug/dung silhouette, the opposite of the flat parallel-sided carrion-beetle read. (b) 'Visually indistinguishable from the Dung Beetle' is true but too narrow. I rendered Dung Beetle and Ladybug side by side: all three are ONE CHASSIS - identical rounded head blob on a trapezoidal pronotum with two white eye dots, identical single midline seam, identical single left-side crescent specular, identical 3+3 hairline legs, identical rim-light arcs, identical ground shadow ellipse. This asset is literally the Ladybug drawing with the red fill swapped for grey and the spots deleted; Carrion vs Dung differ ONLY in body ratio (1.03 vs 1.21) and elytra value ((36,32,35) vs (23,23,22)). FIX DIRECTION: elongate the elytra to ~2:1 and flatten the dome (kill or greatly reduce the crescent specular), paint two or three orange transverse blotches across the black wing cases, add clubbed antennae with a visible terminal knob, and shorten the elytra so one or two abdominal tergites show past their rear margin.

rows.readsAs: an olive-green ladybug
rows.defect: All three must-reads are missing. There is no pale yellow rim anywhere on the shell margin — the olive body just fades to a dark edge. The hind legs are the same three thin grey arcs as every other asset in the batch, with no widening, no flattening and no fringe of swimming hairs, so nothing reads as an oar. There is no silver air bubble under the wing cases. The posture is listed as swimming but the render is the shared crawling ladybug chassis, complete with the ladybug pronotum shield and a ground drop-shadow ellipse that plants it on a floor rather than in water.
rows.fix: Draw a continuous pale yellow border stripe around the whole elytra-and-pronotum margin, replace the rearmost leg pair with broad flattened paddles fringed with hairs and swept backwards, and add a bright silver crescent of trapped air at the rear of the wing cases.
rows.verifyWhy:
UPHELD, and the shared-chassis charge is provable rather than impressionistic. I sampled the shell margin of Diving_Beetle.png and Ladybug.png at the same scanlines: the right silhouette edge sits at x=282 (y=175), x=294 (y=210), x=292 (y=250) in BOTH files. The outline is the same path pixel-for-pixel; only the fill hue and the ladybug's spots differ. Shared parts: identical domed-oval elytra, identical central elytral seam drawn as a single 1px dark line from under the pronotum to the abdomen tip, identical 'mushroom cap' head+pronotum lobe stacked on top with two tiny white eye dots, identical three thin grey leg arcs per side, identical elliptical ground drop shadow, identical glossy vertical specular streak on the left elytron. This asset reads as the Ladybug recoloured olive.

What is genuinely absent is (a) any decurved culmen — the top edge is a dead-straight ramp — (b) any overhanging hooked tip with a horn-coloured or dark distal third, and (c) any cere: the entire bill is one flat #E8B62C yellow with a thin darker outline, so there is no separate swollen fleshy patch at the base and 'yellow cere' cannot be read as present, only as accidentally the same colour as everything else. The head is a plain round dome with no bony brow ridge; the eye is a small dark bead with a specular dot, well under the 'prominent' the row asks for, and carries no shading over it. So: must-read 1 FAILS, but the fix is 'decurve the culmen and separate a cere block', not 'add a hook to a triangle'.

FEET — 'thin twigs' is WRONG. There are no twig legs at all; there is no visible tarsus of any kind. The foot is a single chunky solid-yellow mitten sitting flush against the underside of the breast, with three blunt forward lobes cut out of it by dark wedge gaps and a second smaller yellow lump behind/right (the far foot or a hallux). At 10x the toe tips are ROUNDED and unarmed — no claw shapes, no curved black talons, no scale hatching, no articulated joints. Must-read 2 FAILS, but the fix is 'grow a scaled tarsus and tip each toe with a curved talon', not 'thicken thin legs'.

WING — 'no broad rounded wing is folded over the back' is HALF WRONG and this is the correction most likely to be missed. A wing element IS drawn, and it is broad and rounded: a large dark-rimmed oval panel occupying almost the whole flank, filled with scalloped covert hatching, with a leading edge sweeping up to the shoulder and a set of fine straight feather streaks trailing off its rear point across the base of the tail. The failure is placement and read: it sits centred on the SIDE of the ball like an applied oval shield/badge rather than lying over the back, it has no wrist bend and no separated primary tips, and its outline closes on itself so it scans as a body marking, not as a folded wing. Must-read 3 FAILS on readability, not on absence.

TAIL — correctly called. Eight separate long rectrices with rounded tips splayed through roughly 90 degrees in a display fan, rufous with dark banding between them. Colour is right for a red-tailed buteo but a perched buteo's tail is a closed narrow rectangle; a fan this wide, at this downward angle, off a round breast, is turkey/grouse language and is doing most of the work that makes this read as a gamebird.

NET: the organism on screen is a rufous hen or grouse. All three must-reads fail (beak has no hook and no separable cere, feet have no talons or scaling, wing is present but reads as an oval flank badge) and the posture note is inverted. FAIL stands.

CORRECTION 2 - the back is not 'plain'. There IS dense speckle texture across the mantle, but every fleck is a PALE cream/light-gold chevron on a warm tan-gold ground, i.e. the value is inverted from the requirement. The only dark marks on the whole body are the brown crescent outlining the folded wing and one interior feather line.

The tail is a single flat unbarred mid-brown triangular wedge projecting rearward, about one third of body length, with no bars, no dark subterminal band, no white tip. WHAT IS ACTUALLY ON SCREEN (440x440; zoomed head at 60,130 100x80 @6x, feet at 110,250 110x70 @6x, body at 0,100 440x230 @2x): a fat egg-shaped body sitting on the ground with a small round head at upper-left and two dark tapering planks projecting horizontally out of the left and right flanks. MUST-READ 1 - white underside with a dark mask stripe through the eye: FAILS, and the judge is right on both halves. The whole body is one mid tan/greige field (roughly #b9a68c) overlaid with darker brown scalloped/scaly mottling that runs edge to edge across the belly, breast and back. Zero mask, zero eye-line, zero crown/nape contrast, and no white head at all. Nothing on the head is dark except the eye dot itself.

MUST-READ 2 - crooked M-shaped gull-like wings: FAILS. Both wings are dead-straight, level, and untapered until the very tip; they leave the body at the same height they end at. The right wing carries a few thin trailing-edge primary lines near its base, which is the only feather articulation present; the left wing has none. A translucent grey ellipse floats over the mid-body (the far wing rendered as a ghost) and reads as a smudge rather than a second wing.

MUST-READ 3 - hooked bill and outsized barbed talons: FAILS, and here the claim's DESCRIPTION IS WRONG. The feet are NOT "ordinary thin yellow twigs." At 6x the foot is a single broad, solid, flat yellow mitten/paddle - a wide slab roughly as deep as it is tall - with three short blunt notches cut into its front edge to suggest toes. It reads as a duck's webbed foot or a flipper, not as toes at all, and there is not one curved claw, hook, point or barb anywhere on it. A fix that merely thickens "thin twigs" would be working on geometry that does not exist; the actual defect is that the toes are fused into a paddle and must be rebuilt as separate splayed digits ending in long recurved black talons. The bill is also weaker than the claim implies: it is a short all-yellow wedge with a slight downturn at the tip - a faint hook at best - with no dark tip, no cere separation and no depth; it reads as a dove/finch bill.

Also: packet asks posture: flying, but the bird is planted on a cast ground shadow with its feet under it, so the flight pose does not read either. All three must-reads absent; the organism reads as the wrong bird. FAIL stands.

rows.readsAs: a vulture, or on a bad read a turkey

rows.readsAs: an upside-down scallop shell, or a cream ceramic soup bowl on two wedge feet
rows.defect: None of the three must-reads is present. The body is ONE unbroken solid form - no hinge, no valve seam, no gape, so there are not two symmetric valves at all. The surface carries RADIAL ribs fanning from a bottom point, which is the exact opposite structure to the concentric growth rings a clam is identified by. The two grey triangles under the shell read as furniture feet, not a pale muscular foot or paired siphons. The whole thing is also inverted: the umbo/hinge end sits at the bottom and the shell opening faces up.
rows.fix: Redraw as two mirrored valves meeting along a visible horizontal hinge seam with a small umbo bump at the top, replace every radial rib with nested concentric growth arcs following the shell margin, and push one pale fleshy foot out of the gape at the bottom.

WHAT IS ACTUALLY DRAWN: one cream bowl-shaped form, bright bbox 172x135px (aspect 1.27, so the 1.3 aspect target is met - the aspect is NOT the problem). Silhouette is a gently domed top rim carrying a single bright specular highlight, bulging left and right flanks, diagonal lower corners, and a FLAT horizontal cut bottom edge. Over it, ~15 thin dark radial ribs converge on a dark teardrop spike that sits INSIDE the form, about 8px above the flat bottom edge.

MUST-READ 1, two symmetric hinged valves - ABSENT, claim CONFIRMED. Under contrast stretch the whole body is one uninterrupted surface with a single continuous specular gradient running across it; there is no seam, no hinge line, no gape, no valve edge, no second valve behind. Correction to the claim's framing: the one element that could be mistaken for a hinge is the domed top rim with its bright edge highlight, but nothing meets it, so it reads as the lip of a lampshade, not a hinge.

MUST-READ 2, concentric growth rings - ABSENT, claim CONFIRMED, with three corrections. (a) The convergence point is NOT at the silhouette's bottom point - there is no bottom point. The shell bottom is a straight horizontal cut edge, and the ribs converge on an interior dark spike floating above it, which is why the umbo reads as a painted mark rather than a beak. (b) The rib fan only covers roughly the central 120 degrees of the form; large smooth blank crescents are left on the far left and far right flanks, so the ribbing reads as a fan wedge stamped onto a bowl rather than sculpture following the shell. (c) A defect the first judge read straight past: about 8 rib strokes ESCAPE the silhouette at the upper-left and upper-right shoulders and float in the background as detached dark hairs - an unclipped-stroke bug, clearly visible at 7x on the top crop. These stray hairs are the only thing on the asset resembling ears.

MUST-READ 3, pale muscular foot or paired siphons - ABSENT, claim CONFIRMED and sharpened. The two shapes below are hard-edged mid-grey flat-topped trapezoids (not pure triangles), mirrored left and right, tucked BEHIND the shell's bottom edge with a wide empty gap between them, and they are DARKER than the shell rather than pale flesh. They read as two plinth wedges / furniture feet. A clam foot is a single pale blade out of the ventral gape; siphons are paired tubes out of the posterior. Neither is present.

DECISIVE ADDITIONAL FINDING the first judge did not report: this is not merely a weak clam, it is the wrong sibling. Scallop.png in this same batch is the IDENTICAL chassis - same silhouette, same 15-rib fan converging on the same interior spike, same two grey trapezoid wedges, same escaped hair strokes at both top shoulders - differing only in hue (cream vs copper) and a slight scale. And the fan-ribbed shell is Scallop's own must-read ("fan-ribbed shell with flat wing-like ears at the hinge"). So the Clam is the Scallop recolour, and it delivers the Scallop's identity, badly, while delivering none of its own.

FIX DIRECTION: give the clam a distinct chassis - two valves meeting on a visible seam with the umbo/hinge at the TOP and a slight gape or crenulated meeting line along the ventral margin; replace the radial fan entirely with nested concentric growth arcs parallel to the ventral edge, tightening toward the umbo; and replace the two grey wedges with one pale off-white muscular foot protruding down-forward from the gape (or a pair of soft flesh-toned siphon tubes at the posterior end), lighter than the shell, not darker. Also clip rib/arc strokes to the shell path - the stray hairs at the top shoulders are a bug present on at least Clam and Scallop.

rows.readsAs: a teal paper fan or upturned bowl - the Clam asset recoloured

Reads as a colour variant, not a species.

WHAT IS ACTUALLY DRAWN: one single fan-ribbed valve seen face-on, hinge-DOWN. A wide, rounded, roughly hemispherical teal body; ~14 straight dark radial rib lines converging to a point at the bottom-centre; a thin pale specular highlight running along the top edge; two short dark hairline diagonal strokes flicking outward at the upper-left and upper-right corners (they read as tiny hinge ears / stray tentacles); and two flat teal triangular wedges splayed at the base under the convergence point. Flat single-hue teal with a soft top-lit gradient, on the standard dark card with the standard drop-shadow ellipse. That silhouette reads as a SCALLOP valve, not a clam and certainly not a Tridacna.

THE JUDGE'S CLAIM IS CORRECT AND I CAN QUANTIFY IT. Clam.png, Giant_Clam.png and Scallop.png are all 440x440 and are the SAME DRAWING. Clam vs Giant Clam differ in RGB on only 22,933 of 193,600 pixels (11.8%) -- i.e. 88.2% of the canvas, including the entire background gradient, the drop shadow and every anti-aliased silhouette edge, is byte-for-byte identical; the only pixels that differ are the shell body itself, and they differ purely in hue. The alpha channel is identical everywhere. Bounding boxes are identical. So the judge's 'pixel-identical to Clam recoloured teal' is literally true -- and I extend it: it is THREE species on one chassis, not two. Clam = cream, Giant Clam = teal, Scallop = peach/salmon, same ribs, same ears, same base wedges, same everything. The packet's aspect directive (Giant Clam 1.5 vs Clam 1.3) is not honoured either, since the silhouette is bit-identical.

MUST-READ 1 -- 'heavy fluted shell with wavy zigzag meeting lips': ABSENT. The judge's description is accurate: the top rim is a smooth convex arc with a clean pale highlight line, no scalloping, no wave, no interdigitation. I want to sharpen the cause, though. It is not merely that the zigzag was omitted from a rim -- there is no second valve anywhere in the image, no hinge line, no valve-to-valve seam. The pair is not represented at all, so there is no 'meeting lip' for a zigzag to live on. The ribs are also flat dark strokes painted on a smooth surface, not fluting: there is no ridge-and-trough relief, no lit crest / shadowed valley pairing, so even the ribbing does not read as the heavy corrugated Tridacna shell.

MUST-READ 2 -- 'iridescent patterned fleshy mantle bulging between the valves': ABSENT, exactly as claimed. There is no gape, so no mantle. I looked hard for it drawn small or in an unexpected place -- along the top rim, in the base wedges, in the rib convergence -- and found nothing. The only non-shell marks are the two corner hairlines and the two base triangles, and neither carries any mantle cue. There is also zero iridescence anywhere: the body is a single teal hue with one lightness gradient, no colour shift, no spotting, no blue/green mottling. That is the single feature that makes a giant clam recognisable and it is not present in any form.

Nothing else in the asset carries giant-clam identity either: no sense of massive scale, no thick wall section, no reef substrate. Blind, this asset reads 'scallop shell, teal'. Both must-reads are missing, the organism reads as the wrong bivalve, and the drawing is a recolour of two siblings in the same packet. FAIL stands.

FIX DIRECTION: this needs a new drawing, not a touch-up. Draw two heavy valves meeting along a horizontal-ish seam with the seam itself cut into 4-6 deep interlocking wavy teeth; give the ribs real relief (lit crest, shadowed trough) so the shell reads as corrugated stone; and open the gape to expose a fleshy mantle lobe bulging proud of the lips, painted with a mottled iridescent blue-green-gold pattern distinct in hue from the shell. And it must not share a silhouette with Clam or Scallop.

rows.readsAs: a dark slate-blue bowl or fan - the Clam asset in navy
rows.defect: The silhouette is the family's round symmetric bowl, not a wedge. A mussel is identified by an asymmetric teardrop wedge that tapers to a narrow pointed hinge at one end and swells to a broad rounded margin at the other; here both ends are equally round and the widest point is dead centre. No byssal beard threads anywhere. The radial ribs are wrong - a mussel shell carries fine concentric growth lines, not a fan. Only the dark blue-black colour lands, and it is so dark against the near-black plate that the form barely separates from the background.

rows.verifyWhy:
Upheld, but two of the three stated causes are described wrong and the fix notes need correcting.

WHAT IS ACTUALLY ON THE PLATE (measured on the 440x440 PNG, plus 4x and 16x brightened crops): a bilaterally symmetric FAN/BOWL shell standing upright. The top is a straight, gently up-arched hinge line running x=140..299 at y~128, capped by the asset's only specular highlight (peak pixel RGB 111,119,135 at 210,126). From that hinge the flanks bulge outward to the widest point of 165px at y=180, then sweep down and inward, converging to a narrow rounded base/point at y~255 where about eleven straight RADIAL rays meet. Shell body is RGB ~(41,40,51) dark navy-slate; the rays are a slightly warmer tan-brown (38,37,47 at mid, 35,35,44 at the convergence). Two grey triangular wedges sit under the base as a shadow/mount, plus a soft elliptical cast shadow lower down.

CORRECTION 1 - the shape description. It is NOT a 'round symmetric bowl with both ends equally rounded and the widest point dead centre'. The symmetry is LEFT-RIGHT (mirror), not end-to-end: the top end is a flat straight hinge, the bottom end tapers to a narrow point where the rays converge. The widest row is at y=180 out of a shell span of y=128..258, i.e. ~40% down, upper-middle, not dead centre. The organism this actually reads as is a SCALLOP (Pectinidae) or cockle - fan outline, straight hinge, radial ribs from a basal umbo - which is the worst possible error here because it collides with a sibling on the same family card. The judge is right that the mussel identity is absent; the shape they described is not the shape that is drawn, so a fix aimed at 'make the bowl less round' will miss.

CORRECTION 2 - the beard. The claim 'no byssal beard' is right in effect but wrong in detail: there ARE six thin thread-like strokes visible above the shell, three at the top-left corner and three at the top-right, poking out past the hinge line into the plate. At 16x they are exactly the same tan-brown as the interior rays and exactly COLLINEAR with them - they are the radial rib strokes overshooting the shell clip boundary, not a beard. So this is two defects, not one: (a) no byssal beard anywhere, and (b) an unclipped-stroke rendering bug leaking ribs outside the silhouette, symmetric on both sides. Anyone fixing this must not mistake the corner threads for an existing beard attempt.

CORRECTION 3 - contrast. 'Only the dark navy colour lands, and it is nearly invisible against the plate' overstates it. Plate immediately beside the shell is RGB (8,12,17); shell body is (41,40,51) rising to (111,119,135) on the hinge highlight - roughly a 3-4x luminance step plus a hard specular line. The silhouette is plainly legible at 1x; it is low-key and undersaturated but not invisible. Do not 'fix' this by brightening the shell.

MUST-READ SCORECARD (aspect 1.8, headFrac 0, eyes hidden, sessile): (1) 'wedge-shaped hinged shell narrow at the hinge end' - ABSENT and inverted. Drawn aspect is 165w x ~130h = 1.27, far rounder than the required 1.8, and the shell is WIDEST at the hinge end and narrowest at the opposite end, which is the exact reverse of a mussel's umbo-narrow / posterior-broad wedge. (2) 'dark blue-black glossy shell with growth lines' - HALF. Colour and gloss land (navy-slate body, specular hinge, soft sheen gradient). Growth lines FAIL: the surface carries straight radial rays fanning from a basal point, where a mussel needs concentric arcs running parallel to the shell margin, and a mussel shell is smooth - it must have no radial ribbing at all. (3) 'byssal beard threads anchoring it' - ABSENT (see correction 2).

One of three must-reads half-lands on colour alone; the defining wedge silhouette is not merely weak but reversed, and the asset resolves as a different bivalve on the same card. FAIL stands.

rows.readsAs: a bone-grey paper fan or bowl - the Clam asset desaturated
rows.defect: Same chassis again. The outline is smooth, symmetric and clean, which is the direct contradiction of the must-read: an oyster is identified by an IRREGULAR, ruffled, rough-layered shell with lumpy asymmetric edges. There are no layered growth flanges, no ragged margin. The two valves are neither visible nor unequal - there is one solid form, so no cupped-versus-flat contrast. No pearly interior because the shell never opens.
rows.fix: Break the outline into an irregular lumpy blob with stacked ruffled layer flanges around the rim, split it into an obviously deep cupped lower valve and a thinner flat lid tilted open, and show a smooth nacre-pale interior in the gap.
rows.verifyWhy:
UPHELD, and the true cause is worse than stated. At 440x440 the asset is a single closed bowl/dome: a smooth convex arc across the top margin, smooth unbroken curved flanks, and a flat-cut bottom edge where the form narrows. Across that face are ELEVEN straight dark radiating rib strokes fanning from a dark umbo notch at the bottom centre up to the top margin. Additional elements the FAIL judge did not mention: three short dark hair-like strokes project outward beyond the shell at EACH upper corner (six total), and two mid-grey hard-edged triangular/trapezoid slabs sit under the flat base as props, plus a detached elliptical ground shadow.

WHAT IS CORRECT IN THE CLAIM: the outline is genuinely smooth and perfectly bilaterally symmetric; there is not one stacked layer flange, foliated lamina, or ragged/frilled margin anywhere on the silhouette or the interior; the form is one solid closed body with no gape, no hinge line, no valve-separation seam, so there is indeed no unequal cupped-vs-flat valve pair and no exposed pearly interior. All three of the packet must-reads (irregular ruffled rough-layered shell; two unequal valves one cupped one flat; pearly smooth interior when open) are absent. Zero of three.

WHAT THE CLAIM GETS WRONG OR MISSES: (1) It frames the body as merely blank/featureless. It is not blank — it is positively wearing ANOTHER species' diagnostic. Radiating fan ribbing converging on an umbo is the Scallop's own must-read in this very packet ('fan-ribbed shell'), and the oyster is drawn with it. This is misidentification, not just omission, and it is the fix that matters: the ribs must be REMOVED and replaced with irregular concentric foliated layers, not merely supplemented. (2) There IS a thin bright specular rim line along the top margin, which could be mistaken for nacre in a fast read — it is an exterior edge highlight on a closed shell, not a pearly interior; no interior surface is visible at any point. (3) The six corner hairs and the two grey triangular base props are undescribed and are not oyster anatomy; if they are meant as byssal threads / substrate they belong on Mussel, and an oyster is cemented flat to its substrate, not propped on two legs.

FAMILY-LEVEL FINDING (the decisive one). I rendered all six bivalves side by side. Clam, Giant Clam, Mussel, Oyster and Scallop are ONE CHASSIS: identical smooth fan-ribbed bowl silhouette, identical convergent bottom umbo notch, identical rim highlight, identical six corner hairs, identical pair of grey triangular props. They differ ONLY in fill colour (cream / cyan / navy / beige / orange) and a small aspect stretch. Oyster and Clam are near-indistinguishable even in hue. Only Razor Clam breaks the mould, and it is merely the same ribbed body squashed into a tilted ellipse rather than a straight parallel-edged blade. So the Oyster does not read as an oyster; it reads as a generic ribbed scallop/cockle shell in beige, and the family reads as one shell in five colours. Rebuilding the oyster requires an asymmetric outline with an irregular wavy margin, stacked overlapping growth laminae, a visibly deeper cupped left valve against a flatter right valve with an offset meeting seam, and a chalk-grey/mud exterior against a faint iridescent nacre band if any interior is shown.

WHAT IS ACTUALLY THERE: a single olive-brown (approx R122 G112 B70) lens/pod, oriented -18.4 deg, body bbox x119-317 y147-222. A bright near-white specular rim runs along the whole UPPER-LEFT edge only (the lower edge has no rim) — that highlight plus the olive body colour DOES satisfy the 'glossy olive-brown periostracum' must-read. About ten evenly spaced dark rib strokes cross the short axis. That is the whole render: one plate, no second valve, no hinge line, no umbo, no axial seam anywhere, no siphon, and NO DIGGING FOOT at either end — both ends just stop. So two of the three must-reads (parallel-edged razor blade; digging foot from one end) are absent, and it reads as a generic seed-pod / leaf, not a Ensis blade.

CORRECTION 1 — 'squashed flat' is WRONG. The oriented (PCA) extent is length 208.7 px by width 40.8 px, ASPECT 5.12, against the packet's aspect: 6. The elongation is very nearly on spec; do NOT stretch it. The defect is the EDGE PROFILE, not the length. Half-width sampled along the axis: 40.8 at centre, 40.5 at +/-20, 36.4 at +/-50, 30.7 at +/-70, 22.1 at +/-90, 15.8 at +/-100 — a smooth cosine falloff with no flat run anywhere. A razor clam needs thickness held constant (parallel edges) across roughly the middle 80% of the length, then a squared/obliquely-cut end. That flat section is what is missing.

CORRECTION 2 — 'tapers to a sharp point at BOTH ends' is WRONG. At 9x both ends are BLUNT ROUNDED caps, still about 16 px thick at +/-100 along the axis, with the white rim curving smoothly around the right tip. It is a lens/pod outline, not a pointed leaf. Fixing this as 'de-point the tips' would miss the actual problem (see correction 1).

CORRECTION 3 — the shadow offset claim is WRONG. Shadow centroid x = 219.0; body centroid x = 218.7. The ground shadow is horizontally CENTRED under the body to within 0.3 px, and its x-span (132-306, 174 px) sensibly matches the body's (119-317, 198 px). There is no 'up-left body / low-right shadow' lateral mismatch. The detachment is purely VERTICAL: body bottom edge y=222, shadow top edge y=277 — a 55 px empty gap on a 440 px canvas, so the shell reads as hovering. Fix by raising the shadow, not by sliding it sideways.

CONFIRMED FROM THE CLAIM: the chassis ribs and stray whiskers are real. The ~10 rib strokes are the generic fan-rib chassis, and at least four of them OVERSHOOT the shell mask and hang in bare background at the two tapered ends — visible stubs at roughly (132,188) and (150,227) off the lower-left tip and (293,135) and (302,172) off the upper-right tip. Also confirmed: no hinge and no foot.

BAND: FAIL. One of three must-reads present (glossy olive periostracum); the two that carry the identity — the straight parallel-edged cut-throat-razor blade and the protruding digging foot — are both absent, and the leftover fan-rib strokes leak outside the silhouette. Nothing here is a small feature I could have missed; I checked both ends at 9x specifically for a foot stub and there is none.

rows.readsAs: a scallop shell, but upside down - a salmon-pink fan standing on its point
rows.defect: The one asset the shared chassis nearly fits, since a radial rib fan IS the scallop read - which is itself the family's problem. But it is inverted: the ribs converge at the bottom and the straight hinge edge is drawn across the TOP, so the shell stands on its umbo with the fan opening upward. The flat wing-like ears are not at the hinge - the only triangles present sit at the bottom, opposite the straight edge, and read as feet. Both flesh must-reads are entirely missing: there is no row of tiny bright blue eyes along the mantle edge (the packet flags eyes as prominent) and no fringe of sensory tentacles between the valves. The two hair-thin whiskers at the upper corners are too faint to register as anything.
rows.fix: Flip the shell so the straight hinge and its two triangular ears sit at the top with the ribs spreading down to a wide scalloped bottom margin, then line the gape with a row of bright blue dot eyes and a fringe of short tentacles.

rows.readsAs: a generic anglerfish or piranha — a fat scaled egg with a glowing bulb on a stalk
rows.defect: The must-read that IS the monkfish is missing: there is no enormous flattened head wider than the body. The silhouette is a plain symmetric egg with no head/body boundary, no widening at the front, no taper at the back — the body actually narrows toward the head rather than the reverse. The mouth is a small notch of straight vertical teeth on the front edge, not a huge upturned gape ringed with inward-slanting teeth. No frilly skin flaps anywhere along the jaw or flanks. No pectoral fins at all, so nothing sprawls; the sprawling posture is unreadable. The only monkfish cue present is the lure, and a lure alone reads as deep-sea anglerfish, not Lophius. Rendered aspect is roughly 1.5, well under the specified 1.9.
rows.fix: Rebuild the silhouette as a wide top-down-ish wedge: a broad flattened head disc occupying the front half at 2x the body width, with a crescent upturned jaw across its whole leading edge, inward-raked fangs, a fringe of skin tassels along the jawline and body margin, and the body tapering sharply to a thin tail behind it.

rows.readsAs: a small generic minnow or perch — a scaled leaf shape with a spiky dorsal comb
rows.defect: Two of the three must-reads are absent. There are no pectoral fins whatsoever — the huge fan-like pectorals that prop a sculpin on the bottom, which are the single most recognisable thing about the animal, are not drawn, so nothing props and nothing fans. The head is not oversized, broad or flattened: it is the narrow pointed right-hand tip of a symmetric lens, visibly narrower than the mid-body, the opposite of the reference. The body is not a scaleless tapering tadpole — it is a fore-aft symmetric almond covered in an explicit crosshatch scale mesh. The eye is a tiny dot, not prominent. The zigzag dorsal comb is the only added feature and it reads as a generic spiny-rayed panfish fin.
rows.fix: Draw a pair of enormous rounded fan pectorals with visible rays splayed downward and outward from just behind the head, planted on the substrate, and swell the front third of the body into a broad blunt flattened skull with big high-set bulging eyes while tapering the rear to a thin smooth scaleless tail.

rows.readsAs: A fern frond, or a rowan/ash sprig — some viewers will say an ear of wheat
rows.defect: The must-read that IS fennel — the cloud of thread-fine feathery foliage — is absent. The leaves are discrete, opaque, hard-edged oval leaflets pinned in a strict herringbone along five horizontal ribs, and the whole mass is boxed into a mechanical rectangle with flat vertical sides. That is a pinnate compound leaf, the opposite of fennel's hair-like dissection. The umbel is a small solid yellow crescent lid rather than a flat-topped spray of spoke-like rays carrying florets, the stem is a plain flat olive pole with no ribbing and no blue tint, and there is no swollen white bulb base at the soil.
rows.fix: Replace the leaflet stamp with hundreds of 1px hair-thread strokes fanning from each rib tip so the foliage reads as a soft translucent haze with a broken outer edge, and rebuild the crown as visible radiating rays each ending in a small yellow floret cluster.

rows.readsAs: A spider plant or a young agave — a generic grass clump with a pin stuck in the middle
rows.defect: The bulb is entirely absent. Zoomed on the base, the blades converge to a sharp pinched point that disappears straight into the ground shadow: no swelling, no papery white skin, no clove divisions, no root fringe. That papery cloved bulb IS garlic. The scape is also wrong — it is a rigid straight stalk, not the signature curling loop — and its head is the same flat crescent lid used on Fennel and Onion rather than a bulbil cluster in a beaked spathe. The blades themselves are plain tapering grass straps with a single highlight line; the flat FOLDED keel that distinguishes garlic from onion is not visible, so the asset cannot be told apart from the Onion card beside it.
rows.fix: Draw a fat white papery bulb sitting on the soil with three or four vertical clove seams and a fringe of wiry roots, then bend the scape into its characteristic single loop before the head.

rows.readsAs: A clump of ornamental grass or a small green flax — not a vegetable at all
rows.defect: Same missing identity: there is no swollen papery bulb and no fringe of wiry roots. The leaf fan tapers to a point and enters the black ground ellipse with no base swelling whatsoever, so the harvest organ named in the reference simply does not exist in the picture. The leaves are also flat sword blades with a pale midrib, not the hollow ROUND tubes the must-read calls for — no cylindrical shading, no blunt hollow tips, and several blades flop over sideways the way a grass does rather than arching stiffly. The crown is the same recoloured crescent lid as Fennel and Garlic instead of a spherical allium head of tiny star florets. Placed next to Garlic this is visibly the identical drawing with the fan opened slightly and the grey warmed to green.
rows.fix: Add a large papery-skinned bulb with concentric skin lines and a root fringe at the soil line, and re-shade the leaves as cylinders — dark edge, bright centre stripe, blunt rounded tip — so they read as hollow tubes.

rows.readsAs: a llama or a shaggy long-necked sandy ungulate; 'camel' only on a second look
rows.defect: Of the three must-reads only the long curved neck is clearly delivered. The single hump does not exist as a separate form — the entire torso is one round egg with a woolly lighter oval painted over it, so the topline is a continuous dome from croup to withers and there is no lean back for a hump to rise out of. The legs are short (belly sits low, legs are roughly a third of standing height, not the stilty camel proportion), they have no knobbly knee pads anywhere, and the feet at 4x zoom are tiny dark CLOVEN HOOF stubs — the opposite of the broad splayed padded camel foot the reference names. Only two legs are drawn; the far-side pair is absent entirely, so the quadruped posture reads as a two-legged side cutout. The tail is also wrong scale: a thick rope leaving the rump high and hanging nearly to the ground with a black tassel, longer than the hind leg.
rows.fix: Rebuild the torso as a shallow lean barrel and sit ONE distinct hump on top of it as a separate mass that breaks the topline (a clear notch in front of it at the withers and behind it at the loin), then swap the hoof stubs for wide two-toed padded footpads that flare wider than the leg, add the knobbly knee callus on the foreleg, lengthen the legs so the belly clears the ground by more than the leg is thick, and shorten the tail to a stub with a tassel.

rows.readsAs: a llama - specifically, the exact same llama that ships as the Llama asset, with a few extra stray hairs
rows.defect: Side by side with Llama.png this is the same drawing: same outline, same skull, same eye, same muzzle, same neck arc, same hip flap, same feet. All three must-reads are missing. The face is LONG and tapering like the llama's, not blunt and short. There is no topknot fringe at all - the crown is bare and smooth. The ears are the flat grey teardrop lying inside the skull outline, so no short spear ear exists in silhouette. The fleece is not dense wool: it is a patch of stringy straw-coloured streaks on the mid-torso plus scraggly grey spikes poking off the neck and belly edge, while the neck, legs and rump are smooth bare shapes. At the shoulder and rump the fleece patch ends in a hard straight cutout edge that reads as a pasted-on sticker seam.
rows.fix: Rebuild the alpaca head separately from the llama head - shorten the muzzle to a stub about half its current length, dome the cranium, plant two SHORT straight ears that clear the skull outline, and pile a shaggy topknot forelock over the brow; then run the crimped fleece over the neck and haunches too so the wool ends in a fuzzy edge instead of a straight seam.

rows.readsAs: a shaggy straw-coloured sheep, or a woolly tapir - nobody names a Bactrian camel
rows.defect: The two-hump identity is not legible. At full size the back is ONE broad flat-topped dome; zooming 3x shows a shallow V notch pressed into it, but the two lobes are wide, low and nearly merged, so the dip is a few pixels on a back over a third of the image wide and vanishes at any real display size. There are not two separate humps, there is one lumpy back. The neck is short and thick, not long and curved, and it is completely smooth - no shaggy hanging hair on the neck or chest, and no hair crowning either hump. The legs are short stubs, roughly a third of standing height, with the belly hanging almost to the hocks. A flat un-shaded tan slab sits over the hip and the tasselled tail sprouts from it like a separate pasted object.
rows.fix: Raise TWO distinct humps with real sky between them - each a tall narrow peak with a deep U valley cutting down to the spine line - then lengthen the neck and legs so the belly rides high, and hang shaggy fringe off the throat, chest and both hump crowns.

rows.readsAs: a camel - a stumpy, overfed one, or at a glance a bison with a long neck
rows.defect: The single hump and the raised curving neck do land, so the animal is namable. But the third must-read fails outright: the legs are short stubs at roughly a third of total height, nowhere near the half the reference calls for, with no knobbly knees or hocks - and the barrel is so deep that the belly hangs down to meet them, killing the leggy dromedary stance. The hump is also not read as a hump so much as the whole torso being one round dome, because the back and the barrel are the same continuous circle with no shoulder or rump line to sit between. The head is the shared chassis skull - a big round eye ringed in white with no split camel lip, no nostril slit and no ear breaking the outline.
rows.fix: Roughly double the leg length and lift the belly line well clear of the knees, then narrow the barrel and set the hump as a distinct peak above a visible withers-to-rump back line rather than letting body and hump be one circle.

rows.readsAs: a llama - the long neck, small head, flat hump-free back and slim legs do carry it
rows.defect: The headline must-read is absent: there are no long banana-curved ears. What sits on the head is a flat grey teardrop painted INSIDE the skull outline, so the silhouette is completely earless and the profile reads slightly reptilian. The neck is one plain forward arc, not an upright S-curve - it leans out over the chest rather than rising vertically then tucking the head back. The flat back is correct. The body has the same hard straight cutout seam at the shoulder and a wedge notch at the rump where the paler wool patch ends against the body, reading as a pasted panel. And because the Alpaca asset is this same drawing, the two species are visually undifferentiated.
rows.fix: Grow two long banana-curved ears that clear the top of the skull by about a head height and curve inward at the tips, and re-carriage the neck into an upright S - vertical out of the withers, then a tuck back at the throat.

rows.readsAs: a sandy Shetland pony / hoofed foal with a bushy tail
rows.defect: Two of three must-reads are absent and the third is contradicted. The frame is not lean or wolfish — it is a deep barrel torso with no flank tuck, four straight posts and dark HOOVES at the ground (visible as split dark caps at 4x). The white feet are missing entirely: the feet are the darkest part of the animal and the only white on the model is a blob on the tail tip. The ears are not erect pointed triangles — they are one dark triangular hood laid flat on top of the skull. The tail is bushy but hooks down and forward, not straight.
rows.fix: Rebuild the chassis below the barrel: cut torso depth ~30%, add a rising flank tuck ahead of the hind leg, replace the four posts with a digitigrade canid limb (angled scapula, elbow at the chest line, a real hock bend on the hind) and terminate every leg in a four-toed white paw instead of a hoof cap.

rows.readsAs: a cream pony / donkey foal, not a dog of any breed
rows.defect: Identical silhouette to the Dingo with a paler fill — same barrel, same four hoofed posts, same hooded head. The plumed tail carried above the back is absent: the tail is set low and swings DOWN and forward past the hocks. The ears are not erect or folded dog ears, they are the shared dark triangular hood on the skull crown. The only must-read that lands is the dark nose blob at the end of the snout, and that snout is a tapered anteater wedge with no jaw or lip line.
rows.fix: Re-anchor the tail high on the croup and arc it up over the topline in a plume, and give the skull a real pair of side-set ears plus a stop between forehead and muzzle so the head stops reading as a hooded wedge.

rows.readsAs: a white shaggy pony or a long-nosed goat
rows.defect: None of the three must-reads survive. The coat is a flat bone-white over the whole animal — no grizzled grey saddle on the back and no tawny legs; back, barrel and legs are one value. The tail is low-carried and bushy but has NO dark tip; it is the palest thing on the model. The ears are not large triangles — they are the same small dark hood shape shared with the other three, and it is smaller relative to the skull here than a Pampas fox's ears should be. The body is the shared hoofed barrel chassis with no canid tuck or hock.
rows.fix: Paint a distinct three-zone coat — grizzled grey-and-black saddle over the back, tawny-rufous legs and cheeks, and a black-tipped tail — then enlarge the ears to genuinely oversized side-set triangles.

rows.readsAs: an orange pony / a fox-coloured hoofed foal
rows.defect: The colour says fox and the body says horse. The black stockings are entirely absent — the legs are the same orange as the barrel right down to a small dark hoof cap, and at 4x those caps are split hoof shapes rather than paws. The pointed ears are absent, replaced by the family's dark triangular skull hood. The white-tipped brush is present but it is a modest low-hooked tail, not the enormous brush that is the species' single loudest read; it is no bigger than the Dingo's. The deep barrel torso with no flank tuck and the level thick neck make this read as the same pony as the other three.
rows.fix: Double the tail's mass into a true brush that sweeps horizontally back at hock height with a bold white tip, and paint solid black from the elbow and hock down to real black paws.

rows.readsAs: a generic gold aquarium fish — a stranger would say 'goldfish' or 'bream', not 'carp'
rows.defect: Two of the three must-reads are simply not on the canvas. There are NO barbels — the snout is a bare point with no mouth line at all, let alone two pairs of whiskers at the mouth corners, and barbels are the single feature that makes a carp a carp. The long single dorsal fin running most of the back is also absent: the back carries one tiny rounded nub the same size as the ventral nub, covering maybe 12% of the topline. The body is a symmetric lens, not deep and heavy-shouldered — the dorsal and ventral curves mirror each other, so there is no shoulder mass ahead of the dorsal. Side by side with Goldfish.png it is the identical silhouette in a different colour.
rows.fix: Draw four barbels — a short pair at the upper lip and a longer, thicker pair trailing back from the mouth corners past the gill cover — and replace the dorsal nub with a long low dorsal that starts at the shoulder and runs two-thirds of the back to the peduncle; raise the front third of the topline so the shoulder sits above the belly line.

rows.readsAs: an orange fish — 'goldfish' is a reasonable guess, but only because of the colour
rows.defect: The colour and the stubby depth carry it, but the two shape must-reads are weak. The tail is a single flat solid wedge with two stray hairs — there is no flowing DOUBLE fan, no split, no trailing veil, no translucency; it is the same tail shape as the Carp, only wider. The back is a low symmetric arc rather than high-arched, and the long dorsal fin is a single tiny nub identical to the Carp's, so the arched-back-plus-long-dorsal read is missing entirely. The head is featureless — no mouth, only a dot eye.
rows.fix: Replace the wedge tail with a genuinely split double lobe — two long trailing veils that separate at the peduncle and taper past the body's own length, drawn semi-transparent — and lift the topline into a high arch carrying a long dorsal that runs from the shoulder to the tail root.

rows.readsAs: a small slim silvery baitfish — the right ballpark, though it could equally be a sardine or a smelt
rows.defect: The slim silvery body is correct, and there is a small dorsal roughly mid-back, but the dark lateral stripe is absent: the darkening runs along the TOP edge as ordinary dorsal counter-shading, and the flank itself is uniformly pale with speckles — there is no stripe from gill to tail at mid-flank. The eye is also mis-set: the white ring sits right on the tip of the pointed snout and breaks the head outline, so the fish reads as having its eye on its nose. The dorsal is the same generic nub used on the Carp and Goldfish rather than a soft rayed fin.
rows.fix: Paint a distinct dark lateral band along the mid-flank from the gill cover to the tail root, and move the eye back and up so it sits fully inside the head mass behind the snout tip.

rows.readsAs: A striped pony, okapi, or thylacine — a small hooved ungulate. No stranger names this a cat.
rows.defect: All three must-reads are absent. (1) Triangular upright ears on a round short-muzzled head: there are no triangular ears at all — a single large flat GREY DISC sits on the side of the skull like a ram's horn boss or a pasted-on mouse ear, and the head is a long tapering snout that droops downward at the tip, the opposite of a round short muzzle. (2) Long expressive tail: the tail is a short, thick, blunt-ended grey club that hangs down and hooks forward, rendered in the same flat grey as the ears and feet so it does not even read as continuous with the body. (3) Vertical slit pupils and long whiskers: the eye is a yellow blob with a broad dark smear for a pupil, set far forward on the snout rather than on the face, and there are zero whiskers. On top of the must-read failures the feet are dark blocky HOOVES, not paws; the topline is dead level and the barrel is ungulate-deep; the stripes are dense vertical zebra bars over the whole ribcage rather than tabby whorls; and there is a stray dark stripe fragment floating detached on the near hind shin, well below the striped field.
rows.fix: Rebuild the head and forequarters on a felid skull instead of repainting the pony: shorten the muzzle to about one third of its current length so it is a rounded dome with a short blunt nose, replace the grey side-disc with two TRIANGULAR ears standing upright off the top of the skull, move the eye back onto the cheek plane and give it a hard vertical slit pupil, and add radiating whisker strokes; then swap the hoof blocks for toed paws and lengthen the tail to at least body length with a smooth taper in body colour.

rows.readsAs: a fleecy tan goat or young sheep with lyre horns
rows.defect: The horns are smooth, not ringed, and read as soft putty. The body is a woolly barrel on stumpy tubes, not a deep chest on very fine legs — the legs are as thick as Cow's. No white belly: the underside is the same tan as the flank. No tail is visible at all on this asset.
rows.fix: Halve the leg width and lengthen them so the belly sits high, add a hard white belly/inner-thigh split along the flank, and cut 6-8 ring grooves into each horn.

rows.readsAs: a brown ox with white socks
rows.defect: White lower legs are present and correct, but the white rump patch is absent — the rump is plain brown and is further hidden by the oversized brush tail arcing across it. There is no white band above the muzzle; the face is uniform dark brown. The horns are two small pale crescents perched on a dark cap with no bald forehead plate joining them.
rows.fix: Paint a hard-edged white rump blaze around the tail root and a white bar across the top of the muzzle, and join the horn bases with a pale keratin plate across the forehead.

rows.readsAs: a shaggy capybara or a hairy tapir — nothing on it says bison
rows.defect: It has NO HORNS AT ALL. There is no shoulder hump: the topline is the family's plain convex arc and the hindquarters are as deep as the chest, so the silhouette is rear-heavy rather than front-heavy. The head is small, carried HIGH on a level neck, and clean-shaven — no beard, no low-slung massive skull, no forehead mop. The specified small eye is instead the family's large white-ringed cartoon eye.
rows.fix: Rebuild the silhouette front-heavy — a tall hair-covered hump peaking over the forelegs falling steeply to small hips — drop the head below the shoulder line, add a chin beard and short black upcurved horns.

rows.readsAs: a grey cow or a yak
rows.defect: The horns are two thin pale crescents sitting on top of the skull; there is no fused helmet boss across the forehead, which is the Cape buffalo's whole identity. The ears are a shapeless dark blob tucked behind the horn bases rather than large fringed flaps drooping BELOW the horns. The shoulders are not massive — the topline actually sags behind the neck.
rows.fix: Fuse the horn bases into one thick keratin plate covering the whole forehead, then sweep the horns down and out from it, and hang two big drooping fringed ears below the boss.

rows.readsAs: a brown cow — indistinguishable from the Buffalo and Gaur in this batch
rows.defect: No humped neck or shoulder mass: the neck is the family's short level tube and the topline is the same smooth arc as Cow's. No pendulous dewlap — the throat line is a clean straight edge with nothing hanging from it. The horns curve UP and back rather than short and forward.
rows.fix: Pile a crest of muscle on the neck and withers so the topline peaks ahead of the shoulder, hang a deep scalloped dewlap from jaw to brisket, and re-aim the horns forward.

rows.readsAs: a Holstein cow — the patches carry it
rows.defect: No udder: the belly line is smooth and empty between the hind legs. No throat dewlap — the jaw-to-chest line is straight. The barrel does not sag heavily; it is the same trim arc as the antelopes. The ears are small nubs by the horn position rather than set out sideways, and the tail brush is a long grey broom floating well clear of the rump.
