rows.fix: Add a full pink udder with teats under the hind belly and a hanging dewlap at the throat, and pull the tail in against the rump.

rows.readsAs: a pale cream goat or a generic antelope
rows.defect: Nothing ox-like about it — it is drawn on the LIGHT antelope chassis, the same body as Antelope and Gazelle, with no shoulder hump at all. No dewlap under the throat: the neck line is bare and straight. The horns have only a faint waver rather than a tight straight spiral, so they read as plain lyre horns.
rows.fix: Swap it onto the deep bovine body with a distinct hump over the withers, hang a loose skin dewlap from the throat, and cut a hard corkscrew ridge into the straight horns.

rows.readsAs: a dark brown ox with white socks
rows.defect: White stockings on all four legs are present and read well. But there is no tall muscular ridge along the shoulders — the topline behind the neck actually DIPS before the barrel rises, the opposite of the gaur's dorsal ridge. The forehead is dark brown with no pale grey patch between the horns.
rows.fix: Raise a hard-edged ridge of muscle from the neck crest back to mid-back so the shoulder is the tallest point, and drop a pale grey patch across the forehead between the horn bases.

rows.readsAs: a pale cream goat — and it is visibly the same picture as Antelope and Impala
rows.defect: It is the Antelope asset at a colder tan. The dark flank band between tan and white is entirely absent, so the two-tone side that IS a gazelle is missing. The horns are smooth, not ringed. The legs are thick fleecy tubes, not fine and delicate, and the neck is the family's short thick one rather than long. The specified prominent eye is the same size as every other asset's.
rows.fix: Lay a hard black horizontal band along the flank with white below it, then thin the legs and lengthen the neck so the body reads as a light runner rather than a fleece barrel.

rows.readsAs: a generic tan antelope, the same one as Antelope and Impala
rows.defect: All three must-reads are absent. The face is the family's short rounded wedge with a stubby muzzle — nothing about it is extremely long or narrow, despite the 0.32 headFrac. The back does not slope to the hindquarters: it is the same smooth convex arc, and the rump is actually the HIGHEST point of the body rather than the lowest. The horns are the standard lyre pair set flat on the skull with no bony pedestal and no bracket shape.
rows.fix: Stretch the muzzle to roughly twice the cranium length so the head reads as a narrow wedge, tilt the whole topline down toward the tail, and mount the horns on a tall bony pedestal so they rise as one bracket before splitting.

rows.readsAs: a tan fleecy goat — the third copy of the Antelope drawing in this batch
rows.defect: No vertical black stripes on the rump; the hindquarters are plain tan and there is no white rump for them to sit on. No black tuft above the hind hoof. The legs are thick woolly tubes rather than extremely fine, and the horns are smooth putty crescents with no rings and no out-then-up lyre sweep.
rows.fix: Add the white rump with two black vertical bars flanking the tail and a black tuft at each hind fetlock, and slim the legs to half their current width.

rows.readsAs: a broken decal — a striped animal with a black slab stuck on its side
rows.defect: The flank markings have collapsed into a solid dark rectangular bar spanning nearly the whole barrel with comb-like tines hanging off its lower edge; it reads as a rendering artifact pasted over the body, not as stripes, and its hard rectangular top and bottom edges cut straight across the topline shading. The stripes are also inverted — thick BLACK bars where the reference calls for 6-10 thin WHITE ones. Heavy dark bands also wrap the neck and face, making the head read as masked. The ears are small nubs, nowhere near enormous rounded satellite dishes.
rows.fix: Replace the black slab with 8 thin white vertical stripes that follow the body curve and stop cleanly at the spine and belly, and rebuild the ears as two huge rounded paddles.

rows.readsAs: a shaggy ox with one broken tusk
rows.defect: Only ONE horn is drawn — a single pale curved spike rising from the top of the skull and pointing forward; the asset is visibly asymmetric and the horn does not attach to a boss at all. There is no helmet boss across the forehead and no down-and-out hook. The curtain of hair is missing: the coat ends in a ragged hem above the elbow and the whole lower half of all four legs is bare tan, so nothing hangs near the hooves. The shoulders are not humped and the head is carried level, not low.
rows.fix: Draw the paired horns as one broad boss covering the forehead with both tips hooking down then out, and extend the shaggy coat as a straight curtain of long hair falling to just above the hooves.

rows.readsAs: a white antelope with long back-swept horns — oryx is a fair guess
rows.defect: The long straight rapier horns read well and are the strongest horn work in the batch. But the facial mask is two isolated black discs around the eye and cheek that read as goggles or panda eyes, not the oryx's black bands running down the face; there are no black markings on the legs at all, and no black flank line. The body is the slender fleecy antelope chassis rather than blocky and horse-like.
rows.fix: Replace the two black discs with connected bands — a stripe down the bridge of the nose joined to a bar through the eye — and add black bands at the top of each leg.

rows.readsAs: a pale woolly goat or sheep with straight ringed horns
rows.defect: The identity must-read -- the bulbous drooping trunk-like proboscis -- is only a faint rounded lobe on the front of an otherwise ordinary tapered muzzle; nothing droops or overhangs the mouth. The ringed horns are correct and legible, but the body underneath is the family's woolly barrel loaf, not the light deer-like antelope frame, and the pegs read as sheep legs rather than the slim high-set saiga legs.
rows.fix: Rebuild the muzzle as a distinct swollen down-turned proboscis that visibly overhangs and hides the mouth line, wider than the skull and with the nostrils opening downward at its tip.

rows.readsAs: a grey woolly ox or tapir with a single tusk
rows.defect: The horns -- which ARE the water buffalo -- are absent as specified. What is drawn is one pale ivory tusk-like curve laid across the top of the skull (the identical element reused on the Wildebeest and Yak), not a pair of enormous swept-back crescents sweeping out and back from the brow. The head is also carried high and forward at above back level instead of held low, and the muzzle is a small rounded goat nose rather than a broad flat wet muzzle. The rump carries a pasted-on horizontal fan-and-disc tail that reads as a separate object stuck to the body. Net read is a generic grey woolly bovine loaf.
rows.fix: Replace the single tusk with a symmetrical pair of massive triangular-section horns leaving the brow sideways then sweeping back and up in a wide crescent to roughly the width of the body, and drop the head so the muzzle sits below the line of the shoulder.

rows.readsAs: a striped grey pony or a badly drawn zebra
rows.defect: Two of the three must-reads are wrong on screen. The head is not a heavy boxy cow-like skull -- it is a flat pale oval disc held out horizontally from the neck, painted with dark bars, reading as a mask or shield plate rather than a head, and its horns are the same single pale tusk borrowed from the buffalo and yak instead of paired hooks curving out sideways. There is no shaggy chin beard and no neck mane; the dark bars over the neck and barrel read as zebra striping. The topline is level, so the high withers sloping down to a low rump is absent too, and a large pale plume disc hangs off the rump. A stranger names this a striped pony.
rows.fix: Rebuild the head as a long deep box-shaped skull hanging low off a maned neck, with a visible beard hanging under the chin and two dark horns that leave the top of the skull sideways then hook up, and raise the withers so the back slopes down to the hips.

rows.readsAs: a shaggy brown highland cow or yak
rows.defect: The best asset here -- the long hair pass over the flanks genuinely reads -- but the curtain stops well above the ground, ending at mid-shin and leaving four bare pegs and hooves fully exposed, so the signature skirt-to-the-ground silhouette is lost. The humped shoulder is not visible: the topline runs flat from neck to rump with only a faint darker patch where the hump should be, and the head is carried high and level rather than slung low. The tail is the family's pasted-on horizontal fan-and-disc rather than a bushy plume dropping from the rump, and the horn is again the single shared ivory tusk instead of a symmetrical pair.
rows.fix: Extend the flank hair down past the hocks so it nearly touches the ground and hides the upper legs, and raise a distinct hair-covered withers hump so the neck and head fall away below it.

rows.readsAs: a striped paper-lantern jellyfish with two cat eyes
rows.defect: The W-shaped pupils are genuinely there and correct — the best-observed feature in the batch — and a dark fin ellipse does run the full mantle length behind the body. But the fin is a flat backdrop plate, not an undulating skirt: it has no wave, no edge modulation, and does not attach to the mantle anywhere I can see. The arms are six or seven thin dangling twigs of near-equal length with teardrop tips, so the eight-arms-plus-two-longer-tentacles split does not read; nothing has a sucker. The mantle is a front-on ellipse about 1.4 wide, not the broad flattened aspect-2 cuttlebone body, and the vertical stripes read as lantern ribs rather than chromatophore banding.
rows.fix: Turn the body side-on to a true 2:1 flattened oval and redraw the fin as a narrow scalloped ribbon whose wave crests are visible along the whole mantle edge, then thicken the two feeding tentacles to twice the arms' width so the 8+2 split is countable.

rows.readsAs: a red balloon with a cartoon face and spider legs
rows.defect: All three must-reads miss. The eyes are inset in the middle of the red bulb as two small black dots with catchlights, so the bulb reads as a HEAD with a face — precisely the error the packet note warns about; the mantle never sits above the eyes and there is no head/arm crown beneath it. The arms are about seven smooth hairlines with no taper, no mass and not one sucker, splaying in a symmetric fan; unequal length is not expressible when every limb is the same wire. The pupil is a plain round dot with no horizontal slit. The dark lobes flanking the bulb read as ears, which an octopus does not have. Beyond its own row it is pixel-for-pixel the Octopus card in a redder hue.
rows.fix: Drop the eyes out of the bulb onto a distinct head mass below it, and redraw the arms as thick tapering cones with a visible double row of sucker discs on the near face of the two front arms.

rows.readsAs: the same red balloon-and-threads octopus as the Giant Octopus card, with two long strings added
rows.defect: Nothing here says giant squid. The mantle is a plump egg roughly 1.4 tall, not the aspect-5.5 torpedo the row demands, and the fins are the same soft rounded ear-lobes that appear on every other card in this batch, flanking the mantle's upper flank rather than forming a small triangular pair at a pointed tail. The dinner-plate eyes — the one feature that IS this animal — are two pinprick black dots with catchlights, smaller relative to the body than a housecat's. The two feeding tentacles with knobbed tips are present and are the only correct element. Stood next to the Giant Octopus card it is the identical silhouette in the identical red; a stranger would name it octopus.
rows.fix: Stretch the mantle to a true 5:1 torpedo with a sharp tail-end triangular fin pair and blow the eyes up to at least a quarter of the mantle's width so the head-lamp scale reads instantly.
rows.verifyWhy:
UPHELD, with two of the stated causes corrected. Measured on the 440x440 PNG (background-subtracted row extents, plus 4x/6x zooms of the mantle and the eye region).

WHAT IS ACTUALLY THERE. The creature is drawn upright, mantle up / arms down, so the posterior tail tip is the TOP of the frame. The mantle is a plain vertical egg: apex at y=31, body running to y~170 where the arms attach, constant width x=175-273 (98px) through the whole lower two-thirds. Body length 135px / width 98px = aspect 1.38. The reference row demands aspect 5.5. That is a 4x miss and it is the dominant defect - there is no torpedo, no taper, and the apex is a smoothly rounded dome (width goes 8px at y=31 to 72px by y=57, an egg's narrow end), not a point. A pale grey rim-light arc runs over the top-right of the egg; it is a highlight, not a fin or a tail.

THE FINS. Confirmed absent as specified. What is drawn is ONE wide flat ellipse painted BEHIND the mantle so only its two side lobes show - it spans y=58 to y=109 (51px tall, 38% of mantle length) and reaches x=150 to x=297 at its widest (y=81-82), protruding ~23px past the mantle edge on each side. The width profile down those rows (80, 92, 118, 134, 144, 148, 142, 124, 100) is a smooth ellipse - rounded lobes, not triangles, which would show linear flanks and a hard cut. Critically, the lobes are centred 51px BELOW the apex and their top edge starts 27px below it, so they sit on the upper flank and never touch the tail end. The judge's description of this (rounded ear-lobes on the upper flank rather than a small triangular pair at a pointed tail) is exactly right, and it is the batch's shared part - Giant Octopus carries the identical ellipse behind its bulb, where an octopus should have no fins at all.

THE EYES - JUDGE'S DESCRIPTION IS WRONG, VERDICT STILL STANDS. They are NOT pinprick dots. At 6x they are solid round black discs ~13-14px across, each with a 5x5px white specular highlight (highlight clusters measured at x195-199 and x243-247, y170-174). The judge appears to have measured the 5px highlight rather than the 14px disc. But the must-read is 'dinner-plate eyes' - the single feature that IS this animal - and 14px on a 98px-wide mantle is 14% of mantle width, the batch's generic bead eye, identical in kind to the ones on Octopus and Giant Octopus. Architeuthis needs an eye roughly a third of the head. So the must-read fails on scale, not on absence. Related structural point the judge did not raise: the eyes are painted low on the mantle face, and there is no distinct head between mantle and arm crown at all.

THE TENTACLES - CORRECT, AS THE JUDGE ALLOWED. About 9-10 limbs cross a scanline at y=230-260. Two central limbs run past every other limb down to y=408 and terminate in distinct round 21px-wide knobs at (~136,405) and (~311,405); the remaining thin arms trail off around y=300-315. They are only modestly longer than the splayed side arms rather than 'far longer', and carry no toothed-club detail, but the clubbed pair reads.

CORRECTION TO 'READS AS THE GIANT OCTOPUS RECOLOURED'. The twin is not Giant Octopus - it is SQUID, and the relationship is stronger than a recolour of a cousin: Giant_Squid.png and Squid.png share a PIXEL-IDENTICAL mantle-plus-fin silhouette, translated 24px in x and recoloured dark red instead of pink. Row extents match within 1px at every row from y=34 to y=172 (GS 150-297 vs SQ 174-322 at y=82; GS 175-273 vs SQ 199-298 at y=112-130; solid-body span y=33-167 and max width 148 vs 149 at y=81 in both). Their reference rows demand aspect 5.5 and 3.2 respectively, so one silhouette cannot serve both. Giant Octopus is genuinely a different (rounder, lower-set, wider) bulb - it shares the fin ellipse and the bead eyes, but it is not the source of this trace.

FAIL stands: two of three must-reads are absent or wrong at the scale that defines them, the required aspect is off by 4x, and the asset is a translate-and-recolour of another species in the same batch. Fix order: (1) stretch the mantle to a true 5.5 torpedo with a pointed posterior; (2) replace the ellipse-behind-body with a genuine triangular fin pair sited AT the tail apex; (3) enlarge the eyes to dinner-plate scale at the arm-crown junction; (4) give Squid and Giant Squid different silhouettes.

rows.readsAs: a coiled cream rope, or an ammonite fossil
rows.defect: The render is headless — there is no animal. Not one of the dozens of short tentacles is drawn, there is no leathery hood, and there is no opening: the spiral simply closes on itself. The only thing near the aperture is a stray flat translucent grey disc stranded half off the shell's right edge and a faint grey circle overlapping the coil, both of which read as render debris rather than a body. The shell itself is wrong too: it is a rope of overlapping identical scallops wound like a cinnamon roll, with no septa, no widening whorl and no red-brown flame striping at all — it is uniform cream.
rows.fix: Open the outer whorl into a real aperture and fan thirty-plus short suckerless tentacles out of it under a dark leathery hood, then stripe the outer whorl with radiating red-brown flames.
rows.verifyWhy:
UPHELD, with three corrections to the stated cause. I read the 440x440 PNG at 1x, then re-cropped and magnified four regions (right flank 230,190 140x140 @4x; whole shell 90,90 260x260 @3x; aperture zone 240,240 100x100 @6x; left flank 60,90 160x260 @3x) and ran a colour histogram over every non-background pixel.

WHAT IS ACTUALLY THERE: one coiled spiral occupying the centre of the frame, a soft dark elliptical drop shadow beneath it, one flat grey ellipse at roughly 4-5 o'clock on the shell's outer edge, and a stray thin pale circular outline stroke.

MUST-READ 1 - 'coiled chambered shell striped with red-brown flames': FAILS on two of three counts. Coiled: yes. Chambered: no - there is not a single septum, chamber wall or growth line anywhere. The whorl is built from a chain of ~90 discrete overlapping crescent lobes laid transverse across the coil, each identical in shape, which reads as twisted rope or a scalloped pastry, not as a shell tube. Striped: absent, and this is measurable - of 33,047 non-background pixels, ZERO satisfy (r-b > 45 && r > 90). The entire palette is desaturated cream/bone/warm-grey: modal buckets rgb~(144,144,128), (160,160,144), (224,208,192), (128,128,112). There is no red, no brown, no flame anywhere in the file.

CORRECTION TO THE CLAIM #1 - 'no widening whorl' is WRONG. The whorl does widen, and correctly: lobe width grows from roughly 4px at the centre knob to roughly 40px at the rim across about 3.5 visible turns, a proper logarithmic expansion. The spiral rate is not the defect. The defect is that the expanding band is rendered as a rope of repeated scallop lobes instead of a smooth tapering tube with septal divisions. A fixer told 'the whorl does not widen' would change the wrong parameter.

CORRECTION TO THE CLAIM #2 - the grey disc is not stranded random debris, it is the soft body, drawn as an unmodulated blob. It sits exactly where the aperture belongs (outer whorl, lower-right, centred ~x300 y275 in 440-space, about 60x45px). At 6x it is a uniform mid-grey ellipse with a soft blurred edge and ZERO internal structure: no tentacle divisions, no fan, no hood lip, no eye, no aperture rim, no darker interior. It is also composited ON TOP of the shell face rather than emerging from an opening, so it occludes the outer whorl instead of being framed by it. The judge's READ of it as render debris is exactly right; the CAUSE is a soft-body element that never got its geometry.

MUST-READ 2 - 'dozens of short tentacles fanning from the opening': ABSENT. The packet note calls for around ninety small suckerless tentacles. Zero tentacles exist. I checked the left flank and bottom separately in case they were drawn on the far side; the background outside the shell disc is empty except for the grey ellipse and the drop shadow.

MUST-READ 3 - 'leathery hood over the head': ABSENT. No hood, no head, no pinhole eye. There is no aperture for a hood to sit over.

CORRECTION TO THE CLAIM #3 - the judge missed a second piece of debris. A thin pale blue-white circular outline stroke, radius slightly larger than the shell, is drawn unclipped OVER the whole asset: it enters top-left, arcs across the top of the shell, runs down the right side and exits bottom-left. It is visible in every crop and reads as an unclipped bounding-circle stroke that escaped into the render.

BAND: FAIL stands. Two of three must-reads are wholly absent (tentacles, hood), the third is present only as 'a coil' with its two qualifying features (chambers, red-brown flames) both missing. The asset reads as a coiled cream rope or a ribbed ammonite fossil with a grey smudge on it, not as a nautilus. FIX ORDER: (1) cut the aperture - terminate the outer whorl in a real opening with a dark interior; (2) build the soft body in that opening: leathery hood as a domed flap, dense fan of short tentacles below it, pinhole eye at the hood's lower edge; (3) replace the rope lobes with a smooth tapering whorl carrying septal lines; (4) paint red-brown flame striping radiating from the umbilicus outward across the dorsal whorl, fading to white on the ventral side; (5) delete the stray bounding-circle stroke.

rows.readsAs: a salmon balloon with a cute dot-eyed face and six threads
rows.defect: Same three misses as the Giant Octopus card. The eyes sit inside the bulb, so the mantle reads as a head and the note's warning is violated. Only about six arms are visible, all identical hairline strokes with no taper and not a single sucker anywhere; two sweep wide to the frame edges and the rest hang straight, giving a symmetric daddy-longlegs fan rather than a boneless eight-arm crown. The pupils are round black dots with white catchlights — no horizontal slit. The dark ear-lobes behind the bulb are cephalopod-inaccurate. It is the Giant Octopus image recoloured.
rows.fix: Give the arms real volume — thick at the crown, tapering to a curl, with a visible sucker row — and move the eye pair down onto a head bulge beneath the mantle bag.

rows.readsAs: a pink octopus with two extra long knob-tipped strings
rows.defect: The two long clubbed tentacles read clearly and are correct. Everything else misses: the mantle is a plump egg, not a torpedo, and nowhere near the stated 3.2 aspect; the fins are the batch's standard soft rounded ear-lobes set on the mantle's upper flank instead of a triangular pair at a pointed rear; and the eyes are two tiny dots placed high on the mantle rather than a large eye at the base of the arms. The eight arms are again featureless hairlines with no suckers and no taper. It is the Giant Squid card in pink.
rows.fix: Redraw the mantle as a pointed torpedo with a terminal triangular fin pair, and enlarge the eyes and drop them to the arm crown where the mantle meets the head.

rows.readsAs: a small cloaked deep-sea cephalopod — the only card here that names its own animal
rows.defect: The webbed cloak joining the arms is present and genuinely reads as a cape, the ear-like flap fins on the mantle are there, and the huge glowing red-orange eye is the strongest eye in the batch. The defect is that there is only ONE eye: the mantle, ears and cape are drawn bilaterally symmetric and dead front-on, so the missing second eye reads as cyclopean deformity rather than as a three-quarter view. The cape's lower edge is scalloped into shell-like lobes that read as a clam rather than a webbed membrane, the arm tips do not emerge past the web anywhere, and the whole animal sits small in a large empty frame.
rows.fix: Add the matching second eye on the right side of the mantle at the same scale, and replace the scalloped clam edge with a smooth membrane through which the eight arm tips show as ribs.

rows.readsAs: a pink fish — a salmon or trout in side view
rows.defect: The identity must-read is entirely absent: there is NO long narrow tweezer beak and no teeth. At 8x the head simply tapers to a sharp fish point, with a straight taper where the bulging melon should be, so there is no rostrum/melon break at all. The eye is a large glossy round fish eye, not the tiny reduced eye of a river dolphin. The tail is a symmetric vertically forked fish caudal fin, not a horizontal fluke. The pectoral is a dark ellipse hanging fully below the belly line, unattached. The blowhole is a grey ellipse floating in open water above and clear of the topline — a stranded fragment. The dorsal is a detached oval blob sitting on the back rather than a low ridge blended into the topline.
rows.fix: Rebuild the head: extend a long, thin, parallel-sided beak forward for roughly a third of the head length with a fine tooth comb along it, and set it off with a distinct rounded melon dome rising behind it — then reseat the blowhole into that dome and turn the caudal into a broad horizontal fluke blade.

rows.readsAs: a large grey fish
rows.defect: The packet's own note says the flukes must be horizontal and never vertical like a fish — and they are drawn as a vertical fish caudal fin: two equal lobes above and below the axis with a concave notch, confirmed at 8x, and undersized relative to the body. The flippers must-read fails too: one short rounded dark ellipse drooping below the belly line, not a long paddle. The render is also broken at the head — the pale rim-light stroke has divorced from the silhouette, arcing well above and in front of the snout and terminating in mid-air as a stranded hairline in empty black. The snout comes to a sharp point rather than a blunt baleen rostrum, and the blowhole ellipse sits off the topline rather than in the head.
rows.fix: Replace the forked caudal with a wide horizontal fluke blade — a shallow crescent with a central notch, drawn broad and flat across the tailstock — and clamp the rim-light stroke to the body path so it cannot overshoot the snout.

rows.readsAs: a generic grey bream or moonfish; a plain silver disc fish with no face
rows.defect: Two of three must-reads are simply not drawn. The flat square human-like teeth — the entire reason anyone recognises a pacu — are absent; there is no mouth at all, not even a line. The blunt steep forehead with underslung jaw is absent too: the head tapers to a smooth point identical to Tetra's and Piranha's, so there is no forehead plane and no jaw to be underslung. What remains is the shared lens body in grey with hatched scale texture, and it is a lens rather than a coin (too long and pointed to read as the round compressed disc the reference asks for).
rows.fix: Cut the pointed rostrum back into a steep near-vertical forehead that drops to a small terminal mouth set low on the snout, and draw the mouth open enough to show a visible row of broad flat white square teeth — the human-teeth read must be legible at thumbnail size or the species has no identity.

rows.readsAs: a piranha — the tooth row carries it, but it is a toothy generic disc fish rather than a piranha's head
rows.defect: The teeth are present and do sell the species, but they are pasted onto the outside of the shared silhouette as a long saw of eight triangles running from below the eye diagonally down past mid-belly — that is a serrated keel, not a jaw. There is no jaw line, no mouth aperture and no gape for them to sit in, so they float outside the body edge. The undershot jutting lower jaw is absent entirely and the steep blunt forehead is absent: the head is the same smooth taper to a point as Pacu and Tetra. The deep chunky body is the one must-read genuinely satisfied.
rows.fix: Build an actual head — break the snout with a steep forehead and push a chunky lower jaw forward past the upper lip, then set the triangular teeth inside that gape as a short bite line at the front of the head instead of a saw running along the belly.

rows.readsAs: a small teal disc fish — closer to a cichlid or a generic aquarium fish than to a tetra
rows.defect: The bright lateral stripe from eye to tail, which is the whole identity of a tetra, is not there. The only horizontal feature is a faint darker shading line across the mid-flank that stops short of both the eye and the tail and has no contrast against the body; because the entire fish is flooded the same cyan, nothing reads as a stripe at all. The tiny adipose fin behind the dorsal is absent — there is no second dorsal element anywhere on the topline. The silhouette is also the shared deep lens at roughly 1.5:1 rather than the slimmer 2.5 aspect the reference calls for, and the body is saturated cyan rather than silvery, so 'small deep-bodied silvery fish' only half lands.
rows.fix: Slim the body toward the specified 2.5 aspect, drop the flank to silver, and lay a single high-contrast stripe (neon blue over red, or at minimum one bright band) running unbroken from the eye to the caudal base, then add the small adipose nub between the dorsal and the tail.

rows.readsAs: a generic pointed leaf-shaped fish decal with a paper crown taped to its back and a tail fin floating separately behind it — closer to a sunfish clipart or a leaf than to a tilapia
rows.defect: The caudal fin is fully DETACHED: a rounded grey fan sits in open background with a clear gap between it and the body's rear point, and a thin dark line runs vertically through it and off both top and bottom edges — a stranded fragment plus a stray stroke. The blunt steep forehead must-read is absent: the head end tapers to a sharp point exactly mirroring the tail end, with the eye sitting almost on the snout tip. The dorsal must-read is wrong too — instead of a long spiny fin running the whole back it is a flat opaque sawtooth block covering only the middle ~45% of the topline, floating above the outline with background visible under part of its base and one spike hanging off the body edge. The body is a lens, not a deep laterally flattened disc, and there are no pelvic or anal fins; the pectoral is a grey chevron that reads as a rendering glitch.
rows.fix: Rebuild the silhouette so the caudal fin joins a real peduncle at the rear of the body (no gap, no stray stroke), give the head end a short blunt vertical forehead so the snout stops mirroring the tail, and replace the floating sawtooth plate with a spiny dorsal whose membrane is anchored to and runs the full length of the topline from nape to peduncle.

rows.readsAs: a spotted goat or fawn - an appaloosa pony with leopard blotches
rows.defect: The must-read 'low elongated body on short legs' is absent and inverted: the barrel is deep and slab-sided and it stands on four LONG straight columnar legs whose dark feet are cloven hooves with toe scores, not paws. Belly clearance is roughly a full body depth. The 'masked face' is not a pair of bands through the eyes but one enormous solid black disc painted over the cheek plus a second dark ring around the actual eye, which reads as panda blotching. The ringed tail is the only civet cue present, and it hangs off the rump of a hoofstock body.
rows.fix: Rebuild on a viverrid chassis: halve the leg length, drop the belly to about a quarter of body depth, stretch the trunk to a low tube with a slight lumbar arch, and replace the hooves with short plantigrade paws showing four toes; then repaint the mask as two dark bars running through the eye onto the muzzle rather than a solid disc.

rows.readsAs: an armless tan sack balanced on one leg - a bowling pin with a snout
rows.defect: The render is anatomically broken: at 8x on the chest there are NO forelimbs at all - no shoulder, no arm, no hands - the torso is one smooth featureless bag from throat to groin, and only a SINGLE hind leg is drawn, ending in the same dark cloven hoof used on the Civet and Mongoose. Neither remaining must-read survives: there are no dark rings around the eyes (the eye is a plain pale-blue bead on bare cream fur), and the tail is a flat uniform tan tube with a blunt rounded end and no black tip, hanging free beside the leg rather than propping as the third leg of a tripod. The ears are large brown blobs on TOP of the skull, not small and low on the sides.
rows.fix: Draw the tripod: two short forelimbs tucked against the chest with visible paws, two hind legs planted with clawed digitigrade feet, and the tail angled back to touch the ground with a black terminal third; then add the dark orbital rings.

rows.readsAs: a long-bodied white goat or a shaggy sheep-dog on hooves
rows.defect: The must-read that IS the identity - a very long LOW tubular body on SHORT legs - is absent. The trunk is long but it is a deep shaggy fleece-textured barrel carried high on four long columnar legs with dark cloven hooves, so the animal is tall rather than ground-hugging. The tail is not a thick tail tapering to a point: it is a short bushy squirrel plume stuck horizontally off the croup, blunt at the end and paler than the body. The head is the identical wedge skull, brown ear-blob, blue bead eye and smile line used on the Civet and Meerkat, which gives a generic muzzle rather than the fine pointed herpestid snout.
rows.fix: Cut the leg length by more than half so the belly nearly grazes the ground, slim the barrel into a straight low tube of even depth, swap the hooves for small five-toed paws, and redraw the tail as a thick continuous cone tapering smoothly from the rump to a fine point.

rows.readsAs: a needlefish or a juvenile gar — a slender silver fish with a long wire beak
rows.defect: The must-read is a short pointed CONICAL snout that overhangs the mouth. What is drawn is a hairline needle spike projecting roughly a fifth of the body length past the head, no thicker than a drawn line, with no taper and no jaw beneath it. That single prop moves the animal into a different family: a stranger reads needlefish/houndfish, never bonefish. The flank is also not plain mirror-silver — it carries the same diamond+dot scale mesh as the other two — and the caudal fork is shallow, not the deep sharp fork the row calls for.
rows.fix: Delete the wire spike and replace it with a short fleshy cone: a snout about one head-length long that tapers with visible volume and clearly overhangs an inferior mouth set back underneath it, then deepen the tail notch to a true deep fork and strip the scale mesh off the flank so it reads as plain polished mirror.

rows.readsAs: a generic silver perch or bass with a stray grey bubble stuck to its face
rows.defect: The identity must-read — a blunt, FLAT-TOPPED head — is absent: the head is the family cone, tapering to a single sharp point at the nose exactly like the Bonefish and Tarpon, with no flat crown and no squared-off muzzle. Worse, a translucent grey ellipse floats off the front of the mouth, unattached to the silhouette and overlapping the snout tip; it reads as a render artifact, not anatomy. The two widely separated dorsal fins are present only as two faint ghost lobes so pale and so rounded they read as smudges rather than fins, and the faint body stripes are entirely missing.
rows.fix: Rebuild the head as a broad flat-topped wedge with a squared blunt muzzle and a tiny triangular mouth at the very front, remove the floating grey ellipse, and redraw the two dorsals as opaque, clearly separated fins — a small spiny triangle forward and a soft-rayed one well behind it.

rows.readsAs: a generic deep-bodied silver fish — a shad or a herring, nothing more specific
rows.defect: All three must-reads fail. The huge silver-dollar plate scales are rendered as the same small diamond-and-dot mesh used on the Bonefish and Mullet, so the scale that defines a tarpon has no distinct size at all. The upturned bulldog lower jaw is absent — the mouth line slants DOWNWARD to the same pointed family cone, the opposite of the signature scooped, jutting lower jaw. And the long trailing filament off the rear of the dorsal, the single most recognisable tarpon feature, is nowhere on the image: the dorsal is just a dark triangular shadow on the back with a clean trailing edge.
rows.fix: Add the trailing dorsal filament first — a long whip streaming back from the rear of the dorsal nearly to the tail — then rotate the mouth so the lower jaw juts up and forward past the upper, and blow the flank scales up to large overlapping discs roughly a third of body depth so the plate armour reads at thumbnail size.

rows.readsAs: A generic pink-flowered garden herb — lavender, heather, or oregano; nobody would say sea grape or even name it a coastal tree
rows.defect: Every must-read is missing and the wrong ones are substituted. The leaves are small narrow lance-shaped leaflets, dozens of them in near-opposite pairs along wiry stems — the exact opposite of the large round leathery dinner-plate alternate leaves that ARE the sea grape's identity; there is no red venation anywhere and no orange-red older leaf. The harvest is rendered as five upright terminal mauve-pink pompom flower heads sitting on top of the stems, where the reference calls for long DANGLING strings of round grape-like fruit — nothing hangs in this image at all. The habit is a narrow upright vase/broom taller than wide, fanning from one thin basal trunk, which contradicts the low windswept spreading coastal shrub the note explicitly warns about; the thin whippy stems even read as the vine the note says it is not.
rows.fix: Rebuild the plant from the leaf outward: a low wide-spreading stout woody shrub with a few thick crooked branches, each bearing a small number of very large flat circular leathery leaf plates with heart-shaped bases and bold red-pink midrib and veins (a couple turning orange-red), and hang two or three long pendulous strands of round green-to-purple berries down from the branch joints — drop the terminal flower pompoms and the small lance leaflets entirely.

rows.readsAs: a plump brown grub or bumblebee abdomen with two horns — a soft segmented balloon-bug, not a cockroach
rows.defect: Two of the three must-reads are simply absent. (1) No flat glossy oval wing-covers: the dorsum is an inflated barrel of two ballooning segments ringed by pale outlined hoops, fully three-dimensional and rounded in section, with no tegmina oval and no central seam. (2) No shield-shaped pronotum hiding the head: the largest volume in the whole render IS an exposed spherical head with a visible bead eye on it, which inverts the identity — the roach's head must be concealed under a flat plate. (3) The antennae read but are wrong: two short, thick, rigid dark rods angled forward and upward, not long threadlike whips trailing back over the body. On top of the missing must-reads there is loose geometry: a fan of pale radiating filaments streams off the rear like a shrimp tail-fan or a wing spray, a stray pale outlined arc floats detached above the rear dorsum attached to nothing, and the legs are five unbent parallel sticks (three raked together at the front, two at the back) with no joints, no spines and no visible attachment to a thorax.
rows.fix: Rebuild the body as a single low flat oval: collapse the sphere-plus-barrels into one shallow ellipse whose top surface is nearly planar with a specular glossy highlight, draw a centre seam where the two tegmina overlap, lay a separate darker shield-shaped pronotal plate over the front third so the head is not visible at all from above (delete the bead eye on the dome), delete the rear filament fan and the floating arc, and replace the stick legs with six spined two-segment legs whose femora splay out sideways beyond the shell outline.

rows.readsAs: A generic gold-tan pointed-oval bait fish with a paddle stuck on the back end; nobody says cod.
rows.defect: At 10x the chin is a bare knife point - no mouth, no jawline and NO BARBEL, which is the one thing that makes a cod a cod. The back carries only TWO rounded lobes, not three separate dorsal fins, and both are drawn behind the body so they read as shadows. The lateral line is a straight pale stroke, not a curved one. The tail is a rounded blocky trapezoid separated from the body point by a dark seam so it reads detached, and a stray thin diagonal stroke runs straight through the tail and out into empty background above and below it - a render artifact. The white eye ring sits half outside the topline.
rows.fix: Draw a single thick barbel hanging down from the chin and split the back into three clearly separated dorsal fins in front of the outline, not behind it.

rows.readsAs: A generic grey pointed-oval fish; reads closer to a small silver minnow than a haddock.
rows.defect: The dark thumbprint blotch above the pectoral - the single feature that identifies a haddock - is completely absent; the only dark area is the same generic mid-flank shading blob that Cod and Pollock also carry. The lateral line is drawn PALE WHITE, the opposite of the required black line. The first dorsal is a low rounded ellipse half hidden behind the body, not tall and not pointed, and there are only two dorsal lobes instead of three. Head is the same mouthless knife point as the other two, and the eye ring straddles the topline.
rows.fix: Paint a hard dark thumbprint blotch on the shoulder just above the pectoral fin and switch the lateral line stroke to black.

rows.readsAs: An elongated olive-green fish with a pale side stripe and a forked tail - plausibly a pollock to a fisherman, just 'a fish' to a stranger.
rows.defect: The olive-green back and the pale lateral line are genuinely present and legible, but the fin architecture and the jaw are not. The snout is a symmetric knife point with no mouth drawn at all, so the protruding lower jaw is absent. There are two rounded dorsal lobes rather than three separate dorsals, and one anal lobe rather than two, and every one of them is drawn behind the body outline so it half disappears. The white eye ring is punched through the topline and sits partly outside the silhouette.
rows.fix: Cut the underslung lower jaw into the snout so it juts past the upper lip, and draw three dorsals plus two anals as separate fins in front of the body outline.

rows.readsAs: a generic green coiled cartoon snake
rows.defect: The blotching is INVERTED - pale washed-out light spots scattered over olive instead of the required dark oval blotches, so the signature anaconda pattern is absent. The eye is a huge lateral white lollipop with a vertical slit set on the SIDE of the head, not the small eye set high on top of the skull the reference demands, and no nostrils read at all. Body is reasonably thick but is a constant-diameter tube with no muscular swell.
rows.fix: Repaint the pattern as dark olive-black oval blotches (darker than the base) and move the eye and nostrils onto the dorsal surface of the head so both are visible from above.

rows.readsAs: a plain brown coiled cartoon snake
rows.defect: The saddle blotches are present only as vague soft brown smudges with no defined saddle edges, and because the tail is buried inside the coil the required reddening toward the tail never reads. The head is the shared smooth oval - no heavy arrow shape, no widened jaw, and no dark eye stripe anywhere. The body does not taper.
rows.fix: Give the saddles hard-edged dark outlines that grow rust-red along a visible tail that exits the coil, and rebuild the head as a broad arrow with a dark stripe running from eye to jaw angle.

rows.readsAs: a plain sand-coloured rope, no species at all
rows.defect: The net-like geometric pattern that IS the identity of this animal is completely absent - the body is a flat unmarked khaki tube with only faint tonal shading, so there is nothing on it to name. No heat-sensing pit row along the lips is visible; the lip line is blank. The coils do not overlap heavily, they lie in one flat spiral doughnut.
rows.fix: Paint an actual reticulated net - dark chain-link outlines enclosing pale diamond centres - across the entire body, and add a visible row of dark pits along the upper and lower lip.
rows.verifyWhy:
Verified at native 440x440 plus 7x/10x zooms of the head and a 2nd/98th-percentile contrast stretch of the whole coil. VERDICT UPHELD, but two parts of the original claim are wrong and the real causes are different.

CORRECTION 1 - the blotches are NOT 'entirely absent'. Under contrast stretch there ARE roughly six to eight soft round darker spots scattered over the coils (clearest on the upper-left of the outer coil near px 113,162, two on the inner right coil near px 250-260,225-245, one lower-left). Pixel probe: blotch centre reads 130,112,74 against surrounding body 154,131,85 - a delta of about 24/255, roughly 15% darker, with a soft airbrushed edge. At 1:1 they are effectively invisible and read as dirt/AO smudges, not markings. So the correct statement is: a pattern layer EXISTS but is drawn at ~15% contrast and in the wrong geometry - isolated round dots, sparsely and randomly placed, with no chain, no interlocking, no pale-edged network. The reticulated net that is this animal's identity is not there. The fix is not 'add a pattern layer', it is 'raise this species' pattern amplitude and change its motif from scattered dots to a linked diamond/net lattice'.

CORRECTION 2 - it is not 'only faint tonal shading'. The dominant surface treatment is a dense band of transverse ribbing - 60+ crescent scute rings - that wraps the ENTIRE circumference of the body including the dorsal surface, from just behind the head all the way to the tail tip. Ventral scutes belong on the belly only; here they are painted over the top of every coil, and their high local contrast is what actually drowns the (already weak) blotch layer. This ribbing is the loudest thing on the asset and any pattern fix has to contend with it or reduce it to the ventral arc.

CONFIRMED - no heat-pit row. Correct, and it is worse than described: the head has no mouth line, no lip seam, no labial scale row and no nostril at all. It is a bare, flat, untextured khaki ellipse (10x stretch shows a smooth gradient with zero internal detail). There is literally no lip for the pit row to sit on, so this is a missing-feature problem, not a too-faint problem.

OTHER DEFECTS THE ORIGINAL JUDGE DID NOT NAME:
- The eye violates the row's 'eyes: small'. It is a large white sclera oval with a black vertical slit pupil, occupying roughly a fifth of the visible head ellipse - a cartoon eye, oversized for the head. The vertical slit itself is correct for a python.
- The forked red tongue is DETACHED: it starts about 8px in front of the snout tip with a clear gap of background between it and the head, and since there is no mouth it floats in space.
- The head is a 2D ellipse pasted on the neck, with a hard elliptical edge and no jaw, no snout taper and no skull volume.

FAMILY-CHASSIS EVIDENCE (the strongest argument that this is a fixable per-species failure, not an engine limit): Anaconda and Boa in the same batch use the IDENTICAL chassis - same flat spiral coil with the tail crossing inside, same ellipse head at the same angle, same detached red fork tongue, same full-circumference ribbing. But BOTH of them carry pattern that reads at 1:1: Boa shows dark reddish saddles plus pale spots, Anaconda shows clear pale ovals. So the generator can and does draw legible markings on this exact body; Python alone got a near-zero-contrast dot layer. Python is the family member whose pattern channel is turned almost off.

WHAT IT READS AS: a smooth sand/khaki rope-thick tube with heavy belly-scute ribbing over its whole surface and a featureless spade head. Two of three must-reads (net-like geometric blotched pattern; heat-pit row along the lips) fail outright. Only 'heavy-bodied overlapping coils' partially reads - the coils do overlap and the body is moderately thick, though nearer rope than python girth. FAIL stands.

rows.readsAs: the same coiled cartoon snake as the other three, in gold
rows.defect: Reference says crawling at aspect 3.5 and the render is the identical coiled doughnut used for the other three, only with a slightly fatter tube - the short stubby proportion never reads because the animal is wound into a ring of the same overall length. The blunt wedge snout is absent (same pointed lozenge head as the rest), the eyes are the same big lateral lollipops rather than tiny upward-facing dots, and the abruptly blunt stub tail is hidden inside the coil so the defining head-and-tail-look-alike trait is invisible.
rows.fix: Redraw it uncoiled and crawling, half-buried in sand, as a short fat sausage with a shovel-wedge snout, pinprick eyes on TOP of the head, and a blunt stub tail clearly visible at the far end.
rows.verifyWhy:
UPHELD as FAIL, but two parts of the stated cause need correcting and one part needs sharpening.

WHAT I SAW. Full 440x440 render plus 6x nearest-neighbour crops of the head (255,170,120x90), the coil interior (70,110,200x180) and the doughnut hole (120,150,140x110), and the same head crop taken from Boa, Python and Anaconda for direct comparison.

SHARED CHASSIS - CONFIRMED, AND IT IS THE WHOLE FAMILY. All four constrictors are the identical generated torus: ~1.5 turns of scaled tube, hole in the upper-middle, head emerging from the lower-right at the same angle, identical forked red tongue at the same offset, identical eye asset. Only hue, blotching and tube diameter change. The Sand Boa is NOT a pixel clone though - correcting the judge here - its doughnut hole is actually WIDER than Boa's and Anaconda's (72-92px across at y=190-205 vs Boa 54-66, Anaconda 46-72), so it is the same generator run with a fatter tube parameter, not a recolour.

THE PROPORTION - JUDGE IS RIGHT, AND HERE IS THE NUMBER. Left-limb tube thickness measured on a vertical scan at x=95: Sand Boa 77px, Python 64, Boa 62, Anaconda 46. Overall bbox: Sand Boa 285x148 vs Boa 270x129. So it IS the fattest of the four, by ~20-24% over Boa at only ~5% larger overall footprint, i.e. roughly +18% relative girth. The reference row asks for aspect 3.5 against Boa/Python's 7 - a 2:1 change in length-to-girth. It got 18%. 'Thick stubby cylindrical body' therefore does not read: the tube is chunkier but still wraps a full 1.5 coils, which the eye integrates as a LONG snake tidily stacked, exactly like its three siblings.

SHARPENING THE JUDGE: the cleanest statement of this defect is not aspect, it is POSTURE. The row specifies posture 'crawling'; Anaconda, Boa and Python all specify 'coiled'. The Sand Boa is rendered on the coiled torus anyway. The posture token is simply not honoured by the renderer for this species. Fixing aspect alone on a coil will not produce a stubby read - the shape has to leave the doughnut and lie out as a short fat sausage before 3.5 can be seen at all.

SNOUT - JUDGE IS RIGHT. The head is the shared almond/lance ellipse tilted ~25 degrees down-right, tapering to a rounded POINT at the snout tip. Overlaid against the Boa and Python head crops the outline is the same curve, just scaled ~15-20% larger (consistent with headFrac 0.07 vs 0.05, so headFrac IS being applied). There is no blunt truncated wedge, no shovel-face, no countersunk lower jaw. The only extra mark on the head is a small brown blotch low on the jaw, which is body-pattern noise, not a nostril or a rostral scale.

EYE - JUDGE IS RIGHT. White sclera oval with a black vertical slit pupil, set laterally on the mid-upper face, roughly a quarter of the head's length. It is the same eye asset Boa, Python and Anaconda carry. Row asks eyes:small and 'tiny upward-facing eyes'; neither the size nor the dorsal placement is present. One nuance in the asset's favour: a vertical slit pupil is not itself wrong for a sand boa - it is the SIZE and the lateral placement that fail, so a fix should shrink the eye and move it onto the dorsal surface rather than change the pupil shape.

TAIL - JUDGE IS PARTLY WRONG. It is not fully 'buried'. Inside the doughnut hole, at roughly (150-185, 195-215), the inner tube does terminate in a visible pale rounded cap against the left inner wall of the coil. So a tail END exists and is findable. But it is (a) heavily occluded by the outer coil, (b) the same generic rounded taper the three siblings' tails use, and (c) not abruptly truncated. The reference note - 'the tail is a stub, so head and tail ends look almost interchangeable' - is the thing that fails: the head end is unmistakably a head with eye and tongue, the tail end is an unreadable smudge behind a coil. The two ends could not be less interchangeable.

VERDICT. All three mustReads miss. Nothing in the silhouette distinguishes this from the Boa above it except a warmer sand hue and a moderately fatter tube; a viewer given the four side by side would not pick this one out as the short burrowing species. FAIL stands.

COLLATERAL, for the family sheet: the Anaconda is the THINNEST tube of the four at 46px, against a reference note demanding 'thick as a thigh, not a rope'. The girth parameter appears close to inverted across this family.

rows.readsAs: a kiwi, or a grey duckling with an orange carrot for a bill
rows.defect: The identity feature is absent: the bill is a dead-straight orange cone, not a slender strongly decurved crimson bill — it has no curvature whatsoever and reads as a carrot glued to the face. Plumage is mid-grey with heavy pale mottling and a grey scribble texture, so the glossy all-black requirement is not met; the bird is the lightest thing in the batch. The red legs are the only must-read present, and even those are two disembodied footprints floating in the air below the belly with no leg connecting them to the body. Silhouette is the shared legless egg with no neck.
rows.fix: Redraw the bill as a long thin arc curving smoothly downward through about 30 degrees in saturated crimson, and darken the body to near-black with a blue-violet gloss highlight so the red bill and red legs are the only warm marks on the bird.
rows.verifyWhy:
I looked at the PNG at full size and again at 4x/9x/10x crops of the head, the underbelly and the rump, and I measured pixels. The FAIL stands, but two of the three stated causes are described wrongly and the fix must be made against what is actually there.

MUST-READ 1 — 'slender curved red bill': GENUINELY ABSENT, judge correct and if anything understated. I scanned every red column of the bill and printed its top edge, bottom edge and midline: from x=101 (tip) to x=164 (base) the midline sits at y=166.5-167.0 in EVERY column. That is not 'nearly straight', it is zero curvature to the pixel. It is a symmetric isosceles wedge, 64px long and 10px thick at the base, tapering to a 1px point — a road cone, not a bill. Two further errors the judge did not name: (a) it is far too LONG — 64px against a head ball of ~42px diameter, i.e. 1.5x head width, which is ibis/kiwi proportion; a chough bill is roughly 1.2x head LENGTH and much finer. (b) the colour is orange-vermilion (sampled 217,58,18), not the coral-crimson of a chough. And it has no visible culmen/gonys split — it is one flat filled triangle with no mandible line. The decurve must be a real arc: drop the tip 8-10px below the base line with a smooth concave-down upper edge, halve the base thickness, shorten to ~1.1x head width, and shift hue toward crimson (~205,35,45).

MUST-READ 2 — 'bright red legs': THE JUDGE'S DESCRIPTION IS WRONG. They are NOT 'two footprints hovering unattached in the air below the belly'. I compared, column by column, the lowest body pixel against the highest red pixel: at x=218 bodyBottom=269/legTop=269, x=222 269/268, x=226 268/267, x=234 269/268, x=238 269/266, x=242 268/265 — the red overlaps or exactly meets the belly outline. They are attached, and in places they are tucked UP INTO the body. The real defect is the opposite of detachment: there is ZERO TARSUS. No leg column, no hock, no ankle — two flat red chevrons of toes are welded flush to the underside of the belly, so a species carded posture:biped has no legs at all and sits belly-on-the-ground. They are also drawn inside the black cast-shadow ellipse, which swallows what little contrast they have. Fix is to grow a tarsus (~18-22px of red column per side lifting the body clear of the shadow), not to 'reattach' anything.

MUST-READ 3 — 'glossy all-black crow-like plumage': 'mid-grey' IS WRONG. I took a luminance histogram over the whole body (8,550 opaque samples): p25=30, median=38, p75=47 out of 255 — RGB around 40,42,48, a cool near-black slate. The plumage IS essentially black. What actually fails is the SURFACE: it is covered in short pale grey hair-like streak strokes running to L=115, a dry mottled pelt texture with no specular highlight anywhere, so it reads as fur or as a kiwi's hair-feathers rather than as feathering with a wet gloss. The correction to make is 'kill the pale hair-streak mottling and add a broad specular sheen band', NOT 'darken it'.

WHAT THE JUDGE MISSED IN THE ASSET'S FAVOUR: there IS a tail. A pointed dark wedge with 4-5 faint rachis striations extends down-right off the rump around x=270-292, y=228-258. It is drawn at 15,16,19 against a 5,6,12 background, so it is nearly invisible at full size — but it exists and does not need to be added, only lifted in value.

OVERALL: silhouette is a near-circular ovoid ball (bbox 193x140 = aspect 1.38 against a carded 1.7), a small round head on almost no neck, a huge straight probing bill and no legs. Together that is a kiwi, and the judge's organism call is right. Two of the three must-reads (curved crimson bill, glossy feathering) do not read; the third (red legs) reads only as colour. FAIL upheld.

rows.readsAs: a Common Blackbird, or a charcoal duckling — a yellow-billed thrush, not a crow
rows.defect: Wrong organism. The bill is bright yellow-ochre; a crow's bill is black, and a dark bird with a yellow bill is the diagnostic read of a Eurasian Blackbird. It is also a short blunt triangle rather than a stout deep pointed crow bill. The plumage is charcoal-grey with grey mottled scribble, not all-black glossy. The square-tipped tail is absent — what is there is a thin grey spike tapering to a point off the right flank, in a different colour from the body. Feet are two yellow prints floating unattached under the belly and the body is a neckless egg.
rows.fix: Make the bill black, deep at the base and clearly longer than the head is wide, and rebuild the tail as a body-coloured fan of even-length feathers with a flat square end.
rows.verifyWhy:
I read the 440x440 PNG at full size and then again at 5x on three crops (head, tail, whole bird) and sampled pixel values. The FAIL stands, but two of the three stated causes are described wrong and must not be fixed as stated.

WHAT IS ACTUALLY THERE. A near-spherical, hen/quail-dumpy body with a small round head sitting directly on it (no neck). Bill: bright saffron-yellow, sampled 224,177,60 at (125,158). CORRECTION to the claim: it is NOT a 'short blunt triangle'. It is a reasonably long, straight, sharply-pointed wedge with a drawn gape/culmen line, running roughly 0.65-0.7 of head width - the OUTLINE is close to acceptable crow-bill shape; what it lacks is depth at the base and the faint decurve at the tip, so it reads flat and knife-like rather than stout. The disqualifying property is the COLOUR, not the length. mustRead 'stout straight pointed bill' is therefore half-present (straight, pointed, adequately long) and half-absent (not stout/deep, and rendered in bright yellow where a crow's bill must be black).

FEET, which the claim never mentions and which compound the misread: both legs and the splayed thin toes are the same bright yellow-ochre as the bill (~104,85,45 in shadow, gold in the lit strokes). Yellow bill PLUS yellow legs is the single loudest signal in the image and it is not any corvid. Also note this defeats the judge's 'Common Blackbird' identification - a Blackbird has dark legs and a long-bodied, long-tailed silhouette. What is actually drawn reads as a plump ball-bodied fowl / rail-chick / yellow-billed non-corvid; the judge is right that it is the wrong organism and wrong about which organism it is.

PLUMAGE. Body base samples 47,49,56 and 38,40,49 - dark SLATE GREY, not black. Over it sits a large concentric wing disc filled with pale whitish scribbled hatching, plus a bright pale rim-highlight running the whole mantle/back edge and down the breast, which reads almost as a white outline. There is a genuinely near-black band (15,16,20) separating wing from body, so black ink exists in the file, but the visible mass reads pewter-grey with white streaking. mustRead 'all-black glossy plumage' ABSENT: the grey is too light and the pale scribble is too high-contrast to read as gloss.

TAIL. CORRECTION to the claim: the tail is not 'grey' and not 'in a different colour from the body' in the direction stated - it samples 15,16,20, i.e. it is NEAR-BLACK and DARKER than the mid-grey body. The judge inverted the tonal error. What IS true and is the real defect: it is a narrow triangular spike tapering to a single sharp point, projecting back and slightly down, with no terminal width at all. mustRead 'square-tipped tail' ABSENT. Below the tail base there is also a fan of thin radiating hair-like filaments (vent bristles drawn as whiskers) that adds a fluffy galliform read and does not belong on a corvid.

PROPORTION, unreported by the judge: packet aspect is 1.7 but the body excluding the tail measures roughly 155 wide x 145 tall, i.e. about 1.07 - a sphere. Even counting the tail spike the whole animal is only ~1.3. The chassis is too round for the spec before any corvid-specific feature is considered.

VERDICT: 2 of 3 must-reads outright absent (all-black glossy plumage; square-tipped tail), the third present in outline but rendered in a colour that flips the species identification, plus an off-spec spherical aspect and yellow legs. FAIL upheld.

FIXES THIS IMPLIES: recolour bill AND legs/feet to black (this is the single highest-value change); deepen the bill base and add a slight tip hook without shortening it; darken the body toward near-black and drop the pale scribble hatching and the white rim-light to a low-amplitude blue-black sheen; replace the pointed tail spike with a broad square-tipped tail of even terminal width and delete the vent filament fan; stretch the chassis from a sphere toward the 1.7 spec.

rows.readsAs: a blue quail or a blue chicken with a topknot
rows.defect: None of the three must-reads survive. The barred blue wing patch — the single feature that IS a jay — is absent: the bird is uniformly washed blue head to tail with no patch, no black-and-white barring, and no boundary anywhere on the flank. The long broad tail is absent; the tail is the same short thin grey spike used on Crow and Raven, narrower and shorter than the body. The bill is a small yellow cone, neither stout nor crow-like. The added spiky topknot plus the round dumpy body pushes the read to gamebird rather than corvid, and the feet are again detached prints hovering below the belly.
rows.fix: Paint a hard-edged rectangular wing panel of alternating bright blue and black bars on the flank against a warm pinkish-buff body, and replace the spike tail with a long broad dark tail at least as long as the body.
rows.verifyWhy:
FAIL upheld — zero of three must-reads land, and the asset is the Crow/Raven chassis recoloured blue with a crest bolted on. Looked at 440x440 native and at 5-10x crops of head, mantle, wing panel, tail and feet.

MUST-READ 1 'stout crow-like bill on a rounded head' — HALF-MET AT BEST, and the judge's wording needs correcting. The head IS a clean rounded sphere, so that half is fine. The bill is NOT 'small': at 6x it is a flat triangular wedge roughly 0.6x the head diameter, i.e. reasonably long. What is wrong is its FORM and COLOUR — it is a thin flat-sided finch/songbird wedge with a straight gape line, saturated gold-yellow (same swatch as the Crow's and Raven's bill in this batch), with no depth at the base, no culmen curve, no dark horn colour. A jay bill is blackish, deep-based and stout with a slight hook. So: not 'small', but genuinely not stout and not crow-like. Fix is depth + dark colour, not length.

MUST-READ 2 'barred blue wing patch' — ABSENT, judge correct. There IS a wing: a bounded oval panel outlined by a dark navy arc on the flank, plus a second dark arc over the shoulder. But at 10x its fill is the SAME fine feather-fleck stipple (short pale dashes in loose rows) that covers the mantle, flank and rump identically — a generic plumage texture, not a marking. Colour sampling across the whole bird returns one family of mid-blue (mantle 80,131,193; wing 99,162,237; flank 92,150,219; head 74,132,200) with no second hue anywhere. There is no bounded patch, no alternating black/white banding, no contrast step at any edge. Small correction to the judge: it is not literally featureless 'uniform blue wash' — there is texture — but the texture is body-wide and zero-contrast, so it carries no identity. The fix is a discrete high-contrast black-and-blue barred block on the wing coverts that differs in VALUE from the body, plus (for Eurasian jay) a pinkish-buff body and black moustache, or (for blue jay) a black necklace and white face. None of that exists.

MUST-READ 3 'long broad tail' — ABSENT, judge correct in substance, wrong on colour. The tail is a narrow dart tapering to a single point, projecting back and slightly DOWN from the rump, about 30% of body length and never wider than the rump join. It is dark navy (not grey — the grey read comes from Crow/Raven, which share this exact silhouette). It is geometrically the same spike Crow and Raven use, so the judge's 'same as Crow and Raven' is right about the shape while wrong about its hue here. Needs to be roughly body-length, parallel-sided/broad, and held level.

SHARED-CHASSIS FINDING (confirmed by opening Crow.png and Raven.png side by side): Jay, Crow and Raven are one body. Identical dumpy near-spherical torso, identical shoulder arc + oval wing panel, identical yellow triangular bill, identical short rear spike tail, identical feet — two flat gold H-shaped toe glyphs lying on the ground with NO visible tarsus, the body resting straight on the substrate. Only the palette differs, plus Jay's added crest.

CREST: the topknot is real and clearly drawn — a spray of 4-5 separate outlined filaments curving back off the crown. But it is a quail/roadrunner plume of discrete tendrils, not a jay's streaked erectile crown, and combined with the legless dumpy sphere body it actively pushes the read toward a galliform. The judge's 'blue quail' summary is fair.

Aspect check against the row (aspect 1.9): the painted bird measures roughly 210 wide x 190 tall including tail, i.e. barely over 1.1 — nowhere near the elongated 1.9 the row asks for, which is why it reads dumpy. headFrac 0.22 is roughly met.

rows.readsAs: a grackle, or a black moorhen dragging a grey banana
rows.defect: The pied black-and-white blocking that IS a magpie is completely absent — the bird is uniformly dark charcoal from bill to vent with no white scapular patch, no white belly, no white flank wedge, nothing. The long tail is present in length only: it is a fat blunt-ended grey-brown tube of even width, the wrong colour from the body, with no graduation, no wedge point and no iridescence, and it reads as a separate object attached to the bird rather than as feathers. The heavy straight crow bill is instead a small yellow cone. Feet float detached below the belly.
rows.fix: Block the bird in flat black and clean white — white belly, white scapular oval on the folded wing — and taper the tail into a graduated wedge of feathers of stepped lengths ending in a point, coloured the same black-green as the back.
rows.verifyWhy:
Verdict upheld, but two parts of the stated cause are wrong and one major defect was missed. WHAT I SAW (440x440, measured pixel-wise as well as looked at under 5-10x crops):

1) PIED BLOCKING — CONFIRMED ABSENT, and measurably so. I scanned all 193,600 pixels for near-neutral bright ones (min channel >140, max-min <40): exactly NINE hits, all at (110-112, 155-157), i.e. the single white catchlight in the eye. Nothing else on the bird exceeds luma 150 except the bill and feet, which are all the same yellow rgb(224,177,60). There is no white belly, no white scapular oval, no white primary window, no black/white boundary anywhere. The must-read 'black-and-white pied blocks of colour' is 100% missing.

2) 'uniform charcoal from bill to vent' — DIRECTIONALLY RIGHT, DESCRIPTIVELY WRONG. The plumage is not charcoal and not uniform. It is a blue-grey slate (body core around rgb 60-75, flank flecks rising to rgb 105-115) carrying a dense lighter-grey feather-fleck texture, a large lighter oval wing plate covering nearly the whole flank, and a broad near-black band ringing that wing. So there ARE three tonal steps — they simply all live inside a narrow mid-grey band and none of them is white or black. A fix that only 'adds contrast' to this existing texture will not produce a magpie; the pied blocks have to be authored as flat regions (white belly/flank block, white scapular patch, black hood/breast/tail).

3) TAIL — CONFIRMED, and worse than stated. Column-profile measurement from x=228 to x=362: thickness 20, 19, 19, 19, 19, 19, 20, 20, 21, 20, 21, 21, 22, 23, 22 px. It does not taper — it very slightly WIDENS toward the tip, then stops at a blunt angled cut with a rounded corner. No graduation, no wedge, no central-pair extension. It is actually TWO overlapping straight planks (a lighter upper slab and a darker lower slab offset below it) with a few cross-hatch band lines, not one tube. 'Object stuck to the bird' is understated: the silhouette PINCHES to ~7px of non-background at x=230, so the tail abuts the rump across a near-severed joint rather than emerging from it. A spray of thin dark filament lines hangs down-right from the vent (an attempt at coverts) but it sits below the tail, not along it, and contributes no graduation. Length: tail run 228->362 = 134px vs body 100->228 = 128px, so 'longer than the body' is only marginally met — a magpie's tail should be visibly half again the body.

4) BILL — THE CLAIM IS WRONG ON THIS POINT. It is not 'a small yellow cone'. It is a LARGE, prominent, straight-sided yellow triangular wedge spanning x=77-120, about 43px, nearly as long as the 55px head is wide, with a defined gape/mandible split line running its full length and a faint downturn at the tip. Its failure is COLOUR and PROFILE, not size: it is bright yellow rgb(224,177,60) where a magpie's bill must be black, and it is a symmetric isoceles wedge pinned low on the face rather than the deep-based crow bill with a slightly curved culmen and feathered nasal bristles. As drawn, the yellow triangle plus all-slate body reads as a blackbird or a mis-coloured chough, not a corvid.

5) MISSED BY THE FIRST JUDGE: the bird has NO LEGS. The yellow feet are two flat splayed toe-stars lying on the ground plane directly beneath the belly, with zero tarsus connecting them to the body — the belly floats above unattached feet. And the chassis is a near-spherical fat blob (bbox 285x147, body height 129px against a body length of 128px) with a tiny round head, which reads as a quail/gamebird, not the slim, long-bodied, upright magpie. This body is also the same rounded egg used across this corvid batch.

BAND: FAIL stands. Of the three must-reads, the pied black-and-white blocking is entirely absent, the graduated wedge tail is absent (present only as length via a constant-width blunt plank), and the heavy straight crow bill is present in mass but wrong in colour and profile. No amount of polish reaches a magpie from here; the colour blocking, the tail shape and the legs all need authoring.

rows.readsAs: a black duckling; side by side with Crow it is the same bird a shade darker
rows.defect: All three must-reads are missing and the asset is not separable from Crow. The massive curved bill is a small straight yellow cone shorter than the head is wide — smaller in proportion than a real crow's, let alone a raven's. The shaggy throat hackles are absent: the throat is a smooth unbroken curve into the breast with no lance-shaped feather edges and no silhouette break at all. The wedge tail is absent — the tail is a stubby grey nub barely clearing the rump. The bird is a neckless egg with two yellow footprints floating unattached beneath it.
rows.fix: Give it a huge deep black bill roughly as long as the whole head with a downcurved culmen, and break the throat line into three or four ragged pointed hackle feathers so the underside of the head is visibly shaggy against the sky.
rows.verifyWhy:
UPHELD, but one of the three stated causes is factually wrong and must not be fixed as described.

What I did: read Raven.png (440x440) and Crow.png at full size, then re-cropped both at 5-8x with gamma lift (the plumage sits at luminance 11-45 on a luminance-8 background, so unboosted reading loses the whole rear half of the bird), then measured pixel bboxes and per-column silhouette profiles for both.

CONFIRMED - not separable from Crow, and it IS the darker copy. Raven body tone samples 25-32; Crow 35-45. The rear tail plate reads a flat 11,11,14 on Raven and 15,16,20 on Crow - literally the same shape, one step darker. Both are one chassis: an egg body, a ball head socketed on at the same angle, the same dark crescent shoulder band, the same speckle-fleck feather texture, and IDENTICAL yellow feet (Raven 51x23px, Crow 51x23px, Magpie 50x22px - the same foot stamp across the whole family). Raven's silhouette is 173x158, Crow's 163x152: a 6% scale bump from aspect 1.8 vs 1.7, and nothing else.

CONFIRMED - must-read 1 'massive curved bill' is ABSENT. Bill bbox 107..136 x 147..168 = 30px long, 21px deep at the base. Crow's is 30x20 and Magpie's is 30x21 - the bill is one shared stamp at three sizes of nothing. Head ball measures ~40px across, so the bill is 0.73x head width; a raven's bill should be about as long as the head and visibly deeper than a crow's. Culmen is straight: top edge runs y158@x108 (tip) to y148@x136 (base), deltas -3,-2,-1,-2,-1,-1,0 - a flat isoceles taper that if anything flattens toward the base. There is no arch, no decurved tip, no hook. The judge's phrase 'a small straight yellow cone shorter than the head is wide' is exactly right.
  ADDITIONAL DEFECT THE JUDGE MISSED: the bill and the feet are bright saturated YELLOW (RGB ~230,200,90). A raven's bill and legs are BLACK. Chough is the only corvid in this batch that is supposed to carry a coloured bill (red) and it has zero non-grey bill pixels. The colour assignment is inverted across the family.

CONFIRMED - must-read 2 'shaggy throat hackles' is ABSENT. Traced the front silhouette edge row by row: y215:128, y220:127, y225:127, y230:129, y235:130, y240:133, y245:136, y250:140, y255:145 - a perfectly monotonic smooth arc with zero serration. At 8x the throat is an unbroken curve from jaw into breast; the dark crescent sitting there is a shoulder shading band, not feather groups. The interior speckle-flecks are the generic body texture and do not break the outline. Nothing on this bird says 'shaggy'.

WRONG - the tail claim. 'A stubby grey nub barely clearing the rump' is not what is drawn. There IS a substantial tail: a tapering blade running from the rump at x~268 out to a point at x~313-330, i.e. 45-60px on a 162px body (~30% of body length), 21px deep at its base and narrowing monotonically (x282:21px, x298:14, x310:9, x322:4, x330:2), with a fan of fine rectrix strokes drawn under it. It is invisible at normal exposure only because its tone (11,11,14) is within ~3 luminance of the background - which is a legibility bug worth fixing, but it is NOT a missing tail. The real tail defect is different and worse: Crow's tail is the SAME blade (base depth 17, tip at x322) drawn ~8px shorter. Crow must read 'square-tipped' and Raven must read 'wedge'; both are the same slender pointed spike, and the spike reads as neither - it is a single tapering streamer, not a broad graduated wedge whose central feathers project from a fanned base.

Band: FAIL stands. Two of three must-reads are outright absent, the third exists but is byte-identical in form to the species it is supposed to distinguish this bird from, and the asset as a whole is Crow at 106% scale and one shade darker.

FIX DIRECTION (against what is actually on the canvas, not the judge's description): (1) rebuild the bill as its own shape - roughly head-length (~40px), deeper at the base (~28px), with an arched culmen that curves down over a hooked tip, and recolour it BLACK, not yellow; (2) break the throat/breast outline with 4-6 lanceolate hackle points that project past the silhouette edge between y~190 and y~240 - interior texture will not do it, the edge has to be serrated; (3) keep the existing tail geometry but widen the base and square-graduate the trailing edge into a true wedge, lengthen it past the crow's, and RAISE ITS TONE - at 11,11,14 on an 8-luma field it is functionally invisible; (4) recolour the feet black. Do not shorten or delete the Crow's tail to make room - fix Raven's, and give Crow the square tip its own row demands.

rows.readsAs: a small white-faced dark duck on water
rows.defect: The bill is bright orange-yellow, not white — the must-read is a WHITE bill running up into a white shield, and here only the face blaze is white while the bill is the wrong colour, so the coot's single diagnostic feature is broken. The white blaze is also oversized, wrapping the whole crown and cheek like a duck's head patch instead of a narrow frontal shield. No lobed grey-green toes appear at all; the body is a featureless dark egg cut off at a flat waterline with no foot or leg information anywhere.
rows.fix: Repaint the bill pure chalk-white continuous with a narrow white shield that runs only up the forehead, and shrink the white so the cheek and crown stay sooty black.

rows.readsAs: a plump long-billed plover or stone-curlew — a chunky ground bird, not a crane
rows.defect: There is NO NECK. The head sphere sits directly on the shoulder of the egg-shaped body, so the long straight neck that IS the identity of a crane is entirely absent. The legs are short, thick yellow sticks reaching barely a third of body height — nothing stilt-like. There is no drooping bustle of tail plumes over the rump; instead the rump ends in a flat solid dark triangle stabbing horizontally to the right, the identical tail wedge used on Rail. The crown patch is a white spiky tuft, not a bare red crown. Body depth is barrel-like where a crane is slim and tall. Every one of the three must-reads is missing.
rows.fix: Rebuild the silhouette around a long straight vertical neck at least as long as the torso, lift the body on stilt legs of roughly body-height, and replace the tail wedge with a soft layered bustle of plumes drooping over the rump.
rows.verifyWhy:
Looked at the 440x440 PNG at full size and then at 4x crops of the head, legs and rump. The FAIL stands - all three must-reads (long neck carried straight / drooping bustle of tail plumes over the rump / bare red crown patch and stilt legs) fail - but two of the judge's stated causes are described wrongly and must not be fixed as written.

WHAT IS ACTUALLY THERE. Silhouette is a single huge fat egg-shaped body (roughly 250px tall x 290px wide before the tail) with a small grey sphere head parked on its upper-left shoulder. The packet asks for aspect 0.8 (taller than wide); the asset is decisively WIDER than tall. The read is a squat plover/dotterel, exactly as the judge said.

NECK - CORRECT VERDICT, WRONG DESCRIPTION. It is NOT true that there is 'no neck at all' or that the head sphere is 'fused straight onto the shoulder'.
