At 4x there is a distinct grey neck column: a narrow shaft about 20px wide running down-right from the base of the skull into the shoulder mass, roughly 30px long against a head diameter of ~55px, with its own shading separate from the body. So a neck primitive EXISTS and is already drawn and lit - the defect is length and carriage, not absence. It is about half a head long, i.e. roughly a quarter of body depth, where a crane needs it about equal to body depth and carried vertically. The fix is to lengthen and verticalise the existing neck segment, not to add a neck that isn't there.

LEGS - CORRECT VERDICT, WRONG DESCRIPTION. They are NOT 'short thick stubs'. At 4x they are thin (about 8px wide), fully articulated yellow-ochre legs with a clean backward-bending hock partway down and a splayed foot of three thin forward toes plus a hallux. Craftsmanship is fine; the problem is purely proportion - from body underside (~y265) to foot (~y330) is about 65px against a 125px body depth, so legs are roughly half a body deep. That reads as a medium wader, not a stilt. Fix = scale the tarsus/tibia length up, do not redraw the limb.

TAIL - JUDGE ESSENTIALLY RIGHT, ONE OMISSION. The dominant shape is exactly as claimed: a solid charcoal wedge projecting horizontally backwards from the rump and tapering to a sharp point well past the body edge - a flat tail, not a bustle. However there IS a token bustle already present that the judge missed: a small fan of very fine dark hairline filaments sweeping down-and-back from beneath the rump, visible only at 4x. They are charcoal-on-near-black and about 1px wide, so they are completely invisible at display size and contribute nothing. Fix = keep those filaments but make them a mass - lift them in value, thicken them, and let them droop over and past the flat wedge so the rump silhouette becomes a shaggy droop rather than a hard point.

CROWN - JUDGE FULLY CORRECT. The crown carries a WHITE, hard-edged, spiky crest of five or six splayed quills leaning forward over the skull. There is no red anywhere in the asset. This reads as a cockatoo/hoopoe crest and actively fights the crane read; the bare red skin cap is entirely absent.

ADDITIONAL, NOT IN THE CLAIM. The bill is long - about 1.8 head diameters - straight and dagger-shaped in flat yellow-orange, contradicting the packet note that a crane's bill is SHORTER than a heron's. That long bill is a second driver of the plover/snipe read and should be shortened, not just the neck lengthened. Eye is a single normal black dot with highlight, correctly sized for the 'normal' eye spec.

Net: neck primitive and leg primitive already exist and are competently drawn but are proportioned to a squat wader; tail plumes exist but are sub-visible; the red crown patch is genuinely missing and is replaced by a contradicting white crest. Three must-reads out of three fail. FAIL upheld.

rows.readsAs: a moorhen — the red shield with yellow bill tip lands, but the rear half of the bird carries no information
rows.defect: The head end is right: a clear red frontal shield above a yellow bill reads correctly at a glance. The rear end fails — there is no cocked tail and no white undertail flashes at all; the rump simply dissolves into the water with nothing cocked above the waterline, so the flicking white tail that is half a moorhen's field ID is absent. The white is also in the wrong place: it is painted as a broad white bib down the breast and throat instead of a thin horizontal white streak along the flank at the waterline.
rows.fix: Cock a short black tail up clear of the water with two white patches flanking its underside, and move the white from the breast to a thin horizontal flank line just above the waterline.

rows.readsAs: a kiwi, or a generic brown speckled ground bird — not a rail
rows.defect: This is the Crane asset recoloured brown with the crest deleted; the torso outline, wing swirl, leg placement and tail wedge are pixel-siblings. All four must-reads are absent. The bill is dead straight and yellow, with no downcurve whatsoever. The body is a deep barrel — as tall as it is long — the opposite of the narrow laterally flattened profile that lets a rail slip through reeds. The toes are three tiny nubs at the base of the legs, not outsized; a rail's absurd long toes are the most memorable thing about it and they are simply not drawn. The tail is a flat solid triangle projecting horizontally backwards rather than a short tail cocked upward.
rows.fix: Give it a long reddish downcurved bill, compress the torso to a narrow slab, cock the short tail upright, and draw splayed toes as long as the tarsus.

rows.readsAs: a purple cartoon salamander or smiling gecko toy
rows.defect: The must-read thick tail longer than the body is flatly absent -- the tail is a stubby blunt triangle roughly a quarter of the body length that stops dead. The armoured ridged scute rows are not on the back: they are evenly spaced vertical pinstripes ruled down the FLANK like corrugated card, plus a dark brown trim band with a white pinstripe that hovers off the topline and sticks out forward past the shoulder into empty space as a detached strip. The head is a rounded rectangle slab with a smiley upcurved mouth line that reaches neither the snout tip nor a jaw hinge, no jaw seam, no lip and a single nostril dot placed high on the cheek well behind the snout tip. Head and torso meet at a raw vertical butt seam with no neck, and the jaw plate hangs below the belly line. Colour is mauve-purple.
rows.fix: Redraw the tail as a thick muscular taper at least as long as head-plus-torso, and move the armour off the flank onto the back as an overlapping row of raised keeled scutes that follows the topline instead of a floating trim strip.

rows.readsAs: a green cartoon salamander -- pixel-for-pixel the Alligator in another colour
rows.defect: The bony ridge between the eyes -- the one feature that separates a caiman from an alligator -- is not there. What stands in for it is a single thin dark stroke drawn BEHIND and below the eye on the cheek, which reads as a scratch or a crack in the skin, and it is placed nowhere near between the eyes. The heavily scuted armoured back and neck are absent too: the armour is vertical pinstriping on the flank plus the same detached dark trim band floating off the topline. The whole silhouette -- slab head, nostril dot, smiley mouth, slit eye, corrugated torso, mid-torso forelimb, nub tail -- is identical to the Alligator card with only the hue changed, so the two cannot be told apart.
rows.fix: Build a distinct caiman skull: raise a visible bony bridge across the top of the snout between the eye sockets so it breaks the dorsal profile, and armour the neck with a separate band of raised nuchal scutes the Alligator does not get.

rows.readsAs: a crocodilian -- but most strangers would say alligator
rows.defect: The double-crested laterally flattened tail is absent: the tail is the family's short blunt cone with a single row of small bumps, about a third of body length, with no lateral flattening and no paired crest. The snout is not narrow or V-shaped either -- it is a deep, blunt, rounded slab barely different from the Alligator card, so the alligator-versus-crocodile call goes the wrong way. The enlarged fourth lower tooth IS present but it is one lone white triangle floating on an otherwise completely toothless jaw line, so it reads as a chip of debris rather than as the tooth that interlocks past the upper lip. Dorsal osteoderm bumps along the back are the one clear win here.
rows.fix: Rebuild the tail as a tall laterally compressed paddle carrying two converging scute crests that merge into one, and narrow the snout to a long tapering V so it stops matching the Alligator profile.

rows.readsAs: a gharial
rows.defect: The needle snout with its studded interlocking tooth row is genuinely there and carries the identification, and the ghara knob is present as a small bulb on the snout tip. What fails is the tail: it is the same short blunt cone every other card in this batch got, with no lateral flattening and no tall paddle crest, so a species defined by an oar-like swimming tail ends in a stub. The snout also joins the skull at a hard vertical step and the skull joins the torso at a raw butt seam with no neck, so the head reads as a separate part clipped onto the corrugated body block; the lower jaw is a rectangular plate that ends in a square corner directly under the eye.
rows.fix: Replace the cone tail with a tall laterally flattened paddle carrying a single high scute crest along its top edge, and blend the skull into the torso with an actual neck instead of a vertical butt seam.

rows.readsAs: two unrelated blobs - a spotted tan egg with four pins, and a separate curled grub next to it
rows.defect: The render is broken: there is a clear black GAP between the head oval and the abdomen, so the animal is in two disconnected pieces. Worse, the two white eye dots sit on the ABDOMEN (upper right of the tail unit, next to a black wedge), not on the head - the head carries only a single stray speck at the antenna root. None of the must-reads are present: the body is opaque solid tan, not translucent; the limbs are four bare straight pins, not a row of leaf-like paddles; and the tail ends in a downward-pointing blade fan tucked under the body, not a slender abdomen with a forked tail fan.
rows.fix: Weld the abdomen onto the rear of the cephalothorax so the silhouette is one continuous body, move the stalked eye pair onto the head, and replace the four pins with a ventral row of about eleven overlapping leaf-shaped paddle limbs.
rows.verifyWhy:
FAIL upheld, but the first judge's diagnosis is wrong about WHICH piece is which and about the tail and the eyes, and the fix they imply (close the gap) would not fix this.

WHAT IS ACTUALLY ON CANVAS (measured, not guessed). Connected-component analysis of the warm-pixel mask at a deliberately permissive threshold (r-b > 3, i.e. anything at all warmer than the blue background) returns THREE separate components, not one and not two:
  A  x[271..317] y[183..270]  n=2806  - the right-hand curled mass
  B  x[120..272] y[173..254]  n=2391  - the left oval plus its antennae and legs
  C  x[120..211] y[168..190]  n=236   - one antenna stroke, floating free of everything
A and B share no bridging pixel. At 12x the junction (crop x258-320, y168-230) shows a clean 4-6 px channel of pure background between them, and BOTH sides carry their own finished rim highlight, so these are two separately lit, separately closed bodies, not one body with a seam. Component C is an entire antenna hanging in empty space, its root ~7 px clear of the oval - the judge missed this third orphan.

THE PIECES ARE MIS-IDENTIFIED IN THE CLAIM. The judge called the left oval the head and the right mass the abdomen, and said the eyes landed on the abdomen. It is the reverse. The RIGHT piece is the head-and-body: its top knob carries a V-shaped orange rostrum wedge from which two short orange STALKS radiate, each ending in a dark orb with a white specular square - these are genuinely two stalked eyes, correctly built, and they are on a head. That same right piece then runs down in clear transverse segment bands (a real segmented abdomen) and terminates in a splayed fan of four pointed blades plus a broad rounded left lobe. So the right piece on its own is very nearly a brine shrimp. The LEFT oval is the orphan: an unsegmented, opaque, egg-shaped body carrying ALL four antennae and ALL four legs, with no eye on it at all - the two white marks near its top edge that the judge read as eyes are the specular highlight arc along the oval's rim (pixels 234-241 and 254 at y178-180, part of a continuous sheen), and the only true dot on it is a 2x2 white speck at its left tip (x213-214, y190-191). So: the eyes are NOT on the abdomen; they are on the head, and the defect is that the antenna group and the limb group have been placed at an offset that lands them entirely OFF the animal, on a second free-floating carapace oval ~50 px forward of the body. The fix is the appendage-anchor offset, not a gap-closing weld.

MUST-READS.
  1) 'translucent segmented body with a row of leaf-like paddle limbs' - FAILS, and the judge is right that it is opaque solid tan; neither piece shows any translucency (no background value survives through either mass anywhere). The limbs are, exactly as claimed, four bare pins: at 11x they are four straight uniform-width orange rods with blunt square ends, no joint, no taper, no blade, no wave. Not a row of paddles. Compounding it, they hang from the wrong piece, so the segmented trunk that should carry the paddle row carries nothing at all.
  2) 'two stalked eyes on the head' - actually PRESENT and well drawn (see above). This is the one must-read the judge scored wrong; they are stalked, paired, and on the head knob.
  3) 'slender abdomen ending in a forked tail fan' - PARTIAL, and the judge's description is wrong. The tail is not 'a downward blade fan tucked under the body': at 12x it is a fan of four pointed blades spreading OUT to the lower right, clear of the silhouette, with a broad rounded lobe to the left and a thin stem spike below. A fan is genuinely there. What fails is the abdomen itself - it is a short stubby curl 46 px wide by 87 px tall, curled back on itself, nowhere near slender, and the fan is spiky-serrated rather than two clean forked lobes.

PROPORTION. Reference aspect is 3.5. Measured warm bbox is 197x103 = 1.91 including the antennae; the ORGANISM alone (both blobs, x218-317 y168-270) is ~100x103 = 0.97. The thing is square, not a 3.5:1 swimmer.

NET READ. Because the eyes and the tail fan are at the two ends of one 46 px stub, the right piece alone reads as a curled woodlouse or maggot, and the left oval reads as a tick or mite floating in front of it. Nothing here reads as a translucent 3.5:1 upside-down swimmer with a beating row of paddles. FAIL stands on must-read 1 and on the two-body break; must-read 2 should be recorded as PASSING so the fix does not disturb the eye construction.

rows.readsAs: a pale grub or witchetty larva with long whiskers
rows.defect: The glassy colourless body and the long sweeping antennae do read. But the abdomen curls FORWARD and DOWN so the tail fan ends up underneath the walking legs instead of trailing behind, which breaks the shrimp silhouette; the segment arcs are ruled lines on a smooth sausage rather than a stepped abdomen; and the four legs are featureless straight pins with no joint or foot. There is also a hard oval-on-oval seam where the head balloon meets the body balloon.
rows.fix: Uncurl the abdomen so it sweeps backward and slightly up with the tail fan opening away from the head, and cut each segment as a real stepped overlap in the silhouette instead of a painted line.

rows.readsAs: the Cave Shrimp again in cream - a bottom-crawling grub with whiskers
rows.defect: Every part of the fairy shrimp's identity is absent. It is drawn RIGHT WAY UP standing on four stiff pin legs, not swimming inverted on its back. There is no wave of eleven pairs of leaf-like legs - just four bare pins. It has a fat opaque two-lobe body with a heavy carapace-like head oval when the reference explicitly says there is NO carapace and the body is a bare translucent tube. There are no stalked eyes, only one tiny speck at the antenna root. What is on screen is the shared shrimp chassis recoloured cream and nothing more.

rows.verifyWhy: Looked at the 440x440 PNG, then at 4x and 10x crops of the head and tail. The FAIL stands, and the chassis charge is if anything understated. WHAT IS ACTUALLY DRAWN: a cream, fully opaque, two-lobe body standing right way up on a substrate, with a soft elliptical cast shadow painted on the ground under it - so it reads as a thing perched on a floor, not a thing swimming. Front lobe is a big smooth egg-shaped dome (head/cephalothorax) with ~8 soft darker blotches on it; it reads exactly as a carapace, which the reference note forbids ('has no carapace at all - the body is a bare translucent tube'). Rear lobe is a second fat lobe rising up-and-back then curving down to the right, ringed into ~7 heavy segments. No translucency anywhere: both lobes are solid opaque cream with specular highlights, no see-through, no gut line, and no orange/pink toward the tail that the note calls for. MUST-READS, one by one: (1) 'swims upside down on its back' - ABSENT. Posture is upright and grounded, dorsal side up, legs down, with the ground shadow confirming it. (2) 'eleven pairs of leaf-like legs beating in a wave' - ABSENT. There are exactly FOUR legs, all under the head lobe only, all straight rigid brown pins of identical length and thickness, hanging vertically and ending bluntly with no foot, no blade, no leaf, no phyllopod outline, and no phase offset that could read as a metachronal wave. The whole trunk/abdomen carries NO limbs at all. (I also found two stray thin brown sticks near the tail - one lying across the mid-abdomen, one hanging below the tail fan - but they are unattached-looking single filaments, not limbs, and do not help.) (3) 'stalked eyes' - here I correct the claim slightly. It is not true that there are no eyes at all: at the very tip of the snout, in a small dark notch, there is ONE tiny white dot eye, sessile and sunk against the head. So the defect is one unstalked pinpoint eye where two eyes on projecting stalks are required - the fix is to replace it, not to add eyes from nothing. There is no second eye and no stalk of any kind. (4) 'translucent shell-less body' - ABSENT, see above. Aspect is also wrong: the reference asks 4.5, but the body bounding box (excluding antennae) is roughly 140 x 130 px, about 1.1:1 - a hunched grub, not an elongated tube. A fix that just darkens 'the neck' will collide with that seam; the mane needs to be a separate darker, tufted-silhouette mass hung off the underside and crest of the neck and spilling onto the brisket.

MUST-READ 3 - 'pale cream rump patch': ABSENT, and the judge UNDERSTATED it. The rump is not merely 'the same gold' - it is DARKER than the flank: rear band (0-15% of body length) = 161,132,91 vs mid-flank 181,149,102. That is the opposite of a cream patch. The 'flat faceted panel edge' the judge saw is a pale rim highlight, but it is not local to the rump - the same pale untextured rim runs along the entire outer silhouette including the withers and topline, so it is shell geometry, not a marking. The entire face from eye to nose is bare: nothing projects forward, no brow tine, no palmate plate, no vertical face-plate. The one dark shape near the eye is not antler at all - it is the ear, a dark triangular wedge below-left of the eye pointing down-and-back. CORRECTION to the judge's wording: the rack is not 'backswept'. It is a mirrored pair of near-vertical beams, each carrying three short straight prongs that sweep UP and OUTWARD (a symmetric V), with the front prong on the forward beam angling slightly forward-up. So the defect is 'no forward brow shovel and no brow tine on a plain vertical 3-prong fork', not 'backswept'. The 'reused across the batch' half is correct and I verified it numerically: Reindeer's antler rows y79-y134 produce the same segment count, order and widths as Elk's y55-y115 (Reindeer y79 segs 238-242/263-266/307-310/331-335; Elk y55 segs 241-244/268-271/314-317/340-343) - the identical rack, translated and scaled.

(2) PALE NECK MANE - ABSENT, and the judge understated it. Region-averaged RGB: throat/foreneck rgb(182,151,110) lum156, midneck rgb(184,154,113) lum159, under-neck rgb(174,143,105) lum148, versus upper flank rgb(189,159,117) lum164 and mid flank rgb(182,148,104) lum154. The neck is not merely 'the same uniform gold' - it measures fractionally DARKER than the flank, so there is no pale value break anywhere on it. The ventral neck silhouette is also a clean straight taper from jaw to brisket with zero bulge, fringe or hanging lobe; the only lighter marks on the neck are the same painterly hatching strokes that run over the whole body. There is no mane in colour OR in silhouette.

(3) BROAD SPLAYED HOOVES - ABSENT, with one factual correction. The feet are NOT undivided caps: at 5x each foot clearly splits into two small dark toe caps, so a cloven hoof is drawn. The failure is scale, not cleft. Measured, each hoof spans only ~18-19px across (fore 232-240/242-250, hind 135-143/145-153) while the cannon bone immediately above it is 23-28px wide (y309 x124-152; y319 x129-152). The hoof is therefore NARROWER than the leg it hangs on, where a reindeer's snowshoe hoof must read markedly WIDER than the leg. Tiny dark caps: right. Undivided: wrong.

They are not the same bitmap: Reindeer's ink bbox is 233x263px, Elk's is 251x311px; Elk is taller with a longer, more upright neck and a raised withers/shoulder step, Reindeer is shorter-bodied with a flatter topline and a lower head. But they are one chassis - identical antler rack, identical skull and tapering pointed muzzle with a small dark nose dot and a thin mouth line, identical straight columnar legs, identical cloven caps, identical uniform gold hatched coat - differing only in scale and neck length. Elk fails its own row the same way (no dark shaggy mane: its neck lum 136-163 sits inside its flank's 156-165; no pale cream rump patch: rump rgb(184,155,113) is flank colour). A stranger shown this file names it 'a deer'; nothing about it says arctic, and nothing distinguishes it from the Elk beside it.

1. SHARED-CHASSIS CLAIM: CONFIRMED, and now quantified. A silhouette IoU of Jackal.png against Coyote.png (background-keyed at threshold 24) gives both=16597 px, Jackal-only=829, Coyote-only=2214, IoU 84.5%. The diff map shows the entire non-overlap is a 1-2px halo tracing the outline - Coyote is uniformly a hair larger. The two species differ ONLY in hue (Jackal warmer/tan, Coyote greyer/cream). This is the family defect the packet's warning box asks about, and it is real.

2. WHAT THE CHASSIS READS AS: a foal / stocky pony with a canid head pasted on. Deep round barrel with a horse-like arched back, short thick neck rising near-vertically to a small head carried HIGH above the withers (canids carry the head low and forward, level with or below the topline), and four straight columnar limbs with zero angulation - no hock, no stifle, no elbow, no carpus - front and hind legs are the same column mirrored.

3. FEET - claim is roughly right but described wrong. At 16x each foot is a wide flat dark-brown ELLIPSE/plinth clearly wider than the leg column, with a thin light rim under it. There ARE three faint vertical toe hatch-marks painted on its front face, so it is not literally a bare hoof - but they are interior shading only, they do not break the silhouette, and at full size the foot reads as a hoof puck. Fix must add real toes/paw pads that change the OUTLINE, not more hatching.

4. EARS - the claim "one small triangle rather than large pointed erect ears" is WRONG. At 14x there are clearly TWO erect triangular ears sharing a vertical apex ridge: a near ear (dark inner face, apex to the right) and a far ear behind it (apex to the left), each with a lit outer rim. Measured: ear height ~18px against a head length (occiput to nose tip) of ~62px, i.e. ~29% of head length. So the must-read "large pointed erect ears" IS present and readable - it is undersized for a jackal (should be ~35-45% of head length) and sits too far FORWARD, planted directly above the eye at the top-centre of the skull with a large pale rounded mass behind it that swallows the occiput, so it reads as a crest/forelock peak rather than ears set at the back of the skull. This ear geometry is pixel-for-pixel the same construction as Coyote's - so the claim that Jackal has ears where Coyote does not is false on both ends.

5. MUZZLE - must-read "slender fox-like muzzle" is PRESENT. Long tapering snout with a distinct dark nose pad and a drawn mouth line. It is a touch deep and hooks/droops at the tip, but it reads as a canid muzzle. This is the one part of the asset doing its job.

6. TAIL - claim is wrong twice. It is NOT level: the tail root sits at orig (155,190), just under the topline at the REARMOST point of the rump, and the dark tip sits at orig (118,238), so it runs down-and-back at roughly 50 degrees below horizontal, ending at belly level. "Carried low" is arguably satisfied. It is also NOT a mid-back tail - the root is at the croup, correctly placed; what makes it read oddly is that the proximal cylinder is fat and overlaps forward across the hip. The dark tip is NOT a "flat cut-off cap": it is a rounded dark-brown ELLIPSE stuck on the end like a ferrule. The real tail defect is different: the tail is a smooth tapering CYLINDER with a hair fringe on the upper edge only and a smooth bare underside, so it reads as a horse's dock-with-hair rather than a bushy canid brush; and the dark tip is a pasted-on disc that stops dead at the cylinder edge instead of carrying into the fringe hairs, so the "black tip" does not look like fur.

VERDICT REASONING: all three must-reads are technically findable (ears present but small and mis-sited, muzzle good, tail dark-tipped and low-ish but not bushy). The FAIL stands anyway on two independent grounds the per-feature checklist cannot see: (a) the organism reads as a hoofed pony, and hooves plus unangulated columnar limbs plus a high vertical neck on a canid is a wrong-organism failure regardless of head detail; (b) at 84.5% silhouette IoU with a uniform-halo-only difference, Jackal is not a distinct asset from Coyote - it is Coyote recoloured, so the species has no identity of its own within its own family.

FIX PRIORITY: canid limb model (angulated hock/stifle, digitigrade paws that change the silhouette) > lower the head and lengthen/lighten the body off the pony barrel > rebuild the tail as a true brush with the black tip carried through the fur > enlarge the ears ~1.4x and move them back onto the occiput. Do NOT 'add ears' or 'un-level the tail' - both already exist.

What fails is that it is not BROAD or BLOCKY in the wolf sense and is indistinguishable from Coyote's: the muzzle is a thin flat bar that tapers DOWNWARD off the box, with a separate thin lower-jaw bar under it leaving a visible slot (reads as an open pipe or a beak), and it terminates in an oversized dark-brown oval nose blob pasted on the front. There is no depth to the muzzle, no stop, no mass of jaw. The amber/yellow iris with a black pupil is correct for a wolf and the judge did not mention it - keep it.

CORRECTION 3 - TAIL CARRIAGE. 'Held level from mid-back' is WRONG. The tail attaches at the rump/croup (not mid-back) and angles DOWN-and-back at roughly 30-40 degrees below horizontal. The reference permits 'carried level or low', so the carriage angle is acceptable and is NOT the defect. The tail defects are texture and tip: it is a smooth pale cylinder with three or four darker grey banding blocks across it (their 'striped' is correct), a thin one-sided comb of short spiky bristles fringing only the upper/outer edge instead of a full brush, and the tip is a flat dark-brown ELLIPSE that reads exactly as the open end of a cut pipe (their strongest observation, and correct). It also is not straight - it bows. 'Straight bushy tail' fails on bushiness and on the cut-pipe end, not on angle.

CORRECTION 4 - CHEST. Their 'wide round barrel, not narrow and deep' is right in effect. In profile the barrel is the same depth from shoulder to hip with a high, nearly straight belly line and only a token tuck; the brisket never drops toward elbow level, so there is no deep chest and no tucked loin. Legs ARE long - arguably too long, they read as pony pasterns - so 'long legs' passes and only the 'narrow deep chest' half of that must-read fails.

MUST-READ TALLY: erect triangular ears PRESENT; broad blocky head ABSENT; long legs PRESENT; narrow deep chest ABSENT; straight bushy tail ABSENT (banded cylinder with a flat cut-pipe tip); carriage acceptable. Two of three must-reads fail on their defining half and the organism reads as an equid, so FAIL is correct.

rows.readsAs: a cartoon blue bee or gnat blowing a trail of bubbles
rows.defect: All three must-reads are absent or inverted. The abdomen is not a needle-thin stick — it is a chain of five separate, visibly DETACHED spheres that shrink toward the tail with clear background gaps between them and between the first bead and the thorax, so the body reads as a bubble trail rather than an animal. The wings are not held closed together over the back: there is a single pale feather-shaped plume swept back and OUT to the side at roughly 20 degrees, the same plume used on the Dragonfly. The hammerhead face is nowhere present — the head is a smooth round ball with two tiny dot eyes set close together high on the front, i.e. the opposite of widely separated eyes on a transverse head.
rows.fix: Replace the bead chain with one continuous unbroken hair-thin abdomen rod at least 3x the combined head+thorax length, fused to the thorax, and rebuild the head as a wide transverse dumbbell with a hemispherical eye pushed out to each far end.

rows.readsAs: a stylized blue-and-teal bee or wasp with feathered wings
rows.defect: The identity must-read is missing: the eyes are two tiny white-ringed dots on a smooth blue ball, occupying maybe a twentieth of the head, when huge globe compound eyes should BE the head and meet over the top of it. The abdomen is wrong in kind, not just degree — it is a short thick sausage of four alternating light/dark banded segments only about 1.5x the head+thorax length, which reads as bee/wasp banding rather than a long slender rod. The wings are three opaque grey feather blades with a central quill-like shaft, not two pairs of transparent net-veined membranes; they are also swept back and downward off the thorax rather than held out flat, and the count reads as three rather than four.
rows.fix: Rebuild the head as two enormous dark iridescent hemispheres that fill and overhang the skull and touch at the midline, and swap the feather blades for four flat, near-transparent elongated membranes with a fine cross-hatched vein lattice and a dark pterostigma near each leading tip.

rows.readsAs: a flat sage-green leaf, or a lancetfish/needlefish blade - a stranger would not say eel and would never say electric eel
rows.defect: The must-read that IS this animal - the single long ribbon anal fin running the whole underside - is nowhere on the render. The belly is just the body outline with the tick ladder ending against it. Worse, the two features the reference explicitly forbids are both drawn: a hard triangular blade sits on the spine at ~65% length reading as a dorsal, and a translucent leaf lobe hangs below it reading as a pelvic. The body is a flat symmetric lens, pointed at the tail and squared at the snout, with no cylindrical knifefish mass, and the whole flank is filled with vertical scale ticks that a smooth-skinned electric eel does not have.
rows.fix: Delete the mid-body dorsal triangle and the lower lobe entirely, and replace the plain belly edge with a single continuous translucent ribbon fin that starts just behind the head and runs unbroken to the tail tip, undulating in shallow waves so it reads as the propulsive organ.

rows.readsAs: a lanternfish or a glowing deep-sea sardine - a small dark torpedo with a row of blue belly lights
rows.defect: The enormous pelican pouch mouth - the entire identity of this animal, and the packet's headFrac 0.3 - is completely absent. At 14x the head is the same blunt squared snout cap as the Moray and the Electric Eel, occupying maybe 8% of length, with a straight closed mouth line and six tiny tooth pegs hung under it. There is no jaw, no hinge, no pouch, nothing loose or distended. The whip tail is also missing: the left end is the same 2px grey wisp the other two get, with no taper and no luminous tip. Only the pinhead eye at the snout is arguably delivered, and even that is the shared ring dot.
rows.fix: Rebuild the front third as a hinged pouch - drop the lower jaw to a wide open angle and hang a slack skin membrane from it that is deeper and wider than the trunk behind it, so the mouth visibly outmasses the body, then taper the rear two thirds to a hair-thin whip ending in a single bright bead.

rows.readsAs: a long olive toothy fish - eel is a plausible first guess, mostly from the elongation and the teeth, but a leaf-shaped one with something stuck on its back
rows.defect: Two of three must-reads fail. The gaping mouth is not gaping: the jaw line is a straight closed horizontal edge with a row of white tooth pegs dangling below it, which reads as teeth on the outside of a shut mouth rather than an open maw. The single fin ridge does not run the whole length of the back - instead a soft translucent olive blob floats over the middle ~45% of the body, fading out well short of both the head and the tail, and it is mirrored by an equally large translucent ventral lobe at ~70% length that reads exactly like the pectoral fin the reference says must not exist. The body itself is the shared rigid straight lens rather than a sinuous rope.
rows.fix: Split the head into an upper and a lower jaw hinged open at about 35 degrees with the needle teeth on the inner edges of both, then delete the ventral lobe and stretch the dorsal into a narrow continuous crest that starts behind the eye and runs unbroken to the tail tip.

rows.readsAs: a startled hedgehog, or a brown potato with straw stuck in its back
rows.defect: The quadruped has no legs whatsoever — no forelimb, no hindlimb, no foot, and therefore none of the required stocky splayed digging claws; only a tiny tan nub sits under the front quarter. The spines are not a dome: they are a thin radial fan of hair-fine strokes sprouting from a single line along the top of the back, leaving the entire flank, shoulder and rump as bare flat brown, so the animal reads as smooth-bodied with a spiky halo rather than armoured. The snout is a short cone tapered to a sharp point rather than the straight, constant-width, blunt-tipped tubular beak that is the one feature separating an echidna from a hedgehog.
rows.fix: Rebuild the beak as a narrow parallel-sided tube of constant width with a blunt rounded tip and two nostril dots, then plant four stubby splayed legs that break the belly line with visible spread toes and long pale digging claws, and carry the spine mass down over the flanks so the dome covers the body instead of crowning it.

rows.readsAs: a platypus, but only because of the dark patch on its face — otherwise a manatee or a mole loaf
rows.defect: Two of the three must-reads are missing or wrong. There are no webbed clawed feet at all — not one limb breaks the silhouette anywhere along the belly, so the animal appears to be a legless sausage. The tail is a near-circular lobe stuck onto the left end with a visible seam where it meets the body; it reads as a fat rear haunch, not a broad flat beaver-like paddle. The bill is present but is executed exactly as the packet's note forbids: a hard-edged dark oval disc laid on top of and overlapping the face like a mask, darker than every other value in the image and clearly a separate object rather than soft fleshy tissue fused into the head.
rows.fix: Fuse the bill into the face by widening the muzzle so the head tapers into the bill with a shared contour and a soft value gradient instead of a hard dark ellipse, flatten the tail into a wide low paddle that grows out of the rump without a seam, and add two webbed forefeet with splayed toes and small claws breaking the lower silhouette.

rows.readsAs: an elephant - a stranger names it correctly off the tusks and hanging trunk, but calls it a lumpy, cartoonish one
rows.defect: All three must-reads are present but each is compromised. (1) The trunk is a grey ribbed hose that emerges from a separate lobe on the lower-right of the face, at mouth/jaw height and BEHIND the tusks rather than from the front of the face between them; it descends to roughly foot height but ends in a blunt hook with no two grasping lips at all. (2) The ear is a single dark charcoal oval with a heavy black rim and radiating ribs, planted on the shoulder/flank so it reads as a scallop shell or bracket fungus stuck to the body rather than a huge fan hinged off the skull - there is no visible attachment point to the head and no second ear implied on the far side. (3) The legs are slim tapered posts with a joint band, not pillars, and the back shows a shoulder hump into a rounded rump rather than a clear dipped saddle. Additional: the head plus ear mass visually dominates the small barrel body (reads well over the 0.26 headFrac), the eye is set high and forward like a cartoon decal, and the tail ends in five long stiff splayed black bristles that read as a broom or feather fan rather than a tuft.
rows.fix: Re-root the trunk at the front-top of the face between the eyes so it falls in FRONT of and between the tusks, taper it to a two-lobed finger-and-lip tip resting on the ground, and re-cut the ear as a lighter, body-toned fan whose top edge clearly hinges at the back of the skull above the eye and drapes over the shoulder.

rows.readsAs: an elephant, unspecified species
rows.defect: Reads as an elephant, but the enormous fan-shaped ear -- the one thing that says African -- is not an ear. It is a dark slate slab with a rounded-rectangle outline and vertical corrugations, sitting on the shoulder well behind and below the eye, with the head overlapping its front edge, so it reads as a blanket or a folded wing draped over the withers. It is also darker in value than any other part of the animal, which detaches it from the silhouette entirely. The trunk is a banded tube of constant diameter with no taper toward the tip and no muscular thickening at the base, and the topline is convex where the reference note calls for a saddle-shaped dip.
rows.fix: Redraw the ear as a single soft-edged fan attached at the skull behind the eye -- top edge above the eyeline, trailing edge lobed and drooping past the shoulder -- in the hide colour with only a slightly darker interior wash, no rectangular outline and no vertical ribbing.

rows.readsAs: an elephant, indistinguishable from the African one except that the rug on its shoulder is smaller
rows.defect: The arched convex back and the reduced ear are correctly present, but the twin-domed forehead with the dip between -- the single feature that names this animal -- is entirely absent: the skull is the same plain smooth dome as the African and Forest heads, with no bilateral bulges and no median groove. The smaller ear is still the same dark ribbed rectangle, oval-cornered rather than triangular. The trunk is the same corrugated hose and its lower hook terminates in mid-air well to the right of and below the front foot, so the tip floats off the ground plane instead of touching it, and no single dorsal finger-lip is drawn at the tip.
rows.fix: Sculpt two distinct rounded bumps into the top of the skull with a shallow V-notch between them, breaking the current single dome, and cut the ear down to a small pointed triangle held close to the cheek.

rows.readsAs: the African Elephant again, slightly smaller, with longer tusks
rows.defect: The straight downward tusks do read -- they are the longest and most vertical in the batch -- but nothing else separates this from asset 1. The ear is the identical dark ribbed rectangular slab, barely smaller and not rounded or oval, so the must-read rounded-ear difference is invisible when the two are seen side by side. The hide is the same mid-grey rather than noticeably darker, and the animal is the same overall bulk on the same barrel body, so the smaller-and-darker forest read never lands. The right-hand tusk is a flat white blade with a hard edge that reads as a fang or a leaf rather than ivory.
rows.fix: Give this one an unmistakably oval ear roughly two-thirds the African's area, and drop the hide two full value steps into a damp near-brown so the forest/savanna pair separates at a glance.

rows.readsAs: a lamb or a young sheep
rows.defect: A stranger names this a lamb without hesitating. The body is a cream fleece-textured oval covered in fine curled hair strokes, carried high on four long, slender, clearly separated legs with dark points -- exactly the sheep proportion. The must-read that IS the hyrax, the stubby legs under a low-slung guinea-pig body sitting almost on the ground, is absent: there is a tall open gap of daylight under the belly, and the elbow-to-ground run is roughly a third of the body height rather than the near-zero a hyrax shows. The blunt muzzle carries no whiskers at all, and the dark face mask over a pale fleece body is a lamb marking. The figure is also rendered very small in the frame and floats above the canvas centre with a shadow that sits low and detached.
rows.fix: Halve the leg length so the belly nearly touches the shadow, widen the body into a squat guinea-pig loaf with the shoulder and hip merged into one continuous hump, drop the fleece texture for short dense fur, and add a splayed whisker set at the blunt muzzle.
rows.verifyWhy: Looked at the 440x440 PNG, then decoded it and re-rendered four crops (whole animal 6x, head 14x and 20x, muzzle 32x, feet 8x, rump 18x) and measured the silhouette column-by-column. The FAIL verdict stands: this is a lamb, not a hyrax. MEASURED GEOMETRY (bright-pixel scan, background is near-black so the creature separates cleanly): creature bbox x148-292, y164-259 = 145w x 96h, aspect 1.51 against a spec aspect of 2.0. Torso topline is flat at y=176 and the belly line is flat at y=227-228 across the whole barrel (x192-x216 all read [176,228]); the ground/foot line is y=259. That is a 31 px void of pure background between belly and ground -- 32 percent of the animal's total height -- and the fore and hind legs are separated by a wide open triangle of daylight (the leg crop shows background all the way from the brisket back to the hind thigh). Torso alone is ~96 x 52 = 1.85 aspect, so even the barrel is not the long low tube the row asks for. MUST-READ 3, 'stubby legs', is therefore not merely weak, it is inverted: the legs are long, slender, tapered and clearly articulated, and the animal stands well clear of the ground. MUST-READ 1, 'tailless rounded guinea-pig-like body', is only half present -- the rump crop at 18x confirms a clean rounded tailless hindquarter with no tail nub at all (credit where due), but the body is a fleece: the coat is filled with short pale hair-flicks over cream/oatmeal, which is a woolly texture, and it is carried high, so it reads as a lamb's barrel and not as a ground-hugging rodent loaf. MUST-READ 2 splits: the muzzle IS short and blunt -- at 32x it is a small rounded snout projecting forward and slightly down off the front of the skull with one small dark nostril dot and a single mouth crease -- but there are ZERO whiskers anywhere, no vibrissae strokes, no dots, nothing. CORRECTIONS TO THE ORIGINAL CLAIM (three of its stated causes are wrong even though the verdict is right): (a) 'dark face mask' is inaccurate -- there is no mask pattern; the entire head AND neck are painted a uniform darker grey-taupe than the cream body, so the defect is a wholesale two-tone head/body split, not a facial marking; (b) 'four long slender legs with dark points' is wrong about the points -- the legs are the same cream as the body for their whole length with no stockings or dark points at all; the only dark marking is at the FEET, where each foot ends in two rounded dark toe-caps that read unmistakably as a cloven hoof (this is arguably the single most damaging wrong-organism cue in the piece and the original judge did not name it -- a hyrax has rounded rubbery pads, never a split hoof); (c) the claim is silent on the ears, and 'small rounded ears' is actually the one head must-read that IS present -- at 20x there is a small dark rounded oval sitting on the upper-left skull plus a small nub breaking the rear skull silhouette. It is painted flat onto the dome rather than modelled as a raised ear, so it is weak, but it is not absent and a fix pass should not go looking for a missing ear. ALSO NOT IN THE CLAIM: the eye is far too large and too cartoon -- a big dark pupil ringed by a bright white sclera crescent occupying roughly a third of the skull height -- where the row specifies eyes: normal; this inflates the lamb/plush read. FIX DIRECTION: drop the belly to within ~10 percent of the ground, shorten the legs to stubby columns that barely clear it, stretch the barrel toward aspect 2.0, replace the cloven toe-caps with blunt rounded pads, kill the fleece hair-flicks for a short dense pelt, unify head tone with the body, shrink the eye, and add long whiskers off the blunt muzzle.

rows.readsAs: A needlefish / garfish — or a decorated knife blade or seed pod. Nobody says 'eel'.
rows.defect: The two must-reads that ARE the identity are absent. (1) 'Snake-like body with a blunt-jawed head': the body is a rigid, dead-straight symmetrical lens with no curve, kink or undulation anywhere, and the head is a slender tapering point with an upturned snout and a thin scratched mouth line — there is no jaw depth, no thick blunt lip, no skull mass separating head from trunk. (2) 'Continuous fin fringe running along back, tail and belly': the only thing present is a faint translucent grey rim hugging the dorsal and ventral edges, so low in contrast against the dark field that at 1x it reads as anti-aliasing or a glow, not as a fin. Worse, that rim STOPS before the tail — the tail is a small separate yellow dart-spike with three stray dark whisker strands trailing off it, so the fringe never wraps the tail as the reference requires. Secondary problems: the belly lobe sitting under the pectoral fan reads as a paired ventral fin, undercutting 'no pelvic fins'; the skin is covered in an even ruled grid of dark dots and dashes that reads as woven cloth or a corn cob rather than wet unscaled eel skin; and the eye is an oversized white cartoon ring.
rows.fix: Rebuild the silhouette as an anguilliform: give the axis a real travelling S-curve, hold a near-constant body depth for the front two-thirds before tapering, thicken and blunt the head into a distinct wedge-shaped skull with a deep down-turned jaw line and a small dark eye — then delete the dart tail and the stray whiskers and replace the grey rim with a single opaque, clearly-colored fin membrane that runs unbroken from mid-back around the pointed tail tip and forward along the belly.

rows.readsAs: a pale tan plush quadruped -- most people would guess llama or a cartoon donkey before horse, and nobody would say Przewalski's
rows.defect: All three must-reads are absent. There is NO mane: the neck crest is completely bare from poll to withers, so the stiff upright brush that IS the Przewalski identity does not exist, and there is no dark dorsal stripe. The body is not stocky on short legs -- it is a shallow barrel on four long slender tubes with no joints, so it reads leggy and light. The head is small, not large and heavy. On top of that the render is broken in three places: a single dark triangular ear is fused into a big triangular cheek facet so it reads as a shading error or a horn stub; the eye is an oversized googly eyeball with a white sclera ring; and a stray pale bar crosses the muzzle and protrudes beyond the nose like a stick in the mouth. The tail is a fox-style fan brush shot out horizontally over a flat pasted-on ellipse at the hip, not a horse's long hanging tail.
rows.fix: Build the erect brush mane as a standing hair ridge running the full neck crest from poll to withers, add the dark dorsal stripe, and replace the fan-brush tail with a long hanging horse tail from a rump that is modelled rather than a pasted ellipse.

rows.readsAs: a shaggy sheep or a highland goat that has been given a long muzzle -- the all-over fleece dominates and no one names a pony
rows.defect: The identity must-read is missing: there is no mane and no forelock. The long hair is sprayed uniformly over the flanks, belly and shoulder as a fleece, while the neck crest and the forehead are bare -- the eye is fully exposed with nothing hanging over it -- so the shag reads as sheep wool rather than pony mane. The legs are the same long jointless tubes as the Wild Horse, so the short-leg-under-deep-barrel contrast the note asks for is not there; the fleece merely pads the barrel outward instead of the legs shortening. The head is the same blob as the horse's, not broad-browed. It also inherits every construction fault of the shared chassis: one dark triangle ear welded into a cheek facet, an oversized googly eyeball, a stray plank across the muzzle protruding past the nose, and a flat opaque ellipse pasted over the hip with a horizontal fan-brush tail.
rows.fix: Move the long-hair mass off the flanks and onto the neck crest and forehead as a heavy falling mane plus a forelock that overhangs the eye, and shorten the legs by roughly a quarter so the deep barrel sits low to the ground.

rows.readsAs: a barracuda or a pike — a generic slim olive predator fish
rows.defect: The chin barbel — the single feature that says 'cod' — is completely absent; there is no mouth line at all, just the point where the two body arcs meet, so the projecting upper jaw cannot be read either. The cod's three separate dorsal fins are replaced by two soft rounded olive humps painted BEHIND the body so they read as ghost lobes bulging from under the topline rather than fins on the back, and a matching unattached blob hangs below the belly. The forked tail and large eye are correct.
rows.fix: Draw a short barbel hanging from the lower jaw at the chin, add a real mouth line with the upper jaw overhanging it, and move the dorsal fins IN FRONT of the body fill so they attach to the topline as three separate fins.

rows.readsAs: a sand lance or needlefish — a pale ribbon-shaped fish with an eye
rows.defect: It HAS AN EYE. A bright white sclera ring with a black pupil is drawn on the snout, and at this scale it is the most conspicuous mark on the head — the exact opposite of the must-read 'smooth blank eyeless head'. Beyond that the body is a 4:1 pencil-thin ribbon rather than a tetra shape, there is no dorsal fin on the topline at all, the tail is a small squared-off grey paddle rather than a fork, and the only visible fins are one oversized pale wedge and a grey triangle overlapping each other mid-flank.
rows.fix: Delete the eye entirely and replace it with unbroken skin over a slightly domed cheek, then shorten the body to a tetra's 3:1 with a proper triangular dorsal on the back and a forked caudal.
rows.verifyWhy:
FAIL upheld, but two of the stated causes are wrong in ways that would misdirect the fix.

WHAT I SAW (440x440 png, crops at 5x/12x/16x, plus a pixel column-profile of the silhouette).

1. THE EYE — CONFIRMED, and it is the single loudest mark on the animal. At approx (316,189) in the 440px frame there is a thick cream/near-white circular eye-ring roughly 7px across enclosing a solid near-black pupil. Against a pale pink-cream flank it is the highest-contrast pixel cluster anywhere on the creature, higher contrast than the tail. Minor correction to the claim: it is NOT 'on the snout' — it sits on the cheek/head plate about 10px behind the snout tip, set high, in the anatomically correct place for a normal fish eye. That makes it worse, not better: it is not a stray speck, it is a deliberately drawn, ringed, pupilled eye. mustRead #1 'smooth blank eyeless head' and eyes:hidden are inverted outright.

2. ASPECT — the claim of '4:1' UNDERSTATES it by half. The non-background bounding box measures 214 x 26 px, i.e. 8.2:1 overall; the trunk alone (tail base x~150 to snout x~326, max depth 26px) is still 6.8:1. Spec aspect is 4. It is roughly twice as elongate as it should be, which is why it silhouettes as a lance and not as a tetra.

3. 'NO DORSAL FIN AT ALL' — WRONG AS STATED, right in effect. Two fins ARE drawn on the flank: a grey triangle with its apex touching the topline spanning about x248-266, and a pale rounded, backswept fin below and behind it about x266-288 that just grazes the belly line. Both are painted FLAT ON THE FLANK; neither breaks the silhouette. A column-by-column scan of the topline runs monotone smooth from y192 at the tail through a y183 crest to y189 at the snout with no spike anywhere. So the defect to fix is 'fins are inboard decals that do not break the outline', not 'fins are missing'. There is no anal fin and no visible pectoral separate from those two.

4. TAIL — CONFIRMED. A mid-grey, blunt truncate paddle, near-rectangular with a slightly rounded rear edge and faint ray striations, no fork, no notch, no lobes. It is also off-palette: mid grey on a pink-cream body, as are the two flank fins.

5. WHAT ACTUALLY PASSES — mustRead #2 does read. The flank is genuinely pale unpigmented pink-cream with fine regular vertical scale-row hatching and no banding or dark markings. That is the one identity cue delivered.

6. READS-AS — agreed with the judge: pointed at both ends, unbroken topline, truncate grey caudal, ringed eye. That is a sand lance (Ammodytes) or a small silvery lance-baitfish, not a pale eyeless cave characin. Also note headFrac: the plain head plate begins around x305, so the head is roughly 21 of 214 px (~0.10) against a spec headFrac of 0.28 — the head is far too short as well.

BAND: FAIL. Two of three must-reads fail, and the primary one fails by inversion rather than by omission — the asset draws the exact feature whose absence is the species' identity.

rows.readsAs: a pale pink perch or wrasse with a normal staring eye
rows.defect: It HAS AN EYE — a white ring with a black pupil sitting right on the snout, which directly contradicts the must-read 'completely eyeless smooth head'. The flesh is pale pink but flat and opaque: no translucency, no visible internals, just the same hexagonal scale stipple the whole family wears. The body is a deep rhomboid rather than streamlined, the dorsal is a dark brown wedge floating behind and above the back with black gaps under it, and the tail is a broad rounded fan attached only at a single point.
rows.fix: Remove the eye and paint the socket area as smooth continuous skin, then thin the body toward streamlined and let a spine and gut show faintly through the flank so the flesh reads translucent.
rows.verifyWhy: Verified at 8-10x crops and by direct pixel sampling of the 440x440 PNG. MUST-READ 1 'completely eyeless smooth head' - VIOLATED, and the other judge's description of it is accurate but understates how badly it is placed. There is a small ring roughly 7px across centred at approx (286,195), i.e. on the upper snout well forward of the gill line. Sampled pixels: the ring is near-white (E3E0DA, EFEBE1, F3EFE4, DDDCDC) and it encloses a core of 0C0F14 / 0E1116, which is the page background colour (090E14) - so the 'pupil' is literally a hole punched through the body to the void, not a painted dark iris. It is the only pure-white element anywhere in the frame, so despite being tiny it is the first thing the eye lands on and it unambiguously reads as an eye. Worse: only its lower half overlaps the pink flesh; the top half sits OUTSIDE the silhouette against black (at x=278-283, y=192-193 the pixels are background/edge-dark), so it reads as a white ring stuck onto the nose and breaking the snout contour, not as a seated eye. The head is otherwise smooth. FIX = delete the eye glyph entirely for eyes:hidden, do not merely dim it or move it. MUST-READ 2 'pale pink translucent flesh with visible internals' - VIOLATED, other judge correct. Body pixels sample at alpha=255 throughout (E5BEB7, DFACA4, EEC4BB, EEB9AF): fully opaque flat salmon pink. Surface carries a fine light checkerboard scale grid and a paler dorsal band, but there is zero backlight, zero background bleed-through, and no spine, skull, swim bladder, gut shadow or any other internal form. The only interior marks are a solid dark triangular pectoral fin mid-flank and a curved dark operculum/gill line behind the head - both surface features, not internals. MUST-READ 3 'ordinary streamlined fish body and fins' - partially met: the silhouette is a clean streamlined lens with correct 4:1 aspect and a plausible headFrac, and the fin set is dorsal + pectoral + caudal (no anal or pelvic visible, which is thin but not fatal). CORRECTION to the other judge on the dorsal: their description is wrong. The dorsal is NOT a wedge floating above the back and there are NO black gaps beneath it - it is a smooth, rounded, fully attached dark-mauve dome sitting directly on the dorsal contour, with a light rim where it meets the pale back, no separation whatsoever. What they saw as gaps is ABOVE the fin: a set of near-black vertical fin-ray strokes drawn at almost exactly the background value that extend past the dome's outline into the void, so the fin's top edge reads notched/ragged and the rays read as slits in the sky rather than as rays. Two real defects there, but neither is 'floating': (a) the rays are too dark to be legible against a dark background and should be lighter than the fin, (b) the dorsal and the caudal are the darkest objects in the picture (dark mauve/brown) on a species whose whole identity is unpigmented pallor - the fins should be paler and semi-transparent, not the most saturated masses in the frame. Also for the fix pass: the caudal is a squared-off rectangular paddle with hard corners joined to the body at a pinpoint peduncle, which reads as a stuck-on block rather than a fin. FAIL upheld - the single defining identity trait (eyeless) is contradicted by the most conspicuous mark on the asset, and the second must-read (translucent flesh with visible internals) is wholly absent; as drawn this is a generic opaque pink minnow with an eye.

rows.readsAs: a blue cartoon fish wearing a crown — the dorsal reads as a comb or a paper crown, not a fin
rows.defect: The identity must-read, the single long dorsal that is spiny in front and soft behind, is not drawn. What is there is a row of five isolated sharp triangles hovering ABOVE the back with black sky between every spike and black sky behind the last one — no connecting membrane, no soft posterior lobe, and no contact with the topline. The tail is a rounded fan sitting off the end of the peduncle with a visible dark gap, so it reads detached; there are no pointed trailing fin tips anywhere. The face has no thick lips and no sloping forehead — the head is just the pointed end of the body lens with an eye stuck on. It is the Reef Fish drawing recoloured blue.
rows.fix: Replace the floating spike row with one continuous dorsal fin membrane anchored to the topline from the nape to the peduncle — spiny rays in front, a taller rounded soft lobe with a drawn-out point behind — and give the head a blunt sloping forehead and a thick-lipped mouth.
rows.verifyWhy: Verdict upheld, but two of the three stated causes are factually wrong and must not be fixed as described. WHAT IS ACTUALLY THERE (440x440 PNG, fish faces RIGHT; ink bbox x124-315 y107-272 plus a cast shadow to y323; bright body bbox 159x117 px): a deep, almost circular blue body with banded scale texture, a clean lateral line, a stippled cheek/operculum, a small pectoral fan behind the gill, a tiny ventral nub under the belly, and a prominent white-ringed dark-pupil eye. CORRECTION 1 - the dorsal is NOT 'five isolated triangles with black sky between every spike and no membrane'. Zoomed 12x, it is ONE continuous solid dark-blue membrane spanning roughly the middle 55% of the back; the five spikes are V-notches cut into its TOP edge and the notches bottom out at about 45% of the fin's visible height, leaving an unbroken slab below them. There is no black gap between fin and back either - the slab runs down BEHIND the body and the body's dorsal outline crosses in front of it. The judge's conclusion (it reads as a paper crown) is right; their reason is not. The real defects are: (a) the top edge is the same uniform saw motif end to end, so there is no spiny-front / soft-behind differentiation at all - no rounded soft posterior lobe anywhere; (b) the differentiation that does exist is INVERTED - the tallest, sharpest teeth are at the REAR (left) and the teeth step DOWN toward the head (right); (c) the notches are battlement-deep and square-shouldered, which is what produces the crown/comb read; (d) the fin is a flat dark placard layered behind the silhouette instead of rising out of the dorsal ridge, so it never fuses with the back. CORRECTION 2 - the tail is NOT 'sitting off the peduncle with a visible gap'. At 12x the caudal's radiating ray lines converge to a point that lands exactly ON the body outline; the attachment is contiguous. The dark wedges the judge read as a gap are the normal voids above and below where the fan diverges from the round body - they look wrong because there is NO caudal peduncle at all: the fan is pinned point-first to the edge of a full oval. The tail itself is a blunt truncate fan with rounded corners, which is defensible for a cichlid (oscars/convicts have rounded caudals); the packet's 'pointed trailing fin tips' is missed elsewhere - no dorsal or anal trailing filament extends past the peduncle, and there is effectively no anal fin, only a vestigial nub. CONFIRMED 3 - the head claim is right and understated: there is no mouth AT ALL, not merely no lips. The snout is a plain rounded taper with a smooth convex forehead; the only marks forward of the eye are a faint cheek crease and a faint brow arc. No jaw line, no lip mass, no steep nuchal slope. Scoring against mustRead 'single long dorsal fin, spiny in front and soft behind / deep oval body with pointed trailing fin tips / thick-lipped sloping face': only 'deep oval body' lands, and even that overshoots - body aspect is ~1.36 and full-silhouette aspect ~1.16 against a spec aspect of 2.4, so the animal reads as a discus or butterflyfish disc rather than a cichlid. Dorsal differentiation, pointed trailing tips, thick lips and sloping face are all absent. FAIL stands: the fixes needed are a re-drawn dorsal (short stiff spines forward, taller soft rounded lobe aft, membrane fused to and rising from the back contour), a real mouth with a thickened lower lip on a steeper forehead, pointed trailing tips on soft dorsal and anal, a defined anal fin, a short caudal peduncle, and a body stretched toward the 2.4 spec - that is most of the identity kit, not polish.

rows.readsAs: a plain pink pond fish; nothing about it says reef
rows.defect: Two of the three must-reads are absent. There is no bright banded colour — the flank is a single flat pink with a scale stipple and one white lateral stripe, zero bars, zero contrasting bands. And the tail is not forked: it is a rounded fan, and it floats off the tip of the peduncle with a black gap so it reads as a stranded shape rather than an attached caudal. The body is a fat almond rather than a laterally flattened disc, and the dorsal is the same detached row of hovering triangular spikes as the Cichlid — this is the Cichlid drawing recoloured pink.
rows.fix: Paint two or three hard vertical contrast bands across the flank and rebuild the tail as an attached forked caudal with two pointed lobes and a clear central notch.
rows.verifyWhy:
Verdict upheld, but two of the stated causes need correcting. Looked at the 440x440 native PNG, then at 4x/6x/8x crops of body, tail junction and head, plus a column-mean RGB scan of the flank (rows 185-245, cols 165-295), plus a side-by-side of the family-mate Cichlid.

MUST-READ 1 - 'deep laterally flattened disc body': PRESENT, and this is the one the judge did not dispute and should not. Measured silhouette bbox 173x126 px (aspect 1.37 with fins; body oval alone ~146x97 = 1.50), which is DEEPER than the packet's aspect 1.9 target. It genuinely reads as a disc/plate-shaped perch. So the asset is not failing on shape.

MUST-READ 2 - 'bright banded colour': ABSENT. Correction to the judge's wording: it is not literally 'zero bars'. The column scan shows a real periodic vertical light/dark ripple, period ~17 px, about ten cycles across the flank - peaks at x=192/209/226/243/259/276 (mean R 208-221) against troughs at x=183/201/218/235/251/267 (mean R 159-168). But the RGB ratio is constant across peak and trough (R:G ~2.05:1 at both, e.g. 221,110,140 vs 168,86,106), i.e. it is a pure luminance modulation of ONE pink hue, amplitude ~15%. It is the scale-row stipple shading, not colour banding, and at 1:1 it reads as scale texture. There is no second colour anywhere on the fish - no contrasting bar, no eye-stripe, no saddle, no yellow/white/black field. The pink is also muted rose (peak R only ~215 with G~105), not 'bright'. So the judge's conclusion is right; the phrase 'zero bars' is the only overstatement.

MUST-READ 3 - 'forked tail': ABSENT, and the judge understates how clear-cut it is. At 8x the caudal is a broad paddle whose trailing edge is CONVEX - it bulges outward. Not forked, not even truncate or lunate: there is no notch, no lobes, no concavity of any kind, just a rounded fan crossed by six radiating ray lines.

CORRECTION to 'floating off the peduncle tip': the fin is NOT detached. At 8x the fan's base clearly overlaps the body's flank with no gap between them. The actual defect is different and should be fixed as such: the deep oval body has NO caudal peduncle at all - it just ends in a wide rounded flank, and the fan is pasted flat onto that curve so the fin's straight base edge cuts across the body outline. Attached but unarticulated, not floating.

CHASSIS: the judge's 'it is the Cichlid drawing recoloured pink' is CONFIRMED by direct comparison. Cichlid and Reef Fish share the identical deep-oval body outline, the identical four-tooth triangular spike crown standing above the topline, the identical rounded caudal fan with the same six ray lines, the same eye (white ring, black pupil) at the same relative position, the same lip line, the same small triangular pectoral, the same anal fin, and the same scale stipple with the same pale horizontal lateral-line streak. Only the hue differs. Note the spike crown itself is a defect for both: its base is hidden behind the body so it reads as a floating serrated crown rather than a dorsal fin rising off the back - for an anthias/damselfish it should be a continuous fin along the topline, spiny in front and soft behind.

NET: one of three must-reads present, two absent, and the drawing is a hue-swap of a family-mate. Nothing in the image says 'reef'. FAIL stands. Fix order: (1) recut the caudal into a deeply forked tail on an actual narrowed peduncle, (2) give it a genuine second colour - high-contrast vertical bars or a bright bicolour field, not luminance ripple, (3) replace the floating spike crown with a continuous dorsal fin so it stops being the Cichlid.

rows.readsAs: a small silvery baitfish — a minnow or a herring
rows.defect: All three must-reads are legible: streamlined silvery body, a dorsal on the mid-back, and a properly forked tail with two clean lobes and a notch. The flaws are chassis flaws, not identity flaws — the dorsal is painted behind the body fill so only a dim grey ridge shows above the topline, the anal fin is a formless grey ghost lobe under the belly with no attachment, and the body is a touch deeper than a minnow's. It is also the Arctic Cod drawing in silver.
rows.fix: Move the dorsal and anal in front of the body fill so they attach to the outline as shaped fins instead of half-hidden smudges.

rows.readsAs: a speckled pebble or a flat bread roll with a cartoon face; at second glance a generic cartoon flatfish
rows.defect: The two-eyes-on-one-side cue does land, but the head does not exist as a region at all - no snout, no jaw line, no gill, no operculum, so the eyes float in the middle of an undifferentiated oval instead of sitting on a head. The must-read fin skirt is drawn as a hard uniform grey rim with regular radial ticks, which reads as pie-crust edging or stitching rather than a continuous fin fringe of rays. The twisted asymmetric mouth is only a 4 px hooked tick with no jaw structure behind it, so the asymmetry is invisible unless you are told to look for it. There is also no pectoral fin and no eye-side/blind-side tone split.
rows.fix: Replace the ticked rim with a soft translucent fin skirt whose rays fan out from an inner ray-base line and whose outer edge ripples irregularly, and cut a visible head zone into the front third with a gill slit and a slanted, off-centre jaw so the twisted mouth reads.

rows.readsAs: an oval wooden platter or a dark serving dish with two eyes painted on it
rows.defect: The stated must-read - a diamond-elongate flatfish outline - is absent: this is a mathematically plain ellipse with no snout point, no widest-point at mid-body, no dorsal or anal fin swell, and no caudal peduncle. Stretching the Flounder ellipse to 2.1 made the failure worse, because the constant-width ticked grey rim now reads unmistakably as the raised lip of a platter and the flat, nearly unspeckled brown interior reads as the dish surface inside it. The tail is a tiny fan tacked onto the outside of that rim at the far right and looks like a separate pasted object, not a continuation of the body. No head, no gill, no jaw; the mouth is a single tick.
rows.fix: Rebuild the silhouette as a true rhomboid flatfish - pointed snout, widest at mid-body, tapering to a narrow caudal peduncle before the tail - and merge the fin fringe into that outline as soft rays rather than a constant-width rim band.

rows.readsAs: a dark grey cartoon quail or a black hen with a topknot
rows.defect: Every one of the three must-reads is missing. There is no bony helmet casque — in its place is a tiny sprig of three black quills on the crown that reads as a hoopoe/quail topknot. The neck is flat slate grey with no vivid blue anywhere and no red hanging wattles at all. The plumage is the family's scalloped scale texture with a stippled lower half, not glossy hair-like black. Underneath it is the shared egg body, shared belly medallion, shared blob wing and shared yellow stick legs, so it is simply the Emu render tinted dark.
rows.fix: Replace the quill sprig with a tall solid keratin casque rising off the forehead and continuing down the bill ridge, and repaint the whole neck vivid cobalt-and-turquoise with two red wattles hanging free below the throat.
rows.verifyWhy:
UPHELD. Zero of the three must-reads are present, confirmed by eye at 4-5x crops and by pixel scan of the whole 440x440 image.

(1) CASQUE - ABSENT. Head crop (src 110,10 120x100 @4x) shows a plain smooth circular skull ball with a flat yellow triangular beak pinned to its front. There is no form of any kind above or behind the beak: no keratin blade, no forehead ridge, no break in the skull silhouette, which is an unbroken circle. What is there is a crest of thin curved filaments. CORRECTION to the original claim: it is 4-5 quills, not three, and they sprout from the top-REAR of the skull and arc backward/rightward, clear of the crown apex - so it reads as a hoopoe/secretary-bird/roadrunner crest, exactly as claimed, but the shape and count were described loosely. A casque must be a solid tall wedge rising from the base of the bill, forward-set and continuous with the skull outline; nothing occupies that region.

(2) BLUE NECK + RED WATTLES - ABSENT. Neck crop (src 140,60 90x100 @5x) shows an unmodulated cylinder with no lobes, no dewlaps, no colour break anywhere between skull and shoulder. Full-image pixel scan: ZERO pixels anywhere in the file satisfy red (r>90 and r>1.6g and r>1.6b) - there is no red in this asset at all, so 'no red hanging wattles' is exactly right. PARTIAL CORRECTION to 'the neck is flat slate grey': measured neck RGB is (31,39,51), which IS blue-biased in hue, but at ~20% value / ~39% saturation it reads as near-black slate. So a token blue tint exists; the failure is that it is nowhere near vivid - zero pixels in the image qualify as saturated blue (b>90 and b>1.5r and b>1.3g). Only three hues exist in the whole render: dark blue-slate body, gold beak/legs (224,177,60), and a white eye dot.

(3) GLOSSY HAIR-LIKE PLUMAGE - ABSENT. The body wears the family's scalloped leaf/plume-scale texture with a speckle-dot field down the left flank. It reads as layered feather scales, not draped hair filaments, and there is no specular sheen anywhere on the body. Claim correct.

SHARED-CHASSIS CLAIM - CONFIRMED AND STRONGER THAN STATED. Cropping Cassowary.png and Emu.png at IDENTICAL source coordinates (150,140 160x130) returns the same scallop rows in the same positions, the same flank speckle field, the same circular hatched belly medallion inside the same dark ring at the same pixel, the same rim-lit egg outline, the same lower-right wing blob, and the same pair of gold stick legs with the same flat two-bar toes. The head crops share the same ball skull, the same gold triangle beak and the same eye + highlight dot. The ONLY differences from Emu are palette (dark blue-slate vs warm tan), the added crest quills, and a marginally narrower body. This is a recolour, not a species.

DEFECTS THE ORIGINAL JUDGE DID NOT NAME, needed for the fix: the legs are thin gold sticks - a cassowary's are massive, thick, dark grey-blue, scaled, and carry a dagger claw on the inner toe; none of that is present, and the gold is flatly wrong for the species. The feet are flat horizontal bars, not a three-toed splay. Proportion is also wrong in the same direction as the recolour: aspect 0.95 asks for a bulky near-square barrel, but this is a tall egg on a long thin neck - an emu/ostrich carriage, not the low, deep, hunched cassowary body. FAIL stands.

rows.readsAs: a generic tan ratite — could equally be captioned rhea or ostrich
rows.defect: The shaggy drooping double plumage is absent; the body wears the family's hard scalloped chevron scale texture with no loose hanging strands breaking the silhouette. The neck is short for an emu and is feathered tan rather than bare blue-grey. A wing blob IS visible at the lower right, contradicting 'no visible wings'. The legs and three toes are right. Its worst problem is that it is pixel-for-pixel the Rhea render at a warmer tint.
rows.fix: Break the egg outline with long drooping hair-strand plumage overhanging the flanks, and strip the neck to bare blue-grey skin with sparse black filoplumes.

rows.readsAs: a green chick or a lime-coloured quail — nothing about it says parrot
rows.defect: The two features that make a kakapo are both absent. There is no owl-like whiskered facial disc: the head is the family's small round skull with a single dot eye and no disc, no rictal bristles. There is no parrot bill either — it wears the same short yellow triangular wedge as the ostrich and the emu, where a kakapo needs a large pale deeply hooked bill with a fleshy cere. The mottling is the shared chevron scale map recoloured green, not black-and-yellow barring on moss. Body, medallion, wing blob and toes are the shared chassis with short legs.
rows.fix: Give it a broad pale hooked parrot bill set into a flat forward-facing feather disc fringed with whisker bristles, and turn the head to a three-quarter front view so the disc reads.
rows.verifyWhy:
Looked at the 440x440 full-size render, then re-read the head at 9x (crop x135 y90 w80 h60) and again as a contrast-stretched greyscale at 7x to kill the hue and expose any faint linework, plus the feet at 5x and the whole body at 3x stretched.

WHAT THE JUDGE GOT WRONG — THE BILL. Their claim that it 'wears the identical short yellow triangular wedge as the emu and ostrich' is flatly false and must not be actioned. I cropped the Emu head at 7x for a side-by-side. The emu's bill is a thin flat isoceles triangle: a straight upper edge, a straight lower mandible, tip a sharp horizontal point. The kakapo's is a genuinely different shape — a tall deep-based yellow-orange mass filling the front third of the skull, whose upper mandible sweeps forward and then curves DOWN past the gape line and terminates in a rounded downward hook that hangs below the level of the lower jaw. There is a separate small dark-green lower mandible/chin wedge tucked under it. That is a hooked parrot bill, and it is the ONE must-read element on this asset that is present and reading correctly. 'Nothing parrot about it' is wrong: the bill alone says parrot at full size, unzoomed.

WHAT THE JUDGE GOT RIGHT — THE FACE. There is no owl-like whiskered facial disc, and I confirmed this the hard way rather than by glance. Under the contrast stretch (luma range 9.7-225.1, so any drawn line would show) the head is a completely smooth sphere with a single soft top-left lighting gradient. No disc rim, no radial feather rays, no vertical facial split, no rictal/whisker bristles anywhere at the bill base or under the chin. The one pale feature people might mistake for a facial patch is a soft cream ELLIPSE sitting up and forward on the skull with a tiny black comma pupil clipped to its lower-right edge — that is the eye highlight blob (the Emu carries the same white specular, just small and inside a dark iris), not a disc. It has no rim, no mirrored counterpart, and covers only ~15 percent of the head. Must-read 2 is genuinely absent.

COLOUR / PATTERN — the judge is right in substance, imprecise in detail. It is NOT a bare recolour of the chevron map alone: the shared body texture actually carries two layers, the scalloped chevron bands down the centre/right of the egg AND a real speckle field of small oval dots down the left flank, so 'mottling' as a MARK exists. What is missing is the colour logic — every mark is a lighter green on a mid green, one hue, low contrast. There is no black barring and no yellow flecking anywhere on the body, so the moss-camouflage read never lands and the bird flattens to a single lime tone.

CHASSIS — unchanged from the Emu, which is the underlying cause of both misses. Same egg body, same circular scribble-textured wing disc parked mid-flank, same rounded tail nub at the lower right, same yellow three-toes-forward-plus-hind-spur feet (not the zygodactyl 2+2 a parrot has, though the packet does not demand it). Only the neck differs usefully: it is short and thick so the head sits almost on the shoulders, which is correct for the heavy squat parrot body of must-read 3, and that one does read.

BAND. Must-read 1 partial (green and mottled, but wrong palette, no black/yellow), must-read 2 absent outright, must-read 3 present. The absent one is the defining one — kakapo is the owl parrot and the face is why. As drawn it resolves to a generic plump green parrot, not a kakapo, so FAIL stands. FIX ORDER: (1) build the facial disc — a flat pale-olive saucer around each eye with radiating fine feather rays and a soft rim, plus a fan of dark whisker bristles projecting forward from the bill base over the mandible; (2) repaint the body pattern in black transverse bars with yellow-ochre flecking over moss green instead of green-on-green; (3) shrink the oversized cream eye blob to a small dark eye so the disc, not the highlight, owns the face. DO NOT touch the bill — it is already right.

rows.readsAs: a kiwi, immediately and unprompted
