rows.defect: All three must-reads land: the long slender down-curved probing bill is roughly a third of the body, the body is a round tailless mound of genuine hair-like strokes with loose strands breaking the outline, and the legs sit well back under the rear of the body. Only two soft notes: the plumage is olive-green rather than kiwi brown, and the legs are spindly where a kiwi's are stout and heavy-boned.
rows.fix: Thicken the legs and tarsi to stout heavy props and warm the plumage toward brown-grey; leave the silhouette alone.

rows.readsAs: a dark turkey or a peahen — the stiff barred fan tail dominates and names the bird wrongly
rows.defect: The neck is not remotely ostrich-long: it reads about a fifth of total height where an ostrich neck is roughly half, and it ends in the family's round skull with the standard yellow triangle beak, not a tiny flat head on a bare pink-grey column. The 'fluffy plume wings and tail bustle' is rendered as a hard-edged fan of separated pointed barred feathers spread stiffly to the right — that is a turkey's or peacock's fan, not a soft bustle of loose plumes. The legs are thin yellow sticks with three splayed toes, so the two-toed powerful leg is absent too. The shared blob wing and belly medallion are still visible beneath the fan.
rows.fix: Double the neck length and strip it bare to a thin pink-grey column topped by a small flat head, and replace the stiff barred fan with a soft loose bustle of drooping white-tipped plumes.
rows.verifyWhy:
Upheld, but several stated causes are wrong and the real proportion defect is worse than reported. Measured from a per-row alpha scan of the 440x440 PNG (bg 5,6,12; threshold 40): creature occupies y=19..409, total height ~390px. HEAD+BEAK y=19..78 (~15% of height, spec headFrac 0.12 - acceptable). FREE-STANDING BARE NECK y=82..122, a constant 16-17px-wide column: only ~40px = ~10% of total height, NOT 'about a fifth' as claimed. An ostrich neck is ~40-45% of standing height, so this is off by 4x, not 2x. BODY y=124..355 = 231px = 59% of total height - the egg-shaped body is the single dominant mass and is the root cause of every proportion failure. LEGS y=358..409 = ~51px = ~13% of height (should be ~45%). So the correct fix statement is: the neck must go from 10% to ~40% and the legs from 13% to ~45%, both stolen from a body that must shrink from 59% to ~30%.

HEAD (4x crop): a plain round ball, ~50px diameter, with a chunky wedge-shaped yellow-orange triangular beak that comes to a sharp point - not the ostrich's short broad blunt flat bill on a tiny flat skull. Judge is correct here. They MISSED an extra defect: a stray pale-grey hairline crescent arcs around the top-back of the skull (roughly x=140..160, y=25..75), a leftover generic rim/ear ring shape that does not belong on any bird head. Eye is a small white oval with a black pupil at the beak base - reads only marginally 'prominent'.

NECK: the column plunges into the body and is then drawn ON TOP of the breast as a thick dark-brown strap that crosses the upper body and terminates in a blunt rounded stub around y=200. It reads as a belt laid across the bird, not as a neck entering a shoulder. The neck is also the same brown as the head and body, so 'bare' does not read at all.

TAIL (3x crop): confirmed a stiff, hard-edged fan of ~7 discrete lozenge-shaped blades radiating from the rump out to x=369, each a flat solid fill with rounded tip and hard dark negative-space gaps between them - a turkey/peafowl display fan, not a soft plume bustle. CORRECTION: the blades are NOT 'barred'. They carry no internal pattern whatsoever; the barring/scallop texture the judge saw is on the BODY, in horizontal rows of chevron feather scallops. Cite the correct defect: solid hard-edged separated blades with visible gaps, where the ostrich needs a soft-edged mass of drooping filamentous plumes with no gaps and no individual feather outlines.

FEET (7x crop): CLAIM IS WRONG. These are NOT three-toed. Each foot is a simple two-prong T-bar - one long toe pointing forward and one short stub pointing backward (a hallux). So toe count is coincidentally near ostrich (2), but the arrangement is wrong: an ostrich has BOTH toes forward, the inner one huge with a hoof-like nail, and NO rear hallux. The real leg defect is not toe count but mass: both legs are uniform pencil-thin yellow sticks of constant ~8px width emerging straight from the bottom of the egg with zero thigh, zero drumstick, zero taper - the word 'powerful' in the must-read has no representation at all.

SHARED CHASSIS PARTS (confirmed, but mislocated by the judge): the belly medallion is NOT hidden under the fan. It is a ~90px circular bolted-on porthole - a raised ring with a cross-hatched disc inside - sitting dead centre of the flank at roughly x=155..245, y=205..295, about a quarter of the body width, completely unmissable. The wing is a flat speckled panel occupying the left/front third of the egg, edged by a pale hairline arc and dotted with pale ovoid speckles; it has no plume structure and does not read as a wing at all.

IDENTITY VERDICT: all three must-reads fail. 'extremely long bare neck with a tiny flat head' - absent (10% neck, round head, pointed beak). 'fluffy plume wings and tail bustle' - absent (flat speckled panel, hard-edged blade fan). 'long two-toed powerful legs' - absent (13%-of-height pencil sticks, forward toe + hallux). Dark speckled body plus a stiff fanned tail plus short thin legs reads as a turkey or guineafowl; the judge's 'dark turkey or peahen' read is correct. Nothing here refutes the FAIL.

rows.readsAs: a penguin
rows.defect: Posture, countershading and short rear-set yellow feet all read. But the stiff flipper wings held flat at the sides are missing — the near side has no flipper at all, and the far side shows only the family's grey rounded wing blob poking out at the lower right, identical to the one on the emu and rhea. The black back also still carries the shared scalloped scale texture, which gives a reptilian shingled look no penguin has, and the belly is a floating white oval rather than a countershading boundary that meets the flanks.
rows.fix: Draw a long narrow flat flipper hanging down the near flank from shoulder to hip and delete the round wing blob, then flatten the back texture to smooth packed plumage.

rows.readsAs: a pale generic ratite, indistinguishable from the Emu in this same batch
rows.defect: The long bare legs and three toes are correct and the tail is absent as it should be. But the head has a narrow pointed yellow beak where a rhea needs a small flat head with a broad blunt duck-like bill, the neck is feathered and too short for a bird whose height is supposed to be dominated by neck and legs, and the 'shaggy drooping wings' are just the shared small grey blob at the rear. Body proportion is the family egg, so it is taller-than-long only marginally.
rows.fix: Swap the pointed wedge for a broad blunt flattened bill and lengthen the neck so neck plus legs carry most of the height, then hang large shaggy drooping wing plumes over the flanks.

rows.readsAs: a flying fish - the three huge translucent wing planes are unmistakable and a stranger names it on sight
rows.defect: Two of the three must-reads miss. (1) The tail is NOT unevenly forked: at 7x the caudal fork is essentially symmetric - upper lobe tip and lower lobe tip reach the same posterior x and sit about the same distance above and below the peduncle midline, so the signature long lower lobe is absent. (2) The body is not blunt-nosed: the head tapers to a knife point, and the white ring eye is parked right at the apex sitting half off the outline with almost no snout in front of it - in isolation that profile reads needlefish or halfbeak, not the rounded bullet head of a flying fish. The eye also reads as a floating hoop rather than a seated eyeball.
rows.fix: Round the snout off ahead of the eye so the head ends in a blunt bullet and the eye sits fully inside the head, and rebuild the caudal as an uneven fork with the lower lobe about 1.6x the length of the upper.

rows.readsAs: a mudskipper - a yellow goby on a mudflat with periscope eyes; the identity does land
rows.defect: The eyes are right (two clean domed turrets riding on top of the skull) but the other two must-reads and the posture note do not. The body lies FLAT: the belly line is level on the mud and the front of the animal is not lifted at all, so nothing is propped. The single visible pectoral fin has a good arm-like muscular base and rayed fan blade, but it dangles below the ventral line into the shadow instead of planting on the ground and carrying weight - it looks hung on the fish, not standing on it. The two dorsals are present in count but wrong in form: they are short rounded humps barely clearing the back, not raised sails, and each has four grey spine sticks that overshoot the membrane and float free in the dark air beside and below the fin, reading as loose picket sticks or antennae rather than rays inside a fin.
rows.fix: Lift the front third of the body clear of the mud on a planted pectoral (fin tip on the ground line, belly visibly raised above it) and redraw the two dorsals as tall separate membrane sails, at least head-height, with the rays contained inside the membrane instead of overshooting it.

rows.readsAs: a bat
rows.defect: Reads as a bat unprompted - big paired ears on a small furry body, and the wing membranes do carry visible dark finger struts fanning to the leading edge, so two of three must-reads land. The third is absent: at 9x the torso simply ends in a rounded rump with a tiny notch. There are no hind legs and no uropatagium - no membrane spanning the hind limbs and tail, so the lower half of the animal is a blank capsule. The wing panels also read more as two creased umbrella/kite facets than as a hand: the struts are few and stop short of the trailing edge, so the fingers never fan all the way out.
rows.fix: Add the tail membrane: draw two short hind legs kicking back from the rump and stretch a triangular uropatagium between them and a visible tail spur, then extend the existing finger struts all the way to the trailing edge so each wing terminates in four distinct fingertips.

rows.readsAs: a spotted lamb or a piebald calf standing in a field
rows.defect: This is the wrong organism. There is no gliding membrane anywhere on it - not neck to wrist, not between the limbs, not enclosing the tail - and the patagium IS the colugo. It stands broadside on four separate columnar legs with clear air between them and a ground shadow under its feet, which is the exact opposite of the required flying posture, so it does not even read as a glider caught mid-glide. The eye is a single small side-mounted bead on a long tapering muzzle, not the huge round forward-facing eyes called for. The bare tail hangs down free of any membrane. Only the mottled fur must-read is present, and on this body it reads as cow or sheep piebalding rather than lichen camouflage.
rows.fix: Rebuild it off the quadruped chassis entirely: pose it spread-eagled and flattened toward the viewer, then fill every gap between the neck, the splayed fore and hind limbs and the tail tip with one continuous stretched membrane so the silhouette is a single kite with a head on it, and enlarge the eyes to huge forward-facing discs.

rows.readsAs: a generic cartoon smiley frog / plush toad — no stranger would say 'bullfrog'
rows.defect: None of the three must-reads is visible. There is no large circular eardrum disc behind the eye — only a vague soft olive blotch on each cheek that reads as a dirt smudge, not a tympanum, and certainly not bigger than the eye. The mouth is a small curled smile spanning under half the head width, not a very wide flat mouth line. The hind legs are thin leaf-shaped paddles running straight out sideways from the mid-flank to flat hand-like feet with separated pointed fingers — no muscular folded thigh, no webbing membrane between digits.
rows.fix: Draw a hard-edged circular tympanum disc behind and below each eye, sized larger than the eye with its own rim and a slightly different value from the cheek, then fold the hind limb into a Z (knee peaking above the body topline, ankle high) and fill the toes with a continuous webbing membrane instead of separate fingers.

rows.readsAs: the Bullfrog drawing recoloured pale mint — a mouldy cartoon frog, not a glass frog
rows.defect: The identity of this animal is absent: the body is fully OPAQUE. No translucency anywhere, no heart, no gut, no visible bone or organ silhouette through the underside, and the belly is not even differentiated from the back. The eyes are the same black-pupil, white-sclera domes as every other frog in the batch, set on top of the head pointing up and out, not forward-facing and not pale gold. The grey-green blotches scattered over the body actively read as mould or warts, the opposite of a smooth translucent glass frog. Silhouette, limb geometry, foot shape, mouth curve and shadow are identical to Bullfrog.png.
rows.fix: Rebuild the underside as a genuinely see-through pane — a lighter, desaturated belly field with a red heart shape and a coiled dark gut visibly rendered inside it — drop the grey blotching entirely, and turn the eyes into forward-facing pale gold discs with fine dark reticulation instead of the shared cartoon eyeball.

rows.readsAs: a red ladybird beetle or a shiny red jelly blob — it does not read as a frog at all
rows.defect: The render is broken. The whole face assembly has slid off-centre to the upper right of the body mass: one eye is a plain black disc with no sclera and no highlight while the other has a white ring, they sit crammed against the right edge of the silhouette, and the mouth is not a line but a chaotic dark smear with two black wedges spilling over the right cheek. The limbs are gone — reduced to four small flat red nubs at the base of the blob with no legs, no joints and no feet. The large round black spots on a glossy red dome read straight as ladybird elytra. There is also no bold striping and no readable frog snout.
rows.fix: Re-centre the head assembly on the body axis, give both eyes the same jet-black domed treatment with matching highlights, replace the smeared mouth with a single clean wide mouth line, and restore actual limbs — a slim foreleg and a compact folded hind leg — on a small smooth blunt-snouted body with crisp bold stripes rather than scattered round spots.

rows.readsAs: the Bullfrog drawing in brighter green — 'a frog', never 'a tree frog'
rows.defect: The feature the packet itself names as diagnostic is absent: there are NO adhesive toe discs. Every digit on all four feet ends in a thin point, on the forefeet and on the splayed hind feet alike — not one round pad anywhere. The hind legs are also wrong: instead of long limbs folded into tight Z-shapes they stretch out flat and straight sideways from the mid-flank, running off toward the frame edges like arms. Only 'bulging eyes set high on the head' is present, and those are the identical eye domes reused from the other three frogs. Body, topline, mouth curve, foot shape and shadow are the same asset as Bullfrog.png with the hue pushed to lime.
rows.fix: Terminate every toe in a distinctly oversized round adhesive disc, clearly wider than the toe itself, and rebuild the hind limb as a long tight Z — thigh up and back, knee breaking above the topline, shank forward, foot tucked under the flank — so the tree frog stops sharing the bullfrog's splayed sit.

rows.readsAs: a pale white cartoon frog / a ghost bath toy
rows.defect: The depigmented pallor is genuinely present and is the strongest read in the batch, but the must-read folded hind legs are not there — the haunches splay straight out sideways as flat horizontal wedges with no knee rising above the back, so nothing about it says crouched. There is also no wide flat head as broad as the body because there is no head at all: the cranium and torso are one undifferentiated egg.
rows.fix: Rebuild the hind limb as a folded Z — thigh angled up and back so the knee peaks above the dorsal line, shank folding forward, foot planted beside the body — instead of a horizontal wedge leaving the flank at 3 and 9 o'clock.

rows.readsAs: a green cartoon frog
rows.defect: A stranger does name 'frog', and the bulging eyes plus wide mouth line plus tailless body are present. But the must-read folded haunches with long hind legs are absent: the rear limbs are short flat wedges sticking straight out to either side at mid-flank, with no thigh volume and no raised knee, so the animal reads as splayed flat rather than coiled. The eyes also sit on the front face rather than on top of the skull.
rows.fix: Give the hind leg an actual folded haunch — a bulky thigh mass sitting against the flank with the knee apex above the topline — and raise the eye domes so they break the upper silhouette rather than sitting on the face.

rows.readsAs: the green Frog recoloured brown — a frog, not a toad
rows.defect: Every must-read that separates a toad from a frog is missing. The skin is not warty: it is the same smooth glossy gradient blob as the Frog with the same soft out-of-focus blotches, no bumps, no stippled dry texture. There is no swollen parotoid gland behind either eye — the head is clean. It is not squatter or shorter-legged: the hind limbs are the identical length and identical splay angle as the Frog's, the head is not broader or flatter, and the body is in fact rendered slightly SMALLER than the Frog rather than wider. Zero of the three must-reads survive, and the note's stated differentiation from a frog is entirely absent.
rows.fix: Give it a genuinely different body — widen and lower the mass into a hunched wedge, shorten the hind limbs to half the Frog's, add a hard-edged bumpy wart field across the dorsum, and paint a distinct raised kidney-shaped parotoid gland behind each eye.

rows.readsAs: the same cartoon frog in orange — no species identity at all
rows.defect: The black robber's mask through the eye — the one marking that IS a wood frog — is completely absent; the face is a uniform orange-brown with no dark band behind the eye whatsoever. The pale dorsolateral ridges are also absent: the back carries only the same generic blurred blotches as the other three, with no paired longitudinal lines. The long folded jumping legs are the shared splayed lateral wedges, not folded. All three must-reads are missing, leaving a hue swap of the Frog asset.
rows.fix: Paint the diagnostic dark mask as a hard-edged band running from the snout through the eye to behind the tympanum, and add two crisp pale ridges running the length of the back on either side of the spine.

rows.readsAs: a rosehip or wild-cherry bush - round red berries on bare twiggy stems
rows.defect: The harvest is five perfectly ROUND glossy red spheres with a small dark stalk nub on top. A chili's identity is a smooth tapering elongated pod hanging or pointing up from a green calyx cap, and none of that is present - no taper, no point, no calyx. The must-read white star flower with the purple-black anther ring is entirely absent; there is not a single flower in the render. The leaves are thin sliver lancets scattered sparsely along bare stems rather than smooth pointed OVALS, and the stems read as bare brown twigs rather than a many-branched bushy leafy habit, so the plant looks defoliated.
rows.fix: Replace the spheres with tapered pods - a wide shouldered top narrowing to a curved point over about three times their width - cap each with a small green five-lobed calyx and a short green stalk, and add two or three small white star flowers with a dark purple anther ring at leaf axils.

rows.readsAs: a watermelon or small gourd vine - or, from the leaf shape alone, a hemp plant
rows.defect: The single fruit is a small ROUND green sphere with pale vertical striping - it reads unmistakably as a watermelon, not a cucumber. The must-read warted ELONGATED fruit is absent: there is no length, no ridging and no warty bumps, just the same smooth specular ball used on the chili in a different hue. The yellow star flowers are entirely missing. The leaves are smooth-edged deeply cut STAR-LOBED palmate blades with clean glossy fills, not bristly heart-triangular lobed leaves, so they read as cannabis rather than cucurbit. The tendrils are the one must-read that lands. The vine also does not fill its 2:1 aspect - it sits as a narrow diagonal S with large empty margins on both sides.
rows.fix: Swap the sphere for a cylindrical fruit roughly four times longer than it is wide, hanging under a leaf, with lengthwise ridges and stippled dark warts, and add two or three five-petal yellow star flowers at the nodes; broaden the leaf to a heart-triangular blade with shallow lobes and a bristly stippled edge.

rows.readsAs: a plump golden chick with a spiky topknot
rows.defect: The comb reads as a 3-spike punk tuft sitting on the crown rather than a fleshy red serrated comb, and there are no wattles at all under the bill; the comb/wattle pair is the same tan as the body so nothing reads as bare red skin. The tail fan hangs level-to-drooping behind the bird instead of the short upswept fan called for. The wing is an abstract dark spiral that reads as a hole punched in the flank, not a folded wing.
rows.fix: Make the comb a red fleshy serrated blade fused to the top of the skull and hang two red wattle lobes under the bill, then rotate the tail fan up ~35 degrees so its base lifts above the topline.

rows.readsAs: a generic brown barnyard gamebird — indistinguishable from the Turkey card
rows.defect: The bill is a long straight yellow cone, the opposite of the short rounded gamebird bill in the must-reads. The legs are bare bright-yellow rods with no feathering whatsoever. The tail fan is flat untextured brown with no barring, and it droops below the body line rather than fanning. Side by side with Turkey.png this is essentially the same image at a slightly different tone.
rows.fix: Shorten and round the bill to a stubby dark curve and clothe the tarsi in shaggy feather lobes down to the toes, then band the tail fan with dark cross-bars.

rows.readsAs: a dark grey chick with a few white dots — a speckled pigeon
rows.defect: The identity feature is entirely absent: there is no bare skin anywhere, no bony helmet casque, no blue-and-red face, no red horn wattles. The head is the same fully feathered grey chick skull with the standard yellow bill used on every other card, and it is normal-sized rather than comically small. The neck is not thin or naked — head sits straight on the shoulder like the rest of the family. The white spotting is a sparse rim of dots outlining the wing, not the dense allover pearling that makes a guineafowl.
rows.fix: Replace the head with a tiny bare blue-and-red skull carrying a hard bony casque on the crown and red drop wattles, set it on a thin naked neck, and scatter dense even white pearl-dots across the whole body instead of only along the wing edge.

rows.readsAs: a dumpy tan chick — the Quail card without its topknot
rows.defect: The dumpy body and low short tail are there, but the bill is a straight pointed cone rather than the short curved gamebird bill, and the head/face carries no marking of any kind, so nothing separates this from the Quail, Chicken and Ptarmigan bodies except hue. The same dark spiral 'wing' artefact sits on the flank and reads as a gouge rather than a folded wing.
rows.fix: Give it a short down-curved grey bill plus a partridge face mark (dark eye-stripe and rufous throat patch) so the head is not the shared blank chick skull.

rows.readsAs: a teal chicken with gold dots on its tail
rows.defect: The train — the entire identity of a peacock — is not there. The tail is the SAME short drooping 5-lobe fan used on the Chicken and Turkey cards, no longer than the body, with a single flat gold disc stuck on each lobe tip; those are dots, not ocelli (no blue-black centre, no bronze-green surround). The bird's overall aspect is a round ball, nowhere near the requested 2.2 elongation. The neck and breast are not differentiated from the body — the whole bird is one flat teal, so there is no iridescent neck reading against a duller body. The crest is present but is the same 3-spike tuft the Chicken and Rooster wear, without wire stems or racket tips.
rows.fix: Draw a train that trails two-to-three body-lengths behind and below the bird, made of long overlapping barbs carrying multi-ring eyespots (blue-black pupil, bronze iris, green rim), and reserve the saturated iridescent blue for the neck and breast against a duller brown-green back.

rows.readsAs: a brown chick that has been handed a plank
rows.defect: All three must-reads are missing. The head is the plain tan feathered chick skull — no red bare facial wattle around the eye, no iridescent green-black hood, no white neck ring. The tail is not an extremely long pointed barred tail; it is a short blunt-ended flat brown plank about a third of the body length with a couple of faint bars, and it is stuck on at mid-flank so it reads as a detached board rather than as tail feathers growing from the rump.
rows.fix: Replace the tail with a long tapering pointed spike two body-lengths long, boldly cross-barred, rooted at the rump; then repaint the head bottle-green-black with a scarlet bare-skin mask around the eye and a crisp white collar at the base of the neck.

rows.readsAs: a white chick or a small white dove
rows.defect: The white winter plumage is present and correct, but the other two must-reads are absent: the feet are the family's bare bright-yellow scaly rods with no feathering at all, which is exactly backwards for the one gamebird defined by snowshoe-feathered toes, and there is no red comb above the eye — no red pigment appears anywhere on the card.
rows.fix: Bury the legs and toes in shaggy white feather boots so no bare scale shows, and add a small scarlet fleshy comb arc directly above the eye.

rows.readsAs: a quail
rows.defect: Reads correctly — round feathered-ball body, very short wedge tail, short legs, small head tucked to the shoulder, and the topknot helps. The only weakness is that this is the family's default chassis, so it passes partly because the chassis happens to be quail-shaped.
rows.fix: Curve the topknot plume forward over the bill instead of splaying it into three straight spikes, so it reads as a quail plume rather than the generic tuft shared with Chicken and Rooster.

rows.readsAs: a rust-red robin or a generic brown songbird
rows.defect: Nothing that makes a rooster is present. The comb is the same small 3-spike tuft as the Chicken and Quail, not a tall red blade; there are no wattles hanging from the chin. The tail is two straight flat planks angled backwards and DOWN — the exact opposite of arching sickle plumes, and the same part used on the Pheasant card. The posture is the family's horizontal ovoid, not an upright puffed chest, and there is no hackle cape at all — the neck-to-shoulder transition is the same smooth featureless join as every other card. Requested aspect 1.0 (upright/square) is ignored.
rows.fix: Stand the body up on longer legs so the breast faces forward, add a tall serrated red comb and two long red wattles, cape the shoulders in pointed hackle feathers, and replace the plank tail with two long sickle plumes that arch up above the topline and curve down behind.

rows.readsAs: a brown grouse — literally the Grouse card in a slightly darker tone
rows.defect: The head is a small fully-feathered brown chick skull with the standard yellow cone bill: no bare blue-and-red warty skin, no snood, no dangling wattle. There is no bristly beard on the breast. The tail is not a broad upright fan; it is the same drooping 5-lobe fan as the Chicken and Grouse, hanging below the body line. Nothing about the mass says turkey — the body is the same small round chick ovoid as the quail, not a heavy deep-breasted bird.
rows.fix: Replace the head with a small bare knobbly blue-and-red skull with a red snood drooping over the bill, hang a black bristle beard from the mid-breast, and raise the tail into a broad vertical semicircular fan standing above the topline.

rows.readsAs: a speckled easter egg or a river pebble with five holes drilled in a row
rows.defect: There is no animal here at all - just a smooth mint-green domed ellipse floating over a shadow. The huge muscular foot is absent, the frilly sensory tentacle fringe around the rim is absent, and the shell is a fat 3D egg rather than the flat ear-shaped plate an abalone is. The only must-read present is the row of five holes, and it sits on an egg. It is the identical stamp used for Cowrie and Limpet.
rows.fix: Flatten the shell into a low ear-shaped oval seen from above with the spire knob at the rear-left, and let a pale muscular foot bulge out all around the rim with a dense fringe of short tentacles along its edge.

rows.readsAs: a peeled banana or a yellow chilli lying on its side
rows.defect: The bright yellow shell-less loaf is right and it does carry slug mass, but the head end is a 5-pixel jagged crest - there is no pair of long upper eyestalks with eyes on the tips and no pair of short lower feelers, so the animal has no readable head. The pneumostome (breathing hole) on the mantle saddle is nowhere on the body, and the mantle saddle itself is not delineated from the tail.
rows.fix: Grow two long upper tentacles with dark bulbs at their tips and two short lower feelers from the head end, and cut a visible dark breathing hole into a raised mantle saddle over the front third.

rows.readsAs: a fossil ammonite, or a coiled rope mat
rows.defect: Wrong organism. It is a flat planispiral ridged disc - the same disc used for all six snails here - with no flared lip, no knobby pointed spire, and no stalked eyes; the packet calls for prominent eyes and there are none. There is also a stray unattached brown blob half-hidden behind the shell at the lower right and no foot at all, so the whole thing hangs in mid-air over its shadow.
rows.fix: Rebuild it as a heavy asymmetric shell with a stepped knobby spire at the top-left and a wide glossy pink flared lip sweeping down the right, and push two long stalked eyes out from under that lip.

rows.readsAs: a mottled orange egg with five holes punched in it - the Abalone in a different colour
rows.defect: This is the Abalone stamp recoloured apricot: same ellipse, same tilt, same row of five black holes in the same positions. Those holes are the abalone's diagnostic and they are anatomically wrong on a cowrie. The identity must-read - the long toothed slit running the length of the underside - is entirely absent, and so are the patterned mantle flaps folding up over the shell. Nothing is left that says cowrie.
rows.fix: Delete the hole row, view the shell from below-side so the full-length slit with its comb of teeth on both lips is the dominant feature, and lap two lobed patterned mantle flaps up over the shell from each side.

rows.readsAs: a snail, but on second look a small ammonite parked on a slipper sole
rows.defect: Coiled shell and gliding foot are both present and the silhouette does read snail-shaped, but the shell is a perfectly flat ammonite disc with no spire height and no aperture, and the pair of thin head tentacles is reduced to a 3-prong fork with no head behind it - the animal is a shell sitting on a lens with no body between them.
rows.fix: Wind the shell into a low helical cone so the spire steps back and up, and model an actual head lobe emerging from under it carrying two long thin separated tentacles.

rows.readsAs: a generic snail - indistinguishable from Snail, Water Snail, Sea Snail and Freshwater Snail except for the tan colour
rows.defect: The packet's explicit note is violated: there are no eyes at the tips of long upper tentacles, and there is no second pair of tentacles either - only the same 3-prong fork that every other shelled asset in this batch wears. The foot has no rippling sole, it is a plain flat lens with a hard edge. The shell is a flat coil, not carried up on the back.
rows.fix: Give it two long upper tentacles with visible dark eye bulbs at their tips plus two short lower feelers, and ripple the sole edge of the foot into a wave.

rows.readsAs: a tan egg with five holes in a row - the Abalone stamp again
rows.defect: Wrong organism, and every must-read is missing. There is no simple uncoiled cone shell, no radiating ribbed ridges, no off-centre apex, and it is not clamped flush against anything - it floats above a drop shadow with clear daylight underneath, which is the opposite of the sessile clamped read the packet asks for. What is drawn is the Abalone/Cowrie ellipse with the abalone hole row, recoloured tan.
rows.fix: Replace it entirely with a low ribbed cone seen from a shallow side angle, apex slightly off-centre, ribs radiating from apex to a scalloped rim, and seat the rim flat on a rock line with no gap or floating shadow.

rows.readsAs: a magenta sea slug, or a small punk hairbrush
rows.defect: The best asset in the batch - the comb of cerata on the back reads clearly and the brilliant shell-less body is right. But the cerata are drawn as flat straight quills with no branching or tips, so they read as bristles rather than gills, and the rhinophores are the same generic 5-pixel jagged crest reused from Banana Slug, not a pair of club-shaped horns. The body underneath is the identical flat-bottomed loaf used for the Banana Slug.
rows.fix: Replace the head crest with two distinct club-tipped rhinophore horns standing clear of the body, and taper and tip the cerata so they read as fleshy gill fingers.

rows.readsAs: a walnut-brown ammonite on a foot - the same drawing as Snail and Water Snail
rows.defect: Reads roughly as a snail, but the shell is not tightly coiled with a visible aperture - it is the flat ridged disc stamp, and no aperture opening is drawn anywhere. The siphon tube, which is what separates a sea snail from the land snails beside it, is completely absent, and the head tentacles are the shared 3-prong fork.
rows.fix: Open a dark aperture at the shell's lower right and run a distinct tubular siphon forward from it past the head tentacles.

rows.readsAs: a snail (the most generic reading in the batch) - or an ammonite shell resting on a slipper
rows.defect: Silhouette reads snail, but the two long eye tentacles plus two short feelers are collapsed into one small 3-prong fork with no eye bulbs on anything, and there is no head between shell and foot. The shell is a flat planispiral disc rather than a spire carried up on the back, and the foot is a hard-edged flat lens with no sole texture.
rows.fix: Separate the head token into two long eye-tipped tentacles and two short feelers on a visible head lobe, and raise the shell's coil into a spire so it is carried on the back rather than lying flat.

rows.readsAs: a brass-coloured snail, identical in every line to Snail and Land Snail
rows.defect: Nothing distinguishes it from four other assets in this batch except hue - same disc shell, same lens foot, same fork. The flat-coiled shell technically satisfies its must-read, but the pair of slender head tentacles is the shared 3-prong stub with no separation between the two tentacles and no head, and no aquatic cue (siphon, water context) marks it as a water snail at all.
rows.fix: Draw two clearly separate slender tentacles from a modelled head and add an aquatic tell such as a raised breathing siphon, so it cannot be confused with the land snails next to it.

rows.readsAs: a hollow gelatinous tube or tube sponge standing in the water - close to a pyrosome but a stranger may say sponge
rows.defect: The bioluminescence must-read is the wrong colour entirely - the tunic and its ambient halo are magenta/violet, with no cold blue anywhere in frame. The cone also tapers the wrong way: it is narrowest at the open rim and widest at the sealed lower end, where a pyrosome is widest at the open mouth and tapers to a closed point, and the bottom corners are squared off so it reads as a flat-bottomed bag rather than a sealed cone tip. The zooids render as roughly a hundred flat pale confetti discs floating over the surface, not as thousands of raised pimples - there is no relief, no rim shadow and no density gradient, so the surface reads printed rather than encrusted.
rows.fix: Recolour tunic and halo to a cold cyan-blue bioluminescent glow and flip the taper so the open rim is the widest point, narrowing to a rounded sealed tip at the bottom.

rows.readsAs: a diagonal chain of banded pods - salp chain is reachable, but the first read is closer to beads or small grenades
rows.defect: Transparency, which is the whole identity of a salp, is absent: the barrels are painted opaque dark navy on a near-black field, so nothing shows through them and the chain nearly disappears into the background. The small coloured gut nucleus is missing from all four zooids - there is no internal organ mark anywhere. The muscle hoops are the one strong read and they land well, but 'open at both ends' only registers at one end of each barrel; the far end is closed off by shading, so each unit reads as a sealed pod rather than an open tube.
rows.fix: Drop the tunic to a high-value glassy translucent so the background reads through the body, and drop one small warm orange gut nucleus into each zooid.

rows.readsAs: two industrial chimneys or cement kilns standing on a hill; a tunicate only on a second look, once the paired nozzles register
rows.defect: The surface treatment fights the organism. The tunic is opaque achromatic silver-white with a hard specular sheen, and the internal basket is drawn as a rectangular grid ON the outside of the wall, which reads unmistakably as brick coursing - the combination turns two soft sacs into masonry smokestacks. Neither 'leathery' nor 'translucent' is present: there is no colour at all and nothing shows through the wall. The two raised nozzle siphons are correct and clearly legible, and the sacs do sit convincingly cemented onto the dark rock mound, so the identity survives, but the material read is wrong enough to send a stranger to the wrong noun.
rows.fix: Give the tunic a translucent warm ochre-pink cast and push the basket mesh behind the wall as a soft, blurred internal structure instead of a hard exterior grid.

rows.readsAs: a giraffe — named instantly and correctly
rows.defect: Long neck and knobbed ossicones both read clearly, but the third must-read is weak and the rear third is unfinished. The topline is a low rounded arch that crests mid-back, not a steep ramp from high shoulders to the hips — there is no withers, and the drop from shoulder to croup is shallow. Worse, the reticulated patch field stops in a hard vertical edge at the flank, so the whole near haunch, thigh and croup are a blank cream slab with no patches and no shading; the shoulder is likewise unpatterned. The tail is a fat cream tube as thick as a leg that emerges from the middle of that blank slab well below the topline, with a scribbly speckled artifact where it joins the body. The leg markings are angular splinters that read as cracked paint rather than patches, and the hind legs are straight posts with no hock.
rows.fix: Carry the reticulation continuously over the croup, haunch and shoulder (no hard cut at the flank), then raise and sharpen the withers so the topline ramps steeply down to a lower hip, and rebuild the tail as a thin cord docked at the TOP of the rump.

rows.readsAs: a brown llama or a striped-necked antelope wearing a white girth band — not an okapi
rows.defect: The striping — which IS the okapi's identity — is in the wrong places and the wrong colours. The hindquarters and croup, where the horizontal white bars belong, are plain unmarked chocolate with nothing on them at all. Instead a broad band of VERTICAL cream strands is wrapped around the middle of the barrel like a saddle girth or a shaved patch, sitting forward of the hip and reading as a blanket, not as rump stripes. And the neck carries four heavy DARK horizontal bars from the jaw down to the shoulder — an okapi has no neck stripes; that inversion (dark bars on the neck, nothing on the rump) is exactly backwards and drags the read toward kudu or bongo. The leg markings are irregular white blotches, not clean horizontal bands. The face is uniform brown with no pale muzzle or cheek mask. The eye is broken: it renders as a white crescent ring with the dark pupil occluded by the ossicone base, so it reads as a hole in the head rather than an eye. There is also a hard straight seam with a bluish-grey tint running along the top of the back where the dorsal plate meets the barrel.
rows.fix: Delete the dark neck bars and the vertical cream girth band entirely, and paint crisp horizontal white bars across the croup, rump and upper hind leg only — rear half striped, front half plain chocolate — then move the eye clear of the ossicone so the pupil is visible.

rows.readsAs: a dark brown housefly or midge
rows.defect: Two of three must-reads are visibly absent. The antennae are short thin stubs reaching only about a third of the body length, when the reference demands antennae LONGER THAN THE WHOLE BODY — the single most diagnostic cricket cue. The hind leg is a hairline stick with a shallow bend and no swollen femur at all, so nothing reads as a jumping leg. The body is two overlapping brown ovals with a rear wing-fan, giving a fly silhouette; nothing about it says cricket.
rows.fix: Draw the antennae at 1.3x total body length sweeping back over the body, and rebuild the hind leg with a fat teardrop femur angled up above the topline over a thin tibia kinked sharply down.

rows.readsAs: a pale green mayfly or lacewing
rows.defect: The identity must-read — huge angled jumping hind legs rising above the back — is entirely absent. Every leg is the same hairline stick of constant width, none rises above the topline, none has a femur. The abdomen is a blunt rounded blob, not a long tapered one, and the face is a small round ball with thread antennae rather than a slanted face with short stout ones. Recolored Cricket with a slightly larger wing fan.
rows.fix: Add a genuine saltatorial hind leg: a broad wedge-shaped femur whose apex sits clearly above the wing line, hinged to a long thin downward tibia with visible spines and a small foot.

rows.readsAs: a golden mayfly or long-winged crane fly
rows.defect: The hugely enlarged folded hind jumping leg is missing — the rear limb is a plain straight hairline stick angled down and back, identical in thickness to the front legs. The head is a small round ball, not the tall flat-sided head called for. The long wings do lie along the back and are the one thing working, but they spread and droop below the body line rather than folding flat, so the overall silhouette is a delicate flier, not a locust.
rows.fix: Replace the rear stick with a massive folded hind leg — deep ribbed femur packed against the abdomen with the apex above the back and the tibia folded up alongside it — and square off the head into a tall flat-sided helmet.

rows.readsAs: a small spotted brown bream or freshwater sunfish
rows.defect: Both identity must-reads are absent. There is no mouth on this fish at all -- zoomed 4x the head is a symmetric needle point with only a faint hairline stroke and a gill arc, no jaw break in the silhouette, no jutting lower jaw, no gape. And the body is the opposite of 'thick heavy blunt-headed': it is a pointed lens whose snout tapers to a sharp point, so the heavy square-headed ambush-predator mass is nowhere in the drawing. Only the rounded paddle tail lands. The sawtooth dorsal slab also floats clear of the topline with background showing under its base.
rows.fix: Rebuild the head: blunt the snout into a wide square muzzle at least as deep as the body midline, and cut an actual mouth aperture that opens roughly a third of the head length with the lower jaw jutting past the upper -- the gape must break the silhouette, not be a line drawn on it.

rows.readsAs: a generic silver panfish -- bream, or a small silver perch
rows.defect: There is only ONE dorsal element, the shared floating sawtooth slab, so the required spiny-first-dorsal-ahead-of-a-soft-second reads as a single comb with no soft posterior fin behind it. The large mouth is entirely missing -- at 4x the snout is a closed symmetric point with a faint stroke and no jaw. The tail is a deep swallowtail fork more like a jack or tuna than the squared-to-slightly-forked bass tail called for. The body is the family lens, not a robust perch with a shoulder. The eye circle straddles the upper contour, half of it sitting over the background.
rows.fix: Split the dorsal into two attached fins -- a short spiny triangle over the shoulder joined to the topline, then a distinct lower soft-rayed lobe behind it -- and square off the caudal fin to a shallow notch.

rows.readsAs: a red bream or porgy -- the colour and depth get it close, the head does not
rows.defect: No sloping forehead: the topline is the shared unbroken arc that curves straight into a symmetric point, so the steep brow that makes a snapper's profile is absent. The pair of canine teeth -- the feature the animal is NAMED for -- is not drawn at all; at 4x there is no mouth opening, only a short stroke that stops short of the snout. The 'continuous' spiny dorsal is the shared detached slab hovering above the back over the rear half only, with visible background between its base and the topline, so it neither runs continuously along the back nor connects to it.
rows.fix: Give the head a straight steep brow dropping from the dorsal origin to a pointed snout, and open the jaw enough to show two forward-pointing canines at the front of the upper jaw; anchor the dorsal fin base directly onto the topline running from the shoulder to the tail root.

rows.readsAs: a brown quail or a small partridge
rows.defect: The reed-mimic freeze pose is completely absent — the body is horizontal and dumpy and the bill points DOWN and to the left, the opposite of the vertical sky-pointing dagger that is the whole reason this bird is recognisable. There is no thick hunched neck at all; the head ball sits directly on the shoulder of the egg. Only the brown-and-buff mottling survives, and mottled brown on a round gamebird body just reads as quail.
rows.fix: Rebuild it in the freeze pose: rotate the whole body to vertical, extend a thick heavily-streaked neck straight up from the shoulders, and align the dagger bill with the neck axis so bill, neck and body form one continuous vertical reed.
rows.verifyWhy: Looked at the 440x440 PNG, then re-cropped and upscaled the head (4x) and the body/legs (3x) to check small features before ruling. FAIL stands: two of the three must-reads are absent and the third is only half-present. CORRECTIONS TO THE ORIGINAL CLAIM, in the order they matter for the fix: (1) The bill does NOT point 'down-and-left'. It is a yellow-ochre wedge held essentially HORIZONTAL, tapering leftward from the face to a sharp tip, with only a few pixels of downward tilt (upper edge drops slightly more than the lower edge rises). The defect is that it is horizontal instead of VERTICAL — the reed-mimic freeze needs the bill aimed straight at the sky along the axis of the neck. Calling it 'down-pointing' will send a fix in the wrong direction; it needs a ~90 degree rotation to skyward, not a de-droop. (2) 'There is no thick hunched neck at all' overstates it. There IS a neck and it is clearly visible: a slender tan tube ~55-60px long rising from the shoulder, held near-vertical with a slight leftward lean, carrying a round ball head. So the neck EXISTS and is even roughly upright — what is wrong is its FORM: it is a uniform thin tube markedly narrower than the head ball, with no thickening, no hunch, no retraction into the shoulders, and a visible seam where the ball head is stuck on top instead of flowing continuously into it. A bittern's frozen neck is thick, short, and the same width as the skull so head+neck+bill form one continuous reed-shaped spike. That single continuous spike is the identity and it is completely missing. (3) The body is not 'horizontal and dumpy' — it is a near-CIRCULAR ball, about as tall as it is wide, sitting low on two short ochre legs with forward-bent tarsi and three-toed feet tucked well under the mass. A dark pointed tail spike juts right and slightly down, and a large teardrop wing plate is overlaid on the flank with a heavy dark outline. (4) 'Only the brown-buff mottling survives' is generous. The surface is a fine SCALE/SPECKLE texture in buff over tan — there is no vertical streaking anywhere, and bittern camouflage is defined by bold dark vertical streaks running down the throat and breast (the thing that makes it disappear among reeds). So even the surviving must-read reads as generic bird speckle, not bittern streaking. (5) The organism it actually reads as is closer to a KIWI or a snipe than a quail — long straight horizontal dagger bill, ball head on a thin neck, round body, short legs. A quail would have a short stubby bill; this one's long bill is the loudest feature and it points the wrong way. Net: bill orientation (skyward), continuous thick neck-skull-bill spike, and vertical breast streaking all need to be built; posture must go from perched-round-bird to vertical frozen reed.

rows.readsAs: a white bantam hen or a dove
rows.defect: Pure white plumage is the only must-read present. There is no S-curved neck — there is no neck of any length, the round white head is stuck onto the front of the body. The legs are short yellow stubs about a quarter of body height when they must be long and dark, and the bill is a stubby cone rather than a thin spear. Stripped of neck and legs it is a white chicken.
rows.fix: Give it a long thin neck at least the body's length again, folded into a shallow S, and stretch the legs to roughly body-height and recolour them near-black.
rows.verifyWhy: Verdict upheld, but three of the four stated causes are wrong and must not be used as the fix list. WHAT IS ACTUALLY THERE (measured on the 440x440 PNG; creature bbox x97-345, y101-327): (1) THE BILL IS NOT A STUBBY CONE. It is a genuine thin yellow spear -- goldenrod, ~58px long against a ~48px head diameter (1.2x head width), ~10px at the base and tapering to a single sharp point at x=97, which is the leftmost pixel of the whole silhouette. It is the single most readable feature in the asset. It is somewhat SHORT (a great egret's dagger is closer to 2x head width) but it is unambiguously a spear, not a cone. Do not touch its shape; only extend its length. (2) THERE IS A NECK. A thin white tube ~50-60px long descends from the base of the skull and curves forward-and-down into the breast. The real defect is that it carries only ONE inflection -- a shallow C -- so there is no S. It is also too short: head+neck occupies only ~25% of standing height where an egret needs ~40%, so the head sits almost on the shoulders. Fix = lengthen and add the second bend (fold back at the top, forward at the bottom), not 'add a neck'. (3) THE LEGS ARE NOT SHORT STUBS. Two thin tan legs run y265-y327 (62px = 27% of standing height), each with a correctly REARWARD-bending ankle and a splayed foot carrying a long backward hallux plus forward toes -- the wader ankle anatomy is already drawn correctly and should be preserved. The two real leg defects are (a) length: 27% of standing height where an egret wants ~35-45%, and (b) COLOUR: they are the same goldenrod as the bill, not the 'long dark' legs the reference calls for. (4) THE JUDGE'S ONE CONCESSION IS ALSO WRONG: plumage is NOT clean white. The folded wing is drawn as a heavy medium-grey lasso/hoop ringing the flank, and a large dark-grey pointed primary/tail wedge projects to the right past the body, with fine dark hatch strokes trailing off it. Against a mustRead of 'pure white plumage' that grey wing hoop and grey tail wedge are a defect in their own right. WHY IT STILL FAILS: the body is a plump ovoid measuring 248w x 226h -- aspect 1.10, i.e. WIDER than tall, against a spec aspect of 0.8. The silhouette is therefore inverted from the reference, and combined with the C-neck and the 27% legs the gestalt is a squat, low-slung white bird rather than the tall slender stilt-legged wader that IS the egret. The judge's shorthand 'white bantam hen' captures the body and stance correctly but not the head: no hen has a 1.2x-head-width yellow spear bill, and the bill alone keeps this from reading as a galliform. It reads as an unresolved plump white waterbird. FIX ORDER: raise the body aspect to ~0.8 by narrowing/raising the trunk, lengthen the neck ~1.8x and give it the second bend, lengthen the legs to ~40% of standing height and recolour them dark, strip the grey wing hoop and grey tail wedge to white, and extend the existing bill rather than redrawing it.

rows.readsAs: a pink quail or a pink cartoon chick
rows.defect: All three must-reads are missing. The neck is not kinked into a long S — there is no neck. The bill is a short straight pink-and-yellow cone with no downward break at the middle, so the single most diagnostic feature of a flamingo is simply not drawn. The legs are short yellow stubs with a forward bend, nowhere near extremely long and with no backward-bending ankle. Pink is doing 100% of the identification work.
rows.fix: Draw the flamingo silhouette from scratch — leg length roughly two body-depths with a pronounced rearward ankle break, and a neck the same length again ending in a bill that snaps sharply downward at its midpoint.
rows.verifyWhy:
Upheld, but one third of the stated cause is wrong and the fix list must be corrected. Measured on the 440x440 PNG (bg 5,6,12; figure bbox x96-343, y102-325 counting the feet, so standing height = 223px, silhouette width 247px => aspect ~1.1 WIDE, against the packet's aspect 0.55 TALL-AND-NARROW; the figure is literally wider than it is tall, which is the root geometry error under all three must-reads).

MUST-READ 1 'neck kinked into a long S' — ABSENT, judge correct. The head is a pink ball spanning y103-155, x116-165 (~50px diameter = 22% of standing height against headFrac 0.16). There is NO neck at all, not even a short one: scanning rows, the head's left silhouette edge is x117 at y118 and the BODY's left edge is x117 at y187 — one unbroken pink blob. The skull merges into the shoulder by y~124-133. There is no isolated neck column to inspect for an S; the head sits on the body like a dove's.

MUST-READ 2 'thick bill bent sharply downward at the middle' — ABSENT, judge correct, and worse than described. Row scan of the yellow bill: y117 x126-127 (top edge), widening leftward to the tip at y127-129 x99-100, then closing symmetrically back to y138 x124-128. It is a perfectly SYMMETRIC isoceles wedge — the tip sits at the exact vertical midpoint of the base, upper and lower mandible mirror each other. Length only 29px on a 223px bird. Zero kink, zero downward bias, and it is short as well as straight. This is a finch/canary seed cone glued to a pink ball. (In the 5x head crop it can look tilted down because of the shading break between mandibles; the pixel geometry says it is not.)

MUST-READ 3 'extremely long pink legs with a backward-bending ankle' — THE JUDGE IS WRONG ON THE ANKLE. The ankle IS drawn and it IS backward-bending. Per-row leg extents: the pair runs x192-219 at y257 and drifts BACKWARD (rightward; the bird faces left) to x202-228 by y282, then reverses and drifts FORWARD to x182-209 by y317 — a clean angular vertex at y~282 whose convexity points away from the head, i.e. a correct hock/ankle at ~38% down the leg. Splayed forward toes are present too (y318-325 spread x165-218). So do NOT 'add a knee' as a fix; the joint model is already right. What actually fails here is LENGTH and COLOR: the legs run y255-325 = 70px = 31% of standing height (the judge's 'quarter-height' is close but understated), where a flamingo needs roughly half its standing height in leg alone; and they are rendered yellow-gold (R>150, G>100, B<120), the same hue as the bill, not the pink the packet calls for.

Other observations: the tail is a long dark-mauve pointed spike projecting to x343, a generic passerine tail that adds body length in exactly the direction that is already too wide; a mauve wing-arc and speckled shoulder patch are painted on the flank. The judge's summary that 'pink is doing 100% of the identification' is essentially right — strip the pink and this is a plump ground-bird/quail chassis. Two of three defining must-reads are wholly absent and the third is half-present at a third of the required scale. FAIL stands.

FIX ORDER: (1) rebuild the geometry to aspect 0.55 — narrow the body, kill or shorten the tail spike; (2) add a long S-necked column between skull and shoulder (this is the single biggest identity win); (3) replace the symmetric cone bill with a heavy two-part bill that runs straight for its first half then breaks sharply downward — keep the black tip; (4) roughly double leg length and recolor pink; KEEP the existing backward-bending ankle and toes as-is.

rows.readsAs: a grey-blue quail or a fat pigeon
rows.defect: Nothing that makes a great blue heron is present. There is no long neck, therefore no S-kink. The bill is a short yellow cone, not a heavy dagger. The legs are stubby yellow sticks planted under the belly with small flat feet — no stilt length, no long trailing toes. The blue-grey wash and a stray dark crest smear are the only nods to the reference, on a body that is proportioned like a gamebird.
rows.fix: Replace the chassis: deepen the body vertically rather than horizontally, fold a long neck back on itself into a tight S sitting above the shoulders, and lengthen the legs to at least body height with three long forward toes.
rows.verifyWhy: UPHELD, but two of the three stated causes are wrong and would send a fixer to the wrong parts. Measured on the 440x440 PNG (ink bbox x77-362, y105-323; head circle x139-187 => ~48px diameter). WHAT IS ACTUALLY THERE: (1) NECK - the killer, and the judge is right here. The head ball is planted directly on the shoulder: at y=129, one head-diameter below the crown, the body/wing mass already spans out to x=252. The connecting column is a short, straight, thick pale stub of ~25-35px, roughly half a head deep, with zero curvature. There is no S, no folded recurve, no separate neck cylinder of any length. The packet's own note ('Neck folds back in an S at rest; it is not held straight like a stork's') has nothing to attach to - this bird could not even be graded against the Stork's straight-neck contrast, because it has no neck to hold in either carriage. This alone sinks the identity. (2) BILL - the claim of 'a short yellow cone' is FALSE as stated. The bill is yellow pixels x85-146 at y127-139: 61px long against a 48px head, i.e. ~1.3x head diameter, a long tapered spear that reaches well clear of the face. The real defect is DEPTH, not LENGTH: base thickness is only ~13px (0.27 of head depth), so it reads as an egret/plover needle rather than the heavy, deep-based dagger with a visible gonys that the mustRead calls for. Fix = thicken and deepen the base and add another ~25% length, do not 'add a bill'. (3) LEGS/FEET - 'stubby legs with small flat feet' is half wrong. The feet are NOT small or flat: each foot is an elongate two-prong bar ~47px wide (y315 yellow spans x195-236), i.e. as long as the head is wide, with a clearly drawn backward-pointing hind toe as well as a forward toe, and the tarsus has a correct backward-bending ankle at ~y280 with a visible tibia/tarsus break. What genuinely fails is leg LENGTH: yellow leg ink runs only y255-321, ~60px, against a 105px body depth and a 218px total figure - legs are ~28% of stature where a heron's are near half. So: hind toe present, ankle present, stilt length absent. (4) The judge's summary read is also wrong. 'Grey-blue quail' does not describe this: a quail has a stubby galliform bill and no visible leg, whereas this has a long yellow spear bill, exposed yellow legs with an ankle bend and a hind toe, and a pointed wing/tail sweeping back to x=362. It reads as a plump generic SHOREBIRD - a pale plover or a stocky sandpiper on a fattened ovoid chassis - not a gallinaceous bird. (5) Chassis note for the family pass: the body is the same plump ovoid + oval wing-disc + speckle overlay used across this batch, with only the head/bill/leg furniture swapped; the head-on-shoulder carriage is a chassis property, so fixing Heron means giving the chassis a real neck segment rather than repainting. BAND: FAIL stands - the defining must-read (long S-kinked neck) is wholly absent and stilt legs are absent; only the bill is partially readable.

rows.readsAs: a red robin or a scarlet toy bird
rows.defect: The bill is dead straight — a short yellow cone identical to the Egret's and the Heron's — when the smooth long downcurve IS the ibis. There is no bare facial skin; the red feathering runs uninterrupted to the bill base. The neck is absent rather than held out, and the legs are short stubs rather than long. Scarlet colour is the only signal left.
rows.fix: Give it a long bill that curves smoothly downward through about a quarter-circle, at least head-diameter-and-a-half in length, and clear the feathering off the face to a bare dark patch around the eye.
rows.verifyWhy:
Looked at the 440x440 PNG whole, then at 6x crops of the head, the head/neck junction and the feet. All three packet must-reads (long smoothly downcurved bill / bare skin on the face / long neck held out and long legs) are absent, so the FAIL stands. Detail, because the fix is made against this prose:

BILL — the judge is right and the sub-claim about the Egret is also right, I checked it. At 6x the bill is a flat yellow wedge from x~85 to x~150 at y~140: the top edge is a straight line, the bottom edge is a straight line, they converge to a point, and there is no curvature anywhere along either edge. The whole wedge is tilted a few degrees nose-down, which at 1x can be mistaken for a droop, but it is a rigid straight dagger, not a decurve. It is also SHORT: ~65px against a ~48px head sphere, i.e. ~1.35x head length. A real ibis bill is 2.5-3x head length and sweeps through a smooth 40-60 degree sickle. Side-by-side with Egret.png the two bills are the same primitive at the same yellow, the same wedge, near the same length — this is the shared wader bill with no per-species curve applied.

BARE FACE — confirmed absent. At 6x the head is one uniform mid-red sphere with a standard vertical shading ramp; there is no differentiated skin patch, no dark mask, no lores, no colour break at the bill base. The eye is a plain black bead with a single white catchlight sitting directly on the red.

NECK — absent, and worse than the judge implied. The head ball is planted almost directly on the shoulder with only a ~15px thick stub between them; there is no neck column at all. Notably the Egret on the same chassis DOES have a visible extended neck column, so the Ibis is the shared chassis with the neck collapsed to nothing — the exact opposite of the must-read, which calls for the neck held out.

LEGS — the judge's 'short legs' is directionally right but the diagnosis needs correcting so the fix goes to the right place. The legs are NOT missing or malformed: at 5x there are two clean thin yellow legs, each with a correct rearward-bending wader ankle, plus forward toes and a visible hind toe. The defect is purely length — roughly 65px of leg from body underside (~y245) to ground (~y310) on a 440 canvas, about a quarter of figure height, and again shorter than the Egret's on the same chassis. Fix = lengthen the tarsus and lift the body, not redraw the foot.

GESTALT — 'reads as a red robin' is close but not exact. The body is a very round fat ellipse with a heavy dark-outlined folded-wing ellipse and a short pointed tail spike; with the ball head, the stub neck and the moderate legs it reads closer to a plump red kiwi or a quail than a robin. Either way it does not read as a wading bird, let alone an ibis.

Summary of what to change: replace the straight wedge bill with a long smooth decurved sickle at 2.5-3x head length; add a bare-skin facial patch in a contrasting darker tone around the eye and bill base; extend the neck into a held-out column; lengthen the tarsus. The existing ankle joint, toes and hind toe are fine and should be kept.

rows.readsAs: a spoonbill — but a fat pink quail-shaped one
rows.defect: The identity feature is genuinely here and legible: a long flat bill flaring into a rounded spatula at the tip, on correctly roseate pink plumage. Everything else is the family chassis. The long neck is missing entirely, the legs are short stubs rather than long wading legs, and there is no bare facial skin. The spoon is bolted to the same round-bodied gamebird as the other six.
rows.fix: Keep the bill and add the wader body under it — a long neck carried out and forward, and legs roughly body-height.

rows.readsAs: a white hen with a yellow beak
rows.defect: The bill is a short light cone, not a long heavy straight dagger — it is barely longer than the head is wide. There is no neck to hold straight, which makes the one feature meant to separate stork from heron unjudgeable. The legs are short and yellow rather than very long and red. It is the Egret asset with a slightly greyer wing.
rows.fix: Extend the bill to roughly two head-diameters and thicken it, run a straight neck of similar length forward from the shoulders, and lengthen the legs to at least body height in strong red.
rows.verifyWhy: Upheld, but two parts of the original claim are wrong and would misdirect the fix. What is actually on canvas (440x440; measured off 4x nearest-neighbour crops of the head at src 60,80-260,280 and the legs at src 150,230-350,430): a fat egg-shaped white body with a scaled/stippled painterly fill, a grey scapular arc, a grey pointed tail projecting right past the rump with faint primary streaks, a small round white head, a gold bill, and two amber legs. MUST-READ 1 'long heavy straight bill' - FAILS, but not as described. The bill is NOT 'barely longer than the head is wide': the head circle is 45px across (src x142-188) and the bill runs from the tip at src x80 to the head's front edge at x142, so ~62px of exposed bill, about 1.4x head width. It is straight. What is wrong is the MASS and the LENGTH RATIO: it is a slim needle cone, ~14px deep at the base tapering to a point, where a stork needs ~2.5-3x head width and a deep, near-parallel-sided heavy dagger that stays thick most of its run. So the judge's direction is right (light cone, not heavy dagger) and the measurement is overstated - do not build the fix around 'barely longer than the head'. MUST-READ 2 'neck held straight rather than kinked' - FAILS absolutely, and this is the fatal one, because the packet note names it as the single feature separating stork from heron. There is zero neck: the head's underside sits at src y~155 and the body's top edge is at y~160, so the skull is fused straight onto the shoulder mass with a 5px cream sliver between them. There is no column to read as straight or kinked. MUST-READ 3 'very long red legs' - FAILS on both attributes, but 'short' overstates it. The legs run src y254 (body underside) to y316 (foot), ~62px, roughly 60% of the ~100px body height - moderate, not stumpy, and they are correctly built with a backward-pointing hock and a genuinely well-drawn anisodactyl foot (three forward toes plus a rear toe visible on both feet). They are golden amber (#e0b45c range), nowhere near red. A stork needs legs at least as tall as the body and unmistakably red. CORRECTION TO THE JUDGE'S IDENTIFICATION: this is NOT 'the Egret asset with a greyer wing'. I opened Egret.png alongside it. The Egret has a distinct white neck column roughly 40px tall carrying the head clear above the shoulders; the Stork has none at all, and its head is set lower and further forward on a rounder, fatter body. The Stork is a DIFFERENT and worse pose than the Egret, not a recolour of it - and perversely the Egret is currently the asset that shows the straight neck the Stork is supposed to own. Net: 0 of 3 must-reads readable. The silhouette reads as a generic white gull/plover shorebird. Fix order: (1) grow a straight vertical neck column - this is the identity and it is 100% absent; (2) rebuild the bill as a long deep dagger, ~2.5x head width, thick to near the tip; (3) lengthen the legs to at least body height and recolour amber to red - the foot and hock geometry are already good, keep them.

rows.readsAs: a pink-grey pig, or a dachshund-shaped farm animal
rows.defect: Two of the three must-reads are absent. There is no enormous barrel body — the torso is a long shallow tube of constant depth with a straight belly line and a flat topline, so the animal reads long-and-low instead of massive-and-deep, and the legs are short tapering nubs with small dark trotter-like feet rather than pillar columns rising into visible shoulder and haunch mass. Worse, the ears/eyes/nostrils triad that IS the hippo is missing: the eye is a single large cartoon orb with a white sclera and dark pupil set on the SIDE of the head at mid-height (the packet calls for small eyes), there is no paired nostril bulge on top of the muzzle, and the only ear is an ambiguous notch at the back of the crown — nothing forms the signature horizontal line of ears, eyes and nostrils across the top of the skull. The muzzle block is squared and is the one credible hippo cue, but it is no wider than the skull behind it and the mouth is a thin closed line rather than a jaw that runs far back toward the ear. The head is also stacked above the topline on a visible neck step, where a hippo has effectively no neck. No tail.
rows.fix: Rebuild the torso as a deep barrel — roughly as deep as it is tall-plus-half, widest at the belly, with the topline dropping into a low sway behind a heavy shoulder — set the head DIRECTLY on the shoulders with no neck gap, and replace the side-mounted cartoon eye with the hippo triad: tiny bead eyes on raised bosses, small round ears just behind them, and two nostril bumps at the muzzle tip, all sitting on one horizontal line along the top of the skull.

rows.readsAs: a white fleecy sheep or a young goat
rows.defect: The very long upright ears - the entire identity of a donkey - are absent. What is on the head is a pair of short dark rounded flaps that curl backward and downward, no longer than the head is deep, reading as folded ram ears or budding horns. There is no upright bristly mane at all along the crest, and there is no neck to put one on: the wedge head is welded straight onto the shoulder. The barrel is a deep woolly egg with a hanging belly and the feet are small dark cloven caps, which pushes the read further toward sheep. The tufted-tip tail is the only must-read that landed.
rows.fix: Rebuild the ears as two narrow blades at least half the head length again, standing vertically off the top of the skull with a pale inner-ear channel, and add a short erect black mane ridge along a real (short, thick) neck.
rows.verifyWhy:
Verdict upheld, but THREE of the four stated causes are wrong and would send the fix in the wrong direction. Corrections first, then what actually fails.

WRONG #1 — 'the very long upright ears are ABSENT / two short dark rounded flaps curling backward'. Not what is drawn. At 11x on the head (crop 255,85,70x70) there is ONE large ear, presented inner-surface-toward-viewer: a pale grey outer rim enclosing a dark taupe concha, an elongated oval running from roughly (269,96) to (294,139) in the 440px image — about 50px long against a head (poll to nose tip) of about 77px, i.e. ~65% of head length. It is not short, and it does not curl backward: its long axis is only ~30deg off vertical with the tip up-and-back. So 'ear length' is NOT the defect. The defects are (a) SHAPE — it is a broad blunt-tipped oval, ~19px wide, only 2.6:1, where a donkey ear is a narrow 4-5:1 lanceolate spike; the fat pale-rim/dark-cup oval is exactly the ram/sheep ear read the judge named, but arrived at through width and blunt tip, not through length or backward curl; (b) its lower third is painted as a dark blob lying over the cheek down past the eye, so the free-standing part above the skull is much shorter than the shape's true length; and (c) THE PAIR DOES NOT READ — the far ear is a separate tiny grey triangular nub, tip at ~(289,102), only ~20px long, i.e. 40% of the near ear. Two ears of wildly different length destroy the paired-antenna silhouette that is the whole donkey signature. Fix = narrow both ears to ~4:1 with a rounded-lanceolate tip, lift them off the cheek, and make the far ear the same length as the near one, foreshortened in width only.

WRONG #2 — 'no neck to carry one'. There is a neck: short, thick, sloping forward from the withers up to the poll, clearly a separate mass from the barrel. It is short and thick in a way that is actually correct per the note ('shorter neck than a horse'). The mane is what is missing, not the neck.

WRONG #3 — 'small cloven feet'. At 10x on the feet (crop 130,285,140x60) each leg ends in a single small dark-brown blunt hoof cap, undivided — no cleft, no split toe anywhere. What reads as 'cloven' is the near+far leg of each pair standing close together, each with its own dark tip. The hooves are too small and too flat-capped for an equid, but they are not cloven, and hoof form is not on this species' mustRead line anyway.

OMITTED — the third must-read is PRESENT and correct. 'cow-like tail tufted only at the tip' is drawn well: a long bare grey rope arching out and down from the rump, ending in a splayed fan of four or five dark strands confined to the tip. The judge did not mention it. This is also the single strongest argument against the 'white sheep' read and should be preserved untouched by any fix.

RIGHT — 'no upright bristly mane'. Confirmed at 8x on the crest (crop 175,130,120x90): the topline from withers to poll is a smooth clean pale arc, and every fur stroke on the neck-top hangs DOWNWARD. There is no crest, no bristle, no standing hair of any kind. Must-read 2 of 3 is genuinely absent.

RIGHT — the fleece read. The whole barrel is overlaid with dense white curly/wavy strokes, and combined with a deep hanging belly line and a high sloping croup this is the dominant texture of the asset.

WHY IT STILL FAILS: of three must-reads, one is present (tufted tail), one is flatly absent (upright bristly mane), and one is present-but-unreadable (a single broad blunt oval ear plus a nub, instead of a matched pair of narrow spikes). On top of that the head is long, narrow and finely tapered like a deer or goat rather than the heavy blunt donkey muzzle, and there is no mealy pale muzzle, no pale eye ring, no dorsal stripe and no shoulder cross. The gestalt at 1x is a pale fleecy goat/sheep-cross, not a donkey. FAIL stands.

rows.readsAs: a tan sheep or an alpaca
rows.defect: Two of the three must-reads are missing and the third is broken. There is no long arched neck - the head sits directly on the barrel with zero neck length - and consequently no crest mane anywhere; the topline runs flat from poll to rump. The tail is not long flowing hair from a high dock: it is a solid flat brown fan/paddle shape stuck low on the rump, reading as a damaged or unfinished shape rather than hair. Only the single hooves on slim legs partly survive, and even those are tiny dark cloven-looking caps on featureless tubes with no stifle or hock. The deep hanging belly and blunt downturned muzzle complete a sheep silhouette.
rows.fix: Give it a real neck - roughly one head-length, arching up and forward out of the withers - with a crest mane on top, and replace the tail paddle with a curtain of long strands falling from a high, level dock.
rows.verifyWhy:
Verified at 4-8x on the head, neck/withers, tail dock and both leg pairs. The FAIL stands, but two of the three stated causes are described wrongly and one of the three must-reads actually PASSES.

MUST-READ 1 - 'long arched neck with crest mane': PARTIAL/FAIL, and the judge's description is wrong. A neck IS present and it is NOT flat from poll to rump: the topline steps clearly - level back from rump to withers (y~155), then a distinct cylindrical neck column rising forward-up at roughly 50 degrees to a head whose poll sits ~55px above the back line at x~300. The head does not sit on the barrel. What is genuinely wrong is (a) the neck is SHORT and DEAD STRAIGHT - a straight tapering tube, with a slightly CONCAVE (ewe-necked) upper edge rather than a convex crest arc, and (b) there is no crest mane of ANY kind: the neck carries the identical fine pale fleece stroke texture as the barrel, with zero darker hair band along its upper edge, no forelock, no withers mane break. That absence is real and total.

MUST-READ 2 - 'single hoof on each long slim leg': PRESENT. At first look each leg group appears cloven (two dark tips), but at 8x this is the near/far leg pair overlapping - the far leg is a darker desaturated column, the near leg lighter, and each terminates in ONE solid dark rectangular hoof block. Four legs, four single hooves. Legs are slim and reasonably long. Do not 'fix' this - it is the one identity cue that reads.

MUST-READ 3 - 'long flowing tail from a high dock': FAIL, but not a solid paddle. At 4x the tail is a broad flat tan LOBE with visible internal segment ridges, ringed by a fringe of ~14 short dark radiating spokes - a spoked fan / feathered plume, not a featureless paddle as claimed. The defects are shape and placement, not solidity: the whole assembly is roughly circular and SHORT (it stops around barrel mid-height and never falls toward the hocks), and the dock attaches partway DOWN the rump face (roughly 45% below the croup peak) instead of at the top of the croup continuing the topline. So 'not long flowing hair from a high dock' is correct; 'solid flat brown paddle' is not.

ADDITIONAL DEFECTS the FAIL did not name, and which drive the sheep/alpaca read as much as the neck does:
- NO EARS ON THE SKULL. The cranium is a smooth featureless dome. The only ear-like marks are two small dark triangles sitting BELOW and beside the eye on the cheek, apex-down; they read as nostril or shadow marks, not as ears. A horse silhouette without poll-mounted ears loses its head signature entirely.
- A hard straight dark bar crosses the muzzle at the mouth line and overshoots the muzzle outline to the right - reads as a stray seam/stick, not anatomy.
- The barrel is deep, round-bellied and covered in fine dense pale fleece flecking with no coat sheen or muscle planes; combined with the straight mane-less neck and the round fan tail, the organism does read as a tan alpaca/sheep. The judge's overall read is correct.

FIX PRIORITY: crest mane + arched convex neck line; poll ears; re-dock the tail at the croup top and replace the round spoked fan with long falling hair. Leave the legs and hooves alone.

rows.readsAs: a grey bull or a horned goat
rows.defect: The horns are in the wrong place, which is the whole identity. Both pale horns rise from the TOP of the skull behind the eye and sweep backward like a goat's or antelope's; the nose is bare and ends in the same little curled cartoon mouth as the sheep chassis. The hide has no plating and no deep folds - just faint scribbled speckles over a smooth surface.
