The feet are the same small dark cloven caps as the horse and donkey, not three broad toes, and the eye is a large round cartoon eye set forward rather than a small eye far back on the side of the head. The body is a barrel but it is the family barrel, not a low-slung armoured one.
rows.fix: Move the horn to the tip of the nose as a single forward-curving cone growing off the nasal bone (with a smaller second boss behind it), and rebuild the feet as three splayed toes.
rows.verifyWhy: REFUTED on the primary cause. I read the 440px PNG, then re-read it at 2x whole-body, 4x head, 9x snout, 10x mouth and 16x foot crops (decoder script: scratchpad/crop.mjs). WHAT IS ACTUALLY THERE. Horns: two straight cream cones, and BOTH sit FORWARD of the eye, not behind it. The eye centre is at ~src x=327; the rear (smaller) horn base is ~x=340-357, i.e. just ahead of the eye on the front of the forehead, and the front (LARGER) horn base is ~x=364-385, seated squarely on the top of the nasal bridge, directly above a drawn nostril arc and only ~15px behind the muzzle end-cap. The larger horn is the front one and the smaller the rear one - correct rhino ordering. Neither horn sweeps backward: both are near-vertical cones with tips leaning very slightly FORWARD. Nothing about the arrangement reads goat (goat/bull horns spring from the top-rear skull and sweep back/out); this is a nasal + frontal pair. The must-read 'horn (or two) rising from the nose, not the forehead' is PRESENT and readable at native size. Nose is NOT bare: at 9x the muzzle terminates in a distinct darker-grey rounded end-cap, with a dark curved nostril arc above it and a mid-grey lip pad below. Feet are NOT cloven caps: at 16x each foot cap carries a dark band containing THREE pale rectangular toenails (three clearly on the near foot, two visible on the occluded far foot) - i.e. three toes are drawn on all four feet. WHAT GENUINELY FAILS (the FAIL judge was right about this one thing, and it is the only must-read actually missing). Hide: no plating and no folds anywhere. The torso carries only very faint horizontal banding, a soft shoulder-crease arc and a soft haunch arc, over a scatter of short dark HAIR ticks that make the animal read slightly woolly/hairy rather than naked plated hide. 'Thick plated hide with deep folds' is absent - that is the fix. SECONDARY DEFECTS FOR THE SAME PASS: (1) eye violates the packet ('eyes: small ... set far back on the sides of the head') - it is a large frontal cartoon eye with white sclera and a big brown iris, roughly 3x too large and set too far forward; (2) the tail is a long thin rope ending in an enormous flared feathery brush that hangs to the ground - reads as a lion/cow tail; a rhino tail is short with a small tuft; (3) the three toes, while present, are only ~2px each at native size, so they read as plain dark hoof caps unless zoomed - the toe splits need to be widened/darkened to carry at 440px; (4) a thin grey rod with a blob at its front end runs back along the lower jaw - intended as the lip/mouth line but at native size it reads as a stray bar or a bit in the mouth. OVERALL READ: barrel body carried low on stumpy legs (must-read 3 present), two nasal/frontal horns (must-read 1 present), only the plated-and-folded hide (must-read 2) missing. It reads as a rhinoceros, not as a grey horned bull or goat, so FAIL is not sustainable; band it POLISH and fix the hide plating/folds first, then the eye, tail and toe legibility.

rows.readsAs: a plain grey sheep or lamb
rows.defect: The short flexible proboscis is absent - the muzzle is the same blunt downturned wedge used on the donkey and horse, ending in a tiny curl of a mouth with only a small nub where the trunk should be; nothing overhangs the lower lip. The high rounded rump with a sloping back is absent too: the topline is flat and level from shoulder to tail, and the rump is the flattest part of the animal. No tail is visible at all - not even the stubby nub - so the rear of the silhouette just ends. Deep hanging belly, thin tube legs and small cloven feet leave a sheep.
rows.fix: Extend the upper lip into a short mobile trunk that droops past the chin, and raise and round the hindquarters so the back slopes downhill from rump to shoulder.
rows.verifyWhy:
Looked at the 440x440 PNG whole, then at 5x-7x nearest-neighbour crops of the head (x225-355,y95-225), the snout tip (x300-410,y130-220) and the rear/rump (x55-205,y140-320). The FAIL stands, but the stated cause for the headline defect is WRONG and would send a fixer to the wrong place.

CORRECTION 1 - the proboscis is NOT absent. There IS a dedicated proboscis primitive: a lighter-grey, clearly SEGMENTED/ringed cylinder (3-4 visible bands) hooking downward off the front of the muzzle, sitting right above the mouth line. It is real geometry, not a nub. The actual defect is PLACEMENT/DEPTH, not existence: the muzzle in front of it is a fat rounded near-circular dome, and the trunk is drawn tucked BEHIND/INSIDE that dome's outline, so it never breaks the silhouette. The leading edge of the face is a smooth unbroken curve; the trunk reads as an interior highlight - a lip fold or a lolling tongue - and at read size it vanishes entirely. FIX: push the proboscis forward and down so it projects PAST the muzzle's leading edge and carries the outline, and lengthen it (it is currently ~30px on a 440px canvas, roughly a quarter of head height; it needs to be the frontmost point of the animal).

CORRECTION 2 - the muzzle is not the Horse/Donkey wedge. Compared side by side with Donkey.png: the donkey has a long tapering muzzle and long upright ears; the tapir head is a visibly different, much heavier blunt-dome mass with a backswept flap ear at top-left and two dark triangular facets on the cheek plane. The head is not a copy-paste of the equine head.

CONFIRMED DEFECTS (judge right on these): (a) NO TAIL AT ALL. The rear at 6x shows only a dark faceted wedge that reads as the haunch/thigh plate; nothing protrudes past the rump silhouette. The must-read stubby nub of a tail is entirely missing - and the family chassis clearly HAS a working tail primitive, since the Donkey in the same batch carries a long tufted one, so the tapir was given zero length rather than a short one. (b) NO HIGH ROUNDED RUMP / SLOPING BACK. The topline runs essentially flat and level from rump to shoulder; the high point is mid-back, and the rump is actually slightly LOWER than mid-back. The defining lowland-tapir profile - rump as the highest point with the back falling away forward toward the shoulders - is absent.

ADDITIONAL DEFECTS neither judge named, both pushing the gestalt toward sheep: (c) the pelt is a long shaggy fur texture with heavy dark stroke clumps over the whole barrel. Tapirs are near-hairless with short bristly hide; this fleece is the single biggest reason it reads as a lamb. (d) The feet each terminate in TWO dark toe caps side by side - a cloven-hoof read. Tapir feet are splayed pads, 4 toes front / 3 rear, never cloven.

GESTALT: at 1x and 2x this reads as a shaggy grey sheep or lamb. Two of three must-reads (high rounded rump, tail nub) are outright absent; the third exists but is occluded by its own muzzle and does not read. FAIL is correct.

rows.readsAs: a cream-coloured sheep
rows.defect: Same failure as the Donkey and drawn on the same body. The very long upright ears are absent: the head carries two short dark rounded flaps that curve back and down, barely head-deep, reading as a ram's folded ear. The erect short mane is absent - the crest is bare and there is no neck to carry it, the wedge head being joined straight to the shoulder. The tufted cow-like tail with a bare upper half is the one must-read present. Deep fleecy barrel, hanging belly and dainty dark cloven feet make sheep the unprompted answer.

rows.verifyWhy:
Verdict upheld (2 of 3 must-reads absent, and they are the two that carry the identity), but two of the stated causes are wrong and would send a fix in the wrong direction. Examined at 5-10x on the 440x440 png.

EARS - the claim of 'short dark backward-curling flaps' is WRONG. What is actually drawn is a LARGE pale-rimmed OVAL SAUCER seen face-on (aperture toward the viewer), with a dark brown inner bowl. Its long axis runs approx. y=90 to y=142 in image coords, ~52px, roughly 60% of head length and taller than the skull is deep - so it is not small. Flanking it are TWO dark brown TRIANGULAR POINTS: one above-behind the saucer pointing up-right, one at the poll pointing down-left. Nothing curls backward. The real defect is shape and axis, not size: the saucer is a broad ~1.9:1 rounded disc tilted forward over the face, where an ass ear must be a narrow ~3:1 blade standing UP off the poll, and there must be two of them, both upright. As drawn this reads as one big round ram/bighorn ear plus dark spurs. Compounding it, the eye is composited INSIDE the dark bowl of the saucer - the ear is painted across the face where the eye belongs, so ear and eye occupy the same pixels. Fix the ear as: two narrow upright blades rising off the poll behind the eye, pale inner with dark rim, length >= 0.6 of head length; delete the face-on saucer and the two triangular spurs.

MANE - genuinely ABSENT, judge correct on the fact. But 'no neck to stand it on' is WRONG. There IS a clearly formed neck: a short thick upright column rising from the withers to the skull, about one head-depth tall, with its own distinct front and back edges (visible at x~275-320, y~130-190). The crest/topline from withers to poll is a smooth unbroken cream curve with zero colour break, zero bristle, zero crest band. The mane is simply missing from a perfectly serviceable neck - the fix is to add an erect short brush along that existing topline, not to rebuild the neck.

TAIL - judge correct, this one lands and should not be touched except cosmetically. A thick BARE tapering dock arcs up out of the rump and back down, terminating in a splayed fan of ~5 straight dark hairs. Bare upper half + terminal tuft both read. Minor: the dock is unusually thick and arcs outward like a handle rather than hanging.

OTHER: muzzle is long and fine-tapering with a nostril dot and a long thin mouth line back to the cheek - finer than a donkey's blunt muzzle. Legs are slim with small dark single-hoof tips (hooves do read). Body is a smooth barrel with streaky cream fur texture and a rounded rump.

CHASSIS - the 'identically drawn body' claim is CONFIRMED quantitatively: figure-mask IoU against Donkey.png is 0.860 (vs 0.653 for Horse, 0.719 for Zebra). Wild Ass and Donkey are the same drawing recoloured cream vs grey, same pose, same saucer-ear treatment, same tail. Whatever fix is authored must be applied to both, and the two must then be differentiated (wild ass: leaner, longer muzzle, dorsal stripe/shoulder cross optional; donkey: bigger head, straighter back).

ORGANISM READ - the 'cream sheep' read is fair for the head and body (rounded ear, no mane, fleecy streak texture, short neck), though the big arcing tufted tail is un-sheep-like; overall it lands as a generic pale ruminant/ungulate, not an equid. Nothing in the silhouette says ass.

rows.readsAs: a zebra
rows.defect: The identity survives on the strength of the stripes alone. Bold black bars cross the barrel and ring the lower legs, and the tail is correctly bare on the upper half with a dark tuft at the tip. But the stiff upright brush mane is entirely missing - the crest is a smooth unbroken white line - and there is no neck to stand a mane on, the head being welded to the shoulder exactly as on the horse and donkey. The striping stops at the flank: the belly and the whole hindquarter behind the barrel are blank white, and the face carries only two token bars, so the pattern reads as painted-on decoration rather than as the animal's own coat. Underneath, it is the same fleecy egg body with the same tube legs and same tiny dark cloven feet.

rows.readsAs: a plump green kiwi or a chunky green quail/duckling with a long probing bill — nobody names a hummingbird
rows.defect: The bill must-read is the only one present. The body is a fat horizontal ground bird standing on two splayed yellow feet on a cast shadow — the exact opposite of the packet's own note that hummingbirds hover with the body near-vertical and the feet tiny and tucked. The wings are not blade-like and not blurred: there is a single broad rounded folded-wing teardrop lying flat on the flank, rendered crisply at rest with no motion arc, no hover blur, no second wing. The throat is flat uniform green identical to the breast and back — there is no gorget patch, no boundary, no iridescent hue shift anywhere on the throat, so the one marking that IS the identity is absent. Body mass and stance read as a bird ten times a hummingbird's size.
rows.fix: Rebuild off the perching chassis entirely: rotate the body to a near-vertical hover, tuck the feet to nothing, replace the folded flank wing with two narrow swept blades caught mid-figure-eight as translucent blurred arcs on both sides of the body, and paint a hard-edged saturated magenta/ruby gorget patch on the throat that contrasts against the green breast.

rows.readsAs: An Appaloosa pony / spotted Shetland pony
rows.defect: The identity must-read is absent: the back is level (with a slight rise at the croup) instead of sloping sharply from high shoulders down to low hips. The neck is a short pony neck, not a massive fused shoulder-neck, and the head is a domed foal skull with a drooping blunt muzzle and no jaw mass at all — no crushing bite is readable. Limbs are four equal straight columns ending in blocky hoof-like feet with no digitigrade paw and no hock/elbow angulation. Ears are small rounded pony ears on top of the dome. Only the blotchy black spotting gestures at the reference, and on this body it reads as Appaloosa coat marking.
rows.fix: Rebuild the topline and limb skeleton: raise the withers well above the croup so the spine falls in a continuous steep line to the hips, shorten and angulate the hind limb (visible hock well above the foot, hip mass inside the silhouette), and replace the hoof-blocks with compact four-toed digitigrade paws; then hang a deep-jawed short-faced skull with heavy cheek/mandible bulk off a thickened neck.

rows.readsAs: A shaggy cream pony or a long-haired goat
rows.defect: Two of the three must-reads are missing outright. There is NO erect crest of mane hair along the spine — the topline is a clean smooth level curve with only a faint fur texture, so the single most diagnostic feature of this animal is invisible. The back does not slope: shoulders and hips sit at the same height and the croup is if anything higher, and the front legs are the same length as the hind legs, directly contradicting the packet note. Ears are small rounded pony ears, not the large pointed ears named. The body striping is a soft pale hatched texture rather than bold vertical black bands, and the legs — where the banding is most legible on the real animal — are unmarked. It is the identical silhouette to the Spotted Hyena in this same batch, recoloured.
rows.fix: Add a tall standing crest of coarse mane hair breaking the spine outline from nape to croup, and re-cut the topline so it drops steeply from high shoulders to low hips on longer forelegs; then restate the stripes as bold dark vertical bars, including on the legs.

rows.readsAs: a small hunched brine shrimp
rows.defect: The C-curl and the fanned tail do read, but the underside carries only four identical straight bristles - not the many segmented legs of differing shapes the reference calls for - and nothing about the body reads as laterally flattened; there is also only one antenna pair plus a stray, not two clear pairs. It is the identical painting used for Copepod.

rows.readsAs: a white lampshade or a paper lantern
rows.defect: A smooth ivory cone with evenly spaced vertical seam lines, wide at the base and cleanly truncated at the top. There are no trapdoor plates - just a small dark notch - and there are ZERO feathery cirri sweeping out of the opening, which is the one thing that makes a barnacle read as alive. It is not attached to any substrate, so it floats as a piece of furniture.
rows.fix: Open the summit into a pair of interlocking beak-shaped opercular plates and sweep a fan of curled feathery cirri out of the gap; roughen the plate walls with chalky overlapping ridges and seat the cone on a rock.

rows.readsAs: a generic garden spider
rows.defect: Two tan spheres with a pinched waist and eight symmetrical thin legs, topped by an eight-dot spider eye cluster. Every identity cue is missing: no enormous forward-jutting chelicerae, no long leg-like pedipalps held out front, and no hairy segmented abdomen - the rear is a smooth egg. The note says it should appear to have ten front appendages; it has eight ordinary spider legs and nothing in front of the head.
rows.fix: Mount a pair of huge vertical scissor chelicerae on the front of the head - a third the body length - and add two extra long palps reaching forward past them so the animal reads as ten-limbed.

rows.readsAs: a legless grub or a mealworm larva
rows.defect: A horizontal chain of ten identical tan spheres with a dark round head-ball at the right end. It has no legs at all - not even stubs - no antennae of any kind, and no arched hump; the topline is dead flat. Every one of the three must-reads (humped back, whip antennae longer than the body, huge folded hind legs) is absent, and the silhouette is the same bead chain used for the centipedes with the legs deleted.
rows.fix: Rebuild it as an insect: a strongly arched thorax-plus-abdomen hump, two hair-thin antennae running two body lengths off frame, and a pair of massively folded jackknife hind legs with the knees standing above the back.

rows.readsAs: a centipede, or a legged caterpillar on a bad read
rows.defect: Antennae and a side leg fringe are present so the centipede read mostly lands, but the body is a chain of round beads - visibly tubular, not the flattened plated ribbon the note demands - and the legs only appear under the rear two thirds, leaving the front third bare so you cannot see one pair per segment. At roughly 3:1 rendered it is nowhere near the 8:1 length the reference asks for.
rows.fix: Swap the sphere chain for overlapping flat tergite plates and hang one leg pair off EVERY plate from the head back, then stretch the whole body to about eight times its depth.

rows.readsAs: a small purple crab
rows.defect: It is the Crab painting in purple - same striped barrel carapace, same two lollipop claws, same two stick legs per side. Both claws are the same size and both are small flat paddles, so the massive crushing claw with one much larger is absent; the legs are thin wires that barely exceed the shell width rather than long heavy armoured limbs spanning far wider than the body; the tucked calcified abdomen is not indicated at all.

rows.readsAs: a shrimp - specifically, the Amphipod again in orange
rows.defect: This is pixel-for-pixel the Amphipod chassis recoloured. It reads as the wrong organism: the body is a hunched two-hump shrimp rather than a teardrop that is widest at the front and tapers back, the antennae trail loosely behind rather than standing outstretched as wide as the body is long, and it carries one large glossy paired-looking black eye where a calanoid has a single tiny median eyespot. The forked bristly tail is buried in the same fan the Amphipod uses.
rows.fix: Redraw from scratch as a smooth teardrop prosome with a narrow tapering urosome, two rigid antennae held straight out sideways at full body length, a clean forked caudal ramus with long bristles, and a single dot eyespot.

rows.readsAs: a crab, though a wooden toy one
rows.defect: The broad tailless carapace and forward claws are there, but the shell is painted with even vertical stripes that read as barrel staves rather than a smooth calcified plate, the claws are solid lollipop paddles with no pincer gap or opposing finger, only two legs per side exist where a crab needs four, and the eyestalks are pin-thin wires with white pinpricks so small the prominent stalked eyes barely register.
rows.fix: Split each claw into a fixed and a moving finger with a visible gap, add the missing two leg pairs, and thicken the eyestalks into short columns with dark bulb eyes.

rows.readsAs: a small shrimp with paddles
rows.defect: Built on the Amphipod shrimp chassis with two flat leaf-shaped paddles added in front. Those paddles have no pincer split, so the large pincer claws held forward do not read; the abdomen is a short curled stub tucked under the body instead of a long straight segmented tail, so the tail fan is crushed against the underside; the antennae do sweep long, which is the one must-read that lands.
rows.fix: Straighten and lengthen the abdomen into six clear segments ending in an open spread tail fan, and rebuild the claws as split pincers with a thick propodus and a visible dactyl gap.

rows.readsAs: a plucked bird or a legless blob with mittens
rows.defect: There is no crab here at all - a big smooth egg-shaped body with a smaller ball stuck to its left, each ending in a rounded mitten paddle, and only three or four hair-thin bristles underneath standing in for legs. The two claws are near enough the same size that the defining gross asymmetry is completely absent, which the note calls out explicitly as disqualifying. No carapace edge, no walking legs, and the stalked eyes are two pins on top of a shapeless mass.
rows.fix: Rebuild it as a proper crab silhouette - flat rectangular carapace, four walking legs per side - then hang one claw as large as the entire body off one shoulder and leave the other a tiny stub.

rows.readsAs: a centipede
rows.defect: The strongest read in the batch - dark red bead body, yellow curved venom claws under the head, twin antennae and matching rear trailing legs all present. But it is the Centipede painting recoloured and stretched, and it repeats the same defect: the leg fringe hangs only under the rear two thirds so the front third is bare, and the legs bunch into an undifferentiated comb where you cannot count exactly one pair per segment. The body is still a tube of spheres rather than flattened plates.
rows.fix: Anchor one clearly separated leg pair to every visible segment from the head back, and flatten the segments into overlapping plates with a hard side edge so the body is a ribbon, not a sausage.

rows.readsAs: a long-legged spider
rows.defect: It is the Camel Spider chassis in grey-pink: two distinct spheres separated by an obvious pinched waist, with an eight-dot spider eye cluster on the front one. The single fused pea-like body with NO waist is the entire identity of a harvestman and the reference note says outright not a spider, one fused segment - yet the render shows a textbook cephalothorax-plus-abdomen spider. There is no eye turret on top either, just the spider eye grid on the face.
rows.fix: Fuse the two spheres into one smooth pea with no constriction anywhere, and put a single small raised turret with two side-facing eyes on top of it.

rows.readsAs: a crab next to a snail shell
rows.defect: The borrowed spiral shell is present and coiled, which is the main win, but it is pasted flat beside and behind the body like a coin rather than carried over the abdomen - the crab is not in it, and no part of the animal enters the shell mouth. Both claws are the same small paddle, so the one enlarged claw that plugs the shell mouth is missing. Body and legs are the Crab chassis in orange, striped barrel carapace included.
rows.fix: Slide the shell over the rear of the body so the abdomen visibly disappears into its aperture, and enlarge one claw into a shield sized to seal that opening.

rows.readsAs: a grey domed shell with a spike, roughly a horseshoe crab
rows.defect: The long rigid spike tail and the smooth speckled grey dome carry the read, but the shell is a plain symmetrical ellipse - no crescent horseshoe front edge and no separate hinged rear abdomen, so it is one blob plus a needle. Several leg bristles poke visibly out from the lower sides, which the note forbids outright (nothing should protrude in profile). The pose is also a top-down view with the tail hanging straight down while every other asset in the family is a clean side view.
rows.fix: Cut the front shield into a wide crescent horseshoe with down-swept side points, hinge a smaller spined abdominal plate behind it, and tuck every leg fully under the shell so the outline is unbroken.

rows.readsAs: woodlouse / pillbug
rows.defect: Reads correctly, but the rear ends in a single pointed plate with a crescent highlight - the two flanking uropods are entirely absent. The body is a fat 3D loaf rather than a flattened armour shell, and the seven legs are identical featureless pegs raked at one angle with no joint or foot.
rows.fix: Add two short forked uropods projecting back from the rear plate and flatten the body profile so the segment bands read as overlapping armour, not as a loaf.

rows.readsAs: a two-headed peach blob with a picket fence under it
rows.defect: A SECOND pair of large black stalked eyes on a V-stalk sits on the ABDOMEN lump, so the tail end has a face - the creature reads as two-headed. The body is two opaque spheres, not an elongated translucent shrimp form, and the feathery gills are drawn as a row of hard white zigzag Ms that read as teeth or a fence.
rows.fix: Delete the eye pair on the abdomen (eyes belong only on the head), stretch the body to the specified 3.5 aspect, and redraw the gills as soft translucent plumes rather than a zigzag line.

rows.readsAs: a dark shrimp with a shadow smear in front of it
rows.defect: The pincer claws - the whole identity - are two flat, unshaded dark grey paddles floating in front of the head with no pincer split, no finger and no thumb; they read as a shadow or a torn wing, not as claws. The body is the identical carapace-ball plus curled lump used by Prawn and Shrimp, so with the claws unreadable a stranger names this a shrimp. The whole render is also so dark it barely separates from the background.
rows.fix: Redraw the claws as shaded, opaque, obviously two-fingered pincers of clearly unequal size on jointed arms, and lift the overall value so the animal separates from the dark plate.

rows.readsAs: a coiled millipede or centipede
rows.defect: The trunk is a string of separate round beads rather than a cylindrical tube of identical rings, so it reads knobbly instead of smooth. The legs are sparse single spikes splayed outward and downward - the centipede pattern the note explicitly warns against - instead of a dense two-pairs-per-segment fringe tucked under the body. The antennae are long curved horns, not short clubbed ones.
rows.fix: Fuse the beads into a smooth cylindrical ring stack, double the leg count and shorten them so they ripple as a fringe under the body edge, and shorten the antennae to stubby clubs.

rows.readsAs: a small red house spider
rows.defect: This is the batch's spider chassis recoloured orange and it breaks every explicit prohibition in the note: it has a pronounced waist, a separate head sphere, and four clearly visible black eyes. The legs are long spindles fanning out from both spheres rather than eight short legs bunched at the front, and there is no mouth cone at all.
rows.fix: Replace it with a single seamless unsegmented bag body - no waist, no head sphere, no eyes - and bunch eight short stubby legs at the front third with a tiny protruding mouth cone.

rows.readsAs: a pale hunched shrimp
rows.defect: No serrated rostrum spike over the eyes - only plain smooth antenna rods. The abdomen is a second smooth balloon butted onto the carapace instead of a curved, clearly segmented tail; the segment plates and the fan are crumpled underneath the body rather than sweeping back, so the swimming posture reads as a squat rather than a stretch. The eye is a single tiny dot, not prominent.
rows.fix: Extend a serrated rostrum spike forward over the eye and unroll the abdomen into a distinctly segmented curve sweeping back to the fan instead of a ball tucked under the head.

rows.readsAs: a small brown spider wearing mittens
rows.defect: The oversized pincer arms that ARE this animal are two blank tan ovals on thin sticks with no claw split, no finger and no thumb - they read as paddles or mittens. Behind them is the identical two-sphere spider chassis: the abdomen is a smooth round ball, not the flat teardrop of segmented plates the reference requires, and the four dot eyes belong to the spider body, not to this species.
rows.fix: Redraw the pedipalps as large, obviously two-fingered opposed pincers with a visible gap, and flatten the abdomen into a segmented teardrop with visible cross-banding and a blunt end.

rows.readsAs: a scorpion (from the tail alone)
rows.defect: Only the arched bead-chain tail and its dark sting carry the read. The claws are two featureless yellow ovals on sticks with no pincer split, so the animal's most expressive feature is blank. The body is a single fat sphere rather than a flat broad carapace, the tail is a chain of separate balls rather than jointed metasoma segments, and the legs are thin straight rakes shared with the Spider and Mite renders.
rows.fix: Split each claw oval into a visible two-fingered pincer with a gap, and flatten the round body into a broad low carapace so the eight legs read as spreading from a plate rather than from a ball.

rows.readsAs: a pale hunched shrimp
rows.defect: Reads as the right animal but is indistinguishable from the Prawn asset apart from tint. The serrated rostrum is a plain smooth rod, the eyes are a single tiny dot rather than prominent stalked eyes, and the abdomen is a vertical lump with the tail fan crumpled beneath the body instead of a curved segmented tail ending in a spread fan.
rows.fix: Give it stalked, clearly paired eyes and a serrated rostrum between them, and sweep the segmented abdomen back and up so the fan spreads clear of the body silhouette.

rows.readsAs: a cartoon spider
rows.defect: Three or four legs visibly spring from the ABDOMEN sphere on the right - the one thing the note forbids outright. The legs are straight tapering sticks that rake outward in a single line with no knee, no upward arch and no foot. The front sphere is as large as the abdomen, so the small-front / large-round-rear proportion does not read.
rows.fix: Re-root every leg on the front cephalothorax and give each an obvious knee so it arches up and then down to a foot.

rows.readsAs: the same cartoon spider as the Spider card, in brown
rows.defect: The eight thick densely hairy legs that ARE the tarantula are absent - the legs are the identical thin bare spindles used on the Spider, Mite and Pseudoscorpion, with no bulk and not one hair. There are no downward-stabbing fangs and no pedipalps, and legs again sprout from the abdomen sphere. Set beside the Spider asset it is the same drawing with a hue shift.
rows.fix: Thicken every leg to several times its current width and cover legs and body in visible bristle strokes, then add two downward fangs flanked by short leg-like pedipalps at the front.

rows.readsAs: a tiny white shrimp
rows.defect: It is the shrimp chassis again, and not one of the three Daphnia must-reads survives: the shell is opaque white with no gut and no brood pouch showing, there is no single large dark compound eye (only the shrimp's tiny bead), and the branched rowing antennae are the shrimp's thin unbranched whips. It is also drawn markedly wider than tall against a specified 0.8 aspect that should be taller than long.
rows.fix: Rebuild it as a tall translucent teardrop carapace with the dark gut and egg-filled brood pouch visible through the shell, one big dark eye, and two large forked rowing antennae replacing the whips and peg legs.

rows.readsAs: a cartoon mouse wearing a firework of straw
rows.defect: The spines are not a cape — they are a single starburst tuft anchored at one point on the shoulder, raking FORWARD past the head like porcupine quills, while the entire back from mid-body to rump is left smooth bare fur. The pointed pink snout is absent: the face ends in a blunt round curve with a flat white rectangle pasted on it. The ears are tall pointed triangular cat ears standing proud of the skull, where a hedgehog's ears are small, low and mostly buried. The oversized round eye with a catchlight is mouse eye, not hedgehog eye.
rows.fix: Replace the shoulder starburst with a continuous dense quill mantle that follows the whole dorsal contour from behind the eye to the rump, quills laid backward along the topline, and pull a small pink conical snout forward out of the face while shrinking the ears to low rounded nubs.

rows.readsAs: a small grey duck-billed lump, closest to a platypus or a shaved guinea pig
rows.defect: The identity must-read is absent: there are no huge outward-turned spade forepaws. Both visible limbs are the same tiny belly-line nubs with a small pale claw dot, no bigger than the hind limb, and the front one sits well back from the head near mid-body instead of almost beside the skull. The snout is not a pink pointed fleshy point — it is a wide flat horizontal bill that widens toward the tip and reads unmistakably as a duck bill. The body cylinder is correct and neckless, but the whole animal is also rendered very small in the frame with the shading flat and muddy, so even the correct part barely registers.
rows.fix: Rotate the forelimbs to the very front beside the head and enlarge them into outward-turned pink shovel hands, palms facing out with splayed claws, wider than the head; then replace the flat bill with a narrow pink cone tapering to a point.

rows.readsAs: a fat cartoon mouse
rows.defect: This is the Hedgehog asset repainted grey with a tail added, and it reads as the wrong organism. The long mobile proboscis-like snout that IS the shrew is completely absent — the face is a blunt dome with a flat white rectangle on the front. The eyes are not tiny beads: it is a single large round mouse eye with a white catchlight, the biggest feature on the head. The body is a fat round loaf despite the reference calling for aspect 2.8 and a short low-slung velvety form, and the ears are tall pointed cat triangles. Only the thin tail is right.
rows.fix: Rebuild the head with a narrow wedge skull that extends into a long flexible pointed proboscis overhanging the mouth, shrink the eye to a black bead barely wider than a whisker root, drop the ears into the fur, and stretch the body long and low instead of round.

rows.readsAs: a brown three-lump ant
rows.defect: The petiole — the whole identity — is not drawn: thorax and abdomen are joined by a straight horizontal brown ROD, not a pinched waist node, so the constriction reads as a stick between two beads rather than a wasp waist. The abdomen is a striped disc lifted from the bee's banded gaster, and the rear pair of legs plainly emerges from the ABDOMEN sphere instead of the middle segment; only four to five legs are countable. Head is a bare sphere with no mandibles.
rows.fix: Replace the connecting rod with a genuine pinched petiole node (one small bead at a narrow neck between thorax and gaster), move all six legs onto the thorax, and drop the striping from the gaster.

rows.readsAs: a fuzzy yellow bee
rows.defect: The banded amber-and-black abdomen is not there — the whole animal, head included, is one flat saturated yellow with only a faint pale hatch over the gaster; there is no black band anywhere, which is half the honeybee read. No pollen basket on the hind leg (the legs are the family's jointless sticks). Thorax fuzz is present and is the only thing separating this from the Wasp and Thrips assets, which are the same drawing.
rows.fix: Paint three hard black bands across the abdomen and darken the head to brown-black, then thicken the hind tibia into a visible loaded corbicula.

rows.readsAs: a beetle or ladybird from above
rows.defect: The elytra dome and the central seam are genuinely good and this is the strongest asset in the batch, but the six legs are ghost-grey hairline arcs at almost background contrast — they read as scratches or whiskers, not limbs — and all six leave the silhouette from the SIDES OF THE ELYTRA along the abdomen rather than from the thorax. Head and pronotum are fused into one dark mushroom blob, so the three-section read is really two.
rows.fix: Redraw the legs in the dark head colour at full opacity with a visible femur/tibia bend, and anchor all six under the pronotum.

rows.readsAs: an orange butterfly
rows.defect: Clubbed antennae and two pairs of broad blotched wings both read correctly. The coiled watch-spring proboscis is entirely absent — there is no mouthpart at all, just the family's blank eye-ball head. The only visible legs are two bare sticks hanging off the HEAD sphere, not six off the thorax, and the striped abdomen is the same ball the Ant and Termite use.
rows.fix: Add a tight coiled spiral proboscis under the head and move the legs onto the thorax.

rows.readsAs: a small orange mosquito or midge
rows.defect: Not a caddisfly. The very long thread-thin forward antennae — the single feature that names this insect — are completely absent; there is nothing in front of the head. The wings are swept straight back and held FLAT and separated, not folded tent-like into a roof over the back, and they are smooth and glassy rather than hairy. The body is bright banded orange, not drab moth-brown. The legs are three tiny curled hooks tucked under the chin that never reach the ground. The render is also broken in composition: the whole animal is stranded in the upper-left quadrant while its shadow ellipse sits far below and offset right, so it hangs in space with roughly half the frame empty beneath it.
rows.fix: Give it two antennae longer than the whole body held forward, close the wings into a single steep roof-tent over the abdomen with a hairy matte edge, recolour to drab grey-brown, and reseat the body over its shadow.
rows.verifyWhy: Verdict upheld, but two of the stated causes are wrong and the composition claim is misdescribed. WHAT IS ACTUALLY DRAWN (measured on the 440x440 canvas, foreground bbox x150-318, y130-185, center 234,157.5): a small bright-orange flying dipteran in left-facing side view. Head is a plain saturated-orange sphere carrying TWO large slate-grey eye discs stacked one above the other (upper-rear and lower-front), each with a white specular dot. Thorax is a second orange ball. Abdomen is a chain of five bright orange beads separated by dark chocolate-brown crescent bands - a wasp/hoverfly banding, high chroma, no drabness anywhere. Three hooked legs hang below, and all three sprout from ONE tight cluster directly under the HEAD rather than spread along the thorax. MUST-READ 1, 'hairy wings folded tent-like over the back': ABSENT and correctly described by the first judge. Two long, narrow, glass-CLEAR membranous blades with fine longitudinal veins sweep straight back horizontally and splay apart vertically (upper blade tilted up, lower blade tilted down), tips overshooting the abdomen tip by ~50px. No hair, no opacity, no roof/tent fold - this is dragonfly/mayfly wing furniture. MUST-READ 2, 'very long thread-thin antennae held forward': ABSENT, confirmed at 10x magnification. There is no appendage of ANY kind forward of the head; the leading edge of the silhouette at x=150 is bare orange sphere against background. No stub, no palp, no faint thin line. This is the single defining feature of the animal and it does not exist. MUST-READ 3, 'moth-like drab body': ABSENT - the body is ~#E8952E orange with near-black bands. NET: reads as a hoverfly or gnat, not a caddisfly (the first judge said 'mosquito' - close enough in family, but the beaded banded abdomen and short stout head read hoverfly, not the long-legged thin-bodied mosquito). CORRECTIONS TO THE CLAIM: (a) 'stranded in the upper-left quadrant' is WRONG horizontally - the animal spans x150-318 and its center x=234 sits just RIGHT of the frame midline (220). It is genuinely high (y130-185, occupying only the 30-42% band of frame height), so the defect is vertical, not left-side. (b) 'shadow far below and offset right' is HALF wrong. The shadow ellipse measures x122-278, y281-310, center (200, 295.5). It is indeed far below - a 96px gap between the animal's lowest pixel (y185) and the shadow's top edge (y281), a gap larger than the animal's entire 56px height - but its center is offset ~34px to the LEFT of the body center, not right. ADDITIONAL DEFECTS NOT IN THE CLAIM, needed for the fix: the packet asks for posture 'crawling' and this is rendered hovering/flying with legs dangling and wings deployed; the render is also undersized, filling only 169x56 of a 440x440 frame (13% of frame height); rendered aspect with wings is ~3.0 against a spec of 2.2. FIX ORDER: add the two forward thread antennae at least 1.5x body length (the identity feature), refold the wings into an opaque hairy roof-tent tented over the abdomen with the tips meeting on the midline, desaturate the whole body to drab tan/grey-brown and kill the black abdominal banding, re-seat the legs along the thorax, then re-center the composition and reunite the shadow with the feet.

rows.readsAs: a pale mosquito or crane fly
rows.defect: The huge crossed sickle mandibles that ARE the male dobsonfly are missing entirely — under the head are only the same three tiny curled hooks the Caddisfly has. The body is not a soft flabby elongated abdomen but the family's hard bead-string of alternating light and dark spheres, and the render is broken: the LAST abdominal bead is detached, separated by a clear gap and stranded on its own to the right of the body. The animal also floats in the upper-left with its shadow far below and offset. Only the four long net-veined wings survive, and they are the same wing part pasted on the Caddisfly.
rows.fix: Draw two enormous crossed sickle mandibles projecting a head-length forward, reconnect the abdomen into one continuous soft tapering body, and centre it over its shadow.
rows.verifyWhy:
Upheld, but two of their stated causes are located/described wrongly. WHAT I SAW at 7-12x zoom on the 440x440 canvas (body bbox x98-341, y120-196): HEAD is a bare pale cream sphere at the far left (x~100-130) carrying TWO large dark navy eyes stacked vertically on the same visible side, each with a small specular dot, giving a figure-eight look. Forward of that head there is NOTHING AT ALL - I cropped x60-130 at 12x specifically to hunt for small mandibles and the silhouette edge is a clean empty dome against black. No jaws, no tusks, no palps, and also no antennae of any kind. The defining must-read, 'huge crossed sickle mandibles in the male', is flatly absent, and that alone is the FAIL.

CORRECTION 1 - the curled hooks are NOT 'under the chin'. There are exactly three thin dark filaments drawn as narrow downward LOOPS, and they hang from the UNDERSIDE OF THE THORAX AND FIRST ABDOMINAL SEGMENT (x~115-165, y~170-196), i.e. entirely behind the head, which ends at x~130. They are the leg set, evenly spaced along the belly, not a mouthpart cluster - they are not paired, not crossed, and not at the mouth. So a fix must ADD mandibles at the head apex; it must not try to re-aim these three loops, which are legitimately legs (though they read as limp loops rather than jointed insect legs).

CORRECTION 2 - the wings are actually the ONE must-read that lands. Two pairs of long, narrow, translucent smoky wings with fine lengthwise striations that do read as net venation, spread in an X (correct for the packet's posture: flying, so 'folded' is not a fair complaint). Their only shortfall is length: the tips end at x~305-320, level with the abdomen rather than 'well past' it.

CONFIRMED - the abdomen is a hard bead-string, and worse than stated: SEVEN discrete flat circles alternating pale cream / dark brown with visible dark constrictions between them, reading like a caterpillar or a necklace. Nothing about it is 'soft elongated flabby'. That is must-read #3 violated.

CONFIRMED - the terminal bead is detached. Measured on row scans y=155-165: the last attached bead ends at x~317, then a genuine void from x~318-325 containing only faint translucent wing haze (no body pixels), then a free-floating pale circle at x~326-340. ~9px of black gap, stranded past the wing tips.

CORRECTION 3 - 'floating far above an offset shadow' is half wrong. The vertical float (body bottom y=196, shadow band y~285-318, ~90px of air) is the flying-posture convention and is not by itself a defect. The real, smaller shadow problem is horizontal scale and placement: the shadow ellipse spans only x112-272 (center ~192) while the animal spans x98-341 (center ~220), so it is both too narrow and shifted ~28px left - the entire abdomen tip and the rear wing tips overhang past its right edge with no shadow under them.

CORRECTION 4 - 'reads as a pale crane fly' is loose. A crane fly has one wing pair and enormous trailing legs; this has four spread wings, three stubby leg loops and a beaded abdomen, so it reads closer to a pale generic damselfly/lacewing. The judge's verdict stands regardless: 1 of 3 must-reads present, the identity-defining mandibles absent, plus a hard render break in the abdomen.

rows.readsAs: a grey housefly
rows.defect: The compound eye is a single black dot roughly a third of the head — it does not fill the head and it is not red, so the loudest housefly cue is only half delivered. Wing count is wrong in the other direction: I can count three to four wing plates on the one side, so this reads as a four-winged insect, and there are no knob halteres anywhere. The thorax is flat grey with no bristles and no longitudinal stripes.
rows.fix: Blow the eye up to swallow the entire head and colour it deep red, then cut to exactly two wings plus a visible pair of haltere knobs.

rows.readsAs: a cream grub or maggot
rows.defect: Legless, segmented and creamy-glossy all read. But the taper is missing — it is a stack of ten identical overlapping discs, equally blunt at BOTH ends, so there is no pointed head end and no fat rear. Worse, the head end carries a dark brown ball with a white-highlighted EYE on it, borrowed from the family's head sphere; a fly maggot has no eyes and no head capsule, and that dark bead turns it into a caterpillar. It also hovers a long way above its shadow.
rows.fix: Shrink the discs progressively toward the head into a real cone point and delete the dark eyed head bead, leaving only two tiny black mouth hooks.

rows.readsAs: a green grasshopper or katydid
rows.defect: The spined raptorial foreleg is genuinely drawn — a folded triangle with tick-mark spines along the inner edge — and it is the one thing keeping this out of FAIL. Everything else is wrong: there is NO neck and NO long slender prothorax, the wedge head sits directly tangent on the family's fat thorax ball exactly as every other asset does, and the posture is the family's flat horizontal flight pose rather than upright, with long green wings laid over the back. At thumbnail size the combination reads grasshopper, not mantis.
rows.fix: Stretch the prothorax into a long narrow stalk that lifts the head and forelegs clear of the body, and pitch the whole animal upright.

rows.readsAs: a large drab nocturnal moth
rows.defect: All three must-reads are visibly present and correct: the antennae are unmistakably comb-feathered with clear side barbs, the thorax carries a dense collar of pale bristles, and the wings are broad, dusty and drab. Minor: the wings splay back rather than tenting, and the visible legs hang off the head sphere like the rest of the family.
rows.fix: Rotate the wings forward into a shallower roof-tent and reseat the legs on the thorax.

rows.readsAs: a grey pillbug or globular springtail
rows.defect: The stubby segmented six-legged body is right and there is a curved rear appendage that can be read as a furcula. But that furcula is a single UNFORKED wire that swings out behind and below the animal rather than a forked spring latched flat under the abdomen, so the spring-load never reads. The antennae are two long straight bare wires nearly half the body length instead of short beaded ones, and they read as a shrimp's.
rows.fix: Fork the furcula into two tines and tuck it flat against the underside, then shorten the antennae to a third of their length and bead them.

rows.readsAs: an ant painted cream
rows.defect: This is the Ant asset recoloured and nothing else — same head sphere, same egg thorax, same striped abdomen ellipse, same rod between them, same stick legs at the same anchor points, same shadow. Both of the traits that separate a termite from an ant are drawn the ant way: the antennae are BENT/ELBOWED when a termite's must be a straight bead string, and there is a clear pinched constriction at the thorax-abdomen joint when a termite's must be a broad continuous joint. It also carries the family's glossy dot eye, and a worker termite is blind and eyeless.
rows.fix: Straighten the antennae into a straight bead-string, delete the eye, and fuse thorax to abdomen across a joint as wide as the abdomen itself so no waist survives.
rows.verifyWhy:
VERDICT UPHELD, but two of the three stated causes are factually wrong and must not be used as the fix brief.

WHAT IS ACTUALLY ON CANVAS (440x440, creature spans x~158-291, y~182-224; measured by contiguous luminance run at mid-body y=203, threshold 60):
Three cream/ivory balls in a row - head (depth ~31px, x158-190), a near-perfectly circular thorax (depth 41px, x206-218), and a slightly smaller ovoid abdomen (depth 40px, x259-267) carrying faint vertical striations. Six olive-grey tapered legs. One flat elliptical drop shadow. Two smooth antennae. One large glossy black eye with a white specular catchlight on the head.

MUST-READ 1, 'pale soft translucent segmented body' - PARTIAL. Pale is unmistakable (ivory/cream). But the shading is hard specular pearl/ceramic, not soft or translucent, and only the abdomen carries segmentation (faint vertical striae); head and thorax are featureless smooth spheres.

MUST-READ 2, 'straight bead-string antennae' - ABSENT, but NOT for the reason claimed. CORRECTION: the antennae are NOT bent or elbowed. Zoomed to 12x (crop x128-190, y158-200) they are two perfectly smooth, continuously tapering filaments describing a single gentle arc, with no kink, no joint and no angular break anywhere along their length. For contrast I rendered Ant.png at the same crop: the Ant's antennae ARE genuinely geniculate - a straight scape, a hard visible elbow, then a straight flagellum. The Termite's are a different curve primitive entirely. The REAL defect is (a) zero beading - they are smooth drawn strokes with no moniliform bead segmentation of any kind, and (b) they spring from the top-front of the head and sweep UP AND BACKWARD over the skull like insect 'eyebrows', where a termite's should project forward. Fix brief: replace the two smooth arcs with a forward-projecting straight string of 10-12 discrete beads each.

MUST-READ 3, 'broad joint where the abdomen meets the thorax' - ABSENT/INVERTED, but again NOT as described. CORRECTION: there is NO rod waist. The Ant asset has a literal thin dark petiole rod bridging thorax to gaster (plainly visible in Ant.png, and its legs hang off a connecting under-rod that runs the whole body length). The Termite has nothing of the kind - the thorax and abdomen ellipses simply overlap each other directly. What IS wrong is that the overlap is too shallow: at mid-height the junction measures 21px against 41px thorax and 40px abdomen, i.e. 51% of adjacent segment depth, and the two circle outlines cross in a sharp cusp that cuts a hard V notch into BOTH the dorsal and the ventral silhouette (visible at 13x, crop x218-268). The head/thorax neck is the same story: 22px vs 41px, 54%. So the joint reads as a pinched ant-like constriction and the must-read fails - but the fix is 'push the ellipses together until the junction is ~85-100% of segment depth and kill the cusp', not 'remove a rod'.

EYES - CLAIM CONFIRMED. Packet says eyes: hidden, note says workers are blind. A glossy jet-black eye ~12px across on a ~31px head, with a bright white highlight, is one of the most salient marks in the whole image. Straight spec violation.

CLAIM 'it is the Ant asset recoloured cream - same spheres, same rod waist, same leg anchors, same shadow' - OVERSTATED. Rendered side by side at identical crop and scale the two assets differ materially: the Ant is longer and more spread, has the petiole rod plus an underside connecting rod, brown legs, a wide elliptical thorax and a smaller gaster; the Termite has three tightly abutted balls, olive-grey legs, and a circular thorax equal in depth to the abdomen. They share a chassis FAMILY (three-ball generic insect + striated abdomen + flat ellipse shadow), which is the real problem, but this is not a recolour of the Ant file.

ADDITIONAL DEFECT NEITHER OF US LISTED: the leg anchors are anatomically wrong on their own terms. At 6x (crop x150-295, y200-265) three legs hang from under the HEAD, one from the thorax, and two from under the ABDOMEN. All six should spring from the thorax. Also no mandibles, which a termite worker head badly needs to carry identity once the eye is removed.

BAND: FAIL. Two of three must-reads are unreadable and an explicit spec field (eyes: hidden) is contradicted; the silhouette reads as a pale ant.

rows.readsAs: a small pale bee or fruit fly

The reference asks for aspect 3.5 and a slender cigar-shaped body; what is drawn is the family's stack of three fat spheres at roughly 1.6 — the single least slender shape possible. rows.verifyWhy:
I zoomed the 440px canvas 5x and cropped the head, mouth region and wing tip at 16-34x, and compared the same crops against Bee.png and Wasp.png from the same folder. VERDICT UPHELD, but two of the three stated causes need correcting.

WHAT IS ACTUALLY ON THE CANVAS: a pale straw-yellow insect built from the family's three-ball chassis - a round head sphere (orig x158-192), a fat spherical thorax (x191-231) and a fat spherical abdomen (x235-273), each a separate shaded ball with a visible pinch between them. Six thin ochre legs, two thin curved antennae sweeping up-left from the top of the head, one large glossy black eye with a white highlight, four broad translucent grey-blue wing plates fanned over and behind the thorax, a white/cream crosshatch texture patch laid over the front of the abdomen, and an elliptical ground shadow.

CONFIRMED - CIGAR BODY ABSENT. The silhouette is a bead-string of three balls, not a parallel-sided cylinder. There is no uniform-width segment anywhere: the thorax ball is the widest point and the body necks in hard both fore and aft of it. Against a real thrips (an even, narrow tube with no thoracic bulge) this reads wrong at any size.

CORRECTION 1 - THE ASPECT NUMBER IN THE CLAIM IS WRONG. "about 1.6" is not what is drawn. Measured on a yellow-body mask with 3 passes of erosion to strip the legs, the solid body runs x163-263, H=35 -> 2.89; taking the true nose-to-tail-tip extent including the wing-shrouded abdomen (x~159 to x~273 = 114 long, max depth ~40) gives ~2.6-2.9. So the shortfall against the 3.5 spec is real but modest - roughly 2.7 vs 3.5, not 1.6 vs 3.5. For comparison the same measurement gives Bee 2.65-2.81 and Wasp 3.62-3.68, so Thrips is currently drawn to the Bee's proportion when it should be longer and thinner than even the Wasp. The fix is not "stretch it 2x" - it is "delete the three-ball topology and draw one even tube", because the defect is the beading, not the length.

CONFIRMED - NO WING FRINGE, AT ALL. At 22x the forewing and hindwing margins are clean, smoothly-antialiased curves carrying two or three pale interior vein streaks. There is not a single hair, bristle or serration on any margin. The bee's wing tip crop at the identical coordinates is pixel-for-pixel the same construction. The wings are also the wrong planform: broad rounded leaf-shaped plates roughly 72 long by 18-20 deep (~4:1), where a thrips wing is a ~10:1 strap whose fringe hairs are longer than the blade is wide - the fringe is most of the wing's visual mass and it is the feature the order Thysanoptera is named for. Minor correction: the plates are not "clear" - they are opaque-ish slate/grey-blue with light vein streaks, plus the cream crosshatch patch over the abdomen.

CONFIRMED - NO RASPING MOUTHCONE. I looked hard at this because it is the kind of feature that hides. Boosted 34x on the front-lower head there IS a small angular nub, ~2px, on the leading edge of the head sphere at about (157,205). It is not a mouthcone: the identical nub sits at the identical relative position on Bee.png (I cropped it), so it is a shared chassis jaw stub, not a thrips feature. Nothing cone-shaped, nothing asymmetric, nothing projecting downward from the head. Effectively absent.

CORRECTION 2 - "desaturated Bee" overstates the colour part and understates the size part. The hue is pale straw yellow, which is a defensible thrips colour (many are pale yellow/straw) - colour is not the defect and should not be "fixed". The bee-ness comes from geometry, and from scale: measured on the same canvas the thrips body bbox is 108x41 against the bee's 149x71, i.e. it is the bee chassis shrunk. The one thing that HAS been differentiated from the Bee is the fur - the bee's radiating thoracic bristles are correctly absent here, and the abdomen ball is a bit larger. So this is not a straight recolour; it is the bee's body plan with the fur removed.

ADDITIONAL DEFECT THE FIRST JUDGE DID NOT FLAG: the packet asks for eyes:small, and the eye drawn is a large glossy black bead about 28% of head width, indistinguishable in size from the bee's. Also headFrac reads ~0.29 against the spec 0.2.

BAND: FAIL stands. Two of three must-reads (fringed strap wings, asymmetric cone rasping mouth) are wholly absent rather than merely weak, and the third is contradicted by the chassis topology. Nothing in the image says thrips; it reads as a small pale bee.

That is a petiole pinched to ~16% of thorax height over a ~20px span - dimensionally a correct wasp waist, not 'a solid wedge'. What is actually wrong is that the petiole is INVISIBLE at 1:1 for two separate reasons: (a) it is painted in dark shadow olive - sampling column x=187 gives RGB 102,86,9 for y=216..221 against a 5,6,12 background, so the only body-coloured pixels at the pinch are near-black and read as background; (b) the entire volume ABOVE the petiole (y=192..215 at x=186) is filled by a blown-out white specular bloom (RGB ~200-230 across all channels) plus the two translucent wing roots, which optically bridges thorax to abdomen. So the fix is NOT 'draw a waist' - the waist exists; the fix is to stop the bloom+wing wash from filling the notch, and to lift the petiole out of shadow into saturated gold with a dark chitin outline.

Aposematic contrast, which is half of a wasp's identity, is missing entirely. The fix is a contrast fix (drop the dark bands to near-black chitin), not a 'add bands' fix.

CORRECTION 3 - THE ASPECT IS ON SPEC, NOT 'SQUAT'. Body bbox excluding wings and legs: x=104 (front of head) to x=262 (abdomen tip) = 158px long; y=187 to y=233 = 46px tall. The result at 1:1 is a pale glowing white-yellow blob where the banded gaster should be. Looked at the full-size PNG, then re-rendered three zooms (whole body 3x, head 8x, limb band 6x) and ran a pixel scan for silhouette bbox and for any yellow pixel. VERDICT UPHELD, but two-thirds of the stated causes need correcting and three real defects went unnamed.

WHAT IS ACTUALLY ON THE CANVAS: one taupe egg-shaped body ellipse with soft airbrushed mid-brown blotches; a second, smaller rounded ellipse plugged onto its front-right as the head, with a visible overlap seam where the two ovals meet; a fat crescent tail sweeping UP and back over the body, carrying one big dark charcoal racing-stripe blotch down its inner curve and ending in a blunt rounded club; and four dark olive-drab limbs. Silhouette bbox is 84,154 -> 355,269 = 272 x 116 px.

MUST-READ 1 (heavy limbs splayed out sideways) - FAILED, but NOT for the stated reason. The claim 'thin vertical pegs tucked under the belly' is wrong on two counts: the limbs are not thin (each is a chunky rounded rod roughly 20-24 px wide against a 116 px tall animal) and they are not vertical (the forelimb rakes down-and-back at about 30 deg, the hindlimb rakes down-and-forward, i.e. a mammal walking gait). The actual defect is threefold: (a) they attach at the belly MIDLINE under the body ellipse rather than at the flanks, so no shoulder or hip is visible; (b) there is no laterally bowed elbow or knee anywhere - the rod is a single unbroken taper from attachment to tip, so the varanid sprawl (limb out to the side, elbow above the shoulder line, body slung between them) simply does not exist; (c) there is NO FOOT AT ALL - each limb terminates in a plain rounded blunt cap with zero toes and zero claws, and the belly does not clear the ground because the body ellipse sits almost on the shadow.

MUST-READ 2 (long muscular tail about half the total length) - FAILED, and the judge did not flag it. Measured, the tail runs x=84 to about x=190 = ~106 px of a 272 px total, i.e. ~39%, not half; worse, it does not trail as a heavy tapering muscle mass. It arcs UPWARD in a fat even-width crescent and ends blunt. 'Banana tail' is a fair read; a rat or opossum tail read is also fair. It is the single most eye-catching shape in the asset and it points at the wrong animal.

MUST-READ 3 (long forked yellow tongue and loose scaly neck skin) - FAILED, and the claim here is exactly right. A full-image pixel scan for any yellow-dominant pixel (r>120, g>100, b at least 40 below min(r,g)) returned ZERO hits - there is no tongue geometry of any colour, forked or otherwise. The mouth is a single hairline ruled stroke that does not even reach the snout tip and has no gape, no jaw line and no lip. There is no neck: the head ellipse abuts the body ellipse directly, so there is no surface for loose skin, no dewlap, no throat folds. No scale texture anywhere on the body - the markings are soft blurred airbrush dots, not beaded osteoderms.

DEFECTS THE FAIL DID NOT NAME (fix these too): (1) THE EYE IS THE WRONG EYE. The reference row calls for 'small' eyes; the render has a large pale-cream almond occupying a big share of the skull with a hard VERTICAL SLIT pupil - a gecko/cat eye. A Komodo has a small round dark eye. This is a bigger identity error than it looks, because it is the only detail on the head and it is loudly wrong. (2) ASPECT IS 2.34 AGAINST A SPEC OF 3.2 - the animal is far too short and too deep-bodied, which is the direct cause of the 'fat rat' read; the body ellipse is nearly as tall as it is long. (3) HEAD FRACTION IS ~0.24 AGAINST A SPEC OF 0.2, and the skull is a plain rounded oval with no snout taper, no nostril, no jowl and no temporal mass.

OVERALL READ: a taupe, spotted, blunt-nosed, neckless, footless quadruped with a slit-pupil eye and a fat upcurled club tail. It reads as a cartoon newt/salamander or a spotted rodent. All three must-reads are absent as identity signals. FAIL stands.

rows.verifyWhy:
UPHELD, with three corrections to the stated causes.

WHAT I SAW (440x440, read raw, then re-read at gamma-boosted 5x-8x crops of head, back, feet and tail; silhouette masks of Marine_Iguana.png and Iguana.png overlaid).

1) SNOUT - must-read ABSENT, judge correct. At 8x the head is a plain grey ellipse, body-x 318->392 (len ~74px) by 43px tall, ratio 1.72. The green Iguana's head is the same ellipse at 1.77 (x ~330->415, 85 x 48). Front-edge trace per row on the marine goes 370,377,381,384,387,389,390,391,391,392,392,391,391,387,386,383,380,377,372,366 - a smooth continuous convex arc with no vertical facet anywhere. There is no blunt/square muzzle, no truncated terminal plane, no nostril mass. There is also NO salt crust on the face: the whole head is one flat grey fill with a single bright rim-light along the top-front edge, a white round eye with a vertical slit pupil, and a straight thin mouth line - pixel-identical construction to Iguana.png, same eye at the same relative position, same mouth line at the same height, only the hue changed. The reference note ('stubby blunt face - NOT the long pointed green-iguana profile') is directly violated.

2) TAIL - must-read ABSENT, judge correct, now quantified. Vertical thickness of the tail sampled every 8px from the tip inward: 26,33,34,33,31,30,30,30,30,29,29,29,28,28,28,29,29 - dead constant. Body depth over the ribcage is 49-53. So the tail is a uniform round tube about 55-60% of the body's depth that hooks upward at the tip and ends in a rounded knob, carrying one darker interior stripe. A laterally flattened paddle in side view must be at least as deep as the trunk and taper to a blade/keel; nothing here does. It is the same banana the green Iguana wears (that asset's tail measures 30-38 over the same span). The one feature that makes this animal a swimmer is genuinely missing.

3) CLAWS - must-read ABSENT, judge correct. At 6x the fore and hind limbs are two tapering rounded capsules (upper + lower segment) ending in a blunt rounded stub. Zero digits, zero toes, zero claws; the only appendage is a small backward spur at the fore elbow. Nothing hooked or curved anywhere on the feet.

4) CONTRAST - judge correct, and worse than stated. Sampled body fill = RGB(37,39,42); dorsal background directly above = RGB(9,14,20); left background = RGB(6,9,15). WCAG contrast body:background = 1.29:1 (1.33:1 against the left field). The green Iguana in the same frame measures 4.63:1. The tail's interior stripe samples RGB(13,14,17) - literally background luminance. The 'dark sooty body' note has been taken as a value instruction and the animal has been rendered 3.6x flatter than its own sibling; on first read the silhouette is barely separable from the field.

CORRECTIONS TO THE CLAIM:
- 'This is the green Iguana asset recoloured' is close but overstated. Silhouette IoU against Iguana.png is 0.768, not 1.0: the marine is the same chassis re-scaled, bbox 346x222 vs the iguana's 392x222, with a shorter tail and a slightly shorter head. Head, mouth, eye, limb form, foot, neck carriage, topline and tail are shared; scale is not. Call it recolour-plus-rescale on one chassis, which is the finding that matters for the family.
- The claim omits that ONE must-read IS present and is drawn correctly: the low spiny crest. At 7x there is a clean row of about ten backward-raked triangular dorsal spikes from the nape down the back, noticeably lower and more swept than the green Iguana's tall upright spines - this was genuinely re-authored, not recoloured, and should not be touched by the fix.
- The claim also omits that the flank blotching WAS re-authored: the iguana carries dark-green blotches, the marine carries warm cream/tan mottling that reads plausibly as salt encrustation. The problem is placement, not absence - the pale crust sits on the ribs and shoulder where the reference asks for it on the SNOUT, and there is not one pale pixel on the face.

VERDICT: 1 of 3 must-reads readable; the identity feature (paddle tail) absent; the reference note's explicit prohibition (long rounded green-iguana snout) violated; body value collapsed to 1.29:1. FAIL stands.

FIX ORDER: (a) rebuild the skull as a short deep box - truncate the front of the ellipse into a near-vertical blunt plane, drop head length to ~1.2-1.3x its height, and put the pale salt crust on the snout tip and above the nostrils; (b) rebuild the tail as a laterally flattened blade - depth at least equal to the trunk at the base, tapering as a straight-edged paddle rather than a constant tube, and kill the upward hook; (c) add three or four curved claws per foot; (d) lift the body fill to at least 3:1 against the field (target the Iguana's 4.6:1 minus a step for 'sooty'). Keep the crest and the pale flank mottling.
