Trunk x=205..340 (135px, max depth 65px at x=260-285). Head x=340..410 (70px, max depth 51px). headFrac = 70/385 = 0.18, which is on-spec (0.2); that is the ONLY spec number the asset hits.

MUSTREAD 1 - 'long deeply forked flicking tongue': ABSENT, and not merely small. At 9x the snout tip is a bare rounded ellipse cap; the mouth is a single 2px hairline that terminates exactly at the silhouette edge with nothing protruding. The scan confirms no pixels beyond x=410, so there is no tongue anywhere on the canvas, not hidden, not tucked, not drawn in body colour. The judge is right.

MUSTREAD 2 - 'laterally flattened tail longer than the body': the tail is round and unflattened, and it is worse than the judge described. It is not a tapering tail at all: the scan shows a CONSTANT 36px thickness from x=85 all the way to x=200 (115px of dead-straight uniform hose) ending in a fully rounded capsule cap at x=25. There is no taper, no keel, no dorsal ridge, no vertical blade profile - the dark interior stripe reads as cylindrical shading, reinforcing 'tube'. CORRECTION to the judge's length claim, which the fix must not take literally: the tail (180px) IS longer than the trunk alone (135px). It is shorter than head+trunk (205px), i.e. ~0.88 of snout-to-vent, where a monitor should be ~1.5x SVL. So 'no longer than the body' is only true if 'body' includes the head. Simply lengthening the tail would not fix this shape - the round constant-width hose is the primary defect, the length a secondary one.

MUSTREAD 3 - 'muscular sprawled limbs with large hooked claws': the claws are absent, confirmed at 8x on both pairs. Each limb is a plain tapered tube that narrows to a blunt rounded stub floating just above the ellipse shadow - no foot plate, no toes, no digits, no claw at all. ADDITION the judge missed: the posture is also wrong. Packet says posture 'sprawling'; the limbs are drawn as near-vertical columns hanging straight down under a deep barrel body (the classic pony/ungulate chassis stance), with no lateral splay, no elbow/knee angle out to the side, and no body-close-to-ground line. So this mustRead fails twice, on the claws and on the sprawl.

NOTE - 'the neck is long and snake-like, unlike the neckless build of most lizards': directly contradicted, confirmed by measurement. At x=335 the trunk is 41px deep, at x=340 it is 38px, and at x=345 the head is already 41px and climbing. The head ellipse simply abuts the front of the barrel; there is a single-column waist and then the head. Neck length is effectively 0px on a 385px animal, when the note asks for the single most distinctive proportion of the genus. I cannot verify 'the most neckless asset in the batch' (I only inspected this one), so that superlative should be dropped, but 'zero neck' is exact.

WHAT IS ACTUALLY PRESENT, in the asset's favour: the body carries a scattered brown ocellated blotch pattern (roughly 20 soft dark-brown spots, some in loose diagonal rows across the flank) which is a genuine monitor cue - Nile/savannah monitors carry exactly that ocelli field. The eye is a well-drawn white sclera with a vertical slit pupil. Those are the only species signals on the asset, and neither is a mustRead. Minor extra inaccuracy: monitors have ROUND pupils; the vertical slit reads gecko/crocodilian.

READ CORRECTION: 'brown salamander plush' is close but not quite what I see. The barrel is too deep-bellied and the legs too column-like and too far under the body for a salamander (salamanders sprawl); with the fat spotted barrel, blunt round head, neckless join, pillar legs and uniform round hose tail it reads closest to a generic spotted newt/otter-shaped toy quadruped. Either way the point holds - it does not read as a monitor lizard. FAIL upheld.

rows.readsAs: a grey cartoon newt, indistinguishable from the Monitor and Komodo except for hue
rows.defect: The identity must-read is absent: the head is the same smooth rounded ellipse every other asset in this batch wears — not massive, not blocky, and with no jowls at all (the jaw line is a single straight ruled stroke, so there is no cheek mass to jowl). The body carries scattered random speckles rather than heavy transverse bands, and there is no beaded scale texture anywhere — the surface is a flat airbrushed gradient. Only the thick body-length tail is roughly right, and that is the shared banana shape arriving by default rather than by design.
rows.fix: Widen the rear of the skull into a heavy blocky wedge with bulging jowls behind the jaw line, and replace the speckles with bold white transverse bands across the trunk and tail.
rows.verifyWhy:
I looked at the 440x440 PNG at full size, then re-cropped and upscaled 4-5x on the head, mid-body, tail and legs, and re-rendered the whole frame at 2.6x brightness to pull the near-black limbs out of the background. The FAIL stands: two of the three must-reads are wholly absent and the third is satisfied only by length, not form. Corrections and additions to the original claim follow.

HEAD (mustRead: massive jowled blocky head). At 5x the head is a single smooth ellipse, long-axis horizontal, butted directly against the body ellipse with zero neck articulation. The snout terminus is fully rounded - there is no squared muzzle box, no angular jaw corner, no temporal/masseter bulge, and no cheek lobe of any kind, so the jowl read is genuinely absent. CORRECTION to the claim: the head is not undersized. I measured it at ~90px against a ~142px body ellipse and a ~356px total length, i.e. headFrac ~0.25 against the spec'd 0.28, and it is the largest head-to-body in this family. So the 'massive' half of the must-read is proportionally delivered; what is missing is specifically the jowl mass and the blocky geometry. The fix is a SHAPE change - widen a distinct cheek/jowl lobe behind and below the jaw line and square off the snout terminus and the lower jaw corner - not a scale-up. The claim's 'single straight ruled jaw stroke' is correct and understates it: the mouth is a 1px hairline that slopes slightly upward, and it stops roughly 15px short of the snout tip, so it does not even close at the front of the face. The eye is a large white almond with a black vertical slit pupil - readable, but oversized for the 'normal' eye spec and identical to the Monitor's and Komodo's.

BODY (mustRead: heavy banded body with beaded scales). Confirmed absent, with one refinement. The markings are not 'speckles' in the hard sense - they are soft Gaussian-blurred brown blobs of varying size scattered over the flank. There is a faint diagonal chain of them across the mid-flank that reads as noise rather than as any organised pattern; nothing anywhere approaches a transverse band. Bands here need to be hard-edged, full-height, running dorsum to belly and repeating along the trunk. The surface underneath is a flat airbrushed light-to-dark gradient with no beading, no scale cells, no tessellation, no specular pinpoints. ADDITION the claim did not name: a hard white rim-light arc is stroked along the dorsal edge of both the body and the head, which strengthens the inflated-balloon read and works directly against a heavy beaded lizard.

TAIL (mustRead: thick tail slightly longer than the body). Length is roughly right - the tail runs ~140px against a ~135-142px body, so 'slightly longer' is honestly met. Form is not: at 4x the tail is a constant-width tube that never tapers, ending in a blunt rounded cap, with one dark rounded-rect stripe inset along its length that reads as an interior shading core rather than as markings. No taper, no banding, no scale texture, no dorsal ridge.

DEFECTS THE JUDGE DID NOT NAME. (a) The four limbs are near-black two-segment bent tubes that terminate in blunt rounded tips - there are no feet, no digits and no claws at all, on any of the four. (b) The posture is wrong for the row: the row specifies 'sprawling', but the legs drop as near-vertical columns and hold the body high off the ground shadow, which is a mammalian upright stance. (c) No neck - the two ellipses simply overlap.

CHASSIS / FAMILY. I opened Monitor_Lizard.png and Komodo_Dragon.png to test the comparison. The chassis claim is correct but the phrasing 'except for hue' is imprecise and should not be quoted as the cause: the Monitor is visibly longer and lower-slung (a genuinely different aspect), so hue is not the only variable. The accurate statement is that all three are assembled from an identical primitive set - same ellipse trunk, same ellipse head butted on with no neck, same 1px ruled mouth line, same white-almond slit eye, same four bent near-black tube legs with no feet, same constant-width tail carrying one dark inner stripe, same blurred blob speckles, same white dorsal rim light - with only aspect ratio, hue and tail curvature varied between them. Tegu and Komodo in particular are near-superimposable.

OVERALL. Stripped of hue, this silhouette reads as a generic blob quadruped - closer to a cartoon otter or seal than to any varanid or teiid. Nothing in the frame identifies a Tegu.

rows.readsAs: a dark green flower or unopened rose/camellia with a pale pearl at its centre, or a mossy stone with an egg set in it
rows.defect: A hard, glossy, light-mint SPHERE sits at the exact centre of the head and is the brightest object in the frame; it reads as a separate body (pearl/pistil/egg), which no cabbage has — cabbage identity is a solid uninterrupted head. The thin white lines do not read as thick branching midribs; they are smooth petal-outline arcs radiating from that sphere, which reinforces the flower read. Colour is near-black olive throughout, not the specified blue-green with a waxy pale bloom, so the waxy cabbage surface is absent. The 'loose flaring outer leaves around the base' amount to a single pointed leaf poking out low-right plus one small tab left — there is no skirt of wavy open outer leaves.
rows.fix: Delete the central pale sphere entirely and close the head over it with two more overlapping wrap leaves whose edges spiral off-centre, then lift the whole palette to a pale glaucous blue-green with a dusty bloom and redraw the veins as thick, tapering white midribs that each start at a leaf base and branch outward — and ring the base with three to four wide wavy-edged outer leaves flaring away from the ball.

rows.readsAs: a peacock's fanned tail or a fan-palm/sea-anemone spray, with a lit streetlamp standing behind it
rows.defect: The single tall bare vertical stem topped by a large solid white dome reads unambiguously as a streetlamp and dominates the image; the reference asks for TINY white four-petal flowers, and instead one oversized featureless cap sits on a naked pole. The growth form is a rigid symmetric radial fan of straight rays pinned to one ground point — not a sprawling floating MAT of hollow succulent stems, so the aquatic identity is gone (no waterline, no float, no sprawl). Leaflets are uniform elongated ovals repeated at equal spacing down each ray with NO larger terminal leaflet at any tip, so the pinnate-with-big-end-leaflet must-read is absent. White threadlike roots at the nodes are entirely missing.
rows.fix: Rebuild it as a low horizontal sprawling mat: three or four hollow pale-green stems drifting sideways and overlapping at differing heights rather than radiating from one point, each stem carrying paired rounded leaflets that end in one clearly larger spade-shaped terminal leaflet, with fine white root threads trailing down from the stem nodes and the flower reduced to a few pinhead four-petal white specks at the shoot tips.

rows.readsAs: A young fern frond or a mimosa/acacia sapling with a single acorn stuck on top
rows.defect: Every must-read fails and one is inverted. (1) The leaf is NOT four oval leaflets in two opposite pairs — the stem carries roughly fourteen opposite pairs of tiny feathery comb-shaped leaflets, dozens in total, which is the classic fern/mimosa ladder, not a quadrifoliate peanut leaf. (2) The habit is NOT low and spreading — it is a single ramrod-straight vertical stem, far taller than wide despite the 1.6 aspect, with no branching, no sprawl and no ground-hugging mat. (3) There are no yellow pea flowers anywhere. (4) The pods are absent from the soil AND the note is violated outright: the one tan wrinkled object in the whole image sits on the very APEX of the stem, hanging on the plant, which is precisely what the reference forbids. There is no soil line, no peg driven downward, nothing subterranean. A stranger shown this would say 'fern' and would never say 'peanut'.
rows.fix: Redraw as a low sprawling mat: three or four short arching stems radiating out from a central crown, each bearing two or three leaves of exactly four fat oval leaflets (two opposite pairs, no terminal odd leaflet), a couple of small yellow pea flowers at the leaf axils, a visible soil line across the lower third, and two or three netted tan pods drawn BELOW that line on downward pegs — and delete the tan blob at the top of the stem entirely.

rows.readsAs: a cartoon platypus / blobby newt
rows.defect: The must-read 'long tapering tail longer than the body' is INVERTED — the tail is a short fat club roughly half the body's length and it does not taper. There are no splayed clawed toes: the limbs are four featureless dark pegs hanging straight down from the ellipse's underside with no elbow bend, so the sprawling posture is absent. The head is a plain rounded oval, not a scaly wedge, and there is no ear opening anywhere on it.
rows.fix: Redraw the tail as a slender continuously tapering whip at least 1.6x the snout-vent length, and re-root the limbs on the SIDE of the body with a visible elbow above the topline and a splayed 5-toe foot.
rows.verifyWhy:
FAIL upheld, but three of the four stated causes are measurably wrong and the fixes should be made against these numbers, not theirs. I measured the silhouette by column scan (440x440 canvas, bg #05060C, alpha-difference threshold 40): the animal occupies x=66..374 (308 px nose-to-tail-tip) and y=155..269 (114 px tall incl. limbs), so measured aspect is ~2.7, not the spec'd 3.5 - the body is stubbier than the reference row asks for, which nobody mentioned.

TAIL (mustRead 'long tapering tail longer than the body') - FAILS, but not as described. The judge called it 'a short fat club about half the body length'. Measured: tail runs x=66..~170 = ~104 px; the torso oval alone is x~170..305 = ~135 px; head+body is x~170..374 = ~205 px. So the tail is 0.77x the torso and 0.51x head+body - 'about half the body' is only true if 'body' means head+body; against the torso alone it is closer to three-quarters. The more actionable error is the profile: this tail does not merely fail to taper, it INVERTS the taper. Column heights along the tail are 50 px at the hip end (x=150), swelling to 64 px at mid-tail (x=100), then rounding off at the tip. It is a flat beaver/platypus PADDLE that gets wider as it leaves the body, carrying one long dark sausage-shaped blotch down its middle, and it curves up and back over the hips. Fix is not 'lengthen the club' - it is 'replace the paddle with a cone': base thickness at the vent, monotonic narrowing to a fine point, total length > 1.0x head+body.

LIMBS (mustRead 'sprawling bent-elbow limbs with splayed clawed toes') - FAILS, but the stated reason is wrong. The judge said 'no elbow bend: four smooth pegs hang straight down from the underside'. They do not hang straight down. At 7x-9x zoom the hind pair angle down-and-BACKWARD off a distinct wide hip lobe, and the near hind limb has a visible shallow knee/ankle bend partway along the shank; the fore pair slant down-and-FORWARD. So bend and angle exist. What is genuinely, totally absent is any FOOT: all four limbs terminate in a plain rounded olive stub with zero digit separation, zero claws, no ankle joint, no plantar surface - like the end of a sock. The second real failure the judge did not name is stance geometry: the limbs are columns positioned UNDER the body in mammalian carriage, so the posture spec 'sprawling' fails on a separate axis from 'straight pegs' - there is no elbows-out lateral splay, no visible upper-arm horizontal segment, and the feet plant directly beneath the ribcage rather than outboard of it.

HEAD (mustRead 'scaly wedge head with a visible ear opening') - FAILS exactly as described, plus more. At 14x the head is a plain rounded oval with a blunt hemispherical snout, no wedge, no taper toward the nose, no ear opening / tympanum disc anywhere behind or below the eye. Also absent and worth listing for the fix: no nostril, no jaw or lip separation, no scale or granular texture (the fill is a smooth soft gradient), and the mouth is a single straight ruled 1px line running dead level from mid-cheek to the snout tip. The one thing the judge missed that DOES land: the eye carries a genuine vertical slit pupil in a pale cream iris - a real reptile cue, drawn correctly, and the only lizard signal in the whole asset. The body also carries scattered soft grey-brown blotches which are a fair side-blotched-lizard mottle.

OVERALL. The 'cartoon platypus' read is fair and I reached it independently before reading the claim: fat cream egg-shaped torso, blunt bill-like oval head on a short neck, flat dark-striped paddle tail, four stubby olive legs with no feet. Two of the three identity must-reads are absent and the third (tail) is inverted. Nothing here is a small feature drawn somewhere I did not look - I zoomed head, both limb pairs and the tail at 8-14x nearest-neighbour and the features are simply not drawn. Band FAIL stands.

(Process note: two intermediate crops rendered content from a DIFFERENT species file - orange furry legs with hooves, and a brown ringtail - despite being cropped from this PNG's path. Regenerating each crop individually gave the correct olive/cream content, confirmed against the 3x full-frame view and the raw column scan above. Every observation in this record is from a crop I re-derived and cross-checked against the pixel measurements.)

rows.readsAs: an orange spiny lizard - roughly an iguana
rows.defect: Two of three must-reads land (the yellow-orange colour and a legible row of black dorsal spikes along nape and back; the tail is long and tapering). The third fails: the legs are not stout and clawed, they are four smooth dark pegs with no foot, no toe and no ankle. The 'heavy jowly head' is not modelled either — it is the same plain oval head ellipse used on the other three, with no jowl mass, no tympanum and no dewlap, so it only reads as an iguana because of the spikes and the colour.
rows.fix: Give it a real iguanid head — deepen the jaw into a jowl, add the round tympanum and a hanging throat dewlap — and end each leg in a thick five-toed foot with visible claws.

rows.readsAs: a cartoon platypus / small tan blob-beast
rows.defect: Identical drawing to Coastal Lizard with a browner tint. 'Tail longer than the body' is absent — the tail is a stubby upcurled club shorter than the trunk. 'Four legs splayed sideways with elbows out' is absent and actively contradicted: the four limbs are straight pegs dropping from the belly line in a mammalian under-body stance, the exact error the packet note warns against. 'Wedge-shaped scaly head' is absent — the head is a smooth oval with a straight ruled mouth line and no scale texture.
rows.fix: Rebuild the pose so the humerus and femur project horizontally out from the flanks with the elbows breaking the upper silhouette, and extend the tail past 1.5x body length.

rows.readsAs: a grey cartoon platypus / mole-blob
rows.defect: The identity must-read 'tail longer than head and body combined' is missing by a wide margin — the tail is a short grey club about half the trunk length. The legs are not splayed and have no long clawed toes; only two blunt stubs are clearly visible, the rear pair almost swallowed by the body ellipse, so the animal looks nearly limbless. The body is a fat rounded egg rather than a flattened granular-scaled form — there is no dorsoventral flattening and no scale texture at all, just soft airbrushed mottling.
rows.fix: Flatten the trunk vertically and widen it, add a granular scale pass over the back, and replace the club tail with a long thin tapering one exceeding head+body combined.

rows.readsAs: a long-snouted beaked whale
rows.defect: Beak and the pair of white erupting tusks read clearly and the rake scratches are visible, but the melon behind the beak barely bulges - the forehead is a straight ramp - and the dorsal fin is not a fin: it is two soft grey blobs floating on the topline at roughly mid-back with no edge, so the 'small fin set far back' does not register.
rows.fix: Cut a small sharply-edged falcate dorsal into the topline at 70% of body length and delete the mid-back smudge; add a convex melon step so the forehead bulges above the beak base.

rows.readsAs: a white whale, probably a beluga
rows.defect: White body and absent dorsal are right, but the melon is a wedge rather than a bulging ball - the forehead slopes straight back from the mouth - and there is no neck crease anywhere. The 'low dorsal ridge' is drawn as a hard dark stripe capping the head and shoulders, which reads as a black cap marking rather than a ridge.
rows.fix: Rebuild the head as a circular melon overhanging the mouth line and add a single vertical crease behind it; make the dorsal ridge a low bumpy swell in the silhouette instead of a dark painted stripe.

rows.readsAs: a generic grey fish - the same lozenge as the Dolphin card, only longer
rows.defect: All three must-reads are absent. The rostrum comes to a sharp point instead of a broad flat U and carries no ridge; there are zero throat pleats on the underside; and the dorsal is a soft grey blob at roughly 55% of body length, i.e. mid-back, not the thumb-nub three-quarters back the note explicitly warns about. Nothing on the card says baleen whale, let alone the largest animal alive.
rows.fix: Flatten and widen the rostrum into a U with a single centreline ridge, ink 8-10 long throat grooves from chin to navel, and move the dorsal to 78% of body length as a tiny hard-edged nub.

rows.readsAs: a teal fish
rows.defect: The single feature every viewer uses to name a dolphin - the tall curved sickle dorsal fin - is not there; there is only a faint grey smudge on the back with no leading or trailing edge. There is also no beak: the snout is the plain point of the teardrop, with no crease separating beak from melon and no upcurved smiling jawline. The flukes are a small dark blob. This is the Blue Whale drawing recoloured and shortened.
rows.fix: Give it a proper hard-edged falcate dorsal standing well clear of the back, and cut a distinct short beak with a melon crease and an upswept mouth line.

rows.readsAs: a dugong, or a segmented sea-grub
rows.defect: The notched whale fluke, the downturned bristly disc snout and the absent dorsal are all correctly there - the species-level call against manatee is actually won. What breaks it is the body: eight hard vertical bands ring the barrel from shoulder to tail, so the torso reads as a segmented larva rather than smooth sirenian hide, and the same banding is stamped on the Manatee card.
rows.fix: Delete the vertical band ribbing and replace it with soft mottled hide shading plus a few scattered scar lines.

rows.readsAs: a brown bear cub or a large rodent
rows.defect: This is the terrestrial quadruped loaf, not a pinniped. The fore-limbs are short stubby legs of the same length as the hind legs, tucked under a barrel body - the 'very long fore-flippers propping the chest up', which is the whole reason a fur seal looks different from a true seal, are absent, so the chest sits low instead of reared. The hind limbs end in stubby toed paws rather than rotated-forward flippers, and the ear flaps are tiny rounded knobs indistinguishable from a bear's ears. No flipper webbing anywhere.
rows.fix: Replace both limb pairs with broad flat naked flippers - fore-flippers roughly 1.5x the hind, planted forward of the chest so the shoulders rear up - and make the ear flaps small pointed cones standing off the skull.

rows.readsAs: a dolphin - it is the Dolphin card at a different length
rows.defect: Both identity must-reads are gone. The topline is a perfectly smooth arc with no row of knuckle bumps between mid-back and tail, and the skin is a clean unbroken teal-to-grey gradient with no barnacle crust, no lice patches, no mottling at all. The rostrum is a sleek point rather than a narrow arched bowed jaw. Nothing distinguishes this from the toothed whales in the batch.
rows.fix: Serrate the rear third of the topline with 6-8 knuckle bumps and paint irregular white barnacle clusters and pale lice blotches across the head and back.

rows.readsAs: a humpback whale
rows.defect: The big pale wing-like pectoral and the rows of light tubercle knobs on the head and jaw both land, and they carry the identification. But the tail flukes are a tiny dark stub at the far left, far too small for the body and with a clean straight trailing edge instead of the scalloped one; and a second dark wavy shape overlaps the dorsal hump and runs down past the flipper root with no readable origin, so it looks like a stray stroke rather than the far-side flipper.
rows.fix: Enlarge the flukes to roughly a third of body width and scallop the trailing edge with a deep centre notch; resolve or delete the stray dark shape over the dorsal.

rows.readsAs: a manatee
rows.defect: The rounded spatula paddle tail is unmistakable and correctly beats the dugong fluke, and the blunt whiskered downturned muzzle is there. But the front flipper is only a vague grey lobe merged into the head shading - it never separates from the body - and the split upper lip is not readable at this size. The torso carries the same eight vertical bands as the Dugong, which read as segmentation on a mammal.
rows.fix: Separate the front flipper from the body with a clear outline and a couple of nail nubs, and drop the vertical banding for soft blotchy hide.

rows.readsAs: a narwhal
rows.defect: Strongest card in the batch - the long spiralled tusk and the dorsal-free back both read instantly. Two misses: the body is a smooth pale sage-green gradient with no mottling at all, where mottled grey is a stated must-read; and the tusk exits dead centre from the tip of the snout like a swordfish bill, exactly the error the packet note warns against - it should leave the LEFT upper jaw, offset from the midline.
rows.fix: Offset the tusk root to the left side of the upper jaw so it emerges beside the mouth rather than from the snout tip, and stipple the back and flanks with grey mottling.

rows.readsAs: a black leaf or a lens-shaped blob
rows.defect: The render is broken. The body is a dark crescent that tapers to a hairline at the right and simply stops - there are NO tail flukes at all. The tall triangular dorsal fin, the single most recognisable silhouette in the ocean, is a 10px dark triangle barely clearing the back. The eye patch is a huge white oval sitting where an eyeball would be, so it reads as one enormous cartoon eye rather than a patch above and behind the real eye; the saddle is a soft grey ellipse in the wrong place; and the white underside is a thin sliver rather than a crisp bounded belly field. No pectoral paddles are visible.
rows.fix: Rebuild it: give the body a proper caudal peduncle ending in large horizontal flukes, raise the dorsal to a hard-edged triangle roughly a quarter of body length tall, and re-place the white eye patch as a small oval ABOVE and behind the eye with a crisp hard border against the black.

rows.readsAs: an unlit dark blob whale - no species readable
rows.defect: The identity feature is absent: instead of the long low swept-back dorsal set well forward on the back there is a single tiny dark step on the topline about 45% along, with no length, no sweep and no visible edge. The pale anchor patch on the throat is nowhere on the card. The bulbous melon does not overhang the mouth - the forehead runs straight into the snout. On top of that the near-black body sits on a near-black field so the silhouette barely separates from the background at all.
rows.fix: Draw the dorsal as a long low fin whose base spans a fifth of the back at 35% body length, swept back to a rounded tip, and add the pale anchor-shaped throat patch; lift the body value a step so it separates from the field.

rows.readsAs: a small dark fish or a young dolphin
rows.defect: The blunt beakless head and the stocky short body are genuinely there, so the porpoise-vs-dolphin call is half won. The other half is not: the small low triangular dorsal fin is a faint grey nub with no triangle to it, indistinguishable from the smudge used on the Dolphin and Blue Whale cards, so the fin shape that separates porpoise from dolphin carries no information.
rows.fix: Replace the smudge with a small hard-edged equilateral triangle sitting low on the mid-back, wide at the base and blunt at the tip.

rows.readsAs: a plain grey whale-shaped lozenge, same chassis as Gray Whale and Porpoise
rows.defect: The enormously arched jawline that should occupy a third of the body is completely absent - there is no mouth line drawn anywhere, just a smoothly rounded nose, so the defining bow-shaped jaw never appears. The crusty white callosity patches on the head are also missing; the only white on the card is the single blowhole speck shared with every other cetacean here. The dorsal-free broad back is correct but it is the only must-read that lands.
rows.fix: Cut a deep strongly arched mouth line running a third of the body length with the lower lip bowing up over it, and stipple rough white callosity patches on the rostrum, above the eye and along the lower jaw.

rows.readsAs: a tan dachshund or a stubby otter standing on four short dog legs
rows.defect: There are no flippers anywhere. The fore-limbs are short cylindrical dog legs ending in small rounded paw pads planted flat on the ground, not long paddle fore-flippers lifting the chest clear; the hind limbs are matching dog legs, not rotated-forward hind flippers. The body is a shallow level sausage with a nub tail. The one thing that could carry the identity, the small external ear flap, is drawn as an ambiguous angular wedge behind the cheek that is identical to the shape on the true Seal, so it separates nothing. Muzzle and eye are generic cartoon-dog. Nothing in the silhouette says marine.
rows.fix: Replace all four legs with pinniped flippers: broad flat elongated fore-flippers angled back from a high shoulder and propping the chest and neck up off the ground at a steep angle, and short rotated-forward hind flippers with visible splayed digit tips under the rear — then give the head a small but clearly separate pointed ear cone standing off the skull.

rows.readsAs: a grey dachshund or a grey otter-dog on four legs
rows.defect: It is the Sea Lion asset recoloured grey — identical topline, identical body depth, identical four stumpy legs at identical attachment points, identical paw pads, identical skull and nose. A true seal cannot stand on four limbs at all, yet this one is propped up on four of them with the belly clear of the ground, which is precisely the error the reference note calls out. The hind limbs point down and are planted as feet instead of trailing straight back as a joined flipper pair, there is no smooth torpedo taper, and the same angular flap sits behind the cheek where a true seal must show a bare earless head.
rows.fix: Redraw it belly-down on the ground with the whole body a smooth torpedo taper, the hind flippers fused and trailing straight back off the tail end as one splayed paddle, the fore-flippers as short paddles tucked low against the ribs, and delete the ear flap entirely so the skull is a clean round earless dome.

rows.readsAs: a generic small whale — a pilot whale or a dugong
rows.defect: The head is a soft rounded nose cone occupying maybe a sixth of the body and blending seamlessly into the back; the enormous square blunt head that IS the sperm whale, taking a third of the length and ending in a flat vertical wall, is absent. There is no narrow underslung toothed lower jaw — the mouth is a thin faint smiling line right at the nose tip with no separate slender jaw beneath the head mass. There is no knuckled dorsal hump; the back carries one soft low bump in the middle that reads as a rounded dorsal fin. No blowhole is visible at the front-left of the head. What remains is a smooth grey-green torpedo with one small pectoral and a fluke, i.e. the default cetacean shape.
rows.fix: Rebuild the front third as a tall flat-fronted rectangular block that is deeper than the trunk and ends in a vertical wall, hang a thin pencil-like lower jaw well below and behind that block so the jaw is obviously narrower than the head, replace the mid-back bump with a low triangular hump followed by three or four smaller knuckles running to the tail, and put a single blowhole notch at the top-left front corner of the block.

rows.readsAs: a walrus — but only because of the tusks; the body alone is a pink dachshund
rows.defect: The tusks read and carry the name, so a stranger will say walrus. Everything else is the shared pinniped chassis recoloured pink: the same level topline, the same shallow sausage torso with no blubber mass, no wrinkling and no rolls, and the same four short cylindrical dog legs on rounded paw pads rather than short broad flippers. The dense bristle moustache is not there — only a couple of thin hairline strokes at the muzzle, so the squared muzzle reads as a dog nose with two teeth stuck on it. The tusks also emerge from the side of the cheek rather than descending from under a heavy overhanging upper lip.
rows.fix: Swap the four dog legs for short broad flippers and inflate the torso into a heavy sagging blubber mass with visible neck and shoulder wrinkle folds, then thicken the muzzle into a bulbous overhanging bristle pad — a dense stippled block of whiskers — with the tusks dropping from beneath it.

rows.readsAs: a kangaroo
rows.defect: The upright macropod silhouette, ears and muzzle land, but two of the three must-reads are not visible: the tiny forearms are absent entirely — the chest is an unbroken slab with no arm shape held against it — and the hind leg is one soft undifferentiated blob with no deep-folded thigh-over-shank, so the 'massive muscular hind leg' never reads. The long foot is a flat dark plank projecting to the right that does not visibly attach to the leg above it and reads as a board the animal is standing on.
rows.fix: Build the hind limb as a visible zig-zag — heavy pear thigh, narrow shank folded back, then a long foot hinged off the shank's base — and add two short forearms with paws tucked against the upper chest.

rows.readsAs: a koala
rows.defect: Ears and the big black spoon nose are present and the trunk is there, but the koala has no limbs at all — it is a fur ball pasted in FRONT of the log with nothing gripping it; the two pale smudges on the chest do not resolve into arms and no hands or feet wrap the trunk's edges, so 'gripping a vertical trunk' fails. rows.readsAs: a lamb or a small sheep
rows.defect: Wrong organism. It is the shared barrel-bodied lamb chassis: fleecy off-white body, four long straight columnar legs ending in dark cloven-looking hooves, a small rounded head with tiny round ears and a soft muzzle. Every must-read is missing or inverted — the tail is a short, thin, FURRED grey hook, not a long naked scaly prehensile rat tail; there is no pointed white face and no pink nose (the face is dark grey and blunt); and the coat is smooth fleece, not grizzled shaggy guard hair, with no thin bare ears.
rows.fix: Replace the whole chassis with a low crouching short-legged body and draw the identity feature first — a long bare pink-grey scaly tail as long as the body — then a sharply pointed white face with a pink nose tip and thin naked black ears.
rows.verifyWhy: Upheld, but two parts of the stated cause are wrong and would send the fix in the wrong direction. WHAT IS ACTUALLY ON THE CANVAS (440x440, zoomed 4x-14x on head, ear, tail, feet): a lamb. Deep cream/white barrel torso filled with short painterly wool flicks, level topline, tall straight column legs (front pair and rear pair both near-vertical, no crouch, no arch), standing on four dark grey blunt end-pads each split by two faint vertical toe lines. CORRECTION 1 - the tail is NOT 'furred'. It is a completely flat, untextured, uniform-width grey-tan tube (solid fill, visibly different rendering from the flick-textured body), arcing up off the rump then down with a blunt rounded tip - a pig/dog curl. It has neither fur strokes NOR scale rings. It measures roughly 55px of arc against ~180px of body length, i.e. ~30% of head+body where the Virginia opossum's is ~100%, and it does not taper at all from base to tip. The fix is therefore not 'de-fur it': it needs to be 2-3x longer, strongly tapered base-to-tip, trailing/drooping rather than curled up, pale pink-grey, and carrying the ringed scale texture. CORRECTION 2 - the judge omitted the ears entirely, and there IS ear geometry: a dark brown rounded crescent lying flat and backswept against the occiput (visible at ~x262-292, y135-170 in source px), plus a tiny pointed nub poking off the far left edge of the skull. So 'thin bare ears' is not absent-but-unmentioned, it is present-and-wrong: the ears are fur-toned, thick, rounded and pressed flat to the skull instead of thin, naked, erect and standing clear. CLAIM UPHELD ON: 'no pointed white face or pink nose' is exactly right - the muzzle is a short grey-brown blunt wedge that rounds off at the tip with one small dark round nostril dot; there is no long narrow white snout and no pink rhinarium. 'Fleecy barrel body on four straight hooved legs' is right in substance (the end-pads read hoof-ish at full size, though at 6x they are blunt two-toed pads rather than true cloven hooves - either way they are not the opossum's long splayed grasping hands with an opposable rear thumb). ADDITIONAL DEFECT NEITHER SIDE NAMED: the eye is large, round, glossy and white-catchlit, a fawn/lamb eye, where the packet specifies eyes:small. And the coat is white/cream fleece, not the required grizzled grey shaggy guard-hair coat. Score against the packet's three must-reads: naked scaly rat-like prehensile tail = ABSENT; pointed white face with pink nose = ABSENT; grizzled grey shaggy coat and thin bare ears = ABSENT on both halves. Zero of three read. The asset is the wrong organism.

rows.readsAs: a small white lamb standing on the ground
rows.defect: Wrong organism and wrong posture. Despite posture 'flying' it is the identical lamb chassis standing four-square on straight legs with a cast ground shadow. The gliding membrane — the single feature that IS the identity — is completely absent: there is no skin stretched from wrist to ankle, and the flanks are plain fleece. There are no huge black eyes and no dark facial stripe running to the nose (the face is a small grey lamb muzzle with one small dark eye), and the tail is a short white tuft, nowhere near body length.
rows.fix: Redraw as a spread-eagled glide from above or three-quarters, with a taut kite-shaped membrane joining outstretched fore and hind limbs, oversized black eyes and a dark dorsal-to-nose stripe.
rows.verifyWhy:
Verified at 5x on the body, 16x on the head, 13x on the tail and 9x on the mid-body. The FAIL stands, but two parts of the original claim need correcting.

WHAT IS ACTUALLY THERE. A stocky woolly quadruped standing four-square on level ground, weight on all four columnar legs, with a solid dark elliptical cast shadow beneath it - a standing pose, not the 'flying' posture the row asks for. The coat is thick cream/white fleece painted in short curled stroke clusters (fleece texture, not the smooth silver-grey short fur of a glider). All four legs are straight, evenly-spaced pony/sheep columns ending in small dark hoof-like tips; no grasping hands, no long digits. The head is a smooth grey-tan dome with a long tapering muzzle, a dark mouth line and a tiny dark nostril at the tip. There is NO visible ear anywhere on the head - the crown is a bare dome (a glider's large thin mobile ears are absent entirely; the earlier reviewer did not mention this and it is another miss).

MUST-READ 1, wrist-to-ankle gliding membrane: GENUINELY ABSENT, confirmed at 9x. The belly line is a clean unbroken curve and the gap between the foreleg and the hind leg is open background pixels - dark, not translucent, no patagium, no fold, no fringe, nothing spanning fore to hind limb on either the near or far side. This alone is fatal: the membrane IS the identity.

MUST-READ 2, huge black eyes with dark facial stripe to the nose: THE JUDGE IS PARTLY WRONG HERE - do not fix what is already present. There IS a large dark eye mass on the cheek, and it is disproportionately big for the skull. At 16x it resolves as TWO adjacent dark orbs: a solid featureless black disc forward-of-centre, and immediately behind/right of it a properly rendered eye with a cream-tan iris ring, black pupil and a white specular highlight, sitting in its own dark socket patch. So 'no huge black eyes' is incorrect - the eye is prominent and dark. The real defect is (a) the doubled dark disc reads as a rendering error, two eyes stacked on a strict profile head, and (b) there is NO facial stripe. The only dark marking near the eye is a brown-grey smudge that runs UP AND BACK over the crown of the skull; nothing runs FORWARD from the eye to the nose. So: eye = present, stripe = absent.

MUST-READ 3, long bushy tail as long as the body: ABSENT, and the judge's description of it is imprecise. It is not a 'short tuft'. It is a broad rounded paddle/fan hanging off the rump, roughly 40 px across against a ~115 px body - well under half body length - painted as a smooth pale lobe with a fringe of fine bristle strokes only along its outer rim. Read as a fluffed fan or pom, not a cylinder, and it overlaps and partly hides the hind quarter rather than trailing behind.

NET: 0 of 3 must-reads fully readable (one partial: prominent dark eye without the stripe). The silhouette reads unambiguously as a lamb/sheep - fleece coat, hoof-tipped columnar legs, earless domed head with a long muzzle, standing four-square with a ground shadow. Wrong organism. FAIL upheld.

FIX DIRECTION: rebuild as an airborne, face-on-ish spread-eagle pose - no ground contact and no cast shadow; a taut membrane stretched wrist-to-ankle down both flanks so the silhouette is a square/rectangular kite rather than a barrel with legs; short smooth grey fur with a white belly; a body-length cylindrical bushy tail streaming behind at roughly 1.0-1.2x body; ONE huge black eye per side (delete the duplicate black disc) with a dark stripe running forward from the eye along the muzzle to the nose plus a matching dark dorsal stripe from crown to shoulders; large thin rounded ears on the skull; hands/feet with visible splayed digits instead of hoof tips.

rows.readsAs: a grey ferret, weasel or a small short-legged dog
rows.defect: Wrong organism. Same lamb chassis in grey with a dark head. The head is SMALLER than the neck and rounded, the opposite of the required oversized blocky skull, and the jaws are shut in a soft muzzle with no gape, no teeth and no wide mouth line. The tail is a thin upward hook, not a thick short taper.

rows.verifyWhy:
Verified at 8x and 10x on the head, chest and tail, plus a luminance grid over the whole creature (440x440 canvas; animal spans x~165-315, y~165-270). VERDICT UPHELD - two of the three must-reads that carry the identity are absent - but three parts of the original claim are wrong and must not be used as the fix brief.

WHAT IS ACTUALLY THERE. A mid-grey, deep-barrel quadruped with very short legs and a dark charcoal-brown head, throat, tail and hip patch. Torso luminance runs 70-105/255 with lighter hair strokes and a bright dorsal rim-light along the spine; the head/throat/tail mass runs 35-52/255. So there IS dark fur - it is just confined to the head, throat and tail while the whole torso and all four legs stay mid-grey.

MUST-READ 1 - 'oversized blocky head and gaping jaws': FAILS, but not for the stated reason. The claim 'the head is smaller than the neck' is wrong on both counts. There is no neck at all - the cranial mass joins the shoulder directly, and it WIDENS downward into a dark throat/jaw wedge that overlaps the front of the chest and reaches almost to the elbow. Measured, the head occupies x~255-315 of a ~150px body length, headFrac ~0.40, LARGER than the 0.28 spec. It reads small only because it is a smooth spherical dome and the torso is over-deep (torso depth ~75px vs head height ~50px). The real defect is SHAPE, not scale: a round ball cranium with a short rounded muzzle and one nostril dot, one rounded ear rendered as a dark crescent on the crown, and zero of the devil's blocky architecture - no square jaw hinge, no massive masseter/cheek block, no flat wide brow, no wedge taper to the snout. The 'jaws shut, no gape, no teeth' half of the claim is CONFIRMED: there is only a faint closed seam running from the muzzle back under the eye. No open mouth, no tooth row, no gum, no tongue.

MUST-READ 2 - 'black fur with a white chest band': FAILS, and the polarity is INVERTED, which is the important correction. It is not true that there is 'no black fur' - head, throat, tail and hip patch are dark. It is true that no white chest band reads, and the reason is that the CHEST is the darkest region on the animal (the throat wedge, luminance ~40) while the FLANK is the pale one (~90). A white band cannot be seen because the value map is backwards: the fix is to flood the torso and legs to near-black and then lay a bright white crescent across the dark chest, not to add a band onto the current pale body.

MUST-READ 3 - 'thick short tapering tail on a low stocky body': HALF present. The low stocky body IS genuinely there and is the one thing the asset earns - deep barrel torso, very short legs, ~1.9 aspect, correct quadruped posture, small pale feet with visible toe lines. The tail is the failing half and the original judge did not flag it: at 10x it is a uniform-width curved tube with NO taper (tip is as wide as the mid), it hooks up over the hip then arcs down well below the belly line, and it is roughly 40% of body length. That is a rat/opossum curl, not a short thick tapering cone. Its root is also a hard-edged dark plate with a notch artifact where it overlaps the hip.

ORGANISM READ. 'Grey ferret' is wrong - a ferret is elongate, low-slung and slinky; this is barrel-chested and stumpy. It reads as a small grey pig/peccary or a stocky short-legged dog with a dark head. Either way it is not a Tasmanian devil: the blocky gaping skull and the black-with-white-chest colour signature, which are the entire identity of the species, are both missing.

rows.readsAs: a kangaroo (in grey)

rows.readsAs: a tan lamb or a miniature pony
rows.defect: Wrong organism. The shared lamb chassis again in beige: fleecy barrel torso on four long straight columnar legs ending in dark cloven-hoof blocks, with a small rounded head, a tapering pointed muzzle and small round ears. The must-reads fail — the legs are long, straight and slender rather than short, bowed and powerful, so nothing about it reads as a digger, and the snout is a narrow tapering dog muzzle, not a broad blunt bare-nosed square. rows.verifyWhy:
FAIL upheld, but two of the three stated causes are wrong and would send the fix in the wrong direction.

WHAT I ACTUALLY SAW (440x440 png; silhouette measured by row-run scan: top y=153, ground y=272, left x=121, right x=318). A cream/oatmeal quadruped with a wool-stroke fur texture over the whole barrel, a separate mid-brown head, mid-brown lower legs, and no tail. The overall read is a tan LAMB. That part of the claim is correct and it is driven mostly by the coat: the torso is painted with fine curved wool flicks in cream-on-cream, exactly the fleece treatment, over a body whose topline is a smooth continuous dome from rump to shoulder.

CORRECTION 1 - THE LEGS ARE NOT LONG. Measured: belly/split line is y=243, ground y=272, so ground clearance is 29px; torso depth (back y~181 to belly y=243) is 62px. Legs are 47% of torso depth and only 24% of total silhouette height. That is genuinely short. Telling the artist to shorten the legs will not fix this asset. The real leg defect is FORM, not length: each limb is a straight, near-vertical tapering column - widest at the top (~33px at y=245) narrowing evenly to a ~14px pastern - with NO bow, NO elbow or hock angulation, no shoulder or thigh mass, and no outward-set stance. Nothing about them reads as a digger. Worse, where the limb meets the body there is a hard-edged FLAT UNTEXTURED QUAD PANEL - clearly visible at the shoulder (approx x=265-305, y=185-240) and at the hind thigh (approx x=125-165, y=185-235) - a chassis seam where the leg plate is pasted over the fleece with a straight clipped edge. The feet are small dark-brown pads carrying only three faint pale toe lines (rows y=264-269 resolve as three separate lobes per foot); at full size they read as small cloven hooves, not claws. Fix: bow the limbs outward, put visible bulk in the forearm and thigh, kill the flat quad panels, and enlarge the feet into broad splayed paws with real dark claws.

CORRECTION 2 - IT IS NOT A DOG MUZZLE. At 14x zoom the snout is SHORT: eye-to-nose-tip is roughly one eye width. The skull is a rounded dome and the muzzle projects only slightly, dipping and blunting at the tip. Calling it 'a narrow tapering dog muzzle' overstates it and would prompt the wrong correction (shortening a muzzle that is already short). The must-read that is genuinely ABSENT is 'bare-nosed': the entire snout is FURRED in the same brown as the head, and the nose is nothing but a single small dark oval nostril dot set high on the side of the tip (approx x=304-311, y=176-182). There is no broad naked leathery nose pad, no square blunt terminal face. Fix: replace the nostril dot with a large bare square nose plate spanning the full width and depth of the snout tip, in a different value from the fur.

WHAT THE JUDGE DID NOT MENTION AND SHOULD HAVE. (a) The eye is enormous, glossy and cartoon-round with a thick white sclera ring and a specular highlight (~24px across on a 119px-tall animal). The packet specifies eyes: small. This single feature does more to make it read as a lamb/fawn than anything else. Fix: shrink to a small dark beady eye with no white ring. (b) Aspect measures 197/119 = 1.66 against a spec of 1.9 - the animal is too tall and short-bodied for a wombat; it needs to be lengthened and dropped.

WHAT IS ACTUALLY PRESENT AND SHOULD NOT BE 'FIXED'. (a) No visible tail - that must-read is satisfied; the rump is a clean rounded dome with no appendage. (b) Ears ARE present and are correct in kind - a small dark rounded ear on the near side of the skull (approx x=252-278, y=163-180) plus a paler flap at the back of the skull. Do not add big ears. (c) The torso IS reasonably deep and barrel-like; the failure is that it is a fleecy barrel rather than a low-slung heavy wedge.

VERDICT: two of three must-reads (bare-nosed broad snout; short powerful bowed digging legs) are absent, and the specified small eye is contradicted. It reads as the wrong organism. FAIL stands.

rows.readsAs: a small generic gnat or midge hovering; possibly a firefly because of the pale beaded abdomen
rows.defect: The identity feature is entirely absent — there are no tail filaments of any kind; the abdomen simply ends in a small bare bead. The wings are not triangular and are not held upright together over the back: they are two narrow leaf-shaped blades splayed open backwards in a shallow horizontal V, dragonfly/gnat fashion. The abdomen is not slender or upcurved but a straight horizontal string of five shrinking spheres. Prominent eyes are the only must-read-adjacent feature present. The body is also small and parked up-left of centre with a ground shadow detached far below-right of it, which reads as a compositing error rather than flight.
rows.fix: Add two or three hair-thin filaments at least as long as the whole abdomen streaming back from the abdomen tip, and rebuild the wings as a single large triangular pair raised vertically and pressed together over the back, with the abdomen tapered and curved upward behind them.

rows.readsAs: the same generic hovering gnat as the Mayfly card, tinted grey-blue
rows.defect: This is the Mayfly asset with a hue swap — identical head ball, identical eye dots, identical five-bead abdomen, identical splayed wing pair with the same vein strokes, identical three hook legs, identical framing and identical detached shadow ellipse. Against its own reference every must-read fails: the wings are splayed open in a V rather than folded flat and overlapping down the back; there are no cerci at all, short and stout or otherwise; there are no antennae and the head is a smooth round ball, not flat or squarish. Posture is specified as crawling but the render is airborne over a drop shadow with no substrate contact.
rows.fix: Redraw as a flat-backed crawler: fold the two wings closed into one flat overlapping sheath lying along the top of a broad flattened abdomen, add a pair of long straight antennae off a squared-off head, add two short stout cerci at the abdomen tip, and set the six legs sprawling out sideways onto a rock surface.

rows.readsAs: A generic cartoon lollipop tree — a bare brown stick under a fluffy green blob — with white daisies or chamomile flowers stuck on it; nobody would say eucalyptus, and several would say daisy bush.
rows.defect: All three must-reads are absent and one is actively contradicted. (1) The leaves do not hang: they are short, straight, lance-shaped darts radiating outward and UPWARD from the blob's edge, and the crown is a dense opaque green cloud, the exact opposite of the open sparse crown the vertical-hanging habit produces. (2) The bark is a flat, uniform, untextured mid-brown stick — perfectly straight sides, no taper, no branching, no peeling ribbons, and none of the cream/grey/orange patchwork. (3) There are no woody gumnut capsules anywhere; in their place sit four or five white RAY-PETALLED daisy heads with yellow disc centres, which is the one flower shape a eucalyptus cannot have (its blossom is a petal-less fluffy stamen burst over a woody cup). The leaf colour is also a saturated grass green rather than the matt grey-green/blue-green waxy bloom.
rows.fix: Rebuild the crown as open and see-through — long narrow sickle leaves hung vertically edge-on from thin drooping branchlets so dark background reads between them — kill the solid green blob, repaint the leaves matt blue-grey-green, replace every daisy with clustered woody cup gumnuts plus petal-less cream stamen puffs, and mottle the trunk with peeling cream/grey/orange ribbon patches.

rows.readsAs: a spiky-backed cartoon newt or a chibi dragon, not an agama
rows.defect: The must-read large blunt TRIANGULAR head is absent - the head is a small smooth rounded ellipse with a straight slit mouth, the same head every other animal in this batch has. The must-read sprawled legs holding the belly clear of the ground is also absent: the two limbs are featureless dark cones with no joint and no foot, they hang below the body rather than splaying out to the sides, and the egg belly sits right down on the shadow. The added dorsal spike crest is the only thing distinguishing this from the Skink render and it pushes the read further toward dragon than toward agama.
rows.fix: Rebuild the head as a wide blunt wedge - broad squared-off jaw, deep cheek, snout tapering to a rounded point - and replace the two cones with four sprawling limbs whose elbows and knees stick out sideways above the body line, ending in spread five-toed feet, so the chest visibly clears the ground.
rows.verifyWhy:
Looked at the PNG at 1x, then at 3x/8x/9x/12x crops of the head, both leg groups and the silhouette edge, and measured the alpha silhouette column-by-column. VERDICT UPHELD, but three parts of the claim are wrong and must not be used to drive the fix.

WHAT IS ACTUALLY THERE. Silhouette bbox x=71..368 (297px long), y=149..276. The animal is: one curved tail capsule with a dark inner stripe (x=71..185), one fat spotted trunk ellipse (x=185..290, top ~y=175, underside ~y=250), a row of ~8 solid triangular spikes bolted along the mid-back topline (x=195..300, peaks up to y=149), a separate head ellipse butted straight onto the front of the trunk with no neck (x=290..368, max depth ~58px), and four plain capsule limbs.

CONFIRMED — must-read 1 (large blunt triangular head) IS ABSENT. At 8x the head is a perfectly smooth featureless oval: no jaw hinge, no cheek, no snout plane, no nostril, no tympanum, no neck. Its only features are one hairline straight mouth slit running the lower third and a round white eye with a black vertical slit pupil. Column scan across the head (x=326..366) shows top edge 177,177,178,178,180,181,184,189,195 and bottom edge 235,234,234,232,230,228,224,219,212 — it tapers SYMMETRICALLY toward the snout, which is the signature of an ellipse, not a wedge. A blunt triangular head would hold a flat plane on one side and widen to a broad jaw at the back; nothing here does.

CORRECTION 1 — 'small' is WRONG. The head is 77px long on a 297px animal, headFrac approx 0.26 against the spec's 0.30, and 58px deep against a 75px trunk depth. It is the second-largest mass in the render and is close to spec scale. The defect is purely GEOMETRY (round ellipse instead of blunt wedge), not size. Do not fix this by enlarging the head — enlarging a smooth oval makes it read more chibi, not more agama.

CORRECTION 2 — 'a belly that sits on the shadow' is WRONG, and this is the one half of must-read 3 the render actually satisfies. Measured: the trunk underside bottoms out at y approx 250; the lowest foot tips reach y=276 (columns x=181..186 and x=311..321). That is a 26px air gap, about 35% of the trunk's 75px depth, and the cast shadow ellipse sits below the limb tips, not against the belly. The belly IS held clear of the ground. What fails in must-read 3 is the SPRAWL and the feet, not the clearance.

CORRECTION 3 — 'two cones' undercounts. There are FOUR limbs: a near foreleg (x approx 300-325), a near hindleg (x approx 155-200), a paler far-side foreleg tucked behind the head/trunk junction at upper right, and a darker far-side hindleg plate at x approx 148-190. 'Toeless' is exactly right — every one of them terminates in a plain rounded cap with zero foot, ankle or digits. 'Jointless' is right for the foreleg (a single straight tapered capsule, verified at 12x) but slightly overstated for the hindleg, which is two overlapping capsules with a faint angle break; it still reads as a bent peg rather than an articulated knee and ankle, and because there is no foot plate the limb never turns out laterally, so the sprawl does not read — the render says 'four pegs under a body', not 'elbows and knees out to the sides'.

CONFIRMED — the shared-chassis charge. Opened Skink.png side by side: same head ellipse, same hairline mouth slit, same white-ring vertical-slit eye at the same place, same tail capsule with the same dark internal stripe, same capsule limbs, same spot scatter. Agama differs only by hue (blue vs brown), a somewhat deeper/rounder trunk, marginally longer limbs, and the bolt-on spike row. One chassis, two paint jobs.

Also worth recording for the fix: the spike row sits on the MID-BACK topline, not on the nape, so it does not do an agama nuchal crest's job either — combined with the round dark-slit eye and the featureless oval snout the whole thing reads as a generic chibi dragon, which matches the original claim.

MUST-READ 2 (tail about as long as the body) PASSES and the original judge did not credit it: tail runs x=71 to the hip at x approx 185 along a curve, versus a trunk of x=185..290 — roughly equal, arguably a touch longer once the curve is counted. That is the only clean must-read.

SCORE: 1 of 3 must-reads present, 1 (the primary identity feature) wholly absent, 1 half-present (clearance yes, sprawl and feet no). FAIL stands.

FIX DIRECTION: rebuild the head as a broad blunt wedge — widest at a defined jaw hinge, tapering to a squared-off (not rounded) snout, with a visible jawline, a short thick neck separating it from the trunk, and a tympanum spot behind the eye. Give every limb a foot plate with three to five splayed toes, and break each limb at elbow/knee so the upper segment goes OUT laterally before the lower segment drops to the ground — the 26px belly clearance is already correct and should be preserved, not changed. Move the crest forward onto the nape if it is kept at all, and shrink the spikes so they read as scale keels rather than dragon horns.

rows.readsAs: a green cartoon frog or newt sticking its tongue out

FAIL upheld, but ONE OF THE THREE STATED CAUSES IS WRONG — do not 'fix' the dewlap by moving it, it is already in the right place.

WHAT I ACTUALLY SAW (440x440 canvas; silhouette spans x=43..396, measured by alpha profile, then re-read at 5x-11x crops of head, jaw, feet and tail):

1. DEWLAP — PRESENT AND CORRECTLY PLACED. The judge's claim that the red teardrop hangs 'off the CORNER OF THE MOUTH' and reads 'unmistakably as a lolling tongue' is factually wrong about geometry. At 11x the red mass is a crescent / half-disc whose FLAT TOP EDGE follows the ventral outline of the jaw from x=325 to x=374, bulging down to y=249, with a curved fold crease drawn inside it. The mouth is a thin dark seam at y=209 running x=330..391; it is CLOSED, continuous, and unbroken, and there is a solid ~16px band of face-green (the lower jaw/chin) between the mouth seam and the top of the red. The red never touches the mouth line and does not taper to a tip out in front of the snout. It is a gular fan hanging under the throat — anatomically where an anole dewlap belongs. It is crude (a plain half-moon, no pointed ventral apex, no gular rod, and it sits under the mid-jaw rather than reaching back toward the chest), and at thumbnail size the wide horizontal mouth seam plus the red lobe below gives the face an accidental Kermit-smile read, which is probably what the first judge saw. But the must-read 'extendable coloured throat fan' IS carried. Fixing this feature means refining it, not relocating it.

2. TAIL — GENUINELY FAILS, and the judge's description is accurate. Boundaries from the height profile: tail tip x=43, tail/trunk junction ~x=172 (where the hind-limb mass appears and the trunk ovoid with the dark spots begins), neck constriction / head start ~x=318 (column height dips to 61-62 at x=295..300), snout tip x=396. So tail = 129px, trunk ovoid = 146px, head = 78px, head+body = 224px. Tail/(head+body) = 0.58. The must-read wants >1.0, i.e. the tail should be roughly 1.7-2x what is drawn. Worse, it is not tail-SHAPED: it holds ~39-41px of thickness from x=100 all the way to x=165 (over half the trunk's 70px depth) and only tapers in the final ~40px, so it reads as a fat club stuck on the back, not an anole whip.

3. TOE PADS — GENUINELY ABSENT, judge correct. At 8x the limbs are plain dark-green capsules that terminate in blunt rounded ends. There are no digits, no splay, no lamellae, no pad discs, nothing. Two near-side limbs are drawn (a single-capsule forelimb at x~330 and a two-segment zigzag hind limb at x~180-200) with a faint far-side hind limb behind it. Beyond having no toes, the limbs also fail the 'long slender' half of the must-read: the forelimb is a stubby ~30px capsule on a 354px animal and is as thick as it is proportionate to the trunk.

ALSO (not in the judge's claim, but the reference note is violated): the packet note asks for a 'pointed wedge head longer and narrower than a gecko's'. The head drawn is a fat, blunt, rounded ovoid with a rounded snout tip and no wedge taper at all — head depth stays near-maximal right up to x=375.

FAMILY CONTEXT: this is the same generic chassis the rest of the batch is on — rounded ovoid trunk with scattered blur-dots, capsule limbs, tapering tube tail, blunt ovoid skull. Nothing in the silhouette distinguishes it as an anole except the dewlap.

VERDICT: 1 of 3 must-reads readable, 2 absent — one of them (adhesive toe pads on long slender limbs) has literally no anatomy present to carry it. FAIL stands.

rows.readsAs: a beige speckled newt or a salamander
rows.defect: The identity must-read - huge lidless eyes with vertical pupils - is not merely weak, it is inverted. Despite the row specifying prominent eyes, this render has the SMALLEST eye in the whole batch: a single tiny black dot with no iris, no vertical slit and no bulge above the skull line, smaller than the ordinary-eyed Agama, Skink, Wall Lizard and Whiptail beside it. The broad splayed lamellae toes are absent entirely - the limbs are the standard toeless cones. The skin is drawn as the same smooth gradient with the same generic dark blobs as every sibling, so the granular bumpy texture never reads either.
rows.fix: Blow the eye up to fill most of the side of the head - a domed globe bulging past the skull silhouette, gold iris with a hard black vertical slit pupil and no eyelid - and fan the front foot into broad flat pads with visible lamellae ridges.
rows.verifyWhy:
Looked at Gecko.png at 1x, then at 3x full-body, 7x on the head and 12x on two leg tips, and measured the white-sclera bounding box on all six batch members programmatically. VERDICT UPHELD, but TWO PARTS OF THE STATED CAUSE ARE WRONG and must not be 'fixed'.

CORRECTION 1 (the claim is flatly wrong here): the eye is NOT 'a bare black dot with no iris, no vertical slit'. At 7x the eye is a clean pale near-white iris/sclera oval carrying a crisp, unmistakable VERTICAL black slit pupil, taller than it is wide, sitting mid-head. The vertical-pupil half of the must-read is DRAWN AND CORRECT. Do not touch it; any fix that 'adds a vertical pupil' would be re-doing work that is already right.

CORRECTION 2: 'the SMALLEST eye in the batch' is not quite true. Measured white-sclera bboxes across the batch: Wall Lizard 13x13 (78 px), Skink 13x12 (62 px), Agama 12x11 (61 px), Anole 11x10 (53 px), Gecko 10x9 (38 px), Whiptail 10x8 (32 px). The Gecko is second-smallest, marginally above Whiptail. The INVERSION CLAIM NONETHELESS STANDS AND IS THE CORE DEFECT: the only species in the batch spec'd eyes:prominent carries an eye smaller than FOUR of its five ordinary-eyed siblings, roughly half the sclera area of the Wall Lizard's. Relative to its own head the eye is ~10 px in a ~67 px head ellipse (~15% of head length); a gecko's eye is ~30-35% of head length. The judge's 'no bulge past the skull line' IS correct: the head is a perfectly smooth ellipse and the eye sits flush inside it with no orbital dome, no brow ridge, and no break in the dorsal outline. The head is also mostly empty — a large blank cream ellipse with one small eye and a single pencil-thin mouth line, which is what makes the eye read as under-scaled.

CONFIRMED AND STRONGER THAN STATED: splayed lamellae toes are not merely 'absent' — there are NO FEET AT ALL. At 12x, the front limb is a plain olive-grey capsule that terminates in a blunt rounded cap; the hind limb is a thigh blob ending in a rounded knob. Zero digits, zero pads, zero ankle, on all four limbs. Anole and Skink in the same batch at least carry a small angled foot form at the leg tip, so the Gecko is BELOW its siblings on the one foot feature it is supposed to lead the batch on.

CONFIRMED: skin is a flat smooth radial gradient with the identical blurred dark blob-spots the Anole and Skink carry in the same positions and sizes — no granulation, no tubercles, no surface break of any kind. It is the batch's shared spot vocabulary in a cream palette.

OMITTED BY THE ORIGINAL JUDGE (add to the fix list): (a) the tail. It IS plump, so the third must-read is half-satisfied — but it is drawn as a short thick hook that CURLS UP AND FORWARD OVER THE BACK, ending above the hips like a chameleon's or a possum's prehensile tail. No gecko carries its tail that way; it should extend rearward. (b) Silhouette proportion: measured body bbox is 242x110 = aspect 2.20 against the spec'd 3.0, because the curled tail eats the length. This is the squattest silhouette in the batch (Agama 2.35, Wall Lizard 3.01, Anole 3.34, Skink 3.41, Whiptail 4.04) despite the Gecko being spec'd longer than the Agama. (c) CHASSIS: this is the same body as its five siblings — one fat egg-shaped torso, four tapered stub limbs with no feet, one round head ellipse butted onto the torso with no neck and a single pencil mouth line, one tapered tail with a darker inner streak, the same blurred blobs. Gecko differs from Skink and Anole only in palette, tail length and tail curl.

WHAT IT ACTUALLY READS AS: a plump cream ovoid quadruped with a curled tail — closest to a fat newt/salamander or a shell-less tortoise. Nothing about the silhouette, the head, the feet or the surface says gecko; only the vertical pupil does, and it is too small to carry the identity alone. Two of three must-reads fail outright and the third is inverted, so FAIL is the correct band.

rows.readsAs: a small brown lizard-ish creature, though closer to a newt than a skink

rows.readsAs: an olive-drab newt, indistinguishable from the Skink render except for hue
rows.defect: Every one of the three must-reads is missing. The tail should be roughly TWICE the body length; on this render the tail is about the same length as the body ovoid, so the defining proportion of a lacertid is simply not there. rows.verifyWhy:
Measured the 440x440 PNG pixel-by-pixel (column silhouette profile) and inspected 6x/12x crops of both feet, the head and the tail. All three must-reads are absent; the FAIL stands, with two corrections to the stated causes.

WHAT IS THERE: the creature spans x=56..380 (325 px, drawn noticeably smaller in frame than the Skink's 393 px). Tail tip x=56; the tail/body junction is at x~194 (column height jumps 41 -> 48 there); the body oval runs x=194..313 (119 px long, 76 px deep at its maximum, x=246..258); the head oval runs x=313..380 (67 px long, 56 px deep). Four limbs hang below the body, and a cast ellipse shadow sits on the ground BELOW the belly with a clear gap.

1) TAIL PROPORTION - must-read 'tail roughly twice the body length' is FAILED, and the judge's description is close but slightly generous. Tail = 138 px horizontal (~145 px along its arc, it curls upward). Body oval = 119 px. So tail/body = 1.16x, not 2x. Measured the way lacertid proportion is normally quoted (tail vs snout-vent = head+body = 186 px) it is 0.74x - i.e. the tail is SHORTER than the animal in front of it. Even on the most generous reading of 'body' it needs to be ~238 px and it is 138. IMPORTANT ADDITIONAL FINDING the judge missed: I profiled the Skink in the same packet the same way - Skink tail 189 px vs body 124 px = 1.52x. So the Wall Lizard's tail is proportionally SHORTER than the Skink's, whose own must-read is only 'tail as long as the body'. The two species' tail proportions are inverted relative to their reference rows. A fix must roughly double this tail (target ~2x snout-vent, i.e. ~370 px at this scale) and taper it to a fine whip point; currently it is a thick near-uniform tube (41-43 px tall across x=110..192) that only pinches in the last ~25 px, and it carries the identical dark dorsal blotch-stripe the Skink's tail carries.

2) BODY FORM - must-read 'flattened slender body pressed to the surface' is FAILED exactly as claimed. The trunk is a deep egg: 76 px deep on a 119 px length, depth/length = 0.64. It is not flattened dorsoventrally and it is not slender. It is also held CLEAR of the ground - the shadow ellipse is a separate mass under the belly with visible dark gap between belly and shadow, so the animal reads as propped up on stumps, the opposite of a wall lizard plastered flat against stone. Extra defect the judge did not name: the tail emerges from the UPPER half of the body (tail base spans y~185..227 while the belly bottom is y=241), so the tail is attached above the hip line rather than continuing the ventral line - part of why the body reads as a detached egg with a tube stuck on it.

3) TOES - must-read 'long splayed toes' is FAILED. At 12x zoom on both the left hind limb and the right fore limb, each limb terminates in a plain rounded capsule end. There are no digits, no foot plate, no claws, no splay - zero toe geometry of any kind. CORRECTION to the claim's wording: the limbs are not all 'standard featureless cones'. The hind limb is actually a two-segment limb with a visible knee bend (thigh wedge + shank), the fore limb is a single tapered cylinder; both are featureless at the distal end, so the verdict is right but 'cones' understates that a limb articulation model IS present and only the foot/digits are missing. The fix is a foot, not a whole limb rebuild.

4) CHASSIS - the judge's 'nothing separates it from the Skink' is essentially correct and I confirmed it by measurement, not just by eye. Wall Lizard vs Skink: body 119x76 vs 124x75; head 67x56 vs 79x59; same blunt egg head with no neck taper and no pointed snout; same hairline horizontal mouth slit; same white sclera with vertical slit pupil (wrong for a diurnal round-pupilled lacertid, and identical to the Skink's); same soft brown speckle field over the flank; same thick curved tail with the same dark dorsal stripe; same four limbs at the same angles. The only silhouette differences are overall scale (325 vs 393 px), hue (olive-green vs brown), and a tail that is shorter - so the one silhouette distinction that does exist points the wrong way. This is one lizard chassis in two colours.

Nothing redeeming was found hiding at small scale. Band FAIL, upheld.

rows.readsAs: a long-tailed brown lizard, but not identifiably a whiptail

rows.readsAs: a winged ant, or a small bee with an oversized head

Worse, a long angular bracket of two straight thin lines meets at a vertex far off the right side of the animal, disconnected from any visible body part, plus a comb of short vertical black bars sits under the wing base — both read as stray wireframe fragments stranded outside the silhouette.

rows.readsAs: a mosquito — the plumose antenna and long narrow wings carry it

Measured on the 440x440 png with a per-column luminance segmentation (background lum 13, dorsal-fin membrane a flat plateau at lum 35, bright body lum 55-110). Fish faces RIGHT; bright body runs x=117 (caudal peduncle) to x=315 (snout), 198px long; max body depth 63px at x=192-213; bill x=315-367 (52px, 3-7px thick).

It also carries roughly eight vertical fin-ray strokes inside the membrane (visible at 6x on the dorsal crop), which the Marlin's dome does not have.

CORRECTION 2 - 'about a third of body depth' is close but slightly understated: the peak rise is 24px above the dorsal line against a 63px maximum body depth = 0.38x (0.41x of the local depth at that station). The mustRead demands a sail TALLER than the body is deep, i.e. >=63px and realistically 1.2-1.5x. The drawn fin is ~2.6x too short. THIS is the real defect, and it is a scale defect, not an omission: the fin needs its height multiplied roughly 3x and its leading edge pushed forward to start just behind the skull (x~300) so it runs the full back, and it needs a squared/high-shouldered membrane top with long rays rather than the current low elliptical arc.

CORRECT - the profile is a soft-edged rounded dome. CORRECT - chassis-identical to the Marlin. Same measurement run on Marlin.png: dorsal dome x=171-291 (58 percent of a 207px body), peak rise 21px above a 58px body = 0.36x, peak at x=219-231. rows.readsAs: a quail or partridge chick

rows.verifyWhy:
Looked at the 440x440 PNG, then re-read it at 3x (whole bird), 7x (head) and 8x (head/shoulder junction), and measured the silhouette in pixels. VERDICT UPHELD, but two of the three stated causes are described wrongly and the fix should be made against these measurements, not against their wording.

WHAT IS ACTUALLY ON THE CANVAS. Ink bbox (shadow excluded) x99-335, y118-310: 236 wide x 192 tall. A near-spherical cream body ball (x~120-285, y~142-266 = 165w x 124h) with speckled/scalloped plumage and a big scapular wing arc drawn as a closed ellipse on the flank. 1. LEGS - claim is CORRECT in verdict, WRONG in description. They are not "short yellow stubs." They are anatomically complete bird legs: a bare yellow tibia leaving the belly, a clean backward-bending hock/ankle, a straight tarsus, and a flat foot with forward toes plus a long backward-pointing hind toe on the near foot. The defect is purely LENGTH. Yellow leg pixels run y267-309 = 42px of leg, against a body depth of 124px and a total figure height of 192px. So belly-to-ground is 34% of body depth and 22% of the whole animal - the body ball hangs a third of a body-depth off the floor. A bustard's must-read is the opposite: the tarsus alone should be near body-depth so the barrel rides high and clear, with a long open gap of daylight under it. Here the belly nearly grazes the shadow. Also worth noting the hind toe: bustards have three stout toes and no hallux, and one is drawn here.

2. NECK - claim is CORRECT and the 8x crop confirms it rather than refuting it. I specifically hunted for a neck that the first judge might have missed. There IS a neck, but it is a collar, not a column: a pale vertical band about 23px wide (roughly half a head-diameter, so the THICKNESS is right) and only about 7-10px of exposed height between the underside of the head ball and the shoulder line. Row scans show the silhouette is still head-only and 52px wide at y136, then jumps to 129px wide at y142 - i.e. the head merges into the body within ~24px of the crown, so the skull is half-sunk into the shoulder. Head-welded-to-shoulder is a fair summary. The missing must-read is neck LENGTH/CARRIAGE: a bustard needs a long thick upright column lifting the head well clear of the back line, giving the standing S-profile. Nothing here lifts the head; it rides on the shoulder.

3. SKULL AND BILL - half right, half wrong. The skull claim is CORRECT: the cranium is a mathematically clean circle with a fully domed crown and no flat table at all, which is the single loudest wrong signal in the image. The BILL claim is WRONG. It is not a "thin dagger." Measured, the yellow bill is x102-131 by y132-155 = 29px long by 23px deep, i.e. nearly as deep at the base as it is long, and only ~0.56 of head diameter - that is genuinely a short stout wedge and is close to the must-read already. It only reads sharp because it is a flat untextured triangle with a straight gape line running to a needle point; give it a blunter tip and a slight culmen curve and this element passes. Do not "shorten the dagger" - it is already short.

4. BODY MASS - not in the claim but it is the other half of why this fails. The must-read asks for a HEAVY HORIZONTAL body. What is drawn is a ball: 165w x 124h excluding the tail, and visually it reads as round because the widest rows (y196-238) are centered under the head rather than extending behind it. The horizontal reading in the aspect number comes from the tail wedge, not from the torso.

WHAT IT READS AS. Round ball body + head sunk on the shoulder + domed crown + short bare legs = a quail, partridge or gamebird chick. The first judge's "quail chick" is accurate.
