All three of the packet's must-reads (heavy horizontal body carried high on long bare legs; thick upright neck; flat-crowned head with short stout bill) are missing or unreadable except for the bill's stoutness, so FAIL stands.

rows.readsAs: a small crested diving waterbird — roughly right
rows.defect: The thin sharply pointed bill and the puffy rounded tailless rear both read correctly, and the crest is a nice touch. But the lobed toes must-read is entirely invisible — nothing of the foot is drawn above or through the waterline. The body is a short round egg rather than the long low hull the 2.6 aspect calls for, and it is the identical swimming chassis used for the Loon, so the two are separable only by hue.
rows.fix: Break one lobed foot out to the side of the hull at the waterline so the scalloped toe flaps are visible, and stretch the floating body longer and lower so it is not the Loon's egg in brown.

rows.readsAs: the Grebe asset recoloured black
rows.defect: The identity must-read — the checkerboard black-and-white back — is completely absent; the back is a flat unmarked dark grey with the generic wing-scallop arc on it. The dagger bill is not held level, it tilts noticeably upward, which is the grebe/anhinga cue and the opposite of a loon's carriage. The body is a short round egg sitting high rather than a long body riding low. Side by side with the Grebe it is visibly the same drawing with the brown swapped for black and the crest deleted.
rows.fix: Paint an actual checkerboard — a grid of hard white squares over the black mantle — and level the bill horizontally on a thicker straight neck over a longer, lower-riding hull.
rows.verifyWhy:
Verdict upheld, but two of the three stated causes are wrong and must not be fixed as written.

WHAT IS ACTUALLY ON THE CANVAS (440x440, measured, not eyeballed): a dark charcoal sphere head at x148-195 carrying a small bright eye dot, a straight yellow dagger bill spanning x91-148, a smooth S-curved charcoal neck dropping to a rounded egg body at x195-355 / y182-272, two pale-blue water rings and a blue shadow ellipse under it. No feet and no tail are drawn, which is correct for posture=swimming and for the packet note about rear-set legs.

CORRECTION 1 - 'the mantle is flat unmarked grey' is FALSE. The mantle is NOT unmarked. Zoomed 6x on x195-360/y175-275 there is a real fleck texture: loose diagonal rows of small pale dashes across the upper mantle, a second field of pale dots on the lower flank, and a broad near-black diagonal band crossing the body that reads as a folded wing. The defect is not absence, it is that this is the WRONG marking at far too little contrast. Luminance over the mantle box (210,190)-(300,235): median 38.6/255, p95 63.8/255, max 114.6. The 'white' of the supposed checkerboard peaks at a mid-dark grey around 64/255 against a ground of 38 - roughly 25 levels of separation. A loon's identity mark is high-contrast WHITE squares in ordered rows on a BLACK back; what is here is unordered low-contrast grey speckle. The same box on Grebe.png returns median 67.8 / p95 124.7 - the identical texture, only brighter. So the fix is: replace the generic speckle with ordered square checks and drive fleck luminance to near-white (200+), not 'add markings to a blank back'.

CORRECTION 2 - 'the dagger bill tilts upward instead of level' is FALSE. I measured every yellow column of the bill. Centerline y = 147.0 at the tip (x=91) and 146.5 at the base (x=145); top edge 147->142, bottom edge 147->151, a symmetric even taper. The bill is dead level within half a pixel over its whole 58px length, straight, and evenly tapered. This is the ONE must-read the asset actually satisfies and it should be left alone.

CONFIRMED 3 - 'short high-riding egg, not a long low hull' is CORRECT. Full creature bbox 272 x 149 = aspect 1.83 against a spec aspect of 3.0. Body alone 161 x 91 = 1.77. The waterline rings cross at about y=258 while the body runs y182-272, so roughly 80 percent of the body height sits above the surface. It reads as a duck-shaped float, not a low submarine hull.

CONFIRMED 4 - 'it is visibly the Grebe asset with the brown swapped for black and the crest deleted' is CORRECT and now quantified. Thresholded non-background masks of Loon.png and Grebe.png over the full 440x440 frame give IoU = 0.918 (39,870 shared pixels, 1,350 loon-only, 2,192 grebe-only). Identical head sphere, identical neck S-curve, identical egg body, identical two-ring water and shadow ellipse, identical fleck texture generator. The whole delta is hue plus the Grebe's head tuft. Two of six members of this family are one chassis.

BAND: FAIL stands. Of three must-reads, the level dagger bill passes; the checkerboard black-and-white back is unreadable (present as grey speckle at ~10 percent of required contrast); the long low body is absent (1.83 vs 3.0, riding high). With the head also a plain sphere carrying no white collar or neck striping, nothing on this asset says loon - it reads as a generic dark waterfowl and, side by side with its own family batch, as a recolored Grebe.

rows.readsAs: a pale quail or a chunky dove
rows.defect: The plump pigeon-like body and the small head on a short neck are present and read fine — this is the species the shared chassis accidentally fits best. But the long pointed pin tail is only a short flat wedge that barely clears the rump, nowhere near the needle that defines the bird, and the legs are drawn as bare yellow scaly stubs rather than feathered down to the toes.
rows.fix: Extend the tail into a thin needle spike roughly as long as the body again, and feather the legs so the shanks read as fluff rather than bare scale.

rows.readsAs: a crested quail
rows.defect: Two of the three must-reads are missing and the third is weak. The very long red legs are not there at all — the legs are the same two short yellow stubs as the Bustard and Sandgrouse. The long trailing tail is not there — the tail is the family's short flat wedge. The bristle spray sits on the crown as a small tidy three-prong tuft rather than a ragged spray erupting from the base of the bill. Stripped of the tuft this is the Bustard image.
rows.fix: Give it stilted legs at least half the figure height in saturated red, hang a long banded tail well past the leg line, and move the bristle spray forward to fan directly off the bill base.
rows.verifyWhy:
FAIL upheld, but two of the three stated causes are described wrongly and one is flatly incorrect. What I actually did: read the 440x440 PNG twice, then cut 5x nearest-neighbour crops of the head, legs and tail from BOTH Seriema.png and Bustard.png and compared them side by side, plus pixel measurements.

MUST-READ 1 - 'spray of erect bristly feathers at the base of the bill': PRESENT, and the judge's description of it is WRONG. It is not a 'small tidy tuft'. At 5x it is a fan of about six separate, splayed, spiky filaments with visible gaps between them, sweeping up and forward - i.e. genuinely a ragged bristle spray, and it is not small: roughly 30px tall x 35px wide against a skull only ~45px across. The real defect is ANCHOR POINT, not shape or size. The spray roots on the top of the crown at approx (150,138), which is up and slightly BEHIND the eye (eye centre approx (145,152)) and about 15px back from the bill base (approx (136,155)) - about a third of the skull length rearward. It reads as a cockatoo/quail crown crest. Seriema bristles spring from the forehead immediately at/above the cere, ahead of the eye. FIX = move the spray root forward to the bill base and lean it forward over the bill; do not redraw the filaments, they are correct.

MUST-READ 2 - 'very long red legs': ABSENT. Judge is right. Measured yellow-leg pixel span Seriema y266..317 = 51px against a 204px total silhouette height (25%); Bustard y267..309 = 42px of 192px (22%). So the Seriema legs are ~20% longer in absolute pixels than the Bustard's - a difference the judge missed - but that is nowhere near the required proportion; a seriema's bare tarsi are roughly half the standing height and the bird should look stilty and long-shanked. Colour sampled on the tarsus is ochre/mustard (approx R152 G124 B64 in shade, same ramp as the bill) - there is no red anywhere on the legs. The leg drawing is also the identical chassis part: same two-segment zigzag, same knee kink at the same relative height, same three-toe splayed foot with the same rearward spur, same fill colour as the Bustard.

MUST-READ 3 - 'long trailing tail': ABSENT. Judge is right and precise. The tail is the same short dark wedge as the Bustard's - a solid triangle projecting only ~40px past the rump with the same fan of thin dark undertail hatch-lines beneath it. Overlaid, the two tails are the same shape at the same angle. Nothing trails; a seriema's tail should be long, broad and carried down/behind, adding real length to the silhouette.

CORRECTION to 'remove the tuft and this is the Bustard image': not literally true. Two other head parts do differ. The Seriema's bill is a short, deep, downcurved wedge with a hooked feel (correct for a seriema), where the Bustard's is a long straight yellow dagger. The Seriema eye is noticeably larger with a bright white catchlight, matching its 'prominent' eye spec against the Bustard's 'normal'. Everything BELOW the neck, however, is one chassis: identical egg body, identical scapular/wing oval with the same dark outline sweep, identical topline, identical rump, identical tail wedge, identical legs and feet, identical ground shadow ellipse. So the family-chassis charge stands for the body, and the head is the only place any species differentiation happened.

Net: 1 of 3 must-reads readable (and mispositioned), 2 of 3 - the two that carry the seriema's whole stilty, long-tailed gestalt - missing. The asset reads as a crested bustard/quail. FAIL.

rows.readsAs: a white pigeon standing on the ground
rows.defect: The posture is specified as flying and the bird is drawn standing on two little yellow feet with a ground shadow under it and folded wings — there is no flight. The two extremely long ribbon streamers doubling the body length are absent; in their place is a single broad banded tail wedge about half the body length. The black wedge stripe through the eye is absent entirely — the head is unmarked white. The bill is the family's thin yellow dagger rather than a stout red or yellow one.
rows.fix: Redraw it airborne with wings spread and no ground shadow, and trail two thin white ribbon streamers behind the tail at twice the body length, with a hard black wedge painted through the eye.
rows.verifyWhy:
Looked at the 440x440 PNG whole, then at 5-6x nearest-neighbour crops of the head (55,120,130x100), the tail (200,200,240x120) and the feet (120,240,140x80). The FAIL stands, and the two identity must-reads really are absent, but several of the stated causes need correcting.

POSTURE (claim correct): spec says posture: flying. The asset is a standing biped. The feet crop shows two amber-yellow legs dropping vertically from the belly onto a hard horizontal plane, each ending in a splayed three-toe foot with the toes drawn flat and side-on as if gripping ground, and a large dark elliptical drop-shadow pooled under the body. Nothing is extended, nothing is airborne.

MUST-READ 1 - two extremely long ribbon streamers doubling the body length: ABSENT. The judge said 'one broad half-length tail wedge'; the finer truth is that there are TWO overlapping flat planes back there, not one - a white slab with five dark barb/quill hatch marks ruled across it, and a plain mid-grey wedge sitting behind and slightly above it that terminates earlier. Neither is a ribbon: both are wide flat blades roughly 12-14 px thick at the base tapering to a blunt square-cut tip, i.e. wing/tail-fan geometry, not filaments. Measured on the source image the body runs about x=105 to x=270 (~165 px) and the tail tip reaches about x=390, so the tail is ~120 px, roughly 0.7x body length - short of even 1x, and nowhere near the 2x the row demands. Overall drawn silhouette (bill tip x~60 to tail x~390, top of head y~135 to feet y~290) gives aspect ~2.1 against the specified 3.0, which is exactly the shortfall the missing streamers cause.

MUST-READ 2 - black wedge stripe through the eye: ABSENT, confirmed at 6x. The face is uniform white with only soft grey sphere shading. The eye is a plain black bead with a single white specular dot and a faint grey rim; no dark mark touches it, no stripe runs fore or aft of it, and nothing is hidden at low contrast.

MUST-READ 3 - 'stout red or yellow bill' - the judge did not flag this but it is also missed. The bill is the right colour (saturated amber-yellow) but the wrong form: a very long, very thin needle/dagger roughly 55 px long and only ~10 px deep at the base, tapering to a hair point. That is a tern/sandpiper bill, not the short deep stout bill the row asks for.

CORRECTION to 'folded wings' and to 'reads as a white pigeon': the wing is not cleanly folded - what is drawn on the flank is an open mid-grey ARC/HOOP, a crescent ring that floats over the body outline and does not close into a wing shape, plus a separate white scallop-textured shoulder plate above it. It reads as a stray grey ring artifact laid on the flank more than as a wing. And with the long thin needle bill the animal does NOT read as a pigeon (pigeons have short stubby bills); it reads as a generic white gull/tern/shorebird chick standing on sand. Also visible and worth fixing: a patch of stray dark diagonal hatch lines just behind and above the feet, between the belly and the tail base, that belongs to nothing.

FIX DIRECTION: rebuild in flight posture (wings spread, no ground plane, no drop shadow, no standing legs - feet tucked or trailing), add the pair of hair-thin ribbon streamers issuing from the tail centre and running at least the full body length again beyond the current tail, add the black wedge stripe sweeping back through and behind the eye, shorten and deepen the bill into a stout coral-red/yellow dagger, and delete the grey flank hoop and the loose hatch marks.

rows.readsAs: A starfish
rows.defect: It is the Starfish asset in pink: five THICK tapering arms with rounded tips radiating from a broad central disc, arms only about two disc-widths long. The must-read snaky whip arms — thin, flexible, many times longer than the disc and clearly set off from it — are entirely absent; the reference note names this exact failure ('not the thick tapering arms of a starfish') and the render is that.
rows.fix: Rebuild off the Starfish chassis: shrink the disc to a small button, then run five uniform-width serpentine arms 5-6 disc-widths long that kink and coil, each joined to the disc by a visible constriction.

rows.readsAs: A grub or slug sitting in a shallow dish
rows.defect: The eight overlapping armour plates are only a row of faint low scallops along the top ridge — I can make out five or six soft bumps, not eight discrete overlapping shingles, and they read as a lumpy rim rather than armour. Worse, there is a spurious raised nub with a dark eye dot at the right end, giving this headless animal a head. The body is a flat hard-edged oval loaf with a bright rim highlight (shared with the Sea Cucumber) and no rock to be clamped to.
rows.fix: Delete the eyed head nub, and cut eight hard-edged transverse plate seams with visible overlap shadows across the full width of the back, ringed by a distinct pebbled girdle band of a different tone.

rows.readsAs: A jellyfish with rainbow stripes painted on it
rows.defect: The comb rows are present and coloured, which saves it, but the body is the Jellyfish's opaque grey dome bell — a flat-bottomed hemisphere with a shaded rim — rather than a transparent oval. Because the bell chassis is shared with asset 7, the two sit side by side as one bell in two decorations, and the stripes are thin flat lines painted ON the surface rather than rows of plates with any beat or thickness.
rows.fix: Swap the bell for a genuinely translucent egg-shaped body (background visible through it, no flat bottom rim) and give the eight rows physical width — a ladder of short cilia dashes catching light — instead of drawn-on lines.

rows.readsAs: An earthworm
rows.defect: The ringed segmented tube is right, but the swollen clitellum saddle is nowhere on the body — the tube is a uniform diameter end to end, so the front-third band that identifies an earthworm is missing. Against that, there is a black eye dot on the snout, which the reference explicitly forbids ('no limbs, eyes or head features'), and it is the same eye dot reused on the Flatworm and Leech.
rows.fix: Delete the eye dot and add a smooth swollen collar band of a paler tone across roughly six segments about a third back from the head.

rows.readsAs: An earthworm in grey
rows.defect: This is the Earthworm asset recoloured — the identical S-curve, identical ring count, identical lifted head with one black eye dot. Every must-read is contradicted: the body is a ROUND SEGMENTED tube where a planarian must be paper-flat and unsegmented; there is no arrowhead triangular head, no pair of cross-eyed spots, and no auricle lobes at the head corners.
rows.fix: Throw out the worm tube and draw a flat ribbon seen from above — a triangular arrowhead front with a pointed auricle lobe at each corner, two dark cross-eyed spots set inboard on the head, and smooth unsegmented flanks tapering to a blunt tail.

rows.readsAs: A white sea anemone
rows.defect: It is the Sea Anemone asset with the colour drained out: same squat truncated cone, same rimmed mouth opening, same crown of blunt finger tentacles splaying sideways. The identity must-read — the BLOOD-RED feathery plume — is absent; the plume is the same bone-white as the tube, so there is no red anywhere in the image. The tube is also a short wide cone rather than a tall white chitin tube, and there is no cluster: one column stands alone.
rows.fix: Make the tube tall and narrow (3-4x taller than wide) with two or three shorter tubes behind it, and paint the plume deep blood-red with fine feathery barbs so it contrasts hard against the white tube.

rows.readsAs: A jellyfish
rows.defect: Reads immediately and correctly — domed bell, a long curtain of trailing tentacles dominating the height, and short pale frilled oral arms under the bell centre. Minor: the bell is fairly opaque grey rather than truly translucent, and the oral arms are short enough to be easy to miss.
rows.fix: Lift the bell's transparency so the tentacle roots show through it, and lengthen the frilled oral arms to hang a third of the way down the tentacle curtain.

rows.readsAs: An earthworm in olive-green
rows.defect: The Earthworm chassis again, third recolour: same S-curve, same ring count, same blunt lifted head. The leech identity is the sucker at each end and there is no sucker at either end — both ends are plain rounded stubs. The body is a round tube, not a flattened ribbon, and there is no inchworm looping arch; it lies in the same flat serpentine as the other two worms.
rows.fix: Flatten the body into a broad ribbon that tapers to a narrow front, arch the middle clear of the ground in an inchworm loop, and cap each end with a distinct disc-shaped sucker wider than the body.

rows.readsAs: A cream starfish
rows.defect: It is the Starfish chassis in cream — five tapering arms radiating from a central disc with visible gaps of background between them. A sand dollar is a solid flat circular coin; there is no disc at all here, no five-petal flower pattern on the upper face, and no velvety spine fuzz. The silhouette is the single thing that had to be right and it is a star.
rows.fix: Replace the star silhouette with a solid circular wafer, emboss a five-petal flower of pored petals radiating from the centre, and dust the whole face with fine short fuzz.

rows.readsAs: A sea anemone
rows.defect: Correct on all three must-reads — squat red column planted on a widened base, dense crown of soft waving tentacles, and the central mouth visible as a pale ring inside the tentacle ring. Only quibble: the basal disc is implied by the shadow rather than drawn spreading onto rock.
rows.fix: Add a visible flared basal disc gripping a hint of rock at the column foot.

rows.readsAs: A mussel shell or a brown leaf with a frayed stalk
rows.defect: The body is the Chiton's flat hard-edged lens with a bright specular rim — a rigid shell form, not a soft sagging sausage; there is no sag, no soft-bodied bulge, and the outline is sharper than the animal could ever be. There are no rows of stubby tube feet anywhere along the underside. The feeding tentacles at the left are a flat fan of bare straight lines with no branching.
rows.fix: Round the body into a plump slumping sausage with a soft matte skin and a visible droop, run two rows of short tube-foot nubs along the bottom edge, and branch the mouth tentacles into little bushy heads.

rows.readsAs: A sea urchin
rows.defect: The spherical test bristling with long straight spines is right and it names itself. But the second must-read is absent: the test is a featureless dark ball with no five-part radial pattern under the spines. The whole asset is also near-black on a near-black field, so it is the lowest-contrast image in the batch and the spines nearly vanish at the tips.
rows.fix: Lift the test's value and score five radial ambulacral bands of paler tubercles across it, so the pentaradial structure reads under the spine cage.

rows.readsAs: A starfish
rows.defect: Five tapering arms from a small central disc, correct face-on read, and pale speckling that gives the pebbled granular skin. Tube feet are not visible, but the reference itself puts them underneath on an animal read face-on, so nothing identity-bearing is missing.
rows.fix: Give the arms a slightly heavier base and a faint marginal plate row so the granular skin reads as calcified rather than smooth.

rows.readsAs: A cream sea anemone
rows.defect: Third recolour of the Sea Anemone chassis — the same squat truncated cone, the same dark rimmed mouth opening, the same crown of blunt finger tentacles splaying left and right. Nothing about it says tube: the column is short, wide and soft-shouldered rather than a stiff narrow tube anchored to substrate, and the tentacles are fat fingers, not a feathery fan of pinnate radioles.
rows.fix: Narrow the tube to a stiff parchment cylinder with a hard rim and visible growth rings anchored to rock, and replace the finger tentacles with a two-lobed fan of finely barbed feathery radioles.

rows.readsAs: a generic olive-gold sunfish or bream
rows.defect: Body is a near-round disc (delivered aspect ~1.5 against the requested 2.5) with a smoothly domed topline - the flat straight sloping back running to an upturned mouth is absent, the mouth is a small downward-pointing tip. The bars are faint olive shadows in the flank texture, not bold black wedges, and the coat is yellow-olive rather than silver. The dorsal is a serrated crown set at mid-back, not far back near the tail.
rows.fix: Rebuild the outline as a straight sloping ramp from the dorsal origin down to a snout that turns UP at the mouth, drop the caudal peduncle so the dorsal sits over the rear third, and paint four or five hard-edged black wedges over a silver flank.

rows.readsAs: a chestnut kudu that has been scratched or singed along the shoulder
rows.defect: The stripes are rendered as BLACK/dark-brown scribbled hatching, the inverse of the must-read white stripes - on the chestnut coat they read as claw marks or a shaggy mane rather than markings, and they are bunched on the shoulder and the neck instead of running as ten-plus evenly spaced vertical bands from withers to rump. No white facial chevron: the face carries the same dark hatching. The horns are pale open corkscrews rising vertically, not heavy backswept spirals.
rows.fix: Repaint the stripes as clean cream-white vertical bands (10-14, evenly spaced across the whole torso) and add the white inter-ocular chevron; sweep the horn pair back over the neck.

rows.readsAs: a pale earthworm
rows.defect: Both ends of the body are the same rounded taper, so there is no blunt bullet head at all - the only differentiator is a single tiny dot at the right-hand tip, and no sensory tentacle, mouth line or head width is visible. The annuli are drawn as uniform ladder rungs the full length, which is exactly the earthworm read the reference note warns against, and the skin is matte pink rather than slick and moist.
rows.fix: Widen and square off the leading end into a distinct bullet-shaped head about 1.4x body width, with a dark mouth line and a visible tentacle nub below the eye position, and add a wet specular highlight along the top of the coils.

rows.readsAs: a smooth brown lens-shaped fish with a detached blob floating off its nose
rows.defect: There are NO barbels - the single most identifying feature of a catfish is entirely absent. In its place a dark elliptical blob floats DETACHED in open water in front of the snout, touching nothing, which reads as a render fault rather than anatomy. The head is a pointed continuation of the lens body, not a broad flattened scaleless head, the flank is covered in a dotted scale texture (catfish are scaleless), and no stiff leading spine is visible on the dorsal or pectoral.
rows.fix: Attach four to six long drooping barbels to the mouth corners and chin, delete the floating ellipse, and flatten and widen the head into a shovel with a wide terminal mouth.

rows.readsAs: a salmon-pink goat or young tapir with cow blotches
rows.defect: The back is arched/roached into a hump over the loin instead of the straight level topline that is a must-read, and the torso lacks barrel depth - the belly line sits high and the legs read long, so the animal has no mass. The horns are small pale spikes curving UP off the top of the skull rather than sideways-set. The coat is a pink-salmon with brown blotches rather than a cow's colouring, and the muzzle, while broad, is a smooth cone with no wide flat nose pad or mouth line. The tufted tail is the one clean hit.
rows.fix: Flatten the topline to level from withers to tailhead and drop the belly to deepen the barrel, then splay the horns out sideways from the poll before they curve.

rows.readsAs: a small pale goat or lamb
rows.defect: The diagnostic feature the reference calls out - the hunched arched back higher at the rump - is absent: the topline is flat and if anything the shoulder is the high point, so the crouching hump-backed posture never registers. The legs are long and straight rather than short, which cancels the second half of the read. No forehead tuft. The horns are small pale nubs but they point up and forward rather than backswept.
rows.fix: Raise the rump above the withers into a pronounced croup hump, shorten the legs by roughly a quarter, and add a dark forehead tuft between the backswept spikes.

rows.readsAs: a flying gurnard or sea robin - the closest read in the batch
rows.defect: The wings, spotting and the separate finger-like walking rays all land, but the head is wrong: it tapers to a long thin pointed snout like a pipefish or a needlefish instead of the blunt, square, bony-armoured box the must-read calls for, and the head is the same soft tan as the body with no plate edges or spines. The pectoral fans are milky grey and only the tips of a few rays carry blue, so the electric-blue edge does not register as a rim.
rows.fix: Replace the tapered snout with a short blunt armoured head - hard faceted plates, a squared-off profile and a preopercular spine - and run a continuous electric-blue band around the trailing edge of both pectoral fans.

rows.readsAs: a long-necked gazelle, near enough to a gerenuk
rows.defect: Neck length and stilt legs read, but the huge ears are missing entirely - the head carries horns and only a tiny flap where the gerenuk's outsized paddle ears should dominate the skull. The torso is a hard-edged faceted box glued onto the legs, with a visible straight seam at the shoulder and another at the flank, so the body reads as a separate prop rather than as one animal. The white eye ring and pale belly are not differentiated from the coat.
rows.fix: Add two large rounded ears roughly the length of the skull, flaring outward, and blend the shoulder and flank seams so the torso reads as one continuous mass.

rows.readsAs: a pale dachshund with a duck's bill and a feather duster taped to its hip
rows.defect: The long tapered tubular snout - the whole identity of the animal - is absent. What is there is a small rounded head carrying a SHORT flat stubby bill, which reads as a duck or platypus beak, not a metre-long tube with a pin-hole mouth. The black-and-white diagonal shoulder wedge is completely missing; the animal is uniform dirty cream. The tail is a small flat fan pinned to the hip rather than an enormous bushy flag as deep as the body, and it overlaps the hindquarters as a separate pasted shape. The forefeet are pale blobs with no knuckle-walking pose or curled claws.
rows.fix: Replace the head with a single long tapering cone snout at least a third of the body length, with a pin-hole mouth at the tip and the eye set far back; then paint the black wedge running from the chest diagonally up over the shoulder with a white margin.

rows.readsAs: a brown dachshund
rows.defect: The tail is a thin, ROUND, tapering rope curling upward off the rump - precisely the shape the reference note says it must not be. The broad flattened rudder paddle that defines a giant otter is absent, so nothing in the silhouette says aquatic. There is no cream throat bib: the chest is the same tan as the rest and the only lighter patch is generic underside shading. The head has round ears but no whiskers, no flattened crown and no wide muzzle, and the torso is a rigid constant-width tube on four stumpy legs, giving a sausage-dog stance rather than a swimmer's tapering body.
rows.fix: Rebuild the tail as a wide dorsoventrally flattened paddle, widest at mid-length and at least twice the width of the tail base, and paint a bold irregular cream bib across the throat and upper chest.

rows.readsAs: a spotted pony or a blotchy dog
rows.defect: The spots and the rounded ear disc land, but the skeleton does not: the back drops only slightly from the withers, nowhere near the steep skeletal ramp from high shoulders to low hindquarters, and the hindquarters sit at almost the same height as the front. The head is the shared pony skull with a long slim tapering muzzle - there is no depth of jaw, no bulging masseter and no thick short neck, so the bone-crushing head is entirely missing. The tail hangs as a long horse-like brush from a low root instead of a short bushy black-tipped tail.
rows.fix: Lift the shoulder and lengthen the forelegs so the topline ramps steeply down to a visibly lower rump, and rebuild the skull with a short deep muzzle, a heavy jaw line and a thick trapezoid neck.

rows.readsAs: a generic silver pike or barracuda
rows.defect: The body is opaque silver-white and is covered edge to edge with a drawn SCALE texture - the must-read specifically demands translucent, bloodless, scaleless skin with visible internal structure, so the render contradicts the identity rather than merely omitting it. No skeleton, gill or organ shows through. The head is small and pointed rather than oversized, and the jaws are a thin closed tip with no wide gaping pike-like gape. The pectoral is a small grey triangle, not a large fan.
rows.fix: Strip the scale texture and drop the body fill to a semi-transparent glassy white with a faint spine, ribs and gill arches showing through, then enlarge the head to about a third of body length with a wide open pike jaw.

rows.readsAs: a small dark leaf-shaped fish, unidentifiable
rows.defect: The long ribbon fin rippling along the entire underside IS the knifefish, and it is not there - the ventral edge carries only the same thin pale rim stroke that runs all the way around the body, so there is nothing to distinguish belly from back. The body is a symmetrical lens, blunt at both ends, so the blade-thin tapering tail is absent too; the rear end instead sprouts three stray dark filaments that read as damage. Delivered aspect is roughly 4 against the requested 6, and the whole animal is dark violet on a dark blue field at low contrast, so almost nothing is legible.
rows.fix: Draw a broad pale ribbon fin along the full underside in a visible sine wave, clearly separated from the body by a shading break, and taper the rear of the body to a thin blade point.

rows.readsAs: a tan dachshund or a ferret
rows.defect: None of the three must-reads is present. The head is a small dark rounded knob with a closed muzzle - no orange incisors are visible at any size. The tail is a short, smooth, thin tube curling up off the rump with no scale texture and nothing rope-like about it, and it is far too short for a muskrat or coypu. The hind feet are tiny blunt paw nubs with no webbing and no size difference from the forefeet. The body is the same constant-width sausage tube on stumpy legs used by the Giant Otter and Giant Anteater in this batch.
rows.fix: Open the mouth to show a pair of large chisel-shaped ORANGE incisors and rebuild the tail as a long naked cross-hatched scaly rope at least three-quarters of body length, dragging on the ground.

rows.readsAs: a white shaggy domestic goat or a sheared sheep
rows.defect: The shaggy white coat reads, but the horns are pale cream and sweep back over the neck instead of being short BLACK slightly-curved daggers, the legs are bare smooth white sticks with no pantaloon shag at all, and there is no humped shoulder — the topline is dead flat from withers to rump.
rows.fix: Make the horns short, black and near-vertical with only a slight backward hook, and carry the shaggy stroke texture down over the upper legs into visible pantaloons.

rows.readsAs: a grey woolly sheep with an oversized dog's head
rows.defect: The one feature that makes a tapir a tapir — the short flexible prehensile snout — is absent. The muzzle ends in a flat blocky box with a lumpy grey blob stuck on the side of it and a floppy hound ear above; there is no trunk, no downward-drooping proboscis, and no white lip rim. The body is the goat chassis with the same column legs and the same cloven hooves.
rows.fix: Replace the boxed muzzle with a distinct downward-curving fleshy proboscis that overhangs the mouth line, and ring the lip in white.

rows.readsAs: a small generic brown fish
rows.defect: Not one of the three must-reads is present: the body is a flat leaf-shaped lens tapering to a point at BOTH ends rather than a small cylinder, the snout is sharply pointed instead of blunt and rounded with an upturned mouth, and the dorsal fin sits mid-back rather than set far back near the tail. It is also drawn tiny in the frame with a shadow disc detached well below it.
rows.fix: Round the snout to a blunt cap, thicken the body into a cylinder, and slide the dorsal fin back so it sits over the last quarter of the body.

rows.readsAs: a pale grey goat with a lion-tufted tail
rows.defect: Same goat chassis as the Mountain Goat in a different hue. The coat is a washed silver-white, not the slate blue-grey of a bull; the back is flat, not sloping down from high shoulders; the horns curve backwards in a cream crescent instead of being short, straight and pointing forward; and there is no throat beard tuft. The only nilgai-ish cue present is the tufted tail.
rows.fix: Straighten the horns into short forward-angled black spikes and drop the rump line so the topline visibly slopes down from a raised shoulder.

rows.readsAs: a round silver fish, possibly a mola
rows.defect: The disc body and truncated rear are roughly right, but the towering dorsal and anal fins — the whole silhouette of the animal — are missing: there is only a faint dark grey nub above the body and nothing at all below. The rear ends in a plain rounded curve rather than a frilled rudder, and there is no tiny puckered beak mouth, just a smooth edge below the eye.
rows.fix: Add a tall pointed dorsal and a mirrored anal fin, each roughly as long as the body is deep, and cut the rear edge into a scalloped rudder.

rows.readsAs: an armadillo crossed with an echidna
rows.defect: There are no overlapping keratin scales anywhere — the back carries flat vertical dark BANDS painted onto smooth tan hide, which is the armadillo read, not the pinecone read. The head is worse: it ends in a long flat duck-bill/echidna beak that juts forward past the face. The tail is a short stubby hook curled up over the rump, nowhere near as long as the body, and it is unscaled.
rows.fix: Tile the back, flanks and tail with discrete overlapping teardrop scale plates and replace the beak with a tiny smooth conical snout.

rows.readsAs: a tan deer or young elk
rows.defect: The horns read as four separate pale tines sprouting straight up like small antlers rather than two forward-hooked horns each carrying one short prong. Both white markings are entirely absent — no white throat bands, no white rump patch — so the animal is a single flat tan all over, and the body is the same shaggy goat barrel rather than a slim deep chest on fine legs.
rows.fix: Rebuild the horns as two black forward-hooked blades with a single prong off the front edge, and paint the white rump patch and two white throat bars.

rows.readsAs: a spotted stubby-legged mammal, maybe a small civet
rows.defect: The scattered white — here dark — spots over the back are present and the snout is pointed, but the note's one specific requirement fails: the spots STOP at the base of the tail. The tail itself is a plain pale unspotted brush. The snout is dark grey rather than pink, and the body is the goat barrel on shortened columns rather than a low slinking form.
rows.fix: Continue the spot field the full length of the tail and tint the snout tip pink.

rows.readsAs: a generic dark minnow or a small needlefish
rows.defect: The ridged oval sucker plate on top of the head — the single feature that identifies a remora — is completely absent; the top of the head is smooth and unbroken from eye to dorsal. There is no jutting lower jaw either (the mouth is a plain pointed tip), and the fins are faint grey smudges. What is left is only the slim dark torpedo body, which names no particular fish.
rows.fix: Draw a flat ribbed oval plate lying on top of the skull from behind the eye to mid-body, with visible transverse lamellae.

rows.readsAs: a cream-coloured ferret or a stretched weasel
rows.defect: The tail is a thin limp rope that hangs down and hooks backward, not a thick muscular cone tapering from a broad base. The feet are tiny dark cloven stubs borrowed from the ungulates in this batch — no webbing, no toes. The face has no whiskers and the coat is a bleached cream rather than dark wet brown, so nothing reads as aquatic.
rows.fix: Thicken the tail base to nearly body depth and taper it to a point, and give the feet splayed webbed paws.

rows.readsAs: a wasp or a hoverfly
rows.defect: Both identity features are missing. There is no long downward beak-like snout — the head is a plain black ball with a large eye and no rostrum at all — and there is no bulbous upcurled tail tip; the abdomen is a straight row of yellow and black beads that simply ends. The wings are clear and unmarked rather than narrow and blotched with black. The yellow-and-black banding pushes the read firmly to wasp.
rows.fix: Extend a long vertical beak downward from the head with jaws at its tip, and curl the last abdominal segment up into a bulbous knob.

rows.readsAs: a grey shaggy goat — visibly the Mountain Goat recoloured
rows.defect: This is the Mountain Goat asset in grey: identical topline, identical barrel, identical legs, identical horn placement and near-identical horn shape. The ears are small triangles pinned to the skull, not large donkey-like ears; there is no distinct neck mane separate from the body shag; and the horns curve back rather than standing as short straight backswept spikes on a heavy blunt head.
rows.fix: Enlarge the ears to long donkey lobes standing out from the skull and add a darker coarse mane ridge running from poll to withers.

rows.readsAs: a small pink perch or bream
rows.defect: Every must-read is contradicted rather than merely weak. The body is a hard opaque ovate fish covered in a dense regular scale pattern, where a snailfish is translucent and scaleless. There is no sucker disc on the belly. And instead of fins merging into a tapering point, the rear ends abruptly in a separate dark fan-shaped caudal fin pinned to a narrow peduncle. Nothing about it reads gelatinous or tadpole-shaped.
rows.fix: Drop the scale texture for a smooth translucent skin, taper the rear into a continuous pointed fin fringe with no separate tail fan, and add a round sucker disc on the belly.

rows.readsAs: a pale tan antelope, unspecified
rows.defect: The lyre-shaped horns are the one thing that works — they curve up and hook inward at the tips. But the animal is a single uniform tan from spine to belly: the dark chocolate side stripe that divides tan from white is entirely absent, there is no white belly for it to divide, and the face is plain tan with no white blaze, only a small dark smudge at the eye.
rows.fix: Paint the three-tone flank — tan back, hard dark brown horizontal band, white belly — and blaze the face white.

rows.readsAs: a generic shaggy brown goat
rows.defect: The shaggy coat is painted across the barrel and flank only — the neck and shoulders, where a tahr's mane actually hangs, are smooth and bare, so must-read one is inverted. The horns are two thin pale wires curling back, not the short THICK backswept horns called for. The body is not stocky: the legs are long thin columns and the barrel is shallow, and it is drawn on the identical chassis as Wild Sheep with only a hue change.
rows.fix: Move the hair mass onto the neck and shoulders as a hanging ruff that breaks the topline, and thicken the horns to stubby cones with visible basal ridging while shortening the legs to roughly two-thirds of current length.

rows.readsAs: a water bear, though a teal cartoon one
rows.defect: The plump segmented barrel and eight stubby legs are present and the silhouette does read as a tardigrade, but the blunt snout carries no round tubular sucking mouth at all — the front end is a smooth dome with two dark spots that read as eyes on a face. The leg tips are thin sticks with no readable bunch of curved claws, and the colour is a saturated teal-green instead of the specified translucent amber-tan with darker gut contents showing through.
rows.fix: Draw the terminal circular stylet mouth as a dark ring at the very front of the snout and recolour the body to translucent amber-tan with a darker gut mass visible inside.

rows.readsAs: a fanged silver predatory fish
rows.defect: The huge dagger fangs are the one must-read that lands — they are clearly visible along the closed jaw. The horizontal dark flank stripes are almost invisible, reduced to two or three faint grey hairlines lost inside the scale texture. The tail is forked but is flat dark grey with no red tinge whatsoever, and the dorsal and pelvic fins render as vague translucent grey smudges that look unfinished rather than as fins.
rows.fix: Paint four or five hard-edged dark horizontal stripes running the full length of the silver flank and warm the caudal fin to a red-orange tint with defined rays.

rows.readsAs: a chinchilla or a fat guinea pig
rows.defect: The identity must-read — the long pointed squirrel-like snout — is absent. The head is a round ball with a blunt flat face, big rounded ears and a pair of white square buck teeth sticking out at the front, which is a rodent face, not a shrew's. The body is a fat sphere rather than the slim low 2.2-aspect form specified, the feet are invisible stubs with no grasping claws, and the tail is a smooth thick gradient curl with no bushy fur breakup at all.
rows.fix: Rebuild the head as a long tapering pointed snout with a dark nose tip and no incisors, and stretch the body into a low slim elongated form with visible splayed clawed feet.

rows.readsAs: a yellow baby chick or a canary
rows.defect: All three must-reads are missing. There is no black face mask — the head is uniformly yellow. The bill is a tiny thin dark triangle, not a thick conical seed-cracker. There is no woven grass nest anywhere in the frame and the bird is standing upright on stubby legs on the ground rather than clinging upside down, so the single behaviour that names a weaverbird is absent. The rounded chick proportions and stubby wing complete the wrong read.
rows.fix: Add the solid black face mask covering forehead, eye and throat, fatten the bill into a short deep cone, and hang the bird upside down from a woven ball nest.

rows.readsAs: a pig or a pale boar
rows.defect: The long wedge snout with the flat pink disc nose lands clearly and carries the read. The short upward-curving tusks do not — there is only a dark line along the mouth, with nothing that resolves as a tusk. The high shoulder hump with a bristly dorsal crest is also missing: the topline is flat and the bristles hang off the BELLY as a fringe instead of standing up along the spine. The barrel, columnar legs and cloven feet are lifted unchanged from the Tahr and Wild Sheep chassis.
rows.fix: Raise the shoulder into a hump with an erect bristle crest running along the spine, and add two pale upward-hooking tusks projecting clear of the lower jaw line.

rows.readsAs: a fluffy domestic sheep, or the Tahr recoloured cream
rows.defect: The identity must-read is absent: instead of massive horns spiralling in a full curl beside the head there is one thin pale crescent wire, the same wire drawn on the Tahr. The coat is exactly the failure the reference note warns against — a soft fluffy cream fleece rather than short coarse hair. The body is not muscular or blocky; it is the same shallow barrel on the same long thin columns as the Tahr. Every one of the three must-reads is visibly wrong, and the asset is a hue swap of another species in this same batch.
rows.fix: Replace the horn with a genuinely massive horn curling a full turn back, down and forward past the jaw with visible growth ridges, and strip the fleece back to a short flat hair coat over defined shoulder and rump muscle.

rows.readsAs: a bare brown twig with three golden autumn leaves stuck on it
rows.defect: No palm anywhere: one thin straight stick with exactly three small gold leaf blades alternating along it. No feather fronds, no drooping crown, no clump of slender ringed stilt-rooted stems, and not one berry — the hanging brooms of near-black purple fruit that ARE the harvest identity are completely absent. Colour is autumn gold, not mid green.
rows.fix: Draw 3-4 slender grey ringed trunks in a clump, each topped by a small drooping crown of finely divided feather fronds, with dark purple berry brooms hanging beneath the crown.

rows.readsAs: a generic cartoon fruit tree with brown balls in it
rows.defect: The crown is a soft round mass of pointed lance leaflets in palmate tufts — no rounded oak lobes or shallow bays anywhere. The trunk is a smooth flat brown pole with zero bark texture and zero visible limbs: the massive crooked branching that gives oak its silhouette never enters the crown. The four brown spheres have no scaly cup, so they read as plums, not acorns.
rows.fix: Rebuild the leaf stamp as a single lobed oak blade with rounded bays, give the trunk deep vertical bark ridges and 3-4 heavy crooked limbs visible through the canopy, and cap each nut with a hatched scaly cup.

rows.readsAs: a small agave or dwarf fan palm
rows.defect: The blades are stiff, narrow, sharply pointed sword-spikes radiating in a hard symmetric fan — not broad lance-shaped parallel-veined ginger blades from a sheathed pseudostem. Worse, the flower is a yellow bead spike held HIGH above the leaves on a bare stalk, which is exactly what the reference note forbids: the mauve-pink flower must sit at ground level, separate from the shoot. The knobbly pale rhizome is entirely absent.
rows.fix: Replace the spiky fan with 5-6 broad soft parallel-veined blades arching from one sheathed pseudostem, delete the aerial yellow spike, and put a single mauve-pink flower plus a knobbly rhizome at the soil line.

rows.readsAs: a fern frond, or at best a vetch
rows.defect: The identity of alfalfa is the trifoliate clover leaf — three leaflets, middle one stalked. What is drawn is a rigid pinnate ladder of roughly thirty tiny identical oval leaflets in opposite pairs running the whole height of one straight stem. Nothing trifoliate exists in the image. The corkscrew-coiled seed pods are absent, and the violet pea-flower spike is a single 20px bead column at the tip, too small and too generic to read as pea flowers.
rows.fix: Rebuild the leaf as three narrow oval leaflets on a short common stalk, scatter those trifoliate leaves on branching stems, and add at least one visibly coiled spiral seed pod.

rows.readsAs: a single willowherb or lavender sprig
rows.defect: All three must-reads fail. The habit is a tall solitary erect stem, the opposite of the compact low alpine cushion — the plant is far taller than wide. The stem is a smooth round green rod with no square section, no facets and no purple tint. The leaves are long, smooth-edged lance blades with no teeth at all, and they alternate rather than sit in tidy opposite pairs. It is the Alfalfa chassis with fewer, larger leaves and a white bead instead of a purple one.
rows.fix: Redraw as a low mound of many short branching square stems, each with small round toothed leaves in clear opposite pairs and lilac flower whorls in the leaf axils.

rows.readsAs: a cabbage or a pale hosta
rows.defect: Six enormous pale grey-mint discs overlap into one solid mass wider than the frame's plant area, with no leaf stalks visible at all — the reference calls for kidney-shaped leaves on LONG stalks in a low basal rosette, and the stalks are the thing that makes a rosette read. The leaves are plain round, not reniform (no basal notch), and the colour is a washed-out grey-white instead of bright fresh green flushed red. Only the thin orange bead spike is roughly right, and it is dwarfed by the leaf mass.
rows.fix: Shrink the leaves by half, give each a long visible red-flushed stalk radiating from one crown point, and cut a clear kidney notch into the base of every blade.

rows.readsAs: a bundle of dead winter twigs
rows.defect: The huge pendulous trumpet flowers ARE the identity and they are not present. In their place are six tiny white specks perched on top of the stem tips, pointing UP — which is the Datura error the reference note explicitly warns against. The foliage is small, sparse and dead tan-brown rather than large, soft, coarse mid-green ovals, so the whole plant reads as leafless brushwood.
rows.fix: Hang three or four large white trumpet blooms straight down from the branches, each as long as a third of the plant's height with flared recurved tips, and recolour the leaves to broad soft mid green.

rows.readsAs: a fern with a crumb of white fluff on top
rows.defect: Angelica is defined by architecture this image has none of: the stem is a thin plain green rod, not a thick, hollow, ridged, purple-flushed column, and there is no inflated sheath where any leaf stalk meets it. The huge domed globe umbel is rendered as a single white crescent about 25px across sitting on the stem tip — smaller than one leaflet, so the plant's biggest feature is its smallest mark. The twice-divided leaf of broad toothed leaflets is replaced by the generic fine pinnate ladder shared with Alfalfa and Anise.
rows.fix: Thicken the stem to a ridged purple hollow column with a swollen sheath at each node, and blow the umbel up to a wide domed sphere of tiny florets at least as broad as the foliage.

rows.readsAs: a fern — and specifically, the same fern as Angelica
rows.defect: This is Angelica's picture with slightly finer, yellower leaflets: same straight central stem, same rectangular pinnate ladder, same white crescent speck at the tip, same height and shadow. The must-read that IS anise — two clearly different leaf shapes on one plant, rounded toothed leaves below and fine feathery threads above — is absent, every leaflet is identical top to bottom. The flat-topped white umbels are one crescent crumb, and the ribbed grey-brown seeds never appear.
rows.fix: Put rounded, long-stalked toothed leaves on the lower third and thread-fine feathery ones above, and replace the crescent with two or three flat-topped white umbels on slender ribbed branches.

rows.readsAs: a berry bush — the blue fruit does land
rows.defect: The habit must-read is inverted: this is a narrow upright vase of stems clearly taller than wide, where the reference demands a low sprawling dwarf shrub wider than tall, hugging the ground. The leaves are pale yellow-green and pointed rather than small, blunt and blue-grey with a waxy cast, and the berries cluster in tight bunches at the stem tips instead of being scattered singly along the twigs — and they carry no pale bloom, just flat blue.
rows.fix: Splay the stems outward into a low mat wider than it is tall, recolour the leaves blue-grey, and distribute single bloom-dusted berries along the branches instead of tip clusters.

rows.readsAs: a cabbage — and it is Alpine Sorrel's cabbage in a different hue
rows.defect: Silhouette, disc count, disc overlap order, the central notch, the vein rake and the orange bead spike are all identical to Alpine Sorrel; only the fill has been shifted from pale mint to olive. On its own terms it also misses everything: the clump of LONG-STALKED oblong, arrow-based basal leaves is drawn as six giant stalkless round discs, the stem is olive-green not reddish, and the dense rose-pink papery seed spire is a thin orange bead column narrower than the stem it sits on.
rows.fix: Redraw from scratch as a loose clump of long red petioles each carrying a narrow oblong blade with an arrow-shaped base, and fatten the seed spire into a dense rose-pink column of overlapping papery discs.

rows.readsAs: an upright willow sapling or an olive shrub
rows.defect: The reference note says in as many words: never draw it as an upright tree — and this is an upright vase of tan trunks standing tall on a bare base, the exact forbidden reading. The prostrate ground-hugging mat, which is the whole point of an arctic willow, is absent. The leaves are narrow grey-green lances rather than small glossy rounded ovals, and the catkins are pale cream rather than red-tinged, so they read as seed heads on a reed.
rows.fix: Lay the stems flat along the ground into a low creeping mat only a few leaf-widths tall, put small round glossy leaves on them, and stand short red fuzzy catkins upright out of the mat.

rows.readsAs: a ghost-white agave with a sunflower sticker on a wire
rows.defect: Reuses African Ginger's stiff radial sword-blade fan, so the basal rosette of plain OVAL untoothed leaves is drawn as a spray of sharp pointed spikes, and the colour is a bleached cream-white instead of mid green — the plant does not read as living foliage. The 1-2 opposite stem leaves never appear. The flower is present but tiny and mechanical: a neat symmetric gear-toothed yellow disc, where the must-read is ragged ray petals that visibly droop.
rows.fix: Swap the spiky fan for a flat rosette of six soft mid-green oval leaves, add one opposite pair partway up the stem, and enlarge the head with long uneven drooping ray petals.

rows.readsAs: a cabbage — the same cabbage as both Sorrels, in green
rows.defect: The unmistakable arrowhead leaf silhouette is the entire identity of this species and there is not one arrow-shaped leaf in the picture: it is the Sorrel disc-pile chassis recoloured green, six huge rounded stalkless blades with no backward-pointing basal lobes and no long spongy triangular stalks. Nothing indicates water — no waterline, no emergent stance, the leaves sit on the same dry ground ellipse as the terrestrial herbs. The whorled three-petal flowers are reduced to a single white star at the very tip.
rows.fix: Cut deep twin backward lobes into every blade to make true arrowhead leaves, raise them on long straight triangular stalks from a waterline, and run three or four whorls of white three-petal flowers up the bare stem.

rows.readsAs: a fountain of pampas or fountain grass, or a spray of wheat
rows.defect: The culms arch outward and droop like a fountain grass instead of standing as tall straight hollow culms; the nodes are drawn as bare cross-ticks on naked stems with no leafy sprays anywhere; and the harvest itself — the fat brown-sheathed pointed shoot at the base of the clump — is completely absent, so the thing named on the card does not exist in the picture.
rows.fix: Stand the culms vertical and straight with visible ringed nodes and leaf sprays only in the top third, and plant two or three fat brown scale-sheathed cones pushing up at the base of the clump.

rows.readsAs: a palm or a cycad
rows.defect: It is drawn with a woody brown FORKED trunk and a radial crown of stiff feathery pinnate fronds — exactly the two things the note forbids. There is no smooth green false trunk of rolled sheaths, no torn paddle blades, no hanging bunch and no purple-red terminal bud; the only fruit cue is a small yellow floret cluster sitting up in the crown instead of a bunch hanging below an arching stalk.
rows.fix: Replace the brown fork with a single smooth green sheath-column, swap the fronds for a few huge paddle blades torn into ribs, and hang a downward bunch of yellow-green fingers tipped with a purple bud.

rows.readsAs: a saguaro or an organ-pipe column cactus with a sunflower stuck on it
rows.defect: The body is a tall narrow tapering spire roughly four times taller than wide — the fat squat accordion-ribbed BARREL that is the whole identity is absent. The crown is a point, not a flat top ringed with fruit; the harvest ring of scaly yellow barrel fruits is reduced to one tiny beige cluster tucked to one side; and the spines are sparse straight white sticks with none of the long flattened hooked central spines.
rows.fix: Squash the body to a wide squat ribbed barrel with a flat top, ring that flat crown with scaly yellow fruits, and give each rib crest stout red-brown hooked spines.

rows.readsAs: a sparse bare cane shrub or a dying willow whip with pom-pom seedheads
rows.defect: Drawn on the shared cane-vase chassis: mostly naked brown sticks, airy and see-through, when the must-read is a DENSE CONICAL EVERGREEN. The leaves are tiny thin mid-green slivers, not thick leathery very-dark glossy lances with a rippled margin, and there are so few of them the plant reads as leafless. The cream flowers are white pom-pom balls stuck on the cane tips rather than small clusters tucked into the leaf axils.
rows.fix: Fill the silhouette into a solid dark conical evergreen mass of large leathery wavy-edged near-black-green leaves, and move the cream flower clusters down into the leaf joints.

rows.readsAs: a generic houseplant vine floating in mid-air
rows.defect: None of the three must-reads survive: the runner rises in a diagonal S clear of the ground instead of creeping flat across sand; every leaf is a plain undivided round oval with no trace of the two-lobed goat's-foot notch; and the big pink-magenta funnel flowers are reduced to a few 6-pixel pink blobs pressed against the stem with no funnel, no flare and no dark star throat. The whole plant also floats with the shadow detached below it.
rows.fix: Lay the runner flat and horizontal along a ground line and draw two or three large open pink-magenta funnels in three-quarter view with a dark star throat, on leaves notched into two rounded lobes.

rows.readsAs: a sprig of vetch or a fern frond climbing a wire
rows.defect: The harvest is entirely missing — there is not one purple-magenta pea flower and not one flat green pod anywhere on the card, so the first and defining must-read has no pixels. What remains is the same floating S-vine chassis stood upright rather than a low sprawling mat, the leaflets are minute pale specks instead of thick oval pairs, and the big leafy stipules at the leaf bases are absent.
rows.fix: Add two or three clusters of clearly drawn purple-blue pea flowers with a broad standard petal plus a couple of flat green pods, and lay the vine into a low sprawling mat.

rows.readsAs: a berry bush with purple fruit — plum is a fair guess
rows.defect: Reads as roughly the right thing, but it is the shared cane-vase again: upright and taller than wide when the must-read is a dense low thicket WIDER than tall, and the plums sit as five isolated lollipop balls perched on the cane tips instead of tight clusters held against the twigs. The smother of small white five-petal blossom is absent, and the leaves are grey-sage slivers rather than dull dark ovals with a pale downy underside.
rows.fix: Widen the shrub into a low sprawling thicket and move the plums into tight three-to-five berry clusters pressed against the stems along the branch, not one ball per tip.

rows.readsAs: an upright currant or redcurrant bush
rows.defect: The growth form is inverted: bearberry is a flat trailing groundcover mat at aspect 2.4, and this is the identical upright narrow cane vase used for Bay Laurel, Beach Plum and Bilberry, taller than wide. The reddish peeling stems are the same flat brown as every other card, the leaves are small pointed ovals rather than thick blunt spoon-shaped paddles, and the white-pink urn flowers are absent — the red berries alone carry the read.
rows.fix: Redraw it as a low horizontal mat of trailing reddish stems running sideways off the base, crowded with small blunt spoon-shaped glossy leaves and dull red berries at ground level.

rows.readsAs: a generic herb sprig or an ash seedling — nothing poisonous, nothing nightshade
rows.defect: One ramrod-straight unbranched stem carrying a perfectly symmetrical ladder of identical opposite leaves, which contradicts the must-read of a coarse BRANCHING herb with UNEQUAL leaf pairs. Both identity features are missing: no dull purple-brown drooping bell flowers anywhere, and no glossy black cherry-sized berry cupped in a flared green five-point star — only three lilac pinheads at the apex, too small to resolve as anything.
rows.fix: Break the stem into a coarse branching habit with one large and one small leaf at each node, and draw one big glossy black berry sitting in a flared green star calyx at reading size.

rows.readsAs: a pink daisy or a coneflower on a fern stalk
rows.defect: The flower head is a neat radially symmetric daisy with a round disc and short even petals — the exact opposite of the ragged firework head of long narrow tubular florets that IS Monarda. No leafy bracts under the head, no sign of a square stem, and the leaves are drawn as a fine pinnate ladder of narrow slivers rather than toothed lance-shaped opposite pairs.
rows.fix: Replace the daisy with a shaggy two-tier whorl of long lavender tubular florets spraying off a domed head, and set a ruff of leafy bracts directly beneath it.

rows.readsAs: a blueberry bush
rows.defect: It reads as a low blue-berry shrub, but it is pixel-for-pixel the Bearberry chassis recoloured, and both features the note says separate bilberry from blueberry are inverted: the stems are plain flat brown instead of green and sharply angled, and the berries are gathered into clustered bunches at the cane tips instead of borne singly in the leaf axils. The pink-green globe flowers are absent, and the shrub is a narrow upright vase rather than a low dense mound.
rows.fix: Recolour the twigs to ridged green and scatter the berries one at a time at leaf joints along the stems, then widen the outline into a low mound.

rows.readsAs: a generic lollipop shade tree — a linden or a kids-book apple tree
rows.defect: The trunk is a plain flat mid-brown column with no white bark, no peeling papery strips and no black diamond scars, so the single most identifiable feature of a birch is entirely absent. The crown is a dense round lollipop of large round leaves instead of a narrow airy crown of fine drooping twigs with small triangular toothed leaves, and the trunk is thick and stubby rather than slender. Nothing indicates sap or a tap either.
rows.fix: Paint the trunk chalk-white with black diamond lenticel scars and peeling bark curls, and thin the crown into a narrow airy veil of fine drooping twigs with small triangular leaves.

rows.readsAs: an agave or a century plant with a daisy on a wire
rows.defect: The rosette is made of broad flat pale-grey sword blades spread like an agave, not short fleshy cylindrical finger-like leaves, and they are turgid and prominent rather than already shrivelling. The must-read of a LARGE many-petalled pink flower sitting FLAT on bare gravel with NO VISIBLE STEM is directly contradicted: a small pink daisy is held on a long conspicuous bare stalk high above the rosette, so the two defining traits of bitterroot are both reversed.
rows.fix: Drop the flower down to sit flush on the ground at full width with many narrow pink petals, and replace the sword blades with a small ring of shrivelling fleshy cylindrical fingers.

rows.readsAs: a grapevine
rows.defect: Lobed leaves, coiling tendrils and a purple berry cluster get the read home, but the bunch is far too small and is glued flat to the middle of the stem instead of hanging BELOW the leaves as a tight conical bunch, and it is bright violet with no chalky blue-black bloom. The vine is the shared floating S-spine with no woody gnarled stem and no ground contact, and the leaves are shallow-lobed with no coarse teeth.
rows.fix: Enlarge the bunch into a proper tapering conical cluster of dusty blue-black berries hanging clear below a leaf, and thicken the lower vine into gnarled woody bark.

rows.readsAs: a closed tapered sheaf of straws, like a corn husk or a bundled feather
rows.defect: No Y-forking anywhere — the whole thing is one unbranched teardrop of parallel vertical straps. The bladders are three lone blobs stacked on the centreline instead of PAIRS flanking a midrib, and there are no swollen warty fertile tips (just two tiny knobs at the apex). All three must-reads are absent.
rows.fix: Rebuild as a flat strap that forks in twos at least three times, and put the bladders in mirrored pairs either side of each strap's midrib with lumpy swollen tips terminating the outer forks.

rows.readsAs: a small catkin-bearing willow-ish shrub
rows.defect: The reddish upright twigs and the stubby orange catkins do read. But the leaves are narrow pointed blades set in even rows, not small blunt spoon-shaped leaves broadest near the tip with teeth at the end, and they are blue-grey rather than resin-dotted grey-green. The catkins also sit on fully leafed twigs, so the bare-stem spring read is lost.
rows.fix: Redraw the leaf glyph as a short paddle widest at the blunt tip with two or three teeth near the end, and strip leaves from the catkin-bearing twigs.

rows.readsAs: a bare twiggy bush with pink flecks at the tips
rows.defect: Same fan-of-wands shrub chassis as Bog Myrtle with the catkins recoloured pink. The flowers are flat pink lozenges pointing upward and outward — nothing nodding, nothing urn-shaped, no bell mouth. The leaves are bare grey hairlines with no width, so the inrolled edge and the chalky white underside — the trait that makes this plant flash silver — are entirely invisible.
rows.fix: Give the leaf a narrow blade with a visible pale underside edge curled under, and hang the flowers as downward-facing pot-bellied urns from short drooping stalks at the shoot tips.

rows.readsAs: a generic tropical fruit tree with green striped melons
rows.defect: The round green fruit reads, but the leaves are pinnate fern/palm fronds — rows of small pinnae along a rachis — instead of the huge stiff hand-shaped leaves cut into deep fingers that ARE breadfruit. The fruit skin is drawn with bold meridian stripes so it reads as a watermelon rather than a fine pebbled rind, and two of the three fruits sit inside the crown rather than at the twig tips.
rows.fix: Replace the fern frond with a single large glossy leaf cut into 5-9 deep finger lobes, and swap the melon stripes for a fine even stipple.

rows.readsAs: an ordinary shade tree with three brown nuts or acorns tucked under the crown
rows.defect: The identity per the packet note is the soft-spined green fruit and the lobed leaf, and neither is present. The fruits are three small smooth BROWN spheres with no spines at all, clustered against the trunk top; the leaves are the same fern-frond glyph as Breadfruit, not huge hand-shaped leaves with pale veins. Strip the colour and this is the same tree as Camphor.
rows.fix: Draw the fruit large, pale green and bristling with soft flexible spines out at the branch ends, on a leaf redrawn as a broad hand cut into finger lobes with pale midribs.

rows.readsAs: a stiff upright vetch or ash sapling with one blue flower on top
rows.defect: The paired opposite leaves are correct in arrangement but flat, matte and pointed — nothing fleshy or succulent — and the stem is a thin ramrod-straight vertical green line, so the sprawling, rooting, water-hugging habit that defines brooklime is gone. Worse, there is exactly ONE blue star at the apex; the must-read calls for loose sprays of small blue flowers rising from the LEAF JOINTS, and no axillary flower spike exists.
rows.fix: Bend the stem into a low sprawl with a thick reddish hollow look and rooting nodes, and add two or three short flower sprays springing from leaf axils rather than a single terminal bloom.

rows.readsAs: the exact same closed straw sheaf as Bladderwrack, recoloured brown
rows.defect: Pixel-for-pixel the Bladderwrack chassis in a brown palette, including the three centreline blobs that belong to bladderwrack. Every must-read is absent: there is NO single round onion-like bulb float, NO long straight whip stipe below it, and NO spray of long ribbon blades fanning from the top — the form tapers to a closed point at the bottom and frays into stubs at the top.
rows.fix: Draw one clear silhouette — a long thin whip rising from a holdfast, swelling into a single big round bulb, with six to ten long flat ribbon blades streaming off the top of that bulb.

rows.readsAs: a generic small tree with a few dark slivers hidden in its foliage
rows.defect: Cacao's whole identity is cauliflory, and the trunk is completely bare — a clean brown lollipop stick from ground to crown with nothing on it. The pods are instead scattered INSIDE the leaf canopy as four tiny dark almost-black splinters, roughly the size of a leaf, with no ribbing, no melon bulk and no yellow-to-red colour. The leaves are also small upright ovals rather than very large limp drooping oblongs.
rows.fix: Move the pods onto the bare trunk and thick limbs as large ribbed rugby-ball shapes in yellow-orange-red, and let the leaves hang down twice their current length.

rows.readsAs: a pale-leaved twiggy shrub with a few purple star flowers
rows.defect: The waxy five-pointed purple stars do read, and the chalky pale leaf colour is right. But the leaves are small alternating ovals ranked up thin brown wands — the opposite of the reference's HUGE opposite pairs clasping a thick stem — so the plant's heavy, coarse, dusty mass is lost, and the shared shrub chassis makes it a recolour of Bog Myrtle. The big inflated curved balloon pods are absent entirely.
rows.fix: Halve the number of stems, thicken them, and put two or three very large opposite leaf pairs clasping each stem, then hang at least one fat curved inflated pod.

rows.readsAs: a small tree carrying blackberries
rows.defect: The black berries are present but rendered as tight knobbly clusters that read as blackberries or elderberry heads rather than small round berries sitting singly in shallow cups on loose sprays. The crown is the shared soft glow-blob with leaves stamped as sparse radial spokes, so the broad DENSE rounded dome never forms; the leaf shows no three-veined fan and no pale blue-grey underside; the trunk is a flat untextured brown stick with none of the vertical grey-brown fissuring called out as a must-read.
rows.fix: Fill the crown to an opaque dome, cut three veins fanning from the leaf base with a pale reverse, and score vertical fissures into the bark.

rows.readsAs: a single fern frond with a tiny yellow smear on top
rows.defect: This is the Brooklime herb chassis with the apex ornament recoloured yellow. Canola is defined by a broad flat-topped MASS of vivid yellow four-petalled flowers; here it is one small yellow crescent perhaps a tenth of the plant's height. There are no clasping blue-green upper leaves wrapping the stem — the leaves are a symmetrical pinnate ladder of narrow leaflets — and there are no long thin upward-angled pods at all.
rows.fix: Crown the stem with a wide dense head of separate four-petalled yellow flowers, wrap the upper stem in eared clasping blue-green leaves, and angle a dozen slender pods upward below the head.

rows.readsAs: a short cutting of a pea or bean vine floating with nothing to climb
rows.defect: The tendril curls and the alternate leaves do say vine. But the stem is a thin bright green zigzag — nothing woody, nothing rope-thick — and it hangs in empty space with no host trunk and no free-hanging loop, so the liana read is missing. The leaves are small rounded coins spread evenly along the whole length rather than large heart-shaped blades concentrated at the top, and there are no pale flowers or dark berries anywhere.
rows.fix: Thicken the stem into a grey woody rope with a hanging loop, twist it around a suggested host trunk, and mass big heart-shaped leaves plus a berry cluster only at the upper end.

rows.readsAs: an acacia or mimosa — a feathery-leaved tree
rows.defect: The leaflets are drawn as dozens of tiny narrow pinnae along each rachis, giving a fine ferny texture; carob's identity is 6-10 THICK ROUNDED COIN-like glossy leaflets in pairs, big enough to count. The pods are two dark smudges buried inside the crown, almost invisible against the foliage instead of hanging in obvious bunches. The trunk is tall and thin under a loose crown rather than a short trunk under a broad dense dome.
rows.fix: Cut the leaflet count to eight big round coins per leaf and hang three or four long flat brown pods clear of the foliage on the crown's outer edge.

rows.readsAs: a bronze-red maple-leaved shrub
rows.defect: The palmate star-shaped lobed leaves read well and the bronze-red colour is legitimate — this is the strongest leaf in the batch. What is missing is the harvest: the upright cluster of soft red spiny capsules is nowhere. In its place are a dozen tiny pale yellow tick marks scattered through the foliage that read as dust or render noise, not as seed capsules. The stems are plain brown, not the red-tinged hollow canes of the reference.
rows.fix: Add one or two upright spikes of round bristly crimson capsules standing clear ABOVE the leaves, and tint the stems red.

rows.readsAs: a sago palm / cycad rosette
rows.defect: The fronds are stiff, thick and edged with hard triangular sawteeth, and they radiate as a rigid flat disc rather than soft thin translucent shade-green pinnae arching outward and downward. There is no rock crevice or crevice-wedged crown anywhere in the frame — the crown simply sits on bare ground with a cast shadow — and no rows of brown spore dots on any frond underside. The same frond generator is reused for Date's palm crown.
rows.fix: Redraw the fronds thin, limp and semi-translucent with rounded lobed pinnae, drop the crown into a dark rock cleft that clips the frond bases, and stipple two rows of brown sori along the underside of the two forward-facing fronds.

rows.readsAs: a blue aster or cornflower
rows.defect: The sky-blue colour is right and the flowers are the strongest thing in the frame, but the ray tips are drawn as sharp points radiating like a daisy instead of the squared, fringe-toothed ends that ARE chicory's signature. The flowers also sit on long bare stalks rising well clear of the plant, whereas chicory's flowers sit almost directly on the wiry branching stem. The base is a spiky agave-like tuft of smooth strap leaves rather than toothed dandelion-shaped basal leaves.
rows.fix: Cut each ray petal off square and notch its tip with three or four small teeth, then move the heads down to sit tight against the stems in ones and twos instead of on long naked stalks.

rows.readsAs: a generic pink-flowered twig shrub, closest to a thistle or a spiraea
rows.defect: The identity must-read — the long drooping cylindrical bottlebrush raceme, first of white flowers then of dark red-black cherries hanging in a hanging cylinder — is completely absent. What is drawn is five small pink pompom heads perched on the tips of the standard vase-fan canes, which is the loose-bunch arrangement the reference explicitly rules out. There is no fruit of any kind, and the leaves are thin willow-like lances rather than broad glossy sharply-toothed ovals with an abrupt point.
rows.fix: Replace every terminal pompom with a long pendulous cylinder of tightly packed dark red-black spheres hanging down off the branch tip, and widen the leaves into glossy toothed ovals.

rows.readsAs: a desert shrub with white daisies
rows.defect: Two of the three must-reads are missing. The leaves are long pinnate feather sprays combed along each cane, not tiny thick wedge-shaped leaves with three to five blunt lobes clustered on twiggy branches. There are no silvery feather-plumed seed tails anywhere, and those plumes are the thing that makes a cliffrose recognisable at distance. The flowers are also eight-plus narrow petals reading as daisies rather than five broad overlapping rose petals.
rows.fix: Swap the feather sprays for dense clusters of tiny three-lobed wedge leaves and hang curling silvery plume tails off the spent flowers so the bush looks smoky.

rows.readsAs: a bottlebrush spike or a horsetail, not a berry plant
rows.defect: The render is a tall narrow vertical column of thirty-plus identical pointed leaves stacked in a dense ladder up a single stem — nothing like the reference's short stem carrying one or two rounded, wrinkled, five-lobed leaves. There is no white five-petalled flower, and there is no solitary golden-amber raspberry-like berry; the only harvest cue is a small orange knot buried in the leaf tuft at the very top, far too small and too obscured to read as the single fruit that IS this species.
rows.fix: Strip the stem to two big rounded five-lobed crumpled leaves and put one large amber-orange druplet berry on top of the stem where it cannot be missed.

rows.readsAs: a grey-leaved twig shrub with white flower spikes
rows.defect: The dusty grey-green leaf colour lands, but the growth form does not: the reference asks for a low mounded cushion bush and the render is the family's upright vase of straight brown canes, taller than wide. The flowers are drawn as a continuous string of white beads running along the top third of each cane rather than as distinct ball-like whorls spaced apart with bare stem between them. The leaves are also flat smooth lances with no puckered pebbled surface or rolled-under edge.
rows.fix: Compress the silhouette into a wide low dome and break each white bead-string into three or four separated ring-clusters with visible bare stem between them.
