rows.readsAs: a generic red-berried garden shrub
rows.defect: The single strongest coffee signature — tiered horizontal branch layers spraying out flat from an upright trunk — is absent; the plant is the family's upright vase fan with no horizontal tier anywhere. The red cherries are gathered into five pompoms on the branch TIPS instead of being pressed in tight clusters along the branch in the leaf axils, which the reference calls out specifically. The leaves are small plain ovals rather than large glossy opposite leaves with wavy margins.
rows.fix: Rebuild the plant as one vertical stem with three or four flat horizontal branch tiers, and move the red cherries into tight clusters hugging those horizontal branches where the leaves join.

rows.readsAs: a pink sea pen, a bundle of soft noodles, or a feather duster worm
rows.defect: Every must-read is inverted. The form is six smooth soft-edged tubes with rounded tips, gradient-shaded to look pliable and rubbery — the reference states in as many words that the texture must read stony and brittle, NOT soft or floppy. There are no jointed bead-like segments anywhere along the branchlets; the tubes are unbroken from base to tip. There is no hard pink crust plating any rock, and no rock at all. The pink is the only correct attribute.
rows.fix: Break each branch into a chain of short chalky beads with visible constrictions between segments, flatten the shading to a matte lime-white finish, and plate the base onto a pink-crusted rock.

rows.readsAs: a pussy-willow stem or a florist's snowball twig
rows.defect: The plant has no foliage whatsoever — a bare green stem forking twice, with zero leaves on it — against a reference calling for a bushy shrub of broad three-to-five lobed palmate leaves. The identity must-read, the split brown boll husk with white fibre bulging out of it, is absent: the harvest is four plain white spheres with no brown capsule, no split, no husk points, so they read as flower buds rather than burst bolls. The hibiscus-like cream-yellow flower is also missing.
rows.fix: Draw a brown four-lobed split husk cupping each white puff so the fibre visibly bursts out of a capsule, and clothe the stem in broad lobed palmate leaves with reddish veins.

rows.readsAs: a child's drawing of an apple tree
rows.defect: It reads as an apple tree rather than a crabapple. The apples are five large fruits, each nearly a fifth of the crown's height, sitting directly against the foliage with no stalk at all — the reference asks for masses of marble-sized apples dangling on long slender stalks. There is no pink-and-white blossom. The crown is a soft airbrushed green blob with no twiggy irregular outline or spur shoots, and the trunk is a flat parallel-sided brown slab with no taper and no branching into the canopy.
rows.fix: Shrink the fruit to marble size, multiply it to twenty-plus, and hang each one on a visible thin stalk so the crown looks loaded and dangling.

rows.readsAs: a yellow-daisy desert shrub
rows.defect: The branching is the family's dense crowded vase, not the open airy widely spaced skeleton that is creosote's whole look in the desert. The leaves are long pinnate feather sprays instead of tiny paired leaflets joined at the base into a V, and they are matte rather than varnished with resin. The flowers are four big flat yellow daisies rather than small five-petalled blooms with twisted petals, and the cotton-white fuzzy round seed capsules — the second listed must-read — are nowhere in the frame.
rows.fix: Thin the branches to four or five widely separated twigs, replace the feather sprays with tiny paired V-shaped varnished leaflets, and scatter fuzzy white seed balls through the crown.

rows.readsAs: an upright twiggy shrub with grey seed heads
rows.defect: The identity must-read is a flat creeping heather-like carpet, and the render is its exact opposite: a tall upright vase of straight brown canes, distinctly taller than wide, despite the reference aspect of 2.2 asking for a wide low mat. The berries are wrong twice over — they are pale grey-white clustered pompoms sitting on the bare tips of the canes, not small glossy BLACK berries nestled tight down among the needles. The needle leaves are sparse single strokes on bare brown stem rather than crowded densely along it.
rows.fix: Flatten the whole plant into a low sprawling mat of creeping wiry stems densely packed with short needles, and tuck small glossy jet-black berries down among the foliage.

rows.readsAs: a generic feathery-leaved twig shrub
rows.defect: The pinnate sprays are the closest this chassis comes to a correct reading, but the leaflets are a repeated zigzag comb of identical sawteeth rather than distinct small glossy pointed oval leaflets, so there is no sense of eleven-to-twenty-one separate leaflets on a rachis. The white flowers are drawn as tight round pompoms on the cane tips instead of the flat wide heads of tiny flowers the reference calls for, so they read as berry clusters. The shrub is also crowded and dense rather than slender and open.
rows.fix: Draw the leaflets as separate small ovals paired along a visible thin rachis, and flatten the white flower balls into wide flat-topped corymbs.

rows.readsAs: a cycad or a generic palm
rows.defect: The must-read that is called out first — a massive fruit bunch hanging from the crown on orange strands — is present only as a small brown knot tucked at the crown centre, no bigger than the trunk is wide, with no orange stalks and no hanging weight, so the fruiting identity is invisible at a glance. The fronds radiate as a stiff flat sawtooth disc rather than arching feather fronds, reusing Cave Fern's frond exactly. The trunk is a smooth brown slab that forks into a Y, which no date palm does, and it carries none of the rough diamond-patterned leaf-scar texture.
rows.fix: Hang a large heavy bunch of amber-brown oval fruits on bright orange strands out of the crown so it drapes below the frond bases, and replace the forked trunk with a single column of diamond leaf scars.

rows.readsAs: a generic orange or apricot tree
rows.defect: Stock lollipop tree: a round blurred green ball, not an upright oval crown, on a smooth flat brown post with no blocky bark texture at all. The four fruit are plain orange-brown spheres with no four-lobed papery star calyx — the one feature that says persimmon-family — and they read as oranges.
rows.fix: Give each fruit a visible pale four/five-lobed star calyx cap on the shoulder, stretch the crown to a taller upright oval, and break the trunk into dark blocky bark plates.

rows.readsAs: a squash or cucumber vine cutting
rows.defect: The runner climbs the frame as a vertical S rather than trailing flat across sand, so the ground-hugging habit at aspect 2.6 is lost. No yellow five-lobed flowers anywhere. The single fruit is present and correctly small and striped, but the leaves are near-white and smooth-edged rather than grey-green and bristly, so the whole plant reads pale and cultivated.
rows.fix: Lay the runners horizontally along a sand line and add two or three yellow five-lobed flowers at the nodes.

rows.readsAs: a single fern pinna or an anonymous herb sprig
rows.defect: Chassis-A leaf ladder. The flowers — rings of lavender tubes in whorls at the leaf axils, which is the entire mint read — are collapsed into one tiny near-white bead column on the very tip, so there are no whorls up the stem. The stem is a plain round green line with no square-section or woody base showing.
rows.fix: Put three or four distinct lavender-pink flower whorls at the leaf axils partway down the stem and edge the stem to show a square cross-section.

rows.readsAs: a bundle of dry twigs with a few lavender sprigs
rows.defect: Chassis-B rod broom. The silhouette is a tall upright vase of bare brown sticks, not a rounded low silver bush, and brown dominates because the silver foliage is reduced to a few tiny slivers. The flowers are pale washed-out mauve beads, nowhere near the vivid blue-violet whorls with reddish bracts that are the species' whole signature.
rows.fix: Make the flower whorls saturated blue-violet and much larger, and mass silver spoon-leaves densely enough to hide the brown stems into a rounded mound.

rows.readsAs: a nameless seedling sprig — the same picture as Desert Mint with the tip bead deleted
rows.defect: The woody pod split into two long recurved grappling hooks — the thing the species is named for and the only reason it is recognisable — is completely absent. So is the trumpet flower. The plant is drawn as an upright chassis-A ladder of small pointed leaflets when it should be a sprawling flat-to-the-ground mat of large rounded lobed opposite leaves. Nothing in the frame is Devil's Claw.
rows.fix: Draw the black woody capsule with two long recurved claws as the dominant foreground element, on a low sprawling stem with big rounded lobed leaves.

rows.readsAs: a bare sapling twig with six ordinary leaves
rows.defect: No spines at all — the cane should be armoured in yellow needles, and that armour IS the identity. The leaves are small simple ovals instead of enormous maple-like palmate hands, and the upright pyramid spike of scarlet berries is missing. The stem also runs on bare above the topmost leaf, leaving a naked pole occupying the upper third.
rows.fix: Cover the crooked cane in dense yellow needle spines and replace the ovals with two or three giant palmate lobed leaves under a red berry cone.

rows.readsAs: three scallions or green bean pods with pink pinwheel stickers
rows.defect: The stems are smooth round cylinders standing straight up — no three-winged triangular ribs, no scrambling or hanging habit, no areole spine clusters — so the cactus read is gone entirely. The fruit are flat pink pinwheel rosettes pasted onto the side of a stem; they have no volume, no oval body, and their green points splay flat like petals rather than curling up as scale fins, so they register as flowers, not fruit. No white night flower.
rows.fix: Rebuild the stems as three-ribbed triangular segments with scalloped wavy edges that arch and hang, and make the fruit a solid pink oval with green scales curling off its surface.

rows.readsAs: a bundle of red spaghetti or a sea whip
rows.defect: Every element is a narrow cylindrical strand with a centre highlight, gathered into a tight vase. There is no flat blade anywhere, no hand-shaped lobing, and no ear-like flaps along the margins — dulse is defined by a broad flat leathery hand, and this is a filamentous alga instead. The holdfast is a shadow smudge with no visible disc.
rows.fix: Replace the strands with one broad flat red blade splitting into three or four wide hand lobes, with small ear flaps on the margins and a small disc holdfast.

rows.readsAs: a small silver agave with a flower stalk
rows.defect: The big white star in the frame is the leaf rosette, not the bract star, and the actual flower head is a tiny smooth six-point daisy on a long bare wire above it. The yellow button flower heads in the star centre are entirely absent — no yellow pixel anywhere — and the star that is present reads as smooth painted card, not dense felted wool.
rows.fix: Move the woolly star to the top as the flower head, at three times its current size, with several small yellow buttons packed in its centre and a visibly hairy felted edge.

rows.readsAs: a twiggy brown shrub with red berries — half right
rows.defect: Chassis-B rod broom shared with Desert Sage. The main rods are brown wood, not the yellow-green jointed rods the species is named for, and there are no node bands or scale sheaths anywhere — the green appears only as loose scattered sticks that read as stray leaves, which contradicts the leafless requirement. The red cone-berries are present and correct.
rows.fix: Recolour the main rods yellow-green and band them with visible dark joints every short interval, deleting the loose green sticks.

rows.readsAs: a bottlebrush, a green pinecone, or a caterpillar
rows.defect: The trifoliate clover leaf — three toothed leaflets on a stalk, the read that names fenugreek — does not appear once. Instead the chassis-A ladder is compressed into a solid dense column of overlapping serrated fronds with no visible stem or leaf stalks. No pale yellow pea flowers at the leaf joints, and the sickle-curved beaked pods are reduced to one small dark hook at the apex that reads as debris.
rows.fix: Space out four or five clearly separated trifoliate leaves on a branching stem and hang two long sickle-curved beaked pods off the joints.

rows.readsAs: a generic palm or cycad fan
rows.defect: The tight spiral crozier coils are the harvest and the name, and they are not there — I can find one faint circle the size of a comma near the base, nothing standing in the middle of the crown. No papery brown scale husks either. The crown is also not a vase: it is a low spreading fan crowded against the top edge with one long frond spearing off to the right past the mass.
rows.fix: Stand three or four large tight spirals with brown papery scales in the centre of the crown and pull the fronds up into a vase ring around them.

rows.readsAs: an anonymous sprig with a pink bead on top
rows.defect: Chassis-A leaf ladder again, pixel-for-pixel the Desert Mint stem with the tip bead recoloured magenta. The flower spike should be a tall tapering raceme roughly a third of the plant's height with visible four-petalled flowers opening from the bottom up; here it is a smooth 10%-height bead column with no individual flowers. Leaves are opposite pairs rather than spiralling, and the plant is not tall and narrow as aspect 0.25 requires.
rows.fix: Lengthen the spike to a third of the plant and build it from discrete four-petalled magenta flowers, open at the base and budded at the tip.

rows.readsAs: an anonymous sprig with one small blue star flower
rows.defect: Chassis-A leaf ladder with the tip ornament swapped for a blue star. The stem is a single leaf-dense shoot rather than a slender clump of very thin bare wiry stems, so the airy flax habit is gone. The one flower is a small pointed six-point star, not a flat rounded five-petal sky-blue disc, and the round pea-sized seed capsules are absent entirely.
rows.fix: Split into three or four thin sparse wiry stems, each topped with a flat round five-petalled sky-blue flower, and add a couple of round pointed seed capsules.

rows.readsAs: a strip of pond grass growing out of a shallow trough
rows.defect: The filaments are drawn as coarse arching grass blades with visible taper and dark outlines, not hair-fine cottony threads, and there is not a single gas bubble anywhere in the mat — the buoyancy read that makes it a FLOATING blanket is completely absent. The water is a hard-edged pale rectangle with sharp straight corners and a visible right-hand cut, so the mat sits on a slab rather than in water.
rows.fix: Replace the blade strokes with a dense low-opacity tangle of hair-thin filaments and scatter a dozen pale translucent bubbles trapped inside the mat lifting its top edge, and feather the water band's edges out instead of ending it in a rectangle.

rows.readsAs: a fern frond or a vetch stem — a pinnate leaf ladder, not a flower
rows.defect: The entire identity of a gentian is one huge saturated deep-blue trumpet with a flared five-lobed mouth, larger than the plant that carries it. What is drawn is a tall stem carrying eight symmetric pairs of narrow lance leaflets — a pinnate ladder — topped by five pinhead blue dots about 4% of the image height. There is no trumpet, no flare, no lobed mouth, and the flower is tiny relative to the plant instead of dominant. It is also pixel-for-pixel the same armature as Holy Basil in this batch.
rows.fix: Cut the plant to a low basal tuft of a few broad opposite leaves and put a single upward-facing bell at the top that occupies at least a third of the frame, painted ultramarine, with five visibly separated flaring lobes and a pale throat.

rows.readsAs: a bundled sheaf of dry amber reeds or a besom broom standing on end
rows.defect: The whole plant is a closed bundle of straight tapering strands pinched to a point at the ground — the exact silhouette of a wheat sheaf, and the exact silhouette used for Glasswort in this batch with the hue changed. There is no branching claw holdfast at all (it terminates in a single point), no long bare ropy stipe rising above a crown, and the float bladders are three lone amber pills floating in the middle of the bundle rather than one pear-shaped bladder at the base of every blade. Nothing about it reads as underwater or as seaweed.
rows.fix: Draw one continuous ropy stipe running the full height, hang long wrinkled ribbon blades off it alternately with a fat pear-shaped bladder pinched at each blade's base, and splay a branching claw holdfast gripping rock at the bottom.

rows.readsAs: a single smooth green spearhead or a cypress cone — one leaf, not a plant
rows.defect: All three must-reads are missing simultaneously. There are no joints or articulations: the form is one unbroken cone with faint vertical ribbing, so the 'stacked tiny sausages' that ARE glasswort do not exist. There is no branching whatsoever, let alone opposite candelabra branching — it is a single undivided spike. There is no red flush on any segment; the whole thing is one flat sage green. It is the Giant Kelp bundle recoloured.
rows.fix: Build it from discrete swollen cylindrical segments with a visible constriction between each, fork the stem into two or three opposite candelabra branches, and grade the lower and older segments to crimson.

rows.readsAs: a grapevine — the strongest read in the batch
rows.defect: The bunch fails: it is a small round blob of about a dozen beads, roughly the size of one leaf, tucked against the stem at mid-height rather than a tapering conical cluster hanging free and heavy. There is nothing to read as a crop. The tendrils are drawn as dark closed rings sitting behind the stem, so they read as knotholes or shadow loops rather than as forked coils springing off it.
rows.fix: Enlarge the bunch to two or three times its current size, taper it from a broad shoulder to a point and hang it clear of the stem on a short peduncle, and redraw the tendrils as light-coloured open spirals in front of the stem.

rows.readsAs: a fern or a low sago palm
rows.defect: The fronds are only ONCE-cut — each is a solid green lance with sawtooth notches nicked into its two edges, so the twice-pinnate structure (pinnae themselves divided) is absent and up close it reads as a serrated blade, not a fern leaf. The rosette is a low sideways-spreading fan roughly twice as wide as it is tall, not the upright shuttlecock funnel called for. The brown scaly stalk bases are entirely missing; the crown is uniform green.
rows.fix: Cut each frond into discrete separated pinnae and notch those in turn, tilt the fronds up so the rosette stands taller than it is wide, and darken the bottom third of each stipe to scaly brown.

rows.readsAs: a young cannabis plant, or a stylised conifer
rows.defect: The harvest is missing outright — the top of the plant is just another leaf fan, with no dense green flower or seed heads bunched in the upper leaf joints anywhere on the stem. The leaflets are short, blunt and paddle-like with smooth edges, so the narrow saw-toothed profile is absent, and every fan sits in a rigid opposite pair at a fixed angle, which with the tapering outline makes the whole plant read as a Christmas tree.
rows.fix: Pack tight lime-green bract clusters into the top three leaf joints and at the apex, and lengthen and serrate the leaflets so each fan reads as narrow toothed fingers.

rows.readsAs: a generic purple-leaved herb on a stick
rows.defect: This is the Gentian armature repainted — identical stem, identical eight opposite leaf pairs at identical spacing and angle, identical bead-string flower spike. The leaves are smooth untoothed ovals, so the toothed margin is absent; the stem is a plain round-looking green line with no square section and no hairs; and the flower spike is a single thin column of beads with no tiered whorls stepping out from it. The leaves are fully pink-mauve rather than green with a purple flush, which pushes it away from basil.
rows.fix: Notch the leaf margins, thicken the stem and shade two facets so it reads square, and rebuild the spike as three or four distinct tiers of whorled flowerets separated by bare gaps.

rows.readsAs: a blueberry bush — the exact organism the reference says it must not be
rows.defect: The one feature that separates huckleberry from blueberry is that the berries hang SINGLY in the leaf axils. Here every berry is drawn in a tight terminal cluster of five or six at the top of each cane, which is the blueberry read, inverted from the must-read. The stems are also thick woody brown poles, not sharply angled green twigs, the bush is a dense narrow bundle rather than open and airy, and there are no pink urn-shaped flowers. Zero of the three must-reads are present, and the whole chassis is shared with Juniper Berries.
rows.fix: Delete the terminal clusters and hang single dark berries on short stalks one per leaf axil down the length of the canes, and recolour the canes green with visible sharp angular kinks.

rows.readsAs: a speckled bird's egg or a marble floating in black space
rows.defect: What is drawn is a single smooth pale ellipse, evenly lit from the centre, freckled with gold dots — an object, not a surface condition. There is no ice sheet and therefore no underside to stain: the ellipse floats unattached in the middle of the frame with nothing above or below it. The stringy mucilage strands trailing down into the water, which are half the must-read, do not exist anywhere in the image, and the gold reads as scattered confetti rather than as staining or drips.
rows.fix: Fill the top of the frame with a pale ice ceiling and hang the brown-gold film from its underside as irregular stains and drips, with several long stringy mucus strands trailing down into dark water below.

rows.readsAs: a generic broadleaf tree with pale fruit
rows.defect: The feathery sprays are drawn as stiff straight bristled sticks radiating outward like spokes from the crown centre, several projecting past the foliage into empty space — the opposite of fine drooping twigs, and they read as spines on a green cloud. The fruit is only three small pale clusters, and they sit inside the canopy blur rather than pressed stalkless along a visible branch, so the ridged translucent globe never registers. The trunk is a flat brown rounded rectangle of constant width with no taper, no branching and no bark — the same trunk primitive as Joshua Tree.
rows.fix: Arc the twig sprays downward and let them hang, and line six or eight pale ridged globes directly along two foreground twigs so the fruit sits on wood the viewer can see.

rows.readsAs: a bare forked sapling with four small green sparklers stuck on it
rows.defect: The rosettes are thin sparse asterisks of about ten straight lines, each smaller than the fork it sits on — they read as sparks or starbursts, not as dense bristling pom-poms of stiff daggers, and there is no skirt of dead grey-brown leaves under any of them. The bark is smooth flat brown with a single highlight stripe, so the shaggy grey packed-leaf-base texture that gives a Joshua tree its mass is entirely absent, and the arms are a tidy symmetric Y rather than few contorted upward-crooked limbs. No creamy flower club anywhere.
rows.fix: Triple the rosettes' size and pack them solid with overlapping spine-tipped daggers plus a downward grey skirt of dead leaves, and texture the trunk with dense shaggy grey scale-rows instead of a smooth fill.

rows.readsAs: a sparse twiggy shrub carrying a few blue-grey berries
rows.defect: It is the Huckleberry chassis with the leaf token swapped: the same brown trunk splaying into straight canes, the same terminal berry clusters. The needles are short pale bristles set singly along the canes — there is no whorl of three anywhere, and no white stripe on any needle, so the prickly three-ranked structure that identifies juniper is missing. The bush is thin and see-through rather than dense and scruffy, and the berries lack any dusty pale bloom, reading as flat blue beads.
rows.fix: Replace the single bristles with tight whorls of three stiff needles, each carrying a white stripe down its upper face, and multiply the foliage until the canes are hidden inside a dense conical mass.

rows.readsAs: a woody stem carrying two spiky tan seed pods — closer to a rambutan or a sea urchin than a kiwi
rows.defect: The fuzz is drawn as a halo of long straight spikes radiating off the fruit outline, so the fruit reads as spined rather than as dense soft russet felt. The leaves are plain circles with no heart-shaped basal notch and no point, and the leaf stalks are the same brown as the cane with no red hairy petiole. The cane is a lone free-standing S-curve with nothing to twine around, so the climbing habit never appears, and the two fruit sit singly on opposite sides rather than hanging in twos and threes.
rows.fix: Replace the spike halo with a soft stippled brown fuzz texture inside the fruit silhouette, hang the fruit as a pendant pair from one short stalk, and wrap the cane around a visible post or wire.

rows.readsAs: a generic twiggy garden bush with white blobs on the tips
rows.defect: The identity cue — rusty orange wool on the leaf undersides and young stems — is nowhere on the render; stems are plain mid-brown and every leaf shows only flat dark green. Leaves are flat pointed slivers with no rolled-under edge. The flower clusters are flat white half-discs floating detached above the tips, reading as painted crescents rather than domed heads of florets. Silhouette is the shared shrub fan shared with Lingonberry and Marsh Rosemary.
rows.fix: Repaint the underside of every leaf and the upper stem in rust-orange felt so the fuzz is the first thing seen, and rebuild each white blob as a domed cluster of small round florets seated on the shoot tip.

rows.readsAs: a scallop shell, or a splayed palm fan / firework burst
rows.defect: Wrong organism entirely. The render is a symmetrical spray of ~11 pale rounded rays radiating from a single point at the bottom centre, floating on empty background over an ellipse shadow. There is no rock or bark substrate, no flat crusty rosette, no lobed edge with a chalky pale margin, and no raised cup discs anywhere. It is a radiating fan with a defined foot — exactly the stem-and-frond reading the reference note forbids.
rows.fix: Redraw as a flat irregular crust adhering to a visible rock face: overlapping grey-green lobes with a chalky white rim and a scatter of small raised orange cup discs, with no basal point and no cast shadow.

rows.readsAs: an ornamental red-leaved twig with red berries — a barberry or a young sumac
rows.defect: Every stated must-read is contradicted rather than merely missing. The leaves are large salmon-red simple blades, six of them alternating up a bare dark stem — not mid-green pinnate leaves of 9-17 leaflets. The flowers are replaced by clusters of small orange-red BERRIES pinned along the stem, where the reference calls for upright spikes of pale blue-violet pea flowers. No root, no runner, nothing below ground. The colour alone (red foliage, red fruit) sends a stranger to a berry shrub.
rows.fix: Swap the simple red blades for dull mid-green pinnate leaves with paired oval leaflets and a terminal leaflet, delete the berries, and put a slim upright spike of pale blue-violet pea flowers at the top with a straight yellow root running out below the soil line.

rows.readsAs: a clump of sago-palm or sword fern growing out of the ground
rows.defect: It does read as a fern, but the epiphyte identity is absent: the fronds erupt from a single point on bare ground with a cast ellipse shadow, with no mossy branch or trunk beneath them and no green rhizome creeping through moss. The pinnae are drawn as sharp needle teeth on a stiff midrib rather than blunt-tipped lobes fused along a wing at the stalk, and the green is a flat neon that ignores the yellow-green note.
rows.fix: Anchor the clump onto a horizontal mossy branch running across the frame with a visible green rhizome creeping along it, and reshape the pinnae as blunt rounded lobes joined by a wing down the stalk.

rows.readsAs: a stiff green fern or feather-frond with a small lilac tip
rows.defect: The named harvest is completely missing — there is no root, no runner and no soil line at all, only a stalk that stops at a shadow. The pinnate arrangement is drawn as a mechanically regular double comb of tiny identical leaflets stacked in eleven perfect tiers, which reads as a fern frond or a bottle brush rather than a locust-like legume leaf. The pale blue-lilac spike is present but is a small pixel-scale bead chain crammed at the very top, easy to miss at icon size.
rows.fix: Pull a long straight ropey yellow root with side runners out below the soil line so it occupies the lower third of the frame, and break the leaflet rows into larger irregular oval leaflets with visible gaps.

rows.readsAs: an upright garden shrub with red berry clusters — a coffee or cotoneaster bush
rows.defect: The habit is wrong in the direction that matters: this is a tall upright twig-fan standing on a trunk, when the must-read is a low creeping evergreen mat barely a hand high. Leaves are pointed lance blades spread along the stems, not small thick box-like leathery ovals. The berry clusters sit as flat upward-facing rosettes on the tips rather than nodding under their own weight. It is the identical stem-fan chassis as Labrador Tea with red triplets substituted for white discs.
rows.fix: Flatten the whole plant into a wide low mat with creeping horizontal stems and a squat aspect, shorten the leaves into small rounded leathery ovals, and hang the berry clusters nodding beneath the shoot tips.

rows.readsAs: a water lily floating on a pond
rows.defect: The harvest that names the asset is absent. The render is three flat green pads lying ON the water surface inside a dark pool ellipse with one small pink star flower — no sausage-chain rhizome, no cut cross-section showing the ring of holes, no mud, nothing pulled up at all, despite the reference note explicitly demanding the root chain. The leaves also lie flat like Nymphaea pads instead of being held high above the water on stalks with upturned bowl edges, so even the plant above the waterline reads as the wrong genus.
rows.fix: Put a fat pale sausage-linked rhizome chain in the foreground lifted clear of the mud with one segment cut to show the ring of holes, and raise the round leaves onto tall central stalks with upturned rims.

rows.readsAs: a lollipop tree carrying plums or damsons
rows.defect: The four-lobed green calyx cap — the single feature that separates a mangosteen from any purple stone fruit — is not on any of the four fruits; they are plain unbroken purple spheres. The crown is a soft round fog-blob, not a dense narrow conical crown, and the leaves are small pointed slivers scattered on the blob's rim rather than large thick leathery blades in opposite pairs. The trunk is the same untapered brown pole used for Mangrove, Maple and Marula.
rows.fix: Cap every fruit with a clearly readable four-lobed green star calyx and rebuild the crown as a narrow upright cone of large paired leathery leaves.

rows.readsAs: a generic green shade tree — the batch's default tree with the fruit deleted
rows.defect: The arching stilt roots that ARE the mangrove are entirely absent: the trunk is a single straight brown pole that plunges into flat ground with an ellipse shadow, no water and no root arch anywhere. The propagules are reduced to three or four thin dark slivers hidden inside the crown where they read as shadow gaps rather than long hanging cigar-shaped seedlings, and the leaves are not bunched at branch ends because there are no branches. Strip the fruit off Mangosteen and this is the same picture.
rows.fix: Lift the trunk clear of a water line on a cage of arching stilt roots and hang half a dozen long pale-green pencil propagules below the outer foliage where they break the crown's silhouette.

rows.readsAs: a broadleaf tree with ragged star-shaped leaves
rows.defect: The harvest is missing: there is no spile and no bucket anywhere on the trunk, so nothing on the render says sap. The leaves are ragged many-fingered stars with narrow spiky lobes rather than the classic five-lobed palmate leaf with smooth-sided lobes and deep U notches, so they read closer to hemp than to sugar maple. The crown is the same soft round blob as Mangosteen and Marula, with no visible opposite branching, and the same untapered brown pole for a trunk.
rows.fix: Hang a metal spile and a bucket on the trunk at eye height and redraw the leaf as a clean five-lobed palmate blade with smooth lobe sides.

rows.readsAs: a woody rosemary or heather bush with pink buds
rows.defect: This is drawn as the rosemary the reference note explicitly warns it is not. The render is a woody twig-fan with short grey-green needle leaves along the rods and small pink tulip-shaped buds capping the tips — no flat basal rosette of spoon-shaped leaves, no bare wiry branched stems fanning out level on top, and no dense mist of tiny papery blue-violet florets. The flower colour is pink, not blue-violet, and the whole silhouette is the Labrador Tea / Lingonberry shrub chassis again.
rows.fix: Rebuild it as sea lavender: a flat ground rosette of leathery spoon leaves with bare wiry stems branching up into a level flat-topped spray of a hundred tiny papery blue-violet florets.

rows.readsAs: a lollipop tree hung with oranges or apricots
rows.defect: Two of the three must-reads are absent: the bark is a flat untextured brown pole with no mottled grey flaking, and there is no fallen fruit on the ground — all four yellow fruits are pinned inside the canopy, which is the one place the reference does not put them. The crown is the shared soft round blob rather than a broad spreading crown, though the feathery pinnate leaf sprays are at least a distinct leaf glyph for this family.
rows.fix: Mottle the trunk with grey flaking bark patches and scatter a heap of fallen yellow fruit on the ground under the canopy so the harvest reads from the base of the frame.

rows.readsAs: a squash or gourd vine with one small ribbed fruit
rows.defect: The fruit is far too small and sits up on the vine mid-frame rather than resting heavy on the ground, and its skin is drawn with vertical pumpkin ribs and no netting, so it reads as a mini gourd rather than a netted melon. The leaves are sharply cut star-shaped blades with pointed fingers rather than the rounded shallowly lobed rough leaf of a cucurbit, and they carry no grey hairy texture. Tendrils are present as small dark coils, which is the one must-read that lands.
rows.fix: Enlarge the fruit to sit heavy on the ground at the base of the frame with a tan netted rind, and round off the leaf lobes into broad shallow scallops with a grey hairy surface.

rows.readsAs: a generic ladder-leaf weed stem with a pink speck on top
rows.defect: The warty pod bursting with white silk — the feature everyone knows milkweed by — is not on the render at all. The flower is reduced to one tiny flat pink half-disc perched on the very tip, far too small to read as a drooping domed umbel and not drooping at all. The leaves are paired, but they are small neat identical ovals stacked in a rigid mechanical ladder of nine tiers with no visible pale midrib, so they read as fern or vetch rather than large thick oblong milkweed leaves. Same stem-ladder chassis as Licorice Root.
rows.fix: Add a split warty pod spilling a plume of white silk on the upper stem and enlarge the flower into a nodding dusty-pink ball umbel; widen the leaves and draw a pale midrib down each.

rows.readsAs: a generic leafy stalk with one daisy on top - a wheat ear, or a young sunflower
rows.defect: The circular perfoliate leaf that the stem passes through - the entire identity of this plant - is completely absent. What is drawn is chassis A: a ladder of eleven identical pale-green oval blades up a straight stem, with a single white daisy floating above the top pair. There is no saucer, no basal spade leaves on long stalks, and the flowers are one showy daisy rather than a tiny spray rising out of a disc.
rows.fix: Draw one large flat round disc leaf seen near face-on with the stem visibly piercing its centre, and put a small spray of pinhead white flowers standing up out of that disc; drop the leaf ladder entirely.

rows.readsAs: a dark green bottlebrush or a small conifer with a purple bud at the tip
rows.defect: The hooded flower spike, which is the whole reason this plant has its name, is reduced to three or four tiny flat purple lozenges peeking above the foliage - no helmet, no hood, no spike. The leaves are not deeply palmately cut with narrow toothed segments; they are the standard chassis A blades, blunt and undivided, packed into a dense grey-green column that swallows the stem. Nothing about this says Aconitum.
rows.fix: Make the flower spike the dominant top third of the silhouette - a stiff vertical raceme of six to ten clearly separated blue-purple flowers, each with a rounded helmet hood arching over the lower petals - and cut the leaves into narrow finger-like segments.

rows.readsAs: a twiggy brown berry bush - a hawthorn or a barberry
rows.defect: The must-read is an upright broom of BARE GREEN jointed stems with no foliage at all. What is rendered is the opposite: the main structure is chocolate-brown woody twigs, the green appears only as small scattered leaf slivers pinned along them, and the harvest is drawn as five clusters of glossy RED berries. Papery cones and the swollen nodes with their paper collar of scales are nowhere on the image.
rows.fix: Recolour every stem to yellow-green and make the stems themselves the whole plant - long straight leafless rods with a visible dark banded joint every so often - and replace the red berry pom-poms with small papery tan cones sitting at those joints.

rows.readsAs: a blueberry bush - the right call, if a slightly generic one
rows.defect: The organism reads correctly, but the must-reads are soft. Berries are carried in tight pom-pom clusters of five or six, not singly in the leaf axils, and they are painted flat glossy blue-violet with no dusty pale bloom. The leaves are long lance blades rather than small finely toothed ovals, and there is no trace of the fiery scarlet autumn foliage the row calls for. The armature is the shared chassis B twig-splay, identical to Mountain Cranberry.
rows.fix: Break the berry clusters apart so berries hang singly at leaf joints, and give each a matte pale-blue bloom rim; shorten and round the leaves and tip a few of them red.

rows.readsAs: the same bush as Mountain Blueberry, with the berries repainted red
rows.defect: The row's first must-read is a LOW EVERGREEN CREEPING MAT, wider than tall. The render is a tall upright vase-shaped bush, clearly taller than it is wide, standing on a fat brown trunk stub - the growth form is inverted. Side by side with Mountain Blueberry it is provably the same twig armature and the same leaf stamp with a hue change on the fruit. The leaves are long soft lance blades, not small thick leathery ovals with rolled-under edges and a notched tip, and the berry clusters sit as upright pom-poms rather than nodding at the shoot ends.
rows.fix: Redraw as a ground-hugging mat twice as wide as it is tall with stems running horizontally, tiny stiff glossy dark leaves crowded along them, and small nodding red berry pairs dangling at the tips.

rows.readsAs: a fern frond or a palm leaf with a caterpillar on it
rows.defect: All three must-reads fail. The flowers are a vertical string of white beads running up above the foliage instead of a flat domed corymb - a flat-topped cluster is the diagnostic shape of this plant and there is no flat top anywhere. There is no square branching stem: it is one unbranched central rachis, chassis A again. The pale silvery bracts under the flower heads are absent, and the leaves are wide flat lance blades rather than narrow opposite leaves on a squared stem.
rows.fix: Replace the vertical bead spike with two or three wide flat-topped domes of pinhead white flowers held level at the top of branching stems, and blanch the leaves immediately under each dome to near-white.

rows.readsAs: a cycad or a young palm carrying one gourd
rows.defect: The crown is a rosette of stiff feather-pinnate fronds - exactly a cycad - where papaya needs deeply lobed palmate hands on long stalks. Only ONE fruit is drawn where the row asks for a cluster of small five-angled fruits hugging the stem, and it is a smooth round-shouldered gourd with faint ribs rather than sharply five-angled. The trunk is heavy and clubbed rather than slim and leaf-scarred, and it carries an amputated stub branch on the right that stops in mid-air and reads as a render artefact. That trunk is shared pixel-for-pixel with Nipa Palm Fruit.
rows.fix: Swap the feather fronds for five or six palmate lobed leaves on long stalks, and hang a ring of six small yellow fruits with visible sharp longitudinal ridges directly against the trunk under the crown.

rows.readsAs: a low rosette of round leaves with a red seed spike - a wild ginger or a sorrel, roughly right
rows.defect: The basal mound of rounded fleshy leaves reads well and is one of the few silhouettes in this batch that is not a shared template. But two must-reads miss: the leaf stalks are thin and green, with no sign of the red petioles the row calls out, and the seed head is drawn as the same generic vertical bead string used on Mountain Mint, Mugwort and Nettle - small round beads rather than flat papery winged discs. The leaves are also plain round rather than kidney-shaped with a notch at the base.
rows.fix: Recolour the leaf stalks crimson so they read against the green, and replace the bead string with overlapping flat translucent crimson discs so the seeds look papery and winged.

rows.readsAs: five pink daisies on bare wires - a sparse aster sprig, not a herb mat
rows.defect: The plant has no foliage. The must-read calls for very small paired leaves crowded along creeping wiry stems, and what is drawn is a bare skeletal fan of straight yellow-green lines radiating from a central point with nothing on them - the crowded leaf mat that IS a thyme is absent. The flowers are also wrong in kind: five widely spaced ray daisies with pale pink petals and a dark eye, rather than dense rounded heads of tiny lipped rose-purple flowers. The low wide aspect is the only must-read that lands.
rows.fix: Crowd every stem with pairs of tiny dark grey-green oval leaves until the mat reads as dense foliage, and replace the daisies with tight rounded pompom heads of small purple-pink flowers at the shoot tips.

rows.readsAs: a frost-killed or albino bottlebrush - a dead white plant
rows.defect: The entire plant is rendered chalk-white. The row's headline must-read is a two-tone leaf - dark green ABOVE, white-felted UNDERNEATH, so the plant flickers silver - and painting the whole thing white destroys exactly that read; there is no green anywhere except a sliver of stem at the base. The tall reddish-purple grooved stem is invisible under the foliage column, and the leaves are chassis A blades with sawtooth edges rather than deeply pinnately cut leaves with pointed lobes. It is Monkshood's silhouette with the saturation removed.
rows.fix: Paint the leaf upper surfaces dark green and show white only on the reversed, upturned leaflets, and expose a tall reddish-purple grooved stem running the full height.

rows.readsAs: a tropical tree with feathery leaves and small yellow fruit - close enough to a neem
rows.defect: The crown is not a broad rounded shady canopy; it is a hollow ring of about a dozen isolated pinnate sprays pinned around a soft green glow blob, so it reads sparse and spidery, with the blob doing the work the foliage should do. The leaflets are straight and blunt rather than sickle-curved and toothed, and the loose sprays of small white flowers named in the must-read are entirely absent - only three yellow-green fruits appear. The trunk is a flat brown bar with no taper or bark.
rows.fix: Fill the crown with overlapping drooping pinnate sprays so the canopy silhouette is solid and dome-shaped, curve the leaflets into sickles, and add two or three loose sprays of tiny white flowers.

rows.readsAs: a corn cob, or a green succulent column - certainly not a nettle
rows.defect: The leaves are featureless smooth green ovals overlapping so tightly that they fuse into one solid vertical cylinder with no gaps and no visible stem. Every diagnostic is gone: no heart-shaped base, no coarse teeth, no bristles anywhere, no tiered spacing between leaf pairs, and the drooping stringy green flower tassels in the leaf axils are replaced by a single cream bead spike sticking out of the top. A stranger would not name a plant at all, they would name a vegetable.
rows.fix: Space the leaf pairs into distinct tiers with visible square stem between them, cut a heart-shaped base and coarse saw teeth into every leaf, and hang limp green catkin strings from the leaf joints.

rows.readsAs: the exact same palm tree as Mountain Papaya, with a grey fruit instead of a yellow one
rows.defect: The single defining fact about nipa - NO VISIBLE TRUNK, fronds erupting straight out of the water and mud, with the cannonball fruit head sitting at ground level - is contradicted on every point. The render gives it a tall thick brown trunk that occupies the lower two thirds of the frame, and parks a small grey fruit ball high in the crown notch. Worse, the trunk is identical to Mountain Papaya's down to the same amputated right-hand stub branch, and the frond crown is the same stamp; only the fruit colour differs. There is also no water or mud.
rows.fix: Delete the trunk entirely - spring the huge upright feather fronds directly from a single point at ground level - and set a large spiky brown cannonball fruit cluster on the ground at that point.

rows.readsAs: a thin fern sprig or a single sparse leaf - an almost empty frame
rows.defect: The pods are missing. This asset is named for its pods and the must-read leads with clusters of long bean-like green pods hanging from the stem; not one pod is drawn. There are no waxy flowers either, no aerial roots gripping anything, and no bark or host to climb - the plant floats free on a wire stem. The leaves are small flat dark slivers in a herringbone ladder, the opposite of thick fleshy waxy oblong leaves alternating up a vining stem. It is also the emptiest render in the batch, mostly background.
rows.fix: Hang two or three hand-like bunches of long slender green bean-pods from the stem joints, fatten the leaves into thick waxy oblongs alternating up a climbing stem, and anchor it with pale aerial roots gripping a bark surface.

rows.readsAs: a cream-coloured yucca or flax clump with one thin seed stalk
rows.defect: The huge silver-white feather plume that IS pampas grass is rendered as a 4-bead string about 12px tall on a bare wire - it is smaller than a single leaf blade and reads as a rat-tail, not a plume. Only one stalk, and the foliage is bleached cream-tan rather than the blue-grey green called for, so the clump looks dead.
rows.fix: Replace the bead spike with three or four wide feathery plumes at 2-3x the blade width, each a soft silver-white brush rising a third of the canvas above the clump, and repaint the blades blue-grey green.

rows.readsAs: a young palm or tree fern with a walnut stuck to the trunk
rows.defect: Both identifying must-reads are absent. There is no prop-root cone - the forked brown trunk runs straight into the ground shadow. The crown is a flat rosette of pinnate feather fronds with fine side-barbs, i.e. palm/fern fronds, not long undivided sword straps, and there is no spiral screw arrangement anywhere. The fruit is a small striped acorn-sized ovoid tucked against the trunk instead of a large segmented orange ball hanging below the crown.
rows.fix: Rebuild on a screwpine chassis: undivided strap leaves in three visible spiral tiers around the branch tip, a splayed cone of stilt roots lifting the trunk clear of the ground, and a fruit ball at least a third of the crown width with visible polygonal segments.

rows.readsAs: an ordinary grass tussock with some floating debris
rows.defect: This is the Pampas Herb clump recoloured green. Every must-read is missing: no bare tall triangular stem, no firework starburst of rays at any tip (the arching blades simply taper and end), and no water surface - it sits on the same dry ground shadow as the shrubs. The scattered short yellow-green dashes floating unattached in the middle of the clump are stranded fragments that read as render noise.
rows.fix: Draw bare unbranched stems with no leaves at all, and cap each one with a radial burst of 20+ thin drooping rays, then seat the clump in a water line instead of a ground shadow.

rows.readsAs: a climbing vine with maple-ish leaves and one purple berry
rows.defect: The corona flower with its radiating filament fringe - the single most recognisable feature of a passionflower and a listed must-read - is entirely absent. The leaves are 5-7 lobed and cut like a maple or cannabis leaf rather than deeply three-lobed. The tendrils are present as small coils but they are drawn in near-black at low contrast and vanish against the background.
rows.fix: Add one open corona flower at roughly the size of the fruit, with a visible ring of radiating purple-and-white filaments, and lighten the tendril stroke so the coils read.

rows.readsAs: a hosta clump in a garden bed
rows.defect: Reads as the wrong plant. The leaves are broad rounded ovals with herringbone pinnate veining, overlapping into a low mound pressed to the ground - not thick arrow/heart blades on long upright stalks. There is no water: it sits on the same dry ellipse shadow used by the terrestrial shrubs in this batch, so the emergent-aquatic identity is gone. The blue spike is the shared bead-string stamp on a hair-thin wire, far too slight to read as a dense flower spike.
rows.fix: Lift three or four arrowhead blades on tall separate stalks out of a drawn water line, and thicken the violet spike into a solid dense club standing just above one leaf.

rows.readsAs: a bare acacia or mimosa sapling
rows.defect: The harvest is missing entirely - no pods anywhere, and no yellow red-streaked pea flowers either, so two of three must-reads are absent and the thing the species is named for cannot be seen. The foliage is many-paired pinnate feather sprigs pinned along bare rods, not trifoliate leaves of three lance leaflets. The chassis is the identical splayed brown rod bundle used for Rabbitbrush in this same batch.
rows.fix: Put clusters of flat pods with visible seed bumps on the upper stems plus a few yellow pea flowers, and cut the foliage down to true three-leaflet leaves.

rows.readsAs: a generic lollipop tree with a fuzzy green ball
rows.defect: The broad flat umbrella crown that identifies a stone pine is not there - the crown is a soft round ball, wider than tall by only a hair, sitting on a bare stick. The needles read as loose straight straws fired out of a green fog with no bundling or sheath at the base, and the green fuzz blur swallows most of them. Cones are present but tiny and pinned flat on the fuzz. It is drawn on the same trunk-plus-ball chassis as Pinyon Pine a few rows down, so the two pines are indistinguishable.
rows.fix: Flatten the crown into a wide low parasol with a horizontal underside and a visible gap of reddish trunk beneath it, and draw the needles in discrete tufted bundles instead of a blurred cloud.

rows.readsAs: a pineapple
rows.defect: Named instantly and correctly: diamond-latticed golden fruit, green crown tuft, rosette of arching leaves at the base. Minor - the fruit is oversized against a small rosette and floats clear of it rather than sitting low in the middle as the note asks, and the base leaves are blunt noodles with no spiny margin.
rows.fix: Drop the fruit down so its base is buried in the rosette and enlarge the rosette to match, adding sawtooth edges to the sword leaves.

rows.readsAs: the same generic lollipop tree as Pine Nuts, slightly smaller
rows.defect: This is the Pine Nuts drawing again - same straight bare even-width trunk, same green fuzz ball, same radial straw needles, same two brown cones - which directly contradicts the reference note. The crown is a ball held high on a long clear trunk instead of a low wide bushy mass, the trunk is dead straight rather than crooked, and the needles are long straws rather than short blunt pairs.
rows.fix: Squash the tree: crown down to ground level in an irregular wide dome with several crooked leaders visible through it, trunk short and bent, needles short and stubby in visible pairs.

rows.readsAs: a small agave or fan palm with a seed wand
rows.defect: The leaves are narrow pointed lances in an upright fan, not broad ovals in a flat ground rosette, and each carries a midrib with herringbone side veins instead of the 5-7 strong parallel ribs that are the listed must-read. The rat-tail spike is present but is the same short bead string reused across this batch, too stubby to read as the long slender tail plantain is known for. The fan is bilaterally mirrored, an exact match for Prairie Turnip and Purple Saxifrage.
rows.fix: Widen the leaves into blunt ovals lying almost flat on the ground and draw 5-7 parallel ribs running tip to base, then extend the spike into a long thin green tail.

rows.readsAs: a pale ornamental rosette plant, possibly a cream-leaved hosta
rows.defect: The tap root - the harvest, the food, and the entire reason the species exists in the catalogue - is nowhere in the image; the plant sits on an opaque ground shadow with nothing below it. The five-fingered palmate leaf is also absent: the foliage is a mirrored fan of a dozen broad overlapping cream leaves, the exact Plantain Herb chassis in a paler hue with lavender beads swapped for white. No hairy stems either.
rows.fix: Show the swollen brown spindle root hanging below a cutaway soil line on a thin thread, and rebuild the foliage as a few leaves of five separate narrow leaflets radiating from one point.

rows.readsAs: a fan-palm seedling with one purple flower on a wire
rows.defect: Every must-read is inverted. There is no low cushion or mat - the plant is an upright mirrored fan of ten long straight grey-green blades, the same fan chassis as Plantain Herb and Prairie Turnip. The flower is not stemless resting on the foliage; it is a single tiny star held on a long bare stalk high above everything, the classic error for this species. The tiny paired scale leaves packed along creeping stems are absent, and no rock is present for the cushion to hug.
rows.fix: Replace the fan with a dense low mound of tiny paired scale leaves spilling over a rock, and scatter half a dozen magenta five-petalled flowers sitting directly on the cushion surface with no visible stems.

rows.readsAs: a sparse weedy shrub with five small sunflowers
rows.defect: The flowers are drawn as individual daisies with distinct radiating ray petals and a dark centre disc, which the reference explicitly rules out - rabbitbrush has rayless heads massed into solid flat-topped gold plates. Five isolated blooms on rod tips do not read as a gold-capped broom. The stems are plain brown with no white felt, the crown is a splayed V rather than a rounded broom, and the leaves are lance blobs rather than threads. Same rod-bundle chassis as Pigeon Pea.
rows.fix: Replace the five daisies with two or three dense flat-topped gold cushions of tiny rayless heads capping a rounded stem broom, and pale the stems to white-felted grey.

rows.readsAs: a stacked ladder of small round leaflets - a pea or locust sprig, or a column of coins
rows.defect: The oversized heart-shaped leaves that are the whole identity are absent. Instead a single thin vertical stem carries seven identical pairs of small round leaflets stacked in a rigid ladder, each leaflet a fraction of the canvas and none of them heart-shaped or toothed. There is no haze of stinging hairs on stem or veins, so the second must-read is missing too. The fruit is the same white bead-string stamp used on Pampas and Plantain, stuck on the stem tip rather than clustered in the leaf axils.
rows.fix: Draw two or three enormous toothed heart-shaped leaves filling most of the frame on stout petioles, with a visible fringe of fine pale hairs picked out along the veins and stem.

rows.readsAs: a salmon-orange succulent climber or a string of little starburst flowers
rows.defect: Leaves are orange-salmon starbursts with narrow strap petals - not the big green palmate lobed vine leaf. The harvest, a conical hanging bunch of red-crimson berries, is a single pea-sized pink dot tucked mid-stem, smaller than one leaf. Only the small brown tendril coils are on-reference.
rows.fix: Draw a broad green three- to five-lobed toothed vine leaf and hang a conical crimson bunch at least a leaf-and-a-half tall from a node so the fruit, not the foliage, is the biggest read.

rows.readsAs: five green balloons on red strings
rows.defect: The red stalks fanning from a ground crown are right, but the blades are small smooth round green circles with a single midline. The must-read that IS rhubarb - enormous crinkled puckered heart-shaped blades that are far LARGER than expected - is inverted: the leaves are far smaller than the stalks, so the plant reads as lollipops.
rows.fix: Replace the circles with triangular heart-shaped blades with wavy crinkled margins, sized to roughly triple the stalk length and to overlap each other.

rows.readsAs: a single fern frond, or a green caterpillar
rows.defect: The decussate paired arrangement up a stem is genuinely there, but the leaflets are smooth-edged rounded ovals packed so tightly they fuse into one solid slab and hide the stem, so it reads as one pinnate leaf. No saw teeth, no hairy matt texture, and no drooping green flower tassels at the leaf joints - just one cream spike at the tip.
rows.fix: Space the pairs so the square stem shows between them, cut coarse saw teeth into each blade, and hang a green tassel from three or four of the exposed leaf joints.

rows.readsAs: a conifer sprig hung with baubles
rows.defect: The fat round scarlet hips with a dark crown at the tip read well. The foliage does not: the leaflets are tiny needle-like fronds on herringbone sprigs, reading as yew or fir rather than the wrinkled quilted oval toothed pinnate leaflets. Prickles are rendered as loose white dashes floating off the stems rather than bristles attached to them.
rows.fix: Swap the needle sprigs for five to seven broad oval leaflets with impressed veins and toothed edges, and anchor the prickles onto the cane outline.

rows.readsAs: a bush of pink asters or chrysanthemums
rows.defect: The harvest that defines the species - fat waxy crimson calyces hugging the stem - is completely absent. Instead the render leads with the pale hibiscus-style flower the packet note explicitly says NOT to feature, drawn as five magenta daisies. Foliage is salmon-pink strap starbursts, not green red-veined maple-like lobed leaves.
rows.fix: Put six to eight swollen glossy crimson calyces clasped tight against the upright red stems and cut the daisy flowers back to one, and repaint the leaves green with red veins and three to five maple lobes.

rows.readsAs: an ornamental fountain grass or sedge
rows.defect: Exactly the failure the packet note warns about: the plant is drawn as flat tapering arching blades, when rushes are round smooth leafless pointed stems. There is no brown flower cluster bursting sideways from the stem with the tip continuing past it, so nothing distinguishes it from turf. It is the same tuft drawing as Saltgrass with a different hue.
rows.fix: Redraw as straight round needle-like cylindrical stems with rounded highlights and no taper-to-a-blade, and put a tight brown cluster on the SIDE of two or three stems with the tip carrying on above it.

rows.readsAs: a decorative golden wheat or autumn twig ornament
rows.defect: There is no berry anywhere in the image - the orange-pink thimble fruit that is the whole identity is absent, as are the magenta five-petalled flowers and the shreddy golden bark canes. What is drawn is the generic leaf-ladder chassis: seven pairs of smooth gold almond leaves on one straight stick. The leaves are not trifoliate and not bright green.
rows.fix: Drop to two or three upright canes with trifoliate green leaflets and hang four to six raspberry-textured salmon-orange thimble berries plus one magenta flower.

rows.readsAs: a pale blue ornamental grass tuft
rows.defect: It reads as a grass and the blue-grey colour is right, but it is pixel-for-pixel the Rush Shoots tuft in another hue. None of the three must-reads survive: the blades are long soft arching fountain blades instead of short stiff two-ranked comb-like ones, there are no runners or turf spread, and the compact straw seed head is entirely missing.
rows.fix: Shorten and stiffen the blades into opposed two-ranked combs along low horizontal runners, and top two culms with a compact pale straw spikelet head.

rows.readsAs: a single closed flower bud, or an ear of corn in its husk
rows.defect: The render is one sealed vertical spindle of parallel ribs coming to a point. There is no clump, no branching, no stout finger-lobed succulent leaf segments and no flat-topped yellow-green umbel - all three must-reads are absent. Nothing identifies it as a plant of the carrot family or as a coastal succulent.
rows.fix: Break it into a low bushy clump of several stems ending in fat blunt blue-green finger segments, and cap two stems with flat yellow-green umbels.

rows.readsAs: a hosta or wild-ginger clump
rows.defect: The sprawling low cushion silhouette is right, but the scale is inverted: the blades are four enormous overlapping round discs, not small fleshy heart-to-kidney-shaped stalked leaflets, so the plant reads as a big-leafed shade perennial. The white flowers are one tiny fan-shaped smear on a bare stalk, too small and too few to read as clusters of four-petalled crosses.
rows.fix: Replace the four giant discs with twelve to fifteen small stalked heart-shaped leaves and enlarge the flower head into two or three clusters of visible white four-petalled crosses.

rows.readsAs: a generic flat leaf rosette - agave or a young dandelion crown
rows.defect: The sprawling basal rosette is correct in form, but the blades are matte mid-green pointed lances with straight edges instead of thick glossy dark triangular blades with wavy margins, there is no red-purple stalk or veining anywhere, and the long trailing wiry ropes of green flower spikes - the harvest - are completely missing.
rows.fix: Repaint the blades very dark and glossy with wavy triangular outlines and red stalks, and trail two or three knobbly green flower spikes outward past the rosette edge.

rows.readsAs: a woody shrub topped with orange pom-poms - goldenrod or yarrow
rows.defect: The narrow silvery-grey willow leaves are on-reference and are the strongest read. The berries are wrong in placement: they sit as five round pom-pom clusters perched on the TIPS of the canes like flower heads, when the must-read is orange berries packed tight directly along the length of the twig. No sharp woody thorns are visible.
rows.fix: Move the orange berries off the tips and pack them as dense beads along the middle third of two or three branches, and add a few sharp side thorns.

rows.readsAs: a bottlebrush plant or a fine feathery true-fennel stalk
rows.defect: This is precisely what the packet note forbids. The foliage is fine hair-like herringbone threads packed into a tall dense column, when rock samphire must show a few thick blunt cylindrical fleshy finger segments in a LOW bushy clump. The umbel is a single yellow smear the width of the stem, far too small to read as a flat-topped umbrella.
rows.fix: Cut it to a low spreading clump of a few stems ending in fat glaucous blunt fingers and widen the yellow-green umbel to two or three times the stem width.

rows.readsAs: a bunch of spring onions or a clump of eelgrass
rows.defect: The render is an upright bundle of long green straps - a blade or frond, which the reference says must not exist at all. The identity, upright shoots crowded with tiny stalked glassy spheres, is reduced to three isolated green pill-shaped blobs floating on the straps, and there is no horizontal creeping runner joining the shoots.
rows.fix: Replace the straps with two or three upright stalks completely encrusted in dozens of tiny translucent green beads, joined at the base by a visible horizontal runner.

rows.readsAs: an agave or aloe rosette
rows.defect: The identity must-read is huge thick wavy-CRINKLED cabbage-sized ovate leaves; what is drawn is eleven smooth, narrow, sharply pointed spear leaves in a flat symmetrical radial fan with no undulation, no lobing and no crinkle anywhere on any margin. The white flower froth is a single ~18px dome cap on a bare hairline wire punching straight up through the centre, which reads as a pin, not a broad froth held above the leaves.
rows.fix: Redraw the leaves as wide ovate paddles with a deeply undulating scalloped outline and buckled surface (wave the silhouette in and out 5-6 times per leaf edge), and replace the pin-dome with a wide low mound of many tiny white four-petal dots spread across at least half the image width.

rows.readsAs: a generic fern sprig with a mauve pin on top
rows.defect: All three must-reads are absent and one is actively contradicted. The reference demands wiry branching flower stems with NO leaves on them — the render puts a full ladder of nine leaflets up the entire stem. There is no basal rosette of leathery spoon leaves at ground level at all. The wide airy branched flat-topped spray is a single unbranched ~20px mauve dome cap sitting on the stem tip, which is exactly the spike silhouette the packet note explicitly warns against.
rows.fix: Strip every leaf off the vertical stems, split the stem into 4-6 wiry diverging branches in the upper third, and spread the violet flowers as a broad flat-topped haze of tiny dots across that branch network, with a low flat rosette of spoon leaves at the base.

rows.readsAs: a single opaque olive leaf blade, or a paper bag
rows.defect: Sea lettuce IS its ruffle — and there is not one ruffle in the image. Both long margins are perfectly straight lines and the top edge is a dead-flat horizontal cut that runs to the frame, so the sheet reads as clipped rather than terminated. The colour is a dull opaque olive-yellow with no translucency or glow, so the 'vivid translucent grass-green' read is gone too; only the tiny disc holdfast is correct.
rows.fix: Give both margins and the top edge a heavy high-frequency frilled wave (overlapping lobes folding back on themselves), and drop the fill to a bright translucent green with visible overlap-darkening where sheets cross.

rows.readsAs: a broken render — a succulent rosette with a flower floating detached in the sky above it
rows.defect: The pink star flower is stranded in empty space roughly 80px above the plant with no stem, pedicel or contact of any kind between them; it reads as a stray sprite, not a flower in a leaf axil. Beneath it the plant is an upright bouquet of five fat rounded pale paddles, not a low mat sprawling flat and rooting at the nodes; there are no opposite pairs, no visible red-purple stems, and no narrow leaves.
rows.fix: Attach the flower to the plant — tuck it into an actual leaf axil against a stem — and rebuild the body as a horizontal sprawling mat of reddish stems running out sideways with plump narrow leaves in opposite pairs along them.

rows.readsAs: a fern frond with one mauve daisy stuck on the end
rows.defect: This is the Sea Lavender image with a daisy swapped for the dome. Every must-read fails: the stem is ramrod-straight and unbranched, not sprawling and zigzag; the leaves are smooth pointed lances with entire margins, not thick pinnately lobed fleshy leaves with rounded lobes; there is one radial many-rayed daisy where the reference needs four-petalled cross-shaped flowers; and the fat two-jointed corky seed pods, which are half the identity, are nowhere in the image.
rows.fix: Kink the stem into a visible zigzag with alternating side branches sprawling low and wide, cut deep rounded lobes into each fleshy leaf, and hang several fat two-segment corky pods off the upper stem next to four-petalled lilac crosses.

rows.readsAs: a multi-stemmed berry shrub
rows.defect: The overall read is right — slim multi-stemmed upright trunks, small oval leaves, purple berry clusters at the shoot tips — and it is the only asset in the batch with its own structure. But the trunks are warm orange-brown rather than slim grey; the berries are plain spheres with no five-pointed starry crown scar at the tip; and the narrow strap-petalled white flowers are entirely absent, so two of the three must-reads are unreadable at this size.
rows.fix: Recolour the stems to pale silver-grey, punch a small dark five-point star scar into the top of each berry, and add a few sprays of narrow white strap petals among the upper shoots.

rows.readsAs: a small plain fern sprig — no identifiable crop
rows.defect: The entire harvest is missing. There are no ribbed upright oblong seed capsules held against the stem, and no tubular white-pink foxglove-like flowers in the leaf axils — that is two of three must-reads, and both are the identity of the plant. What remains is the shared ladder stamp shrunk to about 40% of the frame: a bare straight stem with nine plain lance leaflets and absolutely nothing else, floating small in a large empty field.
rows.fix: Line the upper two-thirds of the stem with upright ribbed oblong capsules pressed tight against it, add pale tubular bell flowers hanging in the axils below them, and scale the plant up to fill the frame.

rows.readsAs: a dense upright fern or bottlebrush with three white specks above it
rows.defect: Solomon's seal is defined by an ARCH with flowers dangling in a row underneath it, and this stem is bolt upright and dead straight with no curve whatsoever. The flowers are not dangling and not in a row along the underside — three tiny white bells sit clustered ABOVE the topmost leaves, on top of the plant, which is the opposite of the reference. The leaves are also dense overlapping lances stacked in a tight column rather than broad ribbed ovals held out flat on one plane, and there are no parallel veins.
rows.fix: Bend the stem into a strong single arch leaning to one side, hang paired green-white bells on short pedicels beneath the stem at every leaf node, and widen the leaves into flat ribbed ovals with visible parallel veins.

rows.readsAs: a green rosette weed with a rust-red seed spike
rows.defect: Two must-reads land: the basal clump habit is clear and the rusty-red seed spire stands well above the leaves on a slim stem. The third and most diagnostic one does not — the arrowhead leaf with two backward-pointing basal lobes is absent. Every leaf is a plain smooth-sided pointed spear with no lobes at all, so this is the same radial fan stamp used for Sea Kale, recoloured green.
rows.fix: Cut two backswept basal lobes into the base of every leaf so the arrowhead outline is unmistakable at thumbnail size, and put each leaf on its own visible petiole rather than fanning them from one point.

rows.readsAs: a broadleaf lollipop tree with rust stains on it
rows.defect: This is not a conifer. The crown is a soft round cloud-blob on a straight brown popsicle trunk — the classic deciduous lollipop — with no narrow spire shape and no tiers of stiff branches anywhere, which is the first must-read. The cones point UPWARD, directly contradicting the packet note that spruce cones hang downward. The needles are a scatter of loose pale sticks floating over the blob rather than dense four-sided needles set on twigs, and there is no contrast between vivid light-green new tips and dark old growth — the whole crown is one flat green haze.
rows.fix: Rebuild the silhouette as a tall narrow triangular spire with distinct downward-sloping branch tiers, hang the cylindrical cones point-down from the branch undersides, and paint the outer branch ends a vivid pale green against a much darker interior.

rows.readsAs: a generic cartoon shade tree
rows.defect: The packet says the star fruit shape is the whole identity, and there is no star anywhere in the image. The fruits are drawn as small dark elongated slivers scattered through the crown that read as dead twigs or insect bodies, not as hard brown eight-armed woody stars. The many-petalled greenish-pink flowers are also absent. The tree is the identical lollipop stamp used for Spruce Tips — same brown popsicle trunk with a rounded tip, same round green cloud crown — with leaf tokens instead of needle tokens.
rows.fix: Draw two or three large eight-pointed woody stars in front of the crown at a size the eye cannot miss, each arm a boat-shaped follicle split to show a glossy seed, and swap the leaf tokens for broad glossy untoothed ellipses clustered at branch ends.

rows.readsAs: a fern or horsetail stem with three red berries at the tip
rows.defect: Nothing about this reads as a bulb plant, let alone a tulip. There is no cup flower — the harvest is three tiny separate red blobs clustered on the stem tip, which read as berries. The reference calls for 2-4 broad channelled grey-green strap leaves hugging a low stem, but the render is the shared ladder stamp with eighteen small pale chevron leaflets running the full height of a tall straight stem. The plant is also drawn tall and erect where the must-read is short stature with the flower close to the ground.
rows.fix: Delete the leaf ladder entirely, replace it with two or three broad wavy grey-green strap leaves rising from the base, shorten the stem, and put a single large pointed-petal red cup flower on the bare tip.

rows.readsAs: a small clump of dry golden grass or a shaving brush
rows.defect: The must-read is explicit that the blade is ONE unbranched ribbon that is NEVER split into fingers — and the render is split into roughly six separate narrow straps that fan apart at the top, exactly the forbidden reading. The margins are straight with no crinkled frilly waving on either edge. Three flat yellow lozenges sit on the surface as unexplained blobs. At aspect 0.25 this should be a long trailing belt, but it is drawn as a short stubby tuft occupying the middle sixth of the frame.
rows.fix: Merge the straps into one continuous wide ribbon blade running the full height of the frame, ruffle both long margins with deep waves, and give it a dimpled central band above a short stipe on a small branching holdfast.

rows.readsAs: a lavender or salvia stem
rows.defect: It reads as a purple-flowered aromatic herb, which is roughly right, but all three must-reads fail on inspection. The stem is a plain round cylinder with no square-section shading or edge, so the square stem is invisible. The leaves are smooth-margined lances staggered up the stem rather than toothed ovals in opposite pairs crossed at each node. The flowers form one terminal spike at the very tip — the lavender silhouette — instead of ring-like whorls clustered at the leaf axils down the stem.
rows.fix: Move the flowers off the tip into several distinct ring-shaped whorls encircling the stem at the leaf nodes, pair the leaves opposite at each node with visible teeth on the margins, and shade the stem with a flat face and a hard edge so it reads square.

rows.readsAs: a generic grass or lily-turf tuft with a stray seed spike
rows.defect: The spadix does exactly what the note forbids: it is a thin vertical beaded catkin rising from the very TIP of the clump, not a stubby green finger angled out sideways partway up. There is no flat stem to angle off, the blades arch outward and droop instead of standing as an upright sword fan, and there is no crimped wavy margin anywhere - the blades are smooth-edged strips.
rows.fix: Draw one flat upright sword-shaped scape and hang a short fat green finger off its side at about 60% height, angled 40 degrees out, then crimp the blade edges with a shallow wave.

rows.readsAs: a bundle of dead brown sticks with pink beads glued on - a besom broom
rows.defect: There is no foliage at all. The twigs are rigid straight pale-grey pins stuck at angles into bare brown poles; nothing is feathery, nothing is scale-clad, nothing arches. The pink is six small beaded caterpillars at the stem tips, not clouds of fine plumes, so the silhouette is stiff and skeletal where tamarisk's whole identity is a soft blue-grey haze.
rows.fix: Replace the straight pin-twigs with dense drooping fronds of fine blue-grey scale foliage so the outline is a soft cloud, then bury airy pink plume masses inside that cloud rather than perching beads on bare tips.

rows.readsAs: a small bunch of cut daisies in a vase
rows.defect: Same splayed bare-stem vase as Tamarisk and Tea Tree. It is not a dense twiggy rounded bush - it is five open brown stalks with a handful of small smooth green ovals scattered on them, and the outline is a V, not a dome. The leaves have no serration and no gloss, and there are no pale new bud-and-two-leaves shoots, which is the actual harvest. The flowers are flat forward-facing daisy discs, not nodding cups with a boss of stamens.
rows.fix: Fill the silhouette into a solid rounded dome of overlapping serrated glossy leaves with pale yellow-green shoot tips, and redraw the flowers as small nodding white cups seen from below with a yellow stamen boss.

rows.readsAs: the Tamarisk drawing recoloured, topped with the Tea flower sprite
rows.defect: All three must-reads are absent. The trunk is a plain smooth brown cone with no papery white bark and no peeling sheets. The foliage is the same straight pale pin-twigs as Tamarisk, hard and spiky, not fine soft needles that read feathery in mass. The flowers are the identical white disc-daisies used on Tea, where tea tree's signature is a fluffy creamy bottlebrush spike wrapped around the twig.
rows.fix: Give it a white papery trunk with dark peel-curls, mass the twigs with fine soft needle foliage, and replace every daisy with a cylindrical fluffy white bottlebrush spike encircling a twig.

rows.readsAs: a tobacco plant - big leaves stepping up a stout stalk under a head of pink trumpets
rows.defect: All three must-reads are visibly present: huge ovate leaves clasping and stepping up one thick unbranched stem and shrinking toward the top, a terminal cluster of long pink trumpet flowers with flared mouths, and fine hair spikes bristling from the stem and leaf edges for the sticky texture. The only real miss is colour - the leaves are dark forest green where the reference calls for a pale matt yellow-green, which costs some of the sticky, sun-faded tobacco look.
rows.fix: Lift the leaf colour to a pale matt yellow-green and knock the specular gloss off the blades.

rows.readsAs: a sago palm or cycad rosette sitting flat on the ground
rows.defect: The tree is missing from the tree fern.
