There is no fibrous brown trunk of matted old frond bases - the crown springs straight out of the soil, which is the one structure that separates a tree fern from bracken. The fronds are only once-divided with coarse triangular saw-tooth pinnae, so they read stiff and cycad-like rather than huge and lacy, and the crozier is a single tiny spiral tucked at the crown edge where it should be the readable harvest. The whole crown is also slumped left, leaving the right half of the frame empty.
rows.fix: Stand the crown on a tall shaggy brown fibrous trunk, split the pinnae a second time so the fronds read lacy, and enlarge the coiled croziers into two or three obvious brown-scaled spirals at the centre of the crown.

rows.readsAs: a generic lollipop cherry tree
rows.defect: None of the three must-reads survive. The trunk is a tall straight bare pole running half the image height with no branching into thick limbs - the reference calls for a short brittle trunk splitting low into a few heavy limbs. The canopy is a ball of small round blobs, not big soft heart-shaped leaves. The fruit are tiny clustered red spheres tucked inside the foliage, where tamarillo fruit are large smooth egg-shaped red-orange bodies hanging clear on long stalks below the leaves.
rows.fix: Shorten the trunk to about a quarter of the height, split it into three thick limbs, enlarge the leaves into broad heart shapes, and hang four or five big egg-shaped orange-red fruit on long visible stalks below the canopy edge.

rows.readsAs: a dried ornamental grass tuft
rows.defect: The fountain of arching blades is there and reads correctly, but two of the three must-reads are missing. There is no dense pedestal mound of old dead thatch at the base - the blades converge to a bare narrow point on the soil. And there are no seed panicles at all, which is the harvest: nothing stands clear above the leaf fountain. The whole plant is also uniformly straw-gold with no mid-green above the thatch, so it reads dead rather than living.
rows.fix: Build a fat tan mound of packed dead leaf bases under the fountain, make the upper two thirds of the blades mid-green against it, and raise four or five thin feathery seed panicles well clear of the blade tips.

rows.readsAs: a jasmine or star-flower vine twining on nothing
rows.defect: This is the Water Spinach drawing with a different flower sprite. The stem is a thin wiry green line freestanding in space - not a thick green rope-like succulent stem, and there is not a single aerial root, nothing gripping bark, no host at all. The leaves are small narrow lance blades, not the thick flat fleshy oblongs that make vanilla recognisable. The flowers are symmetrical six-point cream stars with no lip and no orchid asymmetry, and the hanging cluster of long slender green pods - the entire harvest - is absent.
rows.fix: Thicken the stem into a fleshy green rope running up a bark-textured trunk with white aerial roots clasping it, fatten the leaves into broad flat oblongs, and hang a bundle of long slender green pods from one node.

rows.readsAs: a bunch of celery or leeks standing upright
rows.defect: There is no blade anywhere in the image. It is the same splayed vase of straight tapering stalks used for Tamarisk and Tea Tree, recoloured olive - narrow tubular stems pinched at the base and fanning upward. The deeply lobed wings flanking a distinct midrib are entirely absent, and so is the ruffled convoluted sporophyll frill at the base of the stipe, which is the other half of the harvest. Nothing about the silhouette reads feather-like, fan-like, or underwater.
rows.fix: Replace the stalk bundle with one broad olive-brown blade split into wide wing lobes either side of a pale midrib, and bunch a tight ruffled frill of convoluted tissue around the base of the stipe.

rows.readsAs: a young conifer sapling with a mushroom stuck on top
rows.defect: The leaves are the same tiny sprig sprite stamped in perfectly regular ranks up a dead-straight stem, producing a narrow rigid column - a bottlebrush or a spruce, not a twice-pinnate umbellifer with narrow sharply toothed leaflets. The umbel is a single small featureless white dome the size of a thumbnail with no visible florets and no rays, so it reads as a mushroom cap rather than a flat-domed compound umbel of many small flowers. The hollow purple-streaked stem, the one field mark the reference singles out as the difference between this and parsley, is a plain green line.
rows.fix: Widen the umbel into a broad flat dome of many small white florets on visible radiating rays, break the leaf ranks into irregular twice-pinnate sprays with toothed leaflets, and blotch the thick stem with purple streaks.

rows.readsAs: a small aster or michaelmas daisy on a stalk
rows.defect: The identity of water mint is the single round lilac pompom head at the stem tip, and it is not here: instead there are three flat lilac disc-daisies with separate radiating petals, reused from the Tea and Tea Tree sprite, scattered down the upper stem rather than one at the tip. The leaves are opposite, which is right, but they are smooth-edged narrow willow lances with no teeth and no purple-bronze flush, and the stem is a thin round green line with no square section or edge shading.
rows.fix: Replace all three daisies with one dense spherical lilac pompom of many tiny tubular florets sitting on the very tip, broaden the leaves into toothed ovals flushed purple, and shade the stem as a square with two visible faces.

rows.readsAs: a generic climbing vine with white buds - the Vanilla Orchid drawing recoloured
rows.defect: Identical S-curve chassis and tendril curls to Vanilla Orchid. It is drawn as a tall upright climber when the reference and the 2.2 aspect both call for hollow stems trailing horizontally on water and rooting at the joints - there is no water, no float, no joint roots. The leaves are plain narrow lances with no arrowhead or heart-shaped base at all. The flowers are small white teardrop buds seen edge-on, never opening into a funnel face, so the purple throat that identifies the morning-glory family is nowhere.
rows.fix: Lay the stem out horizontally as a fat hollow trailing runner with root tufts at the nodes, give every leaf a clear arrowhead base with two backward lobes, and open two flowers into face-on white funnels with a dark purple throat.

rows.readsAs: a watermelon on a trailing vine
rows.defect: The melon and the ground-trailing runner both read, which is why this clears FAIL, but three details are off. The dark stripes cover only the right third of the fruit and the left side is left plain, so the melon looks half-finished. The leaves are narrow finger-lobed palmate hands that read as cannabis rather than deeply cut lobes with ROUNDED tips and wavy edges, and they are bright green instead of dull hairy grey-green. There is only one tendril and it is unbranched.
rows.fix: Wrap the stripe bands right around the melon so both sides carry them, round off and crimp the leaf lobes into wavy-edged rounded fingers in dull grey-green, and add a second branched tendril at the far node.

rows.readsAs: a generic lobed-leaf vine carrying one small white cauliflower-like blossom
rows.defect: The tendrils and star-lobed vine leaves do carry a grape read, but the harvest is a single small chalk-WHITE globular cluster hung at one node — not a tapering bunch, and the reference note explicitly says white grapes are green to gold and never actually white. The stem is the identical S-curve used for Wild Melon, so the vine carries no woody gnarl.
rows.fix: Replace the white ball with a proper tapering conical bunch of overlapping translucent amber-green berries, hung from a short stalk below a leaf, and give this vine a woodier stem than the melon runner.

rows.readsAs: an upright bundle of brown broom-twigs with blue berries — a tall bush, not a blueberry mat
rows.defect: The first must-read is a low sprawling twiggy mat well under knee height, and the note says explicitly 'a ground-hugging mat, not an upright bush'. What is rendered is the opposite: five straight vertical brown canes fused into a wedge base, standing tall and narrow. It is also the same broom-shrub chassis as Wild Chili and Wild Guava with only the berry hue changed.
rows.fix: Redraw as a wide low mat — stems shorter than they are wide, arching outward and downward from a creeping base, so the silhouette is broader than tall.

rows.readsAs: a generic cartoon apple tree
rows.defect: All three must-reads are absent: the trunk is a plain flat brown stick with no shiny red-brown bark and no horizontal lenticel banding; there is no white blossom anywhere; and the fruits are four large red spheres embedded in the crown blob with no stalks at all, let alone the long stalks and stalked clusters that make a cherry. Crown leaves are spiky slivers rather than oval toothed leaves. Identical trunk-and-blob chassis to Wild Fig and Wild Mango.
rows.fix: Give the trunk banded coppery bark with horizontal lenticel lines and hang the cherries in pairs and threes on visibly long thin stalks below the branches.

rows.readsAs: a red-berry twig bush; chili is a plausible but not confident guess
rows.defect: The upward-pointing pea-sized scarlet fruits are the one must-read that lands. The small white star flowers are entirely absent, and the 'scrambling wiry MANY-BRANCHED bush' is instead the shared broom chassis — five straight unbranched canes radiating from a fused base, with no secondary branching and no scramble. Leaves are thin slivers rather than smooth pointed ovals.
rows.fix: Add white five-point star flowers among the fruit and break each cane into two or three zigzag side branches so the bush reads as scrambling rather than as a bundle of straight rods.

rows.readsAs: a pale agave or spider-plant tuft with a single purple daisy stuck above it
rows.defect: Both identity must-reads are wrong. The blades are wide FLAT arching straps with a visible midrib highlight — they read as flat ribbons, not as hollow tubes round in section. The flower head is a flat open daisy with about ten separate petals around a pale eye, not a tight spherical lilac pompom. Same grass-fountain chassis as Wild Garlic and Wild Onion, distinguished only by tint.
rows.fix: Draw the leaves as narrow cylinders with a rounded highlight running down each tube, and replace the daisy with a dense spherical pompom of many tiny florets on a bare hollow stalk.

rows.readsAs: a cartoon plum tree
rows.defect: Every must-read is missing. The trunk is the same narrow flat brown stick as Wild Cherry and Wild Mango — no buttressing, no pale fused root lattice, no hanging aerial roots anywhere. The crown is a small soft blob, not a massive spreading canopy. The three dark purple figs sit in the leaf canopy at the crown edge, which is precisely where the note says they must NOT be: figs must stud the bark of the trunk and limbs.
rows.fix: Widen the crown well past the trunk, redraw the trunk as a pale buttressed lattice of fused roots with root strands dropping from the limbs, and move the figs onto the trunk and bare limb wood.

rows.readsAs: a clump of ornamental grass with a small white pill floating above it
rows.defect: The leaves are narrow grassy straps — exactly the chive/onion leaf the reference note explicitly rules out ('broad flat leaves, NOT the narrow tubular leaves of chives or onion'), and the render is the same fountain of blades as Wild Onion in the same pose. The flower is a featureless smooth white lozenge with no florets at all, where the must-read is a starburst umbel of separate white star flowers on a three-angled stalk.
rows.fix: Replace the grass blades with a few broad lance-elliptic lily-like blades rising straight from the soil, and rebuild the flower head as a loose starburst of individually drawn six-point white stars.

rows.readsAs: a hosta or cabbage rosette with a small pink flower spike
rows.defect: The identity must-read is inverted. The flower is meant to be a single dark maroon three-lobed cup sitting ON THE SOIL, hidden beneath the foliage; here a bare stalk shoots straight up well ABOVE the leaves carrying a spike of several small pink buds. The leaves are a stack of large overlapping plain ovals with no kidney notch and no visible hairy stalks, so they read as cabbage or hosta rather than paired heart-kidney leaves.
rows.fix: Delete the tall stalk and tuck one dark maroon three-lobed cup flower at ground level in the notch between two leaves, and cut the leaves into clearly paired kidney shapes with a deep basal cleft on short hairy petioles.

rows.readsAs: a small berry bush with glowing pale-green fruit — not a tree at all
rows.defect: The form is specified as a tree and every must-read is bark- or leaf-specific, yet this is drawn on the same broom-shrub chassis as Wild Blueberry and Wild Chili: a fused brown wedge base, straight unbranched canes, tiny paired slivers for leaves. There is therefore no trunk to carry the smooth mottled flaking copper-and-grey bark. The leaves show no quilted impressed parallel veining, and the fruits are plain glowing spheres with no dried calyx crown at the tip.
rows.fix: Rebuild as a small tree with a real trunk showing patchy copper-over-grey flaking bark, opposite oblong leaves with strongly ruled parallel side veins, and a five-point dried calyx crown drawn on the end of each fruit.

rows.readsAs: an orange tree
rows.defect: The four fruits are round bright-orange spheres bedded directly into the crown blob with no stalk showing, so the must-read 'fruit dangling on long stalks' is absent and the fruit colour and shape push the read straight to citrus. The crown is a small pale-centred blob on the same flat stick trunk as Wild Cherry and Wild Fig, not the tall dense dark crown called for, and there is no droop or whorling in the leaf sprigs.
rows.fix: Hang the fruits well below the foliage on long visible pendulous stalks and make them green-yellow ovoids, then narrow and darken the crown with drooping whorls of long lance leaves.

rows.readsAs: a vine bearing one small striped green globe — melon is readable
rows.defect: The striped globe fruit and the coiled tendrils land. But the plant is the identical S-curve vine used for White Grape — same stem sweep, same star-lobed leaves at the same nodes, same tendril rings — floating upright in the frame, so the must-read 'ground-running vine' is contradicted: there is no ground line, no sprawl, no runner. The leaves are smooth and pale rather than grey-green, deeply cut and bristly, and only ONE fruit sits at the same node the grape's bunch occupies.
rows.fix: Lay the stem along a horizontal ground plane so it runs and sprawls, and roughen the leaves into deeply cut bristly grey-green lobes distinct from the grape leaf.

rows.readsAs: lavender, or a generic herb spike
rows.defect: The opposite leaf pairs are there, but the two distinguishing must-reads are not. The stem is a thin round line with no square section or hairiness shown, and the flowers form a single dense lilac spike at the very TIP — exactly the arrangement the must-read rules out ('flowers in rings around the stem, not just at the tip'). The leaves are smooth-edged with no teeth.
rows.fix: Thicken the stem into a visibly four-sided column and move most of the flowers into two or three separate ball-like whorls encircling the stem at lower leaf axils.

rows.readsAs: a spiky green column — a cactus, a bottlebrush, or a cannabis cola
rows.defect: The plant is a solid dense vertical cylinder of overlapping spiky leaves with no open stem visible, capped by a small smeared yellow crescent. None of the three must-reads survive: there is no four-petalled cross flower (just an undifferentiated yellow blob), there are no slim beaked seed pods held out from the stem anywhere, and consequently no flowers-at-tip-with-pods-forming-below progression. The lower lobed leaves with a big end lobe are absent too.
rows.fix: Open the silhouette into a slim branched stem, draw four or five individual yellow flowers each with four petals in a clear cross at the tip, and add a ladder of slender upward-angled pods with pointed beaks below them.

rows.readsAs: a clump of ornamental grass with a white pill above it — indistinguishable from this batch's Wild Garlic
rows.defect: This is the Wild Garlic render again: same fountain of arching blades, same bare stalk, same smooth white lozenge, only a slightly different green. The must-read ball of tiny flowers is a featureless flattened disc with no individual florets, and the papery membrane bursting under the head is absent. Nothing marks it as an onion rather than any grass, and nothing separates it from the garlic beside it.
rows.fix: Rebuild the head as a true sphere of many small individually drawn pink-white star flowers with a split papery spathe hanging beneath it, and show a swollen bulb with a papery neck at the base of the tuft.

rows.readsAs: a single serrated maple-ish leaf with a pink bottlebrush on a wire
rows.defect: The identity of rhubarb IS the stout red-flushed ribbed stalks and the huge puckered wavy-margined basal leaves; there are no stalks at all in this image - the leaf blades spring straight off the baseline with nothing beneath them, the blades are sharply saw-toothed rather than crinkled and wavy, and there is not a trace of red anywhere on the plant. The 'flower' is a thin pink bead spike, not a foamy cream panicle. It is the same drawing as Wood Sorrel in a darker green.
rows.fix: Rebuild it as three or four separate leaves, each on its own thick red-to-green ribbed petiole of visible width (at least 6-8 px) rising from a ground-level crown, and give the blade a wavy puckered margin instead of saw teeth.

rows.readsAs: a tufted grass with a small seed head
rows.defect: The tufted arching blade clump and the blue-grey tint are right and it does read as a grass. The seed spike fails though: the awns exist only as a small yellow fan at the very apex, so the whisker read that separates rye from every other grass is missing along the length of the spike, and the spike itself is short and thin enough that it nearly disappears against the foliage.
rows.fix: Run long straight awns out of every spikelet down the whole length of the spike, angled up and outward, and lengthen the spike so it stands clear above the blade tips.

rows.readsAs: a fern frond or a vetch sprig
rows.defect: Every must-read is absent. The leaves are tiny narrow lance-shaped slivers in a symmetrical ladder, not big paired broad ovals with coarse teeth and a crinkled surface; the stem is a plain round thread with no square section or corner shading; there are no one-sided spikes of seed capsules anywhere. The mauve-grey leaf colour reads dead rather than purple-backed. This is the identical stem-and-leaflet-ladder template used for Wormwood.
rows.fix: Replace the leaflet ladder with three or four widely spaced pairs of large toothed ovals with quilted veining, and add a slim one-sided spike of round capsules at the top.

rows.readsAs: a wild strawberry, unprompted
rows.defect: Named instantly: the red berry carries visible pale seeds sitting proud on the surface, two white five-petal flowers with yellow centres flank it, and a thin red runner strikes out sideways to a plantlet node. The one weakness is the leaf - the leaflets are smooth-edged pointed ovals, so the coarse teeth and sunken veins of the trifoliate leaf never appear, and they do not group visibly into threes.
rows.fix: Add coarse saw teeth and sunken midrib veining to the leaflets and group them into obvious sets of three on a common stalk.

rows.readsAs: a heap of overlapping smooth stones, or a cabbage seen from above
rows.defect: The whole identity of taro - big downward-pointing arrowhead blades held out on long erect stalks - is absent. There are no stalks whatsoever and no arrowhead shape: the image is six or seven near-circular flat discs overlapping in a fan, and the mass floats above the baseline rather than clumping out of the ground. Only one disc has any veining. Nothing here says plant, let alone taro.
rows.fix: Draw three or four distinct arrowhead blades, each hanging tip-down from its own long upright purple-tinged stalk that runs to the ground, with the peltate stalk attachment visible inside the blade.

rows.readsAs: a bunch of dried brown twigs with five purple asters stuck in the top
rows.defect: The must-read is a ground-hugging mat much wider than tall, and the reference aspect is 2; the render is the exact opposite - a narrow upright bouquet roughly twice as tall as it is wide, standing on a single thick trunk-stub. The leaves are sparse thin whiskers rather than minute paired ovals, and the flowers are five separate flat purple daisy florets rather than dense domed two-lipped heads. Bare brown stem dominates the silhouette, which is wrong for a leafy creeping herb.
rows.fix: Flatten the whole plant into a low sprawling mat wider than tall, clothe the wiry stems densely in tiny opposite oval leaves so almost no bare stem shows, and cap the shoot tips with rounded clustered pink-purple flower domes.

rows.readsAs: a floating sprig of pea or bean vine
rows.defect: The two things that make a yam - heart-shaped leaves with strongly arcing veins, and the big knobbly brown tuber at the base - are both missing. The leaves are plain round blobs with a single straight midrib and no basal notch, and there is no tuber, no soil, nothing at the base at all. The stem is a loose S-curve floating diagonally in space with nothing to twine around, so even the vine habit does not read; the little curls hang in mid-air.
rows.fix: Give the leaves a clear heart shape with a notched base and three to five curved veins fanning from the base, spiral the stem tightly around a visible upright support, and put a knobbly brown tuber half-buried at the bottom.

rows.readsAs: one big spiky maple or mallow leaf with a wire and a star on it
rows.defect: This is Wild Rhubarb's picture in lime green with a cream star instead of a pink spike - same radial fan of sharply toothed lobes, same central V-notch, same dead-straight vertical wand. The species requires three separate HEART-shaped leaflets with notched tips, each on its own thin stalk, forming a low carpet; instead there is one solid undivided fan of sharp saw-toothed lobes, no leaflet separation, no stalks, and no carpet. The flower is a small upright star, not a delicate nodding five-petalled cup with purple veining.
rows.fix: Split the mass into several separate three-leaflet clovers, each leaflet a rounded heart with a deep notch at the tip, held on its own thin stalk, and hang the flowers nodding on slender arched stems.

rows.readsAs: a single silvery pinnate frond - a fern or a yarrow sprig
rows.defect: The silver-grey silky feathery foliage does land, which is wormwood's strongest signal. But the form is supposed to be a woody-based bushy clump and this is one flat symmetrical frond on a single straight stem - a leaf, not a shrub. The yellow nodding button flowers are missing; the top ornament is a small upright cream bumpy spike. It is the same stem-plus-leaflet-ladder template as Wild Sesame.
rows.fix: Branch it into a bushy woody-based clump of several arching silver sprays and hang sprays of tiny dull yellow-green button flowers nodding from the upper stems.

rows.readsAs: a coffee bush or a berry shrub cut and bunched
rows.defect: It reads as a woody berry-bearing plant, which is directionally right, and the red-purple berry clusters are clearly present. But the form is a tree and this is the same splayed stick-bundle template as Wild Thyme - a bouquet of bare brown rods off one stub, with no trunk, no branching structure and no dense evergreen crown. The leaves are small plain pointed ovals rather than leathery glossy obovate blades with soft blunt teeth, and the berries sit as pom-poms on the stick tips instead of clustered in the leaf axils.
rows.fix: Rebuild it as a small tree with one real trunk that divides into branches carrying a dense rounded evergreen crown of large glossy blunt-toothed obovate leaves, with berry clusters tucked into the leaf axils.

rows.readsAs: a plain olive-green coiled rubber worm
rows.defect: The must-read that IS the garter snake — long pale stripes running the whole body length — is completely absent; the body carries only a few faint blurred pale blotches. Posture is specified crawling and the render is the same closed doughnut coil as the other eight, so no continuous body line exists for a stripe to run along. Aspect 8 is not visible: the tube is fat and the tail is buried in the coil.
rows.fix: Draw it uncoiled in a crawling S and paint three continuous pale-yellow dorsal/lateral stripes running head to tail tip over a dark olive ground.
rows.verifyWhy:
Looked at the 440x440 PNG at 1x, then re-rendered crops of the body, the dorsal arc and the head at 3x-8x with 1.9x-3.0x luminance boost to make sure faint markings were not being missed.

WHAT IS ACTUALLY THERE: a single closed loop of thick green-olive tube, roughly 1.5 turns, sitting on a soft ellipse shadow. Tube diameter ~37px against a coil outer diameter ~215px. Limbless, correct. A pointed almond head-ellipse at the right end, tapering smoothly out of the neck with no distinct temporal bulge, and a red forked tongue. The whole tube is covered in strong dark crescent ridges running PERPENDICULAR to the body axis, ~90 of them, which is the dominant texture in the image.

THE MUST-READ THAT FAILS: 'long pale stripes running the whole body length' is absent. At 3x boost the only pale marking content is a scatter of soft, blurred, low-contrast round and oval blobs - about six on the upper-left arc, a broken chain of four or five on the lower-left arc, two small dots near the neck - plus a cluster of DARK olive ovals at the far left. They loosely follow the body axis but have long gaps, no shared edge, no shared width, and no lateral (side) stripe at all. The pattern reads as a spotted or mottled snake. Nothing in the image reads as a stripe at any zoom level.

CORRECTIONS TO THE ORIGINAL CLAIM (verdict stands, two of the stated causes are wrong or incomplete):
1. 'there is no continuous body line for a stripe to run along' is WRONG as a diagnosis. The coil is a single unbroken spline and a longitudinal stripe would run along it perfectly well - striped snakes are routinely illustrated coiled. The stripe is missing because the marking system only owns a soft round blob brush; it has no longitudinal band primitive. Proof: King Snake in the same batch, whose must-read is BOLD REPEATING BANDS, is drawn on the identical coil chassis with the identical scatter of soft round blobs and gets no bands either. The fix is a pattern painter that strokes along the body spline (and a transverse one for banded species), not a change of posture.
2. 'plain olive tube' undersells the real second problem: the tube is not plain, it is covered edge to edge in high-contrast transverse crescent ridges. Those ridges run at 90 degrees to the body axis and would actively fight any longitudinal stripe drawn over them. They also push the silhouette toward earthworm / annelid segmentation rather than snake scale; only the forked tongue and the head keep the organism reading as a snake.

OTHER DEFECTS THE ORIGINAL JUDGE DID NOT NAME:
3. Posture spec is 'crawling'; this is a fully closed coil (the family chassis). Correct as stated, and it does cost the aspect-8 read - the body reads as a chunky hose rather than a slender snake even though the unrolled length-to-width ratio is about 15.
4. Eye spec is 'normal' (garter snakes have ROUND pupils). The render gives a large white sclera disc with a black VERTICAL SLIT pupil - a viper/gecko eye on a harmless colubrid. Clearly visible at 8x.
5. The head ellipse is pasted onto the end of the coil with a visible seam where the two overlap, and carries no mouth line, no nostril and no labial detail.

MUST-READS SCORED: stripes ABSENT (fatal, this is the whole identity of the species); slender limbless body PARTIAL (limbless yes, slender no); small head barely wider than the neck PRESENT. One of three, and the missing one is the defining one, so the asset reads as a generic spotted colubrid, not a garter snake. FAIL upheld.

rows.readsAs: a generic green coiled snake, indistinguishable from the Tree Snake render but duller
rows.defect: The pale yellow collar behind the head — the single feature that names a grass snake — is nowhere on the render; the neck is the same flat green as the body. The specified loose S-curve is instead the family's tight closed doughnut. The eye is a white oval with a dark vertical slit, contradicting the required round pupil.
rows.fix: Add a bright yellow-and-black crescent collar across the neck just behind the jaw, and repaint the pupil as a round black disc.
rows.verifyWhy:

CLAIM PART 1 - 'drawn at full family gauge' - CONFIRMED, and it is worse than stated. This is not merely the same gauge, it is the same MESH. Silhouette IoU against family siblings: Tree Snake 0.843, Vine Snake 0.794, Garter Snake 0.738. Measured left-limb gauge at midline: Whip 46 px, Vine 55 px, Tree 36 px, Garter 45 px. Vine Snake (packet aspect 12, note: 'Extraordinarily thin - roughly pencil-width along its whole length') is the SAME fat torus in green and is actually THICKER than the Whip Snake. Tree Snake (note: 'startlingly thin - pencil-width even at a metre long') is the same torus in a different olive. The family's three whip-thin species are indistinguishable from its heavy-bodied ones; only hue and speckle pattern change. So the packet's aspect field is having no effect on the renderer at all for this family - that is the root defect, and fixing Whip Snake alone will not fix it.

CLAIM PART 2 - 'the tail is not visible anywhere' - PARTLY WRONG, correct this in the fix brief. The tail terminus IS present and I located it: trace the head at the right, follow the neck down-left along the outer bottom limb, around the left side, up and over the top, then the body dives inward and runs left-to-right along the inner floor of the coil, ending in a blunt wedge at approximately x 215-235, y 172-185 (the notch/step in the top edge of the dark inner hole; visible at 14x). So it is not missing - it is TERMINATED AT FULL GAUGE with no taper whatsoever, cut off square against the shaded inner wall of the doughnut where the low-contrast inner shading hides it. The judge's conclusion (the defining proportion cannot be read) is right; the reason is 'blunt untapered stump hidden in shadow', not 'absent'. A fix that merely un-buries the tail without tapering it will still fail.

THIRD MUST-READ, not mentioned by the judge - PARTIAL. 'Narrow head with a large round eye': the eye is genuinely large and prominent, a white globe with a clean dark VERTICAL SLIT pupil, well rendered. But the head is a rounded lozenge only marginally narrower than the body, so 'narrow head' reads weakly, and the vertical slit is wrong for a diurnal whip snake, which has a round pupil. Also note the packet specifies posture 'crawling' and the asset is coiled into a closed ring - the coil posture is itself part of why no length proportion can be read.

BAND. Two of three must-reads fail outright (whip-thin body; long tapering tail at half total length), the third only half-reads. The asset reads as a generic fat colubrid coil - the same coil the whole family shares. FAIL is correct.

rows.readsAs: a white duckling or fluffy chick — a cartoon baby waterfowl, not a raptor of any kind
rows.defect: Two of the three must-reads are flatly absent and the third is contradicted. (1) The eyes are BLACK beads with white specular dots — there is no yellow iris anywhere in the face. Brilliant yellow eyes in a white face IS the snowy owl's identity and it is missing. (2) The feet are bare yellow scaled chicken toes with visible segment lines; 'heavily feathered feet' is not merely weak, it is the opposite of what is drawn. (3) The head is round and untufted, which is correct, but it is small and grafted low onto the FRONT of the body rather than sitting on top, and there is no facial disc or rim at all. The note explicitly asks for a rounded column taller than wide; the render is a horizontal egg clearly wider than tall, with the long axis running left-to-right and a grey pointed tail spike stabbing off the right side. Nothing about the silhouette, the eye colour or the foot says owl.
rows.fix: Give it the yellow eye first — large forward-facing discs with a saturated yellow iris ringed in black, set into a dished white facial disc — then stand the body up into a vertical column taller than wide and bury the legs in white feathered trousers so only stubby dark talons show below.

rows.readsAs: a white dove or a white pigeon with a stray tuft
rows.defect: Two of the three must-reads are simply absent. The bill is a small smooth yellow cone with NO hook and no dark heavy mass - a dove's bill, not a cockatoo's black hooked bill. The feet are three-forward-one-back perching feet, not zygodactyl. The crest is a thin four-strand wire spray sitting on top of the skull rather than a raised fan of feathers rising out of the crown, and it is small enough to read as damage. Body is the shared plump pigeon oval with a long grey pointed pigeon tail; posture is horizontal despite the packet asking for upright.
rows.fix: Replace the yellow cone with a heavy dark down-curved hooked bill with a visible cere, and rebuild the crest as a broad layered fan of 6-8 overlapping recurved feathers sweeping back off the crown, tall enough to read at thumbnail size.

rows.readsAs: a red pigeon, or a cardinal that has lost its crest
rows.defect: The identity must-read - a tail streamer far longer than the body - is absent. The tail is a short striped slat roughly a third of the body length, leaving horizontally from mid-body, and it is the SAME tail shape as the Parrot's, only red. The packet specifies aspect 0.5 (much taller than wide, tail hanging vertically); the render is visibly WIDER than tall. There is no bare white facial patch traced with feather lines - just a small white eye smudge. The beak is pale and slightly hooked, which is the only must-read that lands.
rows.fix: Redraw with the bird perched upright and the tail a single long tapering streamer hanging vertically to at least twice body length, so the silhouette becomes tall and narrow, and add the bare white cheek patch with fine feather striations around the eye.

rows.readsAs: a green bird - a parakeet at best, a green pigeon at worst
rows.defect: The hooked yellow beak is present and is the only thing carrying the read. The zygodactyl foot is missing - both feet show three toes forward, one back, ordinary perching feet. The tail is not short and squared; it is the shared long horizontal striped slat also used on the Macaw. The posture is horizontal on the pigeon chassis rather than the biped upright the packet calls for, and the stocky compact body is the family's generic plump oval rather than a parrot's upright barrel. No fleshy cere is visible at the beak base.
rows.fix: Draw the zygodactyl foot explicitly - two toes forward, two back, wrapping a visible perch - and shorten the tail to a short squared fan while tipping the body to an upright stance.

rows.readsAs: a white cartoon duckling / bath-toy duck
rows.defect: The identity must-read — vividly coloured blue or red webbed feet — is entirely absent: the feet are the same thin orange-yellow three-toed chicken sticks used on Gannet and Pelican, with no webbing at all. The eye is one round black dot set on the side of a spherical head, so there is no forward-set binocular stare, and the bill is a short blunt yellow cone with a clear forehead step rather than a long tapered dagger running straight into the skull. Visually it is the same asset as Gannet.
rows.fix: Repaint the feet as large fully-webbed triangular paddles in saturated cobalt blue extending forward of the body, and lengthen the bill to at least head-length with the culmen running unbroken into the crown.
rows.verifyWhy:
FAIL upheld, but one third of the stated cause is wrong and must not be fixed as stated.

WHAT I SAW (440x440, zoomed 5-11x on head and feet, plus a pixel diff against Gannet).

FEET - judge is RIGHT, and this alone fails the asset. At 9x the feet are two thin ochre sticks dropping from the belly, each ending in a simple bent V: one forward prong, one rear prong. Sampled dominant foot colour is RGB(201,162,79) - a dull tan/gold, the same amber family as the bill. There is no blue anywhere on the legs, no red, and no membrane: the prongs are separate strokes with dark background visible between them, no webbing polygon, no lobes, no paddle. Correction to the judge's wording: it reads as TWO prongs per foot, not three, and the hue is dull ochre rather than saturated orange. The single most identity-bearing must-read for a booby - 'vividly coloured blue or red webbed feet' - is absent in both of its parts (colour and web).

BILL - judge is WRONG on the description, half right on the defect. It is NOT a short blunt cone. It is a long, finely tapered dagger: it runs roughly 1.2x the head diameter forward from the skull and narrows from a wide base to a needle point, sharper than most of this family. The length-and-taper half of must-read 2 is genuinely satisfied and should NOT be 'fixed' by lengthening the bill. What fails is the second clause, 'running straight into the forehead': the bill is a flat amber wedge pasted onto the side of a perfectly spherical white cranium, so the dorsal line breaks at a hard step where the ball bulges up and back over the bill base. There is no continuous skull-to-bill ramp. That is the real bill defect - a culmen/forehead junction problem, not a bill-length problem.

EYES - judge is right. One eye only, lateral: a round black disc with a single white specular highlight, sitting immediately behind and just above the bill base. Its placement is actually reasonably forward (it touches the bill's rear edge), so 'side-set' overstates it slightly, but there is no second eye, no forward-facing pair flanking the culmen, and no binocular stare. Must-read 3 is not delivered. No dark facial mask, no bare facial skin, no throat stripe.

SAME BIRD AS GANNET - judge is right, and I confirmed it numerically. I diffed Booby.png against Gannet.png pixel-for-pixel and rendered the delta map: the result is nothing but thin edge lines and interior stipple noise. Head sphere, bill wedge, eye, the white teardrop body, the grey wing wrap arcing over the flank, the grey wedge tail spike and both legs/feet land at IDENTICAL coordinates. Only 5.87% of sampled pixels exceed a visible threshold and every one of those is procedural feather-texture jitter or a marginally larger eye - zero shape displacement. These are one chassis with a re-rolled noise seed, not two species.

FIX ORDER: (1) blue (or red) webbed feet with a visible interdigital membrane spanning three forward toes - this is the whole species; (2) ramp the cranium into the bill base so the culmen is one unbroken line, and drop the spherical ball head; (3) rotate the head toward 3/4 so both forward-set eyes read; (4) differentiate the body from Gannet - booby wants a slimmer, longer-tailed, more pointed rear than the gannet's bulk.

rows.readsAs: a black duck or coot floating on a pond
rows.defect: None of the three must-reads is on screen. The wings are not open — there is no heraldic drying pose at all, just the family's folded grey flank crescent, and that pose IS the cormorant. The bill is a small straight yellow triangle with no hook. The body is the family egg half-sunk in a water ellipse with no low-slung waterline profile and no stiff wedge tail. The neck is a short thick grey tube, not long or snaky.
rows.fix: Redraw it perched and upright with both wings spread wide and half-cocked in the drying pose, add a hooked nail to the bill tip, and extend the neck to roughly body-length with an S-kink.
rows.verifyWhy: Verified at full size and at 6x/14x zoom on head, bill tip and rear of body, plus a pixel bbox/row-span scan. The FAIL stands: all three mustReads (hook-tipped bill on a long snaky neck / wings held open to dry in a heraldic pose / low-slung body with a stiff wedge tail) are absent, and the asset reads as a black coot or duckling floating on a pond. WHAT IS ACTUALLY THERE: a near-circular dark body (137px wide, ~120px tall) sunk to its waterline in a blue pond disc with two concentric ripple ellipses; a big round head (58px across, headFrac far above the specified 0.2); a plain black bead eye with a single specular dot; a short vertical neck stub; a yellow bill; a faint dark crescent on the flank standing in for a FOLDED wing. WING: there is a wing indicated, but it is a closed folded-wing arc drawn as a shading crescent across the body flank, not an open shape. Nothing is spread, raised or held away from the body; the heraldic drying pose, which is the entire identity of this bird, is nowhere on the canvas. TAIL: the judge said 'no stiff wedge tail'; it is stronger than that. There is NO tail of any kind. The 6x crop of the rump shows the body terminating in a smooth unbroken circular dome edge with zero projection past the rump; the silhouette right edge is a clean arc from y182 to the waterline. BODY: not low-slung and not elongated. Row spans give a body 137 wide x ~120 tall, i.e. essentially round; the packet asks for aspect 2.8 and posture 'upright' and the drawing delivers neither - the whole creature bbox (excluding the water rings) is about 165 wide x 185 tall, and it is drawn SWIMMING, not standing upright. NECK - the judge's wording is right but for a reason worth stating precisely: measured, the neck is 14px wide and only ~24px of visible length between the skull base (y158) and the shoulder flare (y182), so it is SHORTER than the head is tall (36px) - a stubby ~2:1 column. It is also perfectly straight and vertical with no S-kink or forward reach, so 'snaky' fails on curvature as well as on length. It is slender relative to the oversized head, so 'thick' is the one word to discard; 'short, straight, stubby' is the accurate description. BILL - one correction to the claim. It is not 'small' and not quite 'straight'. It is a yellow quadrilateral roughly 40px long (about 0.7 head-widths), with a slightly convex culmen and a concave underside, and its tip is canted DOWNWARD into a small point that drops below the gape line. So a shallow droop is present. What is missing is the hook proper: there is no overhanging nail, no separation between an over-curling upper mandible and a shorter lower one - it is one solid yellow wedge, and at full size the droop reads as a blunt duck/coot bill, not as a cormorant's hooked tip. Colour is also wrong-signalling: an all-over saturated yellow bill on a black body is the coot/moorhen frontal-shield read, which is exactly why the whole thing lands on 'black duck'. FIX ORDER: (1) open the wings into the heraldic drying spread - that alone converts the read; (2) add the stiff wedge tail projecting behind the rump and stretch the body into a low horizontal cigar so the silhouette stops being a circle; (3) triple the neck length and put an S-kink in it; (4) put a real overhanging hook on the bill tip and desaturate the yellow to a horn/grey-yellow with only a small yellow gular patch at the base.

rows.readsAs: a dark pigeon or grouse standing on the ground
rows.defect: The asset is not flying — it sits on the family egg body over a cast ground shadow with the two yellow chicken feet visible underneath. The deeply forked scissor tail is absent; the rear is a fan of straight dark streaks with no fork. The wings are not long crooked M-shapes, they are the chassis crescent smeared sideways and do not leave the body as separate airfoils. There is no hooked bill and no scarlet throat pouch of any kind.
rows.fix: Rebuild it airborne with no feet and no ground shadow: two very long angular M-kinked wings spanning the full canvas width and a hard deep V-fork in the tail, plus a scarlet inflated pouch under the chin.
rows.verifyWhy:
Verified at 1x, at 5-10x nearest-neighbour crops of head/feet/tail, and on a gamma-lifted (0.33) full frame so the near-black shapes separate from the near-black background. The FAIL stands; the packet's three must-reads (deeply forked scissor tail / very long crooked M-shaped wings / hooked bill + inflated scarlet gular pouch) are all absent, and the packet's posture:flying is contradicted by the render.

WHAT IS ACTUALLY DRAWN. A near-circular egg body (the shared family chassis) filling the mid-frame, dark charcoal with pale speckle/scale mottling and a thin light rim. A small round head sits high-left with NO neck at all — head sphere abuts the body sphere directly. Two yellow scaled feet with three splayed forward toes each are planted flat under the belly, and a soft elliptical CAST GROUND SHADOW sits beneath them, feet touching it. That is unambiguously a standing/perched ground pose, not flight — the packet asks for flying.

TAIL. The judge said 'just a fan of straight streaks'. Correct, but incomplete in a way a fixer needs: there ARE two separate things back there. (a) At the far right tip of the right wing, five straight, parallel, slightly-splayed dark streaks read as primaries, not tail. (b) Tucked UNDER the right wing plank and slightly below it there is one narrow dark triangular wedge tapering to a point at roughly 20 degrees below horizontal — this is almost certainly the intended tail, but it is a SINGLE unforked spike, it is dark-on-dark against both the wing above it and the background, and it reads as a shadow or a second wing rather than a tail. So the fix is not 'add a tail' — a tail primitive exists; it must be split into two long divergent scissor streamers with a deep V notch between them, and value-separated from the wing it currently hides under.

WINGS. The judge's 'no long crooked M-wings' is right on 'crooked' and 'M' but WRONG on 'long' — total span is roughly 2.2x body width, which is already respectably long. The defect is shape, not length: both wings are perfectly STRAIGHT flat planks held horizontally out from the body's mid-flank, right one long and tapering, left one shorter, with no wrist joint, no forward-swept hand, no elbow. A fixer who reacts to 'no long wings' by lengthening them will make it worse. What is missing is the wrist crook — the sharp angled bend that makes the frigatebird's M/W silhouette — plus the pointed swept-back hand beyond it. As drawn the planks also intersect a standing body, which is why the glider outline never registers.

BILL. Confirmed unhooked, and worse than the judge stated. At 10x it is a short, blunt yellow wedge about half a head-width long, with a straight top edge and a slightly concave lower edge, ending in a plain point that angles very slightly down but has NO hook, NO nail, NO downcurved tip. Frigatebird needs a bill roughly 1.5-2 head-widths long, slender, and terminating in a distinct downward hook. Current bill reads as a dove/pigeon bill.

GULAR POUCH. Fully absent — confirmed. The throat/breast region under the head is the same flat charcoal as the rest of the body; no scarlet, no red, no inflated balloon shape, no colour of any kind other than the yellow of bill and feet. This is the single most diagnostic frigatebird feature and there is zero trace of it.

GESTALT. The judge's 'dark pigeon or grouse' is fair; I read it as a dark pigeon/dove specifically (round no-neck head, short wedge bill, plump egg body, yellow perching feet on ground shadow). The straight wing planks with primary streaks add a faint pasted-on gull quality but the standing round body dominates completely. Nothing in the silhouette says frigatebird.

rows.readsAs: a generic white seabird or gull chick
rows.defect: The overall white body with a grey wing and a pointed pale bill is roughly in the right zone, but all three must-reads are missing: the head is pure white with no buff-yellow wash, there is no dark facial mask or dark bare skin around the eye and bill base, and the wingtip is mid-grey rather than jet black. The bill is also too short and too blunt to read as a plunge-diving dagger.
rows.fix: Wash the whole head and nape buff-yellow, ink a black mask around the eye and gape line, and hard-cut the outer third of the wing to true black.

rows.readsAs: a grey-white gull or duckling standing on a shadow
rows.defect: The enormous bill and slung throat pouch — the entire identity — are absent; the bill is the family's short yellow cone, shorter than the head. The bird is standing on two long visible legs over a ground shadow rather than swimming, and the legs are the family's thin sticks, not the very short heavy set called for. The neck is not long and is not kinked back onto the shoulders; the head sits directly on the egg body. Body is the same chassis as Booby and Gannet in a slightly dirtier grey.
rows.fix: Give it a bill at least twice head-length with a deep sagging elastic pouch hanging beneath, and set it low on the waterline with the neck folded back in an S onto the shoulders and the legs hidden.
rows.verifyWhy:
FAIL upheld, but two of the three stated causes are factually wrong and must not be used as the fix brief.

WHAT IS ACTUALLY ON THE CANVAS (440x440; body bbox x83-354, y130-299, so 271w x 169h). A rotund egg-shaped body in dirty grey-white with a scaled/feather-stipple texture, a dark grey crescent arc across the flank for the folded wing, a grey wedge tail spearing out to the right, a small pale sphere head at upper left carrying a big glossy black bead eye with a white catchlight, a straight yellow bill pointing left, two short yellow legs, and a hard-edged elliptical cast shadow under the feet.

CORRECTION 1 - THE BILL IS NOT 'THE FAMILY'S SHORT YELLOW CONE, SHORTER THAN THE HEAD'. Measured yellow-pixel bbox for the bill: x84-148, y142-166, i.e. 65px long and 25px deep at the base. The head sphere is about 48px across (x141-186, y129-177). So the bill is roughly 1.35x the head's diameter - LONGER than the head, not shorter. And it is NOT the family's cone: the same measurement on Booby gives 58 long x 11 deep and on Gannet 55 long x 11 deep. The Pelican's bill is 2.3x deeper than its family-mates'. It is a broad solid wedge, not a needle. Anyone fixing this against the judge's wording would 'lengthen the bill' and miss the real defect.

THE REAL BILL DEFECT (the identity, and it does fail). There is no pouch, at all. The depth profile climbs monotonically and smoothly from 1px at the tip to 24-25px at the base (84:1 90:9 96:14 102:17 108:20 114:22 120:23 126:24 132:24 138:24 144:24) - a clean isoceles triangle with a straight lower edge. There is no second mandible line, no sagging or bulging curve under the lower edge, no gular skin in a contrasting flesh/orange tone, no distension. At 4x magnification the pixels immediately below the bill's lower edge are plain dark background all the way from tip to gape. So it reads as a thickened heron/tern dagger. It is also not 'enormous' in pelican terms: 65px against a 271px body is 24% of body length, where a real pelican's bill is 40-50% of body length and visually rivals the entire head+neck. mustRead 1 ('enormous bill with a stretchy throat pouch slung beneath') is unmet - the pouch, which is the single most identifying structure on the animal, is entirely absent.

CORRECTION 2 - THE LEGS ARE NOT LONG. At 6x the legs run from the belly edge at about y=275 to the toes at about y=298: roughly 23px against a 169px body height, about 13-14% - genuinely short and mostly tucked under the mass. mustRead 2 ('heavy body on very short legs') is the ONE must-read that is actually satisfied, and the judge scored it as a defect. Do not lengthen or shorten the legs. The legitimate complaints about the lower half are (a) the feet are three thin splayed unwebbed toes, where a pelican is totipalmate with all four toes joined by full webbing, and (b) the posture: the reference calls for 'swimming' and this bird is standing on land on a hard-edged shadow ellipse, so it is not floating on a waterline at all. Both of those the judge got right.

CORRECTION 3 - THE NECK. The judge is correct here. The head sits on a short straight vertical grey column dropping directly onto the shoulder mass - about a head's-depth of neck, no curve in it. There is no long neck and no S-kink folding it back onto the shoulders. mustRead 3 unmet.

SHARED-CHASSIS CLAIM CONFIRMED. Read against Booby.png and Gannet.png side by side, the three are one drawing. Identical egg body outline, identical dark crescent folded-wing arc in the same place at the same angle, identical grey wedge tail exiting right at the same pitch, identical head sphere seated at the same spot, identical yellow legs with the same three splayed toes, identical shadow ellipse. Body bboxes: Pelican 271x169, Booby 248x145, Gannet 256x149 - the same shape scaled. What varies is a slightly dirtier grey wash, a slightly larger head, and the thicker bill wedge. The chassis reads as a generic plump gull/tern standing on a beach.

SECONDARY: headFrac measures about 0.18 (48px head / 271px body) against the required 0.3, and 'eyes: small' is not honoured - the eye is a prominent 14px bead with a specular highlight on a 48px head, matching Booby's 'prominent' eye setting rather than the Pelican row's 'small'.

BAND. Two of three must-reads absent, including the one that IS the organism, plus the wrong posture and a body that is demonstrably a family-mate's chassis. It reads as a stocky gull with a thick yellow beak, not a pelican. FAIL stands.

rows.readsAs: a generic green cartoon fish / vaguely a bass-shaped decal
rows.defect: The large hinged bucket mouth - the single feature that IS a bass - is not weak, it is entirely absent: the head tapers to a bare geometric point with no mouth, lip or jaw line drawn anywhere. The dorsal is one crown of four flat triangles, so there is no spiny-front-joined-to-soft-rear structure either; only the moderately deep compressed body reads. No lateral black stripe, no head/operculum break.
rows.fix: Draw the jaw: cut a wide gape line from the snout back past the eye with a heavy hinged lower jaw and a blunt upper lip, and split the dorsal crown into a spiny triangle set joined by a low membrane to a rounded soft rear lobe.
rows.verifyWhy: UPHELD, with two corrections to the stated cause. I read the 440x440 PNG at full size and then re-cropped/upscaled three regions with nearest-neighbour (head 240,150 120x100 at 8x; dorsal 160,110 180x80 at 7x; whole body 100,150 240x120 at 7x) and measured the alpha bbox. WHAT IS ACTUALLY THERE: the animal is a symmetric pointed lens/almond in flat olive-green, pointed at BOTH ends. Alpha bbox x116-325, y141-241 (210x101 incl. dorsal spikes and tail). Body proper runs ~x130-325 with max depth ~62-66px measured at x=210-240 (the 76px column reading there includes the ventral fin lobe), giving aspect ~3.0-3.1 against the spec 2.8. MUST-READ 2 (large hinged bucket mouth) IS GENUINELY ABSENT and this is the fatal defect: at 8x the snout narrows to a bare geometric vertex at x=325 with zero mouth geometry - no gape, no upper/lower lip, no maxilla line, no jaw hinge, not even a short scratch of a mouth slit. On a largemouth bass the jaw hinge extends BEHIND the eye and is the entire read of the species; here the eye (a small white ring with a dark pupil, sitting high and very far forward at ~x=305) is the only forward feature, so the head is not a head, it is the pointed end of a leaf. MUST-READ 1 (spiny front dorsal joined to a soft rear one) IS ALSO ABSENT AS STRUCTURE: the dorsal is one continuous flat dark-olive sawtooth crown of exactly four identical triangular spikes on a single unbroken base, spanning roughly x=200-270, drawn BEHIND the body silhouette with no ray lines, no membrane shading and no notch. There is no differentiated soft-rayed rear lobe of any kind - the rear two spikes are simply shorter copies of the front two, so nothing reads as 'spiny front joined to soft rear'; it reads as a stegosaur/crown decoration bolted to a fish. CORRECTION 1 TO THE CLAIM: the head is NOT wholly bare. There is a distinct curved dark operculum/gill-cover arc behind the eye (roughly x=288 curving from the topline down to the ventral edge), faint vertical hatch striations on the cheek in front of it, and a pale horizontal lateral line running the body length. So the fixable gap is specifically the MOUTH, not 'no head detail at all' - an artist reading the claim literally might add gill/cheek detail that is already present and still ship a mouthless fish. CORRECTION 2 TO THE CLAIM: 'only the moderately deep body reads' overstates must-read 3. At aspect ~3.0-3.1 the body is slimmer than the 2.8 spec and, worse, it is a top/bottom SYMMETRIC lens - it has none of a bass's deep-shouldered dorsal mass over a flatter belly line, so 'deep laterally compressed body' reads only weakly, at best partially. The claim also omits three things a fix pass should know: (a) the caudal is a flat dark triangular wedge that visually detaches from the sharp caudal peduncle vertex at x~130, leaving a pinched gap; (b) a pectoral fan and a single small ventral triangle (one lump doing duty for pelvic+anal) are present but flat and rayless; (c) there is no dark lateral blotch band, the other classic largemouth cue - not in the must-read list, but its absence plus the missing mouth is why this reads as generic green cartoon fish rather than as Bass. VERDICT: two of three must-reads absent outright and the third only weakly present. FAIL stands.

rows.readsAs: a yellow bluegill or a generic yellow pancake panfish - it is the Sunfish render in another colour
rows.defect: Zero of the three must-reads survive. There is ONE saw-tooth dorsal, not two separate fins. There are NO dark vertical bars - the flank carries only the same uniform dot-mesh scale hatch as every other fish here. The pelvic and anal fins are the same olive-yellow as the body with no orange or red anywhere. On top of that the body is drawn as a near-round pancake (roughly 1.3:1) when the row asks for 2.8:1, which makes it read as the Sunfish rather than a perch.
rows.fix: Rebuild it at a true 2.8:1 with a humped nape, split the crown into a distinct spiny front dorsal and a separate soft rear dorsal with a real gap between them, paint 6-7 hard dark vertical bars from topline to belly, and colour the pelvic and anal fins orange-red.

rows.readsAs: a pale green bluegill / panfish - broadly the right thing
rows.defect: The deep round pancake body does read, but the other two must-reads do not. There is no dark ear-flap tab on the gill cover - only diffuse mottling near a faint gill arc. There is no tiny mouth on a small head: the head is not differentiated at all and the snout ends in a bare point with no mouth drawn. The caudal fin also sits as a flat detached paddle with a stray thin dark line running vertically through it.
rows.fix: Add a solid black opercular ear-flap tab at the rear edge of the gill cover and a small blunt terminal mouth on a short rounded head, and reattach/clean the caudal paddle so it joins the peduncle without the stray stroke.

rows.readsAs: a generic gold baitfish or minnow with a spiky crown
rows.defect: None of the three must-reads are present. The eye - the feature the animal is NAMED for - is the same tiny white-ringed black dot used on the Bass and Sunfish, with no size increase, no cloudy milky pupil and no reflective bloom. The dorsal is one saw-tooth crown, not two fins with a spiny front. The caudal is uniform olive with no white tip on the lower lobe. The snout ends in a bare point with no mouth and no canine teeth.
rows.fix: Blow the eye up to 2-3x the family default and fill it with a milky opaque glassy pupil plus a hot reflective highlight, then add the white flash on the lower caudal lobe.

rows.readsAs: a pink cartoon axolotl - correct animal, mascot-grade
rows.defect: Gills and smile land, but the third must-read is absent: there is no fin crest anywhere. The back is a smooth unbroken curve and the tail is a constant-width pink sausage with a blunt rounded tip. Where the caudal fin should be there are instead two dull grey-mauve circles overlapping behind and below the tail, offset from the tail axis and not attached to the tip - they read as a smeared shadow blob, not a fin. The head is a bulbous egg rather than the wide flat spade the reference asks for, the lower gill fan hangs off the throat and tangles with the foreleg so it reads as a pink hand, and the four limbs are dark chocolate-brown against a pink body, so they look glued on from another animal.
rows.fix: Delete the two grey discs and replace them with a real translucent fin membrane: a continuous crest that starts mid-back, thickens over the tail base and tapers the tail to a paddle-shaped point, tinted the same pink as the body; and re-tint the limbs to the body pink.

rows.readsAs: an albino/leucistic axolotl - a stranger names the other species in this batch
rows.defect: This is the Axolotl file recoloured. All three must-reads fail. (1) The body is not a pale pink translucent eel - it is the axolotl's short fat lozenge at roughly aspect 3 instead of the specified aspect 8, opaque cream-yellow with the axolotl's blotches, with a huge quarter-length head instead of headFrac 0.12. (2) The gills are the same two salmon-pink fans in the same two positions as the axolotl, one of them slung under the throat, rather than a bushy blood-red pair swept back behind the head. (3) Worst, the note says the eyes are skinned over and invisible, yet the render carries a large glossy black eye with a white catchlight, front and centre on the skull - the one feature that makes an olm an olm is contradicted rather than merely missing. The limbs are also short bent lizard pegs in olive-brown, not vestigially thin three-toed threads, and the same stray grey discs sit behind the tail.
rows.fix: Rebuild it off the axolotl chassis entirely: stretch to a genuine aspect-8 near-cylindrical pale-pink translucent eel body with a small blunt snout, delete the eye and leave a faint skin-covered depression, move the gills to a single bushy crimson tuft immediately behind the skull, and reduce the limbs to four thread-thin sticks with three visible toes.

rows.readsAs: a fluffy white chick or a small white quail; some viewers would land on dove because it is a pale plump bird with a yellow bill
rows.defect: The small round head on a plump breast is present, but the other two must-reads are not. The 'slim tapering tail' is a single thin grey blade about a fifth of the body length poking off the lower right — a wisp, not a tapering dove tail with any width or feather structure. The short bill has no fleshy cere: it is a plain flat yellow wedge with nothing at its base. The body is a near-perfect sphere with no neck, so the bird has a chick's proportions rather than a dove's longer, sleeker line, and the big oval wing patch with its dark comma outline reads as a decal rather than a folded wing.
rows.fix: Rebuild the tail as a real appendage — three to four times its current length, wide at the base and tapering to a point, with two or three visible rectrix splits — and add a small pale swollen cere at the bill base.

rows.readsAs: a mallard duckling — grey plump body, solid green cap on the head, flat yellow bill
rows.defect: Reads as the wrong organism. The head carries a solid green cap across the crown and cheek which, combined with the broad yellow bill, is mallard signature; a rock pigeon's iridescence belongs on the NECK, not as a green skullcap. Every one of the three must-reads is wrong or missing: the legs are bright YELLOW, not red; the tail is the same thin dark blade as the Dove, nowhere near a broad fan; and there is no white cere at all on the yellow bill. The 'deep barrel chest' is a plain sphere with no keel and no neck.
rows.fix: Recolour the legs and feet to dull pink-red, move the iridescence off the crown onto a neck patch, replace the tail blade with a wide squared-off fan roughly a third of the body length, and put a white knob of cere at the base of a slimmer grey bill.

rows.readsAs: a grey farm pig, or a capybara
rows.defect: The straight downward-pointing tusks are completely absent — there is only a plain mouth line under the snout disc, so nothing separates this from the Pig asset except hue. The legs are the same short columns as the domestic Pig rather than the slim delicate ones the row calls for. The no-visible-tail read is correct.
rows.fix: Add two short white straight tusks dropping vertically below the upper lip line, and lengthen and narrow all four legs by about a third so the body sits higher off the ground than the Pig's.

rows.readsAs: a pig
rows.defect: The curly corkscrew tail is entirely missing — the rump ends in a bare curve with no tail of any kind, and the corkscrew is the one marking that makes this asset unmistakable. The flat round snout disc with nostrils is present and good; the barrel is only moderately deep and the legs are not the very short stumps the row asks for, so it reads leggier than a farm pig. A stray pink flap hangs below the snout that reads as a lolling tongue rather than a jaw.
rows.fix: Add a tight two-turn corkscrew tail at the rump, and shorten the legs so the belly line sits close to the ground and deepen the barrel.

rows.readsAs: a plain grey-brown pig
rows.defect: All three must-reads are absent or inverted. There are no upward-curving tusks — the only white shape is a flat crescent band laid across the top of the muzzle that reads as a bandage or a paint smear, not a tusk, and it curves the wrong way. There are no fleshy facial warts anywhere on the cheek or jaw. There is no erect bristly mane: the topline is the same smooth dead-level back as the Pig. The tufted tail is present but hangs DOWN in a droopy arc, the exact opposite of the antenna-straight-up carriage that is the warthog's signature, and it sprouts high on the back rather than at the rump. Body is the short-legged barrel of a farm pig, not the leggy flat-fronted wedge described.
rows.fix: Rebuild the head and topline: give it a large flat-fronted wedge skull with two paired wart lumps on the cheek, two tusks curving up and out from the lower jaw, an erect black bristle crest along neck and spine, and re-root the thin tail at the rump pointing straight up with the tuft at the top.

rows.readsAs: a shaggy brown pig with one tusk
rows.defect: The high shoulder hump is absent — the topline is flat and level from shoulder to rump, identical to the domestic Pig's, so the front-heavy wedge silhouette that IS a boar never appears; if anything the rump reads as high as the shoulder. The bristly spinal mane is not there either: the hair strokes that do exist fringe the BELLY, not the spine. The single pale wedge near the snout is the only tusk cue and it sits above the muzzle line pointing back rather than emerging up from the lower jaw, so it half-reads as a horn.
rows.fix: Raise and pile the shoulder into a distinct hump and slope the topline down to a low rump, move the hair fringe from the belly onto the spine as an erect crest, and re-anchor the tusk at the lower jaw curving up past the snout.

rows.readsAs: a generic green mackerel-shaped fish with a row of white spikes stuck along its belly; nobody names a pike
rows.defect: Two of the three must-reads are simply absent and the third is wrong. (1) NO duck-bill snout: the head is an undifferentiated point identical to the tail point, with no jaw line, no mouth, no elongated flattened bill, and no separation between skull and snout. (2) NO dorsal fin anywhere — the topline is one unbroken clean arc from nose to caudal peduncle; brightening the file 3x reveals only five near-invisible hairline vertical strokes over the MIDDLE of the back, which are not readable at normal exposure and are in the wrong place regardless (a pike's dorsal sits far back, over the anal fin, just ahead of the tail). (3) The body is not an elongate torpedo but a symmetric almond lens, deepest at mid-length, and it carries a hexagonal scale net instead of the pale bean markings — no bean blotches are present at all. The teeth that are drawn read as a floating comb of seven white hooks hanging OUTSIDE the ventral outline and running rearward past the gill arc, i.e. under the throat rather than in a jaw. Anal fin also missing.
rows.fix: Rebuild the head instead of decorating it: extend the front third into a long flat-topped duck-bill with a straight upper profile and a hinged lower jaw line that opens the mouth back to under the eye, seat the tooth row INSIDE that jaw on both upper and lower edges, then move the deepest point of the body rearward and add a clearly visible dorsal fin (mirrored by an anal fin) directly over the caudal peduncle.

rows.readsAs: a clump of soap bubbles / a bunch of peeled white grapes / a cauliflower — not a mushroom with hanging teeth
rows.defect: The identity must-read — a pom-pom of LONG icicle spines cascading downward over the whole mass — is essentially absent. The silhouette is ~85% large smooth glossy spheres with hard specular highlights; the spines are a short, sparse band roughly one-fifth of the body height, confined to a narrow horizontal strip across the middle, and they are drawn BEHIND a further layer of spheres that occludes their lower halves. So the teeth do not hang off the underside of the mass at all — they appear to grow out of its equator and then get swallowed. Nothing about the surface is shaggy; Hericium reads as a fuzzy white waterfall and this reads as bubble wrap. The remaining must-reads pass (no cap, no stem, no gills; creamy-white colour; single unbranched mass), and the render itself is clean — centred, uncropped, with a ground shadow — but the one must-read that IS the organism is missing.
rows.fix: Invert the mass-to-spine ratio: shrink the interior spheres so they only suggest the lumpy core, then draw the spines as the outer silhouette — long tapered icicles (40–60% of body height) emitted from the BOTTOM and lower-front of the mass, dense enough that the blob's lower edge is entirely a fringe of hanging teeth, and drawn in front of everything so nothing occludes them.

rows.readsAs: A generic pond minnow or small green chub — a plain sage-green leaf-shaped fish with no species cues at all
rows.defect: All three must-reads are absent or invisible. (1) No red at all: the body is one flat sage green from nose to tail with zero red-edged rear scales — the single feature that names this fish (pirarucu = red fish) simply is not drawn. (2) The dorsal and anal fins are not set far back framing the tail; they are dull near-black smears at roughly 45-70% of body length, tucked BEHIND the body silhouette so they read as shadow blobs, and a long bare gap separates them from the caudal paddle, which therefore reads as a detached square flap rather than the third blade of a paddle cluster. (3) There is no bony flattened head and no small upward mouth — the head end is just the body outline sharpened to a needle point, with no jaw line, no opercular plate, and no mouth aperture whatsoever. The body is a symmetric almond pointed at BOTH ends, where an arapaima is blunt-headed and deepest toward the rear. The eye is a bright white ring pasted near the top of the snout, far too high-contrast and too far forward for the reference small eye.
rows.fix: Rebuild the rear third: push the dorsal and anal fins back so their bases run from ~70% to the caudal peduncle and let them visually merge with the caudal into one continuous paddle, then flood the scales over that same rear third with the crimson trailing-edge rim (a red arc on each scale, not a wash) so the red-tailed identity reads at thumbnail size.

rows.readsAs: A wooden ruler, a stick of butter, or a burlap-wrapped knife handle — the blunt-ended tan slab does not read as a living fish
rows.defect: The silhouette is a flat-sided slab squared off at BOTH ends: the head end terminates in a blunt vertical face and the tail end in another, so the animal reads as a cut length of dowel rather than a fish. Two of the three must-reads are entirely missing. (1) No barbels — the chin is a bare blunt corner; nothing projects from it. (2) No steeply upturned drawbridge mouth — the jaw is a single straight horizontal dark slot scribed low on the snout face, almost parallel to the lateral line, which is the exact opposite of the near-vertical oblique gape that IS the arowana. (3) The long ribbon dorsal and anal fins are only half-present: they exist as a flat grey rim hugging the top and bottom edges, indistinguishable from an outline stroke, with no rays, no depth, and no flare. The caudal is a tiny dark wedge with three or four stray hair-rays hanging off the left end, so small and so disconnected from the blunt body face that it reads as damage. The all-over square knurl texture reads as woven basketwork or canvas, not as the arowana's big metallic mosaic scales, and the flat khaki colour carries no sheen. The eye disc sits at the extreme upper-front corner of the block rather than on a modelled head.
rows.fix: Rebuild the head: cut the snout back into an oblique wedge and swing the lower jaw up to a near-vertical hinged plate that meets the upper jaw at the very top of the head, then hang two long forward-curving barbels off its tip — and give the dorsal/anal ribbons real width with visible rays so they read as fins instead of an outline.

rows.readsAs: a generic tan plush monkey, indistinguishable from the Capuchin and Macaque in the same batch
rows.defect: The long dog-like muzzle that IS the baboon is absent — the face is the family's flat button snout with no jaw projection at all. The tail is the shared smooth C-curve, not the sharply kinked-then-hanging profile the note calls out, and there is no shoulder cape.
rows.fix: Build a real projecting snout: extend the skull forward into a long deep dog muzzle with close-set eyes pushed to the top of it, and rebuild the tail as two straight segments — a steep upward stub at the base then a sharp break into a hanging drop.

rows.readsAs: a small brown monkey — roughly right, but only because the capuchin is close to the family's generic default
rows.defect: The pale face inside a dark cap is only hinted at: the crown arc is the same helmet shape every asset carries and it is lighter than the face rather than darker, so the dark-cap-over-pink-face contrast is inverted. The tail is the shared stiff C, not a long curling prehensile tail, and the body is the family's heavy barrel rather than a small slender frame.
rows.fix: Darken the crown to a true black cap with a hard edge against a pale pink face patch, and lengthen the tail into a loose full curl that wraps past the body.

rows.readsAs: a dark ape — the ears do carry it, but it is nearly invisible against the background
rows.defect: The two protruding round ears are present and are the one genuine variation in the batch, but the pale muzzle and heavy brow are absent — the face is a flat dark disc with the family's white dot eyes. The arms are the shared noodles, so 'reaching past the knees' does not read. The whole figure is near-black on a near-black field with almost no value separation.
rows.fix: Lift the body value several steps off the background and add a pale tan muzzle mask under a dark shelf-like brow so the face reads as a chimp face rather than a shadow.

rows.readsAs: a squatting tan ape — a gorilla or an orangutan, never a gibbon
rows.defect: The identity must-read is inverted: the arms are SHORTER here than on any other asset in the batch, tucked as stubs against the torso, so the arm span that defines a gibbon is not merely weak, it is the least of the family. The posture is specified upright and rendered as the same squat as the thirteen quadrupeds, and there are no hook-shaped hands.
rows.fix: Stand the figure fully upright and draw arms at roughly twice leg length, hanging past the feet and ending in narrow curved hooks with the thumb set far back.

rows.readsAs: a big dark ape — the closest hit in the batch, mostly because the shared chassis already is a squatting gorilla
rows.defect: The peaked sagittal crest is absent; the crown carries the same pale helmet arc as the Capuchin and the Macaque. The hands are blunt paddles resting flat, so there is no knuckle-walking, and the shoulders sit level with the hips rather than higher. The figure is also very dark against a dark ground.
rows.fix: Add a pronounced peaked crest to the top of the skull over a heavy brow ridge, and fold the hands into knuckles so the weight visibly loads the fore-limbs and lifts the shoulder above the hip.

rows.readsAs: a generic dark brown monkey, the same silhouette as the Capuchin in a different hue
rows.defect: The swollen bearded throat pouch — the single feature that identifies a howler — is completely absent; there is no throat mass at all, the head sits straight on the torso. The tail is the shared thin smooth C with no thickness and no bare gripping tip.
rows.fix: Swell the throat into a large rounded bearded pouch that visibly widens the jawline, and thicken the tail with a distinct hairless curled tip.

rows.readsAs: a grey plush monkey — the same asset as the Macaque with the saturation pulled out
rows.defect: Both identity reads are missing. The tail is the family's short C-curve and is clearly SHORTER than the body, the opposite of 'far longer than the body'. The face and hands are the same mid-grey as the coat with no black mask and no dark hands, so the pale-fur-framing-a-black-face contrast that makes a Hanuman langur does not exist. The build is the family's stocky barrel, not slender and long-limbed.
rows.fix: Draw the tail at roughly twice body length sweeping well outside the silhouette, and paint the face and both hands solid black against pale grey fur.

rows.readsAs: a grey monkey wearing a fur hood — no viewer would say lemur
rows.defect: The black-and-white ringed tail, which is the entire identity of the ring-tailed lemur, is a plain unbanded grey C-curve shorter than the body. There is no fox-like muzzle — the face is the same flat button snout as every other asset — no black mask, and the eyes are the family's small white dots rather than bright orange-gold staring discs.
rows.fix: Band the tail in hard alternating black and white rings and run it long and upright, then rebuild the head as a pointed fox muzzle with a black mask and large orange irides.

rows.readsAs: a generic monkey — passable only because the macaque is the least specific brief in the batch
rows.defect: The bare pink or red face is absent; the face is the same tan as the coat with no bare skin. The tail is the shared long C rather than short to medium, and the body is squatting front-on, not dog-postured on all fours.
rows.fix: Give the face a bare pink skin mask distinct from the fur and shorten the tail to about a third of body length.

rows.readsAs: an olive monkey with a fuzzy head — none of the mandrill signal is present
rows.defect: The scarlet nose stripe and ridged blue cheeks are entirely absent — the muzzle carries only a faint off-white smudge with no colour at all, and colour IS the mandrill. The packet's note explicitly warns the tail is a stump, yet the asset carries the family's full-length C-curve tail hooking off the hip. The muzzle is the flat family button, not deep and ridged.
