rows.fix: Paint a saturated scarlet stripe down a deep projecting muzzle flanked by hard ridged cobalt cheek pads, and delete the long tail in favour of a short upright stub.

rows.readsAs: a pale grey monkey with a fur ruff — the same figure as the Lemur in a warmer tint
rows.defect: The white fan-shaped ear tufts are replaced by the batch's generic fluff halo ringing the whole head, so there are no distinguishable tufts and no ears. The tail is the shared plain C with no banding. Nothing conveys the squirrel-sized scale or the upright clinging-to-bark pose — it is the same floor-planted squat at the same size as the Gorilla.
rows.fix: Replace the halo with two large white fan tufts flaring outward at the ear positions, band the tail, and pose the animal vertically gripping a trunk to establish scale.

rows.readsAs: a monkey — the generic brief is the one this chassis can nearly satisfy
rows.defect: The flat forward-facing face with round eyes does read, but the tail is clearly shorter than the body rather than as long as it, and does not curl. The hands and feet are featureless blunt paddles with no digits and no opposable thumb anywhere in the image.
rows.fix: Lengthen the tail to full body length with a loose curl at the tip and articulate the hands into four fingers plus an opposed thumb.

rows.readsAs: an orangutan — the hue plus the fur halo carry it, though the anatomy does not
rows.defect: The shaggy orange coat reads and the halo passes loosely for cheek flanges, but the flanges are a soft symmetric fuzz ring rather than two wide flat discs framing the face. The arms are the same uniform noodles as the rest of the batch, so the enormous arm span against short bowed legs is not expressed — the limb proportions are identical to the Macaque's.
rows.fix: Widen the head into two hard flat cheek flanges with a defined edge, and lengthen and thicken the arms so they clearly outspan the body while the legs shorten and bow.

rows.readsAs: an orange-tan generic monkey, visually the same asset as the Monkey row
rows.defect: The huge drooping pendulous nose is absent — the face carries the family's tiny flat snout smudge, and that nose is the only thing that makes a proboscis monkey a proboscis monkey. The limbs and tail are the same colour as the back rather than pale grey, so the two-tone coat is missing as well.
rows.fix: Hang a large pendulous nose from the brow down past the mouth line, breaking the head silhouette, and repaint the limbs and tail pale grey against an orange-brown back.

rows.readsAs: a hunched juvenile chimpanzee or a bear cub
rows.defect: Every must-read that IS the identity is absent. The limbs are SHORT and thick — chunky tubes barely longer than the torso is deep — where a spider monkey is defined by absurdly long spindly arms and legs. The tail is a short thick C-hook reaching only about half the body length, not the longer-than-the-whole-body prehensile fifth limb, and it has no curled gripping tip. The hands are featureless rounded mitts, so the thumbless hook-hand note is invisible. Head is not read as small (it sits on a big barrel torso with no neck) and there is no pot belly — the torso is a uniform barrel, not a slack round gut on spindly supports.
rows.fix: Rebuild the limbs at roughly 2x torso length as thin, kinked, wire-like arms with visible elbow and knee angles and hooked thumbless hands, and redraw the tail as a long thin whip that exceeds the head-to-rump length and curls back on itself at the tip.

rows.readsAs: a golden lion tamarin, or at least a small orange monkey with a mane
rows.defect: The radial mane fringe around the face does land and is the only thing carrying the ID. But the body is the shared barrel-ape chassis — heavy, deep-chested and broad-shouldered, nothing like a squirrel-sized slight primate. The tail is a short thick C-hook at about half body length rather than a long thin tail exceeding the body. There is no branch anywhere in the frame and no fingers at all — the hands are blunt rounded mitts — so the clawed-fingers-gripping-a-thin-branch must-read is entirely missing.
rows.fix: Slim the torso and limbs to squirrel proportions, extend the tail to a long thin taper longer than the body, and pose it perched on a thin diagonal branch with visible needle-clawed digits wrapped over it.

rows.readsAs: a generic dark-green aquarium fish
rows.defect: The long undulating dorsal is a fused leaf-shaped dark mass covering only about half the back — it never separates from the body as a fin, so it does not read as a fin at all. The bony gular plate under the chin is absent and the black eyespot near the tail is completely missing. The tail is a blunt trapezoid paddle, not a rounded fan.
rows.fix: Detach the dorsal as a low continuous wavy ribbon running from just behind the skull all the way to the tail base, and paint a hard black ocellus with a pale ring at the upper tail root.

rows.readsAs: a generic blue-grey blotched fish
rows.defect: The two identity must-reads are absent. There are no fleshy lobed fins on muscular stalks anywhere — the only fins are two faint flat dark triangles painted onto the back and flank with no stalk and no separation from the body. The tail is the same blunt trapezoid paddle used on Bowfin and Gar: not three-lobed, and there is no small central spike. Only the steel-blue flecked colour lands. The body is the shared almond chassis.
rows.fix: Rebuild the tail as three distinct lobes with a small pointed epicaudal spike between them, and hang four fins off the body on thick fleshy stalks that clearly leave the silhouette.
rows.verifyWhy:
I decoded the 440x440 PNG, gamma-boosted it (the art is very dark on a near-black field) and re-read it at 4x, then at 9-11x on the tail, mid-body and belly. Verdict UPHELD, but two parts of the original claim are described wrongly and would send the fix to the wrong place.

WHAT IS ACTUALLY THERE. Fish faces RIGHT (white-ringed eye at the right tip). Body is the family's symmetric almond/lens chassis, pointed at BOTH ends, with a single straight pale lateral line running nose-to-tail, a hexagonal scale stipple fill, and a faint arc near the eye standing in for the operculum. No head mass at all - headFrac 0.28 is not expressed; the front third is just the taper of the almond.

CLAIM 1 (lobed fins) - CONCLUSION RIGHT, GEOMETRY WRONG. There are NOT 'two flat dark triangles painted onto the flank'. The fin shapes are FIVE rounded humps drawn BEHIND the body and clearly separated from the silhouette: two on top breaking above the dorsal topline (one around x~205-235, one around x~265-290 in source px), and two/three shallow bumps breaking below the belly line (the largest, at x~200-230 y~215-222, is only ~5px tall). They are rounded flaps, not triangles, and they DO poke outside the outline. Separately, painted INSIDE the flank at x~245-270 y~185-200 there is one faint translucent fan of radiating rays in almost exactly the body tone - the pectoral fin - which is invisible at 1x and only appears under gamma boost. So the must-read still fails, but for a different reason than stated: nothing anywhere carries a fleshy muscular STALK. The coelacanth's identity is paired pectoral and pelvic fins mounted on thick limb-like fleshy peduncles that project away from the body and can be seen as two segments (stalk + paddle). Here the dorsal/anal shapes are stubby rounded flaps flush to the outline, and the one paired fin that exists is a flat, near-transparent fan with zero contrast against the flank. Fix target: build a two-segment stalked fin (visible dark peduncle + terminal paddle) for the pectoral AND pelvic pair, in a tone that separates from the body - not 'redraw the triangles'.

CLAIM 2 (tail) - FULLY CONFIRMED, including the sibling comparison. At 11x the tail is a squarish blob with rounded corners and faint radiating rays, butted onto the caudal point. I rendered Bowfin and Gar side by side: all three carry the identical rounded-square paddle with the same ray fan and the same two stray diagonal hairline strokes floating outside it. No upper lobe, no lower lobe, no notch, and no central epicaudal spike - the single most diagnostic silhouette feature of this animal is entirely absent. It is one shared component, not a per-species tail.

CLAIM 3 (colour) - lands, with a caveat. The body is a pale steel blue-grey and does carry small light dots. But those dots are the SAME hexagonal scale stipple used on Bowfin (rendered olive) and Gar (rendered khaki) - it is the chassis texture recoloured, not a coelacanth white-fleck pass. The diffuse darker mottled blotches on the flank do read as coelacanth-ish camouflage patches, which is the one genuinely species-specific mark on the asset.

FAMILY NOTE. Bowfin, Gar and Coelacanth are demonstrably one chassis: same almond outline, same nose-to-tail lateral line, same scale stipple, same eye, same faint flank fan, same tail paddle. Only hue, aspect ratio and the count/placement of the rounded dorsal humps change. Two of three identity must-reads for Coelacanth are absent and both are the silhouette-defining ones, so it reads as a generic primitive fish in blue. FAIL stands.

rows.readsAs: a barracuda or pike
rows.defect: There is no beak. The olive spindle simply tapers to a point at the head end; no narrow rostrum ever separates from the skull, so the single feature that makes a gar a gar is missing. The row of white teeth is a short fringe on the last sixth of the underside, sitting on a taper rather than lining a beak. No diamond armour scale pattern — the flank carries the same generic crosshatch as its neighbours — and there are no dorsal or anal fins set far back near the tail; the tail is the same blunt trapezoid paddle.
rows.fix: Give it a genuine beak: a parallel-sided rostrum a third of body length, clearly narrower than the head, with tooth rows along both jaws, then move the dorsal and anal fins to sit opposite each other right at the tail base.
rows.verifyWhy:
Looked at the 440x440 PNG at 1x, then re-cropped the head, flank and tail at 6-16x with a gamma boost and again as a background-difference silhouette map, and ran a per-column top/bottom scan of the silhouette. Measured body: x-span 91..348 (258 px long), max depth 40 px sustained from x=207..264, aspect 6.45 (spec 6.5 - proportion is fine). Head is at the RIGHT.

UPHELD, and the core of the claim is correct: THERE IS NO BEAK. The column scan shows the front end tapering smoothly and gradually from 40 px deep at x=264 to 32 px at x=300, 28 px at x=320, 25 px at x=330, 20 px at x=340, ending at x=349. Critically the snout does NOT terminate in a point (correct this part of the claim) - the diff-silhouette shows a BLUNT, ROUNDED, bullet-shaped nose still ~20-22 px deep (half the max body depth) right up to the last 3 px. It is a fat cone, not a rostrum. The eye - a small white ring with a dark pupil - sits at x~327, y~182, so the pre-orbital snout is only ~21 px = 8% of body length and about 0.75x the local body depth. A gar needs the pre-orbital rostrum at roughly 25-30% of total length and near parallel-sided at ~0.2x body depth, visibly narrower than and separated from the skull. Nothing like that is present. The taper at the head is essentially a mirror of the taper at the tail.

Teeth: ~7 small white spikes hang below the ventral edge from x~300 to x~347 (a 47 px run), pointing down/outward, lower jaw only, no upper row. The claim's 'short fringe on a taper' is accurate - they are stuck to a blunt cheek, so they read as an underbite on a blunt-headed fish, not as a toothed beak.

CORRECTION 1 - 'no far-back dorsal/anal fins' is wrong as stated. Two fins ARE drawn far back: at 9x diff-render I can see a thin dark hairline stroke above and a matching one below the caudal peduncle, each roughly 9 px long and 1-2 px thick, angled back, sitting essentially ON the base of the caudal fin rather than on the body ahead of it. They have no area and no silhouette contribution, so at 1x they read as two stray scratches, not fins. The fix is not 'add fins', it is 'give the existing far-back dorsal and anal real filled area (soft triangular/rounded lobes breaking the topline and ventral line) and shift them forward off the tail base so a gap of body shows between fin and caudal'.

CORRECTION 2 - 'generic crosshatch flank' is wrong. There is NO crosshatch anywhere. At 16x the flank is flat olive/khaki carrying (a) one pale horizontal lateral-line stripe through the mid-flank and (b) a sparse single row of very faint darker square-ish dots along the lower flank, barely above noise and invisible at 1x. So the finding is right that the diamond ganoid armour is missing, but the cause is 'flank is essentially plain with a lateral line and a faint dot row', not 'wrong pattern applied'. Needs an actual interlocking rhombic plate lattice with visible edge highlights.

CORRECTION 3 - the read. It does not read as a barracuda or a pike; both of those have a distinctly longer, wedge-pointed jaw than this. With a blunt rounded bullet nose, a forward-set eye, a plain olive body and a lower-jaw tooth fringe, it reads as a generic blunt-headed cigar fish - closest to a wolffish/blenny or a nondescript baitfish.

Other observed detail (not defects, for the record): one small dark triangular pectoral fin at x~265-285 pointing down-back, correctly placed behind the head; caudal is a rounded fan ~41x20 px with visible rays and a short peduncle - acceptable for a gar's short rounded tail; a soft drop shadow ellipse sits below the body.

Band FAIL stands: the single identity-defining must-read (long narrow toothed beak snout) is absent, a second must-read (diamond armour) is absent, and the third (far-back dorsal/anal) is present only as unreadable hairlines. Three of three must-reads fail to read.

rows.readsAs: a lamprey
rows.defect: The identity reads — the round jawless disc with concentric rings of rasping teeth is convincing, seven dark gill pores sit in a row behind the eye, and the body carries no paired fins. What is wrong is geometry: a flat opaque grey wedge lies along the whole topline from mid-body to the head, reading as a separate flat sheet floating above the eel rather than as part of its volume, and the tail end flattens into a bare strap with no caudal fin. The gill pore row also sits too far back, nearer mid-body than the head.
rows.fix: Delete or reshade the grey topline sheet so the body reads as one round tube, and finish the tail with a low continuous fin fold.

rows.readsAs: a small brown loach or minnow with a smudge for a tail
rows.defect: Nothing about this is eel-like — it is the short stubby version of the family almond, roughly 3.5:1 not the 6:1 asked for, deepest at mid-length with a blunt snub at both ends. There is no pointed continuous tail fin: the tail is a tiny black bristle brush stuck on the left end, reading as a stranded scribble rather than a fin. The thread-like filamentous limb fins are entirely absent — no filaments leave the silhouette anywhere. The brown core also sits inside an offset grey membrane halo that reads as a ghost outline rather than a body.
rows.fix: Stretch the body into a long eel and run one continuous low fin from mid-back around a pointed tail tip to the vent, then hang four long thread filaments where the paired fins belong.
rows.verifyWhy:
UPHELD, but three of the four stated causes are wrong and the fix would miss if made against them. Measured from the pixels (440x440 canvas, bg 5,6,12, column scan at delta>28): the painted silhouette runs x118-339, y157-213 = 222 x 57 px, aspect 3.9:1 against a spec of 6 -- not 3.5:1. More important, that 3.9 is the OUTER shape. The warm scaled core inside it is x133-339, y170-200 = 206 x 31 = 6.6:1, i.e. the actual fish body is already at (slightly past) the spec aspect. It reads stubby only because a second, featureless blue-grey almond ~1.8x the core's height is painted around it. So 'stubby chassis' is the wrong diagnosis; 'correct-aspect body drowned in an oversized fringe shape' is the right one.

GREY HALO -- the judge calls it 'offset'. It is NOT offset. Grey vertical centre = (157+213)/2 = 185.0; warm-core centre = (170+200)/2 = 185.0. They are exactly concentric over the whole length. The real defect is different and worth naming precisely: (a) the grey almond is completely featureless -- no rays, no membrane texture, no value break -- so it reads as a ghost/drop-shadow rather than as the continuous median fin fringe it presumably wants to be; (b) the brown core carries its own heavy bright-white keyline all the way round, so you get two closed outlines nested inside each other, which is what produces the 'double exposure' look; (c) at the head end the grey almond does not taper -- it stops in a hard vertical square cut at x~315 (clearly visible top and bottom in the head crop) about 24px short of the snout, leaving two stranded grey stubs beside the head.

TAIL -- 'tiny black bristle brush / stranded scribble' is wrong. At 18x the tail is a single smooth solid grey-brown wedge, x117-140 (~22px, ~10% of body length), ~11px tall at its base, tapering to a BLUNT squared-off tip, not a point and not strands. There are no bristles anywhere in it. The 'brush' the judge saw at 1x is the scene's pale diagonal water-streak backdrop, which happens to converge just left of the tail and blends into the wedge when downsampled. The verdict on the tail still stands for a different reason: the body ends in a fully blunt white-keylined capsule end at x~133 and the wedge is stuck on OUTSIDE that closed outline, and the grey median almond does not continue into it. So there is no 'pointed continuous tail fin' -- there is a closed pill with a low-contrast stub glued to its back end. Fix must merge the caudal into the body taper, not redraw a brush.

LIMB FINS -- 'entirely absent' is FALSE and this is the biggest error in the original claim. There is a clearly drawn pectoral fin behind the head at roughly x250-292, y172-205: a broad pale rounded lobe with a dark curved leading edge, plus a fan of about six dark radiating rays sweeping rear-and-down. It is real geometry, not a marking. What is wrong is (i) it is a generic webbed ray-fan, the opposite of the required thread-like filamentous limb, (ii) it is drawn entirely INSIDE the body silhouette so nothing protrudes past the ventral edge and at 1x it reads as a scribble on the flank, and (iii) there is only one pair -- the entire rear 60% of the fish (x150-245) is completely bare: no pelvic pair, no dorsal, no anal, nothing but checker scale texture and one lateral line. So the fix is 'replace the webbed fan with two pairs of protruding threads', not 'add missing fins'.

WHAT IS ACTUALLY THERE AND CORRECT: fine checker scale texture across the whole flank plus a lateral line (satisfies 'smooth scaled skin'); a blunt, undifferentiated head. Against that, the eye is a bold high-contrast white annulus with a black pupil, far too loud for the row's 'eyes: small', and it is the single most salient feature in the whole asset.

BAND: FAIL stands, not POLISH. Two of the three must-reads are unreadable as specified (no pointed continuous tail fin; no filamentous limb fins), the silhouette reads 35% too short because of an artifact shape, and the ghost double-outline is a rendering defect rather than a styling choice. At 1x the asset reads as an anonymous pill-shaped fish, not as a lungfish.

rows.readsAs: a swordfish or billfish
rows.defect: The rostrum is long enough but it is the wrong shape — a narrow tapering spike that comes to a point, not a broad flat spatula, so with the forked tail behind it the whole animal reads as a billfish. The cavernous gaping toothless mouth is missing entirely; the mouth is a single thin line under the eye. The flank carries the same crosshatch stipple as the scaled species in this batch, which contradicts the smooth scaleless skin.
rows.fix: Widen the rostrum into a parallel-sided flat paddle with a blunt rounded tip, and open the jaw into a wide gaping cavern behind it.

rows.readsAs: a generic tan minnow with a dark blob stuck on its nose
rows.defect: A dark grey lozenge floats at the front of the snout, barely touching it — it reads as a detached fragment or a smudge, not as a snout, a mouth or barbels. There are no barbels at all under it. The rows of bony scutes that are the whole identity of a sturgeon are absent: the back and flanks carry only the same flat crosshatch stipple used on Bowfin, Gar and Lungfish, with one generic triangular dorsal bump. The tail is a small symmetric fork, not the shark-like upturned asymmetric tail.
rows.fix: Attach a long tapered snout with four hanging barbels beneath it, then run three ridges of raised pointed scutes along the back and both flanks and make the upper tail lobe clearly longer than the lower.
rows.verifyWhy:
Verified at native size and again at 7-9x nearest-neighbour zoom on head/dorsal/tail, plus a background-subtracted 6x gain pass to hunt for faint thin geometry. The FAIL stands, but ONE OF THE THREE stated causes is factually wrong and must not be 'fixed'.

MUST-READ 1 - rows of bony scutes ridging back and flanks: ABSENT. CONFIRMED. The entire flank carries one uniform checkerboard/stipple grid of tiny same-sized square scales, edge to edge, plus a single pale continuous lateral-line stripe. There is no row of large discrete plates, no size hierarchy, no highlight-per-plate, and critically the dorsal SILHOUETTE (zoomed at 9x, x=130-260, y=158-188) is a perfectly smooth unbroken arc with a clean rim highlight - not one scute bump breaks the outline. The judge's 'same flat crosshatch stipple as its neighbours' is substantiated: I opened Paddlefish.png alongside and it is the SAME CHASSIS - identical fusiform outline, identical checkerboard stipple, identical triangular pectoral fan in the same spot, identical low-contrast dark dorsal hump, identical gill arc; only the hue differs (Sturgeon olive-tan, Paddlefish pale cyan). Note Paddlefish's own mustRead says SCALELESS smooth skin, so that stipple is a generic default painted on every member of the family, not a sturgeon decision. THIS IS THE HEADLINE DEFECT - the scute rows are the whole identity and nothing stands in for them.

MUST-READ 2 - four barbels under a long pointed snout: BARBELS ABSENT, CONFIRMED at 6x gain against a subtracted background (any 1px hair-thin barbel would have blown out to bright yellow; nothing appeared anywhere under the snout). The 'long pointed snout' half is arguably PRESENT - the head does taper to a genuine sharp point over roughly 55px, about 0.25 of body length, matching headFrac. The floating lozenge claim is CORRECT and I can give it coordinates: a flat dark-grey ellipse roughly 41x16px centred at approx (356,207), long axis horizontal, lying almost entirely FORWARD of the snout tip at approx (336,204) and overlapping it by only ~2-4px. It is ~1/3 the luminance of the body, so it does not read as continuous with the head at all - it reads as a detached dark blob parked in front of the face. Best guess at its intent: a rostrum/mouth primitive placed with a forward offset and not colour-matched or hull-merged into the head.

ADDITIONAL DEFECT THE ORIGINAL JUDGE MISSED: the eye is drawn OUTSIDE the head silhouette. The white ring with dark pupil is centred at approx (321,194); the upper edge of the snout at that x sits at y~198, so the ring floats on the dark background ABOVE the snout and is merely tangent to the outline at its bottom. Two detached elements on one head (eye ring + snout lozenge) - this looks like a shared placement bug in how head furniture is anchored when the head is a narrow taper, worth checking across the whole family rather than nudging one species.

MUST-READ 3 - shark-like upturned asymmetric tail: THE JUDGE IS WRONG. This one is PRESENT AND CORRECT. Zoomed at 8x with gain, the caudal is plainly heterocercal: fork joint at approx (118,203), upper lobe tip at approx (64,164), lower lobe tip at approx (89,225). Upper lobe length ~67px, lower lobe ~36px - a ratio of about 1.8:1, with the long lobe swept distinctly UP and back. It is neither symmetric nor especially small (it spans ~80px against a ~218px body). The only legitimate criticism of the tail is TONE, not shape: it is painted very dark, close to the background value, so at native size it reads as a faint smudge and its asymmetry is easy to miss - which is likely exactly how the judge lost it. Do not restyle this tail's geometry; lift its value/contrast so the existing correct shape is legible.

BAND: FAIL upheld. Two of three must-reads fail (scutes absent outright, barbels absent), the body is a verbatim shared chassis with its family neighbour, and two head elements are detached from the silhouette. It currently reads as generic-fish, not sturgeon. FIX ORDER: (1) real scute rows - a dorsal ridge plus one lateral row of large discrete plates that BREAK the dorsal outline, at a clearly coarser scale than the flank stipple; (2) four barbels as a ventral fringe under the snout; (3) merge the snout lozenge into the head hull and colour-match it, and re-anchor the eye inside the silhouette; (4) raise the caudal's value. Do NOT touch the tail's shape.

rows.readsAs: a generic yellow reef fish, closest to a yellow tang or a small sunfish
rows.defect: The identity must-read - a rigid armoured BOX-shaped carapace - is entirely absent. The body is a soft rounded ovoid with a continuous curved outline: no flat facets, no hard dorsal or ventral keels, no square-cut cross section, no hexagonal plate tessellation. The texture over it is ordinary curved fish scaling, not armour. The second must-read fails too: the caudal fan is large and broad rather than a tiny fin poking out of a rigid box, so nothing reads as appendages escaping a shell. The third fails as well - there are no pursed lips or any mouth whatsoever, just blank yellow where the face should end, and the eye is a small flat dot rather than a big prominent one. It is the pufferfish drawing stretched wider and recoloured yellow.
rows.fix: Redraw the body as a hard-edged box: a trapezoidal/triangular cross-section with a straight flat ventral floor, straight angled dorsal slope, visible corner ridges running nose-to-tail, and hexagonal plate tessellation over the whole carapace - then shrink the caudal and pectoral to small fins poking out of holes in that shell, and put a big eye and pursed protruding lips on a blunt squared-off face.

rows.readsAs: a round-bodied khaki fish - plausibly a puffer, but equally a discus or a small drab tang
rows.defect: The round body is roughly there, so the organism is not wrong, but two of the three must-reads are not visibly present. There are no big protruding eyes - just one small flat white dot with a pupil, sitting flush on the flank with no bulge or socket. There is no small beaked mouth: the front of the fish is completely blank, no beak, no lip line, no dental plate. The fins also work against the read - the caudal is a broad rounded fan larger than anything on a puffer, rather than tiny fluttering fins. The body is only mildly rounded (about 1.25:1) so it neither commits to the taut inflated balloon nor to the stated uninflated ovoid, and the drab khaki fill with no prickles or spot pattern gives the eye nothing else to lock onto.
rows.fix: Push the body to a near-circular taut balloon and add the two signature features at the face - a pair of bulging domed eyes standing proud of the outline and a small hard beak with a visible central seam - then shrink the caudal to a small fluttering fan.

rows.readsAs: an ordinary pet rabbit, in brown
rows.defect: The whole identity of a hare is absent. The body is a pudgy round egg, not lean or angular, and the hind legs are two short dark pegs with no hock, no elongated foot and no rangy thigh — the animal is shorter-legged than the Rabbit asset it is supposed to out-run. The ears are dark brown over their full length with no distinct black tip, so the one marking called out is not readable either. Side by side with Rabbit.png this is the same silhouette in a warmer hue.
rows.fix: Rebuild the hind limb as a long visible hock: raise the rump, drop a real thigh mass outside the belly line, add a long flat hind foot planted on the ground, and stretch the body ~25% longer so the topline reads lean rather than egg-shaped — then paint the outer third of each ear black.

rows.readsAs: a pale cream pet rabbit
rows.defect: Same chassis as Hare and Rabbit with the fill lightened. The ears are only marginally longer than the head, not enormous. The 'very long powerful hind legs' are two thin dark stubs poking from under the belly with no thigh, no hock and no foot. The eye is a small round dot sitting mid-skull just behind the muzzle, not large and not set high or far back. Two of three must-reads are simply not on the canvas.
rows.fix: Give it the sprinter's rear: a deep muscled thigh breaking the silhouette, a long angled hock, and a long hind foot on the ground — and enlarge the eye and slide it up and back toward the ear base so the skull reads jackrabbit.

rows.readsAs: a small brown rabbit
rows.defect: This is the rabbit chassis shrunk. The ears are tall pointed upright ovals — rabbit ears — when the packet note says explicitly they must be short and round, not long like a rabbit's. The rear carries the same dark comma swirl plus a protruding stub, so a tail reads where there must be none. The body is not an egg pressed to the rock: it stands on the same two pegs with clear daylight under the belly. The defining pika silhouette is entirely absent.
rows.fix: Replace the ears with two low round pale-rimmed discs set on the sides of the skull, delete the rear stub and swirl so the rump ends in a clean tailless curve, and drop the belly onto the ground so no leg gap shows.

rows.readsAs: a rabbit
rows.defect: The species a stranger would actually name — but it is carrying the family's whole silhouette on its own. The long upright ears read. The short round powder-puff tail does not exist: the rear shows the same dark brown comma swirl the other three have, with no pale round puff anywhere. The hind legs are not heavy or crouched; the haunch is a smooth undifferentiated body curve and the only leg is a thin dark peg with no foot. The white rectangle on the muzzle reads as a stuck-on paper tag rather than incisors.
rows.fix: Add a distinct pale round puff tail clear of the body outline, and separate the hind leg into a heavy folded thigh plus a planted hind foot instead of a peg.

rows.readsAs: a tan lamb or young ram with a lemur's tail stuck on
rows.defect: Every must-read is absent or inverted. The tail is banded but hangs DOWN in a limp droop off the croup — the identity trait is that it is carried straight UP like a flagpole, and the picture shows the exact opposite. The snout is a short blunt DOWN-turned ram muzzle with a forehead bump; the long, thin, UPTURNED flexible probe that names a coati is nowhere. The body is a deep barrel-chested ungulate torso on four straight vertical column legs ending in small dark cloven wedges, not a long low body on plantigrade five-toed feet. The single curled hook ear reads as a horn.
rows.fix: Rebuild the silhouette: drop the barrel to a long low tube, put the head DOWN at shoulder height on a slender neck, replace the muzzle with a narrow snout that extends well past the jaw and kinks UPWARD at the tip, rotate the banded tail to a rigid vertical flagpole, and replace the hoof wedges with flat plantigrade feet showing toes.
rows.verifyWhy:
Looked at the 440x440 PNG whole, then at 8-9x zooms of head (245,115,110x90), tail (95,175,100x100) and feet (150,215,175x85). The FAIL stands: all three must-reads fail on their defining property, and the animal reads as a tan lamb/hogget with a ringed tail hooked on. Corrections to the original claim follow.

TAIL (the identity item). The judge said it 'hangs DOWN in a limp droop'. What is actually drawn: the tail leaves the rump roughly HORIZONTALLY at hip height, rises a few pixels over the first two rings, then arcs down and FORWARD in a hook, the solid dark tip finishing at mid-thigh height, level with the belly line — a question-mark/curl, not a straight droop. That distinction matters for the fix: the whole tail has to be re-rooted and rotated to vertical from the BASE (flagpole, tip above the topline), not merely straightened at the tip. Also correcting the judge by omission: the banding itself is present and is the single most legible coati cue in the picture — 6-7 hard-edged dark-brown rings on cream, high contrast. The packet asks for a FAINTLY banded tail; this is over-contrasted, closer to a ring-tailed lemur/raccoon tail than a coati's soft bands. So the tail is not missing, it is mis-carried and over-marked.

SNOUT. The judge called it a 'short blunt down-turned ram muzzle'. Down-turned and blunt are right; 'short' is wrong and would misdirect the fix. Measured on the zoom, back-of-skull x~273, eye centre x~299, nose tip x~324 — the muzzle from the eye is ~49% of total head length, i.e. already moderately long. The defects are shape and direction, not length: it is a THICK wedge that blends into a heavy jaw with a drooping mouth-line beneath it, and the terminal tip curves DOWN with the nostril dot set on the upper-front. A coati needs that same length thinned to a narrow mobile probe with the last third turned UP past the lip. Length is the one dimension that is already near-correct.

BODY/FEET. Confirmed. Deep barrel chest, level topline barely higher at the withers, very high belly clearance, short upright neck carrying the head well above the shoulder — the low, long, hunched, nose-down foraging line of a coati is entirely absent, and the coat is painted as a woolly fleece stipple which is what pushes the read to lamb. Feet: each column leg tapers to a tiny dark rounded cap about one leg-width across, with a pale highlight on the front edge and a faint vertical split on the forefoot. These read as small dark hooves or dark socks; 'cloven wedges' is close enough but they are more blunt hoof-caps than clean cloven wedges. There is no plantigrade sole, no elongated foot, no toes and no claws anywhere.

THINGS THE JUDGE DID NOT MENTION but that a fix should address: (1) the head is painted a distinctly darker brown than the body and sits above a pale collar band, so it reads as a different animal's head glued on — this amplifies the 'lemur tail attached' impression to the whole silhouette; (2) the ear is a flat dark round disc patch flush against the skull with no pinna outline or projecting rim, plus a small notch bump at the rear of the skull outline; coati ears are small and rounded so this is not fatal, but it is drawn as a marking rather than an ear; (3) the eye is oversized with a full pale sclera ring, more lemur/bushbaby than coati (packet says eyes: normal); (4) the flank carries a faint pale vertical banding texture that could be mistaken for markings and further fights the plain-brown coati coat.

rows.readsAs: a tan fawn or lamb
rows.defect: This is the identical lamb chassis in gold-tan, and all three must-reads are missing. The tail is a thin, uniform, limp taper hanging off the croup — no thickening at the base and no coil or curl, so nothing about it reads as prehensile. The face is the same blunt down-turned ram muzzle with a forehead bump and one hook-curl ear; there is no round teddy-bear head, and although the eye has a dark iris it is a small ordinary side-mounted eye, not the huge forward-set dark eyes that are the whole face. The coat is flat straw-tan with straight brushy striations, reading as sheep fleece rather than golden woolly fur.
rows.fix: Give it a round, short-faced skull with two large forward-facing dark eyes and small round ears set low on the sides, then redraw the tail thick and muscular at the base and curled into a hook or wrapped around a branch so the prehensility is visible.

rows.readsAs: a grey lamb or a grey goat kid
rows.defect: The most recognisable mammal in North America is unrecognisable here. The back is dead FLAT and in fact slightly shoulder-high — the mandatory hunched arch with the rump riding higher than the shoulders is not just weak, it is reversed. The face carries only a soft grey smudge around the eye that blends into the grey head; there is no black BANDIT MASK, no hard-edged dark band running across both eyes bounded by white above and below, so the single trait that IS the raccoon's identity is absent. The ringed tail is present but hangs limp and low instead of arcing behind. The body is the same barrel-chested ungulate torso on straight vertical legs ending in dark cloven wedges, with the same ram muzzle and curled horn-ear.
rows.fix: Paint a hard-edged black mask band straight across the eyes from cheek to cheek with white fur above and below it, and rebuild the topline so the spine rises continuously to a rump clearly higher than the shoulders with the head carried low.

rows.readsAs: an orange lamb or a rust-coloured goat
rows.defect: Same chassis again, recoloured rust. The face is solid dark rust all over: there is no WHITE face mask, no white muzzle or brow patches, and no rust tear-stripes running down from the eyes — the facial pattern that names a red panda is entirely missing. The legs and belly are the same rust orange as the back, so the jet-black legs and black belly that make the two-tone body are absent. The tail is banded but thin, limp and drooping rather than long, thick and bushy. On top of that the silhouette is a barrel-chested hoofed grazer with a high head, a ram muzzle and a curled horn-ear, not a low-slung round-faced arboreal carnivoran.
rows.fix: Paint the face white from brow to muzzle with two rust tear-stripes descending under the eyes, then flood the legs and belly jet-black against the rust back and fatten the tail into a thick bushy plume.
rows.verifyWhy:
Verified at 4x-16x zoom on the head, tail, legs and silhouette edge. FAIL stands: two of the three mustReads are absent and the third is only half-delivered.

WHAT I SAW - SILHOUETTE. A deep barrel-ribbed body with a near-level topline, a heavy dropped brisket, a short thick neck, and a small head carried HIGH above the shoulder line. Four short straight column legs with almost no visible joint, each ending in a dark-brown rounded cap with a tiny pale claw sliver that reads as a small cloven hoof. This is a lamb/ram chassis, not a low-slung musteloid. CONFIRMED SHARED CHASSIS: Raccoon.png in the same packet is the identical body, identical leg columns, identical hoof-caps, identical head carriage and identical down-curved ringed tail, recoloured grey. Red Panda and Raccoon are one sheep in two colours, so this is a family-level defect, not a one-off.

WHAT I SAW - FACE (judge correct, with corrections to the detail). The entire head - crown, cheek, muzzle, throat and ear - is one rust/dark-rust family. There is NO white face mask, no white ear rims, no white muzzle or chin, and no pale patch of any kind above the shoulder. CORRECTION 1: the judge missed the ear form. The ear is drawn as a large CURLED SPIRAL FLAP laid over the back of the skull - a dark-rust inner volute with a lighter rust rim - and it reads unmistakably as a ram's horn; there is a second small triangular point at the far (off-side) edge of the crown. That curl is a major contributor to the ovine read and must be named in the fix. CORRECTION 2: 'no rust tear-stripes' is very slightly overstated. There IS a 1px dark hairline running from the lower-front corner of the eye down toward the muzzle, and a second dark line at the mouth. The geometry of a tear-stripe may therefore already exist, but it is drawn DARK-ON-RUST instead of RUST-ON-WHITE, is hairline thin, and is completely invisible at card size - so the marking does not read and the mustRead is not met. CORRECTION 3: the muzzle is a long tapering snout with the nose at the very tip, closer to the Coati in this same packet than to a red panda's short blunt fox face.

WHAT I SAW - COAT (judge correct). Legs, belly and back are all the same salmon-rust with the same brushed fur texture; the belly is if anything a shade LIGHTER than the back. There is zero jet-black anywhere on the limbs or underside. The only dark on the lower body is the four foot-caps. The rusty-red coat itself is present and correct; only the black two-tone is missing.

WHAT I SAW - TAIL (judge's description is WRONG here even though the mustRead still fails). The tail is NOT thin. It is a stout ringed tube roughly the thickness of a hind leg at its base, carrying about seven clearly readable bands plus a solid dark tip. Its real defects are different and the fix must target these: (a) the rings are DARK BROWN/near-black, not the PALE ochre rings the reference calls for, so it reads raccoon-tailed rather than red-panda-tailed; (b) it is far too SHORT - roughly 40% of body length where a red panda's tail is close to 100%; (c) its outline is a smooth-edged tube with no bushy fur silhouette at all; (d) it exits low off the rump and curves DOWN and FORWARD beneath the hindquarters instead of trailing long and out. So 'long bushy tail with pale rings' fails on length, bushiness and ring colour - not on thickness.

NET: 'rusty-red coat' is the only mustRead partially delivered. White mask + rust tear-stripes: absent. Jet-black legs and belly: absent. Long bushy pale-ringed tail: banded but short, smooth and dark-ringed. On a hoofed barrel-chested high-headed chassis shared verbatim with the Raccoon, the asset reads as an orange lamb with a raccoon tail. FAIL is correct.

rows.readsAs: a pale buff quail or baby chick with cartoon eyes and two little horns
rows.defect: The body is horizontal and wider than tall with a long pointed tail projecting well past the rump, so the perched-owl column the aspect 0.8 / upright posture calls for is absent. Of the must-reads only the pale sandy-buff plumage lands: the facial disc is a weak lighter patch rather than a flat dish, and the feathered legs and hooked bill are both simply missing — the legs are bare yellow wire sticks and there is no bill visible between the eyes at all.
rows.fix: Rebuild it as a vertical perched column — stand the egg upright, bring the feet forward under the chest, cut the tail to a stub that barely clears the body, and add a small hooked bill half-buried in a properly ringed facial disc with feather-trousered legs.

rows.readsAs: a grey pigeon or dove with its wings held out
rows.defect: Not one must-read is present. There is no split double crest — just a single small grey nub on the crown. The talons are the same thin yellow chicken toes as the two owls, not enormous grey grasping talons. The chest band is absent: the bird is a uniform pale grey with no black band and no white belly. The bill is a stubby yellow triangle pointing forward, the beak of a finch, where a harpy's is a huge black hook. The spread wings are two flat stiff planks with no shoulder, no primary spread and no attachment to the body, and they read as pasted-on rather than articulated.
rows.fix: Redraw from a raptor base: deep keeled chest, huge black hooked bill, massive scaled grey feet with visible curved claws gripping the ground, a divided double crest raised off a pale grey head, and a hard black chest band over a white belly.

rows.readsAs: a brown thrush or plump songbird wearing an owl mask
rows.defect: The face half-works — round head, two forward dark eyes with highlights, small pale bill, ear tufts — but the must-read that IS the identity, the upright barrel body with no visible neck, is absent: the body lies horizontal, the feet hang under the belly's middle instead of under the chest, and a long pointed tail projects far past the rump, directly contradicting the note that the tail barely projects. The facial disc is not flat or dished, it is a slightly paler oval, and the eyes are big-ish rather than the enormous eyes that should dominate the skull.
rows.fix: Stand the body up into a vertical barrel with the feet directly beneath the chest and truncate the tail to a stub, then widen the eyes until they fill most of a properly rimmed flat facial disc.

rows.readsAs: a grey paper dart or kite with cartoon eyes and a whip tail — read as a stingray only because of the barbed tail
rows.defect: A cluster of three or four soft dark blobs from the speckle/marking pass is stranded in open water outside the silhouette, off the upper-right leading edge of the disc — the spot pass is not clipped to the body, so marking fragments float beside the head. On top of that the pectoral disc, which IS the identity, is a hard-edged triangular wedge: the trailing margin is a straight square cut with sharp corners, the wingtips are knife points, there is no wing curvature, no fin-margin undulation or thickness, and no pelvic fins at the tail base. The two dark ovals below the eyes read as blank nostrils and the white-ringed googly eyes are far too prominent for the small eyes the row asks for.
rows.fix: Clip the speckle pass to the disc path so no marks land outside the silhouette, then rebuild the disc outline as a rhombic wing — concave trailing margins sweeping back from the wingtips to a narrow tail base with a pair of small pelvic fins — instead of a straight-cut triangle.

rows.readsAs: a grey draped mound / closed umbrella with cartoon eyes and a string; at best a generic cartoon stingray, never an eagle ray
rows.defect: Both must-reads that separate an eagle ray from any other ray are absent. There is no pointed duck-bill snout — the head end is a plain blunt curve, and nothing projects ahead of the body at all. The wings are not sharply pointed: the outline is one smooth convex arc with a single corner at the lower right, and the wings are folded downward so no wingspan reads in the silhouette. The whip tail is present but is roughly the same length as the body, not far longer. The disc reads narrower than it is deep, the opposite of a ray. The whole shape is pixel-for-pixel the Manta Ray and Stingray drawing in a different grey.
rows.fix: Redraw from a three-quarter-above view with the pectorals spread flat and swept back into two sharp acute wingtips wider than the body is long, add a distinct pointed duck-bill rostrum jutting clearly ahead of the wing leading edges, and extend the whip tail to at least twice the disc length.

rows.readsAs: a dark blue-grey draped mound with googly eyes — the identical shape to the Eagle Ray, only darker
rows.defect: The packet's own note warns against a near-side view, and that is exactly what was drawn: the wings are folded down into a drooping skirt so the huge triangular wingspan — the single feature that makes a manta a manta — never appears. There are no cephalic horn lobes flanking the head, and no wide terminal mouth; the front of the head is a featureless blunt curve with cartoon eyes sitting on top like a stingray's. The wings are not triangular or pointed, just one smooth convex arc. The silhouette is indistinguishable from the Eagle Ray in this same batch, so nothing but hue tells the two apart.
rows.fix: Draw from above/front with the pectorals spread into two long sharply pointed triangles wider than the body is long, and put two forward-projecting horn-like cephalic lobes on either side of a wide rectangular terminal mouth at the front of the head.

rows.readsAs: a stingray — the tan colour, spotted skin, top-mounted eyes and barbed whip tail get a stranger to the right answer
rows.defect: It gets there on colour and tail rather than on form. The disc is not a flat kite of fused pectorals: it is the same drooping rounded mound as the other two, so the wing spread and the kite corners never read, and the body looks deeper than it is wide. The barb is a single pale spearhead stuck on the very tip of the tail rather than a serrated spine set on the tail's upper surface. Eyes are correctly on top, but they are oversized white cartoon discs and the grey ovals beneath them read as a second pair of eyes. The tail also emerges from under the belly rather than from a defined tail base at the rear of the disc.
rows.fix: Flatten and spread the pectorals into a wide kite-shaped disc seen from above, wider than long with clear side corners, and move the barb onto the upper surface of the tail a third of the way along, serrated rather than a spearhead tip.

rows.readsAs: a tall yellow discus / freshwater angelfish
rows.defect: The deep striped disc and the long trailing filaments off the dorsal and anal are genuinely there and read well, but there is no mouth drawn at all and no spine on the gill cover, and the disc is drawn tall-and-narrow with vertical stripes so it reads as the FRESHWATER triangular angelfish the note explicitly rules out rather than a Pomacanthid. The 'tail' is a flat trapezoid stuck on the right edge with no peduncle joining it to the body.
rows.fix: Give it a small terminal mouth and a visible backward-pointing spine on the gill cover, and round the disc toward circular with a horizontal or arcing band pattern so it stops reading as a freshwater angel.

rows.readsAs: a tiny needlefish or gar
rows.defect: All three must-reads are absent. The head is not a blunt bulldog head — it tapers to a sharp point with the eye stuck on the very tip; there are no cirri tufts anywhere above the eyes; and the dorsal is not a single long continuous fin down the whole back but four sawtooth triangles confined to the middle third, the same crest stamp used on the disc fish. The whole animal is also rendered at roughly a fifth of the frame width, a fragment floating in a large empty canvas with its cast shadow detached far below it.
rows.fix: Rebuild the head as a short, tall, blunt bulldog snout with the bulging eyes set high on it and a pair of branched cirri tufts rising above them, and replace the sawtooth crest with one unbroken low dorsal running nape to tail base.

rows.readsAs: a yellow disc fish with an eyespot
rows.defect: The near-circular plate body is right, but the dark bar that masks the eye is absent — instead the dark wedge sits back near the tail and the eye itself is drawn as a large white-ringed target mid-flank, which is the exact opposite of the concealing bar. The pointed tweezer snout is a tiny yellow nub barely protruding past the body outline. The dorsal is the shared sawtooth crest, and the whole silhouette is the family chassis in yellow.
rows.fix: Run a solid dark vertical bar down through the eye from the nape to the throat and extend the snout into a long narrow forceps that is clearly longer than it is deep.

rows.readsAs: a plain red aquarium fish
rows.defect: The oversized white-ringed eye and the short deep red body do read, but the two clearly separate dorsal fins are not there — there is one soft rounded hump on the back and nothing else — and the large mouth is absent entirely, replaced by the same scribed jaw wedge every other fish in this batch has. Body, texture, eye and shadow are the shared chassis.
rows.fix: Split the back into two distinctly separated dorsals with a clear gap of bare topline between them, and draw an actual large oblique mouth opening at the snout instead of a scribed wedge.

rows.readsAs: a plain orange sunfish
rows.defect: The single feature that makes a clownfish a clownfish — three white bands edged in black — is completely absent. The body is uniform orange with only the shared hatch texture on it, not one band of any colour. The fins are not rounded paddles either: it wears the batch's five-tooth sawtooth crest on the back. What is left is the family chassis recoloured orange, and it is the same drawing as Parrotfish with a different hue.
rows.fix: Paint the three black-edged white bands — behind the head, mid-body, and on the caudal peduncle — and swap the sawtooth crest for rounded paddle fins.

rows.readsAs: a blue damselfish or a blue cichlid
rows.defect: The deep compressed oval and the forked tail are present and this is one of the closer reads in the batch, but the dorsal is not a single continuous fin — it is the shared row of four detached sawtooth triangles with bare topline showing between them. It is also indistinguishable from Tang and Surgeonfish except for the exact shade of blue.
rows.fix: Join the dorsal spines with a continuous membrane so the fin runs unbroken from nape to tail base.

rows.readsAs: a small pale minnow
rows.defect: The two separate dorsal fins are actually there as two small humps with a gap between them, and the eye is set high, but the belly is completely bare — there is no fused pelvic suction disc, no pelvic fins at all — and the head is not big or blunt: the body tapers to a point at the snout exactly as it does at the tail, giving a symmetric spindle with no head mass. It shares that spindle with Blenny and Wrasse.
rows.fix: Add the fused pelvic disc as a visible oval sucker on the underside beneath the pectoral, and widen and blunt the front third into a broad frog-like head with the two eyes set close together on top.

rows.readsAs: a sea urchin, or a tick
rows.defect: This is not a fish silhouette at all. It is a red-brown ellipse with straight white and red quills radiating in every direction — forward, backward, up and down — with no tail fin, no caudal peduncle, no head separated from the body and only a single dot for an eye. The zebra banding is present, but the fan of dorsal spines reads as an all-around spine halo and the feathery separated pectoral rays are absent (the forward and rear quills are the same stiff needles as the dorsal ones). A stranger names an urchin or a mite before they name a fish.
rows.fix: Rebuild the fish silhouette first — a banded oval body with a real head, mouth and a fanned caudal fin — then restrict the long quills to a dorsal fan above the back and give the pectorals broad feathered, membraned rays sweeping out sideways like wings.

rows.readsAs: a cyan sunfish; the Clownfish drawing in a different colour
rows.defect: None of the three must-reads is present. There is no beak — no fused tooth plate, no mouth of any kind, just the shared scribed jaw wedge; the forehead is not blunt or bulging but the same gently tapering almond nose every disc fish in this batch has; and there are no large paddle pectorals for rowing, only the single shared belly lobe. Pixel for pixel this is the Clownfish silhouette recoloured cyan.
rows.fix: Give it a heavy fused parrot beak with a visible seam between upper and lower plates, and steepen the forehead into a blunt vertical bulge above it.

rows.readsAs: a spotted yellow disc fish
rows.defect: The oval compressed body, the spotting, the small protruding snout nub and the spiny dorsal row are all at least gesturally present, so this is one of the better reads — but the snout is a stub with no mouth on it rather than a rabbit-like face, and the fish is otherwise the identical chassis, texture, eye and crest as Butterflyfish and Tang with a different fill.
rows.fix: Extend the snout into a short concave rabbit muzzle with a tiny terminal mouth actually drawn at its tip, and lengthen the dorsal spine row so it runs the full back rather than one third.

rows.readsAs: a pale blue disc fish; the Tang drawing in a lighter blue
rows.defect: The scalpel spine at the base of the tail — the feature the whole family is named for and the one thing that distinguishes it from every other oval reef fish — is nowhere on the image; the caudal peduncle is bare. The forehead is not steep, it is the same gentle almond taper, and the dorsal is the shared four-tooth crest on the middle third rather than a long low fin running the whole back. With all three must-reads gone what remains is the chassis, and it is the same drawing as Tang two rows down.
rows.fix: Draw the white scalpel blade as a clear contrasting lancet on the caudal peduncle, and replace the crest with one long low dorsal membrane running nape to tail.

rows.readsAs: a blue tang, or just a blue fish
rows.defect: The round plate body and the big swept tail are there and the royal blue helps it land near a blue tang, but the sharp tail-base spine is absent, the snout is a blunt rounded taper rather than a small pointed grazing mouth, and the tail is a broad triangular sweep rather than a crescent. It is the Surgeonfish and Damselfish drawing in a third blue.
rows.fix: Add the black-outlined tail-base spine and pull the snout out into a small pointed grazing beak, then cut the tail's trailing edge concave into a true crescent.

rows.readsAs: a teal sunfish
rows.defect: Every must-read fails. The eyes are not set far back and high away from the mouth — the single eye sits right at the snout tip, as close to the mouth as it can get; there is no erectile trigger spine on the forehead at all, just two soft rounded humps well behind the head; and the body is a plump symmetric oval, not a leathery diamond, with no rowing second dorsal and anal fins (the second dorsal is a small blob and the anal is the shared belly lobe). It is the Clownfish/Parrotfish silhouette in teal.
rows.fix: Push the eye far back and high onto the upper rear of the skull, well separated from the mouth, plant an erect trigger spine on the forehead, and re-cut the body into an angular diamond with tall symmetric soft dorsal and anal fins.

rows.readsAs: a barracuda or a small piranha
rows.defect: The cigar body is right, but the dentition is drawn as a row of about seven big white sawtooth fangs running the whole jaw line, which reads as a predatory barracuda rather than a pair of protruding buck teeth, and the large fan pectoral fins that are supposed to be doing the swimming are absent entirely — there is no pectoral fin on the flank at all. Body, hatch texture and tail are the shared elongate spindle it uses with Blenny and Goby.
rows.fix: Cut the fang row down to two forward-jutting buck incisors at the front of the snout and add a large rounded fan pectoral behind the gill, angled mid-stroke so it reads as the propulsion.

rows.readsAs: a crouched brown cartoon rabbit
rows.defect: The must-read that IS the agouti — slender delicate legs with hoof-like claws under a high rump — is absent: the body is the shared ball and the legs are two stubby dark pegs poking out of the belly outline with no joint, no length and no foot. Erect pink-lined ears and a whiskered wedge face complete the rabbit read.
rows.fix: Redraw the legs as long thin two-segment columns that leave the silhouette at a visible shoulder and hip, ending in three small dark hoof-like nails, and raise the body clear of the ground so the leg length is the first thing seen.

rows.readsAs: a beaver, mostly — or an otter carrying a beaver's tail
rows.defect: The flat crosshatched paddle tail lands and this is the only asset off the family chassis, but the body is long, low and otter-like rather than stocky and humped, and the big orange chisel incisors are simply not drawn — the muzzle is closed and blank, so the single most recognisable rodent feature is missing.
rows.fix: Add two blunt orange incisors protruding below the upper lip and lift the mid-back into a hump so the shoulder sits lower than the loin.

rows.readsAs: the Agouti image again, a brown cartoon rabbit
rows.defect: Pixel-for-pixel this is the Agouti chassis with a marginally different flank shade. The blunt squared-off brick head that IS the capybara is absent — the head is a small round wedge with a tapered whiskered muzzle and erect pointed ears — and a stub tail is visible where the reference says none. The barrel body sits on peg stubs with no hint of a webbed foot, and the eyes/ears/nostrils are not set high on the skull.
rows.fix: Replace the head with a deep rectangular brick, muzzle squared off at the front, and push the eye, ear and nostril up onto the top plane of that brick; delete the tail stub.

rows.readsAs: a plain brown rabbit with a squirrel tail glued on
rows.defect: The bold dark-and-pale back and face stripes — the entire identity of a chipmunk — are completely absent; the coat is an unbroken flat brown gradient from nose to rump. There are no cheek pouches either. All that survives is a tail held up behind, on the same shared ball body as Agouti and Capybara.
rows.fix: Paint the stripe set on: five dark dorsal stripes separated by cream ones running shoulder to rump, plus the dark eye-stripe and pale brow stripe on the face.

rows.readsAs: a grey cartoon rabbit with a thick curled tail
rows.defect: There is no patagium anywhere in the image — no skin flap, no membrane, no wrist-to-ankle edge, and no gap between body and flap. Without it this is just the family ball body tinted grey. The tail is a fat round tube, not a flattened feather-like blade, and the eyes are the small standard chassis dot rather than enormous black domes.
rows.fix: Draw the gliding membrane as a taut sail spanning from the front peg down and back to the rear peg, with a visible free edge outside the body silhouette, and flatten the tail into a wide leaf.

rows.readsAs: a small tan rodent, roughly right
rows.defect: The body-length thin tail is present, but it ends in a bare point — the dark tuft at the tip that the reference calls out is missing. The elongated hind feet are also absent; the hind limb is the same short dark peg used across the family, so there is no long springing foot to see, and the face is the shared blunt wedge rather than a pointed one.
rows.fix: Add a dark brush tuft to the last third of the tail and lengthen the hind foot into a visible long sole resting flat on the ground.

rows.readsAs: a grey-brown cartoon rabbit
rows.defect: Two of the three must-reads are absent and the third is inverted. There are no huge protruding orange incisors — only the family's tiny white two-tooth block tucked inside the lip — and no oversized digging claws, because the forelimb is a featureless dark peg with no foot on it at all. The body is the shared high-rumped ball, not a cylindrical neckless tube, and the erect pointed ears read rabbit.
rows.fix: Push two large orange incisors outside the lip line so they are visible against the background, and give the forefoot a fan of long pale digging claws roughly a third the length of the leg.

rows.readsAs: a tree squirrel, or a rabbit with a squirrel tail
rows.defect: The tail is exactly what the reference forbids — a thick plume arching up and over the back — instead of a thin, short, sparsely furred one. The body is the family ball with a high domed rump rather than a long low tubular one, so the low tube silhouette that separates a ground squirrel from a tree squirrel is nowhere in the picture. Ears are moderate, not tiny.
rows.fix: Swap the arched plume for a short thin tail carried low and straight behind, and stretch the body into a long low tube with the shoulder and rump at the same height.

rows.readsAs: a rabbit, though the loaf body is in the right neighbourhood
rows.defect: The tailless loaf and the near-hidden legs land, but the ears are the family's erect pointed pink-lined rabbit ears instead of the drooping petals that define a cavy, the muzzle is a tapered whiskered wedge rather than blunt and rounded, and a small dark tail stub is visible under the rump where there should be none.
rows.fix: Replace the erect ears with small folded petals drooping sideways off the top of the skull, blunt the muzzle, and remove the tail stub.

rows.readsAs: a small yellow rabbit or gerbil
rows.defect: The rounded neckless body and near-absent tail are right, but the bulging cheek pouches are missing entirely — the cheek is a smooth unbroken curve — and the muzzle is the family's tapered whiskered wedge rather than a blunt short one. The erect pointed ears are too tall and too pointed for a hamster and push the read toward rabbit.
rows.fix: Swell the lower cheek into two visible pouches that widen the head below the eye, and shorten and round the ears.

rows.readsAs: a cream-coloured rabbit on all fours
rows.defect: The reference says biped, standing on stilt hind legs several times the front ones with the forelimbs tucked at the chest — the render is a plain quadruped on four equal-length pegs, standing exactly like every other animal in the batch. The tail is thinner than the body and SHORTER than it, with no black-and-white tuft, and the eyes are the ordinary chassis dot rather than huge round ones.
rows.fix: Rebuild it as a biped: hind legs three to four times the forelimb with a long visible foot, forelimbs tiny and tucked at the chest, and a tail well over body length ending in a black band and a white tip.

rows.readsAs: a fat brown rodent, close enough
rows.defect: The fat round furry body works, but the ears are not buried in the coat — they stand up as the family's dark pointed ears, clear of the head outline — and a dark tail stub is plainly visible under the rump instead of being almost invisible. The coat is a smooth gradient with no fur texture, so 'furry' is asserted rather than shown.
rows.fix: Sink the ears into the fur so only a small rounded tip breaks the head outline, and hide the tail stub inside the rump silhouette.

rows.readsAs: a grey rabbit
rows.defect: This is precisely the shape the reference note forbids — a squat guinea-pig ball. The long slim deer-like legs that are the whole point of a mara are absent; the animal stands on the same four short dark pegs as the rest of the batch with the belly almost touching the ground. Only the tall ears survive, and on this body they read as rabbit rather than as a hare-antelope hybrid.
rows.fix: Raise it onto long slender two-segment legs with a clear knee and hock, roughly as long as the body is deep, and slim the barrel so daylight shows under the belly.

rows.readsAs: a tan rodent blob, plausibly a marmot
rows.defect: The fat barrel on very short legs is the one must-read that lands, and it lands only because the shared chassis happens to be that shape. The head is not blunt and rounded — it is the family's tapered whiskered wedge with an exposed incisor block — and the tail is a bare dark peg with no fur on it rather than a short furry brush.
rows.fix: Blunt and deepen the skull so the muzzle stops at a rounded front plane, and thicken the tail into a short furred brush.

rows.readsAs: a chinchilla or small rabbit with a long thin tail; 'mouse' is reachable but only because of the tail
rows.defect: The pointed twitching snout is absent - the muzzle is a blunt rounded wedge ending in a white square incisor block. The ears are not large round thin discs; they are tall upright pointed pink-lined rabbit ears. The body is a fat egg roughly 1.4 wide to tall instead of the specified 2.8, so there is no long low mouse body. The naked tail is present but reads as a smooth thin curl leaving the rump and is noticeably shorter than the body, not as long as it.
rows.fix: Draw the head as a long tapering cone that narrows to a point past the eye, and replace the upright pointed ears with two large thin round discs set low and wide on the skull.

rows.readsAs: a spiny rodent - porcupine or hedgehog - but the spines look like a bundle of straw stuck into its shoulder
rows.defect: The quills are a pale starburst fan clumped over the SHOULDER and mid-back, radiating up and FORWARD, with several spikes crossing over the neck and poking out in front of the body outline. The rump - where the quills are supposed to be longest - is completely bare, and there is no quilled tail at all. The quills are unbanded pale straw straws, not long banded quills, and the arrangement is exactly the evenly-radiating hedgehog look the reference note warns against.
rows.fix: Move the whole quill mass back over the hips and sweep every quill backward along the topline toward the tail, longest at the rump, and add a short quill-tipped tail.

rows.readsAs: a tan rabbit
rows.defect: The identity must-read - small rounded ears flat to the head - is absent and replaced with two tall upright pointed pink-lined ears standing well above the skull, which is the single loudest shape in the image and reads rabbit. There is no tail visible at all, not even the stubby one specified. The body is the family egg, not a plump cylinder, and the animal is drawn mid-run on peg legs rather than the upright alert stance anyone recognises a prairie dog by.
rows.fix: Replace the tall ears with two tiny rounded ears set low and pressed flat into the fur, and add a short black-tipped stub tail at the rump.

rows.readsAs: the same animal as the Mouse asset, one shade darker - a chinchilla-ish blob with a thin tail
rows.defect: This is pixel-for-pixel the Mouse chassis with a slightly darker fur ramp; nothing distinguishes the two assets. The pointed snout with long whiskers is absent - blunt wedge and the same three short whisker lines. The hunched arched back is absent; the topline is the same smooth family dome. The tail is thin and smooth with no scale banding and reads about half the body length, not as long as the body, and the body itself is the 1.4 family egg rather than the specified 2.6.
rows.fix: Lengthen and thicken the tail past the body length with visible scale rings, and break the smooth dome topline into a distinct hunched arch over the shoulders with a longer pointed muzzle.

rows.readsAs: a grey chinchilla or rabbit with a club stuck to its rump
rows.defect: All three must-reads fail. The tail is a thick smooth grey sausage with a lighter stripe down it, angled up and away to the left - it is not bushy, has no plume edge or hair separation, and does not arch over the back at all. The animal is not sitting on its haunches and holds nothing in its forepaws; it is the same running quadruped egg on two peg stubs as every other asset here. The eye is the same small white-dotted dot, not the large dark eye, and the ears are the family's tall pointed rabbit ears rather than rounded. Rendered at the family aspect, so the tail never makes it read taller than long as specified.
rows.fix: Sit it up on its haunches with forepaws at the chest holding a nut, and redraw the tail as a wide ragged-edged plume curving up and forward over the spine to head height.

rows.readsAs: a taupe rabbit
rows.defect: The must-read that separates a vole from everything else - ears half-buried in fur - is absent and inverted: the asset carries the family's tall upright pointed pink-lined ears standing clear above the skull. No tail is visible at all, so the stubby short tail is not readable as a stubby tail so much as a missing one. The blunt rounded muzzle is the only must-read present, and it is the same blunt wedge every animal in the batch has. Strip the colour and this is the Mouse asset with the tail deleted.
rows.fix: Sink the ears to two small rounded nubs barely breaking the fur line of the skull, and add a short visible stub tail so the rump does not read as tailless.

rows.readsAs: a brown rabbit - indistinguishable from the Vole asset except for hue
rows.defect: Two of three must-reads are absent. The small ears almost buried in fur are instead the family's tall upright pointed ears clear of the skull, and the short furred tail about half the body length is nowhere on the image - the rump ends bare. The chubby blunt face is present only as the same generic blunt wedge shared by all seven. Side by side with the Vole asset the only difference is the brown, so the batch spends two slots on one drawing.
rows.fix: Add a distinctly furred tapering tail about half the body length trailing from the rump and shrink the ears to fur-buried nubs.

rows.readsAs: a small olive-green agave or aloe rosette — a spiky succulent, not a vegetable
rows.defect: Every must-read is absent. There is NO root: nothing red, nothing round, nothing half out of the soil — the image is a leaf fan and a faint ground shadow, full stop. There are no crimson stalks and no crimson veins; the veins are drawn in a darker olive of the same hue as the blade, and no stalk is visible anywhere because the blades spring straight from a hidden hub. The blades are narrow pointed lanceolate spears with straight edges, the opposite of broad glossy heart-shaped wavy-puckered beet leaves, and the whole rosette is flat and outspread rather than upright on long petioles. Colour is a uniform pale yellow-olive with no maroon flush at all.
rows.fix: Draw the organism the reference describes: seat a round-to-top-shaped deep purple-red root half out of the soil with a slender tail below it, and rebuild the foliage as broad heart-shaped puckered blades on long visible crimson petioles with crimson veins running into a dark green maroon-flushed blade.

rows.readsAs: a carrot — the tapering root plus green top gets there, though the root looks like a wafer ice-cream cone
rows.defect: The taproot is pale tan-gold, not orange — it is desaturated to about the colour of raw pastry, and its sides are dead-straight with a hard flat cut across the top, so it reads as a cone rather than a shouldered root. There is no green shoulder where root meets leaves; the junction is a hard horizontal edge with a visible gap of dark background above it. The fine side hairs are three rigid straight sticks, all on the left side only, projecting downward like snapped twigs rather than fine rootlets around the whole root. The carrot-top is not feathery: it is an open wireframe lattice of small stroked crosses arranged on a regular diagonal grid, reading as chain-link fencing or a snowflake mesh instead of finely divided thread-like segments, and no grooved stalks connect it to the root.
rows.fix: Warm the root to true carrot orange, taper it with a slightly convex shoulder that greens where the petioles emerge, and replace the cross-hatch lattice top with soft filled feathery frond silhouettes on visible stalks.

rows.readsAs: a dark cartoon otter pup or spotted newt toy, nearly invisible against the background
rows.defect: The identity IS uniform glossy jet-black skin, and the body is painted with a scatter of ochre-yellow spots - the exact marking of a fire salamander, so it reads as the wrong species. Nothing is glossy: the skin is flat matte with no wet highlight, and the near-black value on a near-black field makes the tail and hind legs merge completely into the backdrop. The tail is a flat dark wedge lifted off the ground, not a rounded tail. The head is the family's big-eyed smiling bulb, not a blunt amphibian skull, and it is the same drawing as the generic Salamander asset in this same batch with the paint darkened.
rows.fix: Delete every spot and repaint the body a single unbroken jet-black raised off the background value, then add a hard specular sheen strip along the spine and skull to sell the glossy wet skin.
rows.verifyWhy:
UPHELD, but two of the three stated causes are wrong and the worst defect is misscoped. WHAT I SAW (read at native, then re-read at 2x with gain 3.5 / gamma 0.55, plus 5-6x crops of head, limbs and tail, plus pixel sampling).

1) IDENTITY — CONFIRMED, this is the decisive failure. Component-labelled the warm pixels: NINE discrete ochre/cream spot blobs (76-203px each) sit on the shoulder, dorsum and flank at (319,185) (279,192) (215,193) (194,195) (292,202) (213,206) (279,210) (231,215), plus a tenth on the cheek just behind the jaw at (346,228). Salamandra atra's entire diagnosis is UNIFORM unbroken glossy black; a spot scatter is Salamandra salamandra, which is item #4 of this same batch (the packet's own note calls #4 'a fire/spotted salamander'). MustRead 1, 'glossy jet-black moist skin', is broken by the paint job. Within the batch, #1 and #4 are the same organism in two hues.

2) 'Generic Salamander with the paint darkened' — CONFIRMED AND QUANTIFIED. Silhouette masks of Alpine_Salamander.png vs Salamander.png give IoU 0.845. Shared verbatim: the same trunk topline, the same tail (same length, same upward hook at the tip), the same ovoid skull, the same white rim-stroke arc over the crown, the same eye glyph, the same four limb stations, the same ground-shadow ellipse. Only the base hue (slate-black vs tan) and the spot seed differ. This is one chassis, repainted.

3) 'The skin is flat matte with no wet sheen' — WRONG AS STATED. There IS a gloss treatment, and it is the brightest thing on the asset: a hard white specular stroke runs the full dorsal ridge from mid-back to the snout, a second white crescent arcs over the crown and brow of the skull, and a broad pale-grey highlight band lies along the top of the trunk. The real fault is different: the rim is a hard-edged OUTLINE stroke, not a blooming wet specular, and the interior of the flank is a single flat value with no form modelling, so the gloss reads as a cartoon keyline rather than a moist surface. Fix the note to 'gloss is an outline stroke; add interior specular falloff', not 'add sheen'.

4) 'Tail and hind legs vanish into the backdrop' — right direction, wrong scope, and understated. Sampled: body base is RGB(9,10,13); backdrop next to it is RGB(5,6,12)-(7,11,17). Mean luminance of the trunk interior is 11.92 against a backdrop mean of 13.65 — the BODY IS ACTUALLY DARKER THAN THE SKY, by ~2 levels of 255. The tail (8,9,12) and the legs (6,9,12 / 3,3,4) are no worse than the trunk; the trunk only looks legible because the white keyline outlines it. Lightening only the tail and hind legs would not fix this — the whole silhouette needs to be lifted off the field, or the backdrop dropped, or the keyline extended around the tail and limbs.

5) DEFECTS THE JUDGE DID NOT NAME. (a) POSTURE: the row specifies 'sprawling' and it is not drawn. The 5x crop of the limbs shows four columnar limbs dropping straight down beneath the trunk, ending in dark wedge/boot feet, with the belly held clear of the ground — mammal-erect carriage, no lateral elbow/knee splay, no splayed soft toes. This is the pony-chassis limb model, not an amphibian's. (b) EYES: the row says eyes 'prominent' and mustRead says 'bulging'. The 6x head crop shows a SMALL flat white ring with a dark pupil, sitting flush inside the head silhouette; it never domes out of the skull profile. It is legible (it is white on black) but it is not bulging, and it is the identical glyph on the generic.

6) WHAT IS ACTUALLY MET: 'blunt rounded head' — yes, a clean blunt ovoid skull with a curved mouth line, no snout point. 'Rounded tail' — yes, thick, smoothly tapering, upcurved at the tip, roughly body length. Those two must-reads pass; the failure is mustRead 1 plus the posture and eye specs.

BAND: FAIL. The single most identity-defining must-read (uniform jet black) is contradicted by the artwork, the asset is provably a repaint of the batch's generic, and the whole body sits below backdrop luminance.

And a large open eye with white sclera, black pupil and a specular highlight is drawn on the head, which the reference explicitly forbids ('eyes are absent or buried under skin - never draw open eyes').
