Looked at the 440x440 PNG, then re-cropped and magnified the head (8x and 20x), the neck, the feet (6x) and the tail (6x). The FAIL stands, but two of the four stated causes are described wrongly and one more defect went unnamed.

CONFIRMED - GILLS ABSENT (the defining must-read). There is no feathery/branched structure anywhere at the neck. The head simply tapers into the trunk through a smooth cream-yellow band; nothing projects from the silhouette behind the skull. I verified this numerically as well as visually: scanning all 193,600 pixels for any red-dominant colour (R exceeding max(G,B) by more than 20) returns SEVEN pixels, all of them cream antialias between a yellow trunk spot and the white body (240,218,175). There is not one blood-red pixel in the image. The single feature that makes an olm / Texas blind salamander recognisable is not present in any form, large or small.

What is drawn is a bare round black pupil about 8px across with a small white specular highlight at its upper-left, sitting directly on the white skin of the head - the 'white' the judge read as sclera is just the head. It is nonetheless unmistakably an open, staring eye, and the reference row says eyes:hidden with the note 'Eyes are absent or buried under skin - never draw open eyes'. Explicit prohibition violated. CONFIRMED - SPOTS. Six pale ochre/khaki blotches sit on the trunk (the tail itself is clean), plus a cream band at the neck. On a 'chalk-white unpigmented skin' must-read these are wrong, and they are the same shared spot pass the other salamanders in this batch carry.

WRONG - THE GREY SHAPE IS NOT A TAIL DUPLICATE. It is not tail-shaped at all. It is a single large FLAT OPAQUE grey ellipse/lobe, uniform RGB(137,130,130) with no gradient and no shading of any kind, roughly 115x75px, centred on the tail base and straddling the tail both ABOVE and BELOW it so the real tail runs diagonally through its middle. It reads as a stray unclipped body-part primitive (a fin/membrane blank, or a shadow ellipse drawn into the wrong layer at the wrong depth), not as a copy of the tail. It is a real and serious silhouette defect - it is the second-largest shape in the image - but it must be diagnosed as an unclipped/mis-depth flat primitive or the fix will be aimed at the wrong code.

Band: with the one identity-defining must-read (red external gills) completely absent, an explicit 'never draw' violated, the head domed instead of flat, and a large flat grey primitive punched through the silhouette, this does not read as a blind salamander - it reads as a pale cartoon newt with a smiley face. rows.readsAs: a brown cartoon otter cub or river-mammal mascot
rows.defect: All three must-reads are missing or inverted. The head is a narrow rounded egg in profile, taller than it is wide, with a smiling mouth - not a broad flattened shovel. The flanks are smooth and spotted with no wrinkled fleshy skin folds at all, which is the texture the whole animal is known for. And instead of tiny lidless dot eyes it carries the family's enormous white-sclera cartoon eye with a highlight, the exact opposite of the spec. Nothing about the silhouette says giant or aquatic; it is the generic Salamander asset in a lighter brown, with the same twig legs, same paddle tail and same duplicated tail ghost behind it.

rows.verifyWhy:
I tried to break this FAIL and could not. Verified at 1x, then cropped and nearest-neighbour upscaled the head (6x and 10x), the flank (8x), the feet and the tail (7x), and pixel-measured features against the generic Salamander, Alpine and Blind assets. Packet row: aspect 5.5 / headFrac 0.24 / eyes small / posture sprawling / mustRead 'broad flattened shovel head - wrinkled fleshy skin folds along the flanks - tiny lidless dot eyes'. No note row.

MUST-READ 1 (broad flattened shovel head) - ABSENT, and the FAIL's description is accurate. At 10x the skull is a plain smooth egg: a domed crown falling to a rounded snout tip, no flattening of the cranial roof, no widened lateral jaw line, no squared shovel muzzle, no separation between cranium and snout. Measured in source pixels the head oval runs roughly x 307-387 by y 177-233, i.e. about 80 long x 56 tall = 1.4:1 in side view; a shovel-headed cryptobranchid at this scale should read as a low wedge nearer 2.5-3:1 with a blunt squared front. The mouth is a single thin upcurved arc that stops well short of the snout tip - a smile, exactly as claimed - where the defining giant-salamander feature is a huge near-straight gape running almost the full head length.

MUST-READ 2 (wrinkled fleshy skin folds along the flanks) - ABSENT. At 8x the flank is a clean unbroken ovoid: one soft lighter dorsal band along the topline and a scatter of soft gold-tan blob spots, and nothing else. Zero fold contours, zero costal grooves, zero lateral frill. Worse than merely absent - the gold spot scatter is the fire/spotted-salamander marking lifted straight off the generic Salamander asset, so the flank actively transmits the WRONG signal (a spotted fire salamander) rather than just failing to transmit the right one. Any fix must remove the gold spots as well as add the folds.

MUST-READ 3 (tiny lidless dot eyes) - ABSENT and inverted, exactly as claimed. The eye is a bright white annulus with a black pupil, measured bbox 13x13 px at x343-355 / y190-202, about 16% of head length. Hard cross-asset proof that this is a shared primitive and not a species choice: generic Salamander eye white measures 12x13 at y191-203, Alpine 11x11 at y192-202 - same size, same vertical seat, same white-sclera cartoon construction on all three, despite the packet asking Alpine for 'prominent' and Giant for 'small'. The eyes token is driving nothing.

WHERE THE FAIL IS IMPRECISE (correct these before quoting it as the fix spec): 'It is the generic Salamander asset in a lighter brown' is overstated. The two are not the same render. The Giant is genuinely longer-bodied (creature bbox 329x81 px vs the generic's much stubbier trunk; packet aspect 5.5 vs 3.5), its head is proportionally larger (headFrac 0.24 vs 0.17), its tail is a thicker blunt cylinder, and it carries an extra large dark elliptical mass sitting behind and under the tail base that the generic does not have - a soft unshaped smudge that may be intended as a compressed caudal fin but reads as a shading blob, not as anatomy. So the difference is more than colour: length, head fraction and tail mass all differ. What is genuinely shared is every identity-bearing primitive - egg skull, white-ring eye, smiling mouth arc, four short dark stub limbs, dorsal band, gold spot scatter, ground-shadow ellipse. The verdict stands on that: parameters were varied, the chassis was not, and all three must-reads are missing.

One small credit the FAIL did not give: posture and aspect are correct-ish - the animal is low, long and sprawling with four short splayed limbs, and the rim light on the topline is clean. The failure is entirely in the three identity features, not in the pose or the paint quality.

rows.readsAs: a spotted amphibian-ish cartoon critter, though a stranger might first say otter or axolotl toy
rows.defect: The strongest of the four and the one the other three are clearly copied from - the skin is correctly smooth, scaleless and unclawed, the ochre spots sell a fire/spotted salamander, and the tail is about body length. But the limbs fail the 'four short splayed limbs' must-read: they are thin vertical twigs dropping straight down from the belly midline with no elbow or knee and no outward sprawl, so the animal stands like a table rather than sprawling. The tail is a fat comma-shaped paddle lifted clear off the ground rather than a long rounded tail resting behind the body, and a duplicate ghost of it sits stranded behind the real one. The trunk is too short and too deep and the head is an oversized smiling bulb with one huge cartoon eye.
rows.fix: Rebuild the limbs to leave the silhouette SIDEWAYS at the shoulder and hip, bend them out and down at the elbow and knee so the belly sits low between splayed feet, and drop the tail onto the ground line.

rows.readsAs: a generic orange-red fish; indistinguishable from this batch's Salmon and Trout except for hue
rows.defect: The single defining field mark is INVERTED. The reference says pale spots on a dark ground, explicitly '(not dark on pale)'; the render is dark grey-brown blotches scattered over a LIGHTER salmon-orange flank — exactly the polarity the row warns against. The white leading edges on the lower fins are also absent: the pelvic/anal lobe and the caudal are flat translucent maroon with no light edge anywhere. And the body is not slender — it is the family's deep symmetric lens, as deep as the Whitefish.
rows.fix: Darken the ground to a deep olive-slate and repaint the blotches as discrete pale cream/pink dots with a thin red halo, then run a 2px pure-white stripe along the leading ray of the pelvic, anal and lower caudal lobe.
rows.verifyWhy:
UPHELD, with two of the three stated causes corrected. WHAT I SAW at 4x-12x zoom (440x440 source; body bbox x=104..335, y=151..239).

MUST-READ 1 -- 'pale spots on a dark ground (not dark on pale)': INVERTED, exactly as claimed, and this alone is disqualifying. The flank ground is a light salmon-orange (sampled 140..212 R on the lower flank, e.g. 188,89,67 / 207,98,73 / 212,124,108 at x=230). Sitting on it are eight or nine large soft DARK grey-brown blotches (sampled ~79,46,34 and darker in the blotch cores), concentrated on the lower flank and belly with a couple more behind the gill. That is dark-on-pale, the precise polarity the row warns against. Worth recording for the fix: a pale-dot rendering path already EXISTS on this asset -- the hexagonal scale mesh carries a small bright specular highlight in every cell (a fine lattice of light-orange dots). It does not read as spots because the dots are lattice-aligned, uniform, and one-third the size they would need to be, and because the big dark blotch layer sits on top and wins. The fix is three moves, not one: (a) drop the ground to a dark olive/slate-brown, (b) DELETE the dark blotch layer entirely, (c) add a discrete, irregularly-scattered pale cream/pink/rose spot layer at roughly eye-diameter, positioned along the mid and lower flank.

MUST-READ 2 -- 'white leading edges on lower fins': ABSENT, claim correct, but the described defect understates it. The problem is not that existing lower fins lack white margins -- it is that there is essentially no lower fin structure to mark. Scanning below the ventral outline, the ONLY sub-belly geometry is a single smooth crescent lobe spanning x=195..228, dipping ~7px below the belly line at its deepest (bottom y=233 at x=210 vs body ventral y=226). At 12x it is a featureless dull-red flat shape (73,36,30) with no rays, no ray-tips, no anterior margin treatment. There is no separate pelvic fin and no separate anal fin -- one merged lobe stands in for both. So the white leading edge cannot simply be painted on; the pelvic and anal fins have to be drawn first. IMPORTANT TRAP FOR WHOEVER FIXES THIS: there IS a bright pale-grey/white line along the belly, and it is easy to mistake for the Char mark. It is not. It is the body silhouette stroke -- it runs the full length of BOTH the dorsal and ventral edges, it passes over the TOP (base) of the ventral lobe rather than along its front margin, and Trout and Salmon in this same batch carry the identical stroke while having no such must-read. Do not count it.

MUST-READ 3 -- 'slender streamlined body': THE JUDGE IS WRONG HERE, and I am correcting it. They wrote 'the body is the family's deep lens, not slender.' Measured: snout tip x=335, caudal peduncle pinch x=140 -> body length 195px; maximum body depth (pale outline to pale outline, fins excluded) 52px at x=230. That is aspect 3.75 against the packet's requested 3.8 -- essentially on spec, and if anything the mid-body taper reads slightly slimmer than the number. The body is NOT deep. What is genuinely wrong with the silhouette is a different thing: it is a symmetric double-pointed almond with a needle-sharp snout and no head modelling at all (no blunt rounded Salvelinus snout, no jaw line, no operculum -- just a thin curved gill arc), and it is bit-for-bit the same outline as Trout, Salmon, Grayling and Whitefish. Filing that under 'not slender' sends the fix in the wrong direction; the note should read 'generic shared lens, no snout/head modelling'.

FAMILY / CHASSIS: the judge's 'same blotch field as this batch's Salmon and Trout, just redder' is correct and in fact stronger than stated. Side-by-side at identical crop, Char and Salmon share the same outline, the same dorsal fin, the same rayed pectoral fan at the same anchor, the same forked tail, the same eye and gill-arc placement, the same hex scale mesh, AND nearly the same hue (both salmon-orange-red; Char is marginally more saturated). They differ only in where the dark blotches happen to land. At thumbnail size Char is not distinguishable from Salmon. Trout is the identical chassis again in olive-gold.

VERDICT: the single defining field mark that separates a char from every other fish in this family is inverted, and the second must-read has no substrate to exist on. The asset reads as 'a second Salmon'. FAIL stands.

rows.readsAs: a generic silver-blue fish; a Whitefish in a cooler tint
rows.defect: The tall spotted sail dorsal that IS the grayling is not there. What is drawn is the same translucent dark rounded lobe every other fish in this batch carries — measured against the Whitefish beside it, it is a few pixels taller and otherwise the identical shape — with no spot rows, no banner-like square trailing edge, and no visible attachment to the topline, so it reads as a shadow behind the back rather than a fin. The 'small mouth' must-read cannot be judged because there is no mouth at all, only the family's needle point. No adipose fin between the dorsal and the peduncle.
rows.fix: Replace the shared dorsal lobe with a purpose-drawn sail: base running from 35% to 60% of body length, height at least 1.2x body depth, square-cut trailing edge, and 3-4 rows of dark red-violet spots between the rays — drawn ON the topline, not behind the body.
rows.verifyWhy:
FAIL stands, but two of the first judge's stated causes are factually wrong and must not be used as the fix brief.

WHAT IS ACTUALLY THERE (440x440 native; measured by per-column top-of-ink vs top-of-pale-body scan, and read at 3x/6x/8x with contrast boost):

1. THE DORSAL FIN IS NOT MISSING, AND IT IS NOT THE FAMILY'S SHARED LOBE. A dorsal IS drawn, it IS attached, and it IS the largest in the batch. It spans x199-x311 of a x103-x337 bbox (~112px, 48% of total length) and rises to a maximum of 23px above the pale topline at x=247. Its lower boundary coincides with the body topline for the whole span -- it is rooted on the back, not floating behind it. The claim 'measurably the same shape as the Whitefish's, only a few pixels taller' is FALSE: the same scan gives Whitefish 13px peak over 59 columns and Trout 14px over 72; Grayling is 77% taller and 85% longer than the Whitefish's. The claim 'no attachment to the topline, so it reads as a shadow behind the back' is also FALSE -- at 8x with gain the fin is a solid mid-blue translucent membrane carrying ~10 evenly spaced vertical RAY LINES, seated flush on the topline.

2. THE DORSAL STILL FAILS, FOR THE RIGHT REASONS. Body depth under the fin's peak is 56px (topPale 180 -> belly 236), so the fin is only ~41% of body depth. A grayling's flag is roughly as tall as the body is deep and, critically, is RECTANGULAR: near-constant height along its length, its tallest point at the POSTERIOR end, and a squared-off (often trailing-lobed) rear edge. What is drawn is a symmetric low DOME -- rising and falling in a single smooth arc, tallest at mid-span, tapering to nothing at both ends. It reads as an enlarged generic fish dorsal, not a banner. And it carries NO SPOTS -- the mustRead's 'spotted' clause is fully unmet; the fin has ray lines only. Fix = re-shape to a tall square banner (>=90% of body depth, roughly constant height, squared trailing edge, rear lobe tallest) and add 3-4 horizontal rows of dark ocelli/spots between the rays.

3. NO MOUTH -- CONFIRMED. At 8x the snout is a bare pale wedge terminating in a point. There is no mouth line, no gape, no jaw seam, no lip. The only line on the head is a curved operculum/gill arc well behind the eye (that is a gill cover, not a mouth). 'Small mouth' cannot read because nothing reads.

4. NO ADIPOSE FIN -- CONFIRMED. At 6x the topline from the dorsal's posterior taper (x~199) to the caudal root (x~139) is a single unbroken smooth curve. No bump, no nub, no separate element.

5. WHAT DOES PASS: the forked tail is present and correct -- deeply forked, ray-lined, clearly bilobed. The eye is 'prominent' as spec'd (large white sclera ring, dark pupil), though it is pasted on top of the head silhouette and breaks the dorsal contour of the skull.

6. BODY SHAPE ALSO MISSES. mustRead asks for a 'trout-shaped body'; spec aspect is 3.8. Measured bbox is 235x87 = 2.70, the DEEPEST of the five (Trout 3.17, Whitefish 2.88). This reads as a deep-bodied bream/sunfish blank, not a slender salmonid.

7. CHASSIS FINDING (supports the FAIL). Rendered side by side at 3x, Grayling and Whitefish are one chassis: identical body outline, identical allover pale scale-grid texture, identical mouthless pointed snout, identical pasted-on ringed eye, identical single triangular pectoral, identical soft ventral shadow lobe, identical forked tail. Hue (blue-grey vs olive) and dorsal size are the only differences. The larger dorsal is the ONE thing distinguishing this asset from the family blank, and it is the wrong shape and unspotted -- so with no mouth, no adipose, and the wrong body depth, nothing on this asset says grayling.

rows.readsAs: a pink-orange trout-ish fish — the salmonid family is legible, the species is not
rows.defect: The adipose fin is missing entirely: the topline between the rear of the dorsal lobe and the peduncle is bare, with no small fleshy nub. There is no kype and in fact no jaw of any kind — the head tapers to the family needle point. The forked tail is the one must-read that lands. The heavy dark flank blotches are the same mottle field as Char and Trout, which pushes the read toward 'trout' rather than 'salmon'.
rows.fix: Add a small rounded adipose nub on the topline midway between the dorsal and the peduncle, then build an actual head — jaw line, gape and an upturned hooked lower jaw for the kype.

rows.readsAs: a brown trout-ish fish — the olive-gold ground and dark speckling carry it further than the rest of the batch
rows.defect: Two of three must-reads fail. There is no adipose fin — bare topline behind the dorsal lobe. The tail is not squared-off and shallow-forked; it is the family's deeply forked caudal with a long swept upper lobe and a deep notch, i.e. actively the opposite of the row. The speckling is present but rendered as soft blurred smudges rather than discrete spots, so at thumbnail size it reads as dirt on the flank rather than as markings.
rows.fix: Swap in a squared caudal with only a shallow concave notch, add the adipose nub, and tighten the flank spots into small hard-edged dark dots with pale haloes.

rows.readsAs: a pale silvery lake fish — believable as a generic silverside or shad, not specifically a whitefish
rows.defect: The blunt overhanging snout above a tiny subterminal mouth — the one thing that separates a whitefish from every other silver fish — is absent and replaced by the family's sharp needle point, which is its visual opposite. No adipose fin behind the dorsal. The large silvery scales do read (the diamond mesh stipple is at its best here) and the tail is the deepest fork in the batch, so two of four must-reads land.
rows.fix: Rebuild the head: blunt the snout into a rounded overhanging nose that projects past a small downward-facing mouth slit, and add the adipose nub on the topline behind the dorsal.

rows.readsAs: a juvenile barracuda or a needlefish - a slim silver predator with a spear snout
rows.defect: The identity feature is completely absent: there is no mouth on this animal at all. The snout is a needle-fine knife point that tapers to nothing, instead of the blunt pig-snout overhanging a cavernous gape whose corner runs back past the eye. The eye is a tiny white ring at the very tip, not the huge forward-set eye called for, and there is no bright silver lateral stripe anywhere - the flank is uniform pale scale texture with only a soft shading gradient down the midline. What is left is the generic lens body plus a spear nose, which reads as a barracuda.
rows.fix: Rebuild the head: give it a short blunt translucent snout that overhangs a wide open gape whose corner terminates BEHIND the eye, triple the eye diameter to roughly a third of head depth, and lay a hard-edged bright silver band the full length of the mid-flank.

rows.readsAs: a sea bream, pomfret or silver moonyfish - a deep round reef disc, or a piranha
rows.defect: The body is a near-circular disc: measured off the render the length-to-depth ratio is roughly 1.7:1 against the 4.2 the reference specifies. The must-read is a STREAMLINED silver body with a keeled belly and this is the opposite of streamlined - the belly is a fat convex curve with no keel, the topline is a high domed hump, and the caudal peduncle is a stubby pinch. The dorsal is a dark translucent smear draped over the back rather than a single small fin at mid-back, the jaw is a plain downcurved line with no upturn, and the tail fork is shallow. Nothing about this silhouette says clupeid.
rows.fix: Cut the body depth by more than half so the fish is a long low torpedo at the specified 4.2:1, flatten the belly into a visible saw-edged keel, and replace the dorsal smear with one small crisp triangular fin at mid-back.

rows.readsAs: a generic green pelagic fish - a mullet or a small pike
rows.defect: Two of the three must-reads are missing or too weak to see. The wavy dark tiger bars are not drawn as markings: what is on the flank is the same scale-texture stipple as its siblings, faintly clumped into straight low-contrast vertical bands that a viewer reads as texture noise, and they sit on a flat mid-green body rather than a steel-blue back over a silver belly, so there is no back-to-belly split at all. The row of small finlets before the tail is entirely absent - the peduncle is a bare narrow stalk running straight into the caudal fork. The two dorsal humps are the same soft translucent blobs as the rest of the family and there is no mouth line at all on the pointed snout. The narrow keeled tail stalk is the one must-read that does land.
rows.fix: Paint the tiger bars as opaque hard-edged wavy dark strokes over the upper third of a steel-blue back that meets a silver belly, and add the row of five to six small separated finlets along the top and bottom of the peduncle.

rows.readsAs: a small silver baitfish - a sardine or herring, correct to about genus level
rows.defect: The colour must-read lands - a bright mirror-silver flank under a dark blue-grey back, with a deeply forked tail - but the other two do not. The single small dorsal fin at mid-back is not a fin: it is the family's soft dark translucent blob smeared over the whole rear half of the topline with loose hair-like spikes escaping its upper edge, so there is no readable fin shape or placement. The large loose scales read as a fine even diamond dot-grid, far too small and too regular to say 'large loose deciduous scales'. The head is the shared knife-point taper with no mouth line drawn and no jaw break, and the body sits noticeably deeper than the 4.5 aspect specified.

What is actually wrong is (a) the arc is a gentle bow with NO terminal reversal - a chamois horn goes near-vertical and then snaps into a tight fishhook in the last fifth of its length, and neither horn here changes direction at all; and (b) the pair SPLAY OUTWARD IN A V/LYRE rather than rising parallel, so the near horn is an almost dead-vertical prong leaning slightly one way while the far horn leans the other. The silhouette therefore reads as generic caprid brow-prongs, not the chamois hook. Fix is a sharp direction reversal in the top ~20% of each horn plus parallel, not splayed, bases.

MUST-READ 3 - slim antelope-like legs: the judge's charge that they are 'the same thick straight posts the whole family wears' is CONFIRMED by direct comparison - I cropped Goat.png at the same scale and the two animals are demonstrably ONE CHASSIS: same barrel outline, same rump facet, same shoulder facet, same leg geometry, same foot. The Ibex wears a single tight, closed ring-curl about 30px across on a 440px canvas — roughly 0.5x the head length. It springs from the brow, arcs UP and BACK only about a quarter turn, then rolls FORWARD and DOWN and terminates in front of the face at eye level. That is a bighorn/mouflon ram curl, not an ibex. A real ibex horn is 2-3x head length, a single shallow scimitar sweeping back and up past the withers with the tip clear of the shoulder, and the drawn shape has none of that length, none of that arc, and no tip beyond the skull. Only ONE horn is drawn (no far horn behind the skull).

BUT the side-by-side proves those bands are a generic horn texture, not an ibex feature: Goat and Sheep carry the SAME banding on the SAME curl. So the fix is not 'add ridges to the existing curl' — the ridges are already there and they are shared. The fix is GEOMETRY: replace the ring with a long backward scimitar and then make the knobs read as a row of raised transverse KNOBS on the front (anterior) face of that scimitar, distinct from the flat banding the other two use.

2. SHARED CHASSIS — confirmed and worse than 'the body is the shared barrel'. Goat, Sheep and Ibex are ONE asset. Same pose, same barrel torso with a dead-flat topline, same four slim straight legs, same dark cloven hoof, same skull, same protruding eye with the same highlight, same downturned muzzle with the same mouth line, same dark oval ear-mark on the cheek, same horn. Sheep and Ibex are near-indistinguishable; Goat is the same figure recoloured white-grey. The ONLY thing that separates Ibex from Sheep is a warmer tan tint plus a spiky dark fringe stroked along the silhouette.

3. BEARD — must-read 'goat beard under the chin'. ★ CORRECTION to the judge: it is not true that nothing is there. There IS a dense fringe of dark spiky strands along the underside of the jaw and down the throat to the chest. However it does not count, because the SAME fringe is stroked along the topline of the back, along the belly and around the rump — it is a global shaggy-coat outline pass applied to the whole silhouette, not a beard. There is no discrete beard tuft hanging from the chin point, no separate mass, no distinct value. So the must-read still fails, but the fix is 'break a distinct beard out of the throat fringe', not 'add hair where there is none'.

4. STOCKY MUSCULAR BODY — not met. The torso is a shallow, even barrel with no chest depth, no shoulder mass, no rump mass; the legs are thin, straight and long relative to the body. It reads as a sheep/lamb, not a mountain ibex. No tail is visible from this angle.

VERDICT: with the defining horn absent and the body, head and horn all identical to the Sheep and Goat in the same batch, the asset reads as the wrong organism (a generic tan ram). FAIL stands.

rows.readsAs: a shaggy golden goat or a small yak — not a bison-built goat-antelope
rows.defect: The long shaggy golden coat is the one must-read that lands, and it is the most distinct asset here. But the horns do not sweep outward then back like a wildebeest's — there is one pale bent tube emerging from a dark blob on the crown, ambiguous in count and direction. There are no humped shoulders: the topline is the family's level line with only a token rise, and the legs are the family's standard-length posts rather than short thick ones. The muzzle is the same bulbous down-curved family snout with no arched Roman nose.

rows.readsAs: a white downy chick or a small grey-and-white quail poult
rows.defect: The identity must-read is inverted: the bill is a short straight yellow-orange cone that if anything tips slightly DOWN, with no upward sweep and no needle thinness - it is the same bill as the Curlew and the Snipe in this batch. There is no crisp black-and-white pied patterning either; the body is a uniform soft white-grey mottle with a grey wing crescent, no blocked black cap, nape or wing panels. The legs are yellow-ochre, not long blue-grey, and they are short and stubby rather than long.
rows.fix: Draw a genuinely long, hair-thin black bill that sweeps clearly upward past the top of the skull, and repaint the body as hard-edged black blocks (crown/nape, two wing bars, wingtips) on pure white, on long slate-blue legs.
rows.verifyWhy:
Upheld, but two of the three stated causes are measurably wrong and must not be fixed as described.

WHAT IS ACTUALLY THERE (440x440; figure bbox x75-363, y109-319, so 288 wide x 210 tall, aspect 1.37 against the spec's 1.8). A plump white egg-shaped body on two thin yellow legs, small round white head (widest span 49px at y127, headFrac 49/210 = 0.23 vs spec 0.30), one round black eye with a white catchlight, a solid gold-yellow tapered wedge bill, a mid-grey C-shaped wing outline arc on the flank, and a long grey pointed tail wedge running back to x363.

MUST-READ 1 - 'thin needle bill sweeping strongly upward': ABSENT, and this alone is the FAIL. I measured the bill's centreline column by column: at the base (x=144) the yellow spans y131-142, mid 136.5; at the tip (x=79) it is a single pixel at y=137.0. That is 0.5px of drop across 65px of length - roughly 0.4 degrees, i.e. dead flat. CORRECTION to the first judge: the bill does NOT 'tip slightly downward' and it is not 'inverted'; it is exactly horizontal and perfectly straight, a symmetric taper with equal slope on the top and bottom edges. It is also NOT especially short - 68px long against a 49px head, i.e. ~1.4 head-lengths and 24% of total profile length, which is in the right neighbourhood. The real defects are (a) zero recurve where the outer half must sweep visibly upward so the tip finishes ABOVE the gape line, and (b) it is a fat opaque wedge (12px deep at the base) rather than a needle - an avocet bill should be near hairline-thin for its whole length and, ideally, black not yellow. Fix the curve and the thinness; do not shorten or 'flip' it.

MUST-READ 2 - 'crisp black-and-white pied patterning': ABSENT. CORRECTION: it is not a 'uniform soft white-grey mottle' - there IS deliberate structure (a broad C-shaped wing outline arc, a shorter scapular bar over the shoulder, and a grey tail wedge). The failure is tonal and positional, not missing marks. The darkest structural grey samples RGB(91,92,93), luminance ~92/255 - a mid-grey, with soft feathered edges. A luminance histogram over the whole figure shows only 2.86% of pixels below L60, and most of that is the eye and the tail's shaded lower edge; there is no black anywhere on the plumage. The head and hindneck are uniformly white (samples 236/216/225) where an avocet carries a hard BLACK cap running from the crown down the nape. Fix: replace the grey outline arc with flat near-black (L<40) blocks with hard edges - black cap + nape stripe, black scapular bar, black wing panel - on an otherwise clean white body.

MUST-READ 3 - 'long blue-grey legs': half present, and the first judge's description is wrong. CORRECTION: the legs are NOT 'short yellow-ochre stubs'. They run y259 to y319, 60px, 28% of the 210px figure height, drawn as two thin shanks with a correct rearward hock bend and splayed front-and-back toes. That is a credible wader leg in form and only modestly short. What is wrong is the COLOUR: they are the same saturated gold-yellow as the bill (the yellow-pixel pass picked bill and legs out with one identical threshold), where an avocet must have cold blue-grey/lead-blue legs. Fix the hue, and lengthen by ~20-25%; do not redraw the leg structure.

NET: three must-reads, zero readable. With a straight horizontal yellow cone, an all-white head, a grey (not black) scribble arc and yellow legs, the asset reads as a generic small white gull or a stylised yellow-billed tern, not an avocet. Also worth flagging for the family pass: the plump egg body, the long grey pointed tail wedge and the identical hocked yellow leg pair look like the shared shorebird chassis, with only bill length and grey placement varying.

rows.readsAs: a buff-coloured downy chick or a small partridge poult
rows.defect: The one feature that IS a curlew - a very long, smoothly downcurved bill up to a quarter of the profile - is absent. The rendered bill is a short straight yellow cone barely longer than the head, pixel-for-pixel the same bill drawn on the Avocet, Godwit, Sandpiper and Snipe. The legs are short and stubby, not long bare wading legs, and there is no neck: the ball head sits directly on the egg body.
rows.fix: Replace the cone with a long dark bill roughly a quarter of the total width that curves smoothly downward through its length, and stretch the legs to at least twice the current length with visible bare tibia above the joint.
rows.verifyWhy: UPHELD, but three parts of the stated cause are wrong and one failing must-read was missed. WHAT I SAW (440x440, decoded and measured pixel-wise, plus 4-5x zooms of head, neck junction, and feet): BILL - a flat yellow wedge running x=107..165, length 58px, max thickness 10px. I traced its vertical midline column by column: 156.0 at the tip, 156.0 at the base, drift 0.0px over the whole 58px. It is geometrically DEAD STRAIGHT, not merely 'looks straight' - top edge rises 5px and bottom edge drops 5px symmetrically, so it is an isoceles triangle, the exact opposite of a decurved scythe. So the core of the FAIL stands: the defining downcurve is absent. CORRECTION 1 to the claim: it is NOT 'identical to the Avocet's and Snipe's' in size - same primitive, yes (I measured all five family bills: Avocet 66px drift -0.5, Snipe 61px drift -1.0, Curlew 58px drift 0.0, Sandpiper 52px drift -0.5, all 10-12px thick), but the Curlew's is the SHORTEST of the three named. The one bird in the family whose bill should be the longest and most extreme has a bill shorter than the Avocet's and shorter than the Snipe's. A fixer who matches it to the Avocet's length will still be wrong. CORRECTION 2: the packet note says the bill 'can be a quarter of the total profile length' - measured against the true profile (bill tip x=107 to tail tip x=337, shadow excluded) the bill is 58/230 = 25%, so it NUMERICALLY hits the note's ratio already. The failure is not raw ratio; it is curvature and slenderness. Do not fix this by lengthening alone - it must become a slender, smoothly decurving arc whose tip drops well below the gape line. Against the head it is 58px vs a ~47px head diameter, i.e. 1.2x head length, so the judge's 'barely longer than the head' is accurate. CORRECTION 3: 'legs are short stubs' is wrong in detail. Zoomed 5x, the legs are thin BARE yellow legs with a clearly drawn backward-bending hock at y~268 and splayed feet showing a forward toe pair and a hind toe. The structure is a wading leg; the defect is purely length - exposed leg runs y=254 (body underside) to y=292 (ground) = 38px against a body depth of ~90px, roughly 40% of body depth where a curlew needs about 100%. So the must-read 'long bare wading legs' fails on LENGTH, and the fix is to raise the belly and extend the tarsus, not to draw legs that are missing. CORRECTION 4: 'there is no neck at all' is an overstatement. There is a short neck taper of roughly 12-15px running from the jaw down-right into the shoulder, with a visible throat wedge. It is far too short and the head effectively sits on the shoulders, so the practical read is neckless, but the neck is not literally absent. MISSED BY THE ORIGINAL JUDGE: the third must-read, 'streaked brown body on a small round head', also fails on the body half. The head IS small and round (that part passes). The body is a fat pale-cream/ivory egg with a faint dappled scale texture, a large elliptical wing panel outlined in mid-brown, and a grey-brown tail wedge - there is no brown streaking anywhere, and the palette and dapple are near-identical to the Snipe's in the same batch. FAMILY CHASSIS: Curlew, Snipe and Sandpiper share one body - same round skull, same eye placement, same yellow triangular bill primitive, same egg torso with the same elliptical wing ellipse, same short yellow hock legs. NET READ: a plump generic wader chick, closer to a kiwi silhouette than a curlew. Nothing in the image identifies the organism as a curlew. FAIL is correct.

rows.readsAs: a plain brown chick or a young brown quail
rows.defect: The very long straight bill that defines a godwit is not drawn - the bill is the batch's standard short yellow cone, roughly one head-length, with no pale base and no length at all. The breast is a flat uniform mid-brown wash with no cinnamon tone and none of the dark chevron barring called for. The legs are short yellow stubs rather than the long dark legs of a godwit, and the body is the same neckless egg as every other bird here.
rows.fix: Give it a bill two to three head-lengths long, straight with a very slight upward tilt and a pale pink base fading to dark tip, and bar the cinnamon breast with a stack of dark chevrons.
rows.verifyWhy:
Tried hard to break this FAIL and could not; the verdict stands, but two of the three stated causes are described wrongly and would send a fixer to the wrong place.

WHAT IS ACTUALLY ON THE CANVAS (440x440, subject bbox x88-351, y123-304 => 263x181, aspect 1.45 against a spec of 1.9). A plump, rotund, hunched brown fowl in right profile: near-spherical head on a short thick neck, a fat egg-shaped body carrying a large folded-wing ellipse and a dark sweeping covert band, a long dark-brown wedge tail projecting back-right, and a scaly/pinecone stipple texture over the whole body. It reads as a quail or a kiwi, not a wader.

(1) BILL - the judge is right that it fails, but wrong on the measurement. It is NOT one head length. Measured: bill occupies x88-153 = 65px; head diameter is ~40px, so it is ~1.6 head lengths and ~25% of total profile length. The real defect is worse and more specific than 'too short': it is the SHARED FAMILY BILL PRIMITIVE, identical in every one of the seven shorebirds. I sampled all seven. Bill lengths: Avocet 65, Curlew 60, Godwit 65, Oystercatcher 60, Sandpiper 60, Snipe 65 (Plover 15). Fill colour is byte-identical rgb(224,177,60) in every one. Taper is identical (2px at tip growing linearly to ~14px at base). Midline is dead-flat horizontal in every one: Godwit mid-y runs 149,149,149,148,149,148,149,148,149,148,147 tip-to-base. Consequences: (a) the Godwit's bill is the SAME ABSOLUTE LENGTH as the Sandpiper's, whose spec is 'about head length' - so the one feature that separates a godwit from a sandpiper in this batch carries zero information; (b) the required 'faint upward tilt' is absent - if anything the axis droops ~2px toward the tip, i.e. a hair of DOWN-tilt; (c) the same primitive is doing duty as the Avocet's 'sweeping strongly upward' bill and the Curlew's 'smoothly downcurved' bill, both also dead flat.

(2) PALE BASE - judge is CORRECT. The bill is one uniform saturated gold rgb(224,177,60) from tip to base with no tonal break at all. A godwit's bill is pink/orange at the base and DARK at the outer half; here there is no dark distal half, so no two-tone reads. (Pedantic note for the fixer: the whole bill is warm-pale, so the problem is missing CONTRAST - darken the outer 40-50% rather than lightening the base.)

(3) BREAST - judge's conclusion is right, his description is wrong. It is NOT 'flat uniform mid-brown'. The breast and flanks carry a dense scale-like feather stipple with scattered dark flecks (base ~rgb(160,110,65) with speckles down to rgb(68,47,27)) plus a big covert ellipse and a dark curved band. What is missing is that none of it is ORGANISED: no chevrons, no bars, just random mottle. And the hue is a generic warm tan (~26 deg hue, moderate saturation), not cinnamon-rufous. So the fix is 'reorganise the existing markings into dark chevron bars and warm the base coat toward rufous', not 'add texture to a flat field'.

(4) LEGS - judge's colour call is right, his shape call is wrong. They are NOT 'stubs'. There are two properly articulated legs in ochre-mustard rgb(201,162,79): a visible tarsus, a clear rearward-bending hock joint, and large flat feet with a long forward toe and a rear projection - I zoomed to 4x on x150-310/y230-340 to confirm. The real defect is length and colour: ochre pixels run y251-301, i.e. ~50px of a 181px figure (~27%), so they are short-to-medium and heavily bent, and the required 'long DARK legs' are a light warm yellow instead. The bird therefore sits low and squat instead of standing tall.

BAND: FAIL upheld. All three must-reads fail simultaneously - the very long straight upward-tilted pale-based bill is a stock 1.6-head-length flat gold cone shared with six siblings, the long dark legs are short ochre ones, and the cinnamon chevron-barred breast is an unstructured tan stipple. Nothing here distinguishes it from the Sandpiper or the Curlew in the same batch, and the silhouette reads as a plump gamebird rather than a wader. ONE FAMILY, ONE CHASSIS: the seven shorebirds share the same bill primitive, the same rotund body oval, the same wing ellipse and the same bent ochre leg pair; only colour and body-fill differ.

rows.readsAs: a black chick or a sooty ball-shaped fledgling crow
rows.defect: All three must-reads fail simultaneously. The bill is the shared short yellow cone, not a long straight orange-red chisel. The plumage is uniformly near-black over the whole body with no white at all, so the bold black-and-white blocking that makes the bird identifiable at a glance is entirely missing. The legs are the same thin yellow stubs used across the batch, not stout pink legs, and there is no red eye ring - just the same small black bead eye.
rows.fix: Draw a long, thick, blunt-tipped orange-red chisel bill about 1.5 head-lengths, split the body into a hard black hood and back over a clean white belly and wing bar, and put thick pink legs and a red eye ring on it.
rows.verifyWhy: Verdict upheld, but one third of the stated cause is factually wrong and must not be fixed as written. WHAT I ACTUALLY SAW (440x440, subject bbox x104-333 y107-323 = 230w x 217h). BILL — the FAIL claim of 'the shared short yellow cone' is WRONG on length and form. Measured yellow bill bbox is x114-166 y155-165: 53px long by 11px deep, a 4.8:1 slender straight spike, roughly 1.4x the head diameter (head circle ~35-40px). It is long and it is straight, so that half of the must-read is already met. What is wrong is (a) HUE — it is goldenrod/amber (~R224 G168 B46), the same family yellow as the legs, not orange-red; 688 yellow pixels in the image versus 3 pixels anywhere in the orange-red bucket, i.e. zero red content; and (b) TIP FORM — it tapers to a needle point like a probing bill, not the blunt, squared-off, laterally compressed CHISEL that is the oystercatcher's whole diagnostic. Fix is a recolor plus a blunt truncated tip, NOT a lengthening. PLUMAGE — the claim is right in substance, slightly wrong in wording. It is not 'uniformly near-black': sampled body region averages luminance 34/255 with highlights to 117, and there is real charcoal-on-mid-grey feather hatching plus a distinctly lighter grey folded-wing/mantle plate outlined against a near-black underbody, so the bird does have internal value structure. But there is NO WHITE ANYWHERE — exactly 1 pixel in the whole image exceeds 200 on all three channels, and that pixel is the specular catchlight in the eye. The bold black-and-white blocking (white belly, white wing bar, white rump) is entirely absent, and this is the single most defining oystercatcher must-read. A thin pale rim-light traces the crown and breast edge; that is a lighting outline, not white plumage, and it must not be counted as the blocking. LEGS / EYE — correct that there is no pink and no red eye ring, but 'thin yellow stubs' undersells them: the legs are a properly articulated pair, yellow bbox x200-245 y256-288, 33px tall, with visible tarsus, a bent ankle joint and forward-splayed toes on the ground plane. They are shortish relative to the body and they are the WRONG COLOUR (amber, matching the bill, zero pink pixels in the image), which is the actual defect. The eye is a large prominent black bead with a white catchlight, satisfying 'eyes: prominent', but it carries no red orbital ring at all. ADDITIONAL DEFECT THE FAIL DID NOT NAME: the reference row calls for aspect 1.9 and the rendered subject bbox is 230x217, an aspect of ~1.06 — the body is a near-circular ovoid, so the elongated shorebird carriage is gone independent of colour. The tail is only a small dark backswept wedge with a few thin filament streaks at lower right. NET: the 'ball-shaped sooty bird with a yellowish bill' read stands, though it reads closer to a dark round probing shorebird / a fat dark kiwi-ish silhouette than specifically a crow fledgling. Two of three must-reads are wholly absent (black-and-white blocking, pink legs + red eye ring) and the third is half-present (long straight = yes, orange-red chisel = no), plus the aspect is off by nearly 2x. FAIL.

rows.readsAs: a small round grey chick - plausibly a plover, but only because the generic chassis happens to be plover-shaped
rows.defect: The stubby bill and dark bead eye are present and the body is compact, so this is the one asset the shared chassis nearly serves. But the head is not large relative to the body - it is the same small ball head used on every other bird, so the big-headed look is missing; the eye is small rather than the demanded big dark eye; and the body is the batch's horizontal egg rather than a compact upright carriage. It is indistinguishable from the Sandpiper in this batch apart from hue.
rows.fix: Enlarge the skull to roughly 0.3 of the body and the eye to about twice its current diameter, and tilt the body from horizontal to a more upright, chest-forward stance so the big-headed silhouette reads.

rows.readsAs: a pale buff chick that could pass as a small sandpiper
rows.defect: The straightish bill of roughly head length is present and the mottled buff tone is right, so the identification is not actively wrong - but this is simply the family's base chassis with nothing added. The body is a fat neckless egg rather than a horizontal crouched wader with a visible neck and slimmer chest, and the legs are short thick stubs rather than long thin wading legs. It is identical to Curlew and Plover in this batch except for hue.
rows.fix: Slim the body, raise it on legs at least twice as long and half as thick, and add a short visible neck so the crouched horizontal wader posture reads instead of a chick's ball.

rows.readsAs: a dark brown downy chick or a young grouse
rows.defect: The extremely long straight dagger bill - the single feature that makes a snipe a snipe - is absent; the bill is the batch's short yellow cone. The eye is set dead-centre on the cheek, not high and far back on the skull, so the snipe's distinctive head geometry is gone. The back carries only generic random speckling with no bold cream longitudinal stripes; nothing on this bird distinguishes it from the Godwit except being slightly darker.
rows.fix: Draw a straight dark dagger bill about three head-lengths long, shift the eye up and back toward the rear crown, and lay four crisp cream stripes running front-to-back along the mantle.
rows.verifyWhy:
Verdict upheld, but the first and headline cause is WRONG and must not be actioned as written. THE BILL IS NOT ABSENT AND IS NOT A SHORT CONE. Pixel-measured on the 440x440 PNG: opaque silhouette spans x=78..360; the bill tip is at x=78 and the skull silhouette begins at x=141, giving a bill of 63px. The skull is a circle spanning x=139..188 (diameter 49px, widest rows y=136..144), so the bill is ~1.3x skull length and 22% of the whole profile. Rendered at 4x it is unmistakably a straight, tapering, dagger-shaped gold-ochre wedge with no curve and no cone/stub character. A fix pass told 'the bill is missing' would draw a bill that is already there.

The REAL bill defect is uniformity, not absence. Measuring every long-billed member of this batch the same way: Avocet 63px, Snipe 63px, Godwit 62px, Curlew 59px, Oystercatcher 59px, Sandpiper 55px (control: Plover, a genuinely short-billed wader, measures 14px). All six are one stamped bill at one length. The Snipe therefore has no more bill than the Sandpiper or the Oystercatcher, when 'extremely long' means it should be at or near the family's extreme (~2.5x skull, alongside the Curlew and Godwit). The must-read fails on DEGREE — the bill needs lengthening to roughly double its current 63px and thinning at the base, not inventing.

SecOND must-read, eye set high and far back: CONFIRMED ABSENT, with a small correction to the wording. The judge said 'dead-centre on the cheek'; measured, it is slightly FORWARD of centre. The eye disc is centred near x=157.5, y=143 (specular highlight resolves at 155.3, 139.7; the dark pupil creates a silhouette gap of x=158..161 at y=140 and x=153..161 at y=144). The skull centre is x=163.5, y=145.5. So the eye sits ~6px toward the BILL from the skull centre and only ~2px above mid-height — i.e. forward-of-centre and mid-cheek, which is the anatomical opposite of the snipe's eye jammed high and rearward near the crown. This is the single most identity-destroying miss and the judge is right that it fails.

Third must-read, bold cream longitudinal back stripes: CONFIRMED ABSENT, description accurate. At 5x the mantle and wing carry a fine, dense, uniform cream dapple of small dashes laid in rows that curve to follow the wing arc — a scale/speckle texture, low contrast, identical in kind across mantle, wing and flank. There is not one discrete bold cream line running shoulder-to-tail anywhere on the bird, let alone the two-to-four braces a snipe needs. Related and unlisted but reinforcing: the head is a flat uniform mid-brown with no median crown stripe, no supercilium and no eye-line, so the striped-head signal is gone as well.

Chassis claim: substantially right. Side-by-side with Godwit.png the two are one body — same round skull, same eye placement, same identical-length gold bill, same round torso with the same dark wing arc and the same long pointed tail wedge, same two-toe stubby foot. Correction to 'nothing but a darker hue': there are two other differences, both minor and both wrong-axis. The Snipe's plumage texture is a rounded scale dapple where the Godwit's is longitudinal streaking (ironically the Godwit is closer to a striped back than the Snipe is), and the Snipe's legs are marginally shorter and thicker — which is the one thing it gets right for the species, since snipe legs are genuinely short.

What I also checked and found acceptable: legs are short, thick, bent at the tarsus, pale ochre with a simple fore/aft toe pair — correct posture and proportion for a snipe, not a defect. Silhouette is a plump horizontal biped, also fine.

Net: one must-read present but under-scaled, two must-reads flatly absent, and the asset is a hue-and-texture recolour of the Godwit stamp. It reads as a generic small brown wader, not a snipe. FAIL stands. Fix order: (1) drive the eye high and rearward on the skull, (2) paint 2-4 bold cream longitudinal braces down the mantle plus a striped crown, (3) roughly double the bill length and thin it. Do NOT 'add a missing bill'.

rows.readsAs: a spotted appaloosa pony or a Jacob-type sheep
rows.defect: The body is the shared ungulate barrel — flat topline, upswept belly tuck, four column legs with fetlock bands ending in blocky hoof-like feet at the corners of the body — with a long wedge muzzle set on no neck. It is not a cat body of any kind, so the 'stocky heavy-boned cat body' must-read is absent. The dark markings are scattered irregular blotches over the back and flank rather than the required rows of solid spots, and there are no neck stripes at all. Worst of all the rear of the animal simply terminates in a bare curved rump: there is NO tail drawn anywhere, so the 'short thick tail' must-read is entirely missing.
rows.fix: Rebuild on a feline chassis — shorten the muzzle to a rounded broad skull, add a visible neck, arch the lumbar spine, bring the legs in under the body on digitigrade paws with toes — then add the short thick tapered tail off the croup and align the spots into longitudinal rows with two dark stripes down the neck.

rows.readsAs: a cream pony or donkey foal with a lemur's ringed tail stuck on
rows.defect: Identical chassis to the other two: straight flat topline, deep slab barrel with the belly swept up into a flank tuck, four straight column limbs leaving the silhouette at the body's corners with pastern bands and blunt hoof-shaped feet. The head is a long narrow forward-tapering wedge carried level on no neck with a single high-set amber eye — the exact opposite of the required 'broad flattened head with low wide-set ears'; the ears here are two small dark triangles pinned high on the crown, not low and wide. The 'short stocky legs with furred feet' must-read fails twice — the legs are long slender columns, and the feet are hard-edged hooves with no fur ruff. Only the banded black-tipped tail is present, and it hangs limply against the hind leg where it reads as an attached foreign part rather than growing from the croup.
rows.fix: Replace the wedge skull with a broad low-slung feline head — wide flat cranium, ears set low and out to the sides, short muzzle — and shorten and thicken the limbs onto furred paws tucked under the body.

rows.readsAs: a zebra foal, and a broken render at that
rows.defect: The render is broken: a solid dark horizontal bar of uniform thickness runs straight across the image from the mid-flank forward through the shoulder, through the entire skull, and out past the tip of the muzzle, cutting the head in half. It is a stray straight stroke unrelated to any coat marking and it dominates the silhouette. Underneath it is the same shared pony chassis as the other two — flat topline, deep barrel with an upswept belly tuck, four straight column legs at the corners with pastern bands and blocky hooves, wedge muzzle on no neck — so 'sturdy build heavier than a house cat' fails because it is not a cat build at all. The vertical black stripes are hard-edged and evenly spaced right down the barrel and across the face, which reads as zebra rather than a mackerel tabby. The ringed black-tipped tail is the only must-read that lands.
rows.fix: Delete the stray horizontal bar overlaying the body and head, then rebuild on a feline chassis with a short rounded skull, a real neck, and digitigrade paws, softening the stripes into broken tabby bars that fade toward the belly.

rows.readsAs: a pale grey coiled snake, or a length of grey ribbed hose coiled on the floor
rows.defect: Pale washed-out colouring and the limbless coil are present, but the third must-read is absent: the head is a small narrow rounded lozenge no wider than the neck, not a BLUNT WEDGE, and there are no heat-sensing pits anywhere on the snout — nothing on the loreal area at all. The head is also far too small for the body mass and is the identical head used on the other two assets. The dorsal ribbing wrapping right over the top of the tube reads as segment rings, not scales, pushing the whole thing toward earthworm. No tail is visible anywhere — the body closes into a perfect ring with no taper or tail tip.
rows.fix: Widen and flatten the skull into a blunt spade wider than the neck, and cut two dark pit openings between eye and nostril on the visible side; break the closed ring so a tapered tail tip lies over the coil.

rows.readsAs: a plain olive-green rope snake — a generic grass snake, with nothing viperine about it
rows.defect: The two must-reads that ARE the viper are both absent. (1) The head is a small narrow rounded lozenge exactly the same width as the neck — there is no broad triangular head, no widened venom-gland cheeks, no neck pinch; it is the identical head geometry pasted on the Cave Snake and the generic Snake. (2) There is no zigzag dorsal band, or any marking at all — the body is flat uniform olive from end to end. WHAT I SAW (440x440 PNG; zoomed the head at 8x/18x, the feet at 8x/10x, the mantle at 7x, and measured non-background bboxes for the whole family).

1) CREST — PRESENT, and at the BACK of the crown, not the front. The judge's 'spiky topknot added at the FRONT of the crown' is factually wrong. The head ball spans source x=150-183 (bill points LEFT, so larger x = rear); centre x~166. The crest stalk attaches at x~167-170 — dead centre to slightly rear of the crown — rises up-and-slightly-forward to a point at (162,148), and then throws THREE shorter tines that fan DOWN-AND-REARWARD, the lowest reaching x~186. The whole plume mass is centred rear of the head centre. So the must-read 'slight peaked crest at the back of the crown' is correctly POSITIONED. Its defect is scale and character, not location: it is a fully raised 4-tine splayed fan (cockatiel / crested-lark / hoopoe register), where the reference asked for a SLIGHT peak — a small pointed rise in the rear crown feathering continuous with the skull, not a separate stalked ornament standing ~10px clear of the head. FIX = shrink it to a low triangular peak merged into the crown silhouette; do NOT move it forward, and do NOT delete it.

2) THE QUAIL READ IS REAL, BUT IT COMES FROM THE BODY, NOT THE CREST. The silhouette is a fat rounded egg with the head ball perched high on the front-top shoulder and the belly bulging below the leg line — an upright, rotund gamebird carriage. The reference note explicitly demands the opposite: 'a horizontal, long-bodied songbird, not an upright perching finch.' Measured bbox is 159w x 130h = aspect 1.22 against a spec aspect of 1.6, and almost all of that width is the tail wedge, not the body: the body core alone is about as tall as it is long. There is no low-slung horizontal topline, no elongated rear body carried out over the legs.

3) 'IT IS THE SPARROW BLOB' — SUBSTANTIVELY RIGHT AT THE CHASSIS LEVEL, BUT NOT A COPY. Side-by-side with Sparrow.png the shared parts are unmistakable and should be named: identical head-ball placement on the front-top of the mass, identical big wing-oval decal with the same heavy dark outline sweeping from shoulder to rump, identical short pointed tail wedge, identical two yellow stick legs. But the measurements refute a literal 'same blob': Lark bbox 159x130 (1.22) vs Sparrow 120x132 (0.91) — the Lark tail wedge is genuinely longer and projects further rearward — and the Lark bill is a slim straight pointed cone, clearly slimmer than Sparrow's fat triangular seed-cracker. Two real differentiations exist; the chassis underneath them does not.

4) HIND CLAW — GENUINELY ABSENT. CONFIRMED. At 10x both feet show a tarsus dropping from the belly and then only FORWARD-raked toe strokes (down-and-left). Nothing whatsoever projects rearward from either ankle: the pixel field behind both ankles is bare background/shadow. The single most lark-specific must-read on the row — the long straight hind claw (elongated hallux) — is not drawn at all. One correction to the judge's wording: at this render each foot resolves to roughly TWO forward strokes plus the tarsus, not a clean 'three-forward-toe' set; the substance (all toes forward, no hallux) is right, the count is not.

5) PLUMAGE — 'streaky brown ground-bird' is NOT delivered. The bird is pale blond/cream sand, lighter than Sparrow, carrying a fine random mottled dapple of short flecks plus two heavy dark contour bands (the wing-oval outline and a back shade). There are no dark longitudinal STREAKS on the breast or mantle, and the ground tone is sandy cream rather than earth brown. The judge's 'sandy tan' description of the colour is accurate.

VERDICT: one of three must-reads (long straight hind claw) is entirely absent; a second (streaky brown plumage) is not delivered — mottled cream, no streaks; the third (rear crest) is present and correctly placed but drawn at ornamental scale; and the row's governing note (horizontal long-bodied ground bird) is contradicted by an upright rotund gamebird body on the shared songbird chassis. FAIL upheld.

rows.verifyWhy:
Verdict upheld, but the headline cause in the original claim is FLATLY WRONG and must not be used to drive the fix. I cropped and rescaled the tail region (src x225-340, y185-270 at 7x) and then thresholded the whole bird to a pure silhouette (src x90-340, y145-275 at 3x). The tail is NOT 'a plain undivided pointed spike'. It is a genuine, deeply forked tail with two long thin outer streamers: the notch apex sits at src x~270, essentially flush with the rear edge of the body mass (x~268), and both streamer tips reach x~323 — so the fork depth is ~55px, i.e. effectively 100% of the tail's length. The streamers are ~4px thick at midpoint, pointed, and diverge in a clean wide V (upper one rising, lower one dropping). In the threshold silhouette this fork is by far the most legible feature on the whole asset. Must-read #1 ('deeply forked tail with long outer streamers') is PRESENT and reads correctly. Do not touch the tail.

What actually fails:

(1) WINGS — must-read #2 ('long narrow pointed swept-back wings') is absent, and the original description understates it. It is not merely 'the family's folded comma stroke': in the threshold silhouette there is NO wing in the outline at all. The body edge is one unbroken plump egg from breast to rump. The 'wing' exists only as a painted panel on top of the back — a broad, blunt, scallop-textured lobe with a dark covert bar, whose rear end is a rounded lump, not a swept point. There is nothing scimitar-shaped anywhere, and no wing is deployed away from the body.

(2) BILL — must-read #3 ('tiny flat bill with a wide gape') is absent and actively inverted. At 9x the bill is a big saturated yellow triangular spear ~26px long against a head diameter of ~32px, i.e. ~80% of head width, projecting well clear of the face with a hard point. That is a thrush/starling dagger, the opposite of a swallow's minuscule stub. There is no gape line, no wide flat base. ('Pointed wedge' in the claim is fair as far as it goes but undersells the scale — the problem is that it is LONG and high-chroma yellow, so it dominates the head.)

(3) POSE / BODY — posture spec is 'flying' and the render is grounded. Confirmed at 9x: two pale-yellow feet with three splayed forward toes plus a hind toe, planted flat, attached almost directly to the belly with no visible leg, sitting on a dark elliptical cast ground shadow. The claim's 'lying prone' is slightly overstated — it reads as a bird squatting/crouched on the ground, not lying on its side. The bigger unstated defect is BULK: the silhouette body is a barrel-shaped oval (~165x70px) with a short neck and a round head, closer to a duck or grebe than to a swallow's slim streamlined dart. Strip the tail off and nobody would name this bird a swallow.

Aspect (~2.1 measured across x103-323 by y155-265) does meet the 2.2 spec, but only because the streamers supply the length; the body itself is stubby.

Net: 1 of 3 must-reads present. The identity feature survives; everything carrying it does not. Fix list, in order: slim the body to a streamlined dart and lift it off the ground (drop the planted feet, splayed toes and ground shadow, or tuck the feet to a nub); replace the folded back-panel with two long narrow swept-back scimitar wings that BREAK the silhouette; shrink the bill to a tiny dark stub with a wide gape. Keep the forked streamer tail and the dark-blue-back/rufous-belly colouring exactly as they are — both are already correct barn-swallow reads.

rows.readsAs: a drab brown bird lying on its belly
rows.defect: This is the Swallow render recoloured grey-brown, and it misses every must-read. There are no scythe-shaped crescent wings swept far back — just the folded comma stroke on the flank. The bill is a pointed yellow wedge, not a tiny bill with an enormous gape. The must-read explicitly demands a cigar body with almost no visible legs, and the render puts two bright yellow legs with splayed toes prominently under the body, planted on a ground shadow. It also has the long undivided pointed tail the packet's note warns against, so it fails as a swift AND as the swallow it was mistaken for.

What I saw (440x440, bird occupies x~85-345, y~155-265; inspected at 3x whole-body, 8x head, 8x feet, 7x tail, plus a 4.5x brightness-boosted silhouette pass to pull the far side out of the dark background).

CHASSIS — the judge's headline is CORRECT and literally verifiable. I rendered Swallow.png through the identical crop and the two images are the same chassis pixel-for-pixel in shape: same plump horizontal duck/tern body, same ball head, same bill, same two stacked folded wing leaves, same forked streamer tail, same yellow feet, same elliptical contact shadow. Only the palette differs — Swallow is steel-blue with an orange belly crescent; Swift is warm pale grey-taupe with cream speckle flecks, a white rim-light along the back and a glossy top highlight. This is a recolour of the Swallow asset, which is precisely the failure mode the packet note names ("Often drawn as a swallow").

WINGS — must-read "scythe-shaped crescent wings swept far back" is ABSENT. Correction to the judge: it is not "just the folded comma stroke" (singular). There are TWO overlapping folded wing leaves lying flat along the back — an upper long speckled leaf from the nape to x~285 and a second, paler leaf beneath it running to the rump. Both are closed-wing perched geometry, hugging the body outline; nothing projects away from the torso, and there is no crescent/sickle curvature anywhere in the silhouette. The boosted pass confirms no faint far-side wing hiding in the dark.

BILL — must-read "tiny bill with an enormous gape" is ABSENT. Judge is right that it is a pointed yellow wedge. Adding detail: it is a solid saturated-yellow triangular spike attached at mid-head height, roughly 0.6x the head diameter long and tapering to a sharp tip, with a thin darker culmen line and NO gape line, no gape corner behind it, no mouth opening. It reads as a tern/shorebird bill. Note it is also not "tiny" — it is conspicuously long, the opposite error from a swift's near-invisible stub.

LEGS — must-read "cigar body with almost no visible legs" is ABSENT/contradicted. Two bright saturated-yellow legs hang clear of the belly line at x~150-215, each with 3-4 long splayed toes, at the highest contrast anywhere in the image apart from the bill. Small correction: they are not "planted on" the ground shadow — they hang free, overlapping the dark elliptical contact shadow without touching down, so the bird reads as floating just above a surface rather than standing. That does not soften the defect; the legs are the single most eye-catching feature of the render. The body is also not a cigar — it is a deep-bellied oval about 2.0 tall-to-long, against the packet's aspect 3.

TAIL — the judge's description is WRONG here, and the truth is worse for the asset. It is NOT a "long undivided pointed tail." At 7x it is clearly DIVIDED: two long tapering streamers spring from a common base at x~275 and diverge into a shallow V with a distinct wedge notch between them, the upper one reaching x~345. That is a deeply forked tail with long outer streamers — the Swallow's must-read, and exactly what the Swift note forbids ("a much shorter notched tail, and no long streamers"). Beneath the tail base sits a fan of ~8 thin dark hairline strokes that read as stray hatching rather than feathers.

POSTURE — packet says flying; the render is a grounded/settled pose complete with a cast contact shadow.

Net: all three Swift must-reads are absent and the asset is a palette swap of the neighbouring Swallow. No reading of the pixels rescues this. FAIL stands.

FIX DIRECTION: this species needs its own chassis, not a tint. Open the wings into two long stiff sickle crescents swept far behind the body (anhedral bow, no folded-leaf overlay); shrink the bill to a near-invisible dark stub with a wide gape line running back under the eye; delete the legs and feet entirely (or leave a barely-visible dark tuck at the belly); replace the streamer tail with a short tail about one-quarter its current length carrying a shallow central notch; slim the torso to a true cigar at aspect ~3; and remove the ground shadow in favour of an airborne pose.

UPHELD, but the stated cause is half wrong and the real defect is worse than described.

WHAT I MEASURED (440x440 render, head faces right).

SHELL — the judge is RIGHT and understated it. I profiled the carapace top edge of Sea_Turtle.png against Tortoise.png from the same batch. Sea: x=101..292 (w=191), apex at x=191 (apexFrac 0.471 of width), apexY=136, plastron baseline y=202 -> dome height 66. Tortoise: x=98..285 (w=187), apex at x=186 (apexFrac 0.471 — IDENTICAL), apexY=141, baseline y=202 -> dome height 61. Sampled top edge at 10% intervals the two curves are the same curve, Sea sitting a uniform 4-5px HIGHER at every station. So the sea turtle's shell is not merely 'the same tall dome' as the family tortoise — it is 8% TALLER-domed than the land tortoise standing next to it in the same packet. The arc is symmetric front-to-back (apex essentially dead centre, in fact 3% REARWARD of centre), so there is zero teardrop: no forward-set high point, no long taper to a pointed rear, no low streamlined profile. Overlaid on it is the same concentric-arc + radial-spoke scute fan used on Tortoise and Box Turtle, pixel-for-pixel the family motif. Must-read 1, 'flattened teardrop shell', is ABSENT. Since the carapace is 231px of a ~275px creature, this alone decides how the sprite reads.

FLIPPERS — the judge's DESCRIPTION IS WRONG, their conclusion survives. They are not 'short rounded lobes' and not 'blobs'. Row-scanning the limb band: the rear limb runs from (169,218) to (82,260) and the front limb from (240,218) to (327,260) — each is an elongated, cleanly tapered ovoid paddle about 96px along its axis, i.e. HALF the carapace length, with a blunt rounded tip and no claws, no toes, no ankle. They are genuine paddles, splayed down-and-out in a shallow V, and the chassis has correctly dropped the tortoise leg columns. Credit where due: whoever drew this did change the limb primitive. The actual defect is that the front paddle is a pixel-mirror of the rear one — identical axial length (96 vs 96), identical width taper, identical root width and root Y. There is therefore no fore/aft asymmetry at all, and nothing wing-like: no long slender blade, no distinct swept leading edge, no forelimb reaching forward past or below the head to a narrow tip, no rear limb reduced to the short broad rudder that makes the contrast legible. Must-read 2, 'long wing-like front flippers', is at best half-present — 'paddles yes, wings no'.

HEAD — the judge did not mention it and it is the one must-read that PASSES. At 8x the head is a full egg-shaped mass carried forward on a short thick neck, entirely outside the shell, with a dark wedge upper beak overhanging a visible lower jaw line, and a small white-ringed eye with black pupil set high and forward. 'Blunt beaked head that cannot retract' is satisfied as written. Caveat for the fixer: it is the identical head primitive used on Tortoise and Box Turtle, so it satisfies the letter of the must-read while contributing no sea-turtle specificity.

OTHER: no tail element anywhere — the rearmost pixel at x=82 is flipper, 19px behind the shell edge. The packet sets posture 'swimming', but the sprite sits on a ground-contact drop shadow with both paddles angled down toward it like splayed legs, which actively reinforces the land read.

NET: one of three must-reads present, one half-present, and the missing one is the silhouette. Standing beside Tortoise.png this is the same animal with paddles instead of columns. FAIL stands.

FIX DIRECTION (in priority order): (1) rebuild the carapace as its own low teardrop — target dome height ~30-35px on a 191px width (ratio ~0.17, roughly half the current 0.35), apex pushed forward to ~0.35 of width from the rear, with a long straight-ish taper running back to a narrow, near-pointed rear margin, and drop the concentric-fan overlay for a forward-fanning row of large flat scutes; (2) make the front flipper roughly 1.7-2x the rear one's length, narrow it into a swept blade that reaches forward and down past the head's leading edge and finishes in a narrow tip, and shrink the rear limb to a short broad rudder; (3) if the packet's 'swimming' posture is meant to render, remove or soften the ground shadow and lift the flippers to a horizontal downstroke rather than pointing them at the floor.
