CORRECTION 1 - 'no massive hooked beak' is partly wrong. A beak IS drawn: a tan/olive wedge that starts at the eye, runs forward and terminates in a distinct DOWNWARD HOOK that overhangs past the face outline (clearly visible at 8x). The defect is scale and character, not absence - it is a small bird-of-prey beak pasted flat on the cheek, not the massive shearing snapper jaw, and it has no gape line, no wide mouth corner, no upturned lower jaw.

CORRECTION 2 - the head is undersized rather than merely 'a small rounded blob'. Measured, the skull is a smooth featureless ovoid ~52px wide (246-298) and with the beak reaches x305, so head+beak is ~59/285 = headFrac 0.21 against the packet's required 0.28. There is no cranial bulk, no cheek mass, no jaw muscle - it is the generic tortoise head primitive.

CONFIRMED - shell. The carapace is a tall, smooth, glossy HIGH DOME with a tortoise silhouette, rising well above the back and easily large enough to withdraw into, the opposite of the must-read. It is not literally featureless: it carries several pale arc scute lines across the dome, but those read as specular highlight arcs on a polished surface, not as the rough keeled ridges and serrated rear margin of a snapper.

Net: two of three must-reads are absent (rough undersized ridged shell; saw-toothed crested tail at the rear) and the third is present only in miniature. Combined with a spike projecting out of the animal's face, the asset reads as a generic domed tortoise with a bird beak and a misplaced spear, not a snapping turtle. FAIL upheld.

rows.readsAs: a softshell turtle — the only asset here that is not the family dome
rows.defect: The pancake carapace is right: low, smooth, mottled, no scutes, with a soft flared rim. The other two must-reads are missing. The snout is the same tiny downturned wedge beak used on every other asset, with no tubular snorkel proboscis — and the head is drawn far smaller than the stated headFrac 0.3, reading as an afterthought on the shell edge. The feet are the same flat rectangular leg columns, not broad fully webbed paddles.
rows.fix: Extend the snout into a narrow tubular snorkel projecting well forward of the eyes, and splay the feet into wide flat webbed paddles clearly broader than the leg above them.

rows.readsAs: a tortoise
rows.defect: The best read in the batch — tall dome, blunt beaked head, upright leg columns — but the detail must-reads are absent. The shell carries a concentric spiderweb fan of thin arcs instead of raised pyramid-growth scutes, so it has no relief and no scute grid. The legs are flat featureless rectangles, not scaly elephantine columns, and the toes are three scratched notches rather than blunt claws. The neck is a short smooth stub with no wrinkles and no sense that it retracts. It is also indistinguishable from the Box Turtle asset apart from being a shade lighter.
rows.fix: Break the carapace into a grid of raised scutes with individually shaded pyramid peaks and a visible marginal row, and give the legs pebbly overlapping scale texture with a splayed clubbed foot.

rows.readsAs: a small dark monkey or a baby gorilla squatting
rows.defect: All three must-reads are missing. The ears are tiny dark round nubs flush with the skull, not enormous naked bat-like ears. The hands are undifferentiated dark paddles with no skeletal wire-thin middle finger anywhere. The tail is a thin smooth crescent stub roughly a third of the body, not a huge shaggy tail bigger than the body. The pelt is flat matte brown with pale blotches and no shag.
rows.fix: Rebuild the head with two oversized bare petal ears wider than the skull, add a single splayed elongated needle-thin middle digit on the near hand, and replace the stub tail with a bottlebrush plume longer and thicker than the torso.

rows.readsAs: a generic dark ant or beetle
rows.defect: Stout dark body and absent wings do read. But the dense insulating hair over the thorax is not there — insulation is represented by a sparse ring of small yellow spikes on the segment joints, which reads as bristle armour rather than fur. Thorax and abdomen are two nearly equal smooth ovals, so the animal has no thoracic mass; the legs are single hairless hairline strokes.
rows.fix: Coat the thorax in a thick shaggy pile that visibly breaks the silhouette edge, and make the thorax clearly the bulkier of the two segments.

rows.readsAs: a bare white winter shrub or a bleached bonsai
rows.defect: The bone-white branching colony is present and the colour rule is respected. The polyps are wrong: they are soft pink blurred beads scattered along the lower TRUNKS and around the base, not cup-shaped polyps opening at the branch tips, and the branch tips are bare. The trunks are also a separate flat grey column layer sitting visually behind the white branchwork instead of continuous with it.
rows.fix: Move the polyps to the terminal tips as small open cups with visible rims, and paint the trunks in the same bone-white material as the branches.

rows.readsAs: a generic aquarium fish, closest to a small trout or bream
rows.defect: Stout torpedo body and soft dorsal are there, but two of three must-reads fail. The tail is a solid swept wedge with only a faint notch, not a forked tail. There is no chin barbel at all. The snout is drawn as a narrowing point rather than a blunt rounded cod muzzle, and the declared 3.5 aspect renders closer to 2.2, so the fish is too deep-bodied for a cod or char.
rows.fix: Cut a true deep V into the caudal and hang a single visible barbel under the chin, then blunt the snout to a rounded muzzle.

rows.readsAs: the Cold-Water Fish recoloured purple with a string of fairy lights glued along its belly
rows.defect: This is pixel-for-pixel the Cold-Water Fish chassis — same outline, same dorsal, same wedge caudal, same scale mesh, same eye — with a hue swap and a bead row added. Every identity must-read is absent: the mouth is a hairline slit with NO oversized jaw and NO needle fangs; the eye is the same tiny white dot as the shallow-water fish, not a large light-gathering eye; the body is a hard-scaled plum fish, not a black soft body, and the photophores are a single tidy conveyor of uniform cyan capsules rather than scattered specks.
rows.fix: Draw a new body: hinge open an outsized jaw crowded with visible needle teeth, blow the eye up to occupy most of the head, and drop the scale mesh for a matte black soft skin with irregular photophore specks.

rows.readsAs: a dumbo octopus, or at a glance a pink cyclops squid
rows.defect: The best asset in the batch — ear fins on the mantle, webbed umbrella and soft body all read. But the head is presented frontally with only ONE eye, dead-centre-right, so it reads as a cyclops; the second eye is simply not drawn. The eight arms are not resolvable — the web is a smooth fan with radial creases and the arm tips are not distinguishable at the hem. The body is opaque saturated magenta rather than translucent gelatinous.
rows.fix: Add the second eye symmetrically on the mantle and let eight arm tips break the web hem as visible points.

rows.readsAs: a tropical red gorgonian or a plastic aquarium ornament
rows.defect: Two failures at once. It is the identical geometry to Cold-Water Coral — same trunk fan, same branch tree, same crown, same polyp-bead scatter, same shadow — with only a hue change. And that hue change breaks the one must-read that IS the identity: the reference demands a pale thicket with NO algal colour, Lophelia-type white, and this is rendered in saturated blood crimson, the exact tropical-reef colour the note forbids. Polyps are again beads on the trunks, not cups at the tips.
rows.fix: Recolour to chalk white with a faint pink cast and rebuild the branch structure so it is visibly a different thicket from the Cold-Water colony, with cup polyps at the tips.

rows.readsAs: a bat, but a cartoon plush one — a banana-yellow toy with a smiling red mouth
rows.defect: Membrane wings over finger struts and large upright ears do read, so the organism is named right. Missing detail: no spike tragus in either ear; no uropatagium — the wing membranes stop at the flanks with a bare gap under the body instead of running to the ankles and enclosing the tail; the feet are two small dark blobs with no visible hooked claws. Palette and face are the bigger problem — a glossy yellow body with round blue eyes and a red grinning mouth reads as a toy mascot, not a vespertilionid.
rows.fix: Run the membrane down to the ankles and enclose a tail between them, add a pointed tragus inside each ear, and drop the yellow-and-blue toy palette for brown fur with a dark face.

rows.readsAs: a bright green reef fish — a tang, discus or surgeonfish
rows.defect: Wrong organism, and wrong body plan. Mahi-mahi is a long ribbon of a fish; this is a near-circular deep disc on a narrow caudal stalk, so the declared 3.4 aspect is not on screen. The blunt vertical male forehead is absent — the head tapers to a point at the snout. The single dorsal running from just behind the eye to the tail is absent; there is instead a short triangular dorsal roughly mid-back plus a few loose spines. The body does not taper hard to the rear, it steps down abruptly to a stalk. Only the forked tail is correct, and the fluorescent lime green is a costume colour, not the blue-gold of a dorado.
rows.fix: Redraw on a long low elongated body with a squared-off vertical forehead and one continuous dorsal fin from the eye all the way to the caudal peduncle.

rows.readsAs: a purple jellyfish
rows.defect: The reference states outright that this is not a jellyfish and has no bell, and the render is a bell: a smooth wide-than-tall purple dome with tentacles hanging from its rim. The crimped sail crest — the must-read that separates it from every jellyfish — is reduced to a single thin white arc on top of the dome that reads as a specular highlight, with no crimping and no fin standing proud of the float. The tentacles are also uniformly short and even, not a curtain of extremely long trailing threads, and the whole thing renders roughly square rather than the declared 0.3 tall aspect.
rows.fix: Replace the dome with a tapered gas float carrying a tall scalloped sail crest standing clearly above it, and drop the tentacle curtain to several times the float height.

rows.readsAs: a generic small yellow daisy or miniature sunflower on a fern-like leafy stalk
rows.defect: The dark eye is actually there (centre samples ~RGB 84,65,24 against golden 232,184,32 rays) so the identity is not absent, but it is a FLAT olive-brown disc with no dome shading, no highlight and no shadowed underside — it reads as a printed dot, not a raised chocolate cone. Two of the three must-reads are simply missing: the rays are short broad upswept wedges in flat lemon-gold (232,184,32), not the long narrow slightly-DROOPING golden-orange rays that give Rudbeckia its shuttlecock profile, and there is no bristle or hair anywhere — the stem is a smooth constant-width green line and every leaf is a clean untextured blade with a single midrib. The head is also far too small for the plant (roughly 30px of a 440px canvas) so the whole read is dominated by eight identical OPPOSITE leaf pairs marching up the stem in a mechanical ladder, when the reference specifies alternate leaves on a rough stem.
rows.fix: Rebuild the head: double its diameter, replace the flat disc with a domed chocolate-brown cone (dark core, warm rim-light on the upper left, cast shadow onto the ray bases), and redraw the rays as 13-16 long narrow orange-gold straps that reflex DOWNWARD below the horizontal — then stipple short pale bristles along the stem and leaf margins and re-space the leaves as alternate rather than opposite pairs.

rows.readsAs: a row of glowing green patio umbrellas / cocktail parasols
rows.defect: The rotting-wood substrate is entirely absent - the four stems plant straight onto a bare shadow ellipse. The glow is emitted uniformly by the whole body including the cap tops, so the reference's 'light comes from the gills and stem, not the cap top' does not read; radial gill lines are present but faint and only on the near edge. The subject occupies about a quarter of the frame width, lost in black.
rows.fix: Seat the cluster on a visible dark rotting log with bark texture, kill the emission on the cap tops so only the gill fan and stem glow, and scale the cluster up to fill the frame.

rows.readsAs: a warty purple-black nugget beside a small ball with a logo decal on it
rows.defect: The whole truffle reads correctly - irregular lump, small pyramidal warts on the rind, no stem or cap. The cut face fails: it is a clean white-outlined circle containing four or five straight scratched lines that read as a printed emblem or peace sign pasted onto a second intact ball, not as a marbled interior. There is no dark flesh field behind the veins and no branching lace.
rows.fix: Redraw the cut face as a flat purple-black ellipse filling the sliced half, with fine white veins branching and reconnecting across it, and remove the circular outline ring so it stops reading as a decal.

rows.readsAs: four white canoe hulls or feathers nailed to a brown fence post
rows.defect: None of the three must-reads is present. The forms are thin flat lens shapes tapering to a sharp outer point, not a thick woody hoof; there are zero concentric growth bands on the top; there is no pore surface, only an unmodulated cream gradient. The trunk is a flat rectangle of solid brown with a straight vertical seam - a post, not a tree. Worst, the packet explicitly says a bracket must read as ONE thick hoof and the shelf as many thin tiers, and this is drawn as four thin tiers.
rows.fix: Replace the four blades with a single thick hoof-shaped half-disc bulging out of a rounded bark-textured trunk, ridged with 5-6 concentric zone bands across the top and a flat pale pored underside.

rows.readsAs: three generic yellow toadstools with burnt-black cap tops
rows.defect: The cap upper surface renders as a hard-edged near-black ellipse sitting on the golden rim, which reads as a hole or a scorch, and directly contradicts 'egg-yolk golden yellow throughout'. The cap is a flat disc perched on a thin post - there is no funnel or vase profile and no wavy lobed margin. There are no blunt forking ridges anywhere, and nothing runs down onto the stem; the stem is a separate pale cylinder of a different colour that meets the cap at a hard butt joint.
rows.fix: Rebuild the profile as a continuous vase - a depressed funnel cap with a wavy lobed rim flowing without a joint into a solid stem, all one egg-yolk yellow - and hang fat blunt forking ridges down the underside onto the upper stem.

rows.readsAs: pale blue-white ice shards or feathers on a brown post
rows.defect: This is the Bracket Fungus image re-tinted - identical brown rectangular post, identical four tapered lens blades at identical heights and offsets - with the fill changed from cream to a cold blue-white. The species' entire identity is colour, and the brilliant sulphur-yellow to salmon-orange top and bright yellow pore underside are completely absent; the render is the coldest thing in the batch. No suede wavy lobed edge, no fleshy thickness, no pore surface.
rows.fix: Draw a distinct chassis - thick fleshy overlapping shelves with soft wavy lobed margins - and paint them salmon-orange grading to a bright sulphur-yellow rim with a yellow pored underside.

rows.readsAs: three bare winter saplings or a dead shrub at night
rows.defect: It reads as leafless trees, not a fungus. There are three separate stems rising from three separate points instead of one dense cluster from one thick base, and the branching is fine, wiry and repeatedly bifurcating to sharp hairline points - the opposite of the required blunt or forked fleshy tips. The mass is open and airy rather than dense, and the outline is a tree crown, not an antler clump.
rows.fix: Fuse the stems into one thick fleshy base, thicken every branch so the taper is gradual and the branch stays plump to its end, and cap each tip with a rounded blunt or two-pronged fork.

rows.readsAs: orange-tipped matchsticks or corn dogs stuck in a brown bread roll
rows.defect: The host is an anonymous smooth brown ellipse lying on the ground with a few short tick marks along one edge - no head, no thorax, no legs, no segmentation, nothing that reads as an insect. The packet's note says exactly this case fails: without a legible host it is just a club fungus. The stalks are hairline sticks of uniform width and the fertile heads are smooth speckled capsules with no roughened swelling, so they read as matches rather than stromata.
rows.fix: Model the host as a recognisable insect - segmented abdomen, curled legs, a head with visible eyes - lying on its side, and have the clubs erupt from between its segments with visibly swollen, pitted fertile heads.

rows.readsAs: a small green-shaded table lamp
rows.defect: Cap colour, the white ring and the white stem all read. Two failures: the sac-like volva - the packet's stated identifying feature - is only a slightly wider rounded solid pedestal at the stem foot, with no cup lip, no ragged sac wall and no separation from the stem, so it reads as a lamp base. And the cap is scored with dozens of hard evenly spaced radial ribs running to the rim, which reads as an umbrella frame or lampshade panelling rather than 'faint radiating fibrils' on a smooth cap.
rows.fix: Replace the pedestal with a distinct white sac cupping the stem base - a torn-edged bag whose rim stands away from the stem - and reduce the cap ribs to a few soft off-centre streaks on an otherwise smooth dome.

rows.readsAs: a white art-deco desk lamp
rows.defect: Entirely white and a thin ring are both present, but this is the Death Cap object with the cap hue removed - same dome, same radial fan under the rim, same straight shaft, same collar disc, same foot - so the two are indistinguishable as designs. The volval cup is again a solid rounded block the stem sinks into, with no visible cup, and the stem is short and thick rather than slender and tall.
rows.fix: Lengthen and slim the stem, and open the base into a real white volval cup with a free ragged rim standing clear of the stem so it silhouettes as a bag, not a lamp foot.

rows.readsAs: a naval mine / a spiked sea urchin ball
rows.defect: The rays are thin needle spikes stabbing outward from the equator of a grey sphere. The must-read is a THICK outer skin split into pointed rays peeled BACK and downward so the sac sits in the bowl of a star - here nothing is peeled back, there is no star lying under the sac, and the rays have no thickness or inner/outer surface. The single raised pore is present as a dark dot, but it is the only correct element. The whole render is also so dark it is barely legible against the background.
rows.fix: Redraw as a fleshy tan outer wall split into 6-8 broad triangular rays curled back and touching the ground, with the papery grey sac resting in the middle of them, and lift the exposure so the form is visible.

rows.readsAs: a bouquet of small white mushrooms - close to enoki
rows.defect: The bouquet reads and the fused stub base reads, which makes this the strongest asset in the batch. But the stems are not needle-thin: each is a triangular wedge that flares steadily wider toward the top, so they read as light beams or paper streamers rather than stalks. And the caps are full domed agaric caps several times wider than the stalk they sit on, not the tiny pinheads barely wider than the stem that the reference requires.
rows.fix: Make every stem a constant hairline width from base to cap, and shrink the caps to small round pinheads only slightly wider than the stem.

rows.readsAs: fly agaric - correctly and instantly
rows.defect: The scarlet dome and irregular scattered white warts read at a glance. Two of three must-reads are missing outright: there is no pendulous white ring skirt anywhere on the stem, and there is no bulbous scaly volval base - each stem is a plain flat-bottomed rectangle that widens slightly and simply stops. The warts are also soft blurred blobs rather than raised veil scraps.
rows.fix: Add a drooping white ring skirt below the cap and swell the stem foot into a bulb ringed with two or three scaly volval belts.

rows.readsAs: two smooth cream eggs or ping-pong balls
rows.defect: Featureless, capless, stemless and pale, which is right, but nothing conveys 'giant' - there is no grass, no ground plane, no scale cue at all, and the two balls float on a shadow smear. The surface is a glossy smooth sphere gradient rather than leathery kid-glove skin, and the scattered grey dots read as mould spots or dirt rather than skin texture. Neither specimen shows the aged split or spore puff.
rows.fix: Seat the balls in visible grass or leaf litter for scale, matte the highlight down to a soft leathery surface, and split one of the two open with a brown spore cloud escaping.

rows.readsAs: a sweet potato or a lump of amber putty
rows.defect: The convoluted brain-like folding that IS this organism is absent - the form is two smooth rounded blobs merged into a potato silhouette, with three or four thin scratched lines drawn on the surface as a substitute for folds. It is fully opaque with a solid amber fill, so no light passes through any lobe. There is no bark and no substrate; it sits on a bare shadow ellipse.
rows.fix: Rebuild the mass out of many overlapping wavy lobes so the outline is frilled and the interior self-shadows, drop the opacity so back lobes show through front ones, and clamp it onto a visible bark surface.

rows.readsAs: a brown broccoli head or a bare-trunk tree crown hovering over a small white cone
rows.defect: The mass is a cloud of smooth chocolate-brown lobes with no ruffled spoon-shaped fronds, no overlapping rosette tiering, and no white branched stalk base — the single white cone below is disconnected from the mass by a visible gap of empty background, so the fronds do not spring from anything. Colour is a flat dark brown with no fawn/grey range and no white undersides anywhere.
rows.fix: Rebuild it as 30-40 overlapping spoon-shaped fronds fanning outward and downward in tiers, each with a grey-brown top and a white underside catching light, all converging into a visible white branched stalk cluster that physically touches the frond mass at the base.

rows.readsAs: a speckled brown rock, a potato, or a lump of ore with gold flecks
rows.defect: It is the batch blob chassis in brown. There is no leaf or fabric substrate at all — the blob is the whole subject, opaque and solid, so nothing shows through a film; the colour is a warm ochre-brown instead of chalky white to pale grey; and the orange sparkle dots read as embedded minerals, not as a flat powdery dusting. Every one of the three must-reads is missing.
rows.fix: Draw a leaf (veins visible) filling the frame and lay a thin translucent chalky-white blotchy film over part of it so the leaf's green and veins stay visible through the patches — the mildew must be a surface film, never the silhouette.

rows.readsAs: a mossy green rock or an asteroid with glowing specks
rows.defect: Identical blob silhouette to Mildew and Yeast with only the hue changed to green and the speckles to pale mint. None of the three must-reads is drawn: no tangled white hyphal fuzz, no upright stalks, and above all no dark round spore capsules on stalk tips — the dots are flat scattered specks inside the blob, not sporangia standing above a mat. No circular colony patches either.
rows.fix: Replace the blob with a low white filamentous mat and stand a forest of thin upright stalks on it, each capped by a distinct dark blue-green round sporangium in silhouette against the background.

rows.readsAs: a morel mushroom
rows.defect: The conical head, the pale cream stalk and the head-fused-at-the-base attachment are all correct and it is the only purpose-built body in the batch. But the pit texture is a flat repeating diamond lattice printed onto the dome — a wallpaper pattern with uniform cell size and no depth. The ridges are thin dark lines rather than pale raised walls, and the cells are not recessed, so the honeycomb reads as a decorative motif rather than a pitted surface.
rows.fix: Invert the value structure of the lattice: make each ridge a pale raised bevel with a highlight along its lit edge and each pit a dark recessed chamber with a cast shadow, and vary the pit size and row alignment so the network deforms with the cone's curvature.

rows.readsAs: orange flame licks or corn kernels jammed into a dark fence post
rows.defect: This is the shared shelf chassis: four sharply-pointed amber lozenges alternating off a dark post, the same shape used for Shelf Fungus and Turkey Tail. Nothing about it is an oyster mushroom — no fan or shell outline (the caps taper to a spike instead of widening to a fan), no gills of any kind let alone white gills running down to a stem, no stubby off-centre stem, and no inrolled wavy margin. The saturated marigold-orange also contradicts the pale grey-to-fawn colour called for.
rows.fix: Replace the pointed lozenges with wide fan/shell caps, broad at the free edge and narrowing to a short lateral stem at the wood, and rake white gill lines across the visible underside of the lower caps so the gills are the read.

rows.readsAs: a generic small brown toadstool, rendered as a doll in the middle of a mostly empty frame
rows.defect: The identity must-read — a fat barrel/bulbous stem far thicker than the cap is tall — is absent: the drawn stem is a narrow straight cylinder roughly a quarter the cap's width, taller than it is wide, which is the profile of a fragile agaric, not a bolete. The white net is drawn but as a small hard-edged rectangular wireframe grid floating on the stem rather than a fine raised reticulation following the stem's curve. The underside is a thin stippled band that could equally be gills. The whole organism occupies about a sixth of the canvas.
rows.fix: Triple the stem's width into a bulging barrel that is wider than it is tall and wider than half the cap, scale the whole subject to fill the frame, and give the underside a visible dome of tiny circular pores with a shadowed sponge texture.

rows.readsAs: a grove of pale bare trees, a banyan, or a mushroom cloud
rows.defect: The fine dichotomous branching is genuinely well drawn, but it is mounted on eight thick bare vertical trunks that rise clear of the ground before branching, and the branch mass is a single broad flat-topped canopy floating above them. That is a tree, not a lichen. The must-read spongy low cushion and springy mat are absent — there is empty background under the canopy where the mat should be — and there is no sense of hollow tubular stalks or of tips all nodding one way.
rows.fix: Delete the clear trunks and let the branching start at ground level, so the form is a low dense hemispherical cushion whose tubular branchlets divide in threes and fours all the way down, with the finest tips drooping consistently to one side.

rows.readsAs: red pepper pods, canoe hulls or flame licks stuck to a dark post
rows.defect: The exact chassis used for Oyster Mushroom and Turkey Tail, recoloured crimson with one extra blade. Each 'shelf' is a pointed lozenge, so there is no semicircular outline, no flat top, no flat underside and no staircase step-out — the blades all project the same distance and taper to a spike. The colour is a saturated tomato red rather than banded ochre and umber, and no pale buff pore surface is visible anywhere. It also fails the packet's own separation test against Bracket Fungus, since it reads as neither.
rows.fix: Swap the lozenge for a true half-disc bracket seen from slightly above — flat top with concentric growth bands, flat pale buff underside — and stagger the stack so each tier projects further than the one above it.

rows.readsAs: two tiny generic tan toadstools
rows.defect: The identity must-read, the cracked cap surface showing white flesh through the fissures, is completely absent — the caps are smooth domes with faint radial streaks. The margin is not inrolled and carries a row of hard dots instead of a fringe of white veil remnants; the gills are implied only by that dot row, never shown; and the stem is a thin, smooth, straight white pin set centrally, not a tough fibrous off-centre stalk. Both subjects are rendered at about a seventh of the frame height, leaving most of the canvas empty.
rows.fix: Scale the pair up to fill the frame and cut a network of pale fissures across each cap so white flesh shows through the umber skin, then roll the cap margin under and hang a ragged white veil fringe from it.

rows.readsAs: a stinkhorn, or at a glance a pair of white candles with green tips
rows.defect: The tall pale pitted phallic stalks and the dark olive thimble heads do land the core read. But the stalk rises from a flat splayed disc foot, not from a white egg sac — the volva, which is half the described identity, is not drawn. The head is a flat matte olive shape with no glisten, no highlights and no drips, so it does not read as slime, and there are no flies on it at all. The stalk pitting is a few soft grey smudges rather than a spongy chambered texture.
rows.fix: Sit each stalk in a split white egg sac at the base, then repaint the head as wet olive-black slime with specular highlights and a drip or two at its rim, and add two or three small dark flies on and around it.

rows.readsAs: tan canoe hulls or dried leaves pinned to a dark post
rows.defect: Third use of the identical shelf chassis, this time in flat tan with six blades. The species IS its banding, and there is none: each blade is a single uniform tan gradient with one faint pale swoosh, so the many contrasting concentric rings of rust, ochre, blue-grey, cream and black are entirely absent, as is the pale cream wavy outer rim and any velvety surface. The blades are also large, few and pointed rather than dozens of small overlapping rosetted fans.
rows.fix: Redraw as many small semicircular fans clustered in rosettes and paint five to seven concentric bands across each one that alternate in HUE, not just tone, finishing with a wavy cream rim at the outer edge.

rows.readsAs: a grey speckled rock or a dust-covered stone
rows.defect: The same blob chassis as Mildew and Mold, recoloured beige with white specks. Yeast is defined by its cells and none are drawn: there are no rounded oval single cells, no smaller bud swelling off one side of any cell, no bud scars, and no loose cluster of a few cells. A single opaque lump reads as bulk paste at best, and the halo of specks reads as dust, not as cells.
rows.fix: Drop the blob and draw five or six translucent oval cells at large scale, each with a smaller round bud budding off one shoulder and a few ring-shaped bud scars pocking the wall, arranged as a loose unattached cluster.

rows.readsAs: a scatter of red-orange medicine capsules on black
rows.defect: Nothing of the acid-mine habitat is drawn: the field is dark navy-black, not rust-red iron-stained water; there is no orange iron precipitate flocking the cells and no corroded mineral or pyrite grains anywhere. The colour is also inverted from the reference — the cells are painted red-orange while the reference calls them colourless in red water. The rods are chunky, not 'very small slender'. Strip the hue and this is byte-for-byte the Cryophile/Halophile/Methanogen rod field.
rows.fix: Flood the field with turbid rust-red acid water and hang orange ferric floc and angular pyrite grains through it, then draw the rods small, slender and near-colourless so the water carries the colour, not the cells.

rows.readsAs: a smooth grey egg or a teardrop-shaped stone
rows.defect: It has no pseudopods at all — the outline is a clean convex egg with one small pointed nub on the right, no blunt finger-like lobes anywhere, which is the single feature that makes an amoeba an amoeba. The interior is a smooth airbrushed gradient with no granular texture, and no clear ectoplasmic rim reads against it. One dark nucleus and two faint pale circles are present but sit in an otherwise featureless blob.
rows.fix: Break the outline with three or four fat blunt lobopodia of unequal length pushing out asymmetrically in one direction of flow, and give the endoplasm visible grain inside a clear hyaline rim.

rows.readsAs: four Euglena — teardrop cells with long whipping flagella and red eyespots
rows.defect: This is the wrong organism: pointed teardrop cells each trailing one long sinuous whip-flagellum and carrying a bright red eyespot is the textbook Euglena read, not a buoyant balloon cell with a stout trailing tentacle from a cleft. The required large near-spherical buoyant cells are absent, the cleft and stout tentacle are absent, and the emitted colour is mint green-teal — the note explicitly forbids green and demands cold blue-cyan. There is no sparking/flash quality; the cells simply glow flat.
rows.fix: Redraw as fat translucent near-spherical balloons with a single short stout tentacle emerging from a cleft, and swap the emission to a cold cyan-blue flash that blooms off the cells into the surrounding water.

rows.readsAs: a scatter of pale blue medicine capsules on black
rows.defect: The ice is entirely missing — no faceted ice-crystal boundaries frame the field and no thin liquid brine veins hold the cells, so the one cue that distinguishes a cryophile from any other rod is absent. The background is the same flat dark navy used by every other asset in this batch. The only surviving must-read is the blue-white cast, which is delivered purely by tinting the identical rod chassis shared with Acidophile, Halophile, Methanogen and Nitrogen-Fixing.
rows.fix: Build the frame out of large faceted ice-crystal polygons and confine the rods into the narrow dark brine veins running along the crystal boundaries between them.

rows.readsAs: filamentous algae / a stack of segmented teal noodles
rows.defect: The filament read is broadly right and the teal is right, but the layout is four near-parallel horizontal strands stacked evenly like ruled lines — there is no curving, no tangling and no loose mat, so it looks machine-stacked rather than grown. The 'beaded chain of identical cells' is rendered as flat ladder hatching drawn on a smooth tube rather than as distinct cells bulging the outline, and the larger pale cell is a single sphere planted dead-centre on every strand in the same place. This is the same drawing as Iron-Oxidizing Bacteria in a different hue.
rows.fix: Let the filaments curl, cross and pile into an irregular mat, make the cells actually bulge the filament edge so the chain scallops, and put the heterocysts at varied off-centre positions.

rows.readsAs: a schematic line drawing of a pennate diatom, or a lined leaf
rows.defect: The striae are regular and the central raphe with its polar and central nodes reads correctly, which carries the identification — but the cell is a hollow yellow wireframe with no painted body at all: there is no glassy silica substance, no sense of two valves fitting like a pillbox and its lid (no girdle line, no overlapping epitheca edge), and no golden-brown chloroplasts showing through the frustule. It is flat outline art in a family that is meant to be painted, and it shares that gold-wireframe language with Dinoflagellate.
rows.fix: Paint the frustule as thick translucent glass with a visible girdle overlap where the two valves meet, and set two golden-brown plastids inside so the pores read as holes through a solid shell rather than lines on empty space.

rows.readsAs: a dartboard, a spider web, or at best a centric diatom / radiolarian
rows.defect: The equatorial girdle groove — called non-negotiable in the reference — is completely absent, and so are both flagella. The cell is a perfect circle divided by radial spokes and concentric rings, which is radial symmetry: that reads as a centric diatom or a radiolarian, not as a dorsoventral armoured dinoflagellate. The 'interlocking polygonal plates' are wheel sectors, not the irregular tessellated thecal plates of a dinoflagellate, and the render is thin gold linework with no armour substance.
rows.fix: Rebuild it as an asymmetric top-and-bottom body split by a deep transverse cingulum belt, tuck a ribbon flagellum into that groove and trail a second longer one from the sulcus, and tile the two halves with irregular polygonal amber plates.

rows.readsAs: a Paramecium — a green ciliate ellipse fringed with cilia
rows.defect: Wrong organism outright: the cell is a blunt symmetric ellipse fringed all the way round with short bristles, which is the ciliate read, and it is literally the same drawing as this batch's Paramecium recoloured green. Every Euglena must-read is missing — there is no spindle body drawn to a tail point (both ends are equally blunt), there is no long anterior whipping flagellum at all, and there is no red eyespot anywhere (nothing red appears in the image).
rows.fix: Redraw as a smooth unciliated spindle rounded at the front and tapering to a sharp posterior point, with one long single flagellum emerging from the anterior reservoir and a small bright orange-red eyespot at its base.

rows.readsAs: a foraminiferan shell, though the halo reads as a sun-animalcule's spines
rows.defect: The chambered coil is the strongest read in the batch — chambers enlarge convincingly along the spiral and the dark aperture on the final chamber is clear. But the pseudopodia are drawn as dozens of straight, rigid, unbranching needles radiating evenly from the whole cell, which is exactly the heliozoan look the note warns against, instead of fine branching threads netting outward from the aperture. The shell walls show no pores, and the colour is a pale mint-green rather than chalky white or honey calcite.
rows.fix: Replace the straight spine halo with a fine anastomosing net of branching threads issuing from the aperture only, and retint the shell to chalky honey-tan with visible fine wall pores.

rows.readsAs: a scatter of hot-pink medicine capsules on black
rows.defect: All three must-reads fail. The cells are not densely crowded — there are about nine sparse rods with large empty gaps, so the field is not stained pink by their density; the brine around them is flat near-black navy. There are no angular salt crystals anywhere. No cells are flattened into squares or plates; every one is the same rounded capsule used by Acidophile, Cryophile, Methanogen and Nitrogen-Fixing. It is that identical rod chassis with the hue dialled to magenta, and it is barely separable from Nitrogen-Fixing Bacteria, which is the same pink at lower saturation.
rows.fix: Pack the frame edge-to-edge with cells so the brine itself glows hot pink from their sheer density, scatter angular halite crystals through the liquid, and flatten a proportion of the cells into irregular square plates.

rows.readsAs: orange segmented worms or noodles — a recoloured copy of this batch's Cyanobacteria
rows.defect: The defining structure is absent: there is no bean-shaped cell trailing a long twisted ribbon stalk. What is drawn is four evenly stacked horizontal filaments each with a sphere at its midpoint and ladder hatching along it — the identical construction used for Cyanobacteria, orange instead of teal. Nothing mats into ochre sludge; the background is the same empty navy. And the note's specific warning is violated head-on: the rust colour is painted onto the whole cell body rather than onto a secreted stalk.
rows.fix: Draw a small pale near-colourless bean cell at the tip of each element with a long rust-crusted twisted ribbon stalk streaming behind it, and let the stalks tangle into a matted ochre sludge instead of floating in a void.

rows.readsAs: a scatter of pale grey capsules on black — generic bacteria
rows.defect: The gas bubbles that the note says must carry the identity are entirely absent — not one bubble is drawn. The cells are also not clumped in irregular packets; they are evenly spread across the frame in the same loose diagonal scatter as every other rod asset here. There is no dark anoxic sediment or sludge; the background is the same empty navy void. With hue and habitat removed, this is indistinguishable from Cryophile.
rows.fix: Bunch the rods into two or three tight irregular packets bedded in dark anoxic sludge and send a rising train of methane bubbles up out of the cluster.

rows.readsAs: a scatter of salmon-pink capsules on black — the Halophile image at lower saturation
rows.defect: The root nodule is missing entirely: there is no host tissue, no enclosing nodule wall and no leghaemoglobin pink flush around the cells — the surround is the same empty navy as every other asset, so the pink appears on the rods instead of in the tissue, which inverts the reference. The cells are loosely scattered rather than densely packed inside anything. The swollen irregular Y-shaped bacteroids are absent; the couple of Y shapes visible are just two plain rods crossing at a corner, same rounded capsule as everywhere else.
rows.fix: Enclose the whole field in salmon-pink nodule tissue with the rods packed tight inside it, and mix in genuinely swollen, branched, club-headed Y bacteroids among the plain rods.

rows.readsAs: a ciliate — probably a paramecium, from the all-over cilia fringe
rows.defect: The cilia fringe is present and well drawn and the ciliate read lands, but the outline is a plain symmetric ellipse: there is no asymmetric slipper or shoe profile, no blunt anterior against a narrower tapered posterior, so the shape that names this species is missing. The oral groove is reduced to a short straight tick beside the centre and does not read as a diagonal groove cutting into the cell side. The khaki-olive tint is duller than the pale grey-green called for, and the body is the same ellipse used for this batch's Euglena.
rows.fix: Reshape the outline into a true asymmetric slipper — broad rounded front, narrowing tapered rear, one flank straighter than the other — and cut a clear diagonal oral groove running back from the front into the side with denser cilia lining it.

rows.readsAs: a long branching chain of lemon-yellow beads - a streptococcus chain or a bent bead necklace
rows.defect: The signature is a flat packet of EXACTLY FOUR spheres and the packet note says a chain reads as something else entirely - what is drawn is roughly 25 spheres in a Y-shaped, three-armed chain. Colour is wrong too: bright lemon-yellow, not salmon pink to red-orange. And there is no heavy layered envelope rim on any cell; each sphere is a plain glossy ball with a soft dark edge, the same bead used inside the Sulfur-Oxidizing filaments.
rows.fix: Draw four spheres only, in a 2x2 flat packet with the cells pressed flat against each other, recoloured salmon-to-red-orange, each ringed by a thick double-line envelope so the wall is visibly several times heavier than the cell outlines elsewhere in the family.

rows.readsAs: a radar sweep screen, or a red dartboard/wheel - a flat UI graphic, not an organism
rows.defect: It is a flat 2-D wireframe: one circle outline, three concentric rings and twelve straight spokes, filled with a red radial glow. Not one spine crosses the outer circle, so the defining halo of long fine radiating needles is entirely absent - the silhouette is a plain unbroken disc. The shell reads as red-on-black rather than clear glassy silica, there is no nested inner shell, and the 'dark central capsule' is a soft glow rather than a body. Nothing about it is three-dimensional or glassy.
rows.fix: Push a few dozen long straight needles out well past the shell so the silhouette is a spiked star, and rebuild the sphere as a lattice of hexagonal holes shaded to read as glass, with a small opaque dark capsule visible through it at the centre.

rows.readsAs: a single spherical colony ball tiled with pale overlapping scales - a scaly seed pod, a pinecone, or a Volvox coloured red
rows.defect: Scale is 'field of many' and the identity is a bloom, but this is one compact sphere floating in black. The water is not discoloured at all - the background is the same near-black void as every other asset in the batch - and there are no surface streaks or swirls. The cells are pale pinkish-white lens shapes with concentric contour rings, reading as scales or onion slices; none carries a girdle groove, and the red only survives as narrow gaps of ground colour showing between them, so the ball reads pale, not brick-red.
rows.fix: Replace the ball with a rust-red field: flood the whole frame with brick-red stained water, run two or three lighter swirl streaks through it, and scatter the plated cells at high density across that field with a clear horizontal girdle groove cut across each cell.

rows.readsAs: a speckled egg or a smooth grey river stone freckled with rust
rows.defect: The pale ground with scattered red-orange specks does get the watermelon-pink idea across, but it is painted as a shaded 3-D ellipse lit from the upper left and vignetted into black, so it reads as one solid object rather than a snowfield. There is no granular snow-crystal texture anywhere - the ground is a smooth airbrushed gradient. The cysts are flat soft dots with no thick wall and no rim, and not a single one shows the green chloroplast core the reference calls for, so the 'still green-cored' must-read is missing outright.
rows.fix: Kill the egg-shaped vignette and fill the frame edge to edge with faceted white snow granules, then sit clearly outlined thick-walled round cysts among them - with a green core left visible in about a quarter of the cells.

rows.readsAs: five long segmented filaments - readable as bacteria, but the beads make them look like snakes that each swallowed an egg
rows.defect: The filaments are stacked as five neat near-parallel horizontal bands with even gaps, a diagram layout rather than a tangled mat, and nothing overlaps or crosses. Each filament carries exactly ONE large sphere instead of being stuffed along its whole length with refractile granules, and that sphere is the same lozenge primitive that builds the coccus chain and the Thermophile rod. Worst of all the filament and the granule are the same pale yellow, so the lemon-yellow-globules-in-a-chalk-white-tube contrast that is the whole point does not exist. There is no dark sediment or vent surface under the mat - just void.
rows.fix: Recolour the filaments chalk-white, pack six to ten small bright lemon-yellow granules along each one, and cross the filaments over each other at varied angles over a dark sediment ground so it reads as a mat.

rows.readsAs: a scatter of generic orange rod bacteria on a slide - could be any bacillus
rows.defect: The rods themselves are fine, but they are sparse and randomly angled with big empty gaps and a stray pair drifting alone at the bottom of the frame - the opposite of the dense streaming bands the reference asks for. There is no banded mat and no sense of flow direction. The pale sinter mineral crust and the steam are both completely absent; the background is the same flat near-black void used everywhere in this batch, so nothing says hot spring. The rods also carry no visible thick wall - they are the plain glossy lozenge primitive stretched to aspect 2.
rows.fix: Pack the rods shoulder to shoulder into two or three curved bands that all flow the same way, and put them on a pale cream sinter crust with steam haze at the top so the heat context is visible.

rows.readsAs: a tortoise
rows.defect: Reads as a tortoise, but the carapace is a semi-transparent glassy dome with a thin concentric wireframe laid over it — it reads as a glass cloche or a covered-wagon canopy sitting on the animal rather than as keratin scutes, and you can see the body silhouette THROUGH it. Only two legs exist in the whole render (one fore, one hind); the far pair is entirely absent, so the animal reads flat and two-legged. The legs themselves are straight-sided featureless rectangles with three nick marks at the bottom for toes. Geometrically identical to s1 and s17 — pure hue swap.
rows.fix: Make the shell opaque with a hard rim-thickness edge and real raised scute polygons instead of drawn arcs, and add a dimmer far-side fore and hind leg behind the body so the animal has four legs.

rows.readsAs: a tortoise
rows.defect: Same identical tortoise geometry as s0 and s17 with only the hue changed to pale blue-grey, which is the family defect in its purest form. The pale palette makes the already-translucent shell dome read almost as an empty glass bubble — the wireframe grid and the body behind it show straight through, and shell and sky are nearly the same value at the top edge. Again only two legs are drawn; the far pair is missing. Legs are flat untapered rectangles.
rows.fix: Opaque, value-separated carapace with a dark rim and raised scutes, plus the missing far-side leg pair — and vary the shell profile/limb length from s0/s17 so the three are not one mesh in three colours.

rows.readsAs: a stubby long-bodied furry dog or weasel
rows.defect: Coherent and namable as a short-legged furry quadruped, but it is the batch chassis with fur texture on top: the same generic snout-blob head with one big round eye and a dot nostril, the same horizontal forward-right neck carriage, the same constant-diameter tube legs dropping out of the bottom of a uniform barrel with no shoulder or hip. The forelimb region is a separate pale lozenge pasted over the torso with a visible seam, and the two hind legs fuse into one slab so the animal reads as having three legs. Bottlebrush tail is a flat brush stroke stuck on at the barrel's end rather than emerging from a croup.
rows.fix: Give the limbs an actual joint break (elbow/stifle) and stagger the near and far hind legs so they separate, and let the torso taper into a haunch that the tail grows out of.

rows.readsAs: a jellyfish, or a mushroom cap on roots
rows.defect: The dome-plus-hanging-strands silhouette does read as a jellyfish or a stalked fungus, but there is a stray unfilled parallelogram outline sitting on the upper-left of the cap that is plainly a render artifact, not anatomy. The three pink dots read as eyes but are scattered without symmetry and one is half-buried under the cap rim so it is clipped. All ten tentacles are the same uniform-width noodle, all terminate at exactly the same ground line with a blunt flat cut, and none taper — they read as spaghetti props rather than as tentacles or roots.
rows.fix: Kill the stray quad outline, taper the tentacles and vary their lengths and terminations, and either place the sensory dots symmetrically or drop them.

rows.readsAs: a red glowing pony-shaped beast with a horn
rows.defect: Straight chassis reissue: same arched topline into a short right-facing neck, same deep untapered barrel, same tube legs exiting the bottom edge of the barrel, same lumpy toe-pad feet, same meerkat snout head with one round eye, same bottlebrush tail. The white glow orbs float unattached in front of and over the body with no emitter on the skin, so they read as lens flare pasted on rather than as bioluminescent organs. The horn is a plain white cone glued to the muzzle with no boss or base. Dark speckle markings clump into a blotch over the shoulder instead of following the form.
rows.fix: Anchor each glow orb to a visible node on the hide (a small raised bump with the glow centred on it) and seat the horn in a thickened frontal boss.

rows.readsAs: a six-legged orange plated beast
rows.defect: Adding a third leg pair does not make a new animal — it is the same chassis with the same dowel repeated: three identical constant-diameter tube legs per side, all dropping vertically out of the flat bottom of the same barrel, all ending in the same lumpy toe pad, all the same length and all evenly spaced like table legs. Same right-facing snout-blob head with one eye, same horizontal neck, same bottlebrush tail. The dorsal plates are five identical teardrop shapes sitting ON the topline rather than growing out of it, and they float clear of the back at the tail end. Glow orbs again unattached.
rows.fix: Differentiate the three limb pairs (thoracic pairs shorter and angled, rear pair heavier) and root the dorsal plates into the back with a base shadow so they read as attached.

rows.readsAs: a dark eight-legged plated beast
rows.defect: The torso is so dark it reads as a hole in the image rather than as mass, and a lighter translucent grey sheet is draped over it that you can see the barrel through, so the body has no solid read at all. The four pale ribbed leg pairs are crammed together with almost no spacing, all identical in length and diameter, all dropping vertically from the flat underside — they read as a row of fluted columns, not limbs. Head is the same snout-blob, nearly lost against the dark torso. Dorsal plates again sit on top of the line rather than growing from it.
rows.fix: Raise the torso value so the body silhouette is solid and readable, and spread/stagger the leg pairs with depth-darkened far-side limbs.

rows.readsAs: nothing — a stray torpedo shape in the corner of an empty frame
rows.defect: Broken render. The entire organism is a small pale-teal torpedo shoved into the lower-right quadrant, leaving the top ~60% and the whole left half of the canvas empty. It has no legs, no readable head-to-body relationship — just a fin/spike at the left end, a tube, and two blunt knobs at the right — and it hovers above the ground shadow rather than standing on it. Worst of all, three vertical tick marks are stranded at the far LEFT edge of the frame at mid-height, completely detached from the body: a fragment orphaned off to one side. Nobody can name an organism from this.
rows.fix: Fix the layout transform so the body is centred and scaled to the frame, and re-parent the stranded left-edge marks (fin rays or whiskers) back onto the body they belong to.
rows.verifyWhy:
FAIL upheld, but several of the stated causes are wrong and one much worse defect was missed. Packet reference row is NONE (procedural — judge coherence and against batch siblings), so I rendered s13/s14/s16/s17 alongside: every one of them faces RIGHT, tail LEFT, head with a visible eye and muzzle, four legs with feet, subject centered and filling the frame. That is the batch convention s15 is measured against.

WHAT IS ACTUALLY THERE (measured on the 440x440 PNG; body bbox lum>45 is x172..381, y272..364, i.e. 209x92 px; only 2.56% of frame pixels are lit; bbox area is 9.9% of the frame):
- LEFT END: a genuinely well-drawn two-lobed FORKED CAUDAL FIN — upper and lower triangular lobes meeting at a clean peduncle, painterly warm-cream rim light on both leading edges. This is the strongest part of the asset and is correctly placed at the tail end per batch convention.
- MIDDLE: a competent fusiform torpedo trunk, desaturated sage/teal-grey with a continuous cream dorsal highlight ridge. Rendering craft here is fine.
- RIGHT END (= the HEAD end by batch convention): THE HEAD IS ENTIRELY ABSENT. The trunk terminates in a hard, perfectly vertical FLAT-CUT WALL (a straight geometric seam, not anatomy) at approx x=352. Out of that truncation emerge two thin tapering stick appendages: an upper one arcing up-right to a rounded club tip at (381,291), and a lower one angling down-right to a hoof/club at (378,340). There is NO cranium mass, NO eye, NO jaw, NO muzzle, NO ear anywhere in the frame — I brightness-boosted 2.6x and zoomed 10x on x300-390/y280-360 to confirm. The other judge said 'no readable head-to-body relationship', which implies a head exists but is illegible; the truth is harder — there is no head object at all, and the flat vertical truncation where it should attach is itself a render artifact.

CORRECTIONS TO THE CLAIM:
1. 'legless' — OVERSTATED. There IS one prominent stick limb ending in a hoof at lower-right (the lower of the two front appendages), plus TWO tiny vestigial dark triangular nubs on the ventral line at approx x=305 and x=340 — the leg system fired but generated near-zero-length limbs. The trunk carries no walking legs, so the read is legless, but the fix target is 'limbs generated at ~0 length' not 'limbs missing'.
2. 'entire left half of the frame empty' — WRONG. The upper caudal lobe reaches x=172, which is 48 px LEFT of the frame midline (x=220). The empty band is the left 39% (x<172), not the left half.
3. 'top 60% ... empty' — CONFIRMED and precise: topmost body pixel is y=272 = 61.8% down the frame.
4. 'shoved into the lower-right quadrant' — CONFIRMED. Body centroid approx (276,318) vs frame center (220,220): +56 px right, +98 px down.
5. 'hovering above its ground shadow' — PARTIALLY RIGHT. The trunk belly (approx y=338) does float roughly 7-10 px above the shadow ellipse (shadow occupies y approx 345..385, centered x approx 255), but the LOWER CAUDAL LOBE dips to y=364 and does cross into the shadow. So it is the torso/limb that hovers, not the whole organism.
6. 'three vertical tick marks stranded at the far LEFT edge at mid-height, completely detached' — FULLY CONFIRMED, exactly as described. Three pale vertical bars at x=58..73, y=305..321, with approx 100 px of pure background between them and the nearest tail tip. Clear feature-placement bug (spines/quills/frill emitted at a detached origin).
7. 'pale-teal torpedo' — accurate for the trunk color.

VERDICT: the craft is not the problem — the fin and the dorsal ridge are well painted. The ASSEMBLY is broken. An organism with no head, a hard vertical seam where the skull should mount, near-zero-length legs, and three detached tick marks a hundred pixels off-body cannot be named by a stranger; the closest read is 'a fish body with a cow's leg where its face should be'. FAIL stands. Fix priority: (a) generate the head/cranium at the front attach point and remove the flat-cut wall, (b) fix the detached spine-row origin at x approx 58-73, (c) restore non-zero limb length on the trunk, (d) recenter and scale the subject — it currently fills under 10% of the frame and sits 98 px below center.

rows.readsAs: a spiked caterpillar or grub
rows.defect: The lumpy segmented body with a row of dorsal spines does read as a grub or caterpillar, but the two ends are ambiguous: the right end has green eyes plus a long backswept spike, while the left end has a curled tendril with a highlight that reads equally like a head, so the animal has no clear direction. It is entirely legless — not a single proleg or foot touches the ground — so it reads as a spiky rock as easily as an animal, and the segment lumps are cloud-blobs with no repeating segment rhythm. The whole body sits in the bottom third with the upper half of the frame empty.
rows.fix: Add a rank of small prolegs along the underside and give the segments a regular repeating boundary, and lift the composition to use the frame.

rows.readsAs: a tortoise
rows.defect: The clearest read of the three tortoises, but it is the same mesh as s0 and s1 with a gold hue — identical shell arcs, identical beaked head, identical flipper crossing the neck, identical two rectangular legs. The shell is still a translucent dome with a wireframe grid drawn on it rather than an opaque scuted carapace, and the body is visible through it. Only two legs are drawn in the entire render; the far fore and hind pair are absent, so it reads as a flat two-legged cutout. The front flipper overlaps and partly hides the head.
rows.fix: Opaque carapace with real scute geometry, add the far-side leg pair, and move the flipper clear of the jaw line.

rows.readsAs: a blue-white striped plated quadruped
rows.defect: Chassis reissue again — same right-facing snout-blob head with one round eye, same horizontal neck, same deep untapered barrel, same tube limbs leaving the flat bottom of the barrel with no hip or shoulder, same lumpy toe pads, same bottlebrush tail plume. The pale blue palette leaves the body value almost identical to the grey stripe markings, so the stripes and the dorsal plates read as one grey smear across the flank and the form flattens out. Six dorsal plates are identical teardrops sitting on top of the topline, and the rearmost floats clear of the back.
rows.fix: Push value separation between hide and markings so the stripes read as pattern on a solid form, and seat the dorsal plates into the back.

rows.readsAs: a green spotted long-bodied civet or mongoose
rows.defect: Namable as a spotted carnivoran, but the head is the worst instance of the shared skull in the batch: an oversized perfect sphere with a dark ring decal on it, with a thin tube muzzle poking out of the right side — it reads as a balloon glued to the neck at the wrong scale rather than a skull, and the eye sits on the sphere far from the muzzle. Below that it is the batch chassis: uniform barrel, tube legs dropping out of the bottom edge with no shoulder or hip, lumpy toe pads. The ringed tail is a separate striped tube that meets the rump at a hard seam with a mismatched tip colour.
rows.fix: Rebuild the head as a tapered skull-plus-muzzle wedge sized to the neck instead of a sphere with a tube attached, and blend the tail root into the haunch.

rows.readsAs: a leopard-spotted civet or genet
rows.defect: The most convincing animal in the batch — the ringed tail, rosette spots and long low body genuinely read as a genet — but it is the chassis underneath: the same generic snout-blob head with a single big round eye and dot nostril, the same horizontal forward-right neck, the same untapered barrel with tube limbs dropping from its bottom edge. The forequarter is a separate pale lozenge pasted over the torso with a visible seam at the shoulder, and each leg pair fuses into a single slab so near and far limb are one shape. Four white glow orbs float unattached over and in front of the belly with no emitter on the hide.
rows.fix: Separate near and far limbs on both pairs with a depth-darkened far leg, and either anchor the glow orbs to visible skin nodes or remove them.

rows.readsAs: a red striped eight-legged beast with a horn
rows.defect: Chassis with four leg pairs added: eight identical constant-diameter tubes, evenly spaced, identical length, all dropping straight out of the flat bottom of the same barrel and all ending in the same lumpy toe pad — a table, not a gait. Same right-facing snout-blob head with one round eye and a plain white cone horn stuck on with no base. The tail is a thin bare noodle curling left that has no mass relationship to the heavy body, and it springs from the barrel's flank rather than from a croup. The dark stripes stop dead at the flank boundary in a straight vertical cut instead of wrapping the form.
rows.fix: Vary limb length and stance across the eight legs and wrap the stripe pattern around the barrel so it curves with the body instead of ending at a hard edge.

rows.readsAs: a plush dachshund-tapir toy with an armadillo hide
rows.defect: Head is grossly oversized against the barrel and sits on a visibly separate cheek/ear oval with a hard overlap seam; the cracked-tile hide is a rectangular decal that stops abruptly mid-flank instead of wrapping the form; legs are the family's stumpy featureless tubes with no shoulder or haunch, and the far-side pair is drawn identical to the near pair with no depth separation.
rows.fix: Shrink the skull to roughly one-third of its current mass and carry the tile pattern around the barrel with the shading so it terminates on the silhouette edge, not on a straight cut.

rows.readsAs: a red zebra-striped six-legged beast with pills stuck to its back
rows.defect: The dorsal row is five separate rounded blobs laid ON TOP of the topline with a hard visible edge - they read as detached capsules resting on the back rather than fins or plates growing out of it, and the frontmost one hangs past the shoulder into empty space. The torso is a stack of overlapping segments whose seams are all visible, and the six legs are the same identical tube repeated six times.
rows.fix: Cut the dorsal plates INTO the topline so the back silhouette itself is scalloped, rather than compositing separate blobs over a smooth back.

rows.readsAs: a green cartoon goat-lizard
rows.defect: Same barrel, same neck arc, same tube limbs, same eye as h0-s8/s9 with only the hue and the horn pair changed. The flank carries a leaf-vein texture that reads as a single leaf decal pasted flat on the side - the veins ignore the curvature entirely - and the shoulder oval seam behind the neck is plainly visible.
rows.fix: Replace the flat leaf decal with a hide pattern that follows the barrel's shading, and break the shoulder seam by letting the foreleg mass actually swell out of the chest.

rows.readsAs: a purple slug with a sail and a cluster of dot-eyes

rows.verifyWhy:
Verified at 1x, then re-read with 2.4x brightness lift and 5x/8x nearest-neighbour crops of both ends (left end 45,180 160x200; right end 290,230 110x110). The FAIL verdict stands, but two of the stated causes are wrong and the fix should not be made against them.

WHAT IS ACTUALLY THERE. A single fusiform, fish-like hull runs horizontally across the frame (roughly x=95 to x=327, y=235 to y=310), lit by a hard warm rim along its entire dorsal contour, with a soft ground-shadow ellipse painted below it. LEFT END: confirmed a large lunate/forked caudal fin -- two swept triangular lobes meeting at a narrow peduncle around x=95,y=280, with a small bright highlight bead at the peduncle joint. This is unambiguously a tail, so the RIGHT end is the head end, and the judge is right about which end carries the identity.

RIGHT END, CORRECTED. The judge says the hull 'simply stops' and that 'two thin knobbed stalks float in empty space with a gap to the body.' Both halves of that are wrong in ways that matter.
(a) The hull does not taper out or fade -- it is cut by a HARD, PERFECTLY VERTICAL STRAIGHT EDGE, a ~35px chord at x=327 spanning roughly y=265 to y=300. This is a clipped/unclosed hull cap: a straight machined wall where a snout should be. That straight vertical chord is the single most diagnostic geometric defect and it is not mentioned in the claim.
(b) NEITHER STALK IS DETACHED. At 8x the upper stalk is continuous with the body -- the dorsal rim highlight runs unbroken out of the back contour, up over the stalk and around its terminal knob, with no seam and no gap; it is a limb growing off the dorsal-caudal corner of the truncation. The lower stalk attaches flush to the BOTTOM corner of the same vertical wall (its proximal end sits at x=327, y=298, exactly on the hull edge) and angles down-right to a rounded pad/hoof terminal at ~x=365,y=320. The dark rectangular wedge between them is a NOTCH BETWEEN TWO ATTACHED LIMBS, not a gap between the body and floating parts. Anyone fixing this against 'reattach the floating stalks' will move geometry that is already attached and the asset will still fail.

WHY IT STILL FAILS. There is a rounded secondary lobe in the silhouette immediately before the truncation (roughly x=275-327) that occupies the position a head would take, but it carries ZERO features: no eye, no eye socket, no pupil dot, no mouth line, no jaw, no nostril, no gill slit or operculum, no cheek plane, no snout taper, no ear or barbel. I checked the terminal knobs of both stalks specifically for eyestalks -- neither knob contains a pupil, iris or any darker inset; they are plain shaded clubs, one club-tipped and one hoof/pad-tipped, so they read as limbs or flippers, not as eye-stalks that could stand in for a head. The result reads as a fish hull with its head sliced off at a vertical plane, with two legs bolted to the cut face. Wrong-organism-level failure: the head end that is the identity is absent, exactly as claimed.

SECOND DEFECT NOT IN THE CLAIM. On the lower flank at roughly x=155-200, y=288-312 there is a small rhomboid drawn as a THIN 2D OUTLINE ONLY -- a four-line diamond with no fill, no shading, no rim light, no shadow, sitting flat on the painted hull. Presumably an intended pelvic/anal fin, it currently reads as a wireframe/debug overlay pasted onto a painterly body and violates the painterly-canvas law on its own. Fix it in the same pass as the head.

FIX DIRECTION: close the hull with an actual cranium forward of x=327 -- snout taper, jaw/mouth line, and a readable eye placed on the rounded lobe -- rather than touching the two limbs, which are correctly attached; and re-render the flank rhomboid as a shaded fin volume.

rows.verifyWhy:
Verified by decoding the 440x440 PNG and re-reading it at 2x with gamma lift, plus 5x-8x crops of the cap, both silhouette edges, the waist, the base and the right-hand dots. The FAIL verdict stands, but two of the three stated causes are wrong and the fix must be made against what is actually there.

WHAT IS ACTUALLY DRAWN (top to bottom): (1) A wide dome/fan occupying roughly x=60..385, y=35..250 — a flat mauve-grey half-dome with a scalloped, beaded pale-pink rim running the whole upper arc, terminating in one slightly larger pale lobe at each end (left lobes at ~x=60-75,y=175-200; right lobe at ~x=360-380,y=185-210). The dome interior is flat with a visible horizontal tonal seam across it at ~y=115 and no volumetric shading, which is what makes it read 'blurry'. (2) The dome narrows to a genuine hourglass waist at ~(228,250), about 40px wide. (3) Below the waist the body flares back OUT into a solid dark triangular skirt (x=180..290 at its base, y=250..345). (4) The skirt bottom carries a fringe of five short rounded foot-nubs with four dark slots between them, spanning x~183..285, y~345..368, sitting on the cast-shadow ellipse.

CORRECTION 1 — the 'stalk does not line up with the base' claim is FALSE as described. The support and the base DO line up: the dark body is continuous cap -> waist -> flared skirt -> nub fringe, all on the same vertical centre (~x=232). The pale down-left bar the judge called 'the stalk' is not the stalk at all; it is a SEPARATE unpaired appendage, a straight pale-pink capsule about 12px wide, attached at the LEFT FLANK OF THE WAIST at ~(207,255) and running down-left to plant its end on the same ground line as the nubs at ~(150,368). It reaches the baseline; it is not dangling and it is not off-axis support. Its real defect is that it is a lone, unpaired, un-jointed stick crossing outside the silhouette with no mirror on the right, so it reads as a prop/staff rather than a limb.

CORRECTION 2 — 'three pink dots float unattached to the right' is FALSE for one of the three. The largest dot, ~9px with a distinct dark ring around it, sits INSIDE the body at ~(301,191), just above the dome's lower-right edge, and actually reads as a single lone eye. Only the other two float: ~(317,232) and ~(300,272), both unambiguously in the dark teal background outside any silhouette, with nothing connecting them. So the defect is two stranded background specks plus one orphan monocular eye, not three stranded specks.

WHY IT STILL FAILS: the judge's core organism read is right. There is no head end anywhere — no muzzle, snout, neck, ear pair, jaw or paired eyes; the dome is a smooth featureless bell. There is no tail. There are no legs other than the five stub nubs and the one unpaired left bar. The scalloped rim + flat bell + pinched stalk + flared fringed foot is the exact silhouette grammar of a mushroom (cap, ring, stipe, basal volva) or a sea fan / gorgonian, and at thumbnail size that is what it will read as in a fauna slot. The single ringed eye dot is the only animal cue in the whole image and one eye on an otherwise faceless bell is not enough to carry an animal identity. Fixes needed: give it a defined head end (paired eyes plus a mouth/oral cue on a distinguishable anterior), pair or delete the down-left bar, and delete or attach the two stranded background specks.

Verified at 1x, at 3x gain, and at 4-10x pixel zoom on the head, the stem field, the stem/slab junction, and the whole frame at 6x gain. Packet row is **NONE** (procedural), so this is judged on coherence alone -- and it is not coherent as a plant. VERDICT UPHELD, with corrections to the stated causes.

No root flare, no basal rosette, no soil contact, no widening. Combined with (3), the silhouette is a capsule with a scale down it — an instrument, not a stem.

Traced: the blade spans y=92 to y=166 (74px, ~17% of frame height) and x=164..207, so it is a substantial appendage, not a speck. The problem is that it is ATTACHED BACKWARDS. Its top edge at y=92 is a DEAD-FLAT HORIZONTAL CUT from x=164 to x=189 — a squared-off chopped end — and that end floats free in space with a 20px air gap to the stalk (at y=128 the blade ends at x=189, the stalk starts at x=210). The blade then sweeps down and right, narrowing, and its POINTED TIP is what finally touches the stem, at x~207, y~164. A leaf attaches at its broad base and its tip is free; this one has its tip welded to the stem and its blunt cut end waving in the air. That inversion is why it reads as a sickle, hook, or bracket handle rather than foliage — and it reinforces the instrument reading (it looks like a clip hanging off a gauge).

SUMMARY OF THE FIX SURFACE: there is no plant here to polish. Needed are taper along the stem, at least one growth node where an appendage leaves the stalk, an apical structure other than a dome cap, a root/base flare, foliage in the plant's OWN hue rather than dead grey, and the leaf re-anchored base-to-stem with the tip free. rows.defect: Five perfectly flat 2D pink ellipses of increasing width threaded onto a thin brown stick. Each ellipse is a pure geometric primitive with a uniform flat fill, an unbroken smooth rim, no leaf edge, no needles, no top-vs-bottom perspective difference and no self-shadowing where they overlap the stem. Nothing in the image says foliage; it reads as stacked crockery or a diagram of a pagoda.
rows.fix: Replace each flat ellipse with a lit, drooping frond tier whose rim is broken into individual leaf tips and which casts shade onto the tier below.

rows.readsAs: a bare thorn shrub, or a pile of pick-up sticks
rows.defect: Every branch is a perfectly straight, uniform-width segment with a blunt cut end, crossing its neighbours at repeating angles, so the shrub reads as scattered rods rather than as growth; there is no taper from trunk to twig, no curvature and no foliage at all. It also occupies barely a third of the canvas height, leaving the asset small and lost in empty field.
rows.fix: Taper and gently curve each branch so it narrows to a point, subordinate side twigs to their parent, and scale the plant up to fill the frame.

rows.readsAs: cotton candy on a skewer — the render is broken
rows.defect: Z-order failure: the dark trunk is drawn IN FRONT of the orange canopy and continues straight through it and on past the top of the foliage to the very top edge of the canvas, so a rigid stick bisects the crown and sticks out above it. The canopy itself is a formless ruddy blob with no leaf structure. The trunk is the same untapered constant-width line as s3/s9/h1-s1.
rows.fix: Draw the crown after the trunk and stop the trunk at the fork inside the canopy so no stem protrudes above the foliage.

rows.readsAs: a berry bush with pale leaves
rows.defect: The berry clusters read well and the red-on-pale contrast is the best colour decision in the batch, but every leaf is the identical circle with the identical radial highlight, repeated ~30 times at the same size, so the crown reads as a bunch of pearls or balloons rather than foliage. The shrub is small in frame and its brown stem segments are straight and untapered.
rows.fix: Vary leaf size, tilt and value across the crown and give the leaves an actual leaf outline (a tip and a midrib) instead of a sphere highlight.

rows.readsAs: a cream umbrella tree, or a table / a flat mushroom
rows.defect: The identical stick-and-pancake chassis as s3 and h1-s1 with the hue changed to cream. The canopy is one flat horizontal slab with a straight underside, jammed hard against the top edge of the frame, with a few pale spheres embedded in it and no leaf structure or branch entering it. The trunk is dead straight and untapered over its whole length.
rows.fix: Pull the crown down off the top edge, give the slab a domed, ragged, multi-lobed mass, and let visible branches carry it.

rows.readsAs: a cyan fern or cycad clump
a purple umbrella tree, or a table with a cloth on it
rows.defect: The third recolour of the same stick-and-pancake chassis (identical trunk length, width, x-position, fork and slab geometry as s3 and s9 — only the hue changed to purple). Canopy is a flat horizontal slab with a straight underside and no foliage read; two or three pale nubs sit on it with no explanation. Trunk untapered from ground to fork.
rows.fix: Give this variant its own crown geometry — e.g. a domed or drooping mass at a different height with real leaf clumps — instead of the shared slab with a hue swap.

rows.readsAs: a red sunflower or daisy
rows.defect: It names correctly, but it is flat clip-art rather than painted: the petals are uniform flat-fill lobes at even angular spacing with no overlap or curl, the central disc is one solid brown circle with zero floret texture or shading, and the two leaves are flat almond shapes stuck on the stem at implausible right-angle-ish attachments. The stem is a uniform-width untapered line.
rows.fix: Give the disc concentric floret texture and a shaded rim, overlap and vary the petals, and taper the stem with leaves that attach via a visible petiole.

rows.readsAs: a bundle of upright purple blades, or a closed tulip bud / a paintbrush
rows.defect: The blades have decent tubular shading, but the whole clump pinches to a single point at the ground with no base or root mass, so it reads as a held bundle rather than a growing plant. The three flat pink pill shapes stuck across the blades are unexplained — they read as capsules or chewing gum, not as buds, nodes or fruit, because they sit on top with no attachment and no shading tied to the blade beneath.
rows.fix: Splay the blade bases apart into a seated clump and re-form the pink pills as shaded buds attached at a node on a single blade.

rows.readsAs: a parasol mushroom, or a satellite dish on a pole
rows.defect: The cap is a featureless grey smear with a blown-out white hotspot at its centre — no foliage, veining or leaf edge anywhere, so the canopy reads as painted fog rather than plant tissue. The stem is a perfectly uniform straight rod with zero taper and no root flare, and it is over half the total height, which pushes the read toward hardware on a stand.
rows.fix: Taper the stem toward the crown and flare it at the soil, and give the cap a radial rib/leaf-edge break-up with a scalloped rim so it reads as fused foliage instead of a grey disc.

rows.readsAs: a pale fountain grass or sedge clump
rows.defect: The small white leaflet dashes along the inner stems are DETACHED — they hang in empty space beside the blades rather than joining them, so a dozen ticks float unattached in the middle of the silhouette. The whole clump also springs from a single infinitesimal point at the ground with no basal sheath or tussock.
rows.fix: Anchor each leaflet dash to its parent blade at the contact point and add a small tussock of short basal blades where the clump meets the ground.

rows.readsAs: an orange fountain grass — visibly the same plant as s13 in another colour
