rows.fix: Break the clone: give this one an oval cell with a visible macronucleus, a contractile vacuole and a full cilia fringe around the perimeter.

rows.readsAs: a teal arrowhead or play-button icon built out of beads
rows.defect: The bead-chains close into a filled triangular wedge, so the silhouette reads as a UI glyph rather than as bacteria; the chains also meet at hard shared beads at two corners, a junction cocci chains do not form. Same uniform bead primitive as s18 and s4.
rows.fix: Open the triangle — let the chains trail off loose at the ends instead of closing a corner, so the arrangement reads as drift rather than geometry.

rows.readsAs: a cloud of green smoke or a nebula — no organism is legible
rows.defect: A frame-filling blur that runs off all four edges with no boundary, silhouette or scale cue anywhere. The only concrete forms inside it are scattered tiny tick-marks and a dozen flat grey circles that read as dust specks or lens dirt rather than cells, and a few hairs escaping the right edge. Nothing in the render is contained by the canvas, so it fails the render test as well as the read test.
rows.fix: Pull the whole mass inside the frame with clear margin and give the colony a defined lobed edge, so it reads as one bounded biofilm with rod cells visible at its rim.

rows.readsAs: scattered rods — but the pearly plastic value reads as medicine capsules more than as bacilli
rows.defect: The rods are near-white with a glossy plastic sheen and several carry a crisp seam line exactly at the midpoint, which is the capsule join, not a division septum. At lower right one rod passes straight through another to form a hard T with no depth separation, which reads as a render glitch. The rods are also uniform in length and thickness.
rows.fix: Drop the value to a translucent stain colour, jitter rod length and width, and give the crossing pair an overlap shadow so one clearly lies above the other.

rows.readsAs: an out-of-focus photograph of dust motes, or smoke with confetti in it
rows.defect: The whole mass is blurred so heavily that no cell has an edge - it is a grey cloud with white rod-specks sprinkled over it, and there is no organism to find. Six curved hairs hang off the RIGHT edge only, three top-right and three bottom-right, attached to nothing visible, so they read as a render artifact rather than flagella. It is also the same drawing as microbe-h2-s16 with only the hue changed.
rows.fix: Cut the blur radius by two thirds so the bacilli read as discrete rods with lit edges, and either give the whip hairs a visible source cell or delete them.

rows.readsAs: a bicycle wheel, a dartboard, or a radar sweep dial - not a living thing
rows.defect: This is flat 1px vector line-work: a perfect circle, sixteen dead-straight spokes and three concentric rings laid over a featureless grey gradient disc. There is no silica texture, no areolae, no valve edge, no cell contents, no volume - nothing that says organism. The one legible read is a wheel. It is also geometrically identical to microbe-h2-s19, which is the same file in violet.
rows.fix: Rebuild it as a painted centric diatom - punch the radial chambers as actual pitted areolae with lit rims and cast shadow into the frustule, thicken and taper the ribs toward the rim, and break the perfect circle so it reads as glass rather than as a drafting compass.

rows.readsAs: pink gumballs or plastic beads, arranged in strings
rows.defect: The streptococcus-chain idea is legible, but every cell is a bare glossy plastic sphere with a hard specular dot and no membrane, no wall, no internal tone - they read as manufactured beads. Composition is scattered and off-centre: a three-sphere fragment floats detached in the upper-left corner with a wide empty gap to the main cluster, so the picture has no subject.
rows.fix: Join or delete the stranded upper-left triplet so there is a single chain, and swap the plastic specular for a soft translucent wall with a faint internal density.

rows.readsAs: flagellated protozoa - a cluster of trypanosome or sperm-like swimming cells
rows.defect: Reads correctly. Minor: the two large cells at right overlap into a symmetrical bunny-ear pair, and the lower-left flagellum crosses back under the group so its owner is momentarily ambiguous.
rows.fix: Rotate one of the two overlapping right-hand cells about 20 degrees to break the mirrored pair.

rows.readsAs: an amber dust cloud or a scan of pollen, out of focus
rows.defect: Same blurred-cloud drawing as microbe-h2-s12 recoloured amber - identical lumpy outline, identical scatter of rod specks, identical six curved hairs hanging off the right edge and nothing else. No individual cell has a readable boundary, and the hairs still attach to nothing.
rows.fix: Give this one a genuinely different colony architecture - a dense chained raft or a biofilm sheet - rather than the s12 cloud in a new hue, and sharpen the rods.

rows.readsAs: a tardigrade / water bear
rows.defect: Correct and legible - segmented barrel trunk, four pairs of stubby legs with visible claws, blunt eyeless-looking snout with a single eye spot. The only issue is family-level: it and microbe-h2-s5 are the same animal in the same green.
rows.fix: Nothing needed on this asset itself; differentiate its twin instead.

rows.readsAs: a paramecium wearing spectacles
rows.defect: The ciliate read is basically there - tilted ellipse, cilia fringe all the way round, an oral groove line - but the two hollow rings placed either side of the dark central oval snap together into a pair of eyeglasses on a face, which is the first thing the eye finds and it is wrong. The cilia are stiff straight spikes of uniform length, so the fringe reads as a burr or a scrub brush rather than as beating hairs.
rows.fix: Make the contractile vacuoles filled translucent bubbles of unequal size and move one off the shared horizontal so they stop pairing as eyes, and taper and curve the cilia with varied length.

rows.readsAs: a violet wagon wheel or a radar screen
rows.defect: Pixel-for-pixel the same construction as microbe-h2-s13 with the stroke and fill hue changed to violet - same radius, same sixteen spokes, same three rings, same flat gradient disc. As with s13 it is bare vector line-work with no silica texture, no cell contents and no volume, so it reads as a diagram of a wheel rather than as an organism, and it additionally carries zero information that s13 did not.
rows.fix: Replace it with a structurally different microbe entirely - a pennate diatom, an acantharian, anything that is not the s13 wheel - and paint it with the volume the engine gives everything else.

rows.readsAs: a tardigrade / water bear, pale
rows.defect: Reads correctly - all the tardigrade must-reads are present and visible. Family-level only: it is the s17/s5 chassis in white, distinguished from its siblings by hue alone.
rows.fix: Vary the trunk proportion or the leg count read so it is not purely a repaint of s17.

rows.readsAs: a bunch of pale grapes caught in a bramble, or a spiky virus
rows.defect: The spines are thin dark blue-grey lines only a shade off the background value, so instead of reading as a radiating axopod halo they read as scratches or damage on the canvas. Their burst origin sits in the small dark hole at the upper-left of the sphere cluster rather than at the cluster's centre of mass, so the halo and the body look like two separate objects overlaid. The spheres themselves are glossy beads with one arbitrary dark oval on the largest.
rows.fix: Light the spines - warm them lighter than the field and taper them from a thick base - and re-centre the burst on the middle of the sphere mass.

rows.readsAs: a group of flagellated protozoa / trypanosomes
rows.defect: Reads correctly - five ivory teardrop cells, each with a red nucleus and a long sinusoidal flagellum. Minor: the cells are near-identical in size and all tilted the same way, so the group is a little mechanical.
rows.fix: Scale two of the five cells differently and vary their long-axis angle.

rows.readsAs: a tardigrade / water bear - specifically, the exact same one as microbe-h2-s17
rows.defect: The tardigrade itself is fine, but this is a colour-identical twin of microbe-h2-s17: same green, same domed topline, same seven segment ribs, same four stumpy clawed legs at the same spacing, same fused snout and eye dot, same ground shadow. Set side by side a viewer cannot tell which is which, so as a distinct species it carries no identity of its own.
rows.fix: Give it a real morphological difference from s17 - a longer flatter trunk, a visible mouth cone or stylets, or claws of a different form - not just a nudged leg position.

rows.readsAs: a green marble, or a jar half full of liquid
rows.defect: There is no organism here at all. It is a single flat-shaded green sphere with one hard specular blob at upper-left, three tiny white dots, and a dead-straight horizontal chord slicing across the lower third in darker green - that chord reads unmistakably as a liquid fill line in a container, which kills any cell read. No membrane, no wall, no organelles, no cilia or flagella, no texture, nothing that distinguishes it from a rendered ball.
rows.fix: Rebuild it as an actual cell - translucent wall with a lit rim, a visible nucleus and granular cytoplasm inside, and delete the straight horizontal chord entirely.

rows.readsAs: two golden flagellated protozoa
rows.defect: Reads correctly - two teardrop cells with red nuclei and long trailing whips. Minor: the two cells meet tip-to-tip in a near-symmetric V and a third flagellum emerges from their junction, so it is briefly unclear which whip belongs to which cell.
rows.fix: Separate the two cells slightly and offset their angles so each flagellum has an unambiguous attachment point.

rows.readsAs: a pink tardigrade / water-bear plush toy
rows.defect: The eight lobopod legs that ARE the tardigrade identity are painted the same magenta as the belly, so at a glance only the tiny dark claw tufts show and the animal reads as a legless pink blob resting on bristles. The cuticle segmentation is three hairline scratches on an otherwise perfectly smooth balloon, so there is no plate structure. The head is an undifferentiated bump with no mouth cone or stylet, just two dark dots stacked vertically that read as one eye plus a nostril.
rows.fix: Darken and lengthen the legs a full value step below the body so each stumpy limb has its own visible shaft against the belly, and cut the segmentation as real overlapping plate edges (shadowed leading edge, lit trailing edge) instead of thin scratch lines.

rows.readsAs: a mint-green tardigrade / water-bear plush toy — the same animal as s8 recoloured
rows.defect: Structurally it is s8 with a hue change: identical topline, identical body depth, identical three scratch-line segmentation, identical mouthless head bump with the same two stacked dots, identical five leg nubs leaving the silhouette straight down from the belly, identical claw tufts and identical shadow. The legs read a little better here only because they are tonally darker. Nothing distinguishes it as a separate organism, and the head still has no mouth or terminal claw pair.
rows.fix: Give this one a different body plan rather than a different colour — e.g. a lower, longer, more distinctly four-pair-segmented trunk with a visible terminal (fifth) leg pair swung backward and a protruding mouth cone at the front, so the two microbes no longer share one silhouette.

rows.readsAs: A woolly lamb or young sheep with a long pointed face — an anteater-headed sheep, not an aardvark
rows.defect: All three must-reads are missing or broken. (1) The snout is long but it is a flat narrow wedge with a separate thin blade of a lower jaw hanging under it like a stray sliver — nothing tubular, nothing of the blunt fleshy pig-disc nose. (2) There are no tall rabbit ears at all; instead a large flat oval disc is plastered against the side of the head with the eye sitting inside it like a lemur eye-patch or a satellite dish, and behind it sit two small dark rounded nubs. The one feature that is 100 percent of an aardvark's silhouette is absent. (3) The back is flat with a mid-spine sag instead of the steep hip arch, and the tail is a thin high-set lamb crescent, not a thick tapering kangaroo tail. On top of that the pelt is dense white fleece strokes (an aardvark is near-naked pinkish-grey with sparse bristles), the feet end in small dark cloven hooves instead of heavy digging claws, and the forelimbs and hindlimbs are the same length so the massive aardvark hindquarters never appear.
rows.fix: Rebuild the body, not the paint: raise the rump so the topline arches to its peak over the hips and drops away to a low shoulder and a low-carried head, thicken the hindlimbs and haunches to roughly 1.4x the forelimbs, replace the hooves with wide splayed claw-toed digging feet, swap the fleece strokes for near-bare grey-pink hide, and most urgently delete the flat cheek disc and stand two tall narrow leaf-shaped ears up off the crown clear of the eye.

rows.readsAs: a coiled earthworm with a giant leaf or spade stuck on the front
rows.defect: The body lies completely flat in the coil plane -- nothing is reared, so the single loudest must-read (front third raised vertically, taller than wide) is simply not drawn. The hood is a huge flat elliptical plate fused INTO the head rather than spread behind it: the eye sits on the plate, the snout and tongue emerge from its lower right edge, and a large wedge is notched out of the lower left as if the disc were bitten, which reads as a render defect. The plate is nearly as large as the entire coil.
rows.fix: Rebuild the pose: lift the front third of the body off the coil into a vertical S standing above the base, put a normal wedge head on top of it, and draw the hood as a symmetric rib-fanned cape flaring behind and below that head, narrower than the coil and with no notch cut out of it.
rows.verifyWhy: UPHELD, but two of the three stated causes are mis-described. WHAT I SAW (440x440 png; I measured the lit-pixel bbox and zoomed the head at 5x-10x): the animal is a thick, uniform-diameter corrugated tube coiled into a flat loop lying entirely in the picture plane, with a large near-circular hood disk at the right end of the loop, at the same height as the coil. Lit-pixel bbox is x71-372, y126-285 = 302 wide x 160 tall, aspect w/h 1.89. The packet asks for aspect 1.1 and states 'the reared cobra is taller than it is wide'. CONFIRMED ABSENT: mustRead 'front third of the body reared vertically'. There is no neck, no vertical column, no elevation of any kind - the head disk sits level with the coil and the animal is nearly twice as wide as it is tall. This alone is a FAIL of the defining identity read. CORRECTION 1 - the head is NOT 'fused into the plate' with the eye on the plate. The head is a genuinely separate lens/almond shape with its own dark outline, drawn ON TOP of the hood disk, and the eye (white sclera, black vertical slit pupil - the 'fixed lidless stare' mustRead IS present and reads well) sits on that head lens, not on the plate. The real geometry error is worse than 'fused': the head lens is entirely CONTAINED INSIDE the hood disk's outline. Its snout tip terminates ~20px short of the disk's right edge, so the hood wraps around IN FRONT of the snout, and the red forked tongue starts on the disk surface at the snout, crosses over the plate, and only exits into open space past the disk's right rim. So mustRead 'flared hood spread BEHIND the head' fails on direction, not on presence - a hood is drawn, with radiating rib striations and a scalloped lower edge (so 'spread ribs, not a collar' is honoured in texture), but it surrounds the head like a plate the head is embossed on rather than fanning out behind it. CORRECTION 2 - there is NO 'big wedge notched out of the lower left' of the plate. The lower edge of the hood is a deliberate two-lobe scallop with a downward point between the lobes (correct fan-edge treatment), and the dark area under the lower-left is the cast ground shadow plus the coil tube passing in front. The only genuine render artifact is much smaller and elsewhere: at the head lens's REAR-LOWER corner (~orig x283-292, y226-236) the outline makes a squared step/jog instead of a curve, leaving a ~7px rectangular chip beside a small round nub, which at 1:1 reads as a bite taken out of the head. Worth fixing but it is not the reason this fails. SCALE: the hood disk is ~120x120px against a coil of ~170x160px - so it is roughly the coil's height and ~70% of its width, large and cartoonish but not 'nearly as large as the entire coil' as claimed. LAST ISSUE the other judge did not raise: the body itself reads as an annelid/corrugated hose, not a snake - evenly spaced hard crescent ridge bands run the whole length with zero taper, no visible tail tip, and no scale-row or belly-scute differentiation. FIX ORDER: (1) rear the front third into a vertical column so the silhouette is taller than wide; (2) move the hood behind the head so the snout and tongue clear its outline; (3) taper the coil and swap the ring corrugation for scale rows; (4) round off the step-notch at the head's rear-lower corner.

rows.readsAs: a dark red-brown earthworm coiled in a ring
rows.defect: Both identity must-reads are absent. The head is the family's rounded bud, no wider than the neck -- there is no blocky triangular pit-viper skull, no cheek flare, no set-off behind the jaw. The mouth is closed with the standard tongue poking out, so the white mouth lining that gives the animal its name is nowhere in the image. The build is not noticeably heavier than the Mamba beside it; it is the identical tube, only darker and more desaturated, and the value is so low the pale blotches barely separate from the ground.
rows.fix: Open the head into a gape aimed at the viewer with a bright white mouth interior and visible fangs, and widen the skull to a broad triangle that steps down sharply to a much thinner neck.
rows.verifyWhy:
FAIL upheld, and the geometry is worse than the original claim states. Packet mustRead: thick heavy-bodied build - blocky triangular pit-viper head much wider than the neck - white mouth lining shown in a gape. All three are absent; I checked each by zoom and by pixel measurement, not by eye alone.

WHAT I SAW. The asset is a 440x440 canvas holding a single flat coil: a tube wound into a doughnut with the tail buried under the near loop and the head emerging at the right on a short straight neck, plus an elliptical drop shadow. The head (visible from x~274 to x~325, y~194 to ~231 in source pixels) is a smooth almond/teardrop ellipse. At 8x and again at 16x it is a plain flat fill with a soft top-lit gradient: no jaw line, no lip, no mouth line of any kind, no set-off neck constriction, no supraocular brow ridge, no loreal pit, no dark eye stripe. It is not wider than the tube it sits on - it is a rounded bud that continues the neck's diameter and then tapers to the snout. The judge's description of the head is exactly right.

THE WHITE MOUTH - CONFIRMED ABSENT, WITH PROOF. I scanned the whole image for near-white pixels (r>170, g>170, b>160). There are 56 such pixels total and they occupy a single 10x11 box at x 302-311, y 202-212 - that is the eye sclera (a white disc with a dark vertical slit pupil), and nothing else. Brightest pixel in the entire file is (304,205) at rgb 248,247,244, inside that eye. So the animal's namesake feature - the gaping white mouth lining - has zero pixels devoted to it. The mouth is not merely closed; no mouth is drawn at all. The only thing forward of the snout is a pink forked tongue.

SHARED CHASSIS - CONFIRMED, AND STRONGER THAN CLAIMED. I ran column run-length scans on all five family members. Cottonmouth and Mamba return byte-identical silhouette runs from x=280 through x=315 (x280 125-279, x285 121-283, x290 133-271, x295 129-275, x300 145-255, x305 145-259, x310 161-239, x315 161-247 - identical in both files). Whole-silhouette areas: Cottonmouth 37,452 px; Viper 38,148; Mamba 40,191; Rattlesnake 40,557; Cobra 42,799. Bounding boxes: Cottonmouth 275x249, Mamba 302x249. So the Cottonmouth is not merely 'no heavier than the Mamba' - it is the SMALLEST and NARROWEST body in the batch, drawn slightly slimmer than the whip-thin mamba it is supposed to contrast against. A head-crop strip of Cottonmouth / Mamba / Viper / Rattlesnake side by side shows four copies of one almond head, one eye, one tongue, differing only in hue and a few pixels of scale; the Cottonmouth's head is the smallest of the four. There is no viper morphology anywhere in this family.

WHERE THE CLAIM IS WRONG - THE COLOUR DIAGNOSIS. The judge says the blotches 'barely separate from the background' because the asset is 'so desaturated'. Desaturation is the wrong cause and would send the fix in the wrong direction. Measured over the body region: median chroma (max-min)/max is 0.21 with p90 at 0.48 - that is respectable saturation. What is broken is VALUE: the median max-channel is 52/255 and p90 is 64/255, i.e. the entire animal is rendered at roughly 20 percent luminance against a near-black field. Gamma-lifting the file reveals markings that genuinely exist: rusty salmon-orange saddle crossbands over the dorsal midline of the coil plus roughly eight pale cream dorsal spots. They are painted; they are simply invisible at ship brightness. Separately, the pattern that IS there is the wrong pattern - cottonmouths carry dark hourglass/pinched crossbands on a lighter ground with a bold dark cheek stripe, whereas these read as scattered pale dots with warm bands.

FIX ORDER. (1) Give this species its own head primitive: a broad blocky triangle whose jaw corners flare to roughly 1.8-2x the neck width, sharply pinched at the neck, with a heavy brow over the eye and a visible pit between eye and nostril. (2) Draw the open gape - the identity read is a wide-open mouth with a matte white/ivory interior lining, which is currently 0 pixels. (3) Thicken the body: it must out-mass the Mamba visibly, not undercut it. (4) Raise exposure/value on the whole render by roughly 2x and restage the markings as dark hourglass crossbands plus a dark eye stripe; do not touch saturation, it is already adequate.

rows.readsAs: the Cottonmouth image recoloured grey
rows.defect: The reference calls for a very long slender whip-like body and the render gives the opposite: the same thick constant-diameter tube as every other member, coiled into the same doughnut despite the posture being specified as crawling. The head is the shared rounded bud, not a narrow coffin wedge, and there is no long fixed grin mouthline -- just the shared closed snout and tongue. The surface is the same coarse transverse ribbing, which contradicts the required smooth uniform scales.
rows.fix: Halve the body diameter and quadruple its length into a long shallow travelling S across the frame, then give it a narrow elongated coffin head with a straight mouthline running well back past the eye.
rows.verifyWhy:
I looked at the full 440x440 render, at a 6x nearest-neighbour crop of the head, at a 6x crop of the body wall, and at a 2.6x brightness-lifted full view (the asset is very dark and the tail is invisible at native exposure). I also pixel-measured cross-sections against Cottonmouth and Viper. The FAIL stands, but three of the stated causes are wrong or imprecise and must not be fixed as written.

WHAT IS ACTUALLY THERE. A grey-olive snake wound into a ~1.5-turn flat spiral: an outer ring plus an inner arc whose tail tapers to a proper point at roughly (250,180) inside the hole. Head exits the ring at the right on a short neck, magenta forked tongue at ~15 deg above horizontal. A detached soft ellipse shadow sits well below the body with no contact point, so the whole animal hovers.

CORRECTION 1 - 'the same thick constant-diameter tube ... despite aspect being 10' is FACTUALLY WRONG and would send the fix in the wrong direction. Measured at the left wall of the coil (row 200, and rows 190/175 as controls) the tube cross-section is 38 px on Mamba vs 48 px on Cottonmouth and 42 px on Viper - the Mamba tube is the thinnest of the three, ~20% thinner than the Cottonmouth. Its centreline loop is also the longest: Ramanujan perimeter of the centreline ellipse is ~493 px vs ~395 px for Cottonmouth. So the rendered length:width is ~13:1 against a spec of 10, and Cottonmouth measures ~8:1 against a spec of 7. The aspect parameter IS being applied and is if anything overshooting. The real defect is that ALL of the extra length is spent adding another turn of spiral inside the same square frame, so the elongation is consumed by the coil and never reaches the silhouette. Aspect 2 (Viper), 7 (Cottonmouth) and 10 (Mamba) all produce the same compact ring outline; at thumbnail size only hue separates them. Do not thin the tube further - change what the length is spent on.

CORRECTION 2 - 'no narrow coffin head' is PARTLY WRONG. Side by side at 6x the two heads are clearly different shapes: Cottonmouth's is a broad blunt oval that bulges wider than its neck; Mamba's is a distinctly narrow, long, forward-tapering lozenge flush with the neck width. The slenderness is present. What is missing is the coffin's ANGULARITY - a squared-off snout tip, straight canthal edges above the eye, a flat top plate. The render gives a smooth almond with no facets. Fix the geometry of the snout, not the width.

CONFIRMED 3 - 'no fixed grin mouthline' is CORRECT and is the outright-absent must-read. At 6x there is zero mouth geometry on this head: no lip seam, no jaw line, no mouth corner, no rictus. The head is a solid unbroken blob with one eye on it. (The eye is also wrong in a smaller way: a white sclera with a black VERTICAL SLIT pupil, though the row specifies eyes: normal and a mamba has a round dark pupil.)

CONFIRMED 4 - 'coarse transverse ribbing instead of smooth uniform scales' is CORRECT, and the precise diagnosis is worth recording: a rib-stroke generator draws short crescent strokes that wrap the FULL circumference of the tube rather than sitting as a ventral scute band on the belly only. On Mamba it fires at higher stroke density and thinner stroke width than on Cottonmouth, so it is parameterised, not copy-pasted - but denser ribbing reads as MORE segmented, not smoother. The surface reads as a millipede or a vacuum hose, not as scales. 'Smooth uniform scales' is failed.

CORRECTION 5 - 'it is the Cottonmouth image recoloured grey' is OVERSTATED as literal fact (different tube diameter, different rib density, different head shape, different hue) but the structural charge holds and should be recorded as the family finding: identical spiral chassis, identical head-lozenge-plus-forked-tongue assembly at the same exit angle, identical scattered pale blob speckles on the dorsum, identical detached floating shadow ellipse. Five venomous snakes share one body.

UNDER-WEIGHTED BY THE ORIGINAL JUDGE - posture. The row specifies posture: crawling and the note says mambas are often drawn rearing the front third. The render is a static hovering spiral with nothing crawling, nothing reared, no ground contact, no forward vector. This is the single highest-leverage fix for this species: an extended, travelling, S-curved body with the head and front third lifted would deliver the whip-like read, the visible elongation, and the posture spec in one change, whereas trimming the tube diameter would deliver none of them.

BAND. Of three must-reads: whip-like body present in measurement but not in read; coffin head half present (narrow yes, coffin no); smooth scales plus grin mouthline absent outright, with no mouth drawn at all. Posture spec unmet. Silhouette not separable from two other members of its own family. That is a FAIL.

rows.readsAs: a coiled tan snake -- readable as a rattlesnake, but only because of four small beads
rows.defect: The rattle is present as a short chain of four pale beads at the lower left, which is the one identity marker in this entire batch that actually landed -- but it is tiny, low-contrast, and reads as loose pebbles beside the body rather than as a segmented horny tip continuous with the tail. The other two must-reads fail: the head is the shared rounded bud with no broad triangular arrow shape and no thin neck behind it, and the neck is not reared in an S -- the whole animal lies flat in the coil plane like the rest of the family.
rows.fix: Scale the rattle up two or three times, taper the tail into it so the segments read as a continuation of the body, and lift the neck off the coil into an S with a wide arrow-head at the top.

rows.readsAs: a khaki earthworm coiled in a ring, indistinguishable from the Mamba but for hue
rows.defect: All three must-reads are missing. There is no zigzag or diamond dorsal chain anywhere on the body -- the only surface incident is the family's transverse ribbing, so the single marking that identifies an adder is absent. The head is the shared rounded bud with no broad triangle and no sharp set-off from a thin neck. The body is not short and heavy; it is the same medium tube coiled into the same doughnut as the ten-aspect Mamba. Only the vertical slit pupil survives, and it is on every asset in the batch.
rows.fix: Paint a high-contrast dark zigzag chain running the full length of the dorsal midline over a pale ground, and rebuild the skull as a wide flat triangle stepping down to a neck about half its width.
rows.verifyWhy:
Looked at Viper.png at full size, then at 6x-10x zooms of the head and body, then at a contrast-boosted (median-centred, gain 3.5) pass over the whole tube, then measured the silhouette numerically (background-delta mask + chamfer distance transform). VERDICT UPHELD, but two of the three stated causes need correcting.

WHAT IS THERE: a tan/olive snake wound into a flat spiral of roughly 1.5 turns, head emerging at the right on a down-left neck, red forked tongue, and a white-sclera eye with a black vertical slit pupil. Silhouette bbox 78,130-361,269 = 284x140, aspect 2.03 (the row asks for aspect 2, so the aspect itself is honoured). Coil sits low and flat as the note asks.

MUST-READ 1 - zigzag or diamond dorsal chain: ABSENT. Confirmed, but the claim's parenthetical is not literally true. The surface is not ONLY the shared ribbing: under contrast boost there are roughly five or six faint circular blotches on the tube (a darker one at ~x110,y200; another at ~x195,y200; pale highlight dots at ~x250,y175 and ~x255,y225) plus a couple on the neck. They are round, scattered, very low contrast and read as noise/spotting, not as a chain, so they do not deliver the must-read - but a fix brief that says 'nothing but ribbing is there' will miss that a spot-noise layer already exists and is the thing that must be replaced by a linked zigzag/diamond dorsal band. Everything else on the body is the transverse crescent scale-row arcs shared by all five assets in the batch. There is no dark vertebral stripe of any kind.

MUST-READ 2 - broad triangular head sharply set off from a thin neck: ABSENT, and stronger than the claim states. The head is a smooth almond/ovoid bud with no jaw corners, no temporal flare and no constriction behind it. Measured with a distance transform: the head's maximum local width is 27.7 px (widest point at 297,218, just behind the eye) while the tube immediately behind the head is 28.3 px (at 268,235). The head is therefore a hair NARROWER than its own neck - not merely 'not set off', but inverted from the required read. Cropping Rattlesnake.png at the same coordinates gives a visually identical almond bud with an identical white-sclera slit eye and identical red tongue in a near-identical tan, so this head is a shared chassis part, not a viper skull.

MUST-READ 3 - short thick heavy body: THE CLAIM IS WRONG ON THE MEASUREMENT. The Viper is NOT 'the same medium tube as the aspect-10 Mamba'. Top-arc tube thickness is 37 px on the Viper versus 28-30 px on the Mamba, and total body pixels are 21,085 versus 16,566 inside near-identical bounding boxes (Viper 284x140, Mamba 299x145). The Viper's tube is roughly 25-30% heavier than the Mamba's, so gauge IS differentiated from that neighbour. What actually fails here is relative, not absolute: the Rattlesnake's tube is 54 px and 27,195 px of body, so within its own family the Viper is the middle-gauge animal, not the stout one, and nothing about the coil length or turn count says 'short'. Call this must-read weakly/partially met rather than absent.

MUST-READ 4 (the row's note) - vertical slit pupils: present, but carries zero identity. Zoomed Mamba.png and Rattlesnake.png heads: both have the exact same white-sclera vertical-slit eye despite the packet listing eyes:normal for all five. The judge is right that this survives and right that it is batch-wide.

FAMILY/CHASSIS: all five venomous snakes render into the same envelope - Viper 284x140 (a2.03), Mamba 299x145 (a2.06), Rattlesnake 299x156 (a1.92), Cottonmouth 264x124 (a2.13), Cobra 299x159 (a1.88) - against reference aspects of 2, 10, 1.3, 7 and 1.1. One flat spiral, one almond head bud, one slit eye, one red forked tongue, one transverse-rib scale texture; the only per-species incident anywhere in the batch is the Rattlesnake's white bead rattle. The Viper is that chassis in tan at medium gauge - i.e. the Rattlesnake with the rattle deleted.

BAND: FAIL. The dorsal zigzag/diamond chain and the broad triangular head on a thin neck are the two features that make a viper a viper, and both are absent, one of them inverted. The asset reads as 'generic coiled snake', identifiable only by elimination.

rows.readsAs: a generic floating duck / wooden duck decoy in olive
rows.defect: The bill is a pointed orange cone, not the flat spatulate mallard paddle the must-read names — it comes to a sharp tip. No webbed feet are drawn at all, set-far-back or otherwise; the body is a legless egg cut off at the waterline. No mallard cues: no green head, no white neck ring, no chestnut breast, no blue speculum — the whole bird is one flat olive with a quilted crosshatch patch and a dark grey scythe on the flank that reads as a painted-on decal rather than a folded wing.
rows.fix: Rebuild the bill as a broad flat paddle — wide at the tip, rounded off, with a visible nail and a nostril, seen slightly from above so its width reads — and give the mallard its head/collar/breast blocking instead of a single olive fill.

rows.readsAs: a white domestic duck / a plain white decoy — not an eider
rows.defect: This is the Duck asset recoloured white; the silhouette, the eye, the cone bill, the flank scythe, the crosshatch patch and the water rings are identical. Every one of the three must-reads is absent. The head has the stepped forehead the note explicitly calls WRONG — there is a clear notch where the bill meets a rounded ball of a skull, instead of the unbroken sloping wedge from bill tip to crown that IS the eider. The black-and-white blocking is gone (the bird is uniformly white with grey shading, no black flanks, no black cap, no black stern), and there is no pale green nape anywhere. It does not sit low and bulky either — it floats at the same height as the tiny Duck.
rows.fix: Redraw the head as a single straight ramp: bill tip, bill and forehead on one continuous line up to the crown with no step, then block the body in hard black-and-white masses (white back and breast, black belly, black cap) with a pale green wash on the nape.

rows.readsAs: a grebe or a loon — a small speckled diving bird, not a goose
rows.defect: The neck is a thin snake-like tube of roughly the same width as the bill, bent forward at a diagonal — it is neither thick nor held upright, and the must-read says the long THICK UPRIGHT neck is the identity. The bill is the family cone, not a flat rounded goose bill. There are no feet and no legs, so 'heavy body on webbed feet' is absent; the bird floats in the same water rings as the swimmers despite the biped posture spec. None of the Canada goose read survives: no black neck, no black head, no white chinstrap — the head and neck are pale tan and the body is a brown-grey speckled dome, which is exactly grebe plumage.
rows.fix: Thicken the neck to roughly three bill-widths, stand it vertical off a heavy chest, and paint the whole head and neck solid black with a hard white chinstrap wedge running under the cheek — then set the body on two visible legs with webbed feet.

rows.readsAs: a swan, or possibly a white goose
rows.defect: The long white neck on a big white floating body does get the read across, but the neck is a shallow forward-leaning arc, not the deep S-curve the must-read names — there is no downward hook at the base and no back-curve at the top, so the classic question-mark never forms. The bill is the family's pointed orange cone with no coloured base at all: no black knob, no black mask running back to the eye, and it tapers to a point instead of being broad and flat. The body does not float high and proud — it is the same squat egg as the ducks, and the grey scythe plus quilted crosshatch across the back muddy what should be a clean white mass.

rows.readsAs: a striped dachshund, or a miniature okapi

rows.readsAs: a beige dachshund with a squirrel tail

rows.readsAs: an orange dachshund; identical to the Fisher card in a warmer hue

rows.readsAs: a pale grey-beige dachshund

rows.readsAs: a tan dachshund with a black-tipped tail

rows.readsAs: a golden bread loaf on dog legs; a small dachshund

The torso is deep and loaf-like rather than tube-like, the body is not arched, and the head is a distinctly wider dog wedge on the neck instead of barely wider than it. The tail is missing altogether.
rows.fix: Shorten the legs to stubs so the belly skims the ground, arch the spine into a shallow hump, and slim the torso and skull to a near-constant tube diameter from nose to hips.

rows.readsAs: a shaggy beige sheep or goat on dachshund proportions
rows.defect: The two marks that name a wolverine are both absent: the topline is dead flat with no humped shoulders, and there is no pale stripe sweeping along the flank to the tail — the coat is uniform shaggy cream with only a darker head. The build is not heavy or bear-like, it is the same mid-weight family sausage, and the paws are small pale toe nubs with no claws at all, let alone huge ones.
rows.fix: Raise a pronounced shoulder hump above a dipping back, paint a broad pale blond band curving from behind the shoulder along the flank into the tail base against a dark chocolate body, and enlarge the feet into wide dark pads with long visible claws.

rows.readsAs: a plump round blackbird or starling pasted diagonally on a plank, with a yellow horn on top of its head
rows.defect: The chisel bill is not on the face - a yellow tapered cone rises from the CROWN of the skull at roughly 55 degrees up-and-back, pointing into open air away from the bark, so it reads as a unicorn horn or party hat rather than a bill. The body is a near-circular plump mass whose left third hangs off the trunk into black background, and its axis runs diagonally down-left instead of parallel to the trunk, so the vertical clinging posture never reads. The single visible foot is a yellow zigzag claw floating entirely OFF the left edge of the trunk, gripping nothing - no foot touches the bark anywhere. There is no neck. A small grey striped fan sprouts from the nape behind the head, reading as a stray fin or a second tail. Only the stiff pointed tail below the body is arguably present, and even that is a thin dark wedge angling down-right rather than propped straight down against the bark.
rows.fix: Rebuild the pose around the trunk: elongate the body into a vertical trunk-hugging teardrop fully inside the trunk silhouette with the belly line flush to the bark, move the bill off the crown to the front of the face and lay it horizontal so its tip meets the wood, and plant both zygodactyl feet ON the bark under the breast with the stiff tail propped straight down beneath them.

rows.readsAs: a plump grey garden earthworm
rows.defect: The body is nowhere near thread-thin - it is the same fat mid-swollen tube as every other asset in the batch, running about 5:1 rather than the specified 10:1, so the 'a few centimetres of hair-thin glacier annelid' read is gone. It also carries a distinct bulbous head knob with a visible black dot eye even though the reference says eyes are hidden, and there is nothing cold, icy or glacial about the presentation - it is the family chassis in slate grey on the same crawling ground shadow.
rows.fix: Halve the body diameter and stretch it to a true 10:1 hair-thin thread, delete the eye dot and the bulbous head knob so the anterior end is just a blunt rounded taper.

rows.readsAs: a cream-coloured earthworm
rows.defect: This is the wrong phylum on sight. A lancelet is a translucent blade pointed at BOTH ends with V-shaped myotome chevrons showing through the skin, a notochord line end to end, and an oral fringe of cirri - none of that is present. What is drawn is the identical annelid chassis in cream: heavily ringed opaque segments, a bulbous distinct head knob, and a black dot eye on an animal that anatomically has no head and no eyes. It is also on a crawling ground shadow despite the swimming posture. Every one of the three must-reads is absent and a directly contradicted feature (an eye) has been added.
rows.fix: Rebuild as a flattened translucent lance pointed at both ends with a straight notochord line and stacked V-chevrons visible through the body, no head knob and no eye, and a small tentacle fringe at the anterior tip.
rows.verifyWhy:
UPHELD after 6x enlargement of both ends. What is on canvas: a cream/bone-coloured tube laid out in a shallow S-arch across the lower-middle of the frame (~230x90px of a 440px square), sitting on an explicit dark cast ground-shadow, i.e. a substrate crawler, not the 'swimming' posture the row specifies. The body is built from roughly 22 opaque overlapping annuli — each ring is a lozenge plate stacked in front of the next with its own hard drop-shadow, giving a rope-of-washers 3D read. There is zero translucency anywhere; the fill is flat opaque cream with a soft top-light gradient. This is the family earthworm/annelid chassis recoloured cream, exactly as the first judge said.

HEAD (crop x95 y180 w100 h100): a distinctly bulbous, near-spherical dome knob wider than the trunk behind it, separated from the first body ring by a neck pinch. Set into it, upper-left, is a small black dot eye WITH a white specular highlight — the highlight makes it read as an eye more emphatically than the judge stated, not less. The head terminus is completely bald: no cirri, no tentacles, no fringe, no oral hood, not even a mouth line. The row says eyes: hidden and 'no head, no jaws and no eyes'; the asset supplies a head AND an eye — an explicitly contradicted feature, correctly flagged.

TAIL (crop x250 y190 w110 h100): NOT pointed. The rings crowd together and terminate in a blunt rounded club, the same diameter as the trunk. So 'blade pointed at both ends' fails at BOTH ends, which the judge's phrasing understated — head is a bulb, tail is a club.

The one near-miss the judge did not address, and the fix must not be fooled by it: the stacked segment plates are arc-shaped and could be mistaken for chevrons at thumbnail size. They are not myotomes. They are transverse annuli running perpendicular to the body axis, each a raised opaque plate with a cast shadow — segmentation you see ON the surface. Myotome chevrons are nested V/<-shaped muscle bands seen THROUGH translucent skin, angled back along the axis, with no relief and no shadow. Present rendering communicates 'segmented worm'; the required rendering communicates 'muscle blocks under glass'. No notochord line of any kind is drawn — no axial stripe, no internal line.

All three must-reads absent (no translucent double-pointed blade, no myotome chevrons, no oral cirri fringe), plus an added contradicted eye, plus wrong posture and a ground shadow. Reads as an annelid, wrong phylum on sight. FAIL stands.

rows.readsAs: a pink centipede
rows.defect: The lateral fringe is there but it is drawn as bare straight red-orange matchsticks radiating stiffly from the flanks, with no paddle-shaped parapodial lobe under them - so they read as jointed centipede legs rather than as fleshy bristle-bearing lobes. The head must-read is entirely missing: instead of a tapering prostomium with short tentacles and palps there is the family's blunt bulbous knob with a single dot eye. No iridescence in the flat matte salmon fill.
rows.fix: Replace each bare spike with a small fleshy paddle lobe carrying a fan of finer chaetae, and taper the anterior end into a pointed prostomium with two palps and a pair of short antennae instead of the bulbous knob.

rows.readsAs: an orange centipede
rows.defect: Identical asset to Marine Worm with the hue shifted to orange and the curve slightly flattened - the two are not distinguishable as different animals. The paddle lobes are absent; the chaetae are bare straight sticks with no lobe beneath them. The head is the family's rounded knob with a dot eye: no palps, no antennae, and no eversible jawed proboscis anywhere, so the single most characteristic polychaete feature never appears.
rows.fix: Give every segment a visible biramous paddle lobe with a chaetal fan, and extend the anterior into an everted proboscis with a pair of dark jaws plus paired palps and antennae.

rows.readsAs: a khaki centipede
rows.defect: The scales - the feature the animal is named for and the only thing that makes it a scale worm - are completely absent. There are no elytra, no two rows of overlapping plates roofing the back; the back is the same plain crescent-ring segmentation used by every other asset here, with the same bare red spikes bolted to the flanks. The body is also the long 5:1-plus S-curve tube of the family chassis rather than the specified short flattened oval at 3:1. Recoloured khaki, this is indistinguishable from the Polychaete and Marine Worm renders.
rows.fix: Shorten and flatten the body to a squat 3:1 oval and roof the entire dorsum with two staggered rows of large overlapping oval elytra, letting only small bristle tufts poke out from the gaps between plates.
rows.verifyWhy:
UPHELD, but two parts of the stated cause are wrong and would send a fixer to the wrong place. Examined at 1x and at 6x (crops of the head/anterior at src x95-225,y190-270 and the posterior at x225-350,y160-270), plus pixel measurement of all five family silhouettes.

WHAT IS ACTUALLY ON SCREEN: a khaki/greyish-olive worm in a shallow S-curve, head lower-left, tail upper-right, over a soft elliptical drop shadow. The head is a smooth featureless dome with ONE small round black dot eye near its top-left; no palps, no antennae, no prostomial detail, no proboscis. Behind the head the body is a series of ~30 transverse crescent plates. Roughly 30 straight red-brown rods radiate from the body margin, above and below, uniform length, no taper, no branching, no tufting.

CORRECTION 1 - "no overlapping scale plates anywhere" is FALSE as written. At 6x the segments are unmistakably imbricate: each crescent overlaps the one behind it like roof shingles, and each overlap casts its own dark shadow band on the plate beneath. This is genuinely plated, not the plain incised ring segmentation the claim describes. A fixer given that claim verbatim would add overlap that is already there and change nothing. The REAL defect is topology, not overlap: there is ONE full-width transverse series running the length of the animal, spanning edge to edge with no midline seam and no discrete scale outlines. The must-read demands TWO ROWS of overlapping scale plates roofing the back - i.e. paired left/right longitudinal rows of discrete oval elytra with a visible midline gap between them and free posterior/lateral scale margins. Nothing paired, nothing longitudinal, nothing discrete is drawn. So the identity must-read is absent, but it is absent because the plating runs the wrong AXIS and is undivided, not because plating is missing.

CORRECTION 2 - the sibling comparison is right in substance but misattributed. I cropped Marine_Worm.png and Polychaete_Worm.png over the same window. Marine Worm is the SAME asset in pink: same S-curve pose, same crescent-shingle segmentation, same straight red bristle rods, same smooth head dome with a single black dot eye, same drop shadow. Ink bounding boxes confirm it - Scale Worm 226x123 px at (107,158), Marine Worm 216x126 px at (112,157). That is one chassis in two colours. Polychaete Worm, however, is NOT the same pose - it is a shallower, nearly straight arc in orange (bbox 208x84). So the collision to fix is Scale Worm vs Marine Worm specifically; Polychaete shares the chassis parts but not the curve.

CORRECTION 3 - the aspect complaint is correct and I can quantify it. Spec is aspect 3 (short flattened oval). Measured body band thickness is ~31-33 px against an arc length of roughly 270 px along the S, i.e. about 8.5:1 - the same as the Marine Worm and Polychaete rows, which are specced at aspect 8. The aspect-3 stubbiness was simply never applied; the animal is the long family tube.

WHAT DOES PASS: "bristle tufts poking out between the scales" is partially met - bristles are present along both margins and do emerge at the plate junctions. But they are single straight rods, not tufts, and they are the identical generic bristle rods used on the two sibling worms, so they carry no Scale Worm identity of their own. eyes:small and posture:crawling are satisfied.

BAND: FAIL stands. The one feature the animal is named for - paired rows of discrete elytra - is not readable anywhere in the image, the flattened 3:1 body is not drawn, and the asset is a recolour of a sibling in the same batch. FIX DIRECTION: shorten the body to ~3:1 and flatten it into a broad oval, kill the S-curve, then replace the single transverse crescent series with two staggered longitudinal rows of discrete overlapping oval scales left and right of a visible midline seam, letting bristle tufts emerge from the gaps between adjacent scales.
